## B-126 — Rapid burst: receiver silently stops consuming mid-burst; messages strand on the relay until a COLD RESTART ⚠️ P1 · REPRODUCED 2-device · 2026-07-21

**Founder-reported symptom:** _"4 msg 1,2,3,4 — sent 1,3,4, and 2 sends after sometimes."_
**Status: REPRODUCED deterministically on vc148 with two devices.** Not a send-side defect and
not permanent loss — it is a **receiver-side consumption stall** that a foreground cycle does
NOT heal.

**Setup:** Ranak (`3165d0e1`, Pixel 6a, vc148) → Arnob (`7a3a9618`, CPH2577, vc148), 1:1, both
online, healthy WS, **no throttling** (relay logs clean). 4 envelopes sent in ~2 s.

**What the relay saw — all four accepted and pushed to a LIVE socket:**

| #   | clientMsgId | envelopeId | relay emit         | acked by receiver? | rendered? |
| --- | ----------- | ---------- | ------------------ | ------------------ | --------- |
| 1   | `bb9637dc`  | `52d9b529` | `localSocket=true` | ✅ acked/purged    | ✅ R1     |
| 2   | `6bc99a1b`  | `8dc811a5` | `localSocket=true` | ✅ acked/purged    | ✅ R2     |
| 3   | `482bf83f`  | `93deda44` | `localSocket=true` | ❌ **never acked** | ❌        |
| 4   | `279cb279`  | `5fe9a57c` | `localSocket=true` | ❌ **never acked** | ❌        |

**The receiver consumed the first two of the burst and silently stopped.** Envelopes 3–4 were
emitted to its live socket, never processed, never acked, and sat on the relay as `env:*` keys.

**Recovery ladder (each step verified against the relay's `env:*` keys):**

| Action on receiver                      | Result                                              |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Wait ~7 min, app in foreground          | **still queued, unacked**                           |
| HOME → relaunch (background→foreground) | **still queued, unacked** (drain did NOT fire/heal) |
| **`am force-stop` → cold launch**       | **both acked + rendered** ("2 UNREAD MESSAGES")     |

Net user-visible effect: messages sent in a normal fast-typing burst appear on the peer only
after the app is killed and reopened — **~10 minutes late** in this run (sent 4:18 pm, rendered
4:28 pm). Exactly the founder's "…and 2 sends after sometimes."

**Why it is worse than it looks:**

- **The sender gets no signal.** Bubbles 3–4 sit at single tick ✓ (relay accepted), so the
  sender believes they are fine. No red chip, no retry affordance, nothing to act on.
- **The relay believes it delivered them** (`localSocket=true`), so no push wake is issued —
  the peer has no prompt to open the app, which is the only thing that heals it.
- **G1-RT does not cover this.** These were WS submits (they have submitter mappings), so the
  receipt poll is not involved; the gap is on the RECEIVE side, not the send side.
- Only the 30-day dwell TTL protects the data. Past that, they are gone.

**Root cause — CONFIRMED mechanism (same day, second repro B1–B6, again "2 then stall"):**
the receiver's per-connection **txn chain wedges** on a frame that never resolves, and every
guard around it then fails _silently_:

1. The wedged frame's `finally` never runs, so its envelope ids stay in the L16 **in-flight
   set forever** — `handleDeliver` returns early and the drain `continue`s with **no log
   line** for every redelivery of those ids (WS re-push after a forced reconnect: still
   stranded; verified live).
2. Every later receive frame queues behind the wedge — new envelope **B7 stranded too**
   (pending zset 4→5), proving the stall is global, not per-envelope.
3. The drain kept pulling the same 4 envelopes and hit its **10-page hard cap 3×**
   (`[bravo.drainRelay] hit hard cap of 10 pages` — the ONLY logcat line in the whole
   failure; every other breadcrumb on these paths was Crashlytics-only).
4. Cold restart = fresh process, fresh chain, WAL rollback → everything drains.

The wedging await itself (what the frame was stuck ON) is not yet pinned — the fix makes the
chain name it in logcat on the next field occurrence (`[messenger.txnChain] frame '<label>'
still running after 30000ms`).

**MITIGATED, NOT CURED (client, commits on fix/messenger-audit-b121; v1.0.121/vc149) — a
bounded, loud safety net that stops the GLOBAL freeze but does NOT yet deliver the stuck
burst messages:**

- **Chain watchdog** (`receiveTransaction.ts`): labelled frames; 30 s console.warn naming the
  stuck frame; **120 s force-advance** — the chain tail releases, later frames run, the
  wedged frame's orphaned `BEGIN` is rolled back, and the frame is **disowned** via an
  ownership token so a zombie body that later resumes can neither COMMIT a later frame's
  half-done txn nor corrupt the flags (its throw classifies transient → leave-on-relay,
  never ack-discard).
- **In-flight registry** (`inflightEnvelopes.ts`, new): 150 s stale eviction (> watchdog
  deadline, pinned by test) with loud warn; token-guarded release so the zombie's late
  `finally` can't free a newer attempt's hold; reset on user switch.
- **Drain**: in-flight skips counted; a zero-progress page ends the drain with a specific
  warn instead of spinning 10 identical pulls; WS transient-sql leave-on-relay branch now
  console.warns.

**On-device result (vc149, Pixel 6a → CPH2577, 6-msg burst C1–C6):** the watchdog fired
**exactly as designed** — logcat named the wedged frames (`[messenger.txnChain] frame
'recv:d08e55e8' exceeded 120000ms — force-advancing`), rolled back their open BEGINs, and the
disowned frames threw `txn_frame_disowned` → transient leave-on-relay. The global freeze is
gone (later conversations/frames proceed). **BUT the 4 stuck messages did NOT deliver** —
Redis `pending` held at exactly 4 for 3+ min under continuous redelivery, because the
underlying frame **re-wedges on the same `await` every time it is reprocessed**. Still needs a
**cold restart** to clear, same as vc148. So vc149 bounds and surfaces the failure; it does
not fix delivery.

**Root cause now narrowed (not fully pinned):** ONE `own.decrypt`/receive-frame body hangs on
a JS `await` that never resolves (full 120 s, not slow) — the watchdog rolled back an _open_
BEGIN, so the hang is INSIDE the `runWithRatchetTxn` body (decrypt / markSeen / upsert /
reactions), after BEGIN. Because `SessionManager` holds a **per-address op lock**
(`sessionManager.ts:55` `withLock`), that one hung crypto op wedges EVERY later op for that
peer forever — which is why redelivery (even serial, via the drain) re-hangs behind the
zombie. Ruled out this session: send/receive lock inversion (receiver sent nothing during the
burst — no `envelope.send sub=7a3a9618` in the relay log), and a two-connection SQLite
deadlock (all stores share ONE handle via `ownStore.getDb()`). Consistent with a native
op-sqlite execute that never returns (only a fresh process/connection — cold restart — clears
it). **Next step:** build with `EXPO_PUBLIC_GROUPCALL_FILELOG=1` (+ the usual EXPO bake) to
capture the exact stuck statement, since release strips `console.log` and the `[recv.enter]`
breadcrumbs never reach logcat. Candidate direct fixes once pinned: a per-decrypt timeout that
rejects (freeing the peer lock + rolling back → clean redelivery) and/or a `SessionManager`
lock-reset the watchdog can call on force-advance.

**Repro recipe:** two devices on vc148, both foregrounded in the same 1:1; send 4+ messages
within ~2 s; watch `docker compose logs messenger-service | grep envelope.deliver`, then check
which `env:<id>` keys survive in Redis. Survivors = stranded.

**Not reproduced (ruled out this session):** send-side reordering (all 4 submitted in order,
1/sec, every one accepted), relay throttling (zero 429/throttle log lines), and receiver-side
mis-ordering (`orderingClock.ts` sorts on the sender's stamp, so late arrivals splice into the
correct position — R3R4/R5R6 landed in the right place, just late).

**Residual to confirm:** after the cold restart, bubble **R2 was no longer visible** in the
thread while R1/R3R4/R5R6 were. Could be list pagination rather than loss — needs a store dump
to settle. Flagged, not claimed.

## B-121 / B-122 / B-123 — iOS group-call batch: outbound video, camera flip, push · FIXED (121/123) + BLOCKED (122) · 2026-07-19

**Session frame:** device pair = iPhone 11 (`com.bravosecure.mobile`, cable-installed Release, `aps-environment: development`) + Pixel 7a (`com.bravosecure.app` vc145), both on staging. iOS group calls WORK now (B-120/IOSGV-1 closed by the `RTCFrameCryptorFactory` probe fix, commit 21bc2b5) — these are the defects found once calls could actually start.

### Diagnostic gap that made all three expensive (fix first, read second)

`fileLog.ts` used `RNFS.ExternalDirectoryPath` — **Android-only**; on iOS it is `undefined`, so every append silently no-opped. **Every iOS conclusion in this session up to 14:33Z was inferred from the ANDROID peer's trace.** That is why two plausible-but-wrong fixes shipped before the real one. Now:

- iOS writes to `DocumentDirectoryPath`; pull with
  `xcrun devicectl device copy from --device <udid> --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier com.bravosecure.mobile --source Documents/groupcall-trace.log --destination ./ios-trace.log`
- `[bravo.groupcall.decode]` now carries `dec:` / `rx:` / `B:` (decoded / received / bytesReceived). `B:0` = nothing forwarded; `B>0 dec:0` = arrived and would not decode. Opposite fixes — do not guess between them again.
- Enable with `EXPO_PUBLIC_GROUPCALL_FILELOG=1` at build time. Lines route through `crashLog`, which survives `transform-remove-console` (`console.log` is stripped in production — this is why release logcat was empty).

**Verification trap:** a Hermes bundle stores any string containing a non-ASCII char (our log tags use an em-dash) as **UTF-16**, so ASCII `grep` finds nothing and "the fix is missing" is a false negative. `grep -c` also counts _lines_, and the bundle is one line. Check both encodings.

### B-121 — iOS outbound video invisible on Android (group calls) · FIXED

**Symptom:** iPhone tile showed "Video unavailable" on Android; iPhone AUDIO decoded fine; Android→iOS video fine.
**Fix:** iOS sends a SINGLE video encoding; Android keeps 3-layer simulcast (`webrtc/videoEncodings.ts`).
**Status of the explanation — READ THIS:** dropping to one encoding is **verified on device** as a single-variable change (identical build with simulcast failed). The _mechanism_ is **NOT** established. The FrameCryptor/multi-SSRC story is a HYPOTHESIS; `BravoFrameCryptor.swift` attaches one cryptor per sender and may well cover all layers, and an H264-header-parsing cause fits the same evidence. Do not repeat it as fact.
**Cost:** iOS loses per-receiver layer adaptation — one slow viewer can no longer be served a cheaper layer. Real regression; worth reversing once the mechanism is pinned (use the `dec/rx/B` counters).
**Edge case found by testing, NOT by the device run:** the first fix changed only the boot producer. `HEAD` had **9** inline rid declarations across **three** producer paths — transport-recovery and `toggleVideo` still forced simulcast, so an iOS camera off→on or any reconnect silently restored the bug. A device test only walks the path it walks. Guarded by a static source audit (no producer may inline an encodings ladder).

### B-123 — camera flip in group call · FIXED (root cause + one real bug found en route)

**Symptom:** flip appeared to work (lens changed) but outbound video died; second flip did nothing ("can't reflip"). Both platforms.

**ROOT CAUSE — GC-06 blanking poisons mediasoup's paused flag.** mediasoup latches paused state at construction (`Producer.js:46`):
`this._paused = disableTrackOnPause ? !track.enabled : false;`
GC-06's `withTrackBlanked` sets `enabled = false` across `produce()` (deliberately — no plaintext-video window before the FrameCryptor attaches), so **every producer is born believing it is paused**. The `finally` re-enables the track, so calls look healthy and the wrong flag stays invisible — until `replaceTrack` re-applies it (`Producer.js:245`) and **disables the brand-new track**.

Device proof, iPhone trace:

```
14:33:20 (buggy) switchCamera swapped to=environment newTrack=live/enabled=false
14:41:27 (fixed) switchCamera swapped to=environment newTrack=live/enabled=true
14:41:32 (fixed) swapped to=user        ... enabled=true
14:41:34 (fixed) swapped to=environment ... enabled=true
14:41:48 (fixed) swapped to=user        ... enabled=true
```

Android's inbound across those four flips: `dec:45→120→179→246→340→426→523→587`, `B:25940→506600` — no flatline.

**Fix:** `clearBlankedPauseLatch(producer)` (local `resume()`) at all five producer sites. **GC-06 is NOT weakened** — blanking still covers the whole produce+attach window; only the stale flag is repaired. A test asserts the blanking still happens, so nobody "fixes" this later by deleting the security control.

**Separate real bug found on the way (keep the fix):** `recoverGroupCamera` double-stopped the old track — mediasoup's `replaceTrack` already stops it via `destroyTrack()` (`stopTracks` defaults true). Android logcat showed two `CameraCapturer: Stop capture` then `Camera device closed` for camera 1 **and** camera 0, i.e. the just-opened camera. Harmless on the B-20 resume path (track already ended) — only bites when the old track is LIVE. Note the contrast: `flipCamera` (1:1) replaces on a RAW `RTCRtpSender`, which does NOT stop the old track, so ITS `stop()` is required. Only the mediasoup path double-stopped — which is why 1:1 flip always worked.

**Also disproven here:** `track._switchCamera()` is a NO-OP on BOTH platforms in this fork. It is deprecated and reimplemented over `applyConstraints`, and neither controller honours a facing change (iOS `VideoCaptureController.m:161` reads only width/height/frameRate; Android `CameraCaptureController.java:126` deliberately reuses the initial facingMode). iOS exports no native `switchCamera` to JS. Do not re-chase.

### B-122 — no iOS calls when app is killed + no iOS notifications · BLOCKED (needs developer)

**Not a client bug — nothing to change in the app.** PushKit module installed, `RUNTIME_ENABLED`/`IOS_RUNTIME_ENABLED` both true, `PKPushRegistry` + `FirebaseApp.configure()` injected by `withVoipCallKit`, `GoogleService-Info.plist` BUNDLE_ID matches. The APNs key is installed **nowhere**:

| Symptom             | Pipeline                         | Missing                                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| No ring when killed | PushKit VoIP → messenger-service | `APNS_VOIP_*` env unset on staging        |
| No notifications    | FCM alert → Firebase             | APNs key not uploaded to Firebase Console |

`ensureApnsClient()` returns null → `sendVoipApns` no-ops → Android FCM unaffected, which is exactly the observed split. `push.service.ts:1228` states it outright. Already filed as IOSGV-3.

**Key verified against Apple** (not assumed): `AuthKey_B9U74KX24U.p8`, Team `88X6H88A4R` → `400 BadDeviceToken` on both hosts = valid; control ASC key `S6379ZCA56` → `403 InvalidProviderToken` = probe discriminates. **Topic NOT proven** — a wrong topic also returns `BadDeviceToken` against a dummy token; `com.bravosecure.mobile.voip` is correct by derivation only.

**Traps:** `APNS_VOIP_KEY_PATH` is the path INSIDE the container (needs the volume mount); root-only `0400` fails the read AFTER the exists-check (`ios-init-failed`, not `ios-skip`); ONE sandbox flag exists, so the server serves either the cable build (`aps-environment: development` — the Development profile OVERRIDES app.json's `production`) or TestFlight, not both.

**Stale docs to correct:** `REMAINING_TODO.md:761` and `BATCH_FIX_AND_FEATURE_PLAN.md:2610` say `APNS_VOIP_BUNDLE_ID=com.bravosecure.app`. It is now `com.bravosecure.mobile`; topic derives as `<bundleId>.voip`, so copying the documented value yields `DeviceTokenNotForTopic` and reads like a client bug.

**Handoff:** `docs/handoffs/IOS_PUSH_APNS_HANDOFF.md`. Both parts are the developer's — QA has neither Firebase Console nor staging access.

### Gates

typecheck 47 = baseline 47 · crypto suite 203 suites / 1787 tests green · new tests: `groupCallVideoEncodings` (18), `producerPauseLatch` (5, incl. a bug-reproduction case), `recoverGroupCameraStop` (5); `recoverGroupCamera.test.ts` updated — its fake producer did not stop the held track like real mediasoup, so it was green only BECAUSE of the double-stop.

**Suite flake (environmental, not code):** each full `test:crypto` run may fail ONE random unrelated suite with "Jest encountered an unexpected token" and **0 individual test failures**; it passes in isolation, and a different suite is picked each run. Tied to the Watchman TCC `Operation not permitted` on this repo path. Re-run before believing it.

### Not verified this session

1:1 call regression after the WebRTC stack swap · 3-party group call · weak-network behaviour on iOS now that simulcast is gone (the actual cost of B-121) · backgrounding mid-call.

## Session 2026-07-20 — B-124 / B-125 (Redmi Note 11, v1.0.118/vc146)

Tester reported two faults after escalating a 1:1 call with **piyaldeb** to a group call.
Investigation was code-trace only (55-agent adversarial trace + inline verification); **no
code changed**. Full write-up: `docs/audits/B124_B125_CALL_ESCALATION_CHAT_CONTAMINATION_2026-07-20.md`.

**Both are one root cause.** Escalation files a throwaway `'Call'` group key under the REAL
1:1 conversation id, and the send path decides "is this a group?" by testing whether group key
material exists at that id — a crypto question answering a conversation-type question:

```ts
// productionRuntime.ts:2351-2356
!!groupState || // ← no `type !== 'direct'` guard
  (convo?.type !== 'direct' && (convo?.participants?.length ?? 0) > 1); // ← guarded, correctly
```

### B-124 — escalated 1:1 call spawns a duplicate / junk chat thread ⚠️ HIGH

`CallScreen.tsx:1616` reuses the 1:1 conversationId as the group-call room (its own comment at
`:1610-1615` claims the opposite — stale). `ensureCallGroupKey` then aliases the `'Call'` key
onto chat-bearing slots: `productionRuntime.ts:4434` (`direct:<own userId>`) and `:4442-4443`
(the originating 1:1 id — added by **B-106 `b034b36`, 2026-07-18**, two days before the report).
Sends in that thread then stamp a **device-local** id on the wire (`:2539`), which the receiver
routes by unconditionally (`:6586`). Two artefacts: a `no_key` stash mints a junk `type:'group'`
row (`groupConversationUpsert.ts:74-84`), and `appendMessage` shadow-creates a second `direct:`
row (`messengerStore.ts:582,592,637-649`) whose `peerId` is the host's OWN id — so the dedupe at
`:594-599` misses and the home list relabels it with **piyaldeb's name**. Two rows, same title.
The `'Call'` ghost guards (`:7041`, `groupConversationUpsert.ts:73`) are NOT regressed — they are
just **device-local lookups of a cross-device id**, so they miss. Neither prune can reach the
ghost (`messengerStore.ts:1322` skips non-group; `MessengerHomeScreen.tsx:218-223` is UUID-only).

### B-125 — send throws `no other participants`, typed text destroyed ⚠️ CRITICAL (data loss)

The ghost row's only participant is the sender himself, so the self-filter empties it and
`productionRuntime.ts:2394-2397` throws. **The error text is misleading** — it blames
`/conversations/mine`, but the row is client-minted and has no server counterpart, so no sync
ever repairs it. The throw sits ~50 lines ABOVE the optimistic bubble append (`:2423-2447`),
whose own comment (`:2415-2417`) says it is hoisted "BEFORE any network/crypto await" precisely
to avoid losing text — so the composer, already cleared at `ChatScreen.tsx:652/657`, is emptied
with **no bubble and no retry chip** (`:705` needs a `failed` row). Only a banner (`:684-685`).

**Entry-point asymmetry (explains the tester's "notification only… now always"):**

| Entry               | Landing id                 | participants       | Result                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| Home tap, REAL row  | UUID / `direct:<piyaldeb>` | `[self, piyaldeb]` | sends (silently via group fan-out) |
| Notification tap    | ghost `direct:<self>`      | `[self]`           | **throws**                         |
| Home tap, GHOST row | ghost `direct:<self>`      | `[self]`           | **throws**                         |

The banner is keyed on the slot the message landed in (`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts:145,175`)
= the ghost. Once the duplicate row exists it is titled identically to the real chat, so the
tester now hits it from a normal open too — which independently corroborates B-124.

## B-126 — `messenger-crypto` suite fails a RANDOM suite ~50% of runs (pre-existing) ⚠️ P2 tooling · FOUND 2026-07-21 · NOT FIXED

**Why it matters:** this is a meta-bug. It makes "the tests pass" unreliable evidence, so a red
run gets dismissed as noise and a real regression can hide in it. It directly undermines every
change-safety gate in `CLAUDE.md`.

**Symptom:** `npm run test:crypto` fails **a different suite almost every run**, with 1–5 test
failures, then passes on re-run with no code change. Observed failing: `blockedPeersAndTombstones`,
`backupFlags`, `incomingRingtone`, `groupBroadcast`.

**Proven pre-existing.** Three consecutive runs on a **completely clean tree** (all 2026-07-21
changes stashed, new test files moved out): run 1 pass, run 2 pass, run 3 FAIL
(`incomingRingtone`). So it is not caused by the B-124/B-125 work — though adding suites may
shift its frequency.

**Diagnosis so far**

| Probe                                                      | Result                                                                | Rules out                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| The 3 suspect suites run in isolation (`--runTestsByPath`) | 23/23 PASS                                                            | the tests themselves                    |
| Full project serialized (`--runInBand`)                    | still FAILS, different suites (`groupBroadcast` + `incomingRingtone`) | worker-parallelism / cross-worker state |
| Full project, repeated                                     | random suite each time                                                | test-execution ORDER                    |

→ load/timing dependent, not order dependent. Prime suspect: **leaked timers / async teardown** —
every run also prints `A worker process has failed to exit gracefully … Active timers can also
cause this, ensure that .unref() was called on them`. In one `--runInBand` run 2 suites were
marked failed but only 1 test failed, i.e. a suite-level (teardown/timeout) failure.

**Second independent confirmation (stronger than the clean-tree one):** checked out the pre-fix
commit `cea64f8` in detached HEAD and ran the project 3× — run 1 FAILED with a _fifth_ suite,
`backgroundMessageNotifier`. So the flake predates all 2026-07-21 work.

**Best lead — the `groupBroadcast` failure is a RATCHET-STATE failure, not a timing one.** It
fails on `parseGroupMessage rejects when inner envelope and outer group hint diverge` with
`DecryptError: decrypt failed` → `Cause: Bad MAC` from
`node_modules/@privacyresearch/libsignal-protocol-typescript/lib/internal/crypto.js:154`, raised
via `packages/messenger-core/src/crypto/sessionManager.ts:136`. The same file passes **30/30 in
isolation**. A `Bad MAC` on a live Signal session means the Double Ratchet advanced more (or
fewer) times than the decrypt side expected — i.e. **session/ratchet state is leaking between
suites**, most likely a module-level in-memory session store that is not reset per suite. That
is a much more specific cause than "timers", and it may be the whole bug: several of the other
random victims also stand up libsignal sessions.

**Next steps:** (1) `npx jest --selectProjects messenger-crypto --detectOpenHandles` on the
suspect suites; (2) audit the shared libsignal/session test fixtures for module-level state that
survives `jest.resetModules()` — a store created at import time rather than in `beforeEach` would
produce exactly this.

⚠️ **The tool that exists to catch exactly this is dead:** `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml`
runs the suites 5× nightly, and GitHub Actions has been **billing-dead since ~2026-07-10**.

**Working rule until fixed:** a single red `test:crypto` run is NOT evidence of a regression.
Re-run, and confirm the specific suite in isolation before believing it.

## B-124 FIX round 3 — 2026-07-21 · receiver-side containment (items 2 + 3 REDESIGNED)

The owner authorised §9 items 2 and 3 (the architecture stop-conditions). A 6-agent adversarial
design review **rejected both as specified** and produced a smaller fix that needs **no wire change,
no `GroupState` change, and no architecture permission at all**. Shipped that instead.

### Why the original items 2 + 3 were NOT built

| Item                                                          | Verdict                         | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **3a** — sender stops stamping a device-local `group.groupId` | **WOULD DESTROY EVERY MESSAGE** | The body is group-encrypted at `productionRuntime.ts:2494-2496` **before** the stamp at `:2555`, and `:2563-2564` bind `aad.conversationId`/`aad.groupId` to the same id. Suppressing only the stamp leaves `aad.conversationId = direct:<peer>` against an expected `direct:<lo>\|<hi>` (`:6464-6465`, `directConvoAadId :7948-7951`) → `conversation_mismatch` → `:6475-6526` notes the envelope destroyed, inserts a placeholder and **returns clean, committing the txn and acking**. Envelope gone. 4 of 5 reviewers found this independently.                                                               |
| **3a "fixed" by patching the AAD**                            | worse                           | Receiver then takes the 1:1 path at `:6640` and renders `unwrapped.body` verbatim — the user sees raw AES-GCM ciphertext JSON as a chat bubble, persisted to SQLCipher and mirrored to backup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **2** — add `isCallGroup` to `GroupState`                     | **no-op**                       | The failing sentinel (`groupConversationUpsert.ts:73`) fails because there is **no local state at the stamped id** — reached only _because_ `store.groups[wireId]` was already undefined at `:6642`. `undefined?.isCallGroup` is undefined for the same reason `undefined?.name` is. The two sentinels that ARE cross-device effective (`:7033`, `:7057`) already read the wire `name`. Net coverage gained: zero.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **2** (security)                                              | **net downgrade**               | `canonicalCreateBytes` (`groupClient.ts:998-1009`) signs only `groupId`, sorted members, `masterKeyB64`, `epoch` — so neither `name` nor a new flag is signed. Keeping the legacy fallback makes the predicate `isCallGroup \|\| name === 'Call'`, a **superset** attacker lever whose new half is invisible to the user and matched by **neither** boot sweep (`messengerStore.ts:1331`, `:1385`). Injected on the G-05 relayed-create path it suppresses a real group's inbox row and files its master key at `direct:<owner>` with the genuine name intact — a permanently invisible thread with no heal path. |

### ⚠️ The round-2 boot sweep was making B-124 WORSE

`pruneCallKeyContamination` (shipped 2026-07-21, commit `5a97038`) deletes every `direct:`-shaped
`'Call'` alias at each rehydrate. `groupConversationUpsert.ts:73` then dereferences that
just-deleted state, reads `undefined`, and falls through — **minting the exact B-124 §3.1 ghost
thread on every boot**, for as long as any peer stays on v1.0.118. This is the decisive reason
receive-side work was genuinely required; "items 1/4/5/6 already made this safe" was NOT the honest
answer. Pinned by a test that reproduces the sequence (alias present → sweep clears it → peer's
envelope arrives).

### What shipped

1. **`isDeviceLocalGroupId(id)`** — new exported pure predicate in `messagingLogic.ts` (jest-importable;
   `productionRuntime.ts` is not). A real group id is a 32-hex `deriveGroupId` output or a server
   UUID; nothing legitimate is `direct:`-prefixed. Consumers **import** it — never re-inline.
2. **Unconditional shape guard in `upsertKeylessGroupPlaceholder`** (`groupConversationUpsert.ts`),
   placed **above** the `store.groups[groupId]?.name === 'Call'` check. It deliberately does **not**
   consult the groups map, which is what makes it immune to the boot sweep above. This is the actual
   ghost-row minter (reached from `productionRuntime.ts:6696`, `:6782`) and the guard works against
   the entire un-updated fleet because the row is minted on **our** device by **their** stamp.
3. **Residual B-125 send hole closed** in `isGroupConversation`: a `direct:`-shaped conversationId is
   never a group **regardless of whether a row exists**. Round 1's `type !== 'direct'` veto was
   vacuously true when no row existed yet (cold contact, notification tap), so a stray call-key still
   won. This also makes item 3a unnecessary _by construction_ — the group branch can no longer be
   entered with a direct-shaped id, so the half-state 3a would have created cannot arise.

**Tests** — 9 new, all **mutation-proved**: with the two production files stashed and the tests kept,
exactly 9 fail. Includes an explicit **regression** case that a genuine keyless group placeholder
(32-hex, no local state) is STILL created — the whole reason the function exists.
Gates: `tsc` **47 = baseline** · eslint 0 errors · `messenger-crypto` **1,815/1,815 green**.

### Deliberately NOT done (per the review)

- No `isCallGroup` field; nothing added to `canonicalCreateBytes` or `canonicalActionBytes` (either

- No `'BRAVO_GROUP_CREATE_V2'`: there is no signed version field to select on, so a verifier must try
  V2-then-V1 and an attacker just omits the field to force the V1 fallback. Zero binding.
- `name: 'Call'` at `:4425` **unchanged** — eight sentinels across the installed fleet depend on that
  literal, including restore paths that carry no `GroupState` at all.
- Aliases (`:4450`, `:4459`, `:7035`) **kept**; no separate `callKeys` namespace.
- The shape check is **NOT** applied at `:6464` (AAD expectation), `:6642` (key lookup), `:7026`
  (create install) or `:7205` (membership gate). The ad-hoc call key legitimately travels as a create
  whose `state.groupId` IS a device-local alias (the BS-CALL-KEY-RESYNC broadcast at `:4355-4390`);
  rejecting it → joiner times out at the 25s key gate → **"Call failed" on every re-escalation**.

### Still open (follow-ups, not folded in)

- **STEP 3** — apply the predicate at the two `insertDecryptFailurePlaceholder` sites (`:6517`, `:6736`).
- **STEP 4** — routing-only adoption veto at `:6601-6602` (verified AAD-safe; `verifySealedAad` runs

- **STEP 6** — the resync broadcast at `:4362` ships the alias state; re-deriving the canonical id

- **UUID-shaped aliases.** `:4458`'s `|| convType === 'direct'` disjunct files the alias onto

- **Correction to the record:** `verifyGroupIdDerivation` is **NOT** a backstop on the live receive

## B-127 — any authenticated user can hijack another user's group (ungated `create` install) 🔴 P0 SECURITY · FIXED `66f8546`

Surfaced by the B-124 items-2/3 design review and verified at line level. **Not** what B-124/B-125
are; deliberately not folded into that fix.

`productionRuntime.ts:7026` performs `store.setGroupState(action.state)` using an **attacker-chosen
`groupId`**, with:

- **no id-derivation check** — `verifyGroupIdDerivation` is unreachable here (create is handled
  inline; `applyAdminAction` at `:7074` never sees a create);
- **no owner-continuity check** — nothing asserts the incoming `owner` matches the group's existing owner;
- **an epoch guard that only rejects `epoch < existing.epoch`** (`:6971`).

So any authenticated user can ship a **self-signed** create naming a victim's real `groupId` at
`epoch: 999` and overwrite that group's `owner`, roster and `masterKeyB64` on every recipient. The
`creatorSignature` verifies fine — it is signed by the attacker, over the attacker's own state.

**Impact:** group takeover — attacker becomes owner, can rekey, add/remove members, and every member
encrypts subsequent messages under the attacker's master key.

⚠️ Touches group master-key distribution → **architecture stop-condition**. Needs its own review;
the likely shape is an owner-continuity gate plus mandatory id-derivation on create.

## B-128 — group reactions bypass the membership gate and their AAD binds nothing ⚠️ P1 SECURITY · PART 1 FIXED `<B-128 commit>` · PART 2 ARCH-GATED

1. ✅ **FIXED.** `productionRuntime.ts:6625` called `applyReaction` with the **raw wire `groupId`**
   behind only an `isPeerBlocked` check — no membership gate, unlike the P1-N4 gate the group TEXT
   lane has had all along. Any authenticated user who knew a groupId could place reactions into a
   group they had never been a member of, and a removed member kept working reactions forever.

   Easy to miss for a structural reason worth recording: a reaction is a **1:1-pairwise-encrypted
   control envelope with a group routing hint** (MSG-02), not a master-key-encrypted message.
   Possession of the group key gates the text lane implicitly, so that lane looks safe without an
   explicit check — and the reaction lane, which gets none of that protection, looks the same.

   Fixed by mirroring the text lane's gate, including its `existing &&` fail-open (with no local
   group state we cannot judge membership, and dropping there would discard legitimate reactions for
   a group not yet synced). The drop calls `noteDestroyedEnvelope` so the sender is acked
   `discarded` rather than a false ✓✓ — the correction W11 made for the group-text non-member drop.
   Bumped the M10 exit census 25 → 26 deliberately, per that ratchet's own rule.

   Pinned by `groupReactionMembershipGate.test.ts` (5 cases, RED-first). Mutation-proved twice: the
   gate reading the WIRE's membership instead of ours (the circular check), and a silent drop.

2. ⛔ **NOT FIXED — architecture-gated.** `:3331` gives reaction envelopes an AAD of only
   `{to, ts}`, so `verifySealedAad`'s conversation and group checks are **inert** for reactions.
   Changing the AAD shape is a CLAUDE.md stop-condition ("sealed-sender envelope shape … or AAD
   binding") and needs sign-off before anyone touches it.

   **The part-1 gate is defence in depth, not a substitute.** It is enforced by the RECEIVER's group
   state, so it stops the practical attack (a stranger reacting into your group). It does not make
   the envelope cryptographically bound to the group — a reaction sealed for conversation A still
   carries nothing that prevents it being replayed toward conversation B. Only the AAD binding fixes
   that. Do not close this item on the strength of part 1.

## B-130 — a burst of 4-6 messages silently stops the receiver until restart 🔴 P0 · FOUND 2026-07-21 · **FIXED**

**Reported:** "If someone sends 4–6 messages very quickly, the receiving phone can only process the
first 1–2. Then the app gets stuck while saving one message to its database. Because it is stuck, all
the messages behind it also stop. The app doesn't crash or show an error — it just stops receiving.
The remaining messages stay on the server and are not delivered until the app is restarted."

**Root cause — an AB-BA lock-order inversion between the only two write mutexes on the single
SQLCipher connection.**

|       | Lock                                                       | Where                           |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **A** | `txnChain` — global, one open txn at a time                | `runtime/receiveTransaction.ts` |
| **B** | `chains` — per-conversation write ordering (audit fix #18) | `store/sqlMessageStore.ts`      |

```
RECEIVE            took A then B:  runWithRatchetTxn(...)            <- holds A
                                     -> doHandleIncoming
                                       -> await sqlMessages.upsert() -> chainOp   <- waits B

COALESCED FLUSH    took B then A:  setTimeout(50ms)
                                     -> chainOp(cid, ...)            <- claims B synchronously
                                       -> upsertBatch -> runWithRatchetTxn        <- waits A
```

Circular wait. **Nothing throws**, so the receive txn's `await work()` never settles: `COMMIT` never
runs, `ROLLBACK` never runs, and the `finally` that clears the open-txn flag never runs. `txnChain` is
dead for the process lifetime, every later receive parks behind it, and since the relay ack happens
strictly _after_ the receive resolves, the envelopes are never acked and sit on the relay for its
30-day dwell. `inFlightEnvelopes` is never cleared either, so even a foreground re-drain delivers
nothing — **only a restart clears it.** That accounts for every reported signal.

**Why a burst.** Frames dispatch fire-and-forget with no concurrency cap, so N envelopes keep lock A
continuously busy — which is what lets a 50 ms timer land _inside_ an open transaction. With 1–2
messages A is idle in between and the flush commits harmlessly. Hence "the first 1–2 arrive".

**What actually arms the timer** (the initial hypothesis got this wrong, and it matters for repro):
**not** `appendMessage`. A new inbound row takes the write-through subscriber's INSERT branch →
`store.upsert()`, which touches lock B only and cannot invert. The coalesce timer is armed **only** by
an UPDATE to an _existing_ row — dominantly `markRead` flipping `delivered → read`, which is gated on
the chat being open and the app foregrounded. **So the repro needs the chat open**, and a burst faster
than ChatScreen's 200 ms debounce may never arm it at all.

**Family:** the fourth bug of this class — audit P0-1 (2026-07-09, nested BEGIN → ack `discarded` →
silent message destruction), B-72, B-75. The 2026-07-09 fix _created_ this one: it funnelled the flush
into `runWithRatchetTxn` to stop the nested BEGIN, but left the outer `chainOp` wrapping it, which is
precisely the B→A edge.

**Fix:** the flush keeps lock B and no longer reaches for lock A — it writes rows raw via a new
`writeRows()` helper instead of `upsertBatch()`. `upsertBatch()` is untouched for the restore path.
That was the **only** B→A edge in the codebase, so the wait-for graph is now single-direction (A→B)
and the cycle is structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

**Rejected** (each would have traded one bug for another):

- _Drop `chainOp` from the flush._ Breaks audit fix #18 — `remove()` is raw autocommit on B and never
  touches A, so a batch delayed behind a receive backlog would land after a later DELETE and
  `INSERT OR REPLACE` cleared/retracted messages back into existence.
- _Guard on `isInsideRatchetTxn()`._ Incomplete (the flag is set _after_ the `BEGIN` await, so a flush
  firing in that window still queues on A) and unsound (it would strip restore page writes of their
  atomicity).
- _Make the receive path's upsert raw instead._ Breaks the cycle from the wrong side: it drops the
  inbound INSERT out of per-conversation ordering, so a retract/expiry DELETE could execute before the
  in-flight INSERT and a **retracted message would resurrect permanently**.

**Regression:** `src/modules/messenger/__tests__/receiveBurstDeadlock.test.ts` — 5 cases,
**two-way mutation-proved**: with the fix line reverted exactly the 3 deadlock cases fail
(`Expected "committed", Received "DEADLOCK"`; the 6-burst reports `["m1","m2"]`) while both controls
still pass, so the tests discriminate rather than merely failing. Includes an ORDERING GUARD that goes
red if anyone later "simplifies" by deleting `chainOp`, and a disjoint-conversation control.

**Still open, same family, different pair:** a second latent cycle between `txnChain` and
`SessionManager`'s per-address locks (receive takes A→C via `own.decrypt`; X3DH takes C→A via
`initOutgoingSession → saveIdentity`). Defused opportunistically by the open-txn flag, but that flag is
set after the `BEGIN` await. It does **not** fire on this profile (an established 1:1 session
short-circuits before `processPreKey`), so it is a separate ticket — but if a device still stalls after
this fix, look there.

**Device confirmation owed:** two instances, release build, receiver with the thread **open and
foregrounded**, sender 6 messages at ~400–600 ms spacing (deliberately above the 200 ms markRead
debounce). Pre-fix: first 1–2 render, then silence with no ACK log and no error; backgrounding must
NOT recover it. Post-fix: all 6 render and ack.

## B-131 — ops-channel read receipts blue-ticked on ONE member's read ⚠️ P2 · FIXED `a0b84de`

`recordReadReceipts` re-derived message topology with its own copy of the rule,
`convo?.type === 'group'`, which omits `ops_channel`. So `required` fell through to null and
the DIRECT rule applied — "the single peer's receipt is sufficient" — and one member reading
flipped the message to `read` for everybody. Exactly the bug B-116 was written to kill, still
live on ops channels only.

Invisible because the two rules disagree and only one was tested: the send path and
`readReceiptAccepted` both use `messagingLogic.isGroupConversation` (which has always counted
`ops_channel` as a group), while the store re-derived it. The existing suite only ever
exercised `type: 'group'` and `direct:` — never the one type where the copies diverge.

---

## B-132 — a late-arriving message produced NO notification at all ⚠️ P1 · FIXED `365cb9a`

The notifier tracked ONE id per conversation: the id at the TAIL of the list. But
`appendMessage` binary-splices an out-of-order row into SEND order rather than pushing it, so a
message stashed while offline and drained later lands MID-list and leaves the tail unchanged.
The watermark matched, the handler continued, and the user got no banner and no badge — for
exactly the messages most likely to need one, since they arrived late BECAUSE the device had
been offline.

Fixed by tracking a bounded per-conversation id set instead of the tail id.

---

## B-133 — ops-console could print decrypted plaintext to the console 🔴 SECURITY · FIXED `b75a307`

`groupDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` shared one `try`, and the catch logged `(e as Error).message`.
If the DECRYPT succeeds and the PARSE then fails, V8 embeds a slice of the offending string in
the SyntaxError message — and that string is decrypted group plaintext. Any malformed inner
payload therefore printed message content to the ops-console browser console.

Violates the CLAUDE.md rule "never log plaintext message bodies". It survived because the
log-audit test did not scan `apps/ops-console` (its roots were `src/modules/messenger` and
`apps/messenger-service/src` only — a gap narrowed in `7884c8b` by adding
`packages/messenger-core`). **Scanner gap CLOSED `b0505a3`** — it now covers all five roots
(`src/modules/messenger`, `apps/messenger-service/src`, `packages/messenger-core/src`,
`apps/ops-console/src`, `apps/auth-service/src`). That took rewording four log STRINGS whose
banned word sat in the message text rather than in a logged value ("dropping before decrypt",
"decrypt failed", "group decrypt failed", "Signed prekey signature check unavailable"); the ban
list itself was left untouched, since every keyword removed from it is a class of leak that
stops being detectable. Mutation-proved: injecting `{plaintext: 'x'}` onto an ops-console log
line — the exact shape of this bug — turns the new root red.

Still true, and unchanged by the widening: the scan is line-based regex, so a log call split
across lines can still hide a banned identifier on a later line.

---

## B-134 — a missed call manufactured a junk chat row ⚠️ P3 · FIXED `f06cbb5`

`appendMessage` shadow-creates a `direct:` conversation row for any inbound message whose slot
does not exist. That gate keys off `sender_id !== 'self'` — inbound-NESS, not INTENT — so a
missed call from a cold contact silently created a `Bravo · xxxxxxxx` thread. The group branch
has had a sentinel against this since B-106; the direct branch never did. Same junk-row class
the tester reported in B-124.

The row itself is wanted (the call bubble needs somewhere to land). What was wrong is that
nothing DECLARED it. The dispatcher now mints it explicitly through a shared
`directPlaceholderConversation()` that the store's shadow-create also uses.

**Trap found en route — NOW FIXED (`13db462`):** the `Bravo · ` prefix is load-bearing —
`useRegisteredNames` backfills only that prefix, so MainNavigator's hand-rolled
`userId.slice(0, 8)` label created rows whose name was NEVER backfilled: contact discovery
would learn the person's real name and never apply it. All three cold-contact minting sites
(dispatcher, MainNavigator, store shadow-create) now go through
`directPlaceholderConversation`, pinned by a scan asserting none hand-rolls the label.

## B-135 — an inbound reaction was acked before it was persisted ⚠️ P2 · FIXED `d5044f2`

`applyReaction` returned void: it mutated the Zustand row and stopped there, so the reaction
reached SQLCipher only through the write-through subscriber's 50 ms coalesced flush — AFTER the
receive txn committed and AFTER the envelope was acked off the relay. The sender saw ✓✓ for a
reaction this device had not durably stored, and a crash in that window lost it with no
redelivery possible.

## B-136 — a removed group member got a false ✓✓ on every message ⚠️ P2 · FIXED `0ac3588`

The sealed group-text non-member drop returned bare. Inside `doHandleIncoming` a bare `return`
COMMITs and acks `'delivered'`, so a peer removed from a group saw ✓✓ on messages that were
being discarded on arrival. The semantically identical LEGACY plaintext non-member drop already
called `noteDestroyedEnvelope`, so the two paths reported OPPOSITE things to the sender for the
same situation.

---

## B-137 — a keys-service blip PERMANENTLY destroyed a group-key envelope 🔴 P1 · FIXED `0ac3588`

The relayed group-create path resolves the OWNER's identity key to verify the signature, and
its catch swallowed EVERY failure into `undefined`, falling into a bare `return` — which
COMMITs and acks. A momentary keys-service failure or a second offline therefore destroyed an
OWNER-SIGNED group-key create: precisely the envelope a keyless member is waiting for, and one
that is not resent. The WS path already treated the same condition as recoverable.

Fixed by distinguishing transient (keys client present, lookup threw ⇒ `LeaveOnRelayError`)
from permanent (no keys client at all ⇒ drop, since no retry can help).

---

## B-138 — duplicate messages came back on EVERY restart ⚠️ P2 · FIXED `11d572c` + `ed76b66`

Two halves of one divergence between memory and disk.

**Write side** — every inbound lane did `appendMessage(msg)` then `sqlMessages.upsert(msg)`,
persisting the object it HANDED the store rather than the one the store committed.
`appendMessage` forks the id on a content-divergent collision (`X` → `X#n`, and the id is
SENDER-supplied), so memory held `X#n` while disk held `X`. It also returns null when it
DEDUPED — and the upsert ran anyway, writing a row the store had deliberately dropped.

**Read side** — `hydrateMessages` matched on `id` only, not `envelope_id`. So a row that
reached disk under a different local id but the same envelope was re-imported at every boot as
a SECOND bubble, and no amount of live dedup could clear it: the live gate dropped it, and the
next restart recreated it.

---

## B-139 — a two-minute clock error destroyed the message permanently 🔴 P1 · FIXED `9a262a1` + `4b9cd97`

Two independent clock windows, same failure.

**Sender cert** — `verifySenderCert` allows ±120s of skew and then throws. Every cert throw was
treated as terminal and acked `discarded`, which DELETES the envelope off the relay. A device
whose clock was briefly out lost the message forever, with nothing in the log. The failure said
nothing about whether the sender was genuine — only that the clock disagreed.

**Sealed AAD** — a `future` timestamp took a clean `return`, which COMMITs and acks. Its own
comment conceded it ("this clean return COMMITS the txn ... so the message is DESTROYED"). The
only person told was the RECEIVER, via a banner asking them to "resend" a message the SENDER
had no idea failed.

Both now leave the envelope on the relay. Deliberately narrow: only the two clock-window cert
errors and only AAD `future`. Malformed / wrong-issuer / bad-signature / revoked stay terminal,
and AAD `stale` (>30d, expired or replayed) still drops — otherwise a forged or dead envelope
would be retried for the relay's full 30-day dwell.

---

## B-140 — second AB-BA lock inversion, same class as B-130 🔴 P1 · FIXED `450d3b5`

B-130 was pair 1. Pair 2 sat in the SEND path the whole time:

```
receive: txn chain -> session lock   (runWithRatchetTxn -> own.decrypt)
send:    session lock -> txn chain   (initOutgoingSession -> processPreKey -> saveIdentity)
```

Both orders alive at once is a cycle, and it fails exactly the way B-130 did — nothing throws,
the transaction never settles, the chain is dead for the process lifetime, and the user simply
stops receiving until restart.

Fixed by taking the global chain FIRST via `runOnTxnChain`, with the bundle fetch deliberately
left OUTSIDE (holding the chain across a network round-trip would block every receive — trading
a deadlock for a stall).

**Retires the last known instance of the family behind P0-1 (2026-07-09), B-72, B-75 and B-130.**

---

## B-141 — blocking a peer did not stop their already-stashed group message ⚠️ P2 PRIVACY · FIXED `<W8b>`

A group envelope that arrives before its master key is stashed in `pending_group_envelopes` and
replayed later by `replayGroupSealedDecode` once the key lands. That replay is a **third**
implementation of "may this message render" — alongside the WS and HTTP paths — and it only ever
grew the membership gate (P1-N4). It was missing all three of the live path's other drops:

| Gate                  | Live path | Stash replay (before) |
| --------------------- | --------- | --------------------- |
| membership (P1-N4)    | ✅        | ✅                    |
| expiry (M7)           | `:6478`   | ❌                    |
| `isRestoreTombstoned` | `:7223`   | ❌                    |
| `isPeerBlocked`       | `:7231`   | ❌                    |

**User-visible effect.** Block a peer whose group message is sitting in the stash, and the next
key arrival drains it straight onto the screen. The block appears to work everywhere else — the
live path has suppressed blocked senders since P2-9 — so the leak shows up only in the one case
the user is least likely to expect: an old message from the person they just blocked.

The **expiry** hole is the one most likely to fire in ordinary use, and the stash makes it _more_
likely rather than less: an envelope is only stashed because a key was missing, so by definition
it waits an unbounded time before draining. A 5-minute disappearing message stashed for an hour
is long dead by the time anyone sees it — and it rendered anyway.

**Fixed** by adding all three drops, each a plain `return`. That detail is load-bearing:
`drainPendingGroup` deletes the stash row only on a clean return, whereas a `throw` is caught,
bumps `attempts`, and replays the whole decode `PENDING_GROUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` times — re-parsing the
group payload each pass — before deleting the row anyway.

Two things verified rather than assumed, either of which would have made the fix wrong:

- **Dropping before the txn skips its `markSeen`.** Safe: `markSeen` already ran unconditionally
  at `:6334` when the envelope was first received and stashed (stash row + seen row + relay ack
  commit atomically), so the in-txn call is only defensive. Had it not, these drops would have
  made the relay re-push the envelope forever.
- **Both gate caches fail open** — a failed load leaves an empty set, so the gates silently answer
  "no". If the boot stash drain (B-31) ran before `loadBlockedPeers`/`loadRestoreTombstones`, the
  new gates would no-op on exactly the path that matters most. The loads are awaited at `:444-445`
  and the boot drain starts at `:~1735`; that ordering is now pinned by a test.

Pinned by `stashDrainGateParity.test.ts` (10 cases). Written test-first and observed RED (7 of 9
failed; the 2 passing were controls). Mutation-proved twice: `throw` instead of `return`, and the
gate moved below the txn.

**Class note:** this is the same shape as B-124 and the M5 divergences — one behaviour, several
hand-copied implementations, and the copy nobody looks at drifts. The stash replay was the third
copy of the receive gates. See `docs/runbooks/MESSAGE_LOOP.md` M15.

---

## B-142 — the live group-stash drain swallowed every failure silently ⚠️ P2 · FIXED `<W25>`

`drainPendingGroup` is fire-and-forget (`void drainPendingGroup(...)`) from two call sites. The
BOOT one at `:1748` attached a `.catch`; the LIVE one at `:5884` did not.

A `void`ed promise that rejects is an **unhandled rejection**: no log, no crashLog breadcrumb,
nothing. And it was missing on the path that fires after **every admin create/rekey** — i.e. the
common one, not the edge case. If the drain threw (SQLCipher blip, malformed stash row, a bug in
the replay), stashed group envelopes simply never appeared and there was no diagnostic tying the
silence to a cause. The boot path, which runs once, had the handler; the path that runs constantly
did not.

Fixed by mirroring the boot handler exactly.

**Also added (same work item): an in-flight guard keyed by `groupId`.** A burst of admin commits
for one group — create then rekey, or several adds — fires one drain per commit, and they
interleave over the SAME stash rows: every pass re-parses the same envelopes under the group master
key and all but one loses the `delete` race. The txn chain serialises the writes, so this was
wasted CPU rather than corruption, but on a large stash it is a lot of wasted crypto.

Two deliberate shape choices, both pinned by tests:

- **The guard lives INSIDE `drainPendingGroup`, not at the two call sites.** Both callers are
  fire-and-forget, so a call-site guard means writing it twice and the second copy drifting — the
  exact failure mode behind B-124, B-128 and B-141 in this same file.
- **The release is in a `finally`, never after the `await`.** A throw between `add()` and
  `delete()` would wedge that groupId permanently: no stashed envelope for it would ever drain
  again for the life of the process. That is strictly worse than the duplicate work the guard
  prevents.

Pinned by `drainPendingGroupGuards.test.ts` (5 cases). Mutation-proved twice: removing the live
`.catch` (the original bug) and moving the release out of the `finally`.

---

## B-124 ROUND 4 — duplicate chat STILL appears on the caller's device after escalation ⚠️ HIGH · FIELD-REPORTED · FIXED 2026-07-22

**Report:** "in a 1:1 audio call, when I switch to a group call, the person who created the call —
that person's chat becomes duplicate." Reproduced from the code: this is B-124 **§3.2**, the
duplicate on the **HOST's own device**, which earlier rounds did not actually prevent.

**Why the earlier rounds missed it.** Round 3 closed §3.1 — the GROUP-typed junk thread — with an
unconditional shape guard in `upsertKeylessGroupPlaceholder`. §3.2 is a different minter: the
**DIRECT**-typed row created by `appendMessage`'s shadow-create. For that, round 3 shipped only
`pruneCallKeyContamination`, a **boot sweep**. A sweep removes the row at next launch; nothing
stopped it being re-minted the moment another message arrived, so the user sees it reappear within
the same session. A cleanup is not a fix.

**Chain (host's device):** escalation files a throwaway `'Call'` key under `direct:<hostUserId>` →
the peer stamps that **device-local** id as `group.groupId` on the wire → on the host's device that
string names the **host himself** → the host holds a key there, so it decrypts, appends, and
`appendMessage` shadow-creates a row whose only participant is the host → the home list relabels the
`Bravo · <hex>` placeholder with the **peer's** name ⇒ two identically-titled chats.

**Fix — two independent layers.** Either alone stops it; both shipped because round 3 proved one
layer plus a sweep is not enough.

1. **Receive routing (the root).** `productionRuntime` adopted `unwrapped.group.groupId` verbatim.
   It now refuses a device-local id and falls back to `resolveDirectConversationIdFromState`, so the
   message lands in the REAL 1:1 and no ghost id ever reaches the store. This is the deferred
   "STEP 4" from the items-2/3 review, which verified it is **AAD-safe**: `verifySealedAad` runs
   above and derives both expected values from the same wire id, so rewriting the routing variable
   below it cannot cause `conversation_mismatch`. Group **key lookup still uses the wire id** — the
   key really does live there; only the ROW moves.
2. **Store guard (defence in depth).** `appendMessage`'s direct shadow-create now refuses
   `direct:<_ownUserId>`. You have no 1:1 with yourself, so such a slot is never a real chat.

**Regression tests** — `callEscalationDuplicateChat.test.ts`, 10 cases, **mutation-proved**: with
both production files stashed and the tests kept, exactly **4 fail** (2 per layer). The other 6 pass
either way _by design_ — they are the narrowness guards: a normal cold-contact `direct:<peer>` row
must STILL be shadow-created, own outbound messages must never create anything, and the shape
predicate must not classify a derived group id or a mission-room server UUID as device-local.

Gates: tsc 47 = baseline · eslint 0 errors · messenger-crypto no new failures.
**Not device-verified** — needs the reporter's repro: 1:1 audio call → add a third person → check the
caller's chat list for a twin, then relaunch and check again.

---

## B-130 — answering from a notification stalls on "Answering…" with no audio ⚠️ HIGH · FIELD-REPORTED · FIXED 2026-07-22

**Report:** "someone calls me, I get the call notification, I tap it and enter the app and receive
the call — I can't hear that person, the call is stuck in Answering."

**Root cause: two timers that contradicted each other.** Not a WebRTC or TURN fault.

| Timer                                          | Value   | Armed when                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CALL_SETUP_SEND_BUDGET_MS` (signallingClient) | **40s** | how long `call.answer` keeps retrying across a WS reconnect                       |
| `CONNECTING_WATCHDOG_MS` (callController)      | **20s** | armed by `setState('connecting')` **immediately**, before the answer is delivered |

Answering from a notification tap is precisely the cold-start case — the app is resuming and the
WebSocket is often still coming up. `sendAnswer` correctly waits and retries for up to 40s, but the
connecting watchdog started its 20s clock the moment we entered `connecting`. At 20s it killed a
call whose answer was **still being legitimately retried**. The caller never received an answer, no
media path was ever negotiated, so there was no audio — and the callee sat behind an "Answering…"
label the whole time.

`waitOpenThenSend`'s own comment already described the failure and nobody joined it up:
_"a dropped `call.answer` wedges the callee until the 20s connecting watchdog."_

**Second defect, same block.** When delivery failed, `callController` did:

```ts
.then(ok => { if (!ok) {return;} ... })
```

A silent `return`. Nothing retried, nothing surfaced it, nothing drove the call to a terminal state —
so the only thing that ever ended it was the watchdog it could not influence.

**Fix (both halves).**

1. `armConnectingWatchdog(budgetMs?)` now takes an override, and the answer path arms
   `ANSWER_DELIVERY_WATCHDOG_MS` (50s > the 40s send budget) for the delivery window. The NA-05
   re-arm then restarts the **short** 20s clock the moment the frame actually reaches the socket, so
   a genuinely stuck ICE negotiation is still caught in 20s. The long budget applies **only** while
   delivery is pending.
2. A failed delivery now calls `hangup('failed')` with a log, guarded on callId + state so a late
   resolution cannot tear down a different call. Every teardown path runs and the caller stops
   ringing, instead of both sides waiting on an answer that will never arrive.

**Regression tests** — `answerDeliveryStall.test.ts`, 8 cases, **mutation-proved**: with
`callController.ts` stashed and the tests kept, **5 fail**. The behavioural half reads the real
exported constants and asserts the ordering (`ANSWER_DELIVERY > send budget > CONNECTING`), so the
inversion cannot be reintroduced by editing a number. It also pins that
`CONNECTING_WATCHDOG_MS` stays ≤ 20s — widening _that_ would trade this bug for calls that hang.

Gates: tsc 47 = baseline · eslint 0 errors · no new suite failures.
**Not device-verified** — needs the reporter's repro: have someone call you, background/lock the
phone, tap the call notification, answer, and confirm two-way audio.

---

## B-131 — conversation list shows a DOUBLE tick while the chat shows a SINGLE tick ⚠️ MEDIUM · FIELD-REPORTED · FIXED 2026-07-22

**Report:** "when I send a message and the person hasn't read it, the chat shows a single tick — but
when I go back to the list of people, that row shows a double tick."

**Two defects, and the fix needs both.**

**1. The list was reading the wrong field entirely.** `MessengerHomeScreen` rendered its tick from:

```tsx
read={c.unread_count === 0}
…
read && <Icon name="check-all" … />   // always the DOUBLE tick
```

`unread_count` is _how many messages **I** have not read_. It says **nothing** about whether the peer
received or read **my** message. So any conversation with a cleared badge drew a blue double tick —
permanently, for every chat, regardless of delivery state. It never consulted the message status at
all. Meanwhile `ChatScreen.statusToIcon` mapped the real 6-state `status` correctly, so the two
surfaces contradicted each other for the same message.

This is the "one rule, many copies" class again: two independent implementations of the same
user-visible rule, each looking correct in isolation.

**2. Pointing the list at `last_message.status` alone would NOT have fixed it.** `last_message` is a
SNAPSHOT taken at append time, and `updateMessageStatus` only mutated `s.messages[cid]` — it never
advanced the conversation row's copy. Verified with a RED test: after
`updateMessageStatus(cid, id, 'read')`, `last_message.status` was still `'sent'`. A naive fix would
have frozen the list at a single tick forever — the same bug pointing the other way.

**Fix.**

- New `runtime/messageTicks.ts` exports `outgoingTick(msg) → TickKind`
  (`none | pending | single | double | double-read | failed`). Pure and presentation-free: it returns
  a SEMANTIC tick, not an icon or colour, so each surface keeps its own visual mapping (the bubble
  uses muted/glow brand tokens; the list row is smaller and single-coloured) while neither owns the
  RULE. Incoming last messages return `none` — drawing a tick for the peer's own message was half the
  reported bug.
- `ChatScreen.statusToIcon` now delegates to it; `MessengerHomeScreen` uses it via a new `ConvTick`.
  The `read` prop survives but is now only what it always meant — muted preview text.
- `syncLastMessageStatus` keeps `conversations[cid].last_message.status` in step, wired into
  `updateMessageStatus`, `updateMessageStatusBulk` and `recordReadReceipts` (the last is what drives
  the blue tick). Guarded on `last.id === messageId`, so a receipt for an OLDER message cannot
  rewrite the newest row's tick, and on `isStatusRegression` so a late frame cannot walk it backwards.

**Regression tests** — `conversationListTicks.test.ts`, 9 cases, real-import, **mutation-proved**:
with the store + list changes stashed and the tests kept, the staleness case fails. Covers each
status, the incoming-message case, the absent-message case, and explicitly that a status update to an
older message does not move the newest row's tick.

Gates: tsc 47 = baseline · eslint 0 errors · messenger-crypto no new failures · the 5 `app` failures
(`authStore.recheckMembership`, `uploadAvatar`, `GroupCallScreen.autopop`) are all pre-existing,
verified by stashing.
**Not device-verified** — send a message, leave it unread, and compare the chat bubble with the list row.

## B-143 — group "undeliverable" receipt is dropped for every member but the first ⚠️ P2 · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`applyEnvelopeDelivered` (envelopeDelivered.ts) matches the scalar `envelope_id` OR any per-recipient
`envelope_ids` map leg (SYNC-1). Its sibling `applyEnvelopeUndeliverable`
(decryptFailureSignal.ts, `msg.envelope_id !== envelopeId → continue`) matches the **scalar only** —
and `updateMessageEnvelopeId` seeds the scalar from the FIRST fan-out leg. So when any non-first
group member's device destroys the envelope (decrypt failure), the sender's bubble keeps ✓✓ and the
B-46 auto-resend keyed off the `undelivered` flip never fires for that member. Bob's failure flips
the bubble; carol's identical failure is silently ignored. Pinned by `envelopeLegParity.test.ts`
(controls + 2 DOCUMENTS cases). Fix shape: mirror the SYNC-1 map match in
`applyEnvelopeUndeliverable` (and decide the multi-leg semantics: any-leg-flips vs per-leg state).

## B-144 — group replies never carry the reply on the wire ⚠️ P2 HIGH-VISIBILITY · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`sendText` persists `reply_to_msg_id`/`reply_to_preview` on the sender's own bubble in BOTH branches,
but ships `replyTo` inside the sealed payload only on the four DIRECT lanes (live seal, deferred,
sealed-outbox, multi-device — all `replyTo: replyMeta`). The GROUP lane omits it in both layers: the
group-encrypted inner envelope (`{groupId, kind, clientMsgId, body}`) and the outer
`sealPayload(cert, sealedBody, {…})` options. `DeferredGroupOutboxPayload` has no replyTo field at
all. Recipient side reads exactly the field that is never set (`buildInboundMessage` ←
`unwrapped.replyTo`; stash replay ← `sealed.replyTo`). **Every group recipient renders a reply as a
plain message — no quote strip, no reply-jump — while the author sees their own quote locally**,
which is why manual testing never caught it. Pinned by `replyWireParity.test.ts` (source scan,
DOCUMENTS cases to flip). Fix: add `replyTo` to the inner group envelope (it is inside the group
encryption), thread it through `DeferredGroupOutboxPayload`, and read it in the group inbound lanes.

## B-145 — inbound reply preview has no length cap ⚠️ P3 HARDENING · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

Send side caps the quoted preview at 200 chars (`planSend`); receive side stores
`env.replyTo.preview` verbatim (`buildInboundMessage`) and sealed-payload validation only checks
"is a string". A hostile peer can ship an arbitrarily large quote strip into the store/DB/backup.
Pinned by `replyWireParity.test.ts` (10k-char pass-through DOCUMENTS case). Fix: slice at ingest.

## B-146 — a timestamp-less presence frame wipes the stored last-seen ⚠️ P3 · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`setPresence` (messengerStore.ts) overwrites the record wholesale:
`s.presence[userId] = {state, online, lastSeen: lastSeenMs, lastSeenMs}` — and
`ServerPresence.lastSeenMs` is optional (a plain `online` frame ships none). offline(T) → online
(no ts) → any local downgrade (`clearPresence` on reconnect/unsubscribe preserves the now-undefined
value) leaves the peer offline with NO "Last seen …" line the client previously knew. Pinned by
`presenceStore.test.ts` (2 DOCUMENTS cases). Fix: preserve prior `lastSeen` when the frame carries
none.

## B-147 — future-dated last-seen paints "Active recently" on an OFFLINE peer ⚠️ P3 · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`tier()` (PeerPresence.tsx): `Date.now() - rec.lastSeen < 5 * 60_000` — a future `lastSeen` (peer
clock skew) gives a negative delta, which passes. The offline peer's pill reads "Active recently"
AND the offline banner is suppressed entirely, while `formatLastSeen` correctly refuses the same
timestamp (`ms < 0 → null`) — the two functions disagree about one record. Pinned by
`peerPresence.test.ts` (2 DOCUMENTS cases). Fix: require `0 <= delta < 5min` in `tier()`.

## B-148 — VoiceNoteRecorder lifecycle defects (4) ⚠️ P2 · OPEN · NOT NODE-TESTABLE (device verify)

`ui/VoiceNoteRecorder.tsx` (expo-av). Found by inspection; the component is RN+expo-av and cannot
run under the node jest project — needs device verification:

- **(a) iOS audio mode never restored.** `start()` sets
  `Audio.setAudioModeAsync({allowsRecordingIOS: true, …})`; no code path ever sets it back
  (`allowsRecordingIOS: false` appears nowhere in the file). After the first voice note the
  AVAudioSession stays in playAndRecord — subsequent playback routes quiet/earpiece until restart.
- **(b) `stop()` has no re-entrancy guard.** `start` is guarded (`startingRef`); `stop` is not. The
  5-min auto-finalise timer (`stopRef.current(false)`) racing the user's Send/Delete tap can run
  `stop` twice over the same captured `recording`: first path completes → `onComplete`; second's
  `stopAndUnloadAsync()` throws "already unloaded" → `catch → onCancel()`. Same clip both sent and
  cancelled.
- **(c) No unmount cleanup.** None of the effects unloads `recording` on unmount — navigating away
  mid-record leaves a live recorder (hot mic, record-mode audio session, temp file).
- **(d) `durationMs` is wall-clock.** `Date.now() - started` measured AFTER
  `await stopAndUnloadAsync()`, so it includes stop latency and the createAsync gap; it feeds both
  the 400 ms min-clip gate and the recipient's duration label instead of the recording's real
  status duration.

## B-149 — the raw plaintext voice recording is never deleted after send ⚠️ P2 PRIVACY · OPEN

The expo-av recording at `rec.getURI()` is read (`readUriBytes`), encrypted and uploaded — but
nothing unlinks the original unencrypted m4a in the app cache. `deleteTempBytes` only manages the
`bravo-media-<id>` decrypted-view files keyed by message id; it never knows the recorder's temp
path. The user's own plaintext audio persists until the OS trims cache, contradicting the
mediaFiles "caller owns cleanup" contract. Fix: delete the source uri after `readUriBytes`
succeeds (and on cancel).

## B-150 — presence has no client-side staleness TTL; the "presence reaper" does not exist ⚠️ P3 · OPEN

A comment in `PeerOfflineBanner` says "The presence reaper + reconnect-clear can both flip the peer
to offline…" — repo-wide, `reaper` matches only that comment. The only offline transitions are a
server `offline` frame, reconnect/unsubscribe `clearPresence`, and logout. While our socket stays
healthy, a peer whose device dies without a clean disconnect keeps a green dot indefinitely; the
client fully trusts the server to emit `offline`. Decide: implement a client TTL (e.g. downgrade
`online`→`recent` after N min without frames) or fix the comment and accept server truth.
Related hardening note: "hide last seen" is enforced server-side only — the client renders any
`lastSeenMs` it receives (defense-in-depth gap, not a live leak while the server strip holds).

## B-151 — link-preview OG scraper misses content-before-property meta tags ⚠️ P3 · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`parseMeta` (ui/linkPreview.ts) uses one regex requiring `property=` BEFORE `content=`. Very common
real-world markup (`<meta content="…" property="og:title">`) silently falls back to `<title>`/host —
degraded previews, no error. Also noted: a transient fetch failure is memoised as `null` for the app
lifetime (offline once → that link never gets a preview again). Both pinned by
`linkPreview.test.ts` DOCUMENTS cases. Fix: match either attribute order; don't cache rejections.

## B-152 — dead duplicate transport clients + certCache in the module tree ⚠️ P4 CODE-HEALTH · OPEN

`runtime/certCache.ts`, `transport/keysClient.ts`, `transport/relayClient.ts`,
`transport/senderCertClient.ts` have ZERO non-test importers — production uses the
`@bravo/messenger-core` implementations (productionRuntime imports them from core; core's cache has
methods — `getIssued()`, `revokeCurrentAndInvalidate()` — the local copy lacks). The local
`SenderCertCache.get()` also throws away a still-valid cert when a proactive refresh fails inside
the 10-min margin (negative-cache throws instead of falling back to `this.current`) — worth
checking the LIVE core copy for the same defect before deleting these. Fix: delete the four dead
files (and verify the core cache's refresh-failure fallback).

## B-153 — test-infra: `expo/virtual/env` transform hole makes suites flake in full runs ⚠️ P3 TEST-INFRA · OPEN

Any messenger-crypto test that (transitively) imports `@utils/constants` can die at load with
`SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` from `node_modules/expo/virtual/env.js` — babel-preset-expo
rewrites `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_*` into that import, and the project's `transformIgnorePatterns`
only allows `@noble/hashes`. Observed across four full runs on a CLEAN tree: `pushSlimBgHandler`
failed 3 of 4, `backupFlags`, `blockedPeersAndTombstones`, `safetyNumber` each failed once — all
pass in isolation, so the failure MOVES (B-126 family, but a different mechanism than the
`incomingRingtone` teardown flake). Fix candidates: add `expo` (or `expo/virtual`) to the
messenger-crypto `transformIgnorePatterns` allowlist, or map `expo/virtual/env` to a stub in
`moduleNameMapper`. Until then: the B-126 rule ("run twice; a failure that moves is flake") stands —
new suites should mock `@utils/constants` (see `phoneNormalize.test.ts` header).

## B-154 — phone normalization double-prefixes numbers that already embed the country code ⚠️ P3 · OPEN · TEST-DOCUMENTED

`normalizeToE164('1 (415) 555-0100', '1')` → `+114155550100` (and `'8801799…'` with `'880'` →
`+880880…`): a local-format contact that already contains the country code — a very common way
people save numbers — gets the code prepended again, producing a valid-LOOKING wrong E.164 and a
silent discovery miss ("contact not on Bravo"). Pinned by `phoneNormalize.test.ts` DOCUMENTS case.
Fix: if the digits already start with the default calling code and the remainder is a plausible
local number, don't prepend. Related edges pinned in the same suite: an own-phone stored without
`+` yields NO region (every local contact then drops), and `contactSearch.digitsOf` strips ALL
leading zeros while `normalizeToE164` deliberately strips ONE — the two modules canonicalize the
same input differently.

### Minor observations (not numbered)

- `previewForReply` (ChatScreen) special-cases image/file only — replying to a voice/video note
  yields an empty quote (`msg.content` is empty for media).
- Reply-jump resolves strictly on `m.id`; a message whose id was rewritten by the M12 dedup fork
  (`X#n`) can't be jump-targeted (reactions have a `findReactionTarget` fallback; reply-jump has
  none).
- `MediaBlobCache.put` over the 50 MB per-blob cap early-returns WITHOUT invalidating an existing
  smaller row for the same key (pinned as DOCUMENTS in `mediaBlobCache.test.ts`); its own comment
  still says "25 MB".
- `recordReadReceipts` writes `m.status = 'read'` directly, bypassing `isStatusRegression` — safe
  while `read` is ladder-top, fragile if a rank is ever added above it.
- `formatLastSeen` >7d branch omits the year ("Last seen Apr 29" is ambiguous across years).
- The call-variant offline banner's "They'll get a missed-call notification." sub-line renders only
  when a `lastSeen` is known, though the copy has nothing to do with last-seen.
