# 2026-07-23 (later) — B-143 … B-154 FIXED + two findings corrected

All bugs from the morning coverage sweep are now fixed, each with a permanent regression test.
**Two of my own findings were wrong and are corrected below — read those first.**

Gates: messenger suite **272 suites / 2678 tests**, run twice; `tsc` 47 = baseline; eslint 0 errors.
The only red in a full run was `incomingRingtone` + `safetyNumber`, both of which PASS in isolation
(`safetyNumber` 16s alone vs 171s under load) — the documented B-126 moving flake, not these changes.

## ⚠️ B-150 — RETRACTED. Not a bug. The presence reaper EXISTS.

I reported "no client-side presence TTL; the reaper a comment references does not exist". **That was
wrong, and the method was the problem: I grepped `src/` (the mobile app) and not `apps/`.**

`apps/messenger-service/src/gateway/presence.cron.ts` is a real reaper — `@Cron(EVERY_5_MINUTES)`,
Redis advisory lock for multi-replica safety, calling `PresenceService.sweepStale()`. And the
liveness model underneath it is stronger than I described: `presence.service.ts` keeps a **120-second
lease** (`LIVE_TTL_SEC`) refreshed by client heartbeats (~4s) and a 30s per-pod re-assertion, and its
own comment states the design intent — _"a pod that dies ungracefully simply stops refreshing, the
lease expires on its own, and the next sweep flips the user offline — no disconnect handler has to
run."_

So a peer whose device dies is reaped in **~7 minutes worst case**, not "indefinitely", and the
client comment I flagged as referring to nothing is accurate. **No client TTL was implemented, and
none should be:** presence frames are transition-based, not heartbeats, so a client-side "no frame in
N minutes ⇒ offline" rule would paint every long-idle-but-online peer as offline. That would be a
worse bug than the one I thought I had found.

The one residual observation stands and is now _partly_ addressed by B-146: last-seen privacy is
enforced server-side, and the client now at least refuses to re-assert a timestamp the server
stripped.

## ⚠️ B-143 — the auto-resend half of my report was WRONG

I wrote that the dropped signal meant "the B-46 auto-resend never fires for that member". It never
could have: `selectUndeliverableResend` (`undeliverableResend.ts`) refuses any non-`direct`
conversation outright — _"a group row can't attribute which member's envelope died"_. Group messages
have no auto-resend path at all, by design. Reading the consumer before changing the producer is what
caught this.

The real defect is narrower but still real, and is what was fixed.

## ⚠️ B-152 — `keysClient.ts` is NOT dead

I listed four orphaned files. `transport/keysClient.ts` has a live consumer —
`vault/vaultOps.ts:22` imports it directly. It was **kept**. Only the three with genuinely zero
importers were deleted.

---

## B-143 — group "undeliverable" dropped for every member but the first · FIXED

`applyEnvelopeUndeliverable` matched only the scalar `envelope_id`, which a group fan-out seeds from
the **first** leg. Its sibling `applyEnvelopeDelivered` has matched the per-recipient `envelope_ids`
map since SYNC-1. The outcome therefore depended on **fan-out order**: the first member's destroy
flipped the sender's bubble, every other member's identical destroy was silently dropped and the
sender kept a ✓✓ for a message that member will never see.

Fixed by using the same match as the sibling. Semantics are now symmetric — "any leg delivered ⇒
advance", "any leg destroyed ⇒ undelivered". For a group that is a deliberately **pessimistic**
display: one member's identity churn marks the whole message failed. That is chosen over the status
quo (a silent loss), and the open question — a true per-leg partial-delivery model — is recorded at
the function rather than papered over. Blast radius is display-only: the auto-resend refuses groups
anyway (see the correction above).

Pinned by `envelopeLegParity.test.ts` (8 cases), including one asserting the result no longer depends
on fan-out order, plus controls that `read` still wins over a late destroy. **Mutation-proved:**
reverting the match turns exactly the 3 B-143 assertions red and leaves the 5 controls green.

## B-144 — group replies never carried the reply on the wire · FIXED

The sender persisted `reply_to_msg_id` on its OWN bubble in both branches but sealed `replyTo` only
on the four DIRECT lanes. Every group recipient rendered a reply as a plain message — no quote strip,
no reply-jump — while the author saw their own quote. That asymmetry is exactly why it survived
manual testing.

**The fix needed five sites, not one** (the original report said one):

1. the live group seal — `sealPayload(cert, sealedBody, …)`
2. the group **reseal** branch in `resealOutboxRow` (the direct branch already had it)
3. the no-cert deferred group row
4. the per-peer crypto-failure deferred group row
5. the SN-06 stored-bytes row whose stale cert is re-minted later

Miss any of 3–5 and an offline-queued group reply still ships stripped, because the drain re-seals
from the stored row. `DeferredGroupOutboxPayload` gained the `replyTo` field the direct shape has had
since XO-2.

**No inbound change was required, and that is the load-bearing detail:** the reply rides the OUTER
per-recipient seal next to `attachment`, and `buildInboundMessage` has always read `env.replyTo` off
exactly that object. The inner group envelope deliberately stays reply-free — pinned, so a later
"fix" doesn't create a second source of truth.

**Not a stop-condition breach, verified rather than assumed:** `replyTo` is an existing
`SealedPayload` field that `isValidSealedPayload` already validates, it rides inside the libsignal
ciphertext exactly like the `attachment` the GROUP MEDIA FIX already put in this same call, and AAD
and sender-cert logic are untouched. Old clients already read this field, so it is
backward-compatible in both directions.

Pinned by `replyWireParity.test.ts` (12 cases) incl. an 8-site census ratchet. **Mutation-proved:**
removing the live group seal's `replyTo` turns 2 tests red.

## B-145 — inbound reply preview had no length cap · FIXED

Send capped at 200; receive copied the wire value verbatim and validation only checked "is a string",
so a non-conforming peer could push an unbounded quote strip into the store, SQLCipher and every
backup mirror. Capped at ingest. The magic `200` existed in **three** copies — now one exported
`REPLY_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS`, with a source scan asserting the literal cannot come back.

## B-146 — a timestamp-less presence frame wiped the stored last-seen · FIXED

An `online`/`active`/`away` frame legitimately carries no `lastSeenMs`, and writing that `undefined`
through destroyed a timestamp the client already had; a later local downgrade (`clearPresence` on
reconnect) then faithfully preserved the wiped value, so the offline banner lost its "Last seen …"
line for the rest of the session.

**The naive fix would have been a privacy regression**, which is the interesting part: the relay
_strips_ `lastSeenMs` when a peer turns off "show last seen" (audit M-06), so blindly backfilling the
remembered value would resurrect precisely what the peer just hid. The fix therefore backfills only
on **non-offline** frames — absence on an `offline` frame is authoritative and clears. Pinned by
both a retention test and a dedicated privacy test.

## B-147 — future-dated last-seen painted "Active recently" on an offline peer · FIXED

`tier()` tested `delta < 5min` with no lower bound, so a negative delta (peer clock skew) passed. The
sharper half: the offline banner only paints for tier `offline`, so skew **suppressed the banner
entirely**. Meanwhile `formatLastSeen` correctly rejected the same timestamp — two functions
disagreeing about one record. Window is now bounded at both ends; boundary tests (0, 5min−1, 5min)
guard against over-correcting.

## B-148 — VoiceNoteRecorder lifecycle ×4 · FIXED (device verify pending)

- **(a) iOS audio session never released.** `start()` set `allowsRecordingIOS: true` and nothing set
  it back, so the session stayed in playAndRecord; playback is a _different_ library (expo-audio)
  that doesn't re-assert a category, so later voice notes played quiet/earpiece until app restart.
  Added `releaseRecordingMode()` on the success path, the throw path **and** unmount.
- **(b) `stop()` re-entrancy.** `start` was guarded, `stop` was not, and `setRecording(null)` is
  batched — so the 5-min auto-finalise timer racing a Send tap let both callers see the same live
  recorder: one reached `onComplete`, the other threw "already unloaded" into a catch that calls
  `onCancel`. **One clip was both sent and cancelled.** Guard is claimed before the first `await`
  and released in a `finally` (a throw in between would otherwise wedge the recorder shut).
- **(c) No unmount teardown.** Navigating away mid-record left a live recorder holding the mic and
  the record-mode session. Added, keyed on `[]` via a ref so it can't tear down the recorder it just
  created.
- **(d) Wall-clock duration.** `Date.now() - started` was measured _after_ `stopAndUnloadAsync()`, so
  it included stop latency and fed both the recipient's duration label and the 400 ms accidental-tap
  floor. Now prefers `getStatusAsync().durationMillis`, wall-clock only as fallback.

## B-149 — the plaintext voice recording was never deleted · FIXED

The raw unencrypted m4a stayed in the app cache after upload, against this module's own
"caller owns cleanup" contract. Added `deleteEphemeralSource()` plus an `ephemeralSource` flag
threaded recorder → queue → sender, deleted immediately after `readUriBytes` (before the size
bail-out, so an oversized clip can't strand plaintext either).

**The deleter is deliberately narrow, and the reason matters:** the obvious generalisation — "delete
the source after upload" — would unlink **library picks, i.e. delete the user's photo out of their
gallery**. It refuses anything that isn't a `file://` path inside the app's own
Caches/Documents/Temporary directories, and a test asserts exactly one call site sets the flag.

## B-151 — link previews: attribute order + negative caching · FIXED

The OG regex required `property=` before `content=`; a large share of real pages emit the reverse and
silently degraded to the `<title>`/host fallback. Now matches either order. Separately, a single
transient failure (offline, DNS blip, 5xx, timeout) memoised `null` for the whole app lifetime, so
that link never got a preview again — the entry is now kept only on a real result, while concurrent
callers still share one in-flight fetch (pinned).

## B-152 — dead duplicate transport clients · FIXED (3 deleted, 1 kept)

Deleted `runtime/certCache.ts`, `transport/relayClient.ts`, `transport/senderCertClient.ts` — all
verified zero importers. Production builds these from `@bravo/messenger-core`; the local
`SenderCertCache` had already drifted (missing `getIssued()` / `revokeCurrentAndInvalidate()`, which
the runtime calls) and threw away a still-valid cert when a proactive refresh failed inside the
10-minute margin. A duplicate nothing imports can't be kept honest by any test and leaves the next
reader unable to tell which copy is real — so deleted rather than pinned. `keysClient.ts` kept (see
correction above). Typecheck stayed at the 47 baseline, which is the real proof.

## B-153 — `expo/virtual/env` transform hole · FIXED

`babel-preset-expo` rewrites `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_*` into an import of `expo/virtual/env`, which
ships as untransformed ESM inside `node_modules` — which the node project deliberately does not
transform. Any suite transitively importing `@utils/constants` could die at load with
`SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`. Now mapped to a stub via `moduleNameMapper`.

**Honest scope note:** this closed one real mechanism — the exact error disappeared and the suite
moved on to failing on a _different_ untransformed module — but it is **not** the whole story. The
`incomingRingtone` / `safetyNumber` failures are a separate resource-contention/teardown flake
(they pass in isolation; `safetyNumber` 16s alone vs 171s under load). The B-126 "run it twice" rule
still stands and is now written into `CLAUDE.md`.

## B-154 — phone numbers that already embed the country code were double-prefixed · FIXED

`normalizeToE164('1 (415) 555-0100', '1')` produced `+114155550100` — a valid-_looking_ E.164 that
matches nothing, so the contact silently never appeared as "on Bravo". Saving numbers with the
country code and no `+` is extremely common.

The discriminator that makes the fix safe is the **trunk zero**: its presence means local format, so
those are always prefixed (UK `07…` → `+447…`, never `+47…`). Only when there is no trunk zero AND
the digits start with the calling code AND the remainder is still ≥7 digits is the code treated as
already present. Leading digits that merely _look_ like the code (cc `1`, local `1234567`) still get
prefixed, because stripping would leave 6 digits — below the E.164 floor.

**Deliberately NOT changed:** `callingCodeFromOwnPhone` still requires a leading `+`. Accepting bare
digits would mean guessing a region from an ambiguous string, and guessing wrong silently misroutes
_every_ contact lookup for that user. Failing closed is the safer half of that trade; the test is
re-labelled as a CONTRACT rather than a defect.

# QA Session — 2026-07-23 (PM) · First-boot messenger lag investigation

**Scope:** founder report "on first boot the messenger fell laggy" — root-cause investigation only,
**fix NOT applied**. Full register: `docs/audits/FIRST_BOOT_LAG_B155_2026-07-23.md`. New regression
suite `bootstrapDrainYield` (source scan + store pins) landed under
`src/modules/messenger/__tests__/`; CLAUDE.md regression table updated. Gates: messenger-crypto run
twice per the B-126 rule — run 1 **273/273 suites / 2697 tests green** (incl. the new suite), run 2
recorded in the session log; `tsc` at baseline.

## B-155 — messenger laggy on first boot: bootstrap drain saturates the JS thread ✅ P2 · FIXED (F1+F3; F2 deferred)

First boot per owner is the only boot where `drainRelay` (`productionRuntime.ts:8210`) pulls with
`bootstrap=true` (AsyncStorage `bravo.relay.bootstrap-done.<ownUserId>` unset), raising the first
page from 50 to **1000 envelopes** (`:8254`) — a deliberate restore-correctness fix whose cost side
was never handled. The envelope loop (`:8274`) then runs, per envelope and with **zero macrotask
yields anywhere in the function**: sealed-sender unwrap (pure-JS curve25519), `wasSeen` SQL,
`admitSenderCert` (+ keys-service fetch per new peer), `handleIncoming` serialized on the global txn
chain (first boot ⇒ X3DH session build per peer — the most expensive envelope kind), and a Zustand
commit that re-renders the home list (`MessengerHomeScreen.tsx:68-69` subscribes to
`conversations` + `conversationOrder`). At 5–20 ms/envelope that is 10–30+ s of continuous JS-thread
occupancy while the WS `flushPendingOnConnect` lane storms the same window — touches and navigation
starve, which reads exactly as "fell laggy". Second boot: flag set, 50-cap pages, small backlog —
self-heals, so it only ever reproduces on first boot. Ruled out: boot hydration (single
`hydrateMessages` commit), B-94 mirror (idle-boot silent), outbox/expiry sweeps (no-ops fresh).
Pinned by `bootstrapDrainYield.test.ts`: `DOCUMENTS B-155` (no yield token in `drainRelay` — the fix
flips it to require one) + control anchors + 2 permanent pins (one-commit hydration, N-30
referential stability of untouched lists). Fix shape (register §5): F1 cooperative yield every ≤25
envelopes (between envelopes only — never inside the receive txn or between decrypt and ack), F2
coalesce per-envelope conversation-preview/reorder churn, F3 defer boot sweeps to first idle;
non-goals: don't lower the 1000 cap, don't touch the txn chain or ack ordering. Device before/after
capture recipe in register §7 (on-device timing still pending — no logcat existed from the report).

**UPDATE (same day) — overall-lagginess follow-up sweep (register §8).** Steady-state audit of every
messenger screen subscription, live timer, and cadence. Headline: **B-155's no-yield loop is NOT
first-boot-only** — every reconnect/foreground catch-up drain (50/page × 10 pages = up to 500
envelopes) runs the same yield-free loop, which is the "stutters for a few seconds after
foregrounding" signature; the F1 fix covers it and the existing `DOCUMENTS B-155` scan already pins
the whole function (L1, P2). Also found: L2 (P3) `ExpirySweeper` walks EVERY hydrated message at
1 Hz whenever ≥1 burn-timer message is live anywhere (F-13 idle backoff only engages at exactly
zero armed; fix = armed-index / next-expiry sleep); L3 (P3) composer `text` state at the ChatScreen
root re-renders the whole ~2 700-line screen per keystroke (bubbles memo'd; fix = extract the
composer); L4 (P4) ForwardList unshallow whole-map subscription; L5 (P4) failed link previews
refetch per view (B-151 kept NO negative cache; fix = 30–60 s TTL, does not conflict with the
`linkPreview` suite pin); L6 (INFO) dead legacy `useRealtimeMessages` hook (zero importers, legacy
store — deadcode-sweep it).

# Fix Session — 2026-07-23 (evening) · B-155…B-160 messenger lag, ALL FIXED

Every finding from the first-boot + overall-lagginess investigation is fixed, each as its own
commit with its own RED-first regression test. Register (per-bug detail, sign-off, and the
device checks still outstanding): `docs/audits/FIRST_BOOT_LAG_B155_2026-07-23.md` §5, §8, §9.

**Gates:** full `messenger-crypto` project green, run **twice** per the B-126 flake rule ·
`tsc` 47 = baseline throughout · eslint 0 errors on every touched file. 35 new tests in 4 new
suites plus 4 added to `linkPreview`.

## B-155 — first-boot/catch-up drain starved the JS thread · FIXED (F1 + F3)

**F1** — the `drainRelay` envelope loop now yields. Time-sliced (`DRAIN_SLICE_MS = 12`, ~one
frame) rather than every-Nth, because envelope cost spans two orders of magnitude (a `wasSeen`
hit vs an X3DH session build); when the slice is spent it awaits `yieldToEventLoop()`, a real
`setTimeout(0)` **macrotask** — a microtask hop keeps the thread and would change nothing. The
yield sits at the TOP of the loop body: outside the W22a in-flight hold, outside the receive
txn, never between an envelope's decrypt and its ack (ack/dwell untouched). This fixes **every**
catch-up drain, not just first boot. Mutation-proved.
**F3** — the boot group-stash drain is deferred via `deferToIdle` (`InteractionManager`, falling
back to inline where there is no RN runtime so deferred work can never silently vanish), with an
`isOurEpoch()` re-check. The B-124 contamination sweep and the stash prunes deliberately stay
inline — reordering data-corruption cleanup to save milliseconds is a bad trade, reasons in §5.
**F2 (home-list churn coalescing) deliberately NOT done** — with F1 the renders spread across
frames, and batching would mean touching `appendMessage`'s store path, the exact surface that
produced B-124/B-125. Take device numbers first.

## B-156 — dead Twilio-era messenger chain · FIXED

`src/hooks/useRealtimeMessages.ts` (0 importers) → `src/store/messengerStore.ts` (Twilio-era,
its only importer was that hook) → `src/services/twilio.ts` (only importer was that store): all
three deleted. The prize is the name collision the pipeline brief warns about — "two files named
`messengerStore.ts`, a grep-driven refactor will hit the wrong file". Now exactly one.
`legacyMessengerStoreGone.test.ts` walks the source tree, so a NEW importer fails too.

## B-157 — link previews refetched on every view after a failure · FIXED

B-151 killed the permanent null memo but left NO negative memory, so each remount of a link
bubble re-kicked a fetch carrying a 5 s abort timer. Now a 60 s TTL + 128-entry bounded map
(expired-first, then oldest-inserted). B-151's real invariant (a failure is never _permanent_)
is still asserted; its "retries on the very next call" assertion was updated **deliberately**,
reason recorded in the test, because per-view retry was the defect.

## B-158 — forward picker subscribed unshallow to the conversations map · FIXED

`useShallow`, matching the M-18 pattern the home list uses. Bounded by modal lifetime (RN
`Modal` unmounts children when hidden), hence P4.

## B-159 — every keystroke re-rendered the whole ChatScreen · FIXED

The draft was `useState` at the root of a ~2,700-line component. `React.memo` cannot save a
component that re-renders itself, so the state moved: the input bar is now `<ChatComposer>`
(memoised, `forwardRef`) owning `text`, `justSent` and the native `inputRef`. The screen gets
`onSend(trimmed)` and `onDraftActivity(hasText)`; the old typing `useEffect` — keyed on `text`,
which is _why_ the draft lived in the screen — is now a ref-only function, so typing cadence is
unchanged at zero render cost. Every composer prop is referentially stable or the memo is
defeated. B-73's imperative native clear preserved and pinned. **Device verification required**
— this is the send path (§9).

## B-160 — expiry sweep was O(all messages) at 1 Hz · FIXED

`ExpirySweeper.sweep()` walked every hydrated message in every conversation once a second for as
long as ONE armed message existed anywhere (~4,000 row visits/s on a 20-chat account). Now a
per-conversation armed index keyed by the message-list **reference** — unchanged lists reuse
their cached armed subset (a steady-state tick visits **zero** rows, proxy-measured), a moved
reference is re-scanned. Same immer reference-stability property N-30 relies on.
**Bonus correctness fix:** F-13's `IDLE_RESCAN_MS` is deleted — it skipped all sweeps for 30 s
after a zero-armed scan, so a 10 s disappearing message sent in that window survived up to ~20 s
past its own countdown.

## Test-integrity finding — naive comment stripping is unsafe on `.tsx`

While writing the B-159 pins: the `src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')` idiom used by the
source scans **ate 64 KB of `ChatScreen.tsx`'s 171 KB**. Cause: `ChatScreen.tsx:1140` passes the
MIME wildcard `'*/*'` to `DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync`; its `*/` closes a block comment
early, and a later real `/*` then pairs with a distant `*/`. Every `not.toMatch` downstream
would have passed **vacuously** — exactly the CLAUDE.md trap. `messengerRenderPerf.test.ts` uses
a line-based stripper (a block comment must open the line) plus a guard test asserting >55% of
bytes survive and known declarations are still present. **Checked and NOT affected:** the `.ts`
runtime scans (`bootstrapDrainYield`, `receivePersistenceInvariants`) — verified by asserting
known code survives their slices; their 50–59% strip ratio is genuine comment density.

## B-161 — the "moving flake" (B-126/B-153) root-caused and killed · FIXED

`test:crypto` has failed intermittently for months, naming a DIFFERENT suite each
run — the documented rule was "one red run is not evidence, run it twice". Two concrete
mechanisms were found and fixed, and the suite now runs green repeatedly.

**Mechanism 1 — `{virtual: true}` on modules that really exist.** Five suites mocked
`@utils/constants`, `react-native` or `@notifee/react-native` with `jest.mock(…, {virtual: true})`.
That flag means "this module is not on disk": Jest registers the factory under the literal
specifier while the real import still resolves to the real file, so **which one wins depends on
resolution order**. Two failure shapes, both seen:

- assertion failures — `pendingActions` / `pushSlimBgHandler` / `serverWakeNotifications` got the
  production fallback `https://msg.bravosecure.com` instead of the mocked `https://msg.test`;
- whole-suite REQUIRE-time death with zero failed assertions — `incomingRingtone`, when the real
  `react-native` won inside the node-env project (untransformed ESM). This is exactly the shape
  B-153 chased and half-closed.
  The two suites that mock `@utils/constants` WITHOUT the flag (`fcmBootstrapOrder`,
  `or3IosBannerLane`) have never flaked — that contrast is what identified it. Flag removed from the
  four demonstrated suites. **Still carrying it (not touched — currently passing, but the same latent
  race):** `launchCallDoubleTap.test.ts:29`, `privacyToggleLatestWins.test.ts:34`.

**Mechanism 2 — a poisoned jest transform cache.** After the mock fixes, `backupFlags` still failed
~1 run in 3 with `Expected "owner", Received null` (its `readFlag` swallows a throwing AsyncStorage
and returns null — i.e. the REAL AsyncStorage was in play, which throws `window is not defined`
under node). `npx jest --clearCache` ended it: 3 consecutive clean full runs immediately after,
and green ever since. If the moving flake ever returns, **clear the cache first** before hunting
a code cause.

**Also fixed — starvation timeouts, not flakes.** The `app` project had no `testTimeout`, so RN
component renders ran on Jest's 5s default. `BackupSetupScreen` BKSET-27 takes ~2s alone but was
measured at **55s** wall-clock when all three projects share workers under `npx jest`; `CreditsScreen`
at 35s. `jest.setTimeout(60000)` in `jest.setup.app.js` (the `messenger-crypto` project already
raised its own to 30s for the same reason). A per-test timeout is there to catch a HANG — 60s still
does, while no longer failing a test that is merely starved.

**Two genuinely stale tests fixed** (red on the untouched tree — verified with a worktree at the
pre-work commit, so NOT caused by the B-155 work):

- `uploadAvatar` — still mocked the pre-DC-21 anon-key `storage.upload()` + `getPublicUrl()` flow;
  production moved to a service-role signed upload URL from the `avatar-upload-url` edge function.
  Every case failed on a real network call. Rewritten against the current flow and extended to pin
  the DC-21 properties (bearer token on the signing request; upload rides the signed token; no
  upload at all when signing is refused). Note the mocks must override the `supabase.functions` /
  `supabase.storage` **getters** — each access constructs a NEW client, so `jest.spyOn` patched a
  throwaway and the real Edge Function call went out.
- `authStore.recheckMembership` — asserted the pre-RS-06 contract ("a 401 is itself a revocation
  signal") while seeding `user: null`. RS-06 narrowed teardown to managed CPOs only, because this
  path also runs on foreground-resume for every shell where a 401 is just as likely to be a
  transient refresh outage. Updated to the current rule and extended with the 403 case and the
  non-CPO counter-case (the false-positive logout wave the rule exists to prevent).

**Result:** `npx jest` (all three projects) — **330 suites / 3221 tests green, twice consecutively**;
`messenger-crypto` alone green 5+ consecutive runs. tsc 47 = baseline; eslint 0 errors.

Four parallel audit agents swept the entire backup module (26 client files, 3 screens, push seams,

`docs/audits/BACKUP_AUDIT_2026-07-24.md`. Highlights:

- **B-162 (P1)** `setDeferBundlePublish(true)` leaked on every restore-failure exit → fresh
  identity never published, peers sealed to a dead bundle all session (silent inbound loss).
- **B-163 (P1)** B-94 ledger seed used `loadAll()` AFTER the archive drain → archive-replayed +
  live-received rows marked "flushed" though the mirror never got them → boot sweep skipped them
  forever, next restore permanently lacked them (30-day archive fuse). Seed now happens INSIDE the
  verified flush, exactly the flushed row set (`restoreBatchHydrate.test.ts`).
- **B-164 (P1)** background msg-wake booted the runtime with NO restore-mode guard (foreground had
  one) → installIdentity + publish over the recoverable identity = the Round-8 stranded-backup
  class; also armed the flag at boot-decision time (60s nav-settle window was unguarded).
- **B-165 (P1)** conversation rows applied BEFORE Merkle verify and via wholesale replace → an
  integrity-failed restore left unverified rows applied; live rows (unlock path / drained rekey)
  stomped with stale member lists → fan-out kept targeting REMOVED members (L9 class). Now staged
  post-verify, live-always-wins, participants re-synced from live group state.
- **B-166 (P1)** kill window between H-2 clear (walk end) and archive-marker arm (drain start) →
  archive never drained, no marker to heal it. Both markers now armed up front.
- **B-167 (P1)** `commitMerkleRoot` had ≥6 unserialized entry points; a slow walk finishing after a
  newer commit 409'd and the I6 adopt RE-SIGNED THE STALE ROOT at a higher seq — server left with
  pre-flush bytes as the newest commit and the pending flag cleared = unhealable equal-count
  `root_mismatch`. Now single-flight (`merkleCommitSingleFlight.test.ts`).
- **B-168 (P1)** flush never checked the owner gate and its failure path requeued into the queue
  `disposeMirror` had just cleared (plus untracked retry timers surviving signOut) → user A's
  plaintext + group master keys could wrap under user B's master key into B's server mirror.
  Session-generation guard + flush-time owner gate + tracked timers (`mirrorSessionHygiene.test.ts`).
- **B-169 (P1)** `markDirty` not-found fallback shipped a REAL `__deleted__` tombstone for rows
  merely evicted from the 200/convo in-memory cap (late outbox drains, receipts on old rows) →
  restores dropped live messages. Fallback removed; H-3 `mirrorRemoval` is the only tombstone path.
- **B-170 (P2)** BackupSetupScreen unlock: `setMirrorKey` fired the catch-up sweep CONCURRENTLY
  with the restore walk (transient `root_mismatch`/`rows_count_mismatch` on healthy accounts),

- **B-171..B-181 (P2)** tombstone dedup self-defeating; wipe left the mirror live under the old key

**BR-1 — background restore (founder feature request).** The user no longer sits on the restore

## B-184 — the Org Chart presence dot was dead: every node painted gray forever ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-07-24 · DEVICE-VERIFIED

**Reported (agency/founder):** "for agency and there is org chart it does not show the blue active
sign when a account is active."

`OrgHierarchyScreen.tsx` renders an always-visible dot on every node and reads it from
`useMessengerStore(s => s.presence[userId])` — but **nothing ever subscribed those ids.** Presence
only reaches a client for user ids it has explicitly watched (the gateway's `presence.subscribe`
joins `watch:<userId>` and replies with a one-shot snapshot), and the only two subscribers in the
whole app are `MessengerHomeScreen` (direct-conversation peers) and `ChatScreen` (group peers). A
roster is neither. So the org chart read a store slice no one ever filled: `rec` was `undefined`,
`state` fell back to `'offline'`, and **every node — including the owner's own — painted the offline
gray on every account, permanently.** No amount of the roster being online could change it.

Same shape as B-157 (which fixed the _roster_ dot's always-render rule) but a different mechanism:
B-157's dot is `on_duty` off the REST payload; this one is socket presence.

**Fix** (`src/screens/agent/OrgHierarchyScreen.tsx`):

- a `nodeIds` memo over owner + managers + members (deduped, sorted), and an effect keyed on the
  joined string that calls `runtime.subscribePresence(nodeIds)` and releases on unmount — the same
  `peerIdsKey` idiom `MessengerHomeScreen` uses, so a re-`load()` returning identical membership
  does NOT churn the subscription. The runtime refcounts per peer (audit MSG-16), so unsubscribing
  here cannot blind a Messenger row still on screen for the same person.
- `usePresenceTone()` replaces the two-state colour pick, so **`away` is amber, not gray**. The
  server ladder is `offline | online | active | away` (`presence.service.ts`) and `away` means
  _connected but backgrounded_ — folding it into the offline gray is exactly what makes a working
  colleague read as absent. Colours are the shared `OnlineDot`'s (`#22C55E` / `#F59E0B` / `#4B5563`)
  so a node here and a Messenger row for the same person can never disagree.
- the tone label now rides the node's `accessibilityLabel` (the dot is colour-only, so it was
  invisible to TalkBack).

**Colour decision:** the founder said "blue"; confirmed with them and kept **green**, matching the
app-wide online convention (`OnlineDot`, `PeerPresencePill`). Cobalt `#5B8DEF` is the _brand accent_
and already carries a different meaning on this screen (the Owner ring).

**No server change was needed** — `presence.subscribe` already accepts arbitrary user ids (only a
blocked pair is refused, M-07) and already strips `lastSeenMs` when the subject hid it (M-06). The
chart displays state only, never last-seen, so nothing new is exposed.

**Regression test:** `src/screens/agent/__tests__/orgChartPresence.test.ts` (6 assertions, source
scan — the screen pulls in navigation/gradients/ZoomableView and the `booking` project is node-env,
so it cannot be imported). Every assertion mutation-proven RED: deleting the subscribe call, the
unsubscribe, the members tier, the dot, the a11y label, or collapsing `away` back into gray each
fails exactly one test.

**Device-verified (BlueStacks, v1.0.130/vc158, agency `AGENT DUE`):** owner node green, `CPO 1`
green while genuinely online and chatting from another device, `Roger` + `CPO 02` gray. Holds at
fontScale 1.3. **Known residual:** immediately after an activity restart the owner's own node can
read gray until the next presence transition — `handleConnection` only calls
`presence.set(sub, 'online')` when `onConnect` reports the FIRST device, so a reconnect that races
the old socket's teardown skips the re-assert. Pre-existing, server-side, self-corrects on a clean
relaunch; NOT introduced here. Not yet exercised: a peer transitioning green→amber (needs a third
device).

## B-185 — "New Channel" left ~240dp of dead space above the tab bar ⚠️ P3 UI · FIXED 2026-07-24 · DEVICE-VERIFIED

**Reported (agency/founder, with screenshot):** "New Channel … and below, there is a menu bar —
there is a lot of space, I don't want that space, they should be closely aligned."

`ChannelEditorScreen`'s primary action lives INSIDE the ScrollView, and the content container had no
`flexGrow`. The "New Channel" form is short, so the container was content-height and **"Create
channel" floated mid-screen with ~240dp of pure `#07090D` between it and the ObsidianTabBar**
(measured on BlueStacks: button bottom y=1140px, tab row y=1505px, density 240 → 243dp). It also
added `insets.bottom + 40` while the tab bar below already reserves the safe area — the B-156
double-count.

**Fix:**

- `ChannelEditorScreen.tsx` — `flexGrow: 1` on the content container plus a
  `{flexGrow: 1, minHeight: 26}` spacer immediately above the action block. Short form → the spacer
  absorbs the free space and the button sits on the bottom edge; content taller than the viewport →
  Yoga has no positive free space to distribute, the spacer floors at 26 and the form simply
  scrolls. Deliberately **not** a fixed footer: when editing, the action block is Save + Members +
  Archive (~178dp) and pinning that would eat the form on a small screen — and a pinned footer is
  also the wrong answer once a keyboard shrinks the viewport.
- `paddingBottom` is now `(inDepartmentalShell ? 0 : insets.bottom) + 12` — the standalone path
  (pushed from MessengerHome with no tab bar under it) still reserves the real inset.
- `ManageChannelsScreen.tsx` — the in-shell footer pad drops 14 → 8. The bar contributes its own
  14dp top pad + hairline + 14dp, so 14 here put two visible hairlines ~29dp apart and read as a
  dead band under the button.

**Deliberately NOT changed:** `ObsidianTabBar`'s internal 14/1/14 top chrome. It is the universal
footer (design-system G8) shared by the root shell, `CpoNavigator` and the Departmental module, and
was tuned specifically to kill an earlier "tabs aren't aligned / too much space" report. The fix
belongs on the screen side.

**Regression test:** `src/screens/deptchat/__tests__/bottomChrome.test.ts` (5 assertions, source
scan; the files are CRLF so the reader normalises line endings first — a `\n`-anchored regex would
pass vacuously). C1–C4 mutation-proven RED.

**Device-verified (BlueStacks, v1.0.130/vc158):** New Channel button bottom now y=1443px vs tab row
y=1505 → **41dp, down from 243dp**. Edit Channel still shows Save + Members + Archive with nothing
clipped, at fontScale 1.0 and 1.3.

**Still open, same class, NOT fixed here** (found while tracing, outside the reported scope):

- `src/screens/agent/AttendanceScreen.tsx:236` — `insets.bottom + 12` on a fixed-bottom footer, and
  it is the member root of the Departmental **Attend** tab, so it double-counts unconditionally on

- `CpoNavigator.tsx:91` mounts `MessengerNavigator` as the `CpoComms` tab **without**

- Scroll containers inside the shell that add `insets.bottom + N` with no shell check:
  `DepartmentChannelsScreen:319`, `FilesScreen:276`, `VaultScreen:292`, `AdminAttendanceScreen:114`,

  `MyIncidentsScreen:55`, `MyIncidentDetailScreen:43`, `EmployeesScreen:113`,

- **fontScale ≥ 1.3 truncation is app-wide and pre-existing** — `AgentDashboardScreen` tiles clip to

# Founder 13-item batch — 2026-07-24 · B-186…B-198

Reported verbatim by the founder in one message. Numbers assigned above the
parallel session's B-183 high-water mark. Every item below is FIXED in code with
gates green; **items marked ⚠️ SERVER do not take effect from the APK alone** —
they need the Contabo `auth-service` / `messenger-service` redeploy.

## B-186 — the group blue tick was STRUCTURALLY unreachable 🔴 P1 · FIXED

**Reported:** "in group … after reading the message all the member the double
tick never show double blue tick."

`recordReadReceipts` built its "everyone must have read this" set as
`participants.filter(u => u !== s._ownUserId)`. But `_ownUserId` is the vault
**OWNER KEY** — `email ?? phone_e164 ?? user.id`, pinned per install by
`MainNavigator` — while `participants`, `receipts` keys and `envelope_ids` keys
are **auth UUIDs**. For any account carrying an email or a phone (i.e. every real
account) that filter matched nothing, so the **AUTHOR remained inside their own
required set**. Nobody ever sends the author a read receipt for their own
message, so `allRead` could never become true and **no group or department-channel
message could ever go blue, for any user, ever.**

The B-116 suite could not see it: it does `setOwner('me')` with
`participants: ['me','bob','carol']` — one id space. Exactly the MESSAGE_LOOP §4
"one rule, two id spaces, the untested one drifts" class.

**Fix:** the store now carries `_ownAuthUserId` (the real UUID) alongside the
vault key; `setOwner(ownerKey, authUserId)` records it _before_ the same-owner
early return and clears it on a genuine user switch. The required set is now also
intersected with the legs actually shipped (`Object.keys(envelope_ids)`), because
a member added to the channel AFTER the message — or one whose leg never shipped
(no prekeys / outbox exhausted) — can never read it and would otherwise deadlock
the aggregate forever. `ChatScreen`'s "Read by" sheet had the same bug and listed
the author against a permanent dash.

**Test:** `groupBlueTickOwnerKey.test.ts`, 6 cases, all mutation-proven RED.

## B-187 — group ✓✓ is optimistic: ONE settled leg marks the whole fan-out ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28 fix-all — schema v19 `retract_tokens` map + `recordDeliveredReceipt` all-legs rule + per-leg probes; see the 2026-07-28 EOF entry)

**Reported:** "double tick is shown immediately after sent the message."

`applyEnvelopeDelivered` is first-leg-wins (`envelopeDelivered.ts` — any match in
`envelope_ids` flips the scalar to `delivered`), and `selectReceiptProbes` only
ever probes the FIRST leg's `(envelope_id, retract_token)` pair, which
`updateMessageEnvelopeId`/`updateMessageRetractToken` seed first-wins. So in an
N-member channel the ✓✓ means "at least one member has it", not "all do".

**In a 2-member channel — which is what was being tested — one leg IS all legs,
so the observed ✓✓ is correct there.** NOT fixed in this batch because a truthful
all-legs rule needs a per-recipient retract-token map (a SQLCipher schema bump)
plus an all-legs probe; requiring all legs with only the first leg probed would
regress straight back to B-155 ("group messages never advance past one tick"),
fixed the day before. `LocalMessage.receipts` already declares a `'delivered'`
variant that nothing writes — that is the intended home for the real fix.

## B-188 — the org owner's profile opened "not related to your organization" ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

The B-159 owner branch in `getMemberProfile` is code-complete but **was never
deployed** — the running auth-service still had the roster-only lookup, and the
owner has no `org_members` row, so it 403'd `not_your_org_member` and the screen
printed "This person is no longer part of your organization."

Two residual defects fixed here: `OrgCpoProfile` was registered **only** in
`AgentNavigator`, so the same avatar tap in a department chat was an unhandled
`NAVIGATE` (a dead tap) from the Messenger and CPO shells — now registered in
both. Deploy closes the rest.

## B-189 — the owner's presence dot flickered green/grey while genuinely online ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

`messenger.gateway.handleConnection` re-asserted `presence.set(uid,'online')`
only when `!superseded && onConnect() === first-device`. Nothing else in the
system can move a state key back up: `touch` only bumps TTLs,
`reassertLocalLeases` only rewrites the lease, and `sweepStale` is strictly
online→offline. So any moment the key went stale-`offline` while the socket was
genuinely up — a sweep racing a momentarily-missing lease, or an underflow
`onDisconnect` after the counter was reset — the user was painted grey until they
happened to background/foreground the app. And because the client pins
`signalDeviceId = 1`, **every** reconnect that raced the previous socket's
teardown landed in the `superseded` branch and skipped the re-assert, so this was
reachable on a single device.

**Fix:** the device COUNTER and the STATE key are now decoupled — the counter
still skips on a takeover (B-11), but a socket being open now always re-asserts
`online`. Clobbering a live `active`/`away` is safe: all three are non-offline and
the client re-sends its real activity on reconnect.

## B-190 — Incident queue: "Any status" label + filter rows folding ⚠️ P3 UI · FIXED

The status row read "Any status" while the severity row above it already read
"All". The severity row was a plain `View` of five `flex: 1` chips, which squeezed
"Critical" to an ellipsis on a narrow screen; and `statusScroll` was a fixed
`height: 44` while `statusRow` still carried `paddingBottom: 12`, leaving 32dp for
a chip that needs ~35 — so the chips were clipped top and bottom. Both rows now
scroll horizontally, never wrap, and the gap moved to `marginBottom` (outside the
fixed-height box).

## B-191 — the mission Ops Room never dissolved on completion ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

Dissolution existed only in `SettlementService.settleEscrowRelease`, which runs
after the **3-day** dispute window, only when `AUTO_DISPATCH_ENABLED`, and never
once `review_required` is set (LM-B3). The handler the CPO's "Finish" and the
agency's LM-C7 confirm actually funnel through — `completeMissionCore` — did
nothing at all. So the room outlived the mission for days, or forever.

**Fix:** `completeMissionCore` now archives the room (`archived_at` +
`archived_reason='mission_completed'`) right after the completion txn commits.
`ConversationsService.listMine` already filters `archived_at IS NULL`, and
`MessengerHomeScreen`'s server-reconciliation sweep then drops the local copy —
so it disappears from the **agency, client AND CPO** lists with no client change.
Metadata only: no key material, no epoch, no rekey. History survives for audit.

## B-192 — the assigned CPO was never a member of the Ops Room ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

`createMissionOpsRoom` was called with `crew_user_ids: []` and the CPO got only a
`dispatch_room_intents` add-intent — i.e. the **crypto** half. No
`conversation_members` row was ever written, and `listMine` is membership-joined,
so the room was invisible to the CPO — and `MessengerHomeScreen`'s prune
(`UUID_RE.test(localId) && !serverIds.has(localId)`) then **deleted** the room the
CPO had just been crypto-bootstrapped into. Managers were never added at all.

**Fix:** new `SystemMessengerService.ensureRoomMembers` seats the crew **and** the
org's active managers as metadata members, and an add-intent is enqueued for each
so the agency device still distributes the key. Both halves are required: seating
without the intent shows an undecryptable room; the intent without seating shows
nothing. The owner is already the room creator/admin — on this path the agency
company account IS the org.

## B-193 — Messenger open flashed every department channel into the list ⚠️ P3 UI · FIXED

`deptGroupIds` was `useState(() => new Set())` and only filled after a network
round-trip, so for ~one RTT every departmental channel rendered into the Messenger
list (and the header count jumped) before vanishing. The id set is now seeded from
the last successful fetch for the lifetime of the JS context, so re-opening
Messenger — the reported path — starts from the correct set.

## B-194 — saving a Region returned HTTP 400 ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

`setAgencyProfile` writes the **caller's own** `agents` row and rejects
`type !== 'company'`. A promoted manager is minted as a managed CPO
(`agents.type='cpo'`) and promotion only flips `org_members.member_role` — yet
`resolveAuthedRoute` sends them into the OWNER's shell, where `region` is in
`ALWAYS_VISIBLE_KEYS`. So every manager who tapped Save got
`agency_profile_is_company_only` with no way to succeed. It now resolves the org
the caller actually administers and writes that row.

The screen also read `Error.message` while Nest puts the reason in
`response.data.message`, so the user saw a bare "Request failed with status code
400" and the existing company-only branch could never match.

## B-195 — the composer hid under the keyboard on first entry ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

`useKeyboardHeight` seeded `useState(0)` and subscribed in an effect. `didShow`
fires **once**, at the end of the show animation — so a screen mounted while the
IME was already up (tapping a conversation row while the Messenger search field
holds focus) never got an event and never lifted. Backing out and re-entering
earns a fresh `didShow`, which is exactly the reported "works the second time".
The hook now seeds from `Keyboard.metrics()` and re-checks on mount.
`ChatScreen` carried an **inline duplicate** of the hook with the same race, so
every fix to the shared hook missed 1:1 chat — deleted.

Also fixed: both chat screens reserved `insets.bottom` on the composer bar **on
top of** the `kbHeight` already applied to the KeyboardAvoidingView, floating the
bar that far above the keyboard.

## B-196 — a manager could demote or remove the ORG OWNER 🔴 P1 SECURITY · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

`department_channel_members.role` is a two-value flag (`admin|viewer`) with **no
link to `org_members.member_role`**, and `syncMemberToOrgChannels` makes every
manager channel-`admin` on every org channel while the owner is a channel member
too. "Is a channel admin" was therefore the ONLY gate on `updateMemberRole` and
`removeMember`. Both preconditions hold by construction, so
`PATCH /department/channels/:id/members/<ownerId>/role {role:'viewer'}` from a
manager **succeeded** — as did deleting the owner from their own channel and
enqueuing a rekey that locks them out.

Worse: `ChannelMembersScreen`'s "Allow post" sends `role: 'admin'`, and admin is
the same flag that gates member management — so granting a CPO post access handed
that CPO the right to change **anyone's** access, including the owner's.

Separately, `OrgCpoService.setMemberStatus` used `actorId` only for the audit row
and `suspended_by`, never for authorization, so one manager could suspend or
remove a **peer manager** — revoking their sessions and stripping them from every
org channel. The owner was safe only by accident (no `org_members` row ⇒ the
UPDATE matched nothing ⇒ 400).

**Fix:** a rank model — owner 3, active manager 2, everyone else 1. Both channel
mutations now require the actor to **strictly outrank** the target
(`cannot_modify_org_owner` / `insufficient_rank_for_target`), with a fast path so
the org acting on its own channels stays one query. `setMemberStatus` refuses a
non-owner actor targeting the owner or any non-CPO. 6 new specs.

## B-197 — the department composer was a chunky two-row block ⚠️ P3 UI · FIXED

The **send button** (44dp), not the text field (pill `minHeight: 42`), set the row
height, and `alignItems: 'flex-end'` pushed all growth upward — leaving the dept
composer ~10dp taller than 1:1 chat before any content. Controls are now 38dp on a
centred row with `hitSlop` keeping the touch targets ≥ 44 (DESIGN_REVIEW_LOOP
§3.4), and `paddingTop` drops 10 → 6.

## B-198 — the manager dashboard showed different rating / jobs than the owner ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

`AgentDashboardScreen` bound both headline KPIs to `me.agent.*` from
`GET /agents/me` — a **self** endpoint returning `SELECT * FROM agents WHERE
user_id = $1`. But `rating` is only ever written against `assigned_provider_user_id`
(the org) and `jobs_total` counts completed **bookings** for the org versus crewed
**missions** for a CPO. A promoted manager therefore saw a null rating (`—`) and
their own personal mission count. `/org/summary` now also returns
`org_rating` / `org_jobs_total`, and the dashboard prefers them, falling back to
the self row for a lone officer.

B-188, B-189, B-191, B-192, B-194, B-196 and B-198 are **server-side**. The APK
alone will not show them fixed. B-189 needs `messenger-service`; the rest need
`auth-service`.

# Founder onboarding + duty batch — 2026-07-24 (evening) · B-199…B-204

Six items. All FIXED with gates green. **Server-side items (B-202 gate, B-203)
need the auth-service redeploy** to take effect.

## B-199 — CPO document-verification back buttons ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

Two navigation defects in the managed-CPO onboarding flow (`CpoOnboardingNavigator`,
which reuses the agency-wizard screens):

- **Docs-upload back was dead.** `AgentDocsUploadScreen` is the initial (only)
  route of that stack, so `canGoBack()` is false and it fell back to
  `replace('AgentAvailability')` — a route that stack never registers (only the
  agency `AgentNavigator` does), so React Navigation silently dropped it. All
  three affordances (chevron, gesture, hardware key) did nothing. Fix: when the
  linear previous step isn't in `navigation.getState().routeNames`, sign out
  (the only real "previous page" for a CPO who starts here) — the same terminal
  exit `AgentRejectedScreen` uses. The agency wizard path, where the target IS
  registered, is unchanged.

- **Post-submit screen was back-navigable and looped.** After submit the CPO
  lands on `AgentAdminApproval`, which had a back chevron → `AgentDocsUpload`
  (which re-showed a "submitted" state with a "Back to Approval Status" CTA) and
  a "Back to Dashboard" CTA, plus a live swipe gesture. So the CPO ping-ponged
  between two submitted-looking screens. Fix: it is now terminal — no header
  back, hardware/gesture back swallowed (`gestureEnabled:false` in both
  navigators + a `hardwareBackPress` → true handler), the "Back to Dashboard"
  CTA replaced with a plain "Sign out" (not a back, never loops). The 3 s poll
  still auto-advances to the CPO home the moment ops approves — "if ops approves
  the request he can enter." `AgentDocsUpload` also now redirects straight to
  the approval screen if it loads already-submitted, so the docs page can never
  re-appear as a second "submitted" page.

## B-200 — an unverified CPO appeared in the assign-crew list ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

A managed CPO is seeded `agents.status = DOCS_PENDING` and only becomes
deployable at `APPROVED`/`ACTIVE` (ops decision). The assign-crew sheet
(`OrgMissionsScreen`) filtered candidates on `status === 'active'` (the org
membership flag) only, so an unverified CPO showed as selectable. Fix: the
candidate filter now also requires `agent_status` ∈ {ACTIVE, APPROVED}. (The
server already rejected the assign with `cpo_not_approved_for_deployment`; this
stops them being offered.)

## B-201 — the assign-crew list showed managers/employees, not just CPOs ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

Same filter: it did not check `member_role`, so managers and enterprise
employees appeared as assignable guards. Fix: require `member_role === 'cpo'`.
(Server already rejected non-CPOs with `cpo_not_in_org`.)

## B-202 — an OFF-DUTY CPO could still be assigned a job 🔴 P1 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

The assign sheet's row even read "Off duty — can still be assigned", and the
server's `assignCrew` never checked `on_duty` — so an off-duty guard was
crewable. Fix, both halves: the client filter now requires `m.on_duty`, and
`assignCrew` rejects any selected CPO whose `agents.on_duty` is false with a new
`cpo_not_on_duty` (mapped to friendly copy). An off-duty guard toggling off
after the sheet opens is caught by the server gate.

## B-203 — the Org Chart green dot showed "app-connected", not "on duty" ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

B-184 made the org-chart dot reflect socket presence (online/away/offline). The
founder clarified the intent: the dot must mean **on duty** — an off-duty guard
with the app merely open was showing green and reading as available. Fix: the
`/org/hierarchy` node now carries `on_duty` (server: `agents.on_duty` joined per
member, plus the owner's own row), and the dot is green iff `on_duty`, grey
otherwise. The socket-presence subscription is removed entirely; the chart
re-fetches on focus so a duty toggle reflects on return. `on_duty` here is the
same availability signal the assign-crew gate uses, so the chart and the crew
sheet can never disagree.

## B-204 — the chat composer sat slightly BELOW the keyboard ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

`useKeyboardHeight` padded by `endCoordinates.height`. On edge-to-edge Android
(`edgeToEdgeEnabled=true`, so `adjustResize` is inert and the app draws to the
physical screen bottom) that height UNDER-reports by the navigation-bar inset,
so a bottom-anchored composer sat a nav-bar's height below the keys — partly
hidden. Fix: a new pure `keyboardOverlap(end, screenHeight)` measures the
keyboard's actual TOP edge (`screenY`) against the physical screen height and
takes the larger of that and the reported height ("dynamically catch where the
keyboard is", as asked), clamped to the screen, falling back to height when the
screen size is unknown. 6 unit tests; the screenY-preference is mutation-proven.

## B-207 — mission Ops Room: client invisible · manager keyless (no send/call/video) · founder wants HARD-DELETE on completion 🔴 P1 · FIXED + DEPLOYED

> Renumbered from the plan's tentative **B-205**: a parallel session on this branch
> had already taken B-205a/b/c (commit 93328e1) and B-206 (`remapConversation`). This
> Ops-Room trio is now **B-207** to keep the bug log unambiguous.

Founder-reported trio on the Lite bodyguard flow (client books → agency accepts →
crews): (1) the client never sees the mission group; (2) the agency's CPO manager
sees it but cannot message/voice/video; (3) on completion the group must **delete
itself for everyone — founder explicitly rejected archive** (supersedes the B-191
archive design).

Root causes (traced, no code changed — full plan with file:line in
`docs/handoffs/MISSION_OPS_ROOM_FIX_PLAN_2026-07-24.md`): the client is seated
only on FIRST room creation and `ensureRoomMembers` re-seats crew+managers but
never the client (`org-mission.service.ts:527-536`), and the client gets NO
`dispatch_room_intents` add-intent — its key delivery is a ONE-SHOT create
fan-out (`ensureAssignedGroup` short-circuits once the agency holds the key), vs
the CPOs' retried intent path. The manager is a metadata member but keyless:
`drainDispatchRoomIntents` runs from exactly one call site
(`AgentDashboardScreen.tsx:204-206`, company only), and the self-heal reshare
SILENTLY drops requesters not in the owner's crypto roster
(`reshareGroupKeyState` filter `productionRuntime.ts:2388-2389`) — every
send/call block is the same missing `masterKeyB64` behind fail-closed guards; the
relay/SFU are group-blind (not the blocker). Confounder: **the B-191/B-192 server
fixes (bd87f62) are ⚠️ UNDEPLOYED — probe the box first (plan §5)**; two of the
three symptoms may be partly already-fixed-but-undeployed. Fix shape: seat client
in ensureRoomMembers + client add-intent (server), widen drain triggers +
key-request→re-drain bridge (mobile, arch-nod owed), and replace archive with the
settlement-style hard delete (conversation+members+intents+broadcasts) at all
three completion boundaries. Regression tests owed with the fix per the B-143+
contract (founder directed: no code this session, plan doc only).

**FIXED 2026-07-24** (owner approved M2 + the Contabo deploy via AskUserQuestion):

- **S1+S2 (server)** — `org-mission.service.ts` assignCrew now seats the CLIENT in
  the `roomMembers` set (prepended) AND enqueues its add-intent, so the room is
  visible on every crew-assign/resume and the client's key delivery is retried
  (not one-shot). The mobile drain (`dispatchRoomIntents.ts`) benign-ACKs an
  ALREADY_MEMBER/NOT_A_MEMBER intent and skips `unknown group` (mirrors
  `membershipIntents.ts` D2-g/D2-e) so the client's intent never churns.
- **S3+S4 (server)** — new `SystemMessengerService.deleteMissionRoom` (one txn,
  6 idempotent statements: SET NULL back-refs → DELETE intents/members/broadcasts/
  conversation) REPLACES `archiveConversation` (deleted). Called at all three
  completion boundaries: `mission.service.complete()` + `abort()`, and INLINED in
  `agent.service.completeMissionCore` (can't inject SystemMessengerService —
  OpsModule imports AgentModule → DI cycle). Legacy `ops.service.completeBooking`
  left as-is (separate manual-booking path). settlement's delete is already
  idempotent → no-op on an already-deleted room.
- **M1 (mobile)** — company-owner-gated drain on MessengerHome FOCUS (+ the drain
  now has an `inFlight` coalescer). **Security:** `drainDispatchRoomIntents` now
  self-gates to `account_kind==='agency' && !is_org_manager` (== agent.type
  'company') because a keyless delegated manager resolves to the same org_user_id
  and running the drain there would make `ensureAssignedGroup` MINT a forking key
  (G-06).
- **M2 (mobile, arch-nod given)** — the owner's reshare handler, on a key-request
  from a user NOT in its crypto roster, fires the (owner-self-gated, debounced)
  `drainDispatchRoomIntents`. Adds NO key-flow authority — the roster gate in
  `reshareGroupKeyState` is untouched; the server intent queue stays the sole
  authorizer; it's a new TRIGGER for the existing authorized add path.
- **M3 (mobile)** — the MessengerHome prune of server-deleted rooms now also
  `removeGroupState` (evicts the cached master key), not just `removeConversation`.

Tests: `dispatchRoomIntents.test.ts` (+6 B-207 cases: owner-gate ×2, benign-ack ×2,
unknown-group skip, coalescer), `missionOpsRoomStaticScan.test.ts` (NEW — M2 + M3
source scans), auth specs updated (org-mission client seating+intent, system-messenger

## B-205a — group "X added Y" showed "Member bc9bc9" instead of the CPO's name ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

When a new CPO is created they're auto-added to every org channel via an E2EE
admin envelope that carries **no display name**, so the "X added Y" system line
was synthesized with the roster not yet hydrated and froze as
`Member <first-6-of-uuid>`. The row is cached by a deterministic id, so it stayed
wrong even after the real name loaded on focus.

Fix: the system membership/rename line now carries **structured event data**
(`event: {kind:'member_added', actorUserId, memberUserId}`) and the renderer
(`DepartmentChatScreen`) resolves names at RENDER time from the live
`groupMemberNames` — which the channel hydrates on focus from
`departmentApi.listMembers` (that DOES include the new CPO's display name). So the
line updates to the real name with no re-synthesis. `content` stays baked as a
fallback for old rows / backup mirrors. New render-time resolution tests in
`groupEventMessage.test.ts` (the auto-add "Member <code>" case + the live-resolve
case).

## B-205b — a manager was OFFERED access controls on the OWNER ⚠️ P2 SECURITY-UX · FIXED (⚠️ SERVER)

B-196 added the server rank gate (a manager modifying the owner 403s with
`cannot_modify_org_owner`), but `ChannelMembersScreen` still SHOWED "Make
viewer"/"Allow post"/remove on the owner's row, so a manager could tap it and it
looked possible (the server rejected, but the UX implied otherwise).

Fix: `listMembers` now returns a per-member `manageable` boolean, computed with
the SAME strict-outrank rule the mutations enforce (`orgRank` caller vs member,
owner short-circuits to rank 3). The screen hides the access + remove controls
when `manageable === false` — so a manager can no longer even tap them on the
owner or a peer manager. One source of truth (the server); `!== false` keeps the
controls when talking to an older server. New department-spec SEC cases (manager
can't manage owner / peer manager / self); mutation-proven.

## B-205c — dept chat scrolled off the newest message when the keyboard opened ⚠️ P3 UI · FIXED

`DepartmentChatScreen` uses a plain (non-inverted) `ScrollView`, so opening the
keyboard shrank the viewport from the bottom and hid the latest message until you
swiped — while `ChatScreen`'s inverted `FlatList` stays pinned to the newest for
free. That's why the founder saw it "only in departmental chat". Fix: scroll to

## B-206 — group key loss + owner "reactivate" WIPED the whole thread for everyone 🔴 P1 DATA-LOSS · FIXED

**Reported (founder):** if the owner (or a member) loses the group ENCRYPTION
KEY, reactivating the thread RESETS it for everyone — the old messages vanish.
Losing and regaining the key must NOT wipe history.

**Root cause (traced, confirmed NOT a delete and NOT a decryption failure):** the
messages are stored **plaintext** in SQLCipher (the group key is irrelevant to
reading them — the DB key is keychain-bound). When an owner opens a channel they
have no `masterKeyB64` for, the "Reactivate?" flow calls `resetGroup` (NULLs the
channel's `group_conversation_id` **server-side, for every member**) then
`ensureChannelProvisioned` → `createGroupChat` → `makeNewGroup`, which mints a
**brand-new random group id**. Every device then reads `messages[NEW_id]`
(empty) while the entire history sits intact under `messages[OLD_id]` — orphaned,
not deleted. Because the server id change propagates to all members, the history
"disappears" for everyone, exactly as reported. (The pure member-loses-key path
is safe — it self-heals with the SAME id via key-request → owner reshare.)

**Fix (store/DB remap — NOT a crypto change, so not arch-gated):** the history
now follows the channel to its new id. `sqlMessageStore.remapConversation(old,
new)` remaps the durable rows (`UPDATE OR IGNORE` on the `(conversation_id, id)`
PK + cleanup); `messengerStore.migrateConversationMessages(old, new)` folds the
in-memory rows (mirrors the B-18 synthetic→canonical fold, dedup by id/envelope);
`runtime.remapConversation` runs both. A **persisted** `deptGroupByChannel`
map (channel id → group id, per-owner vault) lets ANY device detect the change
(the resolved group id differs from the last-seen one) and migrate exactly once,
surviving a restart (the old-id rows still hydrate from SQLite). Wired into
`DepartmentChatScreen`'s focus resolve. New `deptChannelGroupRemap.test.ts` (5
cases: fold, dedup, one-shot detection, vault persistence, no-op guards),
mutation-proven.

**Residual flagged (not fixed here):** the "keep the SAME group id and rotate the
key in place" alternative would avoid the re-mint entirely but is CLAUDE.md
arch-gated (group id / epoch / create-gate) — escalate separately. Also the
readiness guard at `DepartmentChannelsScreen.tsx:121-128` is what stops the
Reactivate prompt firing on an ordinary mid-hydration login; if it regresses, the
owner could be pushed into the (now non-destructive) re-mint with no real key loss.

Gates: tsc 47 = baseline, messenger-crypto 2812 tests pass (the moving 1-suite
teardown failure is the known B-126 flake — a different suite each run, 0 failed
tests), app 3160, booking 189, lint 0 errors.

## B-184 — focused input: blind space on iOS, cut off on Android · ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (one global rule) · 2026-07-24

**Reported:** founder screenshots of the SAME chat composer on two devices — iOS showed a band
of empty screen between the composer and the top of the keyboard; Android showed the composer
sliced in half by the IME. Register: `docs/audits/KEYBOARD_INSET_AUDIT_2026-07-24.md`.
Device test plan: `docs/qa/KEYBOARD_UI_TEST_PLAN.md`. Rule doc: CLAUDE.md § "Keyboard / focused input".

**Root cause — one arithmetic error with two signs.** `endCoordinates.height` is not the same
quantity on the two platforms, and nothing in the app normalized it. Read out of the RN sources,
not inferred:

- **Android API >= 30** — `ReactRootView.checkForKeyboardEvents()` reports
  `imeInsets.bottom - systemBars().bottom`, i.e. RN REMOVES the nav-bar band the IME also covers.
  Under edge-to-edge (`edgeToEdgeEnabled=true`, mandatory on RN 0.81 / target SDK 36) our views run
  to the physical screen bottom, so every surface padded by that number under-lifts by exactly
  `insets.bottom` — 24 dp gesture / 48 dp 3-button. That IS the "cut down" screenshot.
  API < 30 takes `checkForKeyboardEventsLegacy()`, whose display-metrics delta already includes the
  bar — so the compensation has to be API-gated (minSdk is 24).
- **iOS** — `RCTKeyboardObserver` converts the keyboard frame to WINDOW coords, so `height` already
  spans the 34 pt home indicator. Surfaces that also padded `insets.bottom` stacked dead space under
  a keyboard that was already covering it.
- **`KeyboardAvoidingView` compounded it.** `_relativeKeyboardHeight` adds `keyboardVerticalOffset`
  to the padding one-for-one, and ChatScreen passed `insets.top + 10` -> ~69 pt of pure blind space
  on a notched iPhone, on top of the 34 pt above (~100 pt, matching the screenshot). Its `frame.y`
  is `onLayout` (PARENT-relative), so nested KAVs are silently wrong; `behavior=undefined` (the
  app-wide Android idiom, 12+ screens) does NOTHING; `behavior="height"` leaves ghost space.
- **No single owner.** Five idioms coexisted (KAV padding / KAV height / KAV + manual pad / bare
  manual pad / a hand-rolled listener in `NextOfKinModal`), nine surfaces gated the manual pad on
  `Platform.OS === 'android'` and four did not. B-84 fixed the SYMPTOM on 17 screens without
  unifying the ARITHMETIC — which is why the class returned.

**Fix — one global rule, everyone inherits it.** New `src/hooks/useKeyboardLayout.ts`:
`computeKeyboardOverlap()` (pure, platform-explicit) + `useKeyboardOverlap` / `useKeyboardLayout`
/ `useKeyboardBottomPad` / `useRevealOnKeyboard`. The rule: **the bottom-most element of a surface
owns the keyboard inset** and pads by `bottomPad(gap)`, which REPLACES the safe-area inset while
the IME is up (never stacks); a container that lifts a column uses `overlap`; a child inside an
already-lifted container uses `safeBottom + gap`. 30 surfaces migrated, `src/hooks/useKeyboardHeight.ts`
deleted, and `KeyboardAvoidingView` no longer exists anywhere in `src/`. `KeyboardAvoidingScreen`
was rebuilt on the rule and gained a `footer` slot (its docstring had promised for months that a
pinned CTA rides above the keyboard while the code rendered it outside the box).

**Regression contract:** `src/hooks/__tests__/useKeyboardLayout.test.tsx` (23 — the arithmetic on
iOS / Android >=30 / Android <30, the API-30 boundary, floating-keyboard + Reduce-Motion quirks,
noise floor, listener cleanup, replace-not-stack) and `src/hooks/__tests__/keyboardContract.test.ts`
(40 — bans KAV, `keyboardVerticalOffset`, any second `Keyboard.addListener`, `kbHeight`, and the
revived `Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined` branch; asserts all 30 inheritors still
import the rule; pins the ChatScreen composer specifically). Mutation-proved: reverting the composer
to `insets.bottom + 8` and neutralising the Android compensation turned 6 tests RED, green on restore.

**Gates:** 63/63 new tests green; app project 44 suites / 381 tests green; booking 166 green; messenger-crypto green x2
(flake rule); tsc 47 = baseline; eslint 0 errors on all touched files.

**Residual:** (1) Android emits NO event when the IME resizes while already open (API >= 30 fires
only on a visibility transition), so letter-keyboard -> emoji-panel holds the old height until
dismiss; closing that needs `react-native-keyboard-controller` (WindowInsetsAnimation) — a
dependency decision, not a UI diff. Tracked as test-plan case K4. (2) **Device verification PENDING**
— no device attached this session; Tier 1 = Pixel 7a on gesture AND 3-button nav plus one
home-indicator iPhone.

### Group add-member (ask #1a)

- **B-221 (P1, ARCH-GATED) — no request/approval mechanism exists anywhere.** Current model: adds
  are **admin-only at every authoritative layer**, and E2EE "admin" = **only the group creator**
  (`makeNewGroup` marks one admin; **no promote action** in `GroupAdminAction`). Send gate
  `productionRuntime.addGroupMember` throws `NOT_ADMIN` (~:4766, since `a88e9de`); receiver
  `applyAdminAction` (`groupClient.ts:483-489`) **silently no-ops** any non-admin add + epoch guard
  (the `applyGroupAdmin.ts:386` member/admin check is telemetry-only, computed after the drop);
  server `POST /conversations/:id/members` → `requireAdmin`; local sha256 groups never touch the
  server. **The live "Corné … added Member 613949" bubble is this working as coded — Corné is that
  group's sole E2EE admin/creator; no non-member/removed-member add hole exists.** The gap: no
  request/approve/pending variant anywhere (repo-wide greps empty); `pendingAdminActionStore` is
  epoch-order replay, `conversation_membership_intents` is a POST-authorization drain — neither is
  approval. **Design (do not implement without arch sign-off — master-key distribution is a
  stop-condition):** non-admin raises an **inert** `add-request` E2EE action (local groups) or an
  `awaiting_approval` intent (UUID convos); **rekey + `reshareGroupKeyState` fire only at approval
  time** or the invitee gets the master key before approval; and the design must pick its authority
  (E2EE owner-only vs server-promotable admin — the drain already breaks on that mismatch).

**Device:** Pixel 6a (`29271JEGR00258`), v1.0.131/vc159, 2026-07-24. Founder reproduced the group
"No sound" complaint (Jack Bravo + Corné both reported it in-chat). **Capture:**
`bravo_groupcall_log_110924.txt` (repo root, 18 min, 3 calls). **Constraint:** this release build's
JS logs go to Firebase, not logcat, and the native SFrame module logs nothing — analysis is off the
native WebRTC/audio layer.

**Evidence (all pid 7231):**

- Two voice calls (11:09:56 ~14s, 11:11:05 ~12s): mic capture healthy (`WebRtcAudioRecordExternal`
  `startRecording`, `VOICE_COMMUNICATION`, `verifyAudioConfig: PASS`, AEC+NS on), playout healthy
  (`WebRtcAudioTrackExternal startPlayout`, `VOICE_CALL volume 15/15`, **underrun 0**) — but
  **`InCallManager` routed both input and output to Bluetooth SCO `Stone 620`**
  (`AS.AudioDeviceBroker … type:bt_sco_hs name:Stone 620`, `setBluetoothScoOn: true`). If nobody is
  on the paired BT device, both ends go silent (its mic becomes the call mic). Explains the 11:07
  "No sound" call (same conditions two min earlier).
- **Suspected dead speaker toggle:** at 11:10:17 `InCallManager: setSpeakerphoneOn(): true` +
  `setCommunicationRouteForClient … type:speaker`, but the very next `updateCommunicationRoute`
  reverted `preferredCommunicationDevice: bt_sco_hs Stone 620` — the route did **not** move to
  speaker while SCO was active (legacy `setSpeakerphoneOn` loses to an active SCO device on Android
  12+; needs `setCommunicationDevice(speaker)` / `clearCommunicationDevice`). Not fully isolated —
  the toggle line sits inside call teardown, so it may be cleanup not a user tap.
- Group **video** call (11:19:08→): media fully up — remote audio+video consumers created (incl.
  `probator`), peer frames rendered repeatedly, camera streaming, mic unmuted, no BT drop — routed
  to `realme Buds Wireless 3`. Capture cut when the USB cable was unplugged at 11:27, so **clean
  teardown of this call was not observed** (relevant to the B-68 zombie-FGS class).

**Likely product bug:** the call UI gives no indication audio is on a Bluetooth device, and (to
confirm) no working way to force it back to speaker/earpiece — any paired speaker/buds left on
silently eats the whole call. **Confirmation step PENDING:** Bluetooth-off retest (one short group
voice call) + verify the in-call speaker toggle actually moves the route with BT on. Jack's/Corné's
"No sound" may be the same on their phones — ask if they had a BT device connected. Jack's "typing
bar still under phone menu" is a separate composer/overlap UI item (relates to the B-184 keyboard
class) — triage separately.

### B-237 (P1) — "no sound" in Omnidevx = SFrame **epoch fork**, not audio

**Mechanism (all code-verified):**

- Group **text** encrypts with the master key only (`broadcastToGroup` →
  `groupEncrypt(masterKeyB64, …)`, `packages/messenger-core/src/groups/groupClient.ts:167`) —
  **epoch-independent**.
- Group **call** media keys derive per **(masterKey, epoch, participantTag)**
  (`frameCryptorOrchestrator.ts` → `deriveParticipantKey(masterKeyB64, epoch, tag)`,
  `epochToKeyIndex`) and SFrame **fails closed** — wrong epoch ⇒ frames dropped ⇒ pure silence,
  both directions, per member pair.
- Every `add`/`remove`/`rename`/`leave` **bumps epoch by 1 without changing the master key**
  (`groupClient.ts:488-530`), and the reducer **drops any action whose `atEpoch !== state.epoch`**
  — a member who misses ONE admin envelope is stranded on the old epoch **forever**: text keeps
  working (same master key), every group call is mutually silent vs. up-to-date members.
- Heal exists ONLY when the **group owner** hosts a call (owner re-broadcasts `create` @ current
  epoch — laggards accept; `productionRuntime.ts:5064-5099`). A **non-owner host** takes the
  "reuse real-group key, no fan-out" path (`productionRuntime.ts:5120-5125`) — nothing heals.

**Field fit:** per B-221 (2026-07-24), **Corné is the sole E2EE admin/creator** of this group and a
live **"Corné … added Member 613949"** bubble was captured — a **recent add = recent epoch bump** in
a group the founder does NOT own. The founder's calls (both today's calls were founder-hosted,
`from=3165d0e1`) can never heal stranded members. Founder's ">7 members breaks it" observation =
the group that recently ADDED members (crossing 7) is the group with the epoch fork; the small
static group works. Text in the group renders fine on all devices (Corné's "Yes." bubble) —
exactly the discriminating symptom. This is the production recurrence of the **B-10** epoch-mismatch
class (2026-06-07, emulators).

**Founder-reported correlation (2026-07-24, post-session):** "the problem happens when more members
join." Consistent with the mechanism: every JOIN (add) bumps the epoch, so each join is another
chance for a member to miss the envelope and fork; the probability a given call contains ≥1 forked
member grows with every roster addition. Note the two readings both fit: (a) group grows → fork
likelihood grows; (b) a big CALL is silent while a small one works because the forked member(s) are
present only in the big call. Probe idea: call #1 targets minus call #2 targets = {08782d6d
(no-token test acct), 88d34848, 79d63649} — but call #2 was a DIFFERENT group (different master
key), so this narrows suspects only weakly; the member-by-member "who can hear whom" matrix
(confirmation step 3) is the clean discriminator.

**Founder-device evidence (call #1):** native audio fully healthy — `WebRtcAudioRecordExternal
startRecording` + `verifyAudioConfig: PASS`, `WebRtcAudioTrackExternal startPlayout`, teardown
`underrun count: 0`. Media/decrypt is above the native layer; release-build JS (SFrame/epoch) logs
go to Firebase, not logcat — epoch values not directly observable on this build.

**Confirmation steps (any one suffices):**

1. Have **Corné (owner) host** a call in the same group with everyone online: if sound works for
   members that were silent on founder-hosted calls (owner-create heal fires), fork confirmed.
2. Debug/staging build on ANY complaining member: look for `[group-admin] dropped … stale-epoch
action=X state=Y` lines and compare `epoch` across two members' stores.
3. Matrix probe: ask each member who they can hear — an epoch fork predicts a clean bipartition
   (old-epoch members hear each other; new-epoch members hear each other; silence across).

**Files involved:** `packages/messenger-core/src/groups/groupClient.ts` (epoch bump / stale drop),
`src/modules/messenger/webrtc/frameCryptorOrchestrator.ts` (epoch-derived keys),
`src/modules/messenger/runtime/productionRuntime.ts:4990-5130` (owner-only resync),
`src/modules/messenger/runtime/applyGroupAdmin.ts` (stale-epoch stash telemetry — JS-only logs).
**Fix direction (for dev, NOT implemented):** epoch-agnostic heal (e.g. periodic owner state
re-broadcast, or accept owner-signed create at ≥ epoch on call join), and/or call-time key
advertisement so a mismatch is detected and surfaced ("member X has stale keys") instead of silent
frame drops. Master-key distribution is a CLAUDE.md stop-condition → arch review required.
