### B-237 ROOT-CAUSE REFINED (code-verified, 2026-07-24) — the heal ALREADY exists; the live cause is version skew

After reading the actual key path end-to-end, the picture is sharper and **the "key-heal" the founder
approved is already implemented in the current build (vc164)** — writing more key-distribution code is
NOT the fix, and weakening the guards would re-open B-124/B-125.

**What the code actually does (all in vc164 HEAD):**

- SFrame key = `HKDF(masterKey, salt="bravo-fc-v1", info="epoch="+epoch_be32+"|p="+tag)`, keyIndex =
  `epoch & 0x0F` (`packages/messenger-core/src/calls/frameCryptorKeys.ts`). So any `(masterKey, epoch)`
  disagreement ⇒ different key ⇒ **silent fail-closed**. Confirmed.
- A real-group **add bumps epoch WITHOUT rotating the master key** (`groupClient.ts:488`), so an
  Omnidevx-style fork (adds only) is **epoch-only**, same master key.
- On group-call start the **host calls `ensureCallGroupKey`** (`useGroupCall.ts:1550`). For a group the
  host **owns**, that **re-broadcasts the authoritative state as an owner-signed `create`**
  (`productionRuntime.ts:5064-5100`).
- The receiver's create gate (`inboundGroupCreateGate.ts decideGroupCreate`) **ACCEPTS** a behind-epoch
  owner-signed create (case f, normal advance) and heals a same-epoch different-key fork (case e, G-04)
  — so **a behind-member IS healed** by an owner-hosted call, on a build that has this gate.

**So why did the field owner(Corné)-hosted heal still fail (18:41)?** The heal fires only when the
**owner** hosts (a non-owner host takes the no-rebroadcast reuse path, `productionRuntime.ts:5120`) — and
it only lands if BOTH the host AND the stranded members run a build new enough to have the resync +
B-41/B-127 accepting gate (all ~2026-07-17…21). **The A/B already proved builds are individually capable
(the fresh group worked with the same people), but a fresh group uses the keyless-BOOTSTRAP accept path
that ANY FrameCryptor build has — it does NOT exercise the resync-over-a-live-key heal path.** So the
consistent explanation is **version skew**: some members (added to these groups over weeks) are on
older APKs that do fresh calls fine but cannot process the resync-heal of an already-forked group.

**Consequences for the fix:**

1. **No new crypto code fixes the live broken groups.** The heal is present in vc164; the blocker is
   distribution. **Proven operational fix: get everyone onto the current APK + recreate the affected
   groups** (both already confirmed working today).
2. **Do NOT weaken the create-gate guards** (`stale-epoch` / `superseded-key` / `owner-changed` drops)
   to force-heal edge flavors — those are the exact B-124/B-125 / MEDIUM-2 rollback defenses. Declined
   even under founder approval; the evidence doesn't implicate them and weakening re-opens data loss.
3. **The silent-epoch-fork is not JS-detectable** (both sides hold _a_ key and proceed; only the native
   FrameCryptor decrypt-failure would reveal the mismatch, and it isn't surfaced to JS) — so a "keys out
   of sync" banner can only catch the _no-key_ timeout case, not the _wrong-key_ silence.
4. **Safe, additive code improvement available (optional):** make the **owner re-broadcast the
   authoritative state when they JOIN, not only when they HOST** a group call — closes the
   "non-owner-hosted call never heals" gap for updated clients (uses the existing accepting gate; no
   guard change). Marginal for the founder's own groups (he isn't the owner) but a correct robustness win.

**Bottom line:** the highest-confidence fix is distribution (update everyone + recreate), NOT a crypto
change. Debug-build capture of a broken member's `(build, epoch, masterKey)` is still the only way to
confirm the exact flavor if a deeper heal is ever pursued.

### B-240 (P3 UI) — raw server throttle error rendered as a red chat banner

Screenshot 18:22 (+06): banner `Error: rate_limited: event typing rate-limited; retry in 32ms` above
the Omnidevx chat. Server `typing` budget is 2/s, capacity 10 (`ws-rate-limiter.ts DEFAULT_WS_LIMITS`);
the client's typing emitter can exceed it while typing fast, and the resulting `{code:'rate_limited'}`
error frame is surfaced verbatim. Client should debounce typing below 2/s and route `rate_limited`
on cosmetic events to a silent drop, never a user-facing error string.

## MENTIONS · EDIT · DELETE-FOR-EVERYONE + messenger safe-area sweep · 2026-07-25 · SHIPPED

Feature work, not a bug report — logged here because it lands new receive lanes on the
message pipeline and changes the M10 exit census, and because the padding sweep found
five latent UI defects that would otherwise never have been written down.

### What shipped

| Feature                  | Wire                                                           | Gate                                                 |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| **@-mentions in groups** | `SealedPayload.mentions: [{userId,label}]`                     | label-matched, longest-first (prefix-collision safe) |
| **Edit sent message**    | `SealedPayload.edit: {targetMsgId, body, editedAt, mentions?}` | author-only, 15-min sender window                    |
| **Delete for everyone**  | `SealedPayload.deleteFor: {targetMsgId, deletedAt}`            | author-only, 48-h sender window                      |

Schema **v18**: `messages.mentions_json` / `edited_at` / `deleted_for_all`, plus a new
`pending_mutations` stash table.

### The security shape (read before touching it)

Edit and delete are **1:1-pairwise-encrypted CONTROL envelopes carrying a group routing
hint** — the same shape as reactions (MSG-02), and the same shape that went months without
a membership gate (B-128). They are strictly more dangerous than a reaction because they
REWRITE or DESTROY rather than decorate, so `runtime/messageMutationGate.ts` fails closed:

1. blocked peer → drop 2. non-member → drop 3. **target absent → STASH, never drop**
2. target is OUR row → drop 5. **sender ≠ target author → drop** 6. tombstoned → drop
3. edit not newer than the applied one → drop

Rule 5 is the property the whole feature rests on: `fromUserId` is authenticated by the
Signal session + sender cert upstream, so binding to `target.sender_id` means a member can
only ever mutate their own posts.

**AAD is UNCHANGED** — these ride the same bare `{to, ts}` stamp reactions use. Widening it
is a CLAUDE.md stop-condition, so **B-128 part 2 applies to these envelopes too**: the
conversation/group checks in `verifySealedAad` are inert for them, and rules 4–6 are
receiver-STATE enforcement, not a cryptographic binding. Do not treat them as a substitute.

Rule 3 is not politeness: the receive path ACKs before the gate runs, so a dropped delete
means the recipient renders retracted content **forever**. A group's text is master-key
encrypted and can sit in `pending_group_envelopes` while the pairwise directive sails
through — that is the reachable case, and it is why `pending_mutations` exists.

### M10 exit census 11 → 13 (deliberate)

Two new bare returns, one per receive lane. Classified: **accept** on applied/stashed,
**destroy** on every gate rejection — `runMutationEnvelope` calls `noteDestroyedEnvelope`
for those, so the sender is acked `discarded` rather than shown a false ✓✓ (W11's rule,
B-128's precedent). Updated in `receivePersistenceInvariants.test.ts` with the reasoning.

### Padding sweep — five latent defects found (all fixed)

| #    | Screen                                                                          | Defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P-01 | `FloatingCallOverlay`                                                           | `paddingTop: 44` hard-coded — an iPhone-notch constant. ~20px dead space on a 24dp Android status bar; too SHORT on a tall cutout, where the title collided with the clock. Never read insets at all.                              |
| P-02 | `CallScreen` ×3, `GroupCallScreen` ×3, `VaultScreen`, `DepartmentChatScreen` ×3 | Bottom sheets used a fixed `paddingBottom`, so the last row sat under the gesture pill — where the touch target also competes with the system back-swipe. `ChatScreen` already did this correctly; the module had two conventions. |
| P-05 | `VaultOTPVerifyScreen`                                                          | The only `KeyboardAvoidingScreen` caller in the module omitting `insets.bottom` (both siblings had it) — Verify button under the gesture bar.                                                                                      |
| P-06 | `VaultLockScreen`, `VaultNewPinScreen`                                          | PIN keypad is the bottom-most element with **no** bottom inset; the fingerprint/0/backspace row sat on the screen edge.                                                                                                            |
| P-08 | `FileVaultPurchaseScreen`                                                       | Registered `headerShown: false` with **no safe-area handling at all** — the "‹ Back" control B-98b added to keep the paywall escapable rendered under the status bar.                                                              |

`GroupCallScreen`'s in-call-chat sheet also had the wrong keyboard API: its column is
already lifted by `overlap`, so the composer inside owes `safeBottom` (0 while the IME is
up), not a raw inset — stacking them is the iOS blind space.

Pinned by `messengerSafeAreaSweep.test.ts`, which enforces the class mechanically so a new
screen inherits it: no magic notch constants (34/44/47/59), every `*Sheet` style with a
fixed `paddingBottom` must be inset-composed at its render site, every headerless screen
with a back control reads `insets.top`, and no screen reads `insets.top` then ignores the
bottom (centered layouts exempt).

### Tests — 148 new across 9 suites

`mentionEditDeleteWire` (25, incl. bounds + unknown-key rejection) · `mentionEditDeletePersistence`

### B-243 (P1) — "no audio heard in audio/video calls" = the two call stacks fight over ONE audio session

**Reported:** founder, 2026-07-25 — no audio in audio _or_ video calls.

**Mechanism (code-verified, both halves):** the device has exactly one
InCallManager audio session, but two independent stacks reach for it —
1:1 (`callRegistry.ts` + `CallScreen.tsx`) and group/SFU
(`groupCallRegistry.ts` + `GroupCallScreen.tsx`). Neither knew the other
existed, and it broke in **both** directions:

1. **`endActiveCall` stopped the session unconditionally.** Any stale or
   late 1:1 teardown — a missed call cleaning up, a `call.hangup` frame for
   a call that had already ended — called `InCallManager.stop()` while a
   **group call was live**. Symptom matches the report exactly: Ops Room
   joined, tiles rendering, video fine, nobody audible.

2. **`endActiveGroupCall` never stopped it at all.** This is the _mirror of
   CALL-N5_, which landed in `endActiveCall` on 2026-07-02 and was never
   carried across. `GroupCallScreen`'s audio-effect cleanup is the only
   other place that stops the session, and it **cannot run while the screen
   is unmounted** (call minimized). So ending a minimized group call from
   the floating overlay left the device pinned in `MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`:
   routing stuck on the earpiece, the media-volume slider inert, and the
   next call started on top of a session that was never torn down.

Both present to a user as "no call audio", which is why they were fixed
together. Note this is a _session/routing_ bug — it is NOT the SFrame epoch
fork of B-237, and not the ring-delivery gap of B-239. A call can be fully
established, decrypting, and rendering video and still be silent.

**Fix (`bfc61bd`):** new `src/modules/messenger/runtime/callAudioSession.ts`
owns one rule — _stop the shared session only when nobody else owns a call_ —
and all four stop sites route through `stopSharedAudioSession(owner)`. The
caller's **own** registry slot is deliberately not consulted: callers invoke
this mid-teardown when their slot may not be cleared yet, and consulting it
would recreate half 2. Lazy `require`s throughout, because both registries
require the arbiter and a top-level import would be a cycle.

**Files:** `runtime/callAudioSession.ts` (new), `runtime/callRegistry.ts`,
`runtime/groupCallRegistry.ts`, `screens/messenger/CallScreen.tsx`,
`screens/messenger/GroupCallScreen.tsx`.

**Regression test:** `__tests__/callAudioSessionArbitration.test.ts` — 14
tests. 6 are behavioural (the arbiter is pure TS with lazy requires, so it
unit-tests for real); 8 are source scans, because the registries and both
screens load native modules the node project cannot. **Mutation-proved: 6 go
red on pre-fix code**, including the CALL-N5 mirror. The scan also bans a bare
`InCallManager.stop()` at all four sites, so a future direct call cannot
silently bypass the arbitration.

**Gates:** `messenger-crypto` 3279 passed on runs 1/4/5/6 — runs 2/3 failed
with the known **B-126** moving-teardown signature and never named this suite;
`app --testPathPattern screens/messenger` 126 passed; typecheck 47 = baseline.

**⚠️ Device QA owed** — this is an audio-routing change and only a real handset
can confirm it. Minimum matrix: (a) 1:1 call → end → immediately join a group
call, audio present both ways; (b) join a group call, **minimize**, end from the
floating overlay, then play any media — volume slider must control media, not
call; (c) group call live while a stale 1:1 hangup lands — group audio must
survive; (d) voice and video, speaker and earpiece, on both BlueStacks and the
phone.

### B-244 (P3, UX request) — dept chat: paint the whole bubble in the sender's colour

**Requested:** founder, 2026-07-25 — each sender already gets a stable colour,
but it only tinted the name; the whole incoming message should carry it,
"and make sure the contrast, some color dont go with white text or black text".

**The non-obvious half.** Choosing the colour is trivial; painting the bubble
breaks **every foreground nested inside it**, all of which were tuned for the
old `#18202F` surface. Re-based: body text, `@mentions` (both hues —
`#A9C5FF` and `#E2C893` — vanish on a pastel, so the mention signal moved to an
underline and a self-mention keeps its rank via a scrim pill), the reply quote
strip (`rgba(255,255,255,0.04)` is invisible on a pastel), `LinkPreviewCard`
and the attachment card (both carry their own dark palette → given a dark
plate rather than forking a component shared with `ChatScreen`), and the
white top sheen (a glass edge on dark, a stray band on saturated).

**Worth recording:** all six `ROLE_COLORS` resolve to **near-black** — the
palette is uniformly light, so the white branch is never exercised today. The
choice is computed anyway, and pinned by a dark-colour test, because the moment
someone adds a dark entry a hardcoded `'#0B0F17'` ships black-on-black.

**Fix (`8dd0bbe`):** `textOnColor` / `colorForSender` / `scrimOn` extracted to
`src/screens/messenger/senderColors.ts` — `DepartmentChatScreen` imports
`expo-clipboard` and `rn-emoji-keyboard`, which the Jest transform cannot
parse, so anything defined inside it is reachable only by a source scan. Out
there they get real unit tests. Announcements and own messages are excluded
from the paint.

**Regression test:** `screens/messenger/__tests__/deptChatBubbleContrast.test.ts`
— 24 tests, WCAG AA (4.5:1) asserted for every palette entry plus colours the
author never saw. Mutation-proved. Device QA owed (contrast is a screen
judgement).

### B-245 (P2 UI) — bottom-anchored CTAs and FABs double-count the tab-bar inset

**Reported:** founder, 2026-07-25 — screenshots of a large dead black gap
under bottom buttons, plus a FAB sitting on top of list content.

**Mechanism (one root cause for all three screenshots).**
`@react-navigation/bottom-tabs` lays the scene container and the tab bar out
as **siblings** in a column — the scene does _not_ extend under the bar, its
bottom edge **is** the top of the bar. `ObsidianTabBar` then pads _itself_ by
`insets.bottom`. So a footer inside a tabbed screen that adds
`Math.max(insets.bottom, 12)` reserves the system nav bar **twice**:

| Screen                                       | Was                                            | Effect                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `LocationPickerScreen` (SELECT DROP-OFF)     | `paddingBottom: Math.max(insets.bottom,12)+12` | ~60dp gap under CONFIRM LOCATION    |
| `OpsRoomReviewScreen` (BRAVO CONTROL REVIEW) | same formula                                   | ~60dp gap under the waiting CTA     |
| `BookingHomeScreen`                          | `bottom: insets.bottom + 72`                   | FAB ~120dp up, over RECENT BOOKINGS |

On a 3-button-nav Android phone `insets.bottom` is ~48dp — the exact size of
the gap in the photos. On gesture nav it is ~24dp and the result looks nearly
fine, which is why it shipped.

**Fix (`d25cbde`):** new `src/hooks/useBottomInset.ts` — the tab-bar
counterpart of `useKeyboardLayout` (B-184), stating the same rule for the same
reason: _something below you already owns that space_, so **`bottomPad()`
REPLACES the inset, it never stacks on it**.

```ts
const {bottomPad, contentBottom} = useBottomInset();
// footer / CTA / FAB → bottomPad(gap)      scroll content → contentBottom(gap)
```

`ObsidianTabBar` reports its own visibility through a **module-level count**,
not React context — it is a _sibling_ of the scenes, so it cannot provide
context to them. A count rather than a boolean because a shell swap
(root → CPO → departmental, all of which render `ObsidianTabBar`) mounts the
new bar **before** unmounting the old; a boolean would flash `false` and every
footer in the app would jump by the inset mid-transition.

**Scope — the sweep is now COMPLETE (`bf3be06`).** The first pass converted only
the three screens with photographic evidence; the follow-up swept the remaining
36 anchored sites across 35 more files (agent, booking, cpo, liveops, news, ops,
pro, vbg, wallet) — 38 screens pinned in total. The rest were deliberately not swept
blind: each surface needs a look at whether a tab bar is actually below it
(fullscreen map and messenger routes set `tabBarStyle:{display:'none'}`, and
those screens _must_ keep owning the inset themselves — converting them
blindly would clip content behind the nav bar, the opposite failure and just
as bad). Candidates to audit next: everything matching
`(paddingBottom|bottom):\s*[^,}]*insets\.bottom` outside the messenger tree.

**Regression tests:** `src/hooks/__tests__/useBottomInset.test.tsx` (11) —
`computeBottomBase` is pure, so the tabbed _and_ standalone cases are asserted
in one run, same reason `computeKeyboardOverlap` is pure. Plus
`bottomInsetContract.test.ts` (11) — line-based scanning because these files
are **CRLF** and a `\n`-anchored regex passes vacuously; the scan **self-tests
against the pre-fix shape** so it cannot rot into a no-op.

**Two pre-existing assertions reversed, not deleted.**
`fixedOverlayInsets.test.ts` pinned the literal `Math.max(insets.bottom, 12)`.
Its _intent_ was right ("derived from the CTA bar, not a magic number") but the
arithmetic was the bug, so both assertions were rewritten in place with the
history in a comment, per the bug-regression contract.

**Gates:** app 516 passed, booking 446 passed, typecheck 47 = baseline, eslint
clean.

**⚠️ Device QA owed:** Pixel-class **3-button nav AND gesture nav**, plus a
home-indicator iPhone. This is inset arithmetic and the two Android navigation
modes differ by precisely the term at issue — testing one proves nothing about
the other.

### B-246 (P1) — find-by-number says "no account found" for accounts that exist

**Reported:** founder, 2026-07-25 — _"if search with number to message someone
I can't do that, it says no account found on Bravo. I can't find that person to
message."_

**Mechanism.** 7 of 143 rows predate E.164 normalisation at registration and
store the number in NATIONAL format. `lookupByPhones` does an exact
`WHERE u.phone_e164 = ANY($1)`, so the searcher types the _correct_
`+8801878547473`, the client normalises it correctly, and the lookup returns
nothing:

| Row                                        | Display name | Note                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `01878547473`                              | Arif         | BD                                 |
| `01521562457`                              | Arif         | BD                                 |
| `0507356048`                               | John Deer    | **ambiguous** — UAE or Saudi       |
| `0726366878`                               | Jo Jo        | **ambiguous** — South Africa or UK |
| `00000000000` / `123456789` / `1234567890` | —            | junk                               |

`home_region` is populated for **exactly one** user, so it is useless as a
country fallback — which is why converting the data was not the fix.

**⚠️ The trap, found by querying the live table BEFORE writing the fix.**
A naive "also compare national significant numbers" fallback returns the
**wrong person**:

```
0507356048 (John Deer)      collides with  +971507356048 (Ranger Danger)
123456789  (Ranger Big Man) collides with  +971123456789 (Spring Bok)
```

In an app where the wrong recipient means a leaked message, that is strictly
worse than the bug being fixed.

**Fix (`bf3be06`).** Server: `lookupLegacyNationalFormat` compares national
significant numbers, but

1. **only for candidates that matched NOTHING exactly** — an exact hit always
   wins, so a correct number can never resolve to someone else;
2. **per-candidate, not per-batch** — the contact sweep sends hundreds of
   numbers at once, and a batch-level rule would keep legacy contacts invisible
   to everyone who has at least one normal contact;
3. **only against rows that are themselves malformed** (`phone_e164 !~ '^\+'`),
   so well-formed rows keep strict exact matching;
4. with an **8-digit floor**, so a typo cannot reach the junk rows;
5. re-applying the two-sided block filter, the caller exclusion and
   `deleted_at IS NULL` — the rescue is a second query and would otherwise be a
   way around the block list.

Needs no country attribution, so the two genuinely ambiguous rows are handled
without guessing. **Self-healing**: matches nothing once the rows are
normalised.

Client (`NewChatScreen.startChatByNumber`): send the NATIONAL form alongside
the E.164 one, and stop hard-failing when no calling code can be derived — a
searcher whose OWN phone is one of those 7 rows got `undefined` from
`regionFromOwnPhone` and had every local number rejected before any request was
made. An exact E.164 hit is preferred over a national one, and the own-number
guard is backed by a userId check now that `e164` can be null.

**Regression tests:** `users.service.spec.ts` +9 (16 total) — including the
collision case asserting the fallback query is **never issued** when the number
matched exactly. `lookupByNumberCandidates.test.ts` +7 (source scan;
NewChatScreen mounts RN + a Modal).

**Gates:** auth-service 16 passed + typecheck 0; messenger-crypto 3286 twice;
app 587; booking 446; typecheck 47 = baseline.

**⚠️ Device QA owed:** search Arif's legacy row by its correct E.164 (must
find him) **and** search `+971507356048` (must resolve to Ranger Danger, never
John Deer).

### B-247 (P1, FIXED in two parts — `1835904` then `ed21398`) — mission Ops Room call rings nobody but the client

> **PART 2 (`ed21398`, 2026-07-25).** The first fix closed only the
> AGENCY-initiated direction and was reported still-broken. `rosterUserIds` had
> exactly one writer, `ensureAssignedGroup` — the agency path that mints the
> master key. A CPO never runs it (their room arrives through
> `upsertGroupConversationFromState`, the single receive-side writer, which set
> no roster), so a CPO device still fell back to crypto membership: the
> "CPO calls → agent/manager don't ring" half was untouched.
>
> Compounding it, every source in the ring set is a SNAPSHOT:
> `ensureAssignedGroup` early-returns once a key exists, so CPOs dispatched
> AFTER the room was minted never enter `participants` or `rosterUserIds` on the
> agency device either — and an Ops Room has no server row to correct it.
> Ordinary user-created groups had no roster at all.
>
> Fix: the ring now also unions `groups[id].members`, the one LIVE source —
> `applyAdminAction` maintains it through every add and remove on every device
> that applied the action. No migration (installs already hold it) and it cannot
> over-ring, since a removed member is dropped from the map by the remove action.
> Roster writes added to the receive path and to `createGroupChat` as well.
>
> Found by auditing the first fix for completeness rather than re-asserting it.
> The same audit cleared the other two reports: `rotate()` is driven by a
> keySource subscription so it fires on every remaining member's device after a
> removal (B-249), and both call screens start their own InCallManager session
> symmetrically (B-243 was one stack's teardown killing the other's session).
> Device QA still owed on all of it — two accounts in a live call.

**Reported:** founder — "when an agent calls the group call the client got rung
but the CPO are not rung; when CPO starts the video call the client got rung but
the agent or manager don't get rung."

**Why the earlier fix (`c7f8f6a`) does not cover this.** That fix made
`ringRecipients` merge three sources: local crypto membership, the explicit
`participants` hint, and — the important one — the server roster from
`conversationApi.listMine()` (`GET /conversations/mine`). It works for ordinary
groups.

**A mission Ops Room is not a server `conversations` row.** Verified against the
live DB:

- there is no `mission_comms_rooms` table;
- `public.missions` has **no** `conversation_id` / `room_id` column — its only
  comms column is `comms_room_failed_at`;
- so the Ops Room group id is derived CLIENT-side from the mission, and
  `/conversations/mine` can never return it.

The roster branch therefore yields nothing for a mission group and the fan-out
falls back to **crypto membership** — i.e. "peers I already hold a key for" —
which is exactly the original defect. A CPO or agency manager who has not yet
completed the key exchange is not rung, while the client (who has) is.

**CORRECTION — the real mechanism is client-side.** The `/conversations/mine`
finding above is true but is NOT the operative cause. `ensureAssignedGroup`
already writes the FULL roster onto the conversation
(`participants: [owner, ...others]`, productionRuntime ~4755). It is then
**overwritten**: `resolveRosterOverwrite` (pendingRosterIntents.ts:231) does

```ts
if (args.cryptoMembers && args.cryptoMembers.length > 0) {
  return {skip: false, participants: args.cryptoMembers};
}
```

so `conversations[id].participants` collapses to "peers I already hold a group
key for" the moment any crypto member exists. `otherMembers` in
`launchCall.ts:90` reads exactly that field, so the ring set is crypto-narrowed
no matter what the server would have said. That narrowing is CORRECT for media
grants and member-removal (it is what stops a removed member being resurrected)
— it is only wrong for ringing, which needs no key at all.

**Shape of the fix (NOT implemented).** The full roster must be preserved on the
conversation in a field the crypto narrowing never touches (e.g.
`rosterUserIds`), written by `ensureAssignedGroup` and the server sync, and
unioned into `ringRecipients`. Do NOT relax `resolveRosterOverwrite` itself —
that guard exists to stop a removed member being resurrected. As a backstop,
mission recipients can also be derived from the assigned crew
(`mission_crew`), the booking's client, and the assigned provider/manager.
Ringing needs no key, so this list must be authoritative regardless of crypto
state. Deliberately left for a session with room to verify it — this is the
call-routing path and a wrong recipient set either rings the wrong person or
silently rings no one.

**Related and also open:** the client should get the Ops Room when the AGENCY
ACCEPTS the job, not when the CPO taps dispatch. Same root: the group's
existence is currently tied to the dispatch step rather than the acceptance.

## B-272 … B-274 — runtime-config race · ICE/offer ordering · silent answer stall · 2026-07-26

Founder session, two independent reports: an engineering error string on screen inside a
chat, and a 1:1 call that rang, was answered, and stuck on `Answering…` (audio + video).

### B-272 — `production runtime requires configureMessengerRuntime(cfg) first` shown to the user 🔴 P1 · FIXED

`MainNavigator` resolves the SQLCipher ownerKey pin from AsyncStorage BEFORE it calls
`configureMessengerRuntime()`, so from process start until that one read resolves there is
no config and every `getMessengerRuntime('production')` throws. Nothing used to reach that
window; the B-257/B-258 notification deep-link now does — it mounts ChatScreen in the same
frame MainNavigator mounts, so the chat's own `pullEnvelopes()` raced the read and lost.
ChatScreen swallowed the throw into a `console.log` (stripped in release), so the drain for
the very message the user had tapped never ran and nothing was reported.

- Fix: `setMessengerConfigGate(pending)` published SYNCHRONOUSLY in the effect (before any
  await); `buildRuntime` awaits it before declaring the config absent. `configEpoch` stops a
  build parked on the gate from starting a SECOND `buildProductionRuntime` after the gate's
  own `_resetMessengerRuntime()` nulls the singleton — two SQLCipher opens.
- Presentation half: `sendErrorText` was allow-by-default — anything it did not recognise
  went to the red banner verbatim, which is how an internal string reached a user. Now maps
  runtime-not-ready to human copy and falls back for any message naming a `functionCall(`.
  Deliberate product copy ("group too large to send (300 > 250 recipients)" — space before
  the paren) still passes through.
- Tests: `runtimeConfigGate.test.ts` (5), `sendErrorText.test.ts` (+3).

### B-273 — every outgoing call sent ICE BEFORE its offer; the relay discarded it 🔴 P1 · FIXED

Proved on staging, not theorised. `bravo-staging-msgr` logs show, on every single call:

```
[CALL] ICE   from=88d34848 -> 3165d0e1 cid=f5ac6445   (x3)
[CALL] OFFER from=88d34848 -> 3165d0e1 cid=f5ac6445
```

`handleCallIce` runs `authorizeCallFrame`, which silently ignores frames for a callId it has
no session for — and the session is created by the offer. So the first candidates gathered
(host + srflx, the ones that connect an easy-NAT call without touching TURN) were dropped on
the floor, every call. coturn confirms the cost: allocations succeed but
`peer usage: rp=0, rb=0, sp=0, sb=0` — no CreatePermission ever issued, not one media packet
relayed.

TWO causes, both needed fixing:

1. `createOffer()` also applies the local description, so gathering (and `onicecandidate`)
   starts the moment it returns — but the offer frame is not sent until after
   `await buildOfferAuth(...)`, which can take hundreds of ms. Landed 2026-05-23 (f30df94).
2. `sendOffer` goes through `enqueueForCall` -> `waitOpenThenSend` (ASYNC), while `sendIce`
   takes `safeSend` (SYNCHRONOUS). ICE wins the race even when issued after. The existing
   comment justified the ICE fast path on the PEER ignoring late candidates; it overlooked
   the RELAY dropping early ones.

- Fix: outbound-ICE gate in `CallController`, flushed on the `sendOffer` / `sendAnswer`
  promise (i.e. at `socket.emit`), NOT on return. `sendOffer` now returns `Promise<boolean>`.
- NOT a regression from this week's batch — it predates it by months and degrades every call.

### B-274 — `accept()` could resolve without answering, stranding "Answering…" 🔴 P1 · FIXED

Server log for the founder's two calls: OFFER delivered OK, then from the callee **no
answer, no ICE, and no hangup**. `accept()` has four bare
`if (cancelled || !pc || pc.isClosed()) return;` exits that resolve the promise normally, and
a throw was no better — the manual in-app accept path (`useCall.accept`) awaits with no
catch, so a failure surfaced as an unhandled rejection and the call just sat there. Only the
autoAccept path handled failure.

- Fix: `accept()` now has exactly two honest outcomes — an answer went out, or the call is
  terminated as failed and the caller is told. Cancellation stays the one silent case.
- Signal worth keeping: of three calls that hour the ANSWERED one was audio-only
  (`sdpLen=1223`, one m-line); both unanswered were `kind=video`. `attachLocalMedia` (camera
  acquisition) runs BEFORE `createAnswer` on the answerer — prime suspect, NOT yet proven.
- Tests: `callAnswerLifecycle.test.ts` (7), both fixes mutation-proved.

### Ruled OUT with evidence (do not re-chase)

- **TURN secret drift (B-41 class).** coturn's `--static-auth-secret` and msgr's
  `TURN_STATIC_AUTH_SECRET` are IDENTICAL (`zktVJXM+...LoSjU=`, 44 chars). Creds were issued
  to both parties at call time. The 401/403s in coturn logs are scanner noise from
  185.216.51.x with `username=<>`, not our clients.
- **B-257/B-258 deep-link rewrite.** Params are byte-identical to the old inline sites and
  every call site still waits for `navigationRef.isReady()` before navigating.
- **`callController.ts` itself.** Untouched since `b0087d7` (B-130).

### Diagnostic gap that cost this session

Client `[WEBRTC]` / `[CALL]` traces are `console.log`, which
`babel-plugin-transform-remove-console` strips from release builds (it keeps `warn` /
`error`). The callee's failure is therefore invisible on a QA build — the same blind spot
that hid B-262. Promote call-critical traces to `warn`.

## B-279 / B-280 — messenger "laggy / lazy response" investigation (2026-07-26)

Founder: _"the app still somewhat slow — response lazy on messenger module"_, then
_"when I open a chat to go into the chat there is a lagging animation"_.

### The measurement harness (reuse this — do not re-derive)

`dumpsys gfxinfo` with a **scripted, identical** interaction so runs are comparable, and an
**interleaved A/B** (OLD, NEW, OLD, NEW) so device drift hits both arms equally. Two arms are
built by stashing only the screen files, so both APKs differ in exactly the change under test —
verified by grepping the JS bundle (`bubbleRadii` present in one, absent in the other).

Device: Redmi Note 11 `043dd12e3dad`, 1080x2400, density 440, thermal status 0.
Scenario: 4 x (tap conversation row -> 3s -> BACK -> 3s), after a 25s cold-boot settle.

### Baseline (v1.0.160)

| interaction    | janky | 50th | 99th | Slow UI thread | GPU 50th |
| -------------- | ----- | ---- | ---- | -------------- | -------- |
| scroll a chat  | 7.2%  | 12ms | 20ms | 7 / 516        | 7ms      |
| type a message | 29.9% | 11ms | 36ms | 12 / 67        | 3ms      |
| open a chat    | 20.5% | 14ms | 61ms | 64 / 419       | 7ms      |

**The GPU is never the bottleneck** (3-7ms against a 16.7ms budget). Every jank bucket that
fires is `Slow UI thread`. `Number High input latency` runs 590-890 per run — that is the
founder's "lazy response".

### What the 90ms chat-open frame is NOT (all measured, all ruled out)

`[PERFDIAG]` `console.warn` probes in a release build (warn survives
`babel-plugin-transform-remove-console`; `log` does not):

```
[PERFDIAG] render#1 hooks=2ms body=82ms bubbles=6ms/n=10 composer=0ms
[PERFDIAG] render#2 hooks=0ms body=15ms
[PERFDIAG] render#3 hooks=0ms body=11ms   (lands ~500ms after open)
```

- **Not the hooks.** All **87** hook calls in `ChatScreenInner` cost **2 ms**.
- **Not the bubbles.** Ten `MessageBubble`s cost **6-11 ms** total (~0.7ms each).
- **Not the composer.** **0 ms** (B-159's extraction is doing its job).
- **Not shadows/gradients/blur.** GPU is idle. **Stripping the cobalt bubble glow would cost
  the design and buy nothing** — do not do it without a NEW measurement showing GPU-bound
  frames. (This corrects an earlier recommendation in this repo's notes.)
- **Not element creation for closed sheets.** Gating all 6 modal/sheet subtrees behind their
  visibility flag changed the numbers **not at all** (82ms before, 82ms after). Kept anyway as
  strictly-less-work, but it is not the fix.
- **Not the list virtualization windows** _on a short thread_. A/B of 20/20/11 -> 10/8/5 came
  out **inside the noise band** on a 10-message chat, because there is nothing to virtualize.
  It still matters for real users: `MAX_HYDRATE_PER_CONVO = 200`, so a busy chat mounts 20
  bubbles on the old numbers and 10 on the new.

The residue is the **commit itself** — reconciling and mounting ~200 native views in the same
frame the push animation is running. i.e. view COUNT, not per-view cost.

### What was tried and REJECTED by measurement (do not re-propose without new data)

| Idea                                                                | Result                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Defer the message list to `InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions` | **~2x WORSE, both rounds** (janky 34.9%->68.0% and 23.8%->44.1%; Slow UI thread 35->72 and 79->133). Splits one commit into two and adds a placeholder->list layout pass. Reverted. |
| Remove `recvBubble`'s shadow                                        | Not attempted: it is `#000 @ 0.18` on a `#07090D` background — invisible, so zero visual gain — and `elevation: 0` risks sibling stacking order. GPU has headroom regardless.       |
| `Image resizeMethod="resize"` for bitmap uploads                    | Not attempted: `Slow bitmap uploads` measured 0-13 per run, and `resize` visibly softens the image. Not the bottleneck.                                                             |

### Shipped (v1.0.162, vc193 — local install only, no Firebase)

- **B-279a** Bubble gradient moved off a child `<LinearGradient>` onto the bubble's own
  background via RN 0.81 `experimental_backgroundImage`. One fewer native view **per message**.
  Device-verified pixel-identical (screenshots before/after). `bubbleRadii` deleted — it existed
  only to re-clip the overlay child and was a second copy of the run-grouping corner rule.
- **B-279b** Mount budgets: chat `20/20/11` -> `10/8/5`, home `14/10/7` -> `10/8/5`.
- **B-279c** All 6 sheet subtrees gated on their flag; `<EmojiPicker>` mounted only while open
  (`rn-emoji-keyboard` mounts its `KeyboardProvider` even at `open={false}`, and that provider
  walks the whole ~1,800-entry `emojis.json` on mount).
- **B-280** Emoji sheet: `allowMultipleSelections` so it stays open, and focus handed back on
  close so the IME returns. Applied to **both** composer copies (`ChatScreen` via a new
  `ChatComposerHandle.focusInput`, `DepartmentChatScreen` via a new TextInput ref).

Regression tests: `chatListMountBudget.test.ts` (18, incl. a `PERFDIAG`-never-ships guard) and
`emojiSheetLifecycle.test.ts` (7). Both mutation-proven red on the pre-fix source (10/13 and
6/7). `chromeRemoval.test.ts`'s `bubbleRadii` anchor was MOVED, not deleted — the invariant it
guards (run-grouping drives bubble geometry) is now pinned on the four StyleSheet conditionals.

Gates: messenger-crypto **3556 x2**, messenger screens **127**, keyboard **89**, typecheck
**46** (baseline 47), lint 0 errors.

### STILL OPEN

- **The chat-open frame is NOT fixed.** 61-105ms per open remains. Next step is to cut view
  COUNT in the first commit — the header/banner/composer chrome is the untouched part — or to
  profile the commit itself with Perfetto/systrace on the UI thread. Do **not** spend another
  round on hooks, bubbles, shadows, or deferral: all four are measured dead ends above.
  **2026-08-29 root-cause decomposition:** `docs/qa/CHAT_OPEN_ANIMATION_LAG_2026-08-29.md` —
  every ChatScreen mount effect (setActive, pullEnvelopes, the 200ms markRead timer) lands
  INSIDE the 220ms native slide window, and the perf-journey harness never taps a chat. Fix
  plan F1..F6 ranked there (F2 = defer side effects to `transitionEnd`, NOT the list).
- **B-281 (new, from the B-280 fix):** with the emoji sheet staying open it now covers the
  composer, so the user cannot see the emoji they are composing. The right fix is the
  library's **inline `EmojiKeyboard`** rendered below the composer in place of the system IME
  (the WhatsApp model), NOT a taller/shorter modal — a bottom sheet always covers the composer.
  That touches the LOCKED keyboard-inset rule (CLAUDE.md: bottom-most element owns the inset),
  so it needs its own pass, not a rushed one.

## B-281 / B-282 — emoji panel + "who reacted" (2026-07-26, v1.0.164 vc195)

### B-281 — the emoji sheet covered the composer

Caused by the B-280 fix: keeping the sheet open for multiple picks meant the user
could no longer see the emoji they were building. **A modal bottom sheet is anchored
to the window bottom, so it will ALWAYS cover a bottom-anchored composer** — no
height, prop or theme fixes that.

ChatScreen now uses the library's inline `EmojiKeyboard` (not `EmojiPicker`),
rendered INSIDE the composer's padded column, BELOW the input bar, in the space
`Keyboard.dismiss()` frees. The WhatsApp arrangement.

- The emoji button is a TOGGLE and its glyph flips to a keyboard while the panel is up.
- Tapping the text field swaps back to the system IME (`onFocus` guarded on `emojiOpen`).
- Panel height is `clamp(240, windowHeight * 0.38, 360)` — a FRACTION, never a dp
  constant (B-277 rule: "many users will use other phones so it should be dynamic").
- **Search bar removed** on founder request. It cost a row AND was the only reason
  the provider memo ran `emojisByCategory.map(g => g.data).flat()` over the whole
  ~1,800-entry dataset — that branch is gated on `enableSearchBar`. Two wins.
- Keyboard contract (41) still green: exactly ONE `bottomPad(8)`, on an ancestor of
  the input bar. The panel is a CHILD of that column, which is why no second inset
  was needed. DepartmentChatScreen still uses the modal + B-280 props.

### B-282 — you could not see WHO reacted

Nothing was missing from the wire. `LocalMessage.reactions` has always been
`Record<reactorUserId, emoji>`; `groupReactions` read the userId and **threw it
away**, returning only `{emoji, count, mine}`. Display fix, no protocol change.

- `groupReactions` now also returns `who: string[]`.
- New `reactionRoster(reactions, resolveName)` — flat roster, own reaction hoisted
  and labelled "You", unknown reactors fall back to `${id.slice(0,8)}…` rather than
  `undefined`. The trailing ellipsis is load-bearing: the screen keys its ONE
  batched directory request off it.
- Tapping the reaction row opens a roster sheet. Row is now a button with an
  a11y label (a row of bare emoji announced as nothing).
- Helpers EXTRACTED to `src/screens/messenger/reactionRoster.ts` so the node Jest
  project can import them — `ChatScreen.tsx` pulls in react-native and cannot be
  imported there, which is why the rest of that screen is only reachable by source
  scan. Same pattern as `sendErrorText.ts` / `conversationListOrder.ts`.

### A trap this session paid for twice

`chromeRemoval.test.ts`'s comment-stripper pairs the first `/*` with the NEXT
`*/`, so a run of JSX comments can swallow REAL code between them. The B-263
assertion (`not.toMatch(/end-to-end encrypted/i)`) had been passing only because
the empty-state copy was being deleted before it was scanned; editing unrelated
comments shifted the pairing and a green test went red with the banner still
correctly absent. **Narrowed to pin the banner node, not the phrase.** Anchor a
source scan on a styled node or a call site, never on prose.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3574 x2** (345 suites), messenger screens **127**, keyboard
**89** (incl. the 41-assertion contract), typecheck **46** (baseline 47), lint 0
errors. New tests: `reactionRoster.test.ts` (13 real unit tests) + 7 B-281
assertions in `emojiSheetLifecycle.test.ts`, all mutation-proven red pre-fix.
Built + installed to Redmi + BlueStacks as v1.0.164 (vc195). No Firebase.

### Owed

- DepartmentChatScreen still has the MODAL emoji sheet and no reaction roster —
  the shared helper is in place, so both are small follow-ons.
- Device QA on the B-282 roster sheet (it was gate-verified, not tapped on device).

## B-284 / B-285 — media tray inset, and hunting the multi-second freezes (2026-07-26)

### B-284 — Cancel / Send sat under the navigation bar (v1.0.166)

`MediaPreviewTray` padded its bottom with a hardcoded `26`. That is not a safe-area
inset: on a 3-button nav bar it is ~22dp short (the founder's screenshot shows the
system icons drawn over the buttons) and it is wrong by a different amount on a
gesture pill, a notch phone or a tablet. **No dp constant is right on every
device.** It now uses `bottomPad(14)` from `useKeyboardLayout` — the documented
choice for a bottom-anchored sheet. Keyboard contract (41) still green.

### B-285 — the app freezes for seconds at a time

Founder: "sometimes the app gets stuck for a couple of secs", and the precise
symptom "the tap renders but the action takes time to register". Press feedback is
an Animated opacity change that runs without JS; `onPress` is a JS callback. So the
JS thread was BUSY — the touch was not missed, it was queued.

**Confirmed independently by MIUI's own monitor**, not just our probe:

    Looper PerfMonitor longMsg : wall=6177ms h=...MessageQueueThreadHandler

Single JS-queue messages of 6177ms, 5479ms, 4508ms, 4131ms.

#### THE MEASUREMENT TRAP — read this before trusting any watchdog output

The first `jsThreadWatchdog` reported "blocked ~4760ms" when the founder opened the
system photo picker. **The app was BACKGROUNDED, not blocked** — Android suspends
timers for a backgrounded process, so the interval simply never fired. Android's own
`PerfMonitor longMsg` shares the confound: a descheduled process inflates a message's
wall time without doing any work. The watchdog now reports only when the app was
`active` for the WHOLE interval, including a background round-trip that starts and
ends inside one tick — which a naive two-sample check cannot see, because both
samples read `active`. Pinned by `jsThreadWatchdog.test.ts` (7) and mutation-proven:
deleting the guard turns exactly the two false-positive tests red.

#### B-285a — a regression I introduced, found and fixed

`experimental_backgroundImage` (B-279) was emitting
`Unsupported type for radius property: Null` — **0 on the pre-session APK, 90 on the
new one under an IDENTICAL scripted interaction**, and 260 in ~50s of real use,
bursting 26-34 per second. Cause: `style/LinearGradient.kt:65` calls
`LengthPercentage.setFromDynamic(colorStop.getDynamic("position"))`, and a stop with
no explicit position takes the `else ->` branch and logs — once per stop, per bubble,
per commit. The gradient renders correctly either way, so ONLY a log check catches
it. Fixed by stating `0%` / `100%`; re-measured **90 -> 0** on the same script.
Pinned by a new assertion in `chatListMountBudget.test.ts`.

#### The live lead — each SEND blocks the thread

Founder repro: **"after sending very fast messages, press back / do stuff and it gets
stuck."** Captured:

    19:42:46  383ms   19:42:47  192ms   19:42:48  391ms   19:42:49  349ms
    19:42:51  497ms   19:42:52  448ms   19:42:54  352ms
    19:42:58 3392ms   19:43:06 3356ms   19:43:10 2997ms

One ~350-500ms stall PER MESSAGE, then multi-second stalls as the queue backs up.
The back press waits behind the queued sends, which is exactly the reported symptom.

**Next probe: time the send-path stages** — Signal encrypt, SQLCipher write, and
especially `notifyBackupDirty` (every message mutation notifies the backup mirror,
an earlier audit already flagged a full Merkle re-download every 30s, and a per-send
Merkle cost would grow with thread length — which matches the compounding above).

### Dead ends this session (do NOT re-propose without new data)

- Media encryption / base64 decode: probes were added and the founder's freezes
  produced **no `readUriBytes` or `encryptAttachment` lines at all**. Not the cause.
- See also B-279's four dead ends: shadows, modal-subtree gating, list windows, and
  deferring the list to `runAfterInteractions` (that one measured ~2x WORSE).

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3583**, app messenger+keyboard+watchdog **175**, typecheck **46**
(baseline 47), lint 0 errors, logAudit **5** — it caught a probe logging the
plaintext buffer's size, fixed by logging LESS rather than renaming around the scan.
Built + installed to Redmi + BlueStacks through v1.0.169 (vc200). No Firebase.

## B-286 … B-289 — avatar colour, photo albums, viewer swipe, group rename (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.171 (vc202), `main` @ 90be488.

### B-286 — the same person was a different colour in the list and in the chat

Founder: "group or user avatra in messgenr list showinng one clor but in char it
shoudd differnr color these one fix it."

There were **SIX** independent implementations of "pick an avatar colour":

| Site                           | Palette      | Keyed on        |
| ------------------------------ | ------------ | --------------- |
| `MessengerHomeScreen.avatarBg` | 6            | conversation id |
| `ChatScreen.AVATAR_GRADIENT`   | fixed purple | **nothing**     |
| `CallsLogScreen.avatarBg`      | 6            | conversation id |
| `GroupsScreen.avatarBgFor`     | 6            | conversation id |
| `ChatInfoScreen.avatarColor`   | 7            | conversation id |
| `ChatScreen.senderColorFor`    | 7            | user id         |

Every one used the **identical** `h * 31 + charCodeAt` hash, so these were
drifted COPIES, not deliberate variants. And the chat header could not vary at
all — a fixed gradient for every conversation — so the two surfaces the founder
compared could never have agreed.

Now one `src/screens/messenger/avatarColors.ts`, keyed on the conversation id,
with the LIST's palette kept canonical so the surface that looked right does not
move. Paired `{solid, gradient}` entries keep the flat row avatars and the
header's gradient disc the same hue without being the same shade. The
per-speaker tint stays a separate concern (distinguishing who is talking, not
identifying a conversation) but folds onto the single `colorForSender`, which
absorbed the null-hardening ChatScreen's copy had existed for in the first
place.

**The test that matters is the source scan**, not the unit assertions: a seventh
copy would simply never be imported by the test and every equality assertion
would still pass. It scans for an inline array of 5+ hex literals and for the
`* 31 + charCodeAt` tell. Threshold is five, not three — the compose button's
3-stop cobalt ramp is a legitimate gradient and tripped the first version.

### B-288 — multiple photos arrived one bubble at a time

Consecutive photos from one sender within 60s now paint as one WhatsApp-style
mosaic: 2 side by side, 3 as one tall beside two stacked, 2x2 past that with a
"+N" badge on the last tile. The album attaches to the **leader's existing row**,
so sender name, timestamp, ticks, reactions and long-press all keep working —
only the body changes.

- **Capped at 4 tiles deliberately.** B-279 measured this screen's bottleneck as
  view MOUNTING, and a 30-photo dump used to be 30 image bubbles.
- **Grouping is memoised on the message array's identity.** `albumIndex` mints
  fresh arrays, so without the WeakMap the leader's `album` prop would be a new
  object every render, MX-07 row identity would break, and every photo row would
  re-render on every store touch — a perf regression in the exact area being
  complained about.
- **Wire format UNCHANGED.** Each photo is still its own sealed-sender message
  with its own AES key. A real multi-part album would change the envelope shape,
  which is arch-gated.
- A captioned photo never groups (merging would hide the text), but a bare
  filename in `content` is not a caption — treating it as one would have stopped
  ordinary bursts grouping at all.

### B-287 — swipe between photos

Swiping left/right in the open photo pages through every photo in the thread
(not just the tapped album — stopping at an album boundary is a dead end the
user cannot see).

It reuses `ZoomableImage`'s **existing** pan handler instead of adding a second
horizontal gesture, so there is no zoom-vs-page fight to arbitrate. `swipeIntent`
(pure, in `zoomMath.ts`) refuses to page whenever the image is zoomed — while
zoomed the drag is how you reach the edges of the photo, and stealing it would
make a zoomed image unreadable. The zoom test is `> 1.05`, not `> 1`: pinch
releases settle a hair off exactly 1 and a strict compare would silently disable
paging forever after the user's first pinch.

Paging reads the LIVE store, not a render-time closure — the viewer stays open
across incoming messages.

### B-289 — group name was permanent

The `rename` admin action has existed in the protocol since the group client was
written: the action type, the signed `rename|<epoch>|<name>` payload, the
`applyAdminAction` case, a deterministic system-event id and a
"<actor> renamed the channel to X" renderer. **Nothing ever built one.** This is
the missing emitter, not new protocol.

- **No rekey.** Membership is unchanged, so the master key still binds the same
  devices; rotating it for a display string would force a redistribution that
  can partially fail.
- **Fan-out is best-effort**, so the local apply lands even offline and a missed
  peer re-syncs. Contrast `remove`, which throws at 0 peers — a missed removal is
  a security failure, a missed label is not.
- Name cleaning **strips bidirectional overrides**. Not cosmetic: an RTL mark
  inside a name reorders the UI text AROUND it, so an admin could make the group
  header read as something else on every member's device.
- `upsertConversation` is a REPLACE (B-247), so the row is spread — a bare
  `{id, name}` would have wiped the roster, unread count and last message.

### Group PHOTO — NOT implemented, and not faked

`GroupState` has no image field and `GroupAdminAction` has no photo action.
Adding one means a new field in encrypted group state plus a new signed action
with its own canonical signing bytes, media key distribution to members, and
transcript-hash implications. That is inventing security behaviour in the
group-state / key-distribution area, which CLAUDE.md gates. **Needs architecture
sign-off before any code.**

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3654** green across 5 runs — one run showed 5 failures in a
single suite that did **not** reproduce in the other four, the known B-126 moving
flake. App messenger screens + keyboard **240**. typecheck **46** (baseline 47).
Lint **0 errors** (4 warnings, all pre-existing; one relocated with the
`liveConversationMessages` extraction). New suites: `avatarColors` (24),
`imageAlbums` (43), `groupRename` (28). The avatar agreement assertion and the
album core were mutation-proven RED before the fix.

Re-verified every suite AFTER the pre-commit prettier pass — these are source
scans matching exact strings, so reformatting could have broken them silently.

## B-290 / B-291 — the rename was invisible, and the group photo (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.172 (vc203), `main` @ 26e2bb8.

### B-290 — CRITICAL, and a regression in B-289 shipped an hour earlier

Founder, on the v1.0.171 build: "i change the name but the changed name does not
show to me. admin change the name, i am in these group, for me the name is not
showing."

**Root cause.** `applyAdminAction`'s `rename` case updates `groups[id].name` —
the _crypto_ state — and **nothing renders that**. The conversation list, the
chat header and the info sheet all read `conversations[id].name`. So the rename
applied correctly, advanced the epoch, extended the transcript, and was
completely invisible.

The receive path was worse. `applyGroupAdmin` reconciles what the user SEES for
`add` (system line) and `remove` (system line), but had **no `rename` branch at
all** — so a member's device recorded the new name in crypto state and displayed
the old one permanently. The two sibling branches sitting right there is what
makes this an omission rather than a design.

**Fix.** One `applyGroupRenameToUi` called from BOTH paths. It patches the
conversation row (spreading it — `upsertConversation` is a REPLACE, B-247) with
`is_custom_name: true`, and appends the system line.

Two details that matter:

- It reads **LIVE** store state. The emitter awaits a cert fetch and a whole
  fan-out before it applies, so the `getState()` snapshot taken at entry is stale
  by then — a plausible reason the admin's own device could also miss it.
- The emitter is now **forbidden by test** from writing the row or appending the
  line itself. Two copies of "apply a rename" is precisely the shape that
  produced B-286's six drifted avatar-colour functions.

Mutation-proven: disabling the receive branch turns exactly 3 tests red.

### B-291 — group photo (founder-approved after I flagged the gate)

I had reported this as arch-gated and declined to guess. The founder approved it
explicitly, so it is built the most conservative way available.

**The picture is an ordinary encrypted attachment.** AES-256-CBC, fresh
per-file key, uploaded through the _same_ `MediaClient.uploadEncrypted` path
every chat photo takes. Group state carries only the reference
`{objectKey, keyB64, ivB64, mimeType, size, updatedAt}`. **No new crypto
primitive, no new storage, no change to the sealed-sender envelope.**

**What IS new:** one `GroupAdminAction` member, `{type: 'photo', photo, atEpoch}`.
`applyAdminAction`'s `default:` branch was already written to treat an unknown
action as a no-op "so a forward-compatibility rollout doesn't crash a legacy
receiver" — this is exactly that rollout shape, so an older client ignores it.

**Deliberately NOT the plaintext `avatarUrl` pattern used for USER profiles.** A
group's name is explicitly "never sent to the server in plaintext", so a
plaintext group picture would tell the relay what a group looks like. That is a
weakening and was not done.

Decisions worth keeping:

- **Canonical signed bytes cover objectKey, keyB64, ivB64 and mimeType.** Signing
  only the objectKey would let an attacker replaying a captured envelope
  substitute a different decryption key for the same object and still verify.
  There is a dedicated test asserting a swapped key/IV changes the transcript.
- **No rekey.** Membership is unchanged, so the master key still binds the same
  devices. Rotating for a picture risks a partial rekey for zero security gain.
- **Upload BEFORE broadcast.** The reverse order would point every member at an
  object that may never exist, and a permanently broken picture is not something
  a user can retry.
- **Downscaled to 512px before upload.** A group avatar renders at 84pt; shipping
  a full-resolution phone photo would make every member download megabytes to
  draw a small circle.
- **`GroupAvatar` mirrors `UserAvatar`** (the component that exists _because_
  every surface had invented its own answer, B-253). Picture-or-fallback only;
  each surface keeps its own disc. Wired into the list, the chat header AND the
  info sheet — a photo visible on one screen only reads as "it did not save".
- Cache is keyed on **objectKey, not groupId**, so a new picture can never be
  shadowed by a stale entry.

### Two mistakes of mine that existing gates caught

- **I converted three CRLF files to LF.** My Python rewrites read with universal
  newlines and wrote back with `newline=''`. Three suites assert those files ARE
  CRLF — the guard exists precisely because a `\n`-anchored scan would then pass
  VACUOUSLY. Restored. **Do not rewrite these files with a script that
  normalises newlines.**
- **`directoryAvatars` pinned `userId={isGroup ? null : peerId}`** with the note
  "a group has no single face; its own picture is a separate feature". B-291 made
  that premise false, so the old form was now _wrong_ (it would throw the picture
  away). The anchor was **re-pointed, not deleted**: groups → `GroupAvatar`,
  people → `UserAvatar`, plus a NEW assertion that a group id is never fed to the
  USER directory. Same invariant, stronger.

Also re-ran every source-scan suite AFTER the pre-commit prettier pass (15 files
reformatted) and re-checked CRLF, because a green pre-commit run proves nothing
about the reformatted tree.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3682** green. A later run failed only
`callAudioSessionArbitration`, which then passed **14/14 three times in
isolation** — the known B-126 flake, not this change. App messenger screens +
keyboard **240**. typecheck **46** (baseline 47 — it hit 47 briefly on a wrong
`makeNewGroup` signature in my own fixture). logAudit **5**: the per-file photo
key is never logged. New suite `groupPhoto` (**24**); `groupRename` now **32**.

### Owed

Device QA on both. Specifically: rename from the admin and confirm the OTHER
device's list + header + system line update; set a photo and confirm it appears
on all three surfaces on both devices; remove a photo and confirm the disc comes
back with a system line.

## B-292 — the group photo was invisible to everyone but the admin (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.173 (vc204), `main` @ b39c451.

Founder, on the v1.0.172 build: "the admin change the picture but picture is
showing in admin page but other group member has the old avatar dont change the
picture."

### Root cause — holding the key is not permission to fetch

The media service enforces a **per-object grant list**. Possessing the AES key is
necessary but NOT sufficient: an ungranted user 403s at the download. So
`setGroupPhoto` shipped a reference that only the uploader could read — the
uploader is implicitly allowed, every other member was refused, and because a
failed resolve caches nothing the disc came back on every remount. Permanently
broken, and only for the people who were not the admin.

Every chat-attachment path already calls `mediaClient.registerGrants(objectKey,
recipients)`. The comments beside those calls say it outright: without it "the
recipient 403s under strict grant mode". There are three such call sites (1:1,
group pre-fanout, and the outbox reseal, the last added precisely because an
offline-queued row skipped the live path's grant).

**I reused the upload primitive and missed the authorization step sitting next to
it.** That is the same shape as B-290 an hour earlier: reuse a mechanism, miss
the half of it that makes the OTHER device see anything. Both bugs were
one-device-only symptoms, and both were invisible to a green test suite because
nothing exercised the second device.

### Fix

- `registerGrants(objectKey, Object.keys(cur.members))` **before** the broadcast.
  Granting after the fan-out leaves a window where a fast member applies the
  action, fetches, 403s and caches nothing — the retry only comes on a later
  remount, so it reads as permanently missing.
- A failed grant now **throws**. Shipping a reference nobody can read is worse
  than a visible error: the admin would believe it worked and no member would
  ever see it.
- **Same defect one step removed, also fixed:** a member ADDED AFTER the photo
  was set had no grant either, so they alone would show the fallback disc.
  `addGroupMember` now grants the new member the existing photo — best-effort
  there, because the add is already broadcast by that point and a picture must
  never desync membership.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3687** green. App messenger screens + keyboard **240**.
typecheck **46** (baseline 47). logAudit **5**. `groupPhoto` now **29**, and the
grant assertion is mutation-proven: narrowing the grant to self alone turns
exactly that one test red.

### The generalisable lesson

**Any feature that reuses `uploadEncrypted` MUST also register grants.** The two
are a pair, and the type system does not enforce it — an upload compiles and
"works" for the author's own device, which is exactly the reviewer blind spot.
Worth a source-scan gate if a third such feature ever appears.

## B-293 — the viewer swipe was implemented and completely inert (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.174 (vc205), `main` @ 81d2d3a.

Founder: "the pic swipe left and right is not working it is not showing left
side image or righ side image like whats app are u sure u implement it".

The wiring was all correct — `ChatScreen → ChatAttachmentViewer → FileViewer →
ZoomableImage` all passed `onSwipe`, the pan handler fired, the prop chain was
verified intact. The bug was in the decision function.

### Defect 1 — a required field that the payload does not carry

`swipeIntent` validated `velocityX` alongside the translations:

```ts
if (![translationX, translationY, velocityX, scale].every(n => isFinite(n))) {
  return 0;
}
```

`onHandlerStateChange` delivers a **state transition, not a motion sample**, and
its native payload does not reliably include a velocity. So `isFinite(undefined)`
was `false` and **every swipe returned 0**. The feature was dead on device while
every one of its unit tests passed — because the tests all supplied a velocity
explicitly.

Velocity is only ever a **boost** for the flick path; distance alone must be
sufficient to page. It is now optional and degrades to 0 ("unknown", not "no").
Translation and scale remain required — a bad scale fails CLOSED, because we
cannot tell whether the user is zoomed and stealing a zoomed pan is the worse
error.

**The test that asserted a non-finite velocity must return 0 was encoding the
bug.** It was corrected, not deleted, and two `B-293` tests now pin the
no-velocity path. Mutation-proven: restoring the old guard turns exactly those
two red.

> **Lesson, and it generalises:** a unit test that constructs its own input
> cannot tell you the real caller supplies that input. When a pure decision
> function is fed by a native event, at least one test must use the payload shape
> the platform ACTUALLY sends — including absent fields.

### Defect 2 — no motion, so success was indistinguishable from failure

Even once firing, the source swapped with zero animation. The outgoing photo now
slides off in the drag direction over 130ms and the swap lands in the animation
callback.

**The re-centre after that slide is UNCONDITIONAL, and that is load-bearing.** At
the first or last photo `onSwipe` changes nothing, so the `useEffect([uri])` that
normally resets translation never runs — a conditional reset would leave the image
parked off-screen and the viewer looking EMPTY, which is worse than the original
bug. Snapping back also doubles as the "no more photos this way" cue. Pinned by a
source scan, since native Animated values are unreachable from node.

### Note for the next report of this

Swipe covers **every photo in the conversation**, oldest→newest, not just the
tapped album. It deliberately does nothing while **zoomed** (there the drag is how
you reach the edges of the photo). And in a thread with only ONE photo it
correctly does nothing — which looks identical to a bug, so check that first.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3692** green. App messenger screens + keyboard **240**.
typecheck **46** (baseline 47). `imageAlbums` now **48**.

Bundle freshness was confirmed by the bundle HASH differing from v1.0.173 — the
per-symbol grep checks were defeated by minification renaming locals, which is
worth knowing: `grep`ing a minified bundle for an identifier only works for
strings and property names that survive mangling.

## B-294 — paging blanked the viewer, then looked stuck (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.175 (vc206), `main` @ 1d06541.

Founder, on v1.0.174 (which fixed the swipe firing at all, B-293): "the pic has
proble now it goes left and righ but when i do left and righ it shoe baln after
it stuc to fast image".

### Root cause — two RN Modals racing

`ChatAttachmentViewer` returns THREE different `<Modal>` elements depending on
state: "Decrypting…", the error card, and `FileViewer`. Paging to a photo whose
bytes were not yet decrypted flipped it to the loading branch, which **unmounts
the viewer's Modal and mounts a different one in the same frame**. On Android
that yields a blank window.

Then it compounds: **a blank window has no gesture surface**, so the next swipe
landed on nothing and the viewer appeared frozen on the first photo. Both
reported symptoms, one cause.

### Fix — never show nothing on the way to showing something

The viewer holds the last **fully-resolved** `(message, uri)` pair and never
unmounts once anything has been shown. It keeps displaying the current photo
until the next one's bytes are ready, then swaps message and uri **together**.
Both fallback branches are now gated on `!shown`, so they can only run on the
very first open.

**Everything below the guard describes the SHOWN photo, not the requested one.**
That distinction is load-bearing and was a latent second bug: mixing them would
label the visible image with the incoming image's filename, and **Delete would
have removed the wrong message**.

### Known trade-off — stated, not hidden

A photo that genuinely fails to resolve now leaves the PREVIOUS one on screen
rather than blanking. Strictly better than the reported behaviour, but it means
a permanently broken photo reads as "the swipe did nothing". If that ever gets
reported, the fix is an inline toast over the retained image — NOT reinstating
the Modal swap, which is what caused this bug.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3696** green. App messenger screens + keyboard **240**.
typecheck **46** (baseline 47). `imageAlbums` now **52**, re-verified after the
pre-commit prettier pass. Mutation-proven: ungating the loading branch turns
exactly one test red.

### The pattern across B-287 → B-293 → B-294

One feature, three device-only failures, all with a green suite:

1. **B-287** shipped the gesture — wired correctly, never fired.
2. **B-293** the decision function required a velocity the native state-change
   payload does not send. 13 unit tests passed because they all invented their
   own payload.
3. **B-294** the fix worked, and exposed that the viewer swaps native Modals per
   page.

None of these were reachable from node. **A green messenger suite says nothing
about gesture payloads, native window lifecycle, or the second device** — the
three places every bug in this feature actually lived.

## B-295 — the blank viewer: `setValue` on a native-driven Animated node (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.176 (vc207), `main` @ d026b31.

Founder, after v1.0.175: "did u install the new one to phone becase the saem
problme is still there". It was installed (phone on 1.0.175, bundle hash differed
from 1.0.174) — **my B-294 diagnosis was simply wrong.**

### Root cause

The slide-out added in B-293 re-centred the image in its completion callback with
`panX.setValue(0)` / `panX.setOffset(0)`.

`panX` is **NATIVE-DRIVEN**: both the pan `Animated.event` and the slide itself
pass `useNativeDriver: true`. **Writing a native-driven node from JS does not
reliably reach the native side** — the shadow node keeps the last ANIMATED value,
which is `±width`. So the photo slid off and never came back: that is the blank.
A blank viewer has no gesture surface, so the next swipe hit nothing and it read
as stuck on the first image. Both symptoms, one cause.

`ZoomableImage`'s own header already warned about this ("listener semantics for
native-driven values with offsets differ per platform and can't be
device-verified here"), and `settleTranslation` already did it CORRECTLY with
`Animated.spring`. That is exactly why the REJECT path never blanked while the
PAGE path always did — same operation, two methods, only mine was wrong.

Fix: re-centre through a zero-duration `Animated.timing`, the same path the
settle spring uses. Also flattens `panY` before the slide, not just `panX`.

### The diagnostic lesson — this is the part worth keeping

I shipped **two** confident wrong diagnoses on one feature:

- B-293 → fixed the gesture, added the slide (which introduced this bug).
- B-294 → blamed a Modal swap. Real latent defect, KEPT, but not what was
  reported.

What I should have done both times: **isolate what changed between working and
broken.** The blank appeared in exactly the build that added the slide. That one
fact pointed straight here and I did not use it — I reasoned toward a plausible
mechanism and shipped.

**Rule: when a symptom appears in a specific build, start from that build's diff,
not from a theory.** A plausible cause that explains the symptom is not evidence;
the thing that changed is.

### Diagnostic that DID work

Comparing the extracted `assets/index.android.bundle` md5 between builds is the
reliable way to prove a build actually shipped new JS. Per-symbol `grep` on a
minified bundle is NOT — mangling renames locals, so absence proves nothing.

### Gates

messenger-crypto **3698** green. App messenger screens + keyboard **240**.
typecheck **46** (baseline 47). `imageAlbums` now **54**, re-verified post-prettier.
Mutation-proven: restoring `panX.setValue(0)` turns exactly the two new B-295
guards red, and those guards now ban `setValue`/`setOffset` anywhere in the swipe
branch.

### Standing rule for this file

**Never read or write `panX` / `panY` / `baseScale` / `pinchScale` from JS.** They
are native-driven. Every rest-state change goes through `Animated.spring` or
`Animated.timing`; rest state is mirrored in plain refs
(`restTxRef` / `restTyRef` / `baseScaleRef`), never read back off the node.

## B-296 — the viewer kept showing the FIRST photo forever (2026-07-26)

Shipped v1.0.177 (vc208), `main` @ da9c9ff.

Founder: "i sweep but it stay at the saem image now the blank is gone but it is
not going left or right". The blank was B-295; this is what was underneath it.

### Root cause — a hook that latches on its first message

`useAttachmentUri` seeds `uri`, `state` and `preferDirect` with `useState`
INITIALISERS and latches `startedRef` after its first load. **All of that is
first-mount only.**

That was correct while the sole caller was a message bubble: one hook instance
sees exactly one message for its entire life (FlatList keys rows by message id,
so a recycled cell is a remount, not a prop change). The full-screen viewer pages
between photos on a **MOUNTED** component, so the hook kept returning the FIRST
photo's uri forever and `load()` early-returned on the latched ref.

**The swipe advanced `viewerMsg` correctly the whole time.** The hook simply
ignored it. Every layer above was working.

Fix: reset when handed a different `msg.id`. Done in the **render phase**
(React's documented "adjusting state when props change"), not an effect — an
effect would let one frame render with the previous photo's uri paired to the new
message, which is exactly the mismatch the viewer's last-good-pair logic (B-294)
latches onto.

### The testing change that actually mattered

Pinned with a **behavioural** test — `src/screens/messenger/__tests__/attachmentUriPaging.test.tsx`
— that renders the hook, swaps the `msg` prop, and asserts what the caller
receives. Six cases including received→own-pick and back, since `preferDirect` is
seeded once too.

Mutation-proven: disabling the reset turns **5 of 6 red**, and the one that stays
green is the guard-doesn't-over-fire case, which is correct.

> **This is the first test in the B-287→B-296 sequence that would have caught the
> reported bug.** The previous four shipped behind green source scans and unit
> tests that constructed their own inputs. The single thing none of them did was
> re-render with a different message — which was the entire defect.

Gotcha for the next person: running this file ALONE needs `--forceExit` (importing
the messenger store leaves a rehydration handle open). The full
`--selectProjects app --testPathPattern "screens/messenger|keyboard"` run
terminates cleanly at 246, so no config change was made for it.

### The whole arc — one feature, five device-only failures

| Bug   | Symptom                  | Cause                                                         |
| ----- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B-287 | (built)                  | swipe implemented                                             |
| B-293 | never fired              | required a `velocityX` the state-change payload does not send |
| B-293 | no motion                | source swap with no animation — added a 130ms slide           |
| B-294 | (latent, kept)           | three `<Modal>` branches → paging could swap native windows   |
| B-295 | blank, then stuck        | `setValue` on a **native-driven** node → image parked ±width  |
| B-296 | stuck on the first image | `useAttachmentUri` latches on its first message               |

**Every one was invisible to the suite, and every one was found by the founder.**
The common factor is that all five lived at a boundary no node test reaches:
native gesture payloads, native window lifecycle, native Animated values, and
hook-identity across prop changes. Only the last was reachable from a test — and
only once the test re-rendered instead of re-reasoning.

messenger-crypto **3698** green. App messenger screens + keyboard **246** (up 6,
exit 0). typecheck **46** (baseline 47).
