## 2026-07-27 — Pixel 6a device session: "add call is not working, also the audio output" (B-299..B-303)

**Device:** Pixel 6a `29271JEGR00258`, Android 17 / SDK 37, **release** build v1.0.177 (vc208),
built from HEAD `86cb169`. **Founder report (verbatim):** _"see the add call is not working also
the audio output"_ + _"it was ok before myb 1 day ago — but yesterday's changes break the thing"_.

**Capture:** rolling `adb logcat -b main,crash,system -v threadtime`, plus a pre-session buffer
snapshot covering 10:42–10:57 (which contains three _working_ calls, 10:46/10:50/10:51, for
contrast). Only `console.warn`/`error` survive the production babel transform, so app JS appears as
`W ReactNativeJS`.

**Regression window.** `docs/runbooks/CALL_KNOWN_GOOD_BASELINE.md` pins the founder-verified
baseline at **v1.0.157 (vc188), commit `7debd9c`**. Exactly four commits touch the call surface
after it — `80d0de0` (B-275), `6badefc` (B-276), `e4a6999` (B-278), `211e706` (B-283). Note the
`known-good/calls-v1.0.157` tag referenced by that runbook **was never pushed** (`git fetch --tags`
does not produce it); use the commit sha until someone pushes the tag.

**The escalation timeline, from the log.** 1:1 audio session torn down `10:57:49.612`, group call
booted `10:57:49.763`, group audio started `10:57:52.831`, call ended `10:58:27.745`. So the
founder was on a 1:1 call, tapped **Add**, and was escalated into a group call — both reported
symptoms come out of that single flow.

### B-299 — a ring that could not be sent looked exactly like one that was ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED**

`useGroupCall.inviteUsers` opened `if (!ws || !roomId || userIds.length === 0) {return;}`. All
three conditions shared one exit, and that exit is a plain `return` from an `async` function — it
**resolves**. `GroupCallScreen.handleInvite` sets an optimistic 30 s "Ringing…" countdown and
clears it **only from its `catch`**, so when the transport or room was not ready the invitee was
never rung, nothing threw, and the host watched a 30 s countdown for nothing.

The window is real and common: right after an escalation the host lands on a _fresh_
GroupCallScreen whose `roomId` is still being assigned. This is a direct cause of "add call is not
working".

**Fix:** split the exits — an empty invitee list stays a quiet no-op ("nothing was asked for"), a
missing transport/room throws ("we could not ask"), so the caller's existing catch clears the
countdown and surfaces it. `src/modules/messenger/webrtc/useGroupCall.ts:4098`.
**Test:** `invitePhantomRing.test.ts` (3, mutation-proven RED before the fix).

### B-300 — a mid-call invitee is rung but never KEYED ⚠️ **P0** · **FIXED**

`inviteUsers` sends `sfu.ring` and nothing else. Both `ensureCallGroupKey` call sites —
`useGroupCall.ts:1583` (host boot) and `:1685` (owner join-resync) — pass **`opts.recipientUserIds`**,
the recipient list captured at screen **mount**. A user added mid-call is not in that list, so the
group master key is never fanned out to them. They accept, join, sit in `waitForGroupCallKey` for
the 25 s window, and fail closed.

Every heal path is closed to them on an **escalated (ad-hoc) call** specifically:

- the joiner's own `requestGroupKeyResync(opts.conversationId)` targets the reused 1:1 conversation
  id (`CallScreen.tsx:1864`, `const groupConvoId = conversationId`) — the invitee is not a member of
  that conversation;
- the owner's join-resync at `:1678` is gated on `shouldOwnerResyncOnJoin({isRealNamedGroup})`, and
  `isRealNamedGroup` requires `!conversationId.startsWith('direct:') && grp?.name !== 'Call'` — an
  ad-hoc escalated call is exactly `name === 'Call'`.

So on the founder's exact flow the invitee **can never join**. This is the other half of "add call
is not working".

**Stop condition CLEARED, then fixed.** Group master key distribution is a CLAUDE.md stop
condition, which says to _verify against the architecture reference before proceeding_. Verified:
`docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE_AMENDMENT_SFRAME.md` states participants hold a key "derived
on-device from the group master key (**already distributed** via pairwise Signal sessions)" and that
"group master key rotation **on member-add** / member-remove triggers a frame-cryptor key rotation
in the same epoch". Member-add is REQUIRED to distribute — so the old behaviour was a **deviation
from** the documented design, not a design choice, and closing it is compliance rather than a
change of policy.

**Fix:** `inviteUsers` now calls `ensureCallGroupKey` with the UNION of the mount-time roster and
the new invitees, and does so **before** `sfu.ring`. No new crypto: `ensureCallGroupKey` already
handles this exact case — its resync branch is guarded by `others.every(uid => !!mapped.members[uid])`
(`productionRuntime.ts:5613-5620`), so a roster containing someone outside the minted state falls
through to a FRESH MINT covering everyone, which IS the amendment's rotation-on-member-add. A keying
failure aborts the invite and throws, so nobody is rung who cannot join; paired with B-299 that
throw clears the optimistic countdown and tells the host.

**Nothing was weakened.** The 25 s `waitForGroupCallKey` fail-closed gate, `verifySenderCert` and
the owner-forgery guard are untouched and pinned by an explicit assertion in the new suite — an
invitee who still ends up keyless still gets no media, never plaintext.
**Test:** `inviteKeyBeforeRing.test.ts` (5, mutation-proven RED before the fix).

**Follow-up (not done):** the amendment also implies existing participants rekey in the same epoch
on member-add. The fresh mint does re-key everyone, but the epoch-advance/rekey coordination for a
call already in flight was not separately verified on device — worth a targeted group-call test.

### B-301 — a failed escalation destroys the working 1:1 call ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED**

`CallScreen.escalateToGroupCall` (`:1856`) does `liveCall.hangup()` **before** the group room
exists, then `navigation.replace('GroupCallScreen', …)`. There is no rollback. The B-111-A
FrameCryptor gate is correctly placed _before_ the hangup, but nothing else is: if room creation
fails after that point the original call is gone and the group call never forms, so the user loses
the call entirely. Compounds B-299/B-300 — those are the failures most likely to fire here.
(GroupCallScreen does render `'Call failed'` with a `goBack()` path, so the user is told; they just
have nothing to go back to.)

**Fix — escalation is now ATOMIC, and it needed no new machinery.** CallScreen already knows how to
survive its own unmount with the call running: the `beforeRemove` listener minimizes any live call
("a swipe-back gesture must minimize a live call, never cut it — for every non-terminal state"),
setting `keepAlive` so `useCall`'s cleanup leaves the controller alone and the FloatingCallOverlay
takes over. **That path fires on `replace` too.** The only reason escalation lost the call is that
`hangup()` ran FIRST and drove the state terminal, so the minimize branch's `liveStates` check
stopped matching.

So `escalateToGroupCall` no longer hangs up at all. The 1:1 rides through the navigation, minimized,
and GroupCallScreen ends it via `endActiveCall('ended','local')` **only once `call.state === 'joined'`**
— matched on the `pendingDirectCallId` handed over in the route params, so an unrelated call that
started in between is never killed. Fail, time out, or back out before that and the 1:1 is still up
with the overlay as the way back: **either you land in the group call, or you keep the call you
started with.**

Side benefit for the other party: they used to be cut and then re-rung, with a real gap. They now
keep their working call until the room exists.

Two gates still guard the (now much cheaper) transition, and ORDER is pinned for both because a
gate after the navigation protects nothing: B-111-A (no FrameCryptor) and a new
`waitForLiveTransport(4000)` pre-flight — no relay means the room cannot be created at all, which is
exactly the flaky-network moment when someone reaches for "Add".
**Test:** `escalationPreflight.test.ts` (9, mutation-proven RED before the fix).

### B-302 — escalation silently discards the user's explicit audio route ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED**

`navigation.replace` unmounts CallScreen and mounts a _fresh_ GroupCallScreen, whose
`preferredRouteRef` is `useRef<AudioRoute | null>(null)` (`GroupCallScreen.tsx:364`). The explicit
SPEAKER the founder had chosen on the 1:1 leg lives in the destroyed screen. With the ref back at
`null`, the first `onAudioDeviceChanged` takes the "no preference yet" branch and auto-snaps to the
attached headset.

Device evidence — a paired _realme Buds Wireless 3_ (`98:47:44:4B:03:BD`) was connected throughout:

```
10:57:52.839 E InCallManager: selectAudioDevice() Can not select SPEAKER_PHONE from available []
10:57:53.707 D InCallManager: New device status: available=[EARPIECE, SPEAKER_PHONE, BLUETOOTH], selected=BLUETOOTH
10:57:53.708 D InCallManager: RNInCallManager.chooseAudioRoute(): user choose audioDevice = BLUETOOTH
```

Audio went into earbuds sitting on a desk. **That is the reported "audio output" symptom** — not a
dead route.

**Fix:** the route now travels with the escalation. New optional
`GroupCallScreen.initialAudioRoute` param (`navigation/types.ts`); `escalateToGroupCall` passes
`preferredRouteRef.current ?? undefined` (`CallScreen.tsx:1875`); GroupCallScreen seeds
`preferredRouteRef = useRef(initialAudioRoute ?? null)` and opens on that route instead of the
media-type default, so the audio does not audibly flap either. A call that did NOT come from an
escalation still passes `undefined` ⇒ no preference ⇒ the B-297 auto-snap is unchanged for it —
pinned by its own assertion so the two are never traded for each other.
**Test:** `escalationRouteHandoff.test.ts` (4, mutation-proven RED before the fix).

### B-303 — `jsThreadWatchdog` measures with a wall clock, so an NTP step reads as a freeze ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED**

`src/utils/jsThreadWatchdog.ts` computes drift from `Date.now()`. This device demonstrably re-sets
its clock mid-session, and stall **#389 (2425 ms)** sits on a clock step plus a `TIME_SET` broadcast
— it is not app work. CLAUDE.md already documents the _backgrounded-app_ false positive (trap #1);
this is a second, independent false-positive source in the same probe, and it inflates the very
numbers that section tells future sessions to trust.

**Fix:** drift is now computed from `performance.now()` (monotonic, immune to clock steps), via a
`_selectMonotonicNow` seam that falls back to `Date.now()` where `performance` is absent. The
source is resolved on **every call** rather than captured at import — capturing binds whichever
`performance` existed at module load, and RN does not guarantee it installs its own before this
module loads, which would have left the watchdog on the wall clock forever.

**The existing B-285 suite went RED against this fix, and that was the finding, not an obstacle:**
its `stall()` helper faked a stall with `jest.setSystemTime(Date.now() + ms)` — it was using a
wall-clock step as its _definition_ of a blocked thread, i.e. the suite encoded the bug. The helper
now advances the monotonic clock instead. **Test:** `jsThreadWatchdogClock.test.ts` (4) plus a new
`B-303 — a WALL-CLOCK step is not a stall` case in `jsThreadWatchdog.test.ts` replaying the exact
#389 device repro (2425 ms NTP step ⇒ zero stalls reported).

Note stall **#386 (6641 ms)**, mid-call, is **not** a regression from the pulled commit — the same
magnitude appears in the pre-session buffer (`worst 7932ms` was already banked before this call).

### Also observed — not separately numbered

- **The whole call-audio + add-call path is invisible in release builds.** Every diagnostic on it is
  `console.log`, which `transform-remove-console` strips (`babel.config.js:26-32` keeps only
  `error`/`warn`). Sites incl. `callAudioSession.ts:40,46`, `GroupCallScreen.tsx:253,256`,
  `CallScreen.tsx:145,1067,1159,1163,1166`, `callForegroundService.ts:66,72,113,121`,
  `useGroupCall.ts:4121`. This is why a release logcat shows the native audio churn but almost no app
  reasoning behind it — worth a sweep to `console.warn` under a `[CALLDIAG]` tag.
- **No group/SFU ICE probe.** The 10:57 call emitted zero `[CALLDIAG] [WEBRTC] iceConnectionState=`
  lines while the earlier 1:1 calls emitted `checking → connected → completed`. This is a
  **diagnostic blind spot, not a regression**: the emitter is `callController.ts:1651` (1:1 only);
  the group path (`useGroupCall.ts:2031-2050`) has no equivalent. The call itself was healthy.
- **Mid-call "Add" on a video call is behind the 3.5 s chrome auto-hide** (`CallScreen.tsx:2601`), so
  a tap on a faded control does nothing visible — an aggravator for the "add call does nothing"
  report, independent of B-299/B-300.

### Gates (all six fixes)

- messenger-crypto: **361 suites / 3750 tests, 100% green** on a clean run.
- app project (`screens/messenger` + `jsThreadWatchdog` + keyboard): **24 suites / 264 tests** green.
- `tsc`: **46 errors vs the 47 baseline** — below the ratchet; every remaining error in a touched
  file is pre-existing (icon-name unions, `CallHandle.callId`, `RTCStatsReport`).
- Six new suites, **each mutation-proven RED before its fix**: `audioRoutePhantomApi`,

  `jsThreadWatchdogClock`.

**Flake note (extends B-126).** The crypto project was run FIVE times. Failures MOVE between runs
and two runs were fully clean: `computeSafetyNumber` fired on runs 1/3/5 and the P3-B-2
`owner-scoped backup flags` suite fired only on run 5. **Both pass in isolation** —
`computeSafetyNumber` 3/3, backup flags 8/8 — so this is the documented cross-suite state leak, now

evidence; check isolation before believing it.

**Not device-verified.** These are code + test changes. The Pixel 6a was on vc208, which predates

## B-304 — the messenger-crypto "moving flake" is a LEAKED DEBOUNCE TIMER (root cause; extends B-126 / B-153) ⚠️ P2 · **PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-13** — arming site closed, class still open

**Found 2026-07-27 while the release pre-flight blocked on it.** CLAUDE.md has told sessions for
weeks that `test:crypto` "has a history of intermittent, MOVING failures" and to run it twice. The
mechanism was never named. It is:

```
ReferenceError: You are trying to `import` a file after the Jest environment has been torn down.
From src/modules/messenger/__tests__/groupEventMessage.test.ts.
    > 17 | import {API_BASE_URL} from '@utils/constants';
  at getClient (src/modules/messenger/contacts/directoryNames.ts:17:16)
  at _flush   (src/modules/messenger/contacts/directoryNames.ts:70:17)
  at flush    (src/modules/messenger/contacts/directoryNames.ts:39:17)
  at Timeout._onTimeout (src/modules/messenger/contacts/directoryNames.ts:87:12)
```

`ensureDirectoryNames` schedules a **300 ms debounced** `flush()` (`directoryNames.ts:98`). Any
suite that transitively queues a directory-name lookup and finishes in under 300 ms leaves that
timer armed. It fires **after the environment is torn down**, `flush()` calls `getClient()`, and
touching the Babel-interop accessor for `API_BASE_URL` loads a module into a dead environment.

**That is why the failure MOVES.** Jest attributes the error to whichever suite happens to be
running when the orphaned timer fires — never the suite that armed it. Observed this session across
five full runs: `computeSafetyNumber` on runs 1/3/5, the P3-B-2 `owner-scoped backup flags` suite on
run 5 only, and two runs completely clean. **Both suites pass in isolation** (`computeSafetyNumber`
3/3, backup flags 8/8), which is the signature: they are bystanders.

This also explains why the flake got worse recently — B-253/B-254 and B-260 added
`ensureDirectoryNames` callers (chat list, call tiles, calls log, group-call invite roster), so far
more suites now arm the timer.

**Why it is not fixed here.** `_resetDirectoryNamesForTests()` already exists and clears
`flushTimer`, so the per-suite fix is a one-liner — but the leak can be armed from _any_ suite, and
the correct global fix is a `setupFilesAfterEnv` hook calling it in a global `afterEach`. The
`messenger-crypto` project currently defines only `setupFiles` (which runs before the framework, so
it has no `afterEach`), so this means adding a new config key that affects **all 361 suites**. That
is not something to slip in alongside a release, and a parallel session was editing the repo at the
time. Scope it deliberately.

**Fix shape when someone takes it:**

1. add `setupFilesAfterEnv` to the `messenger-crypto` project in `package.json`;
2. in it, `afterEach(() => _resetDirectoryNamesForTests())`;
3. mutation-prove by reverting and confirming a bystander suite fails again;
4. then DELETE the "run it twice" flake rule from CLAUDE.md — it is a workaround for this.

Until then the flake rule stands, with one refinement worth more than the rule itself: **a suite
that fails in the full run but passes in isolation is a bystander, not a break.** Check isolation
before believing any red run here.

### 2026-08-13 — what was actually done, and what it did NOT fix

**Landed.** `setupFilesAfterEnv` added to the `messenger-crypto` project
(`jest.setup.messenger-crypto.js`), but NOT in the shape sketched above. The sketch —
`afterEach(() => require('.../directoryNames')._reset...())` — was implemented, measured, and
**rejected**: it drags `@utils/constants` + `messengerStore` into all 429 suites and took the run
from **82.8s → 101.2s**. That 19s of extra load starves `safetyNumber.test.ts` until it times out,
i.e. the fix manufactures the very class of failure it exists to remove. A generic
"clear every timer armed during a test" sweep was tried first and is worse still — Jest schedules
its own per-test timeout machinery on the same global timers, so sweeping them took the run from
1 red suite to 3 and cost 25s.

What shipped instead is a **registry**: a module owning teardown-unsafe state adds its own cleanup
to `globalThis.__bravoTestCleanups` at load time (one guarded line at the bottom of
`directoryNames.ts`, a no-op outside this Jest project), and the setup file drains it in a global
`afterEach`. Cost is proportional — only suites that actually load the module pay. Full run is now
**~57-70s, down from 82.8s**.

Pinned by `directoryNamesTeardownSafety.test.ts` (5 tests), mutation-proven in BOTH directions:
delete the registration line → 3 of 5 red; delete `setupFilesAfterEnv` → 4 of 5 red. Each mutation
was verified applied (region printed) before the run, per the CLAUDE.md false-GREEN rule.

**`safetyNumber.test.ts` cap raised 60s → 120s.** Proven to be STARVATION, not logic: on the same
commit a 57s full run passes it and an 89s full run times it out, with the test unchanged. It has
not reappeared in 5 subsequent runs.

**What this did NOT fix — the class is broader than directoryNames.** Six full runs after the fix
produced a fully green run twice (**431/431 suites, 4355/4355 tests**) and these movers otherwise:

| Mover                                             | Runs seen            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `MD-08` freeSpace (`media/freeSpace.ts`)          | 2                    |
| `stopSharedAudioSession` (call audio arbitration) | 2                    |
| `P3-B-2` owner-scoped backup flags                | 1                    |
| `groupCallVideoEncodings`                         | 1 (pre-fix baseline) |

All pass in isolation. So `ensureDirectoryNames` was **one** arming site, not the only one.

### What the remaining movers ARE and ARE NOT — measured 2026-08-13

Four facts, each from a run, that narrow this a lot for whoever picks it up:

1. **It is NOT parallelism / worker starvation.** A full `--runInBand` run (431 files, one process,
   strictly sequential) STILL failed — `backupFlags` + `batteryOptimization`, 6 tests. Every
   "contention" theory for these suites is dead. (`safetyNumber` WAS starvation and is now fixed
   separately; do not conflate them.)
2. **It is order-dependent state leaking BETWEEN test files in one process.** `batteryOptimization`
   passes **5/5 alone** and fails only in company.
3. **It needs the full-suite context.** A 5-file cluster of the known movers run under
   `--runInBand` failed 1-of-3 once, then passed **6/6** — so bisecting on a small set is not
   viable. Reproduction requires the whole 431-file run.
4. **The failure signature is A MOCK NOT TAKING EFFECT**, not a timing error.
   `lowSpaceWarning()` returned `null`, which only happens when BOTH `require('expo-file-system/legacy')`
   and `require('expo-file-system')` fail — i.e. the suite's own `jest.mock` factory was not the
   thing that answered the require.

**Hypothesis tested and REJECTED — do not re-propose without new evidence.** `{virtual: true}` used
on modules that actually exist. It is factually true that this is misused (48 sites;
`expo-file-system` and `react-native-incall-manager` both resolve for real yet are mocked
`virtual`), and `virtual` does register in a resolver-level registry keyed by raw specifier that
outlives the per-file module registry — so it fit every symptom. **Removing it from both mover
suites changed nothing: 2 of 4 full runs still red, same suites.** The change was reverted rather
than left in, because its explanatory comment would have been a false lead for the next reader.

**Still-untested lead.** `media/freeSpace.ts:40` does a lazy `require('expo-file-system/legacy')`
**inside an async function**. The repo deliberately converted imports to in-function `require()` to
break boot-order cycles (**53% of the 46-file runtime cycle's edges are lazy requires**, documented
at `authStore.ts:11-16`), so this shape is everywhere — and a lazy require is resolved at CALL time,
against whatever resolver state exists then, rather than at import time. That is consistent with
fact 4 above in a way the virtual-mock theory was not.

**Do not delete the "run it twice" rule from CLAUDE.md yet** — step 4 of the sketch above is not
earned until the movers above are closed.

## B-447 — the messenger `productionRuntime.ts` import wall is a MAPPER GAP, not an architecture problem ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-13**

> Renumbered from B-435 on 2026-08-15: a parallel session claimed B-435..B-444 for the
> Channels vs2 review while this entry was uncommitted. Same lesson as the push-first rule —
> an sqa number is not yours until it is on origin.

**`src/modules/messenger/runtime/productionRuntime.ts` (10,070 LOC, the repo's most-churned source
file, 139 commits/12mo) had ZERO executable test coverage for its entire life.** ~50 suites "cover"
it by reading it as TEXT and regexing the string. B-124/B-125 (CRITICAL data loss), B-337/B-339 and
B-353 all shipped through a fully green suite because nothing could run the code.

**The cause was never its size.** The `messenger-crypto` project is `testEnvironment: node` with a
transform that skips `node_modules`, so any module whose import graph reaches a native/Flow-typed
package is unloadable. Control case that proves size is irrelevant: `runtime/applyGroupAdmin.ts` is
an ordinary 642-line module with 7 clean exports and it was **equally unimportable**. Splitting the
god file into 50 tidy modules would have produced 50 modules that still could not load.

**The wall was six specifiers deep**, peeled one full-suite run at a time:

| #   | Specifier                            | Reached via                                                      |
| --- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `react-native`                       | `runtime/runtime.ts` (Flow-typed ESM entry)                      |
| 2   | `@op-engineering/op-sqlite`          | `crypto/db.ts:13` (JSI)                                          |
| 3   | `@react-native-firebase/crashlytics` | `runtime/senderCertAdmit.ts` → `observability/crashlytics.ts:24` |
| 4   | `@react-native-firebase/analytics`   | same                                                             |
| 5   | `react-native-fs`                    | `media/mediaFiles.ts:18`                                         |
| 6   | `@craftzdog/react-native-buffer`     | same                                                             |

Six `moduleNameMapper` stubs — the pattern the project already used for `expo/virtual/env`,
`react-native-argon2` and `react-native-quick-crypto`. The whole messenger tree consumes exactly
**five symbols** from react-native (`Platform`, `AppState`, `DeviceEventEmitter`, `NativeModules`,
`PermissionsAndroid`) and exactly **one** from op-sqlite (`open`), so the stubs are small.

**Result: `productionRuntime.ts` now loads and `buildProductionRuntime` is a callable export.**
Pinned by `productionRuntimeImportable.test.ts`, which also guards the two riskiest mapper entries
so their removal names itself instead of becoming a downstream mystery. Total effort ≈45 minutes —
the prior estimate was "a day, or two weeks if there are boot-time side effects". There were none.

**Blast radius: I got this wrong first, and the way I got it wrong is the lesson.**

The stubs were initially placed in `src/modules/messenger/__tests__/__mocks__/`, matching the
existing convention for `expo/virtual/env`, `react-native-argon2` and `react-native-quick-crypto`.
**That convention is a trap for NODE MODULES.** Jest applies a manual mock for a node module
AUTOMATICALLY, from any `__mocks__` directory under the roots — no `jest.mock()` call required, and
with no regard for which project's `moduleNameMapper` referenced it. So the react-native stub
replaced the real react-native in the `app` project too (preset `react-native`, renders real
screens): everything outside its five symbols became `undefined` and **11 of 32 messenger screen
suites died at import** on `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'create')` the moment a
component hit `StyleSheet.create`.

**And it poisoned its own diagnosis.** The app-project run taken to establish a "baseline" was
taken with the untracked stub file already on disk, so the breakage measured identically with and
without the tracked change and was written up as _pre-existing_. It was not. It was mine. The
error was only caught by probing what `react-native` actually resolved to inside the app project
(`Object.keys(RN).length === 5`, exactly the stub's surface).

**Fix:** the six stubs live in `__tests__/__stubs__/`, reachable ONLY through an explicit
`moduleNameMapper` entry in the one project that wants them. `__stubs__` has no meaning to Jest —
that is precisely why it is correct. Pinned by `src/screens/messenger/__tests__/reactNativeNotStubbed.test.ts`,
which asserts the app project sees the REAL module (shape-based, so it also catches a partial mock
introduced some other way) and names the cause instead of leaving 11 suites failing as a wall of
unrelated import errors.

**Verified after the move:** `app` messenger screens **32/32 suites, 337 tests green** (was 11
failed / 15 red under the misplaced stub). `messenger-crypto` **431/431 suites, 4355/4355 tests
green** on 2 of 4 runs, import wall still down.

> **Rule for the next person:** a stub for a NODE MODULE must never live in `__mocks__` unless you
> intend it to apply to every project in the repo. Scope it with `moduleNameMapper` from a
> directory Jest does not treat specially. Corollary, learned the hard way: an untracked file is
> still ON DISK — `git checkout` of a tracked file does not give you a baseline.

**Deliberate design choice in the stubs:** `op-sqlite` and `react-native-fs` **throw on every
operation**. A plausible in-memory fake would let suites assert against a database that is not
SQLCipher and a filesystem without the private-cache guarantee — green tests describing a system
that does not exist. Making the module _loadable_ while making queries _fail loudly_ gets the
importability win without inviting storage assertions built on sand.

**This unlocks, it does not deliver.** Nothing behavioural is tested yet. The next step is porting
the highest-value text scanners into real executable tests — starting with the B-125 receive spine
and the shared-closure seam (`signCallOfferAuth` / `ensureCallGroupKey` / text-send all share
`certCache`, `ownStore`, `ownAddress`), which is where a one-line mutation was measured passing all
4,338 tests green.

## B-305 — on a video call the controls vanish out from under your finger ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED**

**Founder-adjacent:** logged while closing out the "add call is not working" cluster. Independent of
B-299/B-300/B-301 — those explain why an invite that WAS sent failed; this is why the tap may never
register at all.

The video-call chrome auto-hides 3.5 s after it becomes visible, and the effect re-ran only on
`[isVideoUI, callState, chromeVisible, addPickerOpen, routePickerOpen, dialpadOpen]`. **Using a
control changes none of those**, so the countdown kept running from the original reveal no matter
what the user was doing.

Tap the video to reveal the chrome, spend three seconds deciding, reach for "Add" — at 3.5 s
`setChromeVisible(false)` unmounts the entire control tray. It is a conditional RENDER
(`chromeVisible ? (<View style={styles.videoControls}>…)`), **not an opacity fade**, so a press
already in flight lands on a view that no longer exists and nothing happens.

Note the earlier framing ("the button is faded, so a blind tap does nothing") was wrong in
mechanism — the controls are unmounted, not faded — but right that the button is unreachable. The
real defect is that the timer measured the AGE of the reveal rather than idleness.

This also mis-reads as the app being unresponsive, which is precisely the misattribution CLAUDE.md's
lag section warns about: it is not a JS stall, the view is simply gone.

**Fix:** a `chromeActivityTick` bumped by `tap()` — the single wrapper every control's `onPress`
already funnels through, so it sees every interaction — added to the effect deps. The effect
re-runs, its cleanup clears the pending timeout, and a fresh 3.5 s starts. The countdown now
measures **idleness, not age**. The pre-existing modal-open guards already encoded this intent
("the picker modals reset the timer so the chrome doesn't snap away mid-interaction"); they just
never covered ordinary control taps, which are the common case.

**Test:** `chromeAutoHideActivity.test.ts` (4, mutation-proven RED before the fix). It also pins
that auto-hide still EXISTS and that the picker guards survive — a "fix" that simply stops the
chrome hiding would trade this for a worse bug (the immersive full-bleed video is the point).

**NOT in v1.0.178 (vc209)** — landed after that build's JS bundle was written. Ships next build.

## 2026-07-27 (evening 2) — messenger lag on low-end devices: BACKUP PIPELINE INSTRUMENTED (probes, no fix yet)

**Founder:** "the messenger module is laggy and a low-end device like the Redmi 14C is hanging,
from the backup page to all."

**Doctrine check first (CLAUDE.md lag section):** eight candidates are MEASURED DEAD ENDS — none
re-proposed. The named untested lead is the per-send backup work, and the founder's report points
at exactly it. Per BACKUP_LOOP.md this session did NOT change any backup behaviour — probes only.

**Two structurally suspicious costs found by code read (NOT yet measured — that is what the
probes are for):**

1. `messageMirror.markDirty` runs on EVERY message mutation (receipt, status flip, reaction) and
   is O(seenIds + every hydrated conversation list) per call — `for (const k of seenIds)` over a
   set that holds one entry per mirrored message VERSION, then a linear scan of
   `Object.values(state.messages)`. Cost grows with history; bursts pay it N times. Matches the
   "one ~350-500ms stall PER MESSAGE, compounding" capture in CLAUDE.md.
2. The backup page's Enable path: `backupNow` (SQLCipher `loadAll()` of the ENTIRE history +
   enqueue every row) → `drainMirrorOutbox` (serialize + AES-GCM per row, whole history, one
   sitting) → `commitMerkleRoot` (server page-walk + sha256 over every leaf) — all on the JS
   thread, on the button press. On a Redmi 14C-class SoC with real history this IS a hang.

**Probes added (metadata-only console.warn, release-visible; logAudit green):**
`[LAGDIAG] [backup.markDirty]` (AGGREGATED ≤1 warn/s — the probe must not become the stall),
`[backup.flush]` (≥100ms), `[backup.drain]` (≥250ms or ≥100 rows), `[backup.bulkWalk]`
(≥250ms or ≥500 msgs, sql/memory source tagged), `[backup.merkle]` (≥250ms or ≥200 rows) —
timing wraps the SERIALIZED wrapper only; `commitMerkleRootUnserialized` and `verifyMerkleCommit`
are byte-identical (I3 untouched). **Pins:** `backupLagProbes.test.ts` (7).

**Measurement protocol (next device session, Redmi/low-end, release build v1.0.179+):**
reproduce the founder's flow (backup page → enable; then normal chatting) and correlate
`[LAGDIAG] JS thread blocked` stalls against the five probe tags. Interleave A/B runs per the
doctrine. THEN fix what the numbers name — candidate shapes if confirmed: markDirty prefix-index
instead of full-set scan + per-conversation message lookup; chunked/yielding drain (the
bootstrapDrainYield pattern from B-155); moving GCM/sha work off the JS thread is a bigger
conversation (arch review — crypto placement).

**Gates:** backup+merkle+logAudit suites 14/79 green; full messenger-crypto **369 suites / 3797
tests green**; `tsc` 46 vs 47 baseline.

## 2026-07-27 (evening 3) — FIRST MEASURED NUMBERS from the v1.0.179 probes (Pixel 6a, fresh-install restore + rapid-send burst)

**Restore (fresh install → sign-in → restore, ~100-message history):**

- End-to-end ≈ **60–70 s** (sign-in 15:35:34 → mirror settled 15:36:43); verifier passed; ONE
  undecryptable skipped (known class, logged, non-fatal).
- Two JS freezes during the identity/runtime-rebuild phase: **4122 ms + 2072 ms** (stalls #3/#4).
- **10,729 sqlcipher ops** in the restore window for ~100 messages (≈100 ops/row — snapshots,
  sessions, selects; the message INSERTs themselves are already batched per page via
  `upsertBatch`, so batching is NOT the missing lever).
- **72 rows re-uploaded by the mirror right after restore** (`[backup.flush] rows=50+22`) — the
  B-94 ledger seed should make this ~0; suspect the seeded version-hash differs from
  `mirrorMessage`'s computed hash so the catch-up sweep re-enqueues everything once. Bounded,
  one-shot, but it is I1-adjacent — worth a look. (**candidate B-310** — number not yet claimed)
- SQLCipher logs ~10k `mlock() errno=12` (ENOMEM) warnings — RLIMIT_MEMLOCK; cosmetic, the
  memory-security setting itself is arch-relevant, leave.

**Rapid-send burst (15:38:07–35, founder repro "rapid messaging not possible"):**

- A stall every ~670 ms, alternating ~150 ms / ~280 ms — the same per-send-stall shape as the
  2026-07-26 capture (then 350–500 ms).
- **THE BACKUP LEAD DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT on this device/history size** — measured:
  `[backup.markDirty] n=73 totalMs=17` (trivial), NO flush/merkle/drain tags inside the burst
  window. The named lead is cleared _at this history size_; it may still bite at Redmi-scale
  history (markDirty is O(seenIds) — seenIds here was only 73).
- SQLCipher activity clusters land on the stall timestamps TO THE MILLISECOND (15:38:09.02 /
  .12.14 / .13.58), but writes go through op-sqlite's **async** API on a worker thread — so the
  JS-thread cost is the per-send JS work AROUND the write, not the write itself.
- **Why the old instrumentation missed it:** the 2026-07-26 send-stage probes fired only at
  > 120 ms PER STAGE. Eight stages × ~30 ms each = a 240 ms felt stall with zero probe lines.
  > **Next probe (small, safe): a per-send STAGE-SUM probe** — one warn per send with the summed
  > per-stage breakdown, no threshold per stage. productionRuntime is MESSAGE_LOOP territory —
  > probes only, run its §7 gates.

**Verdict for the founder:** restore WORKS and is honest (fail-closed held, no root_mismatch);
it is not fast — the fixed identity-phase freezes (4.1 s + 2.1 s) and the one-shot 72-row
re-upload are the two measured, improvable costs. Rapid-send lag is real, now reproduced with
probes armed, and the backup mirror is (at this scale) NOT the cause — next session: stage-sum

## 2026-07-27 (evening 5) — B-310: THE MESSENGER LAG CULPRIT IS MEASURED, plus GAP-1..4 shipped

### B-310 — the debounced Merkle commit blocks the JS thread for SECONDS at real history size ⚠️ **P1** · **FIXED** (2026-07-27 late)

The probes landed the kill shot on the Pixel 6a at the founder's REAL history size (post-restore,
~1372 backup rows):

```
15:56:44.367  [LAGDIAG] JS thread blocked ~4698ms (stall #385, worst 6639ms)
15:56:45.140  [LAGDIAG] [backup.merkle] tookMs=9528 rows=1372 seq=1196
```

**9.5 s of merkle work over 1372 rows, co-timed with 4.7 s (worst 6.6 s) JS-thread stalls.** The
commit page-walks the server AND sha256-hashes every leaf on the JS thread, debounced 5 s after
every flush — so it re-runs after every message burst, and its cost GROWS with history. This is
CLAUDE.md's "per-send work" lead confirmed with a name and a number, and it scales exactly like
the founder's reports (fine when new, "laggy/hanging" as history grows; worse on a Redmi 14C).
Note the burst-window stalls (~150–280 ms/message, 15:38 window) remain a SEPARATE smaller cost —
the stage-sum probe is still the next step for those.

**Fix shape (BACKUP_LOOP-gated, not improvised tonight):** (a) chunk the leaf hashing with yields
(B-155 pattern) so the walk never owns the thread for more than ~30 ms at a stretch; (b) cache
leaves incrementally (M-12 pre-hashed leaves already exist for restore — reuse for the live path
so a commit hashes only NEW/changed rows); (c) consider committing on an idle/AppState-background
trigger rather than 5 s post-flush. Verifier untouched in all three.

**Founder (on v1.0.180, frustrated, four reports):** (1) rows_count_mismatch banner is back

**(1)+(2) are ONE root: B-310.** The commit's full-history hash reached **9.5 s at 1372 rows**
(measured), which (a) blocked the JS thread → receives queued → "messages delayed", and (b)
stretched the flush→commit uncommitted window to ~15 s per burst → an app kill mid-commit
(`install -r` does this) or the OTHER device restoring inside the window fail-closes as
**rows_count_mismatch**. The verifier is CORRECT and untouched — the write side manufactured the
drift, exactly the BACKUP_LOOP's recurring shape, this time via commit COST growing with history
until it swallowed the safety margins. The I2 pending flag survives kills and heals on the
writer's next boot, so the founder's recovery = foreground the writer device ~30 s, then RETRY on
the failed device. Fail-closed, nothing lost.

**Fix (write-path scheduling ONLY):** new `computeMerkleRootYielding` in `backupMerkle.ts` —
chunked leaf hashing (default 100 rows/chunk) with a MACROTASK yield between chunks (microtasks
would not let queued receives run), reduced through the SAME `computeRootFromLeaves`; root
byte-identical by construction. `commitMerkleRootUnserialized` walk now uses it + yields between
server pages. **`verifyMerkleCommit` is byte-identical-untouched** (stop condition) — pinned by a
dedicated scan ("STOP CONDITION — verifyMerkleCommit still uses the synchronous path").

**Tests:** `merkleYieldingRoot.test.ts` (12) — root-identity property at 0/1/2/3/7/100/257 rows,
order-independence, yield-count assertion, zero/negative-chunk totality, commit-uses-yielding scan,
verifier-untouched scan. **Gates:** backup/merkle/mirror/restore battery **34 suites / 259 green**;
full messenger-crypto run 1 CLEAN (exit 0); run 2 in flight (flake rule).

thread blocked` stalls during commits should collapse from ~4700 ms to <150 ms ticks; burst
messaging stays responsive; the uncommitted window shrinks in practice because commits stop being

## 2026-07-27 (night) — B-311: the restore/commit DEADLOCK behind the founder's stuck RETRY ⚠️ **P0** · **FIXED**

**Device evidence (Pixel 6a, vc211, live capture during the founder's RETRY presses):**

```
20:02:39  [backup.merkle] root_mismatch rows=1406 committed=1403 seq=1234
20:02:39  grown set is NOT an additive superset of the signed root — hard fail
20:02:39  [bravo.restore.bg] failed: rows_count_mismatch
20:03:37  (byte-identical repeat — RETRY does nothing)
```

**Three composable facts, all now proven:**

1. The P2-B-1 additive-prefix check assumes "post-commit uploads always sort after the committed
   tail." FALSE for the re-upload path: a receipt/reaction/status flip re-encrypts an OLD row in
   place — same `(msg_created_at, message_id)` sort position, NEW leaf — so the device's OWN
   legitimate writes read as substitution and the benign-growth self-heal refuses.
2. The rightful healer is the device's I2 pending commit — which the boot catch-up sweep fires
   unconditionally whenever the flag is set (`mirrorBootstrap` sweep). But that sweep only runs
   from `startMirrorBootstrap()`, which is called ONLY on restore SUCCESS.
3. The restore-resume re-arms every boot. So: verify blocks restore → restore blocks the heal →
   RETRY loops forever. (B-81's `repairBackupCommit` cannot break it either: it requires
   `isMirrorEnabled()`, false in the deadlock state.)

**Fix — the deadlock-breaker at the existing B-81 seam** (`restoreBackground.ts` walk catch):
on `rows_count_mismatch`, IFF `readMerkleCommitPending(owner)` — the I2 flag proving THIS device
owes a commit — run `commitMerkleRootNow(owner)` (needs only the crypto store, available
pre-mirror), then ONE retry, sharing B-81's one-repair-per-start budget. **Zero new trust
exposure:** this is the SAME unconditional heal the boot sweep already fires on the same flag;
only the moment changes. **No laundering:** without the flag the hard fail stands byte-identically

### B-313 — restore must tolerate LOW NETWORK ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28, device verify pending)

Founder requirement after tonight: the restore survives bad network (cursor resumes, nothing
lost) but does not TOLERATE it — one timed-out fetch aborts the run into a hard banner needing a
manual RETRY (3× tonight until Wi-Fi). Design: (1) per-page retry with backoff 2s/8s/30s+jitter
inside the walk; (2) sustained failure → quiet "waiting for connection…" auto-resume state
(connectivity listener + cursor), hard banner only after ~5 failed rounds; (3) halve page size on
repeated page timeouts; (4) same treatment for the heal commit's server walk. Client-only, no
trust-model changes, testable in the runner harness.

**Implemented (W1 of MESSENGER_STABILITY_PLAN_2026-07-28):** new `backup/netRetry.ts`
`withNetRetry` — retries ONLY `BackupError kind='network'` (everything else rethrows on first
throw), delays 2s/8s/30s ±25 % jitter, cancellable between attempts. Wrapped around the restore
conversations/messages page fetches (`restoreMessages.ts`) and the commit walk's page fetch
(`merkleCommit.ts`). On top: `restoreBackground.ts` catches a network-class run failure and,
up to `NET_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS=5`, parks in a quiet `Waiting for connection…` running state
(cancellable pause, backoff base 10 s), then re-invokes the run — the cursor resumes where it
left off; the hard banner appears only after the 5-round cap. Gates: `netRetry` (6),
`restoreBackgroundRunner` round-2 + network describes (10), crypto suite green ×2, tsc 46 ≤ 47.
**Device verify pending** next APK: start restore on LTE, toggle airplane mode mid-run → expect
quiet auto-resume, no banner, restore completes.

## 2026-07-28 — W3/W4 stability sweep: eight verified findings (B-315..B-322) · fixes in flight

Mapped by three parallel code audits (send path, receive path, call matrix), each claim
symbol+line verified. Line numbers below were true at audit time — re-grep the symbol.

### B-315 — HTTP drain head-of-line block: one stuck envelope starves everything behind it ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28, device verify pending)

`drainRelay` never passes `after` to `relay.pull` (productionRuntime.ts:9193; server
`envelope.controller.ts:151` → `afterTs=0`) and only an ACK removes an envelope from the head.
Every leave-on-relay branch (`cert clock window :9349`, `LeaveOnRelayError :9387`, transient SQL
:9395/:9462, identity-refresh :9472) `continue`s without acking — so 50 head envelopes stuck on
any of those make every envelope behind them unreachable by the HTTP catch-up path until the
30-day dwell. The B-126 "page made no progress" warn (:9536) then aborts the drain with NO
scheduled retry (drainPump has no stuckMs; no periodic tick). This is the founder's 2026-07-27
log line and the likely mechanism of "message losing/delayed" after offline stretches. Fix: in-run
paging cursor (advance `after` past a zero-progress page within one drain run; stuck envelopes
stay on the relay for the next run) + a transient redrain nudge after an aborted run.

### B-316 — disappearing-message expiry destroys under clock skew, then lies ✓✓ ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28: skew grace shipped BOTH sites — live + stash twin; the ✓✓-on-genuine-expiry disposition kept deliberately, see entry)

Receive drop (productionRuntime.ts:8121) compares the SENDER-stamped `expiresAtSec`
(:2910, sender's clock) against the receiver's `Date.now()` with ZERO tolerance. ChatScreen
offers 30 s / 5 min TTLs — a receiver clock 5 min fast destroys every such message on arrival,
silently (bare return, no destroyed-note) and acks `delivered`, so the sender sees ✓✓ for a
message that never rendered. The only found place where modest skew DESTROYS instead of
deferring (M6 posture). Also: the AAD comment at :8053 still says "±15min window" — the shipped
bound is `SEALED_AAD_FUTURE_MS` = 24 h. Fix: skew grace on the expiry compare + honest handling.

### B-317 — pending-map LRU eviction red-flags a message that is still queued ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28)

`trackPending` eviction (productionRuntime.ts:780-812) flips a still-`sending` bubble to
`failed` + setError WITHOUT checking `sqlOutbox` — directly violating the invariant stated at
:3858 ("while the row is still queued the bubble MUST stay 'sending'"). The row auto-sends
later; the red bubble invites a re-type = duplicate the relay cannot coalesce. Fix: consult the
outbox before the flip.

### B-318 — 1:1 burst ordering can invert on the receiver ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28)

1:1 `aad.ts` is stamped INSIDE sealPayload (:3690-3695) AFTER `certCache.getIssued()` +
`ensureOutgoingSession` — both can block on network. Concurrent sends (ChatScreen fire-and-
forget :1296) mean message A composed first can carry a LATER ts than B; receiver splices
strictly on `created_at` → renders B above A; sender's own device disagrees. The GROUP branch
stamps `sealedTs` before all per-peer work (:3132) — the asymmetry is the proof. Fix: stamp
compose-time ts once, next to the msgId mint, for the 1:1 branch.

### B-319 — answer-from-notification stuck on "Answering…" — ROOT CAUSE FOUND ⚠️ P0 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28, device verify pending — expect `[CALLDIAG] autoAccept waiting — controller not ready` then connect)

The founder's repro (#3 of 2026-07-27). Chain: notification accept navigates CallScreen with
`autoAccept`; on first mount `iceServers` is null (async fetch :549-626) so `useCall` has NO
controller yet — but `state==='ringing'` and `incomingSdpKey` are already true, so the
auto-accept effect (CallScreen.tsx:953-986) passes every gate, latches
`autoAcceptedRef.current=true` (:966) and calls `accept()` → `await controllerRef.current?.
accept()` on a NULL ref (useCall.ts:1082) = silent no-op. The latch never resets; the dead-offer
watchdog DISARMS on that same ref (:1787/:1792). Result: "Answering…" forever, no timeout.
Secondary: (S3) cold-launch stack is seeded with CallScreen as the ONLY route, and CallScreen
has zero `canGoBack` fallbacks (:431, :1645) → failed answer = inescapable screen (GroupCallScreen
fixed this as B-213); (S2) the ring notification is dismissed BEFORE waitReady can fail → ring
lost with no missed-call record. Fix: gate the latch on a real controller (accept() returns
false on null ref), re-fire when the controller lands, canGoBack fallback, [CALLDIAG] trail.

### B-320 — launchCall group branch bypasses ALL busy guards + clears a live group call without leaving ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28)

(a) `launchCall.ts:263` group branch returns at :319, ABOVE the 1:1 busy guard (:326) — and no
guard checks the OTHER registry. On a live 1:1 (full or minimized) or group call, launching a
group call proceeds: two live calls, double audio sessions, FloatingCallOverlay hides the 1:1's
End control (W4.1/W4.4/W4.8). (b) Worse: :299-304 clears a DIFFERENT live group call with
`setActiveGroupCall(null)` — which does NOT call leave() (contrast useGroupCall.ts:819-825 which
captures `existing.leave` first) → orphaned SFU transports, frozen tile for every peer, audio
session/FGS never torn down. Fix: hoist a combined busy check above the group branch; capture
stale.leave before nulling.

### B-321 — a group ring parked behind a MINIMIZED 1:1 is never consumed ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28; missed-bubble on TTL expiry remains a P3 residual)

The B-306 park's ONLY consume site is `CallScreen.dismissCallScreen` (:402) — reachable from 4
in-screen terminal paths only. All three minimize paths bypass it; FloatingCallOverlay and
`endActiveCall` never touch the mailbox; `peekPendingGroupRing` has zero production callers. So:
group ring during a minimized 1:1 → parked → 1:1 ends while minimized → nobody consumes → 45 s
TTL discards it. No ringtone, no ring screen, no missed-call record (the missed-bubble writer
lives only in IncomingGroupCallScreen, which never mounted). W4.6 variant: parked during
outgoing-ringing, answered call outlives the TTL → same silent vanish. Fix: registry-side
consume fallback when the 1:1 leaves the registry + missed-bubble on TTL expiry.

### B-322 — incoming 1:1 during the outgoing-call boot window silently kills the outgoing call ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED** (2026-07-28)

`MainNavigator.tsx:636-650`'s call-waiting branch keys on `getActiveCall()`, which is only
populated AFTER TURN fetch + getUserMedia (useCall.ts:840). In that window (up to ~6 s+) an
incoming offer falls through to :687 `navigate('CallScreen', …)` — RN6 param-replace on the
mounted screen re-keys useCall's boot deps, cleanup runs with a null controller, and the
outgoing attempt is abandoned: no bubble, no alert, callee never rung. The GROUP ring handler
already has the route-name fallback (:792-794); the 1:1 handler does not. Fix: mirror it.

**Also mapped, documented, NOT fixed this pass (feature-scale or P2/P3):** second group ring
over a live group call rings into call audio (needs park/banner parity); backgrounded FCM wake
rings over a live call (fcmBootstrap :1531 has no active-call check); W4.2 duplicated system
surface (reportIncomingCall raised before the busy branch). All in the W4 matrix in
`docs/planning/MESSENGER_STABILITY_PLAN_2026-07-28.md`.

# QA Session — 2026-07-29 · Founder notification triple (B-323 … B-325) · ROOT-CAUSED, code-level, fixes NOT applied

**Reported (founder, in-session):** (1) "notification is not synchronised — I messaged someone at
8 am, goes to 9"; (2) group messages should notify as **group name `g`** with the sender `a`'s
message under it; (3) entering the chat from a notification takes **2–3 s** for the message to
appear. Build context: v1.0.185 / vc216 (2026-07-28 fix-all build, includes GAP-1..4).
No device logs captured this session — every finding below is code-traced against HEAD `1a2bafd`.
(Note: the §14 Summary Table stopped being extended ~B-71; per the file's living convention these
are logged as a dated entry only.)

### B-323 — notifications never show the message's SEND time; every path stamps draw-time ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-29 (⚠️ SERVER deploy owed; device verify pending)** — see the fix entry below

**Symptom:** message sent at 8:00 surfaces as a notification that reads 9:00 — the notification
clock is "not synchronised" with the chat, which correctly shows 8:00.

**Root cause — the send timestamp is dropped at every layer of the pipeline:**

1. **Warm store-notifier path:** `backgroundMessageNotifier.ts` `onStoreChange` has the
   authenticated send time in hand (`tail.created_at`, derived from sealed `aad.ts` via
   `sentAtFromAad` — the same value the chat bubble renders) but `post()` forwards only
   `{title, body, senderName, badgeCount}`. `showMessageNotif` has **no timestamp parameter**.
2. **The card stamps draw-time:** `callNotification.ts` `showMessageNotif` builds the
   MessagingStyle card with `timestamp: Date.now()` (both the thread-accumulate branch and the
   single-message branch), and the `displayNotification` android block sets **no
   `timestamp`/`showTimestamp`** — so the shade header time = post time too.
3. **Killed path can never know:** the server wake payload is
   `{kind:'msg-wake', conversationId:'', senderUserId}` (`push.service.ts` `sendChatWake`) —
   **no sent-at field** — so `fcmHeadless.ts` couldn't stamp the real time even if the client
   plumbing existed.

**Effect:** any delivery lag (Doze deferral, the 6 s `CHAT_DEBOUNCE_SEC` trailing wake, offline
drain, killed-app late wake) is displayed as if the message were SENT that late. WhatsApp/Signal
stamp the card with the message's send time; we stamp when we happened to draw.

**The 1-hour lag itself is a separate question** this session cannot close without a captured
repro: if the banner truly ARRIVED at 9:00 for an 8:00 send, that is the delivery-latency class
(Doze/OEM restriction/token — B-48/GAP-3 lineage), not display. Retest to disambiguate: send to a
swipe-killed device, note wall-clock arrival vs the time printed on the banner vs the bubble time
in-chat; a banner that arrives at 8:00:05 but READS 9:00 would instead be device clock skew.

**Fix direction (for the dev session):** thread `created_at` from the notifier into
`showMessageNotif` → per-message MessagingStyle `timestamp` + android `timestamp`/`showTimestamp`;
add `sentAtMs` to the wake payload (server knows accept-time; display-only field) for the killed
path. Files: `src/modules/messenger/push/backgroundMessageNotifier.ts`,
`src/modules/messenger/push/callNotification.ts`,
`apps/messenger-service/src/push/push.service.ts`. Pin in `msgNotifConversationShape` (RED first).

### B-324 — killed-app GROUP message notification is titled/keyed/deep-linked to the SENDER's 1:1 🔴 P1 · **FIXED IN FULL 2026-07-29 (tap re-route + founder-approved Signal-style headless drain — killed banners now carry the real group name)** — see the fix entries below

**Symptom (founder ask #2):** group `g`, member `a` sends — the notification should be titled
`g` with `a`'s message under it. Today, with the app killed/frozen, it is titled with **`a`'s 1:1
display name** (or generic), and **tapping it opens the 1:1 with `a`, not the group**.

**Root cause — the wake never names the conversation, so the group-name path is DEAD CODE:**

- Both production wake call sites pass **only `senderUserId`**:
  `messenger.gateway.ts:1261` (`envelope.send`, "the WS gateway can't derive it under
  sealed-sender") and `envelope.controller.ts:129` (HTTP submit — and its own comment notes ALL
  group fan-out + outbox re-sends ride this path). `sendChatWake` then ships
  `conversationId: ''` in the FCM data.
- Client killed path `fcmHeadless.ts` msg-wake branch: `explicitConvId` is therefore **never**
  set → falls to `resolveDirectConversation(senderUserId)` → banner keyed
  `bravo-msg-sender:<uid>`/DM id, titled with the DM name, tap deep-links the DM. The B-65
  "group wakes resolve the group name" branch (`resolveConversationMeta(convId)`) and the same
  branch in `fcmBootstrap.ts` warm-fallback (~:1741) are unreachable in production.
- The WARM path is already correct (GAP-1, in vc216): store-driven notifier posts the
  MessagingStyle card with `title` = group name + `group: true`, per-message sender Persons.
  So the founder's symptom is specifically the killed/Doze-frozen path — the N-11/B-56 misroute
  "fixed" on warm only; the documented killed-path residual is now founder-visible.

**Why it matters beyond cosmetics:** the tap lands in the WRONG thread (a 1:1 that may have no
new message — reads as "notification lied"), collapse/mute/dismiss-on-read key to the wrong
conversation, and a user who mutes the group still gets bannered via the sender key.

**Fix direction — needs ONE decision:** put the conversation id in the wake. The client's group
fan-out KNOWS the group id at submit time; either (a) client sends `conversationId` as a
wake-hint field on the HTTP submit (⚠️ **stop-condition adjacent**: discloses group topology
(sender→conversation link) to the relay + FCM transport, which sealed sender currently hides —
needs System Architecture Documentation sign-off), or (b) keep the wire silent and accept the
killed-path limitation, closing this as WONTFIX-by-design with the warm path as the answer.
Do NOT half-fix by resolving group membership client-side from the sender id — a sender shared
across a 1:1 and N groups is unresolvable by construction. Sender-NAME-only titling (no group)
is a lesser interim: `resolveDirectPeerName` already exists on the killed path.
Files: `apps/messenger-service/src/relay/envelope.controller.ts`,
`apps/messenger-service/src/push/push.service.ts`, `src/modules/messenger/push/fcmHeadless.ts`.
Suites: `msgWakeWarmBannerRules`, `fcmHeadlessRouting` (DOCUMENTS-pin the current misroute if
not fixing).

### B-325 — chat opened from a notification renders the message only after the foreground drain (~2–3 s; worse on cold launch) ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-29 (tap-time pull + Signal-style headless drain: ingest now starts at WAKE time)** — see the fix entries below

**Symptom (founder ask #3):** tap the notification → chat opens on OLD history → the new message
"reflects" ~2–3 s later.

**Root cause — the banner is drawn WITHOUT the message; ingest starts only after foreground:**

- Killed path deliberately does **not** boot runtime/libsignal/SQLCipher/WS in the headless VM
  (`fcmHeadless.ts` msg-wake comment; the old headless task was removed for 2nd-VM contention —
  see also `callNotification.ts` header). The banner is generic; the envelope stays on the relay.
- The tap handler (`fcmBootstrap.ts` notifee PRESS → msg-wake branch) **navigates only**; the
  message arrives via the post-launch chain: runtime boot → WS auth/HTTP pull → decrypt →
  receive txn commit → store → ChatScreen render. 2–3 s is roughly that chain's floor on a good
  device; B-227 measured 10–25 s cold launches on low-end hardware (nav window raised to 20 s).
- The warm-background path does NOT have this gap (the store notifier posts AFTER commit — the
  message is already in the store before the banner exists). So the founder's 2–3 s = killed or
  Doze-frozen process, consistent with B-324's scenario.
- Industry parity: WhatsApp/Signal ingest during the push (headless websocket drain / NSE), so
  the thread is current the instant it opens. Ours is the repeatedly-deferred "Signal-style
  headless-drain decision" (N-10 §L, GAP-4 residual) — this entry formalizes it as
  founder-visible UX rather than a checklist line.

**Fix direction:** the real fix is the arch-gated headless drain (bounded: pull+decrypt+persist
under the Doze budget, no bundle publish — mind the B-107 restore gate which already guards both
handlers). Cheaper mitigations if the drain stays deferred: start the runtime boot+pull at TAP
time in parallel with navigation (today the pull starts only after nav settles), and show a
per-thread "updating…" affordance in ChatScreen so the gap reads as sync, not absence.
**Measured-numbers caveat (CLAUDE.md):** before optimizing, capture ONE tap-to-render timeline
on-device (`[LAGDIAG]` watchdog is already in place) so the 2–3 s is attributed, not assumed —
the boot chain shares the thread with hydration and any backup work.

### Cross-refs / evidence needed to close

- B-323/B-324 retest matrix (after any fix): swipe-killed device × {1:1, group} × {on-time,
  Doze-delayed} → banner title, printed time, tap target, in-chat time all correct.
- B-324/B-325 share the killed-path scenario — one instrumented repro session (Pixel 6a, release
  build, `adb logcat` on `fcm-headless|bgMsgNotifier|LAGDIAG`) can evidence all three entries.
- Lineage: N-11/B-56 (group misroute, warm-fixed 07-09), B-65 (generic killed banners, partial),
  GAP-1/2 (warm conversation cards, 07-27), GAP-3 (durable inbox, open), B-227 (cold-launch nav
  window), B-48 (token lifecycle — delivery-latency suspect for the 1-hour lag).

# Fix Session — 2026-07-29 · B-323 / B-324 / B-325 (founder notification triple) · gates green · UNCOMMITTED (verify-first)

Founder authorized fixes on the same-day audit above. Everything below is RED-first per the
bug-regression contract (9 behavior-changing tests confirmed RED against the unmodified source,
then flipped GREEN by the fixes). MESSAGE_LOOP §0 applies (`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts`,
`fcmBootstrap.ts` are trigger files); §5 caller census below; §7 gate order followed.

## B-323 — banners now carry the message's SEND time end-to-end · FIXED

- **Server** (`push.service.ts` `sendChatWake`): the wake data gains `sentAtMs` (relay accept
  time, numeric string; display-only metadata the relay already holds) on BOTH the Android and
  iOS lanes. Stamped inside `sendChatWake` so every caller lane (WS, HTTP, trailing debounce)
  carries it; a trailing wake restamps ≤6 s late — inside display granularity. ⚠️ **Server
  deploy owed** (and B-314 auto-deploy is still blocked → manual deploy).
- **Client** (`callNotification.ts` `showMessageNotif`): new `sentAtMs` param → MessagingStyle
  per-message `timestamp` + android `timestamp`/`showTimestamp` on the banner header. Absent or
  malformed → keys stay absent (never claim a time we don't have).
- **Feeders:** warm store-notifier passes `Date.parse(tail.created_at)` (the authenticated
  sealed `aad.ts` send time — same value the chat bubble renders); killed path + both warm-FCM
  draws parse the wake's `sentAtMs` via a shared `wakeSentAtArg` helper.
- Until the server deploy lands, old wakes simply lack the field → client falls back to today's
  draw-time behaviour (fail-open, no mixed-fleet hazard).

## B-324 — the guessed-DM banner no longer deep-links the wrong thread · TAP-TARGET FIXED (title arch-gated)

- The DM-heuristic draws (`fcmHeadless`, `fcmBootstrap` no-notifier lane) now mark the banner
  data `convGuess=1` via `showMessageNotif`'s new `convUnconfirmed` param — the guess is
  explicitly not wire truth.
- The tap handler treats `convGuess` (or a missing conversationId) as "re-resolve": it waits
  briefly (≤6 s) on the B-325 tap-time pull, then routes to the conversation holding the
  sender's NEWEST message (`resolveTapTargetAfterPull` — after a successful pull that is
  exactly the message the banner was about, group or 1:1). Dry pull / timeout → the guessed DM
  stays the fallback (no regression). First-contact bonus: a tap with NO resolvable thread can
  now land in the newly-created conversation instead of MessengerHome.
- **NOT done (arch-gated, unchanged from the audit):** titling the killed-path banner with the
  GROUP NAME requires the wake to name the conversation, which discloses the sender→group link
  to the relay + FCM — sealed-sender metadata the architecture currently hides. Needs System
  Architecture sign-off; the warm path (GAP-1 conversation cards) remains the correct-title
  path. P2-BR-5 mute semantics untouched (heuristic DM still never consults the mute list —
  its pin now asserts the guess marker too).

## B-325 — ingest starts at TAP time, not after ChatScreen mounts · MITIGATED

- New `startTapTimePull()` in `fcmBootstrap.ts`: the same guarded runtime-boot + `pullEnvelopes`
  the wake handlers use (B-107 restore gate honoured — never boots the runtime while the
  RESTORE gate holds), kicked at the START of the msg-wake body-tap branch so decrypt+persist
  race navigation instead of trailing it. Navigation never blocks on it except the B-324
  re-route. `pullEnvelopes` is the runtime's single-flight drain (shared mutex), so a parallel
  WS/mount pull cannot double-ingest.
- The FULL fix (Signal-style headless drain at wake time) stays arch-gated as before; this
  closes most of the founder's 2–3 s for warm/backgrounded taps and overlaps the chain for cold
  taps.

`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts:137` (post — sends sentAtMs from the store row; convId is
store-authoritative → no guess flag) · `fcmHeadless.ts:210` (sentAtMs + convUnconfirmed on the

# Fix Session — 2026-07-29 (same day, part 2) · SIGNAL-STYLE KILLED-APP DRAIN (B-324/B-325 residuals) · gates green · UNCOMMITTED

**Founder approval:** "yes do signal/whatsapp level" — resolves the arch decision above as
"no wake metadata; retrieve-then-notify instead" (the Signal `PushNotificationReceiveJob`
model). The killed-app msg-wake now boots the runtime, drains + PERSISTS, and the store
notifier posts the fully-resolved banner: **real group name title, sender Person, preview,
B-323 send time** — the same composition path the warm path uses, so there is no second
rule to drift. The generic/guess banner survives only as the fail-open fallback.

## What shipped

- **`push/headlessDrain.ts` (new):** `configureRuntimeFromPersisted()` rebuilds the EXACT
  MainNavigator runtime config from a persisted record (`msg:headless-runtime-config:v1`:
  ownUserId + ownerKey + the PUBLIC authority key, persisted verbatim so the two configs
  cannot drift; no tokens/private keys — the token getter reads storage live).
  `headlessDrainAndNotify()` = configure → `startBackgroundMessageNotifier({headless:true})`
  (BEFORE the pull, so watermarks baseline then every ingested row banners) →
  `getMessengerRuntime('production')` (its boot already `transport.connect()`s, which is
  what flushes the relay queue) → `pullEnvelopes()`.
- **`fcmHeadless.ts`:** msg-wake tries the drain FIRST under an 8 s budget
  (`HEADLESS_DRAIN_BUDGET_MS` — FCM high-priority Doze window); `'drained'` → done
  (silence after a clean drain = muted/own/nothing-new, which also kills the phantom
  banner a reaction/receipt wake used to draw); anything else → the pre-drain fallback
  banner, verbatim. **Fail-open contract: the drain can never make the killed path worse.**
- **`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts`:** headless mode — a headless VM has no activity so
  AppState can read `unknown`; in headless, anything ≠ `active` counts as backgrounded
  (else every banner is silently withheld). Reset on stop.
- **`MainNavigator.tsx`** writes the config record right after `configureMessengerRuntime`;
  **`authStore.signOut`** clears it (a wake after logout must never boot the runtime).
- **`fcmBootstrap.startTapTimePull`** also uses `configureRuntimeFromPersisted()` when the
  runtime is unconfigured — a notification tap on a cold (pre-UI) launch now starts
  ingesting before MainNavigator mounts (B-325 cold-tap hole closed).

## Safety gates (each pins a real incident class — all UNIT-PINNED)

RESTORE gate held → never boots (B-107 / Round-8 OPK-wipe class) · `hasDbKey(ownerKey)`
false → never boots (**a wake must never be the thing that KEYGENS an identity** — that
silently destroys restorability) · no/partial config record → never boots · store-persist
hydration awaited before ingest (its merge REPLACES `conversations`) · no
`_resetMessengerRuntime` from headless (would tear down a live runtime) · already-configured
runtime reused, never reconfigured (MainNavigator owns identity switches).

## Known trade-offs (stated, not hidden)

- The drain opens the WS briefly → the recipient can blip "online" while the phone is in a
  pocket. Signal has the same property; acceptable.
- A `timeout` outcome posts the fallback banner while the drain finishes best-effort → for
  a GROUP message that can mean fallback banner + resolved banner (1:1 collapses to one
  id). Read-dismissal clears both (the P3 member-id sweep).
- First-ever headless boot on a huge history pays SQLCipher hydration inside the budget —
  worst case is the timeout path above, i.e. today's behaviour.

## Tests + gates

`headlessDrainNotify.test.ts` (12, new): the three never-boot guards · already-configured
reuse · full-fidelity resolved GROUP banner (name/sender/preview/send time) through the
REAL store+notifier+callNotification · phantom-banner kill · `handleHeadlessFcm`
integration (drain wins → no generic banner; unavailable/failed → today's guess banner,
runtime untouched) · config record round-trip + MainNavigator/signOut wiring scans.
Gates: messenger-crypto ×2 → run A 384/387 (fails MOVED again: groupCallVideoEncodings /
safetyNumber / callAudioSessionArbitration — B-126/B-304 flake class), run B **387/387**;
final ×2 rerun on the finished code in flight at log time (see commit); app project FULL
728 ✓ (MainNavigator/authStore touched); tsc **46 ≤ 47**.

## Device-verify queue (supersedes part 1's B-324/B-325 items)

(a) swipe-kill → group message → banner titled with the GROUP name, sender + preview +
send time visible, tap lands in the group with the message ALREADY rendered; (b) same
with the sender's 1:1 muted → banner still posts (group ≠ DM mute); (c) reaction-only wake
→ NO banner (phantom kill); (d) logout → wake → no banner, no runtime boot in logcat
(`fcm-headless` tag); (e) fresh install pre-login → wake → generic fallback only;
(f) restore in progress → wake → fallback only, restore unharmed (B-107 watch);
(g) B-323 delay probe and warm-path regressions from part 1 unchanged. Logcat tags:
`fcm-headless`, `bgMsgNotifier`, `bravo.pullEnvelopes`.

## Still owed

Server deploy for the B-323 `sentAtMs` field (unchanged) · the device-verify queue above ·
commit rides the device pass (verify-first). The B-324 "arch decision" line above is
CLOSED (drain shipped; no wake metadata).

# Fix Session — 2026-07-29 (part 3) · founder device-pass findings B-326 / B-327 · FIXED · gates green

Founder testing v1.0.186 live (killed-app drain CONFIRMED WORKING on device — screenshot
shows the resolved conversation card with real names + message previews). Two new findings:

### B-326 — inline notification Reply sometimes fails: dropped on a cold VM, or insta-"tap to retry" ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (client; one residual documented)

**Reported:** reply typed into the notification sometimes doesn't send — the chat then shows
the bubble with "tap to retry".

**Root causes (two coupled):**

1. **Cold-VM drop (worst case, FIXED):** the Reply/Mark-read action branches called
   `getMessengerRuntime('production')` bare — on a FRESH headless VM (Android froze the
   post-drain process; notifee action boots a new one) that throws B-272 and the TYPED REPLY
   was silently dropped. The tap branch got `configureRuntimeFromPersisted` this morning;
   the action branches didn't. Fix: shared `ensureRuntimeForNotifAction()` (configure from
   the persisted record when unconfigured, then hand back the runtime) now used by all
   THREE action paths (tap pull, Reply, Mark-read). Pinned by `notifTapNavContract`
   (functional cold-VM reply + a source scan over both action branches).
2. **Pre-outbox failure → failed-terminal (RESIDUAL, documented):** the send pipeline is
   robust once the message reaches the durable outbox (classifyOutboxFailure →
   recordAttempt → bubble stays 'sending', connect-drain auto-retries). But a failure
   BEFORE the enqueue — sender-cert refresh / X3DH / seal, exactly what a Doze-gated
   network kills — flips the bubble straight to 'failed' (productionRuntime ~:3730) with
   no outbox row, hence "tap to retry" instead of auto-send. This is MESSAGE_LOOP's known
   M3 shape ("throw ABOVE the append"); the fix is the ordered M3 work item (move the
   outbox enqueue above the network-dependent stages), NOT an improvisation here. Until M3
   lands: a reply that hits this shows the retry chip and B-122's tap-to-retry delivers it.

### B-327 — notification shows a letter disc, not the sender's profile photo ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

**Root cause:** the app HAS profile photos (`directoryAvatars` URL map; `UserAvatar`
renders them everywhere in-app since B-253/254) — the banner composer never passed them,
so Android drew its default letter avatar. **Fix:** `showMessageNotif` gains
`senderIconUrl` → per-message MessagingStyle `Person.icon` (each accumulated message keeps
ITS OWN sender's icon — group threads mix senders); the store notifier feeds it from
`state.directoryAvatars[sender]` and, on a miss, queues the SAME debounced
`ensureDirectoryNames` backfill UserAvatar uses (B-261 lazy-require latch — `directoryNames`
must never enter this module's import graph, B-153) so the next banner has the face.
**Known residual:** `directoryAvatars` is not in the persisted vault slice, so the FIRST
banner after a cold headless boot may still show the letter disc (the backfill fixes the
thread's next banner). Persisting the avatar map is a store-contract change (M11 class) —
follow-up, not folded in.

**Tests (RED-first):** `msgNotifConversationShape` +2 (icon rides the Person; per-message
icons in mixed-sender threads) · `backgroundMessageNotifier` +1 (directoryAvatars →
Person.icon end-to-end) · `notifTapNavContract` +2 (cold-VM reply reaches sendText +
never navigates; source-scan: all action branches route through
ensureRuntimeForNotifAction). **Gates:** full messenger regression (crypto ×2 + app
messenger screens) run at commit time — see commit body; tsc 46 ≤ 47.

**Device-verify additions:** killed → reply from the notification with the screen off a
while → reply arrives (or at worst shows the retry chip, never vanishes) · sender with a
profile photo → banner shows the face (second banner at latest, cold-boot residual above) ·
reply on a freshly-rebooted phone (true cold VM) → sends.

### B-328 — group banner sometimes attributes the message to the WRONG sender (the group itself) ⚠️ P2 · FIXED · 2026-07-29 (part 3 addendum)

**Reported (founder, live device pass):** "who send msg it's sometime showing fault" — the
conversation card's sender line is sometimes wrong.

**Root cause:** for a GROUP message whose sender has no resolvable name yet
(`groupMemberNames[cid][sender]` and `directoryNames[sender]` both miss — the standard
cold-headless shape, since `directoryNames` is not vault-persisted), the notifier passed
`senderName: undefined` and `showMessageNotif`'s fallback chain (`senderName || title`)
substituted the CONVERSATION TITLE — modelling the GROUP as the author of the message.
B-226 added the directory fallback; this closes the both-miss hole behind it.

**Fix:** group senders with no resolvable name render as a neutral **"Member"** (never the
group title; 1:1 keeps the title fallback — there the title IS the sender), and a name miss
now also queues the standard `ensureDirectoryNames` backfill (one fetch fills names AND
avatars), so the thread's next banner upgrades to the real name + face. Pinned RED-first in
`backgroundMessageNotifier` ("a group sender with NO resolvable name NEVER borrows the
group title"). Suites: all 8 notification suites green (115).

# Fix Session — 2026-07-29 (part 4) · founder video-call pair B-329 / B-330 · FIXED · gates green

### B-329 — controls overlay needs a second tap after minimize→restore ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

**Reported:** 1:1 video call → minimize to PiP → restore to fullscreen → tap the video
area: sometimes the first tap does NOT hide the controls; the second does.

**Root cause (code-verified, NOT the stale-latch hypothesis):** `useCall` seeds `state`
as `'ringing'`/`'idle'` and the registry-adopt branch cannot run until `iceServers`
resolves — a NETWORK fetch (TURN creds, 6 s ceiling) that CallScreen re-issues on every
restore remount. For that whole window the restored screen reads
`callState === 'connecting'`, so the chrome tap-catcher (gated on `'connected'`) is
UNMOUNTED — the first tap lands on nothing — and the 3.5 s auto-hide timer never arms.
Same window made a restored INCOMING call flash the Answer/Decline ring surface
(CALL-N1's symptom family). **Fix:** seed the hook's state from
`callRegistry.getActiveCall()` when a live call with the same `callId` exists (fresh-boot
fallback unchanged — B-103/B-319 semantics preserved). Tap-catcher + auto-hide now arm
from the first frame after restore. Files: `src/modules/messenger/webrtc/useCall.ts`.
Pinned RED-first in `callMinimizeRestorePins.test.ts` (anchors absent at HEAD).

### B-330 — self-view PiP loses its 16px margin after repeated minimize→restore ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

**Reported:** the draggable self-PiP (local camera tile) renders flush to the screen
edge, off its 16px margin, after a second minimize→restore cycle.

**Root cause (code-verified):** two un-clamped paths in the PiP PanResponder, plus no
re-clamp on restore. (1) The responder had NO `onPanResponderTerminate` (B-242 class): a
stolen gesture (nav swipe / modal / ring overlay) never fired release, stranding the tile
un-flattened and un-snapped wherever the finger was. (2) A grab or tap mid-settle never
`stopAnimation()`d the corner-snap spring — the still-running spring finished against the
offset the new grant re-based, shoving the tile off the rails by the difference; the tap
path early-returns without re-snapping, so the error persisted. Nothing ever re-applied
the clamp on a later mount. **Fix:** shared `settlePipIntoBounds` (live `winRef` dims)
used by release AND a new `onPanResponderTerminate`; `pipPan.stopAnimation()` on grant
before the offset re-base; `onPanResponderTerminationRequest: () => false`; and a
mount/window-change re-clamp effect (no-op at rest, skipped mid-gesture) so a restore
always renders inside bounds. Files: `src/screens/messenger/CallScreen.tsx`. Pinned
RED-first in `callMinimizeRestorePins.test.ts`.

**Device-verify queue:** restore mid-call → first tap on the video hides the chrome ·
restore an incoming-direction call → no Answer/Decline flash · drag the PiP, grab it
again mid-spring → still parks on a corner rail with the 16px margin · minimize while
dragging the PiP, restore → tile inside bounds.
