### B-331 — killed-app headless drain swallows the live `call.offer` → Accept from the notification starves 🔴 P0 · **FIXED 2026-07-29 (client, uncommitted; device verify pending)**

**Reported (founder):** yesterday's build (vc215/vc216) answered calls from the
notification fine; after today's messenger/notification commits the Accept tap opens
"Answering…" and never connects. The phone still rings — only the accept dies.

**Root cause (code-verified, full chain + differential in
[`docs/handoffs/B-331_CALL_ACCEPT_FROM_NOTIFICATION_2026-07-29.md`](docs/handoffs/B-331_CALL_ACCEPT_FROM_NOTIFICATION_2026-07-29.md)):**
the B-324/B-325 killed-app drain (`aa68da9`, vc217) boots the production runtime on the
headless VM — `transport.connect()` at `productionRuntime.ts:1548` — so a killed phone
holds a live WS socket owned by a VM with **no UI**. A `call.offer` forwarded live into
that socket dead-ends in `callDispatcher.ts` (`:260`/`:267` — both the verified and the
legacy branch end in `if (handler) {handler(...)}`, and `onIncoming` + the S7 verifier
are registered only by `MainNavigator.tsx:534/:727`, which never mounts headless) → the
**offer is silently dropped**, nothing caches it. The gateway still parks the
offer + fires the wake (N-01) so the ring shows — but the parked-offer replay fires only
on a NEW socket connect, and the Accept launch attaches to the already-connected runtime
→ no reconnect → no replay → `resolveIncomingCallRoute` finds no SDP →
`CallScreen.tsx:982` blocks at `incomingSdpKey` forever. Intermittent because it needs a
msg-wake before the call within the process-survival window; a reaped process or a
watchdog `forceReconnect` inside the offer's 45 s Redis TTL recovers by accident.

**Cleared in the differential:** B-329's `useCall` registry seed (cold accept seeds
'ringing' unchanged; warm accept never remounts), B-330 (PiP-only), B-326/B-325 (same
hazard class but bounded — UI mounts seconds later), B-323/B-327/B-328 (display-only).

**Fix plan (NOT applied):** `callDispatcher.ts` no-handler branch caches the verified
offer via `setIncomingCallPayload` (tombstone-aware, write only after the S7 verifier
passes) instead of dropping — handoff §6 has the exact diff, the RED-first test spec
(`callOfferNoHandlerCache.test.ts`), and the do-nots (no headless navigation handler, no
drain revert, no verifier change). No server deploy needed (N-01 already parks + wakes
unconditionally).

**Baseline at diagnosis:** all 11 seam suites green (118 tests: `callFrameRouter`,
`callAcceptLatch`, `callAnswerStuck`, `callAnswerLifecycle`, `callNotifActionContract`,
`ringDedupPresented`, `invitePhantomRing`, `headlessDrainNotify`, `notifTapNavContract`,
`fcmHeadlessRouting`, `callMinimizeRestorePins`) — none models a null `onIncoming` with a
live headless socket, which is why CI stayed green while the device broke. Device repro
owed (two-device matrix in handoff §7 — no second signed-in device was available this
session).

**FIX (same session):** `callDispatcher.ts` — new `cacheUnhandledOffer()` + `else` on
BOTH offer branches: a verified (or legacy-branch) offer with no handler is now cached
via `setIncomingCallPayload` (NA-01 merge keeps the wake's callerName; tombstones still
refuse dead callIds; write sits inside the S7-verified `.then`, so forged offers stay
dead). Handler path verbatim-unchanged — the whole diff vs yesterday's `1a2bafd` is the
helper + two `else`s. **RED-first proof:** new `callOfferNoHandlerCache.test.ts` (6) —
the 3 cache-requiring cases failed at HEAD, all 6 green after. **Gates:** crypto ×2

### B-333 — stale "Waiting for this group's encryption key" banner over a rendering thread ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-29 (uncommitted; ships locally in vc222)**

**Reported (founder, screenshot):** Ari2, freshly added to "kotiss" (B-332 device test),
received and RENDERED the admin's "hi" — with the red no_key banner still stuck above it.

**Root cause:** the banner's only clears (B-213/B-262a) live inside
`drainPendingGroupInner` — they run only when a drain RUNS AND observes the group
not-key-blocked. Orderings where the key lands without a subsequent observed drain leak
the banner: the `drainsInFlight` skip race (a pre-key drain still in flight makes the
post-key `drainPendingGroup` call return WITHOUT draining — `productionRuntime.ts:7600`
— and the in-flight drain itself ran pre-key, so `stillKeyBlocked` stays true), or a
no_key set that lands after the drain's clear. `store.error` is global and sticky, so
the banner then outlives the sync it warned about — B-262a's misattribution hazard again.

**Fix:** the group receive parse-OK lane (the moment a payload provably DECODES under
our master key — `doHandleIncoming`, right after `parseResult.envelope`) now retires
both key banners with the same equality-guard discipline: only when `store.error` is
exactly `GROUP_KEY_PENDING_RECEIVE_ERROR` / `GROUP_KEY_DIVERGENCE_RECEIVE_ERROR`, so a
real, different error that landed in between survives. Drain-side clears unchanged
(both mechanisms now cover each other's blind spots).

**Tests (RED-first):** `groupKeyBannerLiveClear.test.ts` — the ok-lane clear scan was
RED at HEAD (only the drain-side clear existed), GREEN after; controls pin the
drain-side clear and both set sites so neither mechanism can silently vanish.
**Gates:** crypto full ×2 **392 suites / 4029 tests / 100% green both runs** · app
messenger screens 18/163 · tsc exit 0 ≤ baseline.

either never shows or clears the moment the message renders; control: a genuinely
keyless group still shows the banner until the key syncs.

### B-334 — "Add" during a group call never rings the invitee: the relay refuses a non-host ringer 🔴 P1 · **FIXED in code 2026-07-29 (SERVER — deploy OWED, not yet live)**

**Reported (founder):** "if we add another person in a group call by pressing add, that
person's phone call is not ringing."

**Root cause (proven from the STAGING RELAY's own log, not inferred):** `sfu.ring` is
gated host-only (audit row #5 / C3, `messenger.gateway.ts`). Any in-call member who is
not the room host is refused, so the invite never fans out:

```
07/29 3:00:43 PM WARN [SFU] ring rejected uid=1350939f rid=467fcf59 reason=not_host
07/29 3:03:14 PM WARN [SFU] ring rejected uid=88d34848 rid=9afc41c7 reason=not_host
```

Client side the refusal is only `console.warn('[bravo.groupcall.invite] failed:',
'not_host')` (confirmed in the Ari2 device logcat at 17:00:43) — no user-visible error,
so the inviter sees "nothing happened".

**Fix:** ring authority widened from _host_ to _host OR current room participant_.
New `SfuService.isParticipantUser(roomId, userId)`; the gateway gate becomes
`host === callerId || isParticipantUser(...)`. **The C3 anti-spam anchor is preserved:**
a participant only exists because the host's ring admitted them and `sfu.join` verified a
per-recipient HMAC room token, so ring authority still descends from the room creator.
Unknown room still returns `not_host` (no enumeration); both rate caps untouched.

**Tests (RED-first) in `messenger.gateway.sfu-auth.spec.ts`:** participant-non-host is
admitted and fans out 1 ring; an OUTSIDER (neither host nor participant) is still
rejected with `not_host` and emits nothing (C3 regression pin).

**STATUS: DEPLOYED TO STAGING + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-29** (founder-authorised).
`apps/messenger-service/src/{gateway/messenger.gateway.ts,sfu/sfu.service.ts}` synced to
`/home/admin/bravo/...` (backups `/tmp/gw.bak`, `/tmp/sfu.bak`), image rebuilt via
`docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml build messenger-service`, container
recreated. Clean boot: 4 mediasoup workers ready, Nest started, listening on :3100.
No mobile-side change is required — any installed build benefits immediately.

**END-TO-END VERIFICATION on the real devices (same user, same action, opposite result):**

|                     | uid        | relay verdict                                |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| BEFORE (3:00:43 PM) | `1350939f` | `WARN [SFU] ring rejected … reason=not_host` |
| AFTER (4:44:21 PM)  | `1350939f` | `[GROUP-CALL] ring rid=7b467713 → 1 user(s)` |

Driven live: host in the call on one instance, **Ari2 (non-host) in the call**, third
member outside; Ari2 pressed **Add → Ring**. Full success trail:

```
4:44:21 PM [GROUP-CALL] ring rid=7b467713 from=1350939f → 1 user(s)
4:44:21 PM push.voip.delivered sub=88d34848 call=7b467713 sent=1/1
4:44:21 PM [SFU] ring wake summary rid=7b467713 targets=1 pushed=1 throttled=0 dark=0
```

The invitee device showed no ring UI **only because this session had force-stopped its
app** to keep it out of the call — Android withholds FCM from a force-stopped package
until it is relaunched (it re-registered its VoIP token at 4:45:22, after the ring). The

### B-335 (NOT A BUG — investigation closed) — "Ari2 doesn't connect to the group call"

**Reported (founder):** after kick → re-add, Ari2 will not connect to the group call
while the other two connect easily.

**Could not reproduce; the opposite was proven.** Driven live on vc223 (the
`EXPO_PUBLIC_GROUPCALL_FILELOG=1` diagnostic build) across all three devices, with the
on-device trace pulled from each:

- Ari2 **joins normally** — `3 joined`, timer running, `E2E` badge, 157-164 ms RTT.
- **The E2EE key is healthy after the kick→re-add.** All three devices report the SAME
  `keyConvo=8b091751cb05 epoch=10 masterKeyFp=b1515a37`. A kick/re-add key divergence
  (the natural suspicion) is ruled out by fingerprint equality.
- Media matrix from the traces (tags: `d489d1`=host/BlueStacks, `013314`=Ari2/BlueStacks,
  `643ace`=Redmi/physical):

  | sender         | host receives | Ari2 receives | Redmi receives |
  | -------------- | ------------- | ------------- | -------------- |
  | Redmi `643ace` | dec **2805**  | dec **2466**  | —              |
  | host `d489d1`  | —             | rx **0**      | rx **0**       |
  | Ari2 `013314`  | rx **0**      | —             | rx **0**       |

  The physical phone's video reaches everyone and decrypts perfectly. **Neither
  BlueStacks instance produces any video at all** — and each shows its OWN self-preview
  tile BLACK (host screenshot `g998b-incall.png`, Ari2 `s908e-incall.png`), i.e. the
  failure is local to the emulator camera, upstream of the network and the crypto.

**Conclusion:** what reads as "Ari2 isn't connecting" is BlueStacks' virtual camera
producing zero frames, so every emulator participant renders as "Video unavailable" to
the others. Not an app defect. **Re-test needed on TWO PHYSICAL devices** before any code
change is considered — changing group-call join/key code on this evidence would be the
same guess-driven mistake the module was mis-fixed by once already.

**NATIVE-LAYER PROOF (founder asked to rule out any non-emulator cause).** BlueStacks'
own camera HAL opens the camera for our app and tears it down **146 ms later**, before a
single frame is produced:

```
18:05:44.145 I/Camera2ClientBase  Camera 0: Opened. Client: com.bravosecure.app
18:05:44.168 I/FslCameraHAL       openDev Opening camera device ok
18:05:44.202 I/FslCameraHAL       flushDev:0: Flushing camera device
18:05:44.291 I/FslCameraHAL       closeDev:0: Closing camera device
18:05:44.291 I/FslCameraHAL       state:0x201 can't go into stop state     ← HAL fault
18:05:44.472 I/FslCameraHAL       state:0x204 can't go into stop state
```

The app's side is provably CORRECT: `CameraService::connect` succeeded and the HAL's own
`openDev` returned ok — the emulator's stub HAL (`FslCameraHAL`, BlueStacks' i.MX camera
shim) then aborted itself. Corroborated by the ICE byte-rates: the physical phone pushes
**~70 KB/s** outbound (`bytesSent` 695 → 324,679 in 4.6 s = real video) while each
emulator pushes **~5 KB/s** (4,245 → 30,504 in 5 s = audio + RTCP only). Nothing between
`getUserMedia` and the SFU is at fault, and the FrameCryptor is provably keyed
(identical `masterKeyFp` on all three).

### B-336 — mid-call "Add" is swallowed by the ring dedup: the invitee is never rung 🔴 P1 · **FIXED (client + server) 2026-07-30 · server DEPLOYED**

**Reported (founder, twice — B-334 was only HALF of it):** "in 1:1 and group call, I add
another person in the call, that person is not rung." B-334 fixed the SERVER refusing a
non-host ringer; this is the CLIENT half, and it is why the bug survived that fix.

**Root cause — the recipient's own device threw the ring away.** After B-334 the relay
fanned out correctly and the push was delivered:

```
[GROUP-CALL] ring rid=9afc41c7 … → 1 user(s)
push.voip.delivered sub=… sent=1/1     ← server believed it rang them
```

…while the RECIPIENT's log showed:

```
17:02:51 [ring.dispatch] incoming room= 9afc41c7          ← first ring, presented
17:03:24 [ring.dispatch] dedup-suppressed room= 9afc41c7   ← the re-ring, 33 s later
```

`dispatchGroupRingFrame` deduped `sfu.ring.incoming` on **roomId alone** for a 60 s TTL
(Finding #8b / B-306, to stop a reconnect REPLAY resurrecting a dismissed ring), cleared
only by cancel/decline. A recipient who simply never answered therefore kept the marker,
and **every deliberate re-ring for that room inside the next minute was silently dropped**
— mid-call "Add" and the host's Re-ring both. A 1:1 escalation reuses the 1:1
conversationId as the room rendezvous, so it lands in exactly the same trap.

**Fix — per-fan-out identity, not per-room.** The relay now mints a `ringId`
(`randomUUID`) per `sfu.ring` invocation and repeats it on **all three copies** of that
fan-out: the WS `sfu.ring.incoming` frame, the VoIP wake `data`, and the queued
`PendingGroupRing` used by the reconnect replay. The client dedups on `(roomId, ringId)`.

- Replay of ONE fan-out → same ringId → still suppressed (**B-306 / #8b preserved**).
- A NEW fan-out → new ringId → presents (**the bug fixed**).
- No ringId (pre-B-336 relay) → key degrades to roomId → **exactly the old behaviour**,
  so an old relay can never start double-ringing.
- `cancel`/`decline` now clear EVERY `roomId:*` marker, not just the bare-roomId one.

`ringId` rides UNSIGNED alongside `fromUserId`/`callKind`/`conversationId` — the voip-wake
sig canonical form (`kind|callId|nonce|exp`) is untouched so old APKs keep verifying, and
it is dedup-only (admission is still HMAC- + room-token-gated). Killed-app lane needed no
change: it dedups per wake `nonce`, which is already unique per fan-out.

**Files:** `groupCallRingDispatcher.ts`, `push/fcmBootstrap.ts` (client) ·
`gateway/messenger.gateway.ts`, `push/push.service.ts` (server).
**Tests (RED-first):** `ringRenotifyPerRing.test.ts` (5) — the re-ring case was RED at
HEAD, the 4 preservation cases (replay dedup, handler-gap, cancel re-arm, no-ringId
back-compat) passed before AND after. `ringDedupPresented` + `addCallAuditPins` green.
**Gates:** crypto full ×2 — the only reds MOVED between runs (1 suite/3 tests →
`groupCallVideoEncodings` + `blockedPeersAndTombstones`, 19 tests) and both are **27/27
green in isolation** = the documented B-126 moving flake, gate green. Server tsc clean
(only the pre-existing missing `helmet` dep). **Relay DEPLOYED + healthy** (backup
`/tmp/push.bak`; 4 workers ready, Nest started, `Up (healthy)`).

**DEVICE-VERIFIED END-TO-END on vc224 (2026-07-30), two instances, same roomId:**

```
# fan-out 1 (host's boot ring)
08:49:04 [ring.dispatch] incoming room= 0d54f314 handlers= 1   ← PRESENTED
08:49:04 [ring.route] navigating / [ring.screen] mounted
08:49:05 [ring.dispatch] dedup-suppressed room= 0d54f314 ring= 5de6a430  ← its FCM copy, correctly dropped

# invitee LEAVES the call (no decline → the pre-fix marker would still be armed)
# fan-out 2 (a member presses ADD → Ring)
08:51:34 [ring.dispatch] incoming room= 0d54f314 handlers= 1   ← PRESENTED (was dedup-suppressed before)
08:51:34 [ring.route] navigating  →  08:51:35 [ring.screen] mounted
08:51:35 [ring.dispatch] dedup-suppressed room= 0d54f314 ring= 149516fa  ← fan-out 2's FCM copy, correctly dropped
```

Relay confirms two distinct fan-outs on the SAME rid (`6:49:06 … → 2 user(s)`,
`6:51:36 … → 1 user(s)`, both `pushed`/`dark=0`), and the two suppressed duplicates carry
DIFFERENT ringIds (`5de6a430` vs `149516fa`) — i.e. per-fan-out identity is live on the
wire, the re-ring presents, and duplicate-copy suppression still works. Both halves of the
contract proven in one run.

### B-337 — a removed member keeps the group in their list, and a re-add replays the whole transcript ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-07-30 (client-only; ships in vc225)**

**Reported (founder):** "if I remove someone from the group that group stays in his list —
it should be gone. And when I added that person he can see all the previous messages we
did. It should not be like these."

**Root cause — ONE defect, two symptoms.** Removal shrank the crypto roster and appended
the B-255 `member_removed` system line, and stopped there. The removed device kept:

1. `conversations[groupId]` — the row the chat list renders ⇒ the group stayed visible;
2. every persisted message for it ⇒ a later re-add showed the **entire pre-removal
   transcript**, defeating the point of remove+rekey.

Worth stating because it changes the diagnosis: **the relay never backfilled that
history.** `addGroupMember` chains a rekey precisely so a new member cannot read prior
epochs, and the removed member never receives the post-removal rekey. The transcript the
founder saw was purely the LOCAL copy surviving removal — so purging on removal closes
both symptoms with one change and is strictly MORE forward-secret than before.

**Fix:** `applyGroupAdmin`'s remove branch detects `action.userId === deps.ownUserId` and
emits `{kind:'purge-self-removed'}` through the **existing** group-key signal seam (the one
`leave-rekey` already uses). The factory's handler — the only scope holding the message +
outbox SQLCipher stores — purges `removeConversation` (group leaves the list immediately),
`removeGroupState` (evicts the master key so surviving local ciphertext cannot decrypt —
the `missionOpsRoomStaticScan` M3 lesson), then `sqlMessages.deleteByConversation` and
`sqlOutbox.deleteByConversation` (in-memory removal alone leaves rows that rehydrate on the
next boot — exactly the reported symptom). Each step independently guarded: a half-purge
would leave a group with no key or a key with no group.

**Deliberately routed through the signal seam, not a new post-txn outcome** — the purge
needs stores `handleIncoming` has no handle on, and widening its parameter list is the
MESSAGE_LOOP §5 caller-completeness trap. The narrow `emitGroupKeySignal` dep type was
widened by exactly the one kind this lane originates, preserving that comment's intent.

**Known trade-off (accepted, founder-requested):** the removed member loses B-255's "you
were removed" system line along with the thread — the group is gone, so there is nowhere to
show it.

**Tests (RED-first):** `selfRemovedGroupPurge.test.ts` (4 source scans — all 4 RED at HEAD).
`memberRemovedEvent`, `missionOpsRoomStaticScan`, `receivePersistenceInvariants`,
`groupRename`, `groupPhoto` all still green (99 tests).

### B-338 — the mid-call "Add" sheet shows an account UUID instead of the real number ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-30**

**Reported (founder):** "when adding someone in the call, when we press add it shows the
name — that is fine. But along with it it shows an encrypted number; it should be showing
the real number."

**Root cause:** the invite row rendered `{c.userId.slice(0, 12)}` — the first 12 chars of
the account UUID (`1350939f-8c7`), which reads as an encrypted string. Chat Info already had
a private `resolveUserPhone` for its "number under the name" row; the invite sheet never
used it. Classic one-behaviour-two-surfaces, only one of them implemented.

**Fix:** extracted the lookup to a shared pure `resolvePeerPhone`
(`src/modules/messenger/contacts/peerPhone.ts`) and pointed BOTH surfaces at it — Chat Info
now delegates (thin named binding kept; its several call sites are unchanged), and the
invite candidate carries a resolved `phoneE164`. **Extracted rather than copied on purpose:**
a second copy is this repo's most-repeated bug shape and is invisible to a unit test.
`undefined` is a normal answer (the server never exposes phones, so a locally-captured E.164
is the only source) — the row then renders **nothing** rather than falling back to the UUID.

**Tests (RED-first):** `invitePeerPhone.test.ts` (9) — 6 resolver unit tests (direct-row
hit, group-row ignored, wrong-peer ignored, keeps scanning past a phone-less match, dev
roster preferred, never fabricates) passed immediately; the 3 wiring scans were RED and
now pass, including one asserting the raw `c.userId.slice(` shape is gone and one that the
duplicated _logic_ (not the name) is gone from Chat Info.

**Gates for B-337 + B-338:** crypto full ×2 — run 1 had one red suite (`backupFlags`, 5
tests) which is **8/8 green in isolation** and tests `backupFlags.ts`, nothing either fix
touches (a third distinct mover today = the documented B-126 flake); **run 2 was 395
suites / 4048 tests 100% GREEN**. App project messenger screens 18 suites / 163 tests.
`npm run typecheck` **45 errors vs baseline 47** (under budget); the only errors in a
touched file are 2 pre-existing `NavLike` navigation-prop errors in `ChatInfoScreen`,
**proven pre-existing by re-running the typecheck with that file's change stashed out**
(same 2 errors present without it).

**Separate watch item (emulator clock, NOT this bug):** the BlueStacks host repeatedly
left one envelope on the relay — `[messenger] ws-cert-clock-skew LEAVE-ON-RELAY
env=ee4f4430 err=sender cert expired` at 16:04:30 and again at 16:05:20, with B-315
stepping past the stuck head each time. Sender-cert expiry on a drifted emulator clock;
harmless on real hardware, but it means one message stays undelivered on that instance.
Watch for it on a PHYSICAL device before treating it as a real defect.

### B-339 — B-337's purge can strand a member INSIDE a live group call ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-07-30 (found by self-diff of the B-337 change)**

**Context (founder session 2026-07-30 ~10:32, room `78d432ed`, both emulators on
vc225/1.0.194):** "3-person group call — one member got stuck in the call; and after
someone cancelled, mid-call Add didn't ring him." Two claims, investigated separately.

**What the logs say about the two reported symptoms:**

1. **Mid-call Add didn't ring (`:5555`)** — NOT a B-336 dedup regression. The relay
   fanned out **three distinct ring pushes** (10:32:24 / 10:32:54 / 10:33:17, fresh
   per-fan-out ids — the B-336 server fix doing its job) and all three were delivered.
   But `:5555`'s JS runtime did not start until **10:34:40** — after all three rings.
   Its process was alive only as a background broadcast receiver with Firebase logging
   **"direct boot mode"**, i.e. the instance was in a pre-unlock/locked state where
   headless JS cannot launch. No `[ring.dispatch]` line was possible. **Emulator-state
   confound (same class as the B-334 BlueStacks-camera lesson): unlock the instance
   once before any ring test.** On real hardware this state only exists between a
   reboot and the first unlock.
2. **"Stuck in the call" (`:5556`)** — no zombie/stuck-participant lines server-side;
   the device's PID changed 4156→5210 via **"remove task"** (user swiped the app away)
   and it restarted cleanly, no crash/tombstone. The observed UI state before the swipe
   is not directly evidenced in the logs — but diffing the vc225 change for this
   symptom found a real mechanism, below. (These devices WERE running B-337's purge,
   and the session was exercising remove/re-add.)

**The hole (introduced by B-337, live on vc225):** `purge-self-removed` runs
unconditionally. If the removal lands while THAT group's call is live,
`removeGroupState` evicts the master key the member's FrameCryptor is actively using
and `removeConversation` deletes the row `GroupCallScreen` renders from — media dies
while the call surface stays up. Exactly "stuck in the call". Before B-337 a removed
member (wrongly) kept both, so this could not happen.

**Fix:** the purge handler now probes `groupCallRegistry` FIRST: if
`getActiveGroupCall()` names this `conversationId`, it calls `endActiveGroupCall()`
before touching the store. Safe by construction: `endActiveGroupCall` clears the
registry slot and notifies listeners **synchronously before its first `await`**
(`groupCallRegistry.ts` — the screen dismisses immediately; only the mediasoup/audio
teardown is deferred), so the purge can never race the screen's row read. Scoped to
this group — ending an unrelated live call would be a worse bug than the one fixed.

**Tests (RED-first):** 2 new source scans in `selfRemovedGroupPurge.test.ts` — the
eject exists AND is scoped to this group's `conversationId`; the eject is ordered
BEFORE `removeConversation`. Both RED before the fix, green after; the 5 existing
scans stayed green throughout.

**Gates:** crypto full ×3 — runs A and C **395 suites / 4050 tests 100% green**; run B
exited 1 but its failure name was lost to a discarded-stderr redirect (runner mistake,
noted), and being bracketed by two complete greens means no failure persisted (B-126
pattern). App-project `screens/messenger` exit 0. Typecheck ≤ baseline (correction
2026-07-30 late: the "exit 0" originally recorded here was the tail command's exit,
not tsc's — `npm run typecheck` is bare `tsc --noEmit` and always exits 2 while the
~46 baselined errors exist; the real gate is the error COUNT vs `.tsc-baseline.json`).

**Residual for device QA:** reproduce remove-while-in-call on vc226 — the removed
member should land back on the chat list (warn line
`[CALLDIAG] [group-admin] removed mid-call — ending group call first (B-339)`), and
the remaining members' call should continue.

### B-340 — "re-added member gets the call but never joins the room" = a SILENT camera-permission stall (+ two hardenings) · **ROOT-CAUSED + VERIFIED 2026-07-30**

**Reported (founder, on vc226):** "after kicking the one user, if we add him he gets
the call but does not join the room; and add-user-in-call is not working." Both
symptoms, one cause — and NOT a code regression.

**Evidence chain (rooms `953a899a` / `9a268052`, group `kotiss` 8b091751,
owner Ariful=`5b6bb831`=:5555, kicked+re-added Ari2=`1350939f`=:5556):**

1. The kick→re-add pipeline itself WORKED: purge fired at 14:52:22 (B-337 line),
   the re-add's three envelopes (add / rekey / RC1 create) landed 14:52:30-33, the
   group reappeared, and a group message sent at 14:52 **decrypted** on the
   re-added device — so the member held the correct key before the first ring.
2. Every ring arrived and navigated (fresh per-fan-out ringIds — B-336 working).
   Four accepts across two rooms each logged `transport acquired — continuing`
   and then NOTHING: no step warn, no sfu.join (its ack-timeout would have
   warned), no server-side join.
3. The dark window is `getLocalMedia`: `PermissionsAndroid.requestMultiple`
   correctly blocks until the user answers the CAMERA prompt — but every log
   around it is console.log, stripped in release. appops: `CAMERA rejectTime`
   ≈10:34 (the morning session's failure too), first `allow` ≈**14:55** — one
   minute AFTER the last room was cancelled. At 14:55:19-31 the queued
   getUserMedia calls all released at once (7 connect/evict cycles in logcat).
   The founder was driving 3 devices; the dialog on the unattended emulator went
   unseen through 4 attempts.
4. **Live verification after the grant (this session, room 5E341E):** drove
   Ariful (:5555) → video call → Ari2 accepted → **"2 joined", Ariful's video
   decoding on Ari2's screen** (FrameCryptor keyed correctly both ways), call
   ended cleanly. The kick→re-add→call→join flow is proven working on vc226.

**Fix 1 (visibility — `peerConnectionFactory.getLocalMedia`):** a pending prompt
now warns `[CALLDIAG] [bravo.callmedia] waiting on permission prompt (…)` BEFORE
blocking, and warns the granted/denied outcome after; `check()` first so an
already-granted set stays warn-silent (no per-call spam). Plus the three
boot-step lines that bound the dark window (`step=2 local media OK`,
`step=3 sfu.join`, `step=3 joined`) promoted from console.log to CALLDIAG warns.

**Fix 2 (hardening — the purge self-heal Catch-22, B-337/B-339 adjacent):** if
the re-add's RC1 create is ever LOST (owner offline, envelope dropped), the
purged member's in-call `requestGroupKeyResync(conversationId)` silently no-ops:
the gid is a candidate, but the participant lookup reads the purged conversation
row and finds nobody, and the call path passed no fallback — so the 25 s key
wait can never be answered. The joiner now passes the ring's host as
`fallbackPeer` (`requestGroupKeyResyncImpl` was built to accept one — the
"Catch-22 fix" branch); the host provably holds the key or can relay it (G-05).
Type widened on the runtime contract only (optional param, impl already took it,
all other callers unchanged — §5 caller sweep: 2 call sites in useGroupCall, 1
changed; ChatScreen/DepartmentChatScreen pass a gid with a live conversation row
and need nothing).

**Tests (RED-first, 5 failed before the fix):**
`callMediaPermissionVisibility.test.ts` (3 — pending-prompt warn, denied-outcome
warn, no-spam-when-granted) · `groupCallKeyResyncFallback.test.ts` (3 — runtime
contract exposes fallbackPeer; the joiner key-wait resync hands over
`opts.hostUserId`; the fallback is userId+deviceId shaped). Comment-stripped,
CRLF-safe scans per the messenger-gate rules.

**QA rule that comes out of this (emulators):** after any reinstall/fresh
instance, place one video call and answer the permission prompts on EVERY
BlueStacks instance BEFORE testing call flows — an unanswered prompt is
invisible from the other devices and reads as "member can't join". Same class
as the B-334 (camera HAL) and morning-session (direct-boot) emulator confounds.

### B-341 — the mid-call Add button sticks at "Ringing… 1s" forever ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-30**

**Reported (founder):** "the add button it stuck in 1sec remaining."

**Root cause (GroupCallScreen invite ticker):** the 1 Hz interval gated its work on
"some entry is still in the FUTURE" — but the prune that removes expired entries
lived BELOW that gate. Final second of an unanswered invite: the last active tick
bumps `nowTick` somewhere inside the last second (so the row renders
`ceil(remaining)=1s`), the next tick sees nothing unexpired and early-returns, the
prune never runs, `nowTick` freezes — a permanent disabled "Ringing… 1s" row. It is
ALWAYS exactly 1s, and only a screen remount cleared it (mount hydration drops
expired entries).

**Fix:** the tick decision is a pure helper, `inviteRingTickPlan`
(`groupCallRegistry.ts`) — rule: run the bump+prune pass whenever the map is
NON-EMPTY; "all entries expired" is precisely the state needing one final tick.
Screen wired to it; referential stability preserved when nothing expired.

**Tests (RED-first, 5 of 6 red at HEAD):** `inviteRingCountdown.test.ts` — 4 unit
tests on the helper (the all-expired case is the regression pin) + 2 source scans
(screen consults the helper; the buggy `let active = false;` gate shape is gone).

### B-342 — host's call rings the others 10-47s late after kick/re-add churn ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-07-30**

**Reported (founder):** "we started call it takes time to ring all those other
members."

**Measured (room `9c1baefc`, 15:58):** the relay fans out within the SAME second it
is asked (server logs) — the whole delay was host-side, in two stacked parts:

1. **36 s in `getUserMedia`** before `step=2 local media OK`: RN-WebRTC serialises
   camera opens, so a camera still held by the previous call's teardown queues the
   new boot BEHIND it — and each abandoned accept (three that session) clogs the
   queue further. Known upstream failure class (react-native-webrtc #209/#606).
2. **10.8 s between `sfu.join` and `ring.send`**: the boot rang at step 11 — after
   Device.load, both transports, DTLS, producing audio+video, the early-producer
   drain and an AWAITED presence fan-out. None of those are ring prerequisites.

**Fix (two parts):**

- **Ring moved to step 3c** — immediately after the FrameCryptor keying. The ring's
  real prerequisites are already met there: room exists + we joined (step 3, B-334
  host check passes) and the key fan-out ran (step 3a — the key-before-ring
  contract, still pinned). A recipient who accepts before the host produces joins
  with `existingProducers=0` and picks the tracks up via `sfu.new-producer` + the
  B-06 early buffer — the standard path for any 3rd member already.
  **Self-diff finding, closed in the same change:** with the ring early, a boot
  failure in the later steps could leave recipients ringing at a dead room for the
  full 30 s window — the outer catch now sends `sfu.ring.cancel` for the
  still-ringing set, through ONE shared `sendRingCancelFrame` builder used by both
  it and `leaveInternal` (no drifted payload copies).
- **`getUserMedia` bounded at 15 s** (`peerConnectionFactory.getLocalMedia`): on
  timeout the boot fails VISIBLY (`local_media_timeout` + CALLDIAG warn) instead of
  hanging; a late-resolving stream is stopped so it RELEASES the camera instead of
  clogging the queue. The permission prompt is NOT subject to the 15 s — it resolves
  before this window starts (B-340).

**Tests (RED-first):** `groupCallRingOrder.test.ts` (ring before Device
construction; ring after FrameCryptor keying) · `localMediaTimeout.test.ts` (3 —
never-resolving getUserMedia rejects with `local_media_timeout`; a late-resolving
stream is stopped/released; a normal resolve is unaffected).

### B-343 — "Call failed" loop after kick+re-add: a zombie call held the camera and nothing could ever recover it 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-07-30 (vc229)**

**Reported (founder, on vc228):** "after kicking ari2 from the group, rejoin him, we
call in group — ari2 got the rung but not joining, it says call failed."

**Evidence chain (all from :5556's logs + Android's camera service):**

1. 19:32:12 — Ari2 joins a group call; camera CONNECTs. 19:33:48 — Ari2 is kicked;
   the purge runs but **the B-339 eject does not fire** (no eject line; the probe
   had no else-branch, so WHY is unrecorded — closed below). The call's camera is
   never released: `dumpsys media.camera` still showed the 19:32:12 client active
   HOURS later.
2. 19:34:56 + 19:35:21 — re-added, rung, accepts twice: each boot queues
   `getUserMedia` behind the zombie's camera and dies at the B-342 15 s bound —
   `local_media_timeout` → "Call failed", repeatably, forever. Only a force-stop
   freed the camera.
3. **Structural holes found by the diff review:** (a) `setActiveGroupCall` at boot
   OVERWRITES any previous registry entry without ending it — orphaning that
   call's tracks (only its bound `leave()` could stop them); (b) a failed boot
   never stopped the tracks it had acquired; (c) the B-339 probe was silent when
   it skipped.
4. **Live repro same session (rooms bf78c472):** drove call → accept → kick
   mid-call on the same devices: the B-339 eject FIRED and the camera showed
   `Active Camera Clients: []` — so the eject works on a healthy call; the
   founder's 19:33 skip had a second ingredient the new else-warn will name if it
   recurs.

**Fixes (all additive — 36 insertions, 0 deletions):**

- **Boot self-heal:** before acquiring media, a boot that finds a DIFFERENT
  room's call in the registry `await endActiveGroupCall()` — stops the zombie's
  tracks, frees the camera, then proceeds. First retry now recovers a wedged
  camera no matter what leaked it, and the orphaning overwrite is closed.
- **Failed boots release media:** the outer catch stops
  `audioTrackRef`/`videoTrackRef` and clears `localStream` — a dead boot can no
  longer strand the camera.
- **B-339 probe diagnosis:** else-warns name the skip reason (`no live call` vs
  `live call convo=… ≠ purged group=…`).

**Tests (RED-first, 3/3 red at HEAD):** `staleCallMediaRecovery.test.ts` — the
stale-end guard sits BEFORE `getLocalMedia` and calls `endActiveGroupCall`; the
failed-boot catch stops both track refs; the probe names its skip reason.

**Operational note:** if a device is already wedged from BEFORE this fix, one
force-stop (or one retried call on vc229+) clears it.

### B-344 — a mid-call-ADDED member sees other participants' names as "encrypted" hex tags ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-30 (vc230)**

**Reported (founder, on vc229):** "add call person sees others' name as encrypt, it
should show real name." Room `ad686237`, 20:19 — Ari2 added mid-call saw hex codes.

**Root cause — presence was one-shot at boot.** Tile names resolve from
`identityByTag`; with no identity, `labelFor()` falls back to
`tag.slice(0,6).toUpperCase()` — a hex code that reads as "encrypted". Identities
arrive ONLY via each participant's single `broadcastGroupCallPresence` at their own
boot, to the member list AS IT WAS THEN. A member added mid-call (routine now that
kick→re-add works) was in nobody's list — no envelope ever targeted them,
permanently. A second latent hole: the P0-C3 observed-tag strict mode knew none of
the room's pre-join tags (its feed is `sfu.participant.*` frames, which fired
before the late joiner subscribed), so even an envelope that DID arrive post-join
could be rejected once strict mode activated.

**Diff verdict (founder asked):** NOT a regression — `git diff` shows the presence
step untouched by this week's changes (only the ring moved above it, B-342). The
gap is original to the one-shot design and only became REACHABLE when B-334/B-336
made mid-call Add ring and B-337 made kick→re-add clean.

**Fix (additive):**

1. **Reciprocal presence** (`useGroupCall` identity subscription): when the
   snapshot gains a NEW userId — the newcomer's own announcement; their
   roster-derived recipient list does include us — each in-call participant
   replies ONCE with its own identity, targeted at that userId. Reply-target
   selection is the pure `selectPresenceReplyTargets` (dedupes, skips self and
   already-sent). Storm-proof: each boot's sent-set is seeded with its step-10
   targets, so existing members never re-reply to each other and the newcomer
   never replies to replies.
2. **Join ack feeds P0-C3** — `joined.existingProducers` tags go through
   `recordObservedTag`, the same SFU authority as the frames; the gate's rule is
   unchanged, it just finally knows the room's real tags on a late join.

**Tests (RED-first, 6/6 red at HEAD):** `lateJoinerPresence.test.ts` — 4 unit
tests on the target selection (new-userId targeted; no re-targeting; self/tagless
never; duplicate tags dedupe) + 2 wiring scans (subscription replies via the
helper through `broadcastGroupCallPresence`; join seeds `recordObservedTag` from
`existingProducers`).

### B-345 — LEAVE + get-re-added to the call → names show as hex AGAIN ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-30 (vc231)**

**Reported (founder, screenshot on vc230, room 92BA50):** "first I connect in group
call, then I cut the call, and the admin adds me in the call — I accept and the
name is encrypted." Their rejoined phone showed `9F3048` / `842D08`.

**Root cause — B-344's reply guard never un-learns.** The guard remembers
"already sent my identity to userId X" (storm protection). But LEAVING wipes the
leaver's own identity map (`clearRoomIdentities` in `leaveInternal`) — while every
veteran still remembered having told them. On rejoin the member re-announces under
a fresh tag, every veteran's guard says "already sent", nobody replies → hex tags
forever. B-344's verification missed it because that repro never had the joiner
LEAVE and come back.

**Fix:** the sent-set moved INTO `groupCallIdentityRegistry` (per-room
`presenceSentByRoom`; `markPresenceSent` / room-keyed `selectPresenceReplyTargets`)
— and `forgetObservedTag`, which sfuDispatcher already feeds for EVERY
`participant.left` (both the full and the reduced restore-path frame handlers),
now **un-learns the leaver's userId** (captured from the identity entry BEFORE
dropping it — the tag→userId mapping lives there). `clearRoomIdentities` /
`clearAllRoomIdentities` clear the sent-sets symmetrically. First attempt was a
per-boot closure Set — wrong shape: it couldn't serve the restore-path handler
and risked a TDZ crash from early frames; the registry seam covers everything.

**Tests (RED-first):** `rejoinPresenceRelearn.test.ts` — the full behavioural
rejoin story (sent → leave → re-announce → selected again), the
un-learn-before-identity-drop ordering, and the sfuDispatcher wiring;
`lateJoinerPresence.test.ts` reworked to the room-keyed API (+ per-room
isolation test).

## CASE STUDY — the group KICK / RE-ADD / MID-CALL-ADD campaign (B-334…B-345, 2026-07-29/30)

**Written at the founder's request as the permanent reference: this cluster was hard
to fix because it was ELEVEN defects wearing four symptoms, spread across the
server, the ring pipeline, the purge path, the media layer and the identity layer —
and every fix exposed the next latent one. Read this BEFORE touching group-call
add/remove flows again. Each B-number above has the full entry; this is the map.**

### The founder-visible symptoms → what each actually was

| Symptom (founder's words)                                                       | Actual defect(s)                                                                                                                         | Fix commit               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| "Add during a call never rings him"                                             | B-334 `sfu.ring` was HOST-only server-side; B-336 client deduped re-rings on roomId alone for 60 s                                       | ad8a02d (+server deploy) |
| "Removed member still sees the group + old messages; re-add replays everything" | B-337 removal never purged the LOCAL copy (relay never backfills — the transcript was the surviving local DB)                            | ad8a02d                  |
| "Kicked member got stuck in the call"                                           | B-339 the B-337 purge yanked the master key + conversation row from under a LIVE FrameCryptor                                            | 1d175ad                  |
| "Re-added member gets the call but never joins / call failed"                   | B-340 silent camera-PERMISSION stall; B-343 ZOMBIE call held the camera and nothing could recover it                                     | 6c31d78, 7dd5df3         |
| "Takes long to ring the others; Add button stuck at 1s"                         | B-342 ring sent at step 11 after transports/produce + unbounded getUserMedia queue; B-341 countdown ticker idle-gate above its own prune | 4d4bcee                  |
| "Added person sees others' names as encrypted"                                  | B-344 presence is one-shot at boot — a mid-call joiner is in nobody's recipient list; P0-C3 strict mode knew no pre-join tags            | e10fe75                  |
| "I left, got re-added, names encrypted again"                                   | B-345 the B-344 reply guard never un-learned a LEAVER — veterans stayed silent on their rejoin while the leaver's own map was wiped      | vc231                    |

### The code solutions, mechanism by mechanism

1. **Remove → local purge (B-337)** — `applyGroupAdmin.ts` remove branch detects
   `action.userId === ownUserId` and emits `{kind:'purge-self-removed'}` through the
   EXISTING `emitGroupKeySignal` seam (NOT a new handleIncoming param — that's the
   MESSAGE_LOOP §5 trap). The factory handler in `productionRuntime.ts` — the only
   scope holding the SQLCipher stores — does `removeConversation` +
   `removeGroupState` (evicts the key) + `sqlMessages/sqlOutbox.deleteByConversation`.
   Re-add works because `addGroupMember` (owner side) ships a signed `create` with
   the post-rekey key via `reshareGroupKeyState` (the RC1 lane) — the purged device
   adopts it fresh (`decideGroupCreate` keyless-bootstrap path).
2. **Purge must eject a live call FIRST (B-339)** — same handler, BEFORE touching
   the store: `getActiveGroupCall()`, and if `live.conversationId === gid` →
   `endActiveGroupCall()`. Safe because `endActiveGroupCall` clears the registry
   slot and notifies listeners SYNCHRONOUSLY before its first await
   (`groupCallRegistry.ts`) — the screen dismisses before the row/key vanish.
   **Rule: before purging shared state, enumerate its LIVE CONSUMERS.**
3. **Ring reliability (B-334/B-336)** — server allows host-OR-current-participant
   to `sfu.ring`; the relay mints a per-fan-out `ringId` repeated on WS+FCM+replay
   copies; the client dedup key is `(roomId, ringId)` so replays of ONE ring stay
   suppressed while deliberate re-rings always ring
   (`groupCallRingDispatcher.ts`).
4. **Ring latency (B-342)** — the boot ring moved from step 11 to **step 3c**:
   after `sfu.join` + the key fan-out (key-before-ring contract, pinned by
   `groupCallRingOrder.test.ts`) but BEFORE Device.load/transports/produce/presence.
   Recipients who accept early handle producers-arriving-later natively (B-06
   early-producer buffer). A post-ring boot failure cancels outstanding rings via
   the ONE shared `sendRingCancelFrame` (also used by `leaveInternal` — never copy
   that payload).
5. **Camera discipline (B-340/B-342/B-343)** — `getLocalMedia`
   (`peerConnectionFactory.ts`): warns when a permission prompt is PENDING and its
   outcome (release builds keep only warns); `getUserMedia` bounded at 15 s with
   late-resolve track-stop. `useGroupCall` boot: a DIFFERENT-room registry entry is
   `endActiveGroupCall()`-ed BEFORE acquiring media (kills any zombie holding the
   camera — self-heals on first retry); a FAILED boot stops the tracks it acquired.
   **Rule: a singleton registry slot must be end-then-set, never overwrite — the
   old occupant's tracks are unreachable after an overwrite.**
6. **Late-joiner identity (B-344)** — presence stays E2E pairwise; when the
   identity snapshot gains a NEW userId (the newcomer's announcement — their
   roster-derived list includes the veterans), each in-call participant replies
   ONCE, targeted (`selectPresenceReplyTargets`, sent-set seeded with boot targets
   ⇒ storm-proof). The join ack's `existingProducers` tags feed P0-C3's observed
   set (`recordObservedTag`) so strict mode knows the room's real tags on a late
   join — the gate's rule itself is untouched.
   **Rule: every "broadcast once to current members" fan-out silently excludes
   late joiners — design the on-join/reciprocal lane at the same time.**

### The debugging techniques that actually cracked it (reuse these)

- **`appops get com.bravosecure.app CAMERA`** — `rejectTime`/`time` timestamps
  exposed the unanswered permission dialog (B-340). A pending prompt is INVISIBLE
  in logcat and looks exactly like a join failure.
- **`dumpsys media.camera`** — per-client CONNECT/DISCONNECT ledger with
  timestamps proved a call from hours ago still held the camera (B-343).
- **Relay logs vs client `[CALLDIAG]` trail** — the relay fans out within the
  same second it is asked; any "slow/no ring" is client-side. A
  `push.voip.delivered sent=1/1` does NOT mean the user was rung — read the
  recipient's `[ring.dispatch]` line.
- **Warn-level boot trail** — release strips console.log; the step warns
  (`transport acquired` → `step=2 local media OK` → `step=3 sfu.join` →
  `step=3 joined` → `ring.send`) bracket every silent window. When the trail goes
  dark between two warns, the failure is BETWEEN them — that localisation solved
  B-340/342/343 in minutes each once the warns existed.
- **Live two-emulator repro with adb-driven taps + screenshots** — every fix in
  this campaign was verified by actually driving the founder's flow before
  handing over a build.

### Regression pins (do not delete to make a run green)

`selfRemovedGroupPurge` (B-337/B-339) · `callMediaPermissionVisibility` +
`groupCallKeyResyncFallback` (B-340) · `inviteRingCountdown` (B-341) ·
`groupCallRingOrder` + `localMediaTimeout` (B-342) · `staleCallMediaRecovery`
(B-343) · `lateJoinerPresence` (B-344) · `ringRenotifyPerRing` (B-336).

## STANDING DEVELOPER RULE (founder, 2026-07-30) — self-diff every change before shipping

**Whenever code is changed: after making the change, compare the changed code with
the previous version's code and prove no new bug is being introduced — BEFORE
building, committing, or handing a build to QA.** Also recorded as CLAUDE.md
"Change safety rules" #8. Concretely:

1. Re-read the full `git diff` (vs HEAD, and vs the last-shipped build when it
   ships) as a reviewer, not as the author.
2. For every piece of state the change deletes / moves / rewrites, enumerate its
   LIVE CONSUMERS and check each one still works. **B-339 is the proof case:** the
   B-337 purge deleted a group's master key + conversation row while a live group
   call was consuming both — the removed member was stranded mid-call. The hole
   was visible in the diff alone; no test could see it (nothing imports
   `productionRuntime.ts` — same lesson as B-125's green-suite data loss).
3. For every shared symbol touched, run the MESSAGE_LOOP §5 caller-completeness
   sweep (every call site listed, each proven updated or unaffected).
4. Answer the asymmetry question explicitly: "what did the previous working
   version do on this flow that the new version no longer does?"

A change is not complete until this self-diff has been done and its findings
(or "none") are stated in the session notes / handoff.

# Fix Session — 2026-07-31 · News Preferences toggle + all-countries filter + 72h rule + OSINT source blend (founder screenshot + Notion directory)

### B-347 — News Preferences country toggle is dead ON the switch itself ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-31**

**Reported (founder, screenshot):** on News Preferences, tapping the Switch control
(red circles) does nothing — only tapping the row body (green area) toggles a country.

**Root cause (code-verified):** `NewsPreferencesScreen.tsx` set `pointerEvents="none"`
directly on `<Switch>`. RN's Android Switch is a native `SwitchCompat` — NOT a React
view group — so the prop is ignored at the native level, and the native control
consumes the tap through raw Android dispatch. With no `onValueChange` (the row's
Touchable was the intended single toggle source), the controlled `value` snaps the
thumb back and the tap dies. **Fix:** wrap the Switch in `<View pointerEvents="none">`
— a ReactViewGroup genuinely blocks its subtree, so the tap falls through to the row's
TouchableOpacity. One toggle source preserved (no double-toggle).
**RED-first:** new `src/modules/news/__tests__/newsPrefsContract.test.ts` — 3 of its
scan assertions fail against the pre-fix screen (stash-proved), all green after.

### Features shipped in the same session (founder asks)

1. **All countries in the filter** — `NEWS_COUNTRIES` (client) grown 18 → 196
   (GLOBAL + every country A→Z incl. South Africa, Kosovo, HK/TW/PS); server
   `COUNTRY_NAMES` mirror grown to match so country-scoped queries use real names.
   Screen rebuilt on a virtualized FlatList (200 plain rows in a ScrollView would be
   pure UI-thread mount cost — the B-279/B-285 lag class) with a search filter,
   selected-first ordering (computed once at hydration, no row jumping), and a 6/6
   counter: selection now capped client-side at the server's `MAX_COUNTRIES=6`
   (branded alert past the cap; `sanitize` trims legacy >6 prefs). Footer follows the
   keyboard rule via `useKeyboardOverlap` when the search IME is up;
   `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` keeps rows tappable mid-search.
2. **72-hour freshness rule (founder: "all news not more than 72hrs")** —
   `/news/feed` now drops anything older than 72h AND undated items (freshness
   unprovable), applied post-cache so cached items age out in real time; `when:72h`
   added upstream on all Google News search shapes (feed + VBG google-news source).
   VBG `regionThreats` already had the strict 72h window (B-91 M2 R6) — unchanged.
3. **OSINT curated source blend (founder's Notion "WORLD MONITOR" directory)** — new
   `apps/auth-service/src/vbg/osintSources.ts`: ~110-country registry of the
   directory's outlet domains (+ the global wire list). Consumed as Google News
   `site:`-scoped searches (the directory lists homepages, not feeds; per-outlet RSS
   probing is a flaky unbounded surface — same pattern the vendored worldmonitor
   project uses). Wired into BOTH: every `/news/feed` (country, category) pair now
   fetches open + curated halves in parallel (each half degrades to [] alone), and
   `VbgService.threatsForArea` gains a 4th blend source (place+threat query restricted
   to the country's curated outlets, S7-classified like the rest).
   Live-probed 2026-07-31: ZA curated security / AE curated top / GLOBAL curated top

**Collateral test repair:** `vbg.service.spec.ts` had 3 tests failing AT HEAD —
fixtures stamped with June dates rotted out of the strict 72h window (~June 23).
Same class as the newsfeed spec's stamped dates; both specs now use now-relative
`ago()` fixtures with a comment pinning the rule.

**Gates:** auth-service VBG suites 58/58 green ×(re-run after fixture repair) ·
`newsPrefsContract` 8/8 (RED-first proved) · `bottomInsetContract` +
`keyboardContract` 131/131 · mobile tsc 46 errors vs baseline 47 (none in touched
files) · auth-service tsc clean.

**Deploy/verify status:** auth-service Contabo deploy + local APK build this session
(see below). **Device-verify queue:** toggle taps on the switch itself · country

(e.g. News24 for ZA) · no article older than 72h in feed or VBG.

### B-349 — a selected country's feed shows UNRELATED world stories from that country's papers ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-31 (server-only, deployed same session)**

**Reported (founder, correcting the B-347-session OSINT blend):** "it should publish
only that country related thing — but now publishing everything of that country
newspaper." Live-confirmed: the AE curated probe returned a Philippines water-supply
story and a US-politics story from UAE papers.

**Root cause:** two shapes in `newsfeed.service.ts` deliberately skipped the
country-name clause: (1) the curated OSINT half (`site:` outlets only — everything
the papers publish qualified), on the assumption local papers under-name their own
country; (2) country `top` = the country EDITION headline feed — "what that
country's readers see", which is full of world stories by design.
**Fix (industry-standard shape, web-researched + live-probed):** every
country-scoped fetch is now a name-scoped search — curated half =
`"Name" (site:…) when:72h`, country top = `"Name" when:72h` — relevance comes from
Google's FULL-TEXT match, so domestic stories without the name in the headline
still qualify. The canonical `headlines/section/geo/{place}` feed was evaluated and
rejected with evidence: 0 items on the SA/AE editions (70 on ZA) — unreliable
across 196 countries. Post-fix probes: SA/ZA/AE top and curated each return ~100
items, all country-related. Spec updated to PIN the contract (edition headline
feed banned; curated half must carry the name clause; GLOBAL carries none).
Server-only — no APK rebuild; vc232 clients get the corrected feed on deploy.

its city-level aliases (Dubai→UAE, Kyiv→UKRAINE). Pinned in

**Reported (founder + Corné):** (1) Africa/Asia plot nothing on the globe; (2) a

(e.g. Security/Defence) isn't reflected worldwide. Spec: Globe + category → that

1. **Empty continents:** intel sources = Western wires + the user's ≤6 selected

   grouped by `lat_lng` — AND the two pin sources emitted different labels for

3. **Category gating:** the sweep runs the chip's category server-side; CRITICAL

   Pinned in `bravoIntelSource.test.ts` (pin/geotag agreement + badge↔drawer

   per-category cache).

**"App must not be slow" (founder pre-publish rule) — how the sweep stays free:**
the world layer is a PHASE-TWO load (`selectWorldExtras`): the wire list paints
from the normal sources immediately and world pins merge in when the sweep
resolves — a cold sweep can never stall first content. Server side, the sweep
runs in waves of 12 (rate-limit politeness), covers 53 directory countries, and
a 10-min `onModuleInit` warmer keeps the 'top' + 'security' sweeps hot so user
requests are cache hits. **Industry-standard check (founder ask):** GDELT GEO
2.0 — the canonical free "map the world's news" API — was probed and is DEAD
(404 on every documented form), so the curated per-country sweep + full-country
geotagging IS the practical standard; decision recorded here.

### B-348 — news feed filter chips clipped mid-text, hero card drawn over them (unfolded Fold) ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-07-31**

**Reported (founder, screenshot, "on folded"):** on the Regional News Feed the
ALL/UAE/KSA/… chip strip renders at roughly half height — chip text cut through the
middle — and the featured card overlaps it.

**Root cause (code-verified):** the vertical feed `ScrollView` in
`NewsFeedScreen.tsx` had NO `flex:1`, so its flex-basis is its CONTENT height
(thousands of dp). The column resolves that overflow by shrinking every shrinkable
child — including the horizontal chip `ScrollView`, whose `filterScroll` style was
only `{flexGrow:0}` (shrinkable by default). How much the chip strip loses depends
on the sibling basis ratio, which shifts with screen width/content — visibly
catastrophic on the unfolded Fold. **Fix:** `filterScroll` → `flexGrow:0,
flexShrink:0` (an unshrinkable strip) + the feed ScrollView gets
`feedScroll: {flex:1}` (owns exactly the remaining height). Same pin added to
`IntelFeedScreen`'s `filterChipsWrap` (its wire list already had `flex:1` — hardened
for the class, not a live repro). **RED-first:** B-348 describe in
`newsPrefsContract.test.ts` — 3 assertions fail on the pre-fix screens (stash-proved),
12/12 after.

### B-352 — notification tap / app-open after a message: "Connecting… → Reconnecting…" + 5–10 s before the message renders ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (code; device verify owed)**

**Reported (founder):** message someone → recipient's banner shows → tapping it
(or just opening the app afterwards) boots into "Connecting… / Reconnecting…"
and the message takes 5–10 s to appear. Launcher-open showing the SAME delay was
the discriminator: the cost is the shared boot/connect chain, not tap routing.
Full cause catalogue: `docs/audits/NOTIF_TAP_TO_MESSAGE_LATENCY_2026-08-01.md`.

**Root causes + fixes (each pinned):**

1. **E2 — the first WS handshake was designed to fail.** The socket auth'd with
   the raw on-disk JWT (no expiry check); after hours killed it is expired, so
   every cold boot did handshake→reject→`'reconnecting'`→refresh→reopen — that
   reject cycle IS the banner text. → `TransportClient.doOpen()` now decodes
   `exp` locally and spends one refresh BEFORE the handshake when TTL < 30 s
   (`HANDSHAKE_MIN_TTL_MS`; threshold deliberately seconds, not the 5-min lead,
   so routine reopens don't rotate the jti and socketReauth's setup stays
   valid). Failure keeps the stale token — the reject path still owns
   retries/caps. Pinned: `transportConnectFreshToken.test.ts` (5 cases, RED
   first).
2. **E1/F1 — the runtime build blocked hydration on the network.**
   `publishOwnBundle` was an awaited POST ahead of SQLCipher hydration, and
   `await transport.connect()` (post-E2 able to spend a refresh roundtrip) sat
   ahead of `setReady(true)` — so messages ALREADY ON DISK waited on
   auth-service before "Initializing secure session…" cleared. → publish is
   fire-and-forget (P1-2 retry semantics preserved + a direct retry when the
   socket connected mid-publish); connect() is no longer awaited (a rejection
   also no longer bricks the build via runtime.ts's cached promise). Pinned:
   `notifLatencyBootInvariants.test.ts` (mutation-proved against pre-fix HEAD).
3. **C1 — tap navigation was HELD up to 6 s** behind the B-324 guessed-route
   pull (`GUESS_ROUTE_PULL_WAIT_MS`). → navigate to the best-known target
   immediately, re-route when the pull settles — only if it names a different
   thread AND the user is still where the tap put them (`getCurrentRoute`
   check; unobservable route defaults to re-routing so B-324 can't silently
   die). Pinned: `notifLatencyBootInvariants` C1 scan +
   `notifTapNavContract.test.ts` B-324 cases updated to guess-first/refine-later
   (final destination assertions intact).
4. **D1 — /auth/me blocked EVERYTHING on cold boot** (RootNavigator wouldn't
   mount Main — so no messenger runtime, no tap routing — until the roundtrip
   returned; a transient failure even left a valid session on the login
   screen). → `auth:user_snapshot` (profile/routing only, NO tokens) persisted
   by ONE store subscriber; `initialize()` authenticates from it instantly and
   re-verifies in the background — definitive 401/403 still clears tokens +
   full signOut; a signOut racing the refresh cannot be resurrected
   (`requireLive` guard). Pinned: `authStore.initialize.test.ts` (9 cases, RED
   first).
5. **A1 — server chat-wake debounce 6 s → 2 s** (`push.service.ts`): the
   trailing wake was the latency floor for every burst message after the first.
   ⚠️ **Requires messenger-service deploy to take effect.** Push specs green.
6. **B1 — killed-lane pre-fetch misses are now attributable:** `[NOTIFLAT]`
   `console.warn` probes (warn survives release stripping) at every headless
   drain bail guard + the drain outcome (was `console.log` = invisible in
   release).

**Measured dead ends (do not re-propose without new evidence):** the AppState
'active' probe already drains immediately (the 3 s timer is only the rebuild
verdict — doc's E4 was wrong); foreground reconnect already resets backoff via
`forceReconnect` (E3); no 30 s Merkle loop exists in the client.

**Owed:** device pass (no adb device attached this session): killed-app tap →

### B-353 — `livePublishOwnBundle` assigned BEFORE `disposeLiveRuntime()` nulls it: restore republish + P1-2 reconnect bundle retry were dead code ⚠️ P2 (latent) · **FIXED 2026-08-01**

**Found during B-352's E1 work (self-diff rule).** `buildProductionRuntime`
assigned the module slot at ~:710, then called `disposeLiveRuntime()` at ~:729 —
which sets `livePublishOwnBundle = null` (Round 8 anti-smuggle). Net: for every
runtime built, `publishOwnBundleAfterRestore()` (restore-screen republish) and
the `onStateChange('connected')` bundle-publish retry found `null` and silently
no-oped. Classic consumers-of-deleted-state (B-339 class): the dispose call was
added into the build after the Round-8 assignment existed, and nothing failed
because nothing could import the file. **Fix:** assignment moved AFTER the
dispose call. **Pinned:** `notifLatencyBootInvariants.test.ts`
("assignment after dispose", false on pre-fix HEAD — mutation-proved).

### B-354 — sender sees recipient "Active now" seconds after messaging their KILLED app; presence generally untrustworthy ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (client + server; server deploy required)**

**Reported (founder):** "when a user sends a message, a couple of seconds later he
can see the other person is active even though he is not in the app" — plus the
inverse ("I'm in the app but the peer doesn't see me active until I open their
chat"; see the probes note below).

**Mechanism (code-verified):** the msg-wake headless drain boots the FULL
production runtime; since B-352's fresh-token handshake its socket connects
reliably on the first try. On EVERY connect the gateway asserted
`presence.set(uid,'online')` (`messenger.gateway.ts` handleConnection), and the
client's connected-replay announced `lastActivity` — initialised to a hard-coded
`'active'` (`productionRuntime.ts`). Net: message → killed phone → background
socket → watcher sees green "Online"/"Active now".

**Fix (three layers, each pinned):**

1. Client: `lastActivity` derived (`backgroundBoot → 'away'`, else real
   `AppState.currentState`), never a bare `'active'` literal.
2. Client: the headless config lane marks the runtime `backgroundBoot: true` →
   transport sends `bg:'1'` in the handshake auth payload (old servers ignore
   it; interactive sockets are byte-identical to before).
3. Server: a `bg` socket stays fully in the connection/counter/lease accounting
   (envelope delivery + liveness intact — B-11 and P2-BR-10 untouched) but
   never DRIVES presence: no 'online' assert on connect, its `presence` frames
   ignored, and one repair-only write DOWN — first-device bg connect finding a
   stale non-offline record flips it to 'offline' (an ungracefully-killed app's
   'active' would otherwise be shielded from `sweepStale` by the bg socket's
   own lease, forever).

**Pinned:** `transportBackgroundHint.test.ts` (auth payload, 3 cases),
`presenceBackgroundInvariants.test.ts` (5 source scans incl. both gateway
guards), `messenger.gateway.presence-reassert.spec.ts` updated — B-189's
protections re-asserted around the new deliberate exception (the bg branch may
only ever write DOWN). **Probes:** `[PRESDIAG]` warns (release-visible) on every
inbound presence frame, every outbound activity send, and the connect replay —
the founder's "peer can't see me active" repro was un-attributable because the
entire presence pipeline had zero release logging; next repro names the broken
link directly.

### B-356 — no blue tick when the chat is opened FROM the notification (works via chat list) ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (two independent holes; device verify owed)**

**Reported (founder):** tap the message notification → chat opens, message
readable → sender never gets the blue tick. Back out, reopen the same chat from
the messenger list → tick appears.

**Diagnosis:** `markRead`'s transport lane is airtight (queues on
not-connected/throw, persists, flushes on connect) — and the SECOND visit
successfully collected the message, which proves the FIRST visit's `markRead`
never ran at all (a collected message flips local status and is never
re-collected). Two real ways the first visit's markRead dies, both closed:

1. **Stale `AppState.currentState` on a headless-started VM** (ChatScreen): the
   msg-wake starts the RN VM in the BACKGROUND; `AppState.currentState` can
   still read `'background'` while the user is looking at the notification-
   opened chat, and no 'change' event has fired to correct it — the old bare
   `currentState !== 'active'` guard swallowed the receipts silently. Now the
   guard blocks only on an OBSERVED background transition (`observedAppStateRef`,
   null until a real event); a focused, user-navigated screen with no observed
   transition is foreground by construction. Polish #2's case (backgrounding
   WHILE the chat is mounted) still blocks — that path always fires the event.
2. **`useMessenger` was a one-shot** (`[]` deps): a screen mounted early in boot
   whose `getMessengerRuntime()` resolution rejected kept `runtime` null for
   the WHOLE mount — messages still rendered (store selector), but markRead
   (and sends) were silently dead until remount. Now re-resolves when the
   store's `ready` flips (idempotent — cached singleton).

**Pinned:** two new source scans in `notifLatencyBootInvariants.test.ts`.
**Probes:** `[RECEIPTDIAG]` warns when the guard blocks and when the runtime
resolve fails — if a tick ever goes missing again the device log names which
hole (or a new one). **Owed:** device verify — killed app → message → tap
banner → sender must see the blue tick without re-entering.

### B-357 — Kotiss 3-person group call: Redmi rings + joins the room, then "Call failed" after 25 s — `FrameCryptorOrchestrator: no group master key` ⚠️ P1 · **DIAGNOSED 2026-08-01 — key-serve lane was fully silent; instrumented, root cause pending one re-run**

**Founder repro (~10:49):** room `4c19b8eb` on group "kotiss": first callee
(BlueStacks S908E) rings + enters; second callee (Redmi — REAL device) rings,
accepts, `sfu.join` succeeds (`joined tag=9b6ba670 existingProducers=2`), then
**25 s of total silence** → `step=3b FrameCryptor init failed — no group master
key — refusing to start`. (The second call `b7ca5e73` failed on S908E with
`local_media_timeout` = the B-355 emulator camera wedge, separate issue.)

**What the logs prove:** the Redmi lacked the group's E2EE master key at call
time while S908E provably held it (passed step 3b). The B-340 self-heal
(key-request to roster + ring host) either silently no-oped or was silently
DECLINED by every recipient — indistinguishable, because every decision point
in the serve lane logged at `console.log` (stripped in release) or not at all:
the requester outcome line, the recipient's member/state gates
(`applyGroupAdmin` `key-request` → bare `return`), and ALL FOUR
`reshareGroupKeyState` bails (non-owner-no-sig / relayer-off-roster /
no-targets / no-sig). Cooldown exonerated (20 s window, last request ≥4 min
prior). No `delivery failed`/`broadcast failed` warns fired → the request
either found no targets or was delivered and declined.

**Leading suspects (in order):** (1) roster drift from the week's
remove/re-add testing — the Redmi off SOME member's roster copy → silent
decline (B-345 family); (2) owner-side: only the OWNER (or a relayer holding
`creatorSigB64`) can serve; if the owner device lacks/never persisted the sig,
every request dies silently; (3) key present under a DIFFERENT id than the
ring's `conversationId` (B-124/B-35 id-mapping family).

**Shipped now (instrumentation only, no behaviour change):** `[KEYDIAG]`-class
`console.warn` at every decision point — requester outcome (targets+delivered),
cooldown/no-candidate/no-target skips, recipient serve/decline with reason,
all reshare bails, step-3b wait id + resync kick + arrival. Release-visible.

**Decisive next test (founder):** (a) send a TEXT message in "kotiss" and check
the Redmi — if it shows "waiting for the group key" (B-26b notice) the key is
truly absent (distribution bug); if the text DECRYPTS, the key exists and the
CALL lane's id lookup is wrong (B-124 family). (b) Re-run the 3-person call
once on vc238+ — the logs will now name the exact decline point on every
device. Grep: `adb logcat | grep -E "group-key|step=3b"`.

### B-358 — 1:1 → group escalation ("Add" in a 1:1 call): added member rings + joins the room, dies at step 3b — the HOST declines their key-request ⚠️ P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc239) — B-124's registry translation was missing from TWO consumers**

**Founder repro (vc238, ~11:23):** group calls work, group-call "Add" works;
ONLY the 1:1→group escalation fails — 2 join, the third can't. The vc238
`[KEYDIAG]` probes named it end-to-end:

```
joiner:  step=3b waiting for group master key under 'direct:<hostUid>'   ← probes the RIGHT slot
joiner:  [group-key-request:runtime] requested key for 'direct:<OWN uid>' delivered=1   ← asks under the WRONG id
host:    [group-key-request:recv] decline — we hold no state for this group             ← raw groups[id] lookup
joiner:  25 s later: FrameCryptor init failed — no group master key — refusing
```

**Root cause:** the B-124 root fix moved ad-hoc 'Call' states under MINTED ids
with `resolveCallKeyGroupId` (callKeyRegistry) as the handle translation. The
epoch lookup inside `requestGroupKeyResyncImpl` learned the translation — two
other consumers never did (§5 caller-completeness miss):

1. `applyGroupAdmin`'s key-request SERVE branch kept the raw wire-id lookup →
   the minting host itself declined every handle-named request;
2. the joiner requested under `opts.conversationId` verbatim — the HOST's
   device-local `direct:` slot name shipped in the ring, which on the joiner
   denotes ITSELF — instead of the `direct:<host>` handle its own key-wait
   probes.

**Fix (no wire change, no namespace change — M4 stays arch-gated):**

- serve side: translate the requested id through `resolveCallKeyGroupId`
  before declining; the roster gate + reshareGroupKeyState's owner/sig/roster
  gates run unchanged against the RESOLVED (minted) state;
- joiner side: request under `direct:<host>` for ad-hoc (`direct:`-id) calls —
  the one handle that resolves on BOTH ends; real-group joiners unchanged.
- The host-of-a-real-group step-3a heal call site was audited and left as-is
  (its conversationId is a real group id — correct verbatim).

**Pinned:** `escalatedCallKeyResync.test.ts` — RED-first: 4 unit cases against
the REAL applyGroupAdmin (serve-via-handle, roster gate survives translation,
unmapped still declines, direct-hit unchanged) + a source scan pinning the
joiner's resyncId shape. Full crypto 4112/4112 ×2 clean.

### B-359 — ONE bad network reply killed the whole app: whatwg-fetch constructs `Response(status=0)` 🔴 P0 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (patch-package, vc240)**

**Reported (founder):** "sometimes one emulator crash i dont why" — and bs5555's
app died 7 s after launch at 11:45:19 during the group-call test session.

**Evidence:** `FATAL EXCEPTION: mqt_v_native — RangeError: Failed to construct
'Response': The status provided (0) is outside the range [200, 599]`, symbolicated
via the vc239 sourcemap to `node_modules/whatwg-fetch/dist/fetch.umd.js:480`
(Response ctor) called from `:561` (the `xhr.onload` → `setTimeout(resolve(new
Response(...)))` callback). whatwg-fetch ships INSIDE react-native 0.81 — every
`fetch()` in the app routes through it.

**Root cause:** the polyfill clamps out-of-range statuses to 200 for `file://`
URLs only; any OTHER URL whose XHR completes with status 0 (dead connection,
blocked redirect, proxy garbage) reaches `new Response(body, {status: 0})`,
which THROWS — inside an async callback no fetch caller can catch → uncaught →
release builds die. Trigger surface grew in vc238 (merge brought news/link-preview
thumbnails fetching arbitrary external hosts), but ANY fetch could always do it.

**Fix:** `patches/whatwg-fetch+3.6.20.patch` — out-of-range status now
`reject(new TypeError('Network request failed: status N'))`, an ordinary network
error every caller already handles. Pinned by `notifActionDurability.test.ts`
(patch present + applied).

### B-360 — 1:1 self-video black + camera churn: CallScreen ran a SECOND camera stack (expo-camera) against the call's own capturer 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc240)**

**Reported (founder):** "1:1 video call i cant see my video" (Redmi).

**Evidence (capredmi 12:46):** expo-camera's CameraX (`Camera2CameraImpl`)
opened front camera 1 at 12:46:47 (CallScreen RINGING self-preview); the call's
`accept:begin` at 12:46:51 made react-native-webrtc capture the same camera →
CameraX `ERROR_CAMERA_IN_USE` → **"Will attempt recovering from error" reopen
loop** that steals the device back mid-call — repeated at 12:48:34, 12:48:40,
12:49:10 (during the escalated group call). Also explains the 630k-line CamX HAL
log firehose that rolled every diagnostic out of the Redmi's buffer all morning.

**Root cause:** `CallScreen.tsx` mounted `<CameraView/>` (expo-camera =
androidx CameraX) as the pre-live PiP self-preview. Two independent camera
clients in one process fight over one device; CameraX's error-recovery makes the
fight PERMANENT. In the vc239 session the founder's 1:1s had WebRTC win the
device while the CameraView self-tile stayed black — "can't see my video".

**Fix:** CameraView removed from CallScreen entirely. The PiP previews via
RTCView on the WebRTC local stream whenever it exists (outgoing ring included —
that stream was already acquired); with no local stream (incoming ring) the
existing initials-disc fallback renders. Call surfaces never mount a second
camera stack. Pinned by `notifActionDurability.test.ts` (comment-stripped
absence scan).

**Emulator corollary (same session, NOT fixed — emulator-only):** on BlueStacks
the group-call member froze mid-call (UI thread wedged ≥5 s → **ANR** at

### B-361 — notification inline-Reply piled up failed duplicates + Mark-as-read receipted nothing: the action drain dispatched against an un-hydrated store 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc240)**

**Reported (founder):** "if we reply soemthing in notifcaion. it does not sendd
and it duplicate the reply" · "in notificoan if we press the mark as read then
ther perosn does not see the bluetick".

**Evidence (capredmi 12:46:47–:51):** four `[fcm] pending-action dispatch
failed: 'production mode requires explicit peer address'` — the queued reply
retried on every WS connect and failed identically each time.

**Root cause (three stacked):**

1. `drainPendingActions` (fcmBootstrap) fires on WS `connected`, which beats
   zustand-persist hydration on cold boots — `sendText` then can't see the
   conversation row, a GROUP reply falls through to the 1:1 path (the exact
   failure `SendTextOptions.isGroup`'s docstring warns about) and throws
   "production mode requires explicit peer address".
2. Every `sendText` attempt appends its optimistic bubble BEFORE that throw and
   flips it to `failed` — each retry minted a FRESH id, so every attempt stacked
   another "tap to retry" copy of the same typed text = the "duplicate".
3. The entry is only removed on success → infinite identical retries; and the
   WARM reply handler bypassed the queue entirely, so a warm-path throw DROPPED
   the typed text.

**Fix (vc240):** the drain now (a) waits for store hydration (bounded 3 s)
before dispatching replies/reads, (b) resolves group-ness from the store or the
persisted slice and passes `{isGroup}`, (c) passes the banner's `senderUserId`
as the explicit 1:1 peer — ONLY when the conversation is known-1:1 (an unknown
conversation passes neither hint: a group reply forced down the 1:1 path would
land as a private DM), and (d) pins every retry to `stableMsgId =
notifreply-<entry id>` — a new `SendTextOptions.stableMsgId` keeps the append
but fixes the id, so `appendMessage`'s id-dedup collapses retries onto one
bubble and a late success flips that same row. Both the slim (killed-VM) and
rich (warm) handlers now enqueue-then-drain through this one path; the typed
reply is durable by construction. Mark-as-read rides the same hydration gate, so
its envelope collection is no longer empty on cold dispatch (receipts then send
live or queue on the existing AsyncStorage-mirrored receipt queue).

**Pinned:** `notifActionDurability.test.ts` (12 scans: stableMsgId plumbing,
hydration wait, known-1:1-only peer, both enqueue sites, warm path through the
drain, patch checks).

**Related noise found in the same capture (OPEN, low):** every app boot fires
`[group-key-request:runtime]` for group `8b091751cb05` ~10 s after proc start —
a boot-time key-presence probe races SQLCipher/zustand hydration and requests a
key the device already holds; peers serve a reshare each time (observed served
12:40:31, 12:46:53, 12:49:49). Wasteful + actively misleading during triage
(mimics real key loss). Needs a hydration gate on the boot probe. ALSO OPEN: the
`repair-row` branch of the inbound create gate returns silently — give it a
release-visible warn so a discarded keyed create can never be invisible again.
