**Evidence (host capture, 13:31:43):** `[group-key-request:recv] decline from
88d34848 — we hold no state for this group` — logged by the ESCALATING HOST
seconds after it rang the invitee for room b7c7a31d.

**Root cause — the B-358 fix closed two of three ends and missed the third.**
Recipients of an ad-hoc 'Call' create alias the key under `direct:<OWNER>` =
`direct:<host>` (the name==='Call' receive branch), and the B-358 joiner now
requests under that same handle. But `ensureCallGroupKey` (the mint) wrote only
the ORIGIN mapping (`direct:<peer>`/UUID → minted id) into the callKeyRegistry —
the host itself never held a `direct:<own uid>` entry, so the B-358 serve-path
translation resolved the invitee's request to nothing and the host declined.
The B-358 unit test passed because it seeded that mapping by hand — a test
fixture inventing state the production mint never wrote (the
tests-cannot-vouch-for-invented-payloads class).

**Fix:** at ad-hoc mint time the host also writes
`setCallKeyMapping('direct:<ownUserId>', mintedId)` (plain overwrite on
re-escalation — a host runs one live escalated call at a time; no GC, the prior
state stays reachable via its own origin mapping). Serve path unchanged — it
now simply resolves. Pinned by `notifActionDurability.test.ts` (mint-block scan).

### B-363 — killed-app notification Reply/Mark-as-read only QUEUED ("will send when you open Bravo") instead of sending — not WhatsApp behaviour 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc241)**

**Reported (founder, vc240 retest):** "when i try to send a messge by
notificoain it does not go it saus when i will be in the app … that not the
correct awya it should be like whats app" · "mark as read then it stays as
unread no blue tick".

**Root cause:** in a killed app only the slim bundle-entry notifee handler
exists, and it deliberately never booted the runtime (P1-9's old 2nd-VM
contention concern) — it enqueued the action and posted the "Reply will send
when you open Bravo" banner. `drainPendingActions` only runs via
`ensurePushRegistered` (gated on the warm `started` flag) or the rich handler
(registered only once MainNavigator runs) — so a killed-app action sat until
the next app open. The contention concern is stale: the msg-wake drain
(`headlessDrainAndNotify`) has booted the runtime in this same killed VM since
B-324/B-325, and onBackgroundEvent is single-slot so slim and rich never
coexist.

**Fix:** new `headlessDispatchNotifActions()` (fcmBootstrap): persisted-config
boot (ALL headlessDrain safety gates kept: restore mode / missing db key /
missing config → bail false), runtime up, `drainPendingActions()`, then a
bounded (8 s) wait for the bg socket's `connected` so markRead's queued
receipts flush inside the VM's lifetime. The slim handler enqueues durably
FIRST (mid-dispatch process death loses nothing), then dispatches NOW; the
"will send when you open Bravo" banner survives only as the failure fallback.
Replies ship over HTTP relay (no WS dependency); receipts flush on the bg
socket connect. Presence stays invisible (B-354 backgroundBoot flag).

### B-364 — the 1:1 send path had NO peer derivation: any caller without an explicit peer address always threw ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc241)**

**Evidence (Redmi 13:33:21, ON vc240):** six queued replies looping
`'production mode requires explicit peer address'` at every drain.

**Root cause:** `sendText`'s 1:1 branch is `const target = opts.peer ?? {userId:
'', deviceId: 1}` — it never derived the recipient from a `direct:<uid>`
conversation id (which NAMES its peer) nor from the conversation row's `peer`
field. ChatScreen always passes the peer explicitly, so only the
notification-action lane ever hit it; B-361's `peerUserId` fix covered NEW
entries but the six pre-fix entries (no peerUserId, guessed `direct:` conv ids)
poisoned the queue forever.

**Fix:** derive the peer when `opts.peer` is absent — `direct:<uid>` slice
first (post-canonicalisation), else `conversations[id].peer`. Existing callers
unchanged (they pass a peer); the fallback fires only where the send previously
threw unconditionally. Pinned by `notifActionDurability.test.ts`.

### B-362r2 — escalation invitee STILL stuck at "Joining…" on vc241: the self-handle mapping sat on the fresh-mint path while every real attempt took the REUSE lane 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc242)**

**Reported (founder, vc241 retest):** "1:1 video call turn into group call — one
person join, 2nd person stuck at joining stage."

**Evidence (captures, 13:58–13:59, room c5e5f67a):** Redmi (the 1:1 peer)
joined the SFU, waited under `direct:5b6bb831-64`, its key request was
`delivered=1` — and the host logged `decline from 88d34848 — we hold no state
for this group` at 13:59:08. The vc241 `self-handle mapped` warn is ABSENT from
the host's boot: `ensureCallGroupKey` took the REUSE lane (host already owned a
minted state for this thread from earlier escalations, roster covered) which
`return`s at the resync — the B-362 mapping at the fresh-mint tail never
executed on any real attempt after the first. A second silent gap compounded
it: the reuse lane re-broadcasts the SAME state, and on the recipient the
duplicate create lands in the gate's `repair-row` branch, which returned
WITHOUT the name==='Call' aliasing — so the peer held the key under the minted
id but probed an empty `direct:<host>` slot for 25 s.

**Fix — three independent routes, any one suffices:**

1. **Structural host resolution (the load-bearing one):** the key-request
   serve path now resolves a request naming `direct:<MY OWN uid>` — "you, as
   the call host" — from the ad-hoc 'Call' state this device OWNS whose roster
   contains the requester (newest `updatedAt`; owned + keyed + member-gated).
   No registry dependency at all. Every downstream owner/sig/roster gate
   unchanged.
2. The reuse lane maps the self-handle too (`setCallKeyMapping` before its
   return), matching the fresh-mint tail.
3. `repair-row` now also repairs the call alias from the LOCALLY-trusted
   existing state (`direct:<owner>` slot), so a deduped re-broadcast still
   heals the joiner's probe target.

**Pinned RED-first:** `escalatedCallKeyResync.test.ts` +5 cases run with an
EMPTY registry — the exact real-device state the original B-358 test papered
over by seeding the mapping by hand (invented-fixture trap, second offence).
Structural serve, newest-state preference, non-member/keyless/foreign-owner
refusals, and foreign-handle refusal.

### B-365 (root) — roster drift heal: same-epoch owner-signed SUPERSET rosters are now adopted; roster-declines trigger a resync 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-01 (vc244)**

**Founder fleet map (vc243):** Ariful ↔ Ae2 (`aeb2e71e`) show each other's
names encrypted; Redmi capture holds the decline: `requester not on our roster
copy` (14:15:07, 14:15:11).

**Root cause — two compounding rules:**

1. `decideGroupCreate` treated same-epoch + same-key as an unconditional
   idempotent duplicate (`repair-row`), silently discarding a create whose
   MEMBER LIST had grown — a device that missed an `add` kept its stale roster
   forever (the owner's re-broadcast could never fix it).
2. Nothing ever RE-ASKED: the decliner stayed stale until doomsday.

**Fix:**

- Gate: same-epoch + same-key + **owner-signed** + incoming members a **strict
  superset** of local → `accept` (`rosterHeal: true`). Replay-safe by G-03:
  removals bump the epoch, so pre-kick states sit below the current epoch and
  drop at the stale-epoch arm — a same-epoch superset can only be members the
  owner signed at this epoch. Unsigned creates still drop/repair as before
  (the unsigned-over-live-key arm runs first). Subset/disjoint unchanged.
- `applyGroupAdmin`: a roster-gated key-request decline now ALSO returns
  `{kind: 'request-group-key'}` (the existing post-txn resync lane, 20 s
  cooldown) — the decliner pulls the owner's current signed state and the
  superset heal adopts it. "We hold no state" declines still return nothing.

**Pinned:** groupCreateGate T20-T23 (superset adopt / unsigned drop / subset
refusal / identical stays repair-row) + escalatedCallKeyResync non-member case
now pins decline-with-resync. Note: the arch model is unchanged — membership
authority remains the OWNER'S SIGNATURE (canonicalCreateBytes covers the
sorted member list); the server grants nothing.

**Same session:** one BlueStacks INSTANCE (emulator process) died during a
group video call — no app FATAL/ANR in captures; the instance's adb bridge
came back on a new port (5555→5557). Emulator-level video weakness (B-334/
B-355 family), not app code; group-call verdicts stay on real devices.

## Session 2026-08-03 — iOS navigation audit (back button / gestures) · B-367..B-372

**Trigger:** founder — "now on iOS: navigation problem (back button or navigation), audit and fix."
**Scope:** every `BackHandler` site (17 files), every navigator's gesture config, every
`gestureEnabled: false` screen's on-screen exits, no-back-affordance sweep across all
screens, Android-only `onRequestClose` modal sweep. Core fact: `BackHandler
('hardwareBackPress')` NEVER fires on iOS, and never fires for the react-native-screens
swipe gesture on Android either (the documented BS-022 mechanism) — the only
cross-platform intercept is `beforeRemove`. Only the two call screens used it; everything
else was Android-hardware-key-only.

### B-367 — swipe-back on an UNANSWERED incoming 1:1 ring MINIMIZED instead of DECLINING 🔴 P1 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

CALL-07 (back on incoming ring must decline — minimizing leaves the caller ringing out
the full 45 s) lived ONLY in the Android BackHandler branch. The `beforeRemove` listener —
the only path iOS's swipe (and OneUI's) can hit — minimized every live state including
`ringing`: the callee swiped away, the overlay showed a ring nobody would answer, the
caller rang out 45 s. Fix in `CallScreen.tsx`: the listener now declines first
(`dismissCallScreen({skipPop: true})` then `declineCallRef.current()`), gated on
`isIncoming && ringing && !hangupInFlightRef`. The new `skipPop` mode of the B-306
dismissal helper latches `dismissedRef` (the decline watchdog can't double-pop onto the
parent) AND still consumes any parked group ring — a hand-rolled latch was the first cut
and `escalationRingHandoff`'s B-306 pin correctly rejected it. Pinned by
`iosSwipeBackParity.test.ts` (red-first).

### B-368 — FilesScreen multi-select bypassed by swipe-back ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

Selection mode exited on hardware back only; an iOS swipe (or Android RNS swipe) popped
the whole screen with the selection active. Now a selection-scoped `beforeRemove`
listener converts back-shaped removals (GO_BACK/POP) into exit-selection
(`preventDefault` + `setSelected(null)`); RESET/REPLACE pass through. The header arrow
now also exits selection first — matching hardware-key semantics. MessengerHome's chat
multi-select needs no equivalent: it is the stack root (nothing to pop) and has the
on-screen ✕. Pinned by `iosSwipeBackParity.test.ts`.

### B-369 — registration wizard: swipe-back popped the WHOLE wizard instead of stepping back ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

B-98a made hardware back mirror the chevron (step 2-4 → previous step), but the gesture
path bypassed it: a swipe popped to AgentTypeSelect, whose status auto-forward bounced
the user back in remounted at step 1. Now `beforeRemove` steps back (GO_BACK/POP +
`stepIndex > 0` → `preventDefault` + `setStep(prev)`). Pinned by
`wizardSwipeStepBack.test.ts` (booking project, red-first).

### B-370 — OpsRoomReview back arrow visible (and live) while the payment lock is active ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

`lockBack` blocks hardware back + the swipe gesture during ops-pending AND the auto-pay
countdown/debit window — but the arrow's visibility was gated on `state === 'pending'`
alone, so during countdown/paying/paid the rendered arrow's `goBackOnce()` bypassed the
lock on BOTH platforms (on iOS it is the primary affordance). The ternary now gates on
`lockBack`. Bonus: after the 5-min poll cap releases the lock (`pollGaveUp`), the arrow
now REAPPEARS (previously hidden forever on a screen we had stopped polling). Cross-
platform bug found by the iOS audit. Pinned by `opsRoomReviewBackLock.test.ts`
(red-first).

### B-371 — EmployeesScreen has NO back affordance at all ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

Pushed from DepartmentChannels with `headerShown: false`; its `ObHeader` had no `onBack`.
Android was saved by the hardware key; on iOS the only exit was the undiscoverable edge
swipe. Now renders the sibling ManageChannels header shape
(`onBack={() => navigation.goBack()}`). Found by the all-screens no-back sweep — every
other hit was a legitimate root/terminal (dashboards, Login, gates, Done-button results).

### B-372 — `fullScreenGestureEnabled: true` hijacks horizontal pans on iOS ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-03**

Round 7 enabled it globally (Messenger/Booking/Agent/Auth/News) so ANDROID gained
swipe-back; on iOS it upgrades the platform-standard EDGE swipe to swipe-back-from-
ANYWHERE, which fights every horizontal pan surface: the GroupCallScreen tile pager (JS
PanResponder — cannot negotiate with a native recognizer; the B-242 termination work is
exactly this class), the draggable FloatingCallOverlay bubble, sliders/carousels. A tile
swipe mid-call could pop → minimize the call being interacted with. Now
`fullScreenGestureEnabled: Platform.OS === 'android'` in all five navigators — Android
byte-identical, iOS gets the conventional edge-only pop (which `beforeRemove` still
intercepts, so B-367/BS-022 are unaffected). Pinned by `iosEdgeSwipeGesture.test.ts`
(red-first).

### Audited, NO change needed

- **Gesture-off screens all have on-screen exits:** IncomingGroupCall (Decline),
  VaultLock (arrow→exitToHome), BackupRestore (arrow shares the B-107 guard),
  MissionComplete/AttendanceResult/IncidentSubmitted (Done→popToTop), FindingDetail
  (Cancel search + SOS), IncomingOffer (Accept/Decline), AgentAdminApproval (Sign out,
  terminal by design — B-199).
- **VBGGeoRisk** dropdown-close-on-back stays Android-only: iOS convention is that
  swipe leaves the screen; the dropdown has tap-away/select closes.
- **Agent KYC/Coverage/Availability/DocsUpload**: back = plain goBack/replace fallback —
  chevron works on iOS, no intercept to lose.
- **Modal sweep:** no modal relies solely on Android-only `onRequestClose`; all have
  button/backdrop closes.
- **Product switcher:** B-95's Android root-back → gate is mirrored on iOS by
  `SwitchDashboardSection` (on-screen), so iOS can always switch products.
- **`VoiceCall` route** is registered but unreachable (legacy alias, nothing navigates
  to it) — dead code, left for a deliberate cleanup pass.

## Session 2026-08-04 — iOS build 153 · B-373

### B-373 — four static-scan CRLF guards can only pass on Windows ⚠️ P2 · **FIXED 2026-08-04**

Found while pushing the 1.0.219 (153) build bump: the unconditional static-scan sweep in
`.husky/pre-push` (step 3) went red on four suites, none related to the diff —
`chatScreenMutationUi`, `composerSendRace`, `mutationLaneWiring`, `messengerSafeAreaSweep`.
Each opened with a guard asserting its target file **is CRLF** (`expect(source()).toContain('\r\n')`),
the premise the scans were written around.

Root cause is the checkout, not the code. `ChatScreen.tsx` and `productionRuntime.ts` are
**LF in the git object store at every commit** — including `565ab194`, the commit that
_added_ the first guard, and `origin/main` as of 2026-08-03. There is no `.gitattributes`
and `core.autocrlf` is unset at local/global/system level, so `git check-attr` reports
`text: unspecified`. Git for Windows, however, defaults `core.autocrlf=true`: the previous
sessions ran on the Windows box (see the B-367..B-372 device note above), where checkout
converts LF→CRLF and the guards pass. On macOS/Linux the same tree yields LF and they fail
100% of the time — so the sweep has been red for any non-Windows clone since 2026-07-25,
and the pushes in between went out on `--no-verify`.

Fix keeps the guard and removes the trap instead of warning about it: each scanner now runs
its source through a local `normalizeEol()` (`\r\n`→`\n`) at the `readFileSync` boundary, so
every existing assertion reads identical text on either platform. The guard test itself is
now non-vacuous on both — it asserts the mechanism against synthetic input
(`normalizeEol('a\r\nb') === 'a\nb'`) **and** that the normalization is actually applied.
Nothing was deleted or weakened; the assertion is platform-independent where the old one was
platform-dependent. Sweep after the fix: **40/40/40/40/27 suites, 0 failures.**

Second, unrelated red in the same run — and the **third** time it has bitten (already noted
in the B-367..B-372 gates above): `patches/whatwg-fetch+3.6.20.patch` was not applied in
`node_modules`, failing `notifActionDurability`'s B-359 pin. `npx patch-package` fixed it.
**Run `npx patch-package` after every pull and every `npm install`.**

> first) — this session's two bugs were renumbered B-373→B-374, B-374→B-375 at
> rebase time; code comments and spec names use the final numbers.

Building the founder-requested Linked Members features (member last location on the
owner screen + per-member "which feature did they spend on" breakdown) surfaced two
pre-existing **family money bugs** in the exact seam being extended. Both found by
code-reading the settle paths before touching them (self-diff rule), both FIXED in the
same diff, both pinned by unit tests that were RED against the pre-fix code.

### B-374 — family booking refunds credited the MEMBER (or nobody), not the holder who paid ⚠️ P1 (money) · **FIXED 2026-08-04**

A family member's booking debits the HOLDER's wallet (`resolvePayer` →
`lite_bookings.payer_user_id`), but every refund path targeted the member:

- `refundEscrowHold` / `settleEscrowSplit` / `clawbackReleasedHold`
  (apps/auth-service/src/wallet/wallet.service.ts) credited
  `escrow_holds.client_id` — the MEMBER. Cancelled/no-show/disputed family
  bookings refunded the holder's money into the member's wallet.
- Legacy cancel (booking.service.ts:970) called `refundForBooking(clientId,…)`
  which sums payment debits on the MEMBER's wallet → finds none → silently
  refunds NOTHING. Holder's money stayed gone.
- `family_members.spent_credits` was never decremented on any refund, so a
  cancelled booking consumed the member's cap forever.

**Fix:** `WalletService.bookingSettleTarget(tx, bookingId, fallback)` resolves
`{creditTo: payer_user_id ?? fallback, actorId: client_id}`; all three escrow
settle paths credit `creditTo` (ledger row, balance, expiry batch), and
`reverseFamilySpend` decrements the member's `spent_credits` (GREATEST(0,…))
on every family refund — preferring the CHARGE-TIME membership row via
`metadata.family_row_id` stamped at both charge sites, so revoke→re-invite
between charge and refund can't eat the fresh row's spend (critic finding).
**Caller-completeness (adversarial critic caught 2 missed callers):** ALL THREE
`refundForBooking` callers now pass the payer — booking cancel
(booking.service.ts), ops mission abort (mission.service.ts, RETURNING gains
payer_user_id), stale-expiry janitor (mission-drift-janitor.service.ts).
Pinned by: wallet.service.spec.ts "refundEscrowHold (family)" / charge-time-row
/ "settleEscrowSplit (family)" / "clawbackReleasedHold (family)", plus B-374
family-case tests at each caller seam (booking.escrow.spec, mission.service.spec,
mission-drift-janitor.service.spec) — the caller seams were previously
vacuously green with payer-less mocks.

### B-376 — stale-checkout `deploy-staging.sh` run wiped ~6 weeks of auth-service code off staging (Pro member "not in service") ⚠️ P0 (staging outage class) · **SERVICE RESTORED 2026-08-05**

**Founder report:** `piyaldeb87@gmail.com` is on an ACTIVE 3-month Bravo Secure
Pro plan (activated 2026-08-03) but the app dumped them into the blank "Build
Your Requirements" application form, with a raw red `Cannot GET
/pro-applications/me` under the submit button.

**Symptom mechanics:** `GET /pro-applications/me` returned Nest's 404
(`Cannot GET …`) because the ROUTE did not exist on the running server; the
client's status lookup treats that as "no application" → SecureServices smart
routing falls through to the apply form; the raw 404 message leaked into the
form's error line. **The user's plan row was intact the whole time**
(`pro_applications` status=ACTIVE, 3 months, start 2026-08-03 — verified by
SQL) — only the serving binary lost the module.

**Root cause (forensics):** some machine ran the rsync-based
`scripts/deploy-staging.sh` against the box from a **~July-era feature-branch
checkout** at 2026-08-04 23:17 IST (auth image build time) and again the
following morning (auth container restarted minutes before this
investigation). The script's `rsync --delete` made the box tree EQUAL that
stale checkout: `src/` mtimes 2026-07-05..25, `pro-applications/` +
`pro-management/` GONE (added 2026-08-03), executive/hourly-checkin code GONE
(added 2026-08-04), plus **feature-branch files main never had**
(`department/enterprise-join.service.ts`, `org/workspace.service.ts` — these
later broke rebuilds with 7 TS errors because they reference APIs that no
longer exist). The resulting image served July-era code while the DB carried
August schema (exec_transport, mission_hourly_checkins, pro tables) — old
code doesn't reference the new columns, so everything ELSE limped along and
`/ready` stayed green, which is why nothing alarmed.

**Blast radius while the stale image ran (23:17 IST → restore):**

- messenger-service: tree partially reverted (Aug-01), container untouched.

**Fix applied (2026-08-05):** backed up the one real env file
(`apps/messenger-service/.env`), `rm -rf`'d the four synced dirs on the box

contains pro-applications + pro-management; in-container pricing smoke exec
86→258 flat / Lite 86→344; `/ready` 200; container healthy.

deploy last night (the box shows repeat activity the next morning; the same
period saw the `siraajul` iOS-buildNumber push from a checkout that predated
the v1.0.221 release bump) still has: (a) an outdated checkout, (b) working

deploy when `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" fetch && git status` shows the checkout
behind origin/main (the script already warns that main is the source of
truth; it cannot know, today, that the checkout is stale).

proves NOTHING about which modules are in the image — probe a

### B-388 — the client's bookings list was down for everyone (found 2026-08-05, FIXED)

`GET /bookings` threw on **every call**. The auth-service container log held
**888** occurrences, roughly one every eight seconds — which matches
`BookingHomeScreen`'s `DASH_POLL_MS = 8000` exactly, i.e. one per poll per open
client. The client's whole bookings list, and everything downstream of it, was
dead on staging.

```
ERROR: 42883: operator does not exist: lite_booking_status = text
LINE 3:  WHERE client_id = $1 AND ($2::text IS NULL OR status = $2)
```

**Cause.** `BookingService.list` (the `C-6 list(status,page) honored` change)
wrote:

```sql
WHERE client_id = $1 AND ($2::text IS NULL OR status = $2)
```

`lite_bookings.status` is the enum `lite_booking_status`. The `$2::text` **pins
that parameter's type to text for the whole statement**, so the bare
`status = $2` beside it resolves to `lite_booking_status = text` — an operator
Postgres does not have. It fails at parse/analyze, never reaching execution, so
it threw whether or not a status filter was supplied. Reproduced twice against
the live schema, including with fully inferred parameter types (the shape
node-postgres actually sends).

**Fix.** Cast the COLUMN: `status::text = $2`. Casting the PARAMETER
(`$2::lite_booking_status`) also compiles but raises `22P02: invalid input value
for enum` on any unexpected string — and that was not hypothetical, see below.
`status::text = $1` is the idiom already used at `dispatch.service.ts`.

**Index note.** `lite_bookings_status_idx` exists, and casting the column does
make it unusable in general (the planner refuses it even with seqscan penalised
1e10). For THIS query it is irrelevant: `client_id = $1` drives the plan via
`lite_bookings_client_idx`, and both forms produce an identical plan (cost 18.23
vs 17.87). Verified with EXPLAIN on both.

**Second defect, found while verifying the first.** `VALID_STATUS` allow-listed
11 values but not _the_ 11 — the count matched by coincidence, which is why the
drift survived:

- **`LIVE` was MISSING**, and it is reachable (`state-machine.service.ts`:
  `CONFIRMED → LIVE`). An unlisted value is coerced to `null`, which DROPS the
  filter — so `GET /bookings?status=LIVE` answered with _every booking the
  client had ever made_ instead of the live one. A wrong answer that looks like
  data, which is worse than the 500.
- **`REJECTED` was PRESENT** and is not a `lite_booking_status` at all (it
  belongs to `dispatch_offers` / `agents`). This is also what refutes the
  "the allowlist makes the enum-cast objection moot" argument: the allowlist
  itself contained a value that would have 500'd under a parameter cast.

**Regression test.** `apps/auth-service/src/booking/enumParamCast.spec.ts`. No
test in this service executes SQL — `DatabaseService` is mocked everywhere — so
a query can be fully covered and still be rejected by Postgres at plan time.
This is the DB-only defect class from 2026-08-04. The spec is therefore a source
scan that pins the CLASS: any query pinning a param to a text-ish type and then
comparing a known enum column to that same param, uncast. It resolves table
aliases from FROM/JOIN (so `d.status` is attributed to `booking_disputes`, which
is text and safe, rather than to a JOINed enum table), covers `=`/`<>`/`!=`/
`IN`/`ANY`, and covers `::varchar` as well as `::text`.

**Sweep.** All 21 enum columns checked against `information_schema`; 65 candidate
query blocks reviewed across both services. Exactly one live instance existed —
this one. `apps/messenger-service` uses PostgREST and has no positional params.

**Still owed:** `BookingHomeScreen`'s auto-resume navigation and its
"one mission at a time" gate both read this endpoint and have therefore NEVER
run against live data — while the list 500'd, `bookings` stayed `[]`. Those two
paths need a device pass (LITE_BOOKING_LOOP lane A1/A4/A5); lanes B/C/D are not
implicated by a read-only client SELECT.

### B-387 — founder's own Pro plan dated to expire 2 months early (found 2026-08-05, FIXED by migration)

While preparing the B-383 migration, a read-only probe of the three ACTIVE Pro
plans found `piyaldeb87@gmail.com`'s row carrying
`current_period_end = 2026-09-02 09:26:12+00` — exactly **activated_at + 30 days**
— while the proposal he PAID for (4 000 BC, version 1) covers
**2026-08-03 → 2026-11-03**. The lazy `sweepExpired` read-path would therefore
have flipped his 3-month plan to EXPIRED on **2026-09-02**, two months early,
silently taking his Pro entitlement (and his linked family members' access with
it — `getMine` surfaces the owner's ACTIVE plan to members).

**Cause:** no committed code writes a 30-day period to `pro_applications`
(`activate()` has always written `coverage_end`; the only `INTERVAL '30 days'`
writers target `users.pro_active_until`, a different table). His activation at
09:26:12 on 2026-08-03 landed against an intermediate build during that day's
Pro session — the deployed binary and the committed source diverged, exactly the
class B-376 made visible. The other two ACTIVE plans carry midnight timestamps
from the committed path, confirming the divergence was per-activation.

**Fix:** the B-383 migration was rewritten to DERIVE the period from the paid
proposal instead of blanket-bumping every ACTIVE row by one day:
`current_period_end := latest_proposal.coverage_end + 1 day` (exclusive
end-of-final-day). That repairs B-387 and B-383 in one statement, is
**value-idempotent** (re-running is a no-op — no marker table needed), and only
touches ACTIVE rows. Verified pre-state: `confirmed_at` absent, no marker table,
3 ACTIVE plans.

**Gotcha for future sessions:** `pro_applications.current_period_end` is the
EXCLUSIVE end of coverage (it drives the expiry sweep). Never render it as
"covered until" — read the derived `covered_until` column instead. Rendering the
raw field was itself caught by the fix-diff review as a fresh off-by-one.

## B-389 — "Could not turn on video" on an unanswered call (MESSENGER, founder-reported)

**Symptom (device screenshot):** `Could not turn on video — Something went wrong
adding video to this call. End the call and start a fresh video call to
continue. (upgradeToVideo: call must be connected (got calling))`

**Root cause, in order:**

1. `CallScreen.tsx` `isRinging = isIncoming && liveCall.state === 'ringing' && …`
   suppresses the control tray ONLY for an **incoming** ringing call.
2. The tray renders on `!isRinging`, so on an **outgoing** call — state
   `'calling'` until the peer answers — every control including **Camera** was
   live before the call connected.
3. The Camera button's only guard was `liveCall.isUpgrading`; nothing looked at
   call state.
4. `useCall.upgradeToVideo` correctly refuses (`currentState !== 'connected'`).
   **That guard is right** — renegotiating a PC that has not finished its initial
   offer/answer is real glare — and was NOT weakened.
5. The catch maps known failures to friendly copy. `must be connected` matched
   NO branch, so it fell to the generic body telling the user to **end the
   call** — advice that tears down a healthy encrypted call for a condition that
   clears itself the moment the peer answers. That is what made this dangerous
   rather than cosmetic.

**Fix:** gate in `setIsCameraOn` (the shared choke point — the peer-added-video
alert's "Turn on mine" is a SECOND entry point, so gating only the button leaves
it open), `disabled` + dimmed styling on the Camera control, and a dedicated
`/must be connected/` catch branch that says to wait.

**Why it cannot regress anything:** the screen gate uses the identical predicate
as the underlying guard (`state === 'connected'`), so every state it now blocks
would have thrown anyway — it converts a guaranteed failure into a prevented
tap. Camera off/on during an established video call is unaffected (it returns
early via `toggleVideo()` before the gate).

Regression test: `src/modules/messenger/__tests__/callVideoUpgradeGate.test.ts`
(RED first on 3 of 5 assertions; the 2 that were green pin the invariants that
must survive).

## B-391 — call audio never reaches a CAR hands-free kit (1:1 AND group). HIGH.

**Reported (founder):** "in driving a car when connected with car bluetooth the
1:1 call is not coming by bluetooth … and also the group same thing".

**Root cause — one bug, duplicated across both call screens.** Both screens
clear InCallManager's internal force-speaker flag before choosing a route by
calling `setForceSpeakerphoneOn(false)`. That reads like "don't force the
speaker". It is not what the library does. Traced in the INSTALLED
`react-native-incall-manager@4.2.1`:

| Step                    | Evidence                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| boolean `false` → `-1`  | `index.js:67` — `typeof _flag === "boolean" ? (_flag ? 1 : -1) : 0`                                                   |
| `-1` → pin the earpiece | `InCallManagerModule.java:891` — `selectAudioDevice(AudioDevice.EARPIECE)`                                            |
| the pin is STICKY       | `:1642` — `userSelectedAudioDevice = device`                                                                          |
| the pin beats auto-BT   | `:1879-1885` — `userSelectedAudioDevice != NONE` wins; the `audioDevices.contains(BLUETOOTH)` branch is never reached |
| so SCO never starts     | `:1813-1817` — `startScoAudio()` only runs when the resolved device is BLUETOOTH                                      |

`startScoAudio()` is the ONLY caller of `startBluetoothSco()` /
`setCommunicationDevice(TYPE_BLUETOOTH_SCO)`. No SCO link is ever requested, so a
car head unit — which carries call audio over HFP only — is never handed the
call.

**Why a car and not earbuds.** The earpiece pin is installed by the B-309
opening settle on the FIRST device list, which `InCallManager.start()` emits
synchronously, before the `BluetoothProfile.HEADSET` proxy has connected. This
repo already measured that gap at ~870 ms (B-297, sqa.md). A car kit enumerates
more slowly than earbuds, so it reliably loses that race — and once the pin is
in, the later discovery cannot matter. It also explains why B-251's
"headset already connected at call start" fix did not cover it; that device QA
was never closed (`sqa.md`: _"B-251 needs a real BT headset paired BEFORE the
call is answered"_).

**Fix** — `src/modules/messenger/runtime/callAudioForceFlag.ts`, one shared
`forceSpeakerFlagFor(route)` consumed by BOTH screens (9 call sites: 2 in
CallScreen, 7 in GroupCallScreen):

- `SPEAKER_PHONE` → `true` — pin the speaker (unchanged)
- `EARPIECE` → `false` — pin the earpiece; that IS how "speaker off" is said
- `BLUETOOTH` / `WIRED_HEADSET` → **`0`** (a NON-boolean) → `selectAudioDevice(NONE)`
  → clears the pin, so `chooseAudioRoute` can select the headset and, if it is
  rejected because the device is not enumerated yet, the library's own auto-BT
  branch can still take it when the car appears.

`forceSpeakerOn = flag` runs BEFORE the branch (`:884`), so `0` still clears the
internal flag that `InCallManager.start({media:'video'})` sets — the **B-276 echo
fix is preserved**, which was the only reason these calls existed.

**NOT the cause** (checked and refuted): `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` is declared
(`AndroidManifest.xml:13`, no `maxSdkVersion`) AND requested at runtime on both
paths before `InCallManager.start()`; `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS` present; the
library's SCO implementation exists and is simply never reached.

Tests: `src/modules/messenger/__tests__/btCarRouteForceFlag.test.ts` (9, RED
first on both screens). It also pins the LIBRARY premise — if an upgrade changes
the `boolean → ±1` mapping the rationale is void and the suite fails loudly.
`btRouteRestore` and `callRouteStickiness` were UPDATED, not deleted: their
intent ("the flag tracks the route, never a hardcoded false") is preserved and
strengthened.

> ⚠️ **DEVICE QA OWED — this is the one that matters.** Verify in the car, on a
> 1:1 AND a group call. Decisive logcat signature of the OLD bug:
> `adb logcat | grep -E "InCallManager|AppRTCBluetoothManager|bravo.callaudio"`
> showing `BT state=HEADSET_AVAILABLE` with `user selected=EARPIECE` and **no**
> `startSco:` line. After the fix that line must appear and `user selected`
> must not be pinned to EARPIECE while a car kit is available.

### B-391b — the OTHER audio owner: Telecom was never told the route

Follow-on to B-391, same symptom, second cause. The phone account is registered
**`selfManaged: true`** (`callKitBridge.ts`), and that file's own setup comment
states the intent: _"The OS Telecom layer just provides the system UI +
**Bluetooth routing**."_ Nothing ever wired that up.

For a self-managed call the framework route lives on the Telecom Connection —
`Connection.setAudioRoute(CallAudioState.ROUTE_BLUETOOTH)`, which
`RNCallKeep.setAudioRoute(uuid, 'Bluetooth')` wraps
(`RNCallKeepModule.java:848-866`). **That method was never called anywhere in
`src/`.** So Android had two audio owners for one car HFP link: InCallManager
driving `AudioManager`, and Telecom sitting on its default having been told
nothing.

**Fix:** `reportAudioRoute(route)` in `callKitBridge.ts`, called from the single
apply primitive on each screen (`pickAudioRouteNative` on 1:1; the six apply
sites on the group path). It mirrors the SAME target we hand InCallManager —
mirroring, never diverging, is what makes it safe; divergence is what would flap
the route.

Guard rails, because a routing hint must never be able to fail a call:

- Android only (iOS routes through CallKit's own audio session);
- no-ops when the bridge is inactive or no call is registered — the bridge
  tracks `activeTelecomCallId`, set on report-incoming/outgoing/connected and
  cleared on report-ended, so a stale id can't be used;
- the native side already returns silently when the Connection is gone
  (`if (conn == null) return;`), and every JS path swallows;
- maps to CallKeep's Android vocabulary (`'Bluetooth'`/`'Headset'`/`'Speaker'`),
  NOT ours — the native switch compares those exact strings and falls through to
  Earpiece for anything else, so `'BLUETOOTH'` would be a no-op that looks wired.

Tests: extended `btCarRouteForceFlag.test.ts` (16 total).

> ⚠️ Same device QA as B-391 — verify in the car on a 1:1 AND a group call.
> Expect `[RNCallKeepModule] setting audio route: Bluetooth` in logcat alongside
> the InCallManager `startSco:` line. If only one of the two appears, say which:
> that distinguishes which owner is still losing.

---

### B-428 — the second caller rings NOBODY · P1 · FIXED

`launchCall` decided ring-vs-join from whether the probe returned a room id at
all (`direction: liveRoomId ? 'incoming' : 'outgoing'`), and `direction` is the
only gate on the boot ring. But `findRoomForConversation` deliberately hands out
a room for a 30 s grace **before anyone is in it**, so the second person to tap
Call was told a call was already live, entered SILENTLY, and summoned nobody —
while their own screen showed a call in progress.

The admin was never special. They were simply the one who habitually tapped first.

**Fix:** the relay now reports `live` (`SfuService.roomHasParticipants`) alongside
the room id, and the client rings unless somebody is genuinely in the room. It
still JOINS the discovered room, so a second caller does not fork the call.
Ringing as a non-host is already allowed — the gate is host-OR-participant
(B-334) and the ring is sent after `sfu.join`.

An old relay omits `live`; the client defaults it to **false** (ring anyway),
because a redundant ring is stripped server-side while a missing one is the bug.

---

### B-429 — a lone joiner is told it is not the host · P1 · FIXED

Device 5556: `joined tag=498d64e4 isHost=false existingProducers=0` — alone in
the room and not its host. `hostUserId` was pinned to whoever POSTed
`/sfu/rooms`, so a creator whose boot died before joining stayed "host" forever.

Not cosmetic: `isHost` gates the **call-key mint** and the **ring-cancel**. The
one device that intended the call could neither key the people it rang (they wait
25 s for a master key that never arrives and fail closed — symptom 1) nor dismiss
their ringing screens.

**Fix:** `if (room.participantTags.size === 0) room.hostUserId = userId` — the
host is whoever is first ACTUALLY in the room. Cannot demote a live host: a room
is deleted when its last participant leaves, and the SFU-05 supersede loop only
ever drops the _same_ user's ghost tag.

---

### B-430 — a failed boot never released its room · P1 · FIXED

Boot order is create-room (step 1) → media (step 2) → join (step 3). Any failure
in between left a room with this user as host and nobody in it, and nothing
reaped it — `sfu.leave` matched no participant tag because we never joined. The
relay then advertised that corpse to every other member for the grace window,
manufacturing exactly the rooms B-428 tripped over. One struggling device poisons
the whole conversation.

**Fix, two halves.** Client: the boot-failure path sends `sfu.leave`. Server:
`handleSfuLeave` reaps a never-joined room via `endRoomIfEmptyByHost`, placed
ABOVE the `if (!tags) return` early-return — such a caller has no tags at all,
which is the whole point. No new authority: that helper independently refuses
unless the caller IS the recorded host AND the room is empty.

**Three ordering constraints, each found in review and each load-bearing:**

- **After the ring-cancel, never before.** Leaving deletes the room and
  `sfu.ring.cancel` is host-gated on a room that still exists — reaping first
  made the cancel fail `not_host`, so everyone already rung kept ringing the full
  30 s at a room that was gone.
- **Only when we never joined.** With a tag the frame takes the normal path,
  which runs `hostTerminatesRoom` — a boot that threw _after_ a peer answered
  would have evicted that peer from a working call.
- **Immediately or not at all**, never via `wsRequest`. Not because anything is
  buffered (`emitWithAck` rejects at once when the socket is down) but because a
  10 s-late frame can land after the user's retry has re-created and joined the
  same room id, and would then tear that call down.

A `room_not_found` at join now re-creates once and retries (outgoing only —
P1-BR-1 forbids an incoming boot minting a room), **re-pointing every room-scoped
binding**: the SFU frame handler keys strictly on roomId, so a handler left on the
reaped room means joining a live call whose grid never populates.

---

### B-431 — escalation keeps the camera, so nobody is rung · P1 · FIXED · **the one true regression**

`0bc67a62` (B-301) correctly stopped hanging up the 1:1 before the SFU room
existed, so a failed escalation has something to roll back to. It also removed
the `liveCall.hangup()` that had been releasing the capture devices. The 1:1
keeps the camera; the group boot immediately asks for the same one;
react-native-webrtc serialises camera opens; the boot dies at the 15 s bound —
and because the boot ring is sent AFTER `sfu.join`, **nobody is ever rung.**

**Fix:** release the 1:1's video track and patch the registry
`{videoTrack: null, isVideoOff: true}` immediately before `navigation.replace`.
The MIC is deliberately left alone — it is the rollback target, and muting a
still-live call to fix a camera contention trades a visible failure for a silent
one. Rollback re-derives `videoReleasedRef` from `isVideoOff && !videoTrack`, so
the next camera tap re-acquires normally.

---

### B-432 — the fix would have rung people already in the call · caught in review

Introduced by B-428 and never shipped. Once a caller rings even when handed an
existing room, ringing an in-call member becomes reachable. Foregrounded members
are unaffected (the client suppresses a ring for the room it is on) but a
MINIMIZED member gets a VoIP wake and a full-screen incoming-call notification
for the call they are already in, plus a missed-call marker that nothing clears
on join — so they later receive a "missed group call" they actually answered.

**Fix:** the relay filters recipients who are current participants. With one
exception that matters more than the rule: a member inside the 10 s
post-disconnect leave grace still reads as "in the room", and filtering them
would make a host's Re-ring return `{ok: true}` while their phone stays silent —
the B-336 silent-success shape. `isReachableParticipant` exempts them.

---

### NOT A BUG — the 7-failure camera wedge on BlueStacks 5555 ⚠️ measured dead end

Device 5555 logged the first join succeeding and then **seven consecutive**
`getUserMedia did not resolve within 15s (B-342)`. It looks exactly like an app
leak and it is **not one**. The native trace shows
`CameraCapturer: Stop capture: Waiting for session to open` never completing —
BlueStacks' `FslCameraHAL` failing to bring the session up, which blocks
rn-webrtc's single-thread executor for the life of the process.

Both other devices ran the identical stop→start cycle and recovered: BlueStacks
5556 (689 ms) and the Redmi Note 11 (156-250 ms, balanced open/close, **zero**
B-342). This is the standing rule in memory `b334-group-call-add-not-host`
("never diagnose group-call video on emulators") arriving in a new costume.

**Do not ship a client-side camera "recovery" for this without a repro on real
hardware.** What IS genuinely open, and separate: `MediaStreamTrack.release()`
has zero call sites in `src/`, so every `.stop()` is a mute rather than a full
dispose; and `withTrackBlanked` toggles `enabled` on a live capture track, which
on Android is a full stop/start of the capturer. That is a real hazard whose fix
is arch-gated (GC-06 is the no-plaintext-window security control) and needs a
device capture proving the peer receives nothing during the produce→attach
window. Not attempted here.

---

  cancel the rings they sent — `sfu.ring.cancel` is still host-only. Widening it
  the way B-334 widened `sfu.ring` is an authority change and was left alone
  deliberately rather than rushed.

## 2026-08-13 — B-433: a REMOVED member still gets rung

> **Next free number: B-434.** B-419..B-427 remain claimed by the parallel
> call-audio branch `fix/calling-b419-b427`.

**Founder, on the vc272 build:** "if i remove someone from the group and start a
call that removed person got a ring, it should not be like that."

**Status:** FIXED, client-only (no relay change). First cut shipped with the
B-428..B-432 batch; **a review round then found the fix INCOMPLETE and the
follow-up is what actually closes it** (below). Built and installed on all three
devices as **v1.0.235 / vc273**. **No device pass.**

### Review round — three things the first cut got wrong

1. **`leave` had the identical hole.** `remove` was fixed and `leave` was not, so
   a member who WALKED OUT kept getting rung. Same one-line narrowing, hoisted
   above the rekey-designation branch: every remaining member must narrow their
   own row, while only the designated admin rekeys.
2. **No repair for rows already stale — the founder's own group would have
   stayed broken.** `rosterUserIds` is persisted and has no self-repair (the
   Home sync omits the field, so stickiness re-carries the stale value on every
   focus). Narrowing on the removal event only helps FUTURE removals. Added
   `repairRosterFromRemovalHistory`, called from `ringRecipients`: it replays
   the group's own `member_removed` / `member_added` system rows, **last event
   per user wins** (so removed-then-re-added is correctly kept), and narrows the
   row. Release-visible marker: `[group-roster] repaired stale roster …`.
3. **`participants` was never the bug — my own comment was wrong.**
   `setGroupState` already rewrites it from `Object.keys(state.members)` for
   group / ops_channel rows (messengerStore L9), and both removal paths call
   that first. So the helper's `participants` write is a no-op in every
   reachable shape, kept only so one helper states the whole rule. The original
   test encoded the wrong belief as a device state no phone can produce — the
   invented-payload trap. Corrected.

Also from review: the `productionRuntime` call is now gated on
`stateAfterRemove !== cur`, mirroring the receive side's `next !== args.existing`
— an inbound admin action can advance the epoch during the ~40 lines of `await`
between snapshot and apply, and narrowing behind a no-op would drop a member
from send fan-out while they still hold the key.

⚠️ **Known gap, NOT fixed:** `ringRecipients` also unions the LIVE server roster
from `/conversations/mine`. If a removal was queued rather than written
(`pendingRosterIntents`, offline / 5xx), the server source can still name the
removed user on a UUID-backed conversation. Not reachable for locally-derived
32-hex groups. Pre-existing, unaddressed.

### Root cause — the ring set is only as good as the row it reads

`computeRingSet` (B-247) is a deliberate **union** of five sources, because each
one is blind in a different situation and the bug it was built to fix was "not
enough people get rung". Two of those sources are conversation-row fields:

| source          | what it is                         |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `participants`  | the local conversation row         |
| `rosterUserIds` | the create/receive roster snapshot |

Removing a member updated **neither**. It updates the CRYPTO state
(`groups[id].members`, via `applyAdminAction`) and appends a system line — and
`upsertConversation` keeps `rosterUserIds` **sticky** on purpose (B-247), so a
flagless upsert cannot wipe it. The removed user therefore survived in the row
forever, the union put them straight back into the ring set, and the relay
dutifully rang them.

**Why not just drop the roster from the union:** `groupMembers` is authoritative
for who is GONE but _not_ for who is NEW — a just-added member may have no
crypto state on this device yet — so "not in `groupMembers` ⇒ do not ring" would
re-open B-247 from the other side. Pinned by the second test below.

**Why not patch `computeRingSet`:** a stale roster is wrong everywhere it is
read, not only for ringing. Fixing the row kills the class; patching the one
caller would have left the next one to rediscover it.

### Fix — one helper, two callers

`src/modules/messenger/runtime/applyMemberRemoval.ts` — `applyMemberRemovalToUi`
narrows `rosterUserIds` + `participants` on the conversation row. Passing
`rosterUserIds` explicitly is what makes the write _allowed_ to narrow (the
store keeps the previous roster only when the upsert omits the field); a signed
removal is precisely an upsert that knows the true roster. It spreads the
existing row because `upsertConversation` is a REPLACE, not a merge.

Called from **both** removal paths, because the founder's repro runs the first
and only fixing that one leaves the other side stale:

1. **the remover's own device** — `productionRuntime.ts`, right after it applies
   the remove to local group state. This is the device that then taps Call.
2. **every other member** — `applyGroupAdmin.ts`, receive branch.

Two copies of "apply a removal" is exactly the shape that produced B-286's six
drifted avatar-colour functions — same one-helper-two-callers rule as
`applyGroupRenameToUi` (B-290).

### Regression test

`src/modules/messenger/__tests__/removedMemberNotRung.test.ts` — 8 cases:
demonstrates the stale-roster ring, holds B-247 (a just-added member with no
local crypto state is STILL rung), asserts both fields are narrowed, and covers
idempotence, a missing row, and a row with no roster fields. A third describe
block pins that **both** removal paths call the helper.

### B-418 — multi-org: the header was the easy half (vs2 item 4, review round 1)

**Status:** FIXED, committed `04435323`, **not deployed, migration not applied.**

Founder decision 2026-08-12: a person may belong to as many organisations as
they like, and a manager may administer all of them, with authority following
the org they are currently VIEWING. The mechanism is an `X-Org-Context` header
the client stamps; the server uses it only to NARROW the caller's real
memberships.

Two review agents. Both independently confirmed the header design is sound —
it is read in exactly two places, `pickOrgContext` only ever selects from rows
the guard itself just fetched, and no route reads it without re-checking
membership. **The design was never the problem. Everything around it was.**

| #   | What                                                                                       | Severity              |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| 1   | Header stamped on EVERY authed request from a store cleared only at sign-out               | Cross-tenant, live    |
| 2   | Workspace settings resolved the caller's OLDEST org, not the viewed one                    | Wrong-org WRITE, live |
| 3   | `workspaces[]` built from a `LATERAL LIMIT 1` → the hub could only ever show ONE tile      | Feature dead          |
| 4   | `myInvites` refused the second-org invite the ACCEPT would have allowed                    | Feature dead          |
| 5   | Four more role-blind / unordered `org_members` resolvers                                   | Mis-attribution       |
| 6   | Redundant unique index duplicating the primary key; 23505 matched a name that never raises | Wrong error text      |
| 7   | `/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i` accepts 36 dashes                                                     | Latent                |

**#1 is the one that mattered.** `activeWorkspace`'s own docblock promised
"every pre-existing entry point is untouched by construction" — true only while
the Departmental surface was its only reader. Stamping it in the shared
interceptor broke that silently: an agency owner who once opened a client
workspace carried that org id into the AGENCY product, because nothing clears
the store on leaving. Manager routes then rendered the wrong company, and
dispatch — which scopes against the provider on the booking, not the header —
compared two orgs and **403'd**. The agency's core lane was dead until sign-out.
Reachable WITHOUT the migration, because a workspace owner has no `org_members`
row of their own.

Fixed with an allowlist (`org|department|enterprise|attendance|incident`), not a
blocklist: a route that forgets behaves exactly as it did before item 4.

**#2:** unifying the settings read and write onto one resolver made them agree
with each other; it did not make either agree with the org on screen. A manager
inside Borealis saw Acme's toggles and, on Save, rewrote Acme — 200, audit row,
no error. The sheet now also refuses to save when the echoed `orgUserId`
disagrees with the workspace on screen.

#### The self-diff caught one of my own fixes

Role-filtering the ops CPO pool (`AND om.member_role = 'cpo'`) was the obvious
read of "stop the officer appearing twice". Probed against staging first:

```
cpo agents with a non-cpo membership : 3
would VANISH from the ops pool       : 2
```

Three CPO agents hold a `manager` membership and **two hold only that** — the
filter would have deleted them from ops outright. Replaced with a `JOIN LATERAL`
that **prefers** a cpo row rather than requiring one; re-probed: 11 officers
before, 11 after, no fan-out. Same shape applied to `assertCpoEligible` and
`setCpoSuspension` (`ORDER BY (member_role = 'cpo') DESC, ...`).

**This is the founder self-diff rule earning its keep** — 2,683 green tests and
two APPROVE-hunting agents could not see it, because no test in this repo
executes SQL against real rows.

#### Two traps hit again while doing this

- **A literal `0x08` byte in a regex.** A shell heredoc collapsed a word-boundary
  escape into a real backspace character, so `/^\/?(org|…)<0x08>/` matched nothing and the header was
  never sent. Five tests failed with "Received: null" and the source LOOKED
  correct — `od -c` was what found it. A later `.replace()` "fix" then silently
  no-opped because its anchor never matched, and I had not asserted. **Never
  push escapes through a heredoc; use the Write/Edit tools.**
- **A backtick in a comment inside a template literal** terminated the SQL
  string — CLAUDE.md records this as having happened twice; this is the third.

#### Owed

Device pass, and the migration + deploy. Deploy order for this one is
**migration FIRST** (recorded in the migration file): the old code's own
role-blind checks keep the feature closed during the window, whereas
service-first would 23505 every accept with the exact refusal item 4 removes.

### B-391c — the RESTORE path never told Telecom, and a car is the only device that needs it

**Reported (founder, 2026-08-11):** "the client cant connect call with car bluetooth" —
i.e. B-391 again, on a build that already carries the B-391/B-391b fixes (`ca1845e6`,
shipped v1.0.224 vc258; the device is on vc269). **B-391's device QA was never done** —
its own entry says so in a warning block — so this is the first real signal either way.

**Third cause, same symptom.** B-391b wired `reportAudioRoute` into
`pickAudioRouteNative`, so the seed, the auto-snap and the picker all mirror our target
onto the self-managed Telecom Connection. An audit of every apply site found ONE that
did not: the `onAudioDeviceChanged` **restore** branch in `CallScreen.tsx`, which
hand-rolled `setForceSpeakerphoneOn` + `chooseAudioRoute` and mirrored nothing.

| apply site                                         | Telecom mirrored? |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `pickAudioRouteNative` (seed / auto-snap / picker) | yes — B-391b      |
| `onAudioDeviceChanged` restore branch              | **NO** ← B-391c   |
| `GroupCallScreen` (6 sites)                        | yes — B-391b      |

**Why that one site decides the car case.** With earbuds the restore branch rarely
runs. A car head unit drops SCO routinely — engine stop/start, the unit taking its own
navigation prompt, a phone↔car audio handover — and every one of those lands here. So
the ONE path that runs after a car drops the link was the only path that could not
bring it back: InCallManager was told to go back to the car, Telecom was not, and for a
self-managed call Telecom owns the HFP link.

**Second defect in the same branch.** Funnelling it through `pickAudioRouteNative`
alone would have been a no-op: that helper short-circuits when the target equals what
we last ASKED for (the BS-CALL-CHOPPY de-dupe). Reaching the restore branch means the
OS has already moved us off that target, so the cache is stale by definition —
`invalidateAppliedRoute()` must run first. B-278 learned this on the AppState path; the
transition path never did.

**Fix:** the restore branch is now `invalidateAppliedRoute(); pickAudioRouteNative(want);`
— one apply primitive, one mirroring rule, no hand-rolled copy.

Tests: `btCarRouteForceFlag.test.ts` +3 (19 total) — the funnel, the invalidation, and a
sweep asserting EVERY `.chooseAudioRoute` in CallScreen sits inside the primitive.
`callRouteStickiness` re-anchored: it pinned one variable in one branch, so moving that
branch read as the rule vanishing; it now checks that every `setForceSpeakerphoneOn`
argument comes from `forceSpeakerFlagFor`, which is screen-agnostic and strictly
stronger.

⚠️ **Two false-green traps hit while writing this, logged because they recur:** the new
describe was appended without its closing `});`, so the SUITE FAILED TO PARSE while a
combined run still reported "16 passed" from the other file — a mutation looked
survived when the test had never run. And the first sweep anchored on
`chooseAudioRoute?.(` while the primitive captures the function into a local first, so
it matched ZERO sites and looped over an empty set; only its own count assertion caught
that.

> ⚠️ **DEVICE QA STILL OWED, and it is now the only thing that can close this.**
> Three causes have been fixed on this one symptom without a single in-car
> verification. In the car, on a 1:1 AND a group call:
> `adb logcat | grep -E "InCallManager|AppRTCBluetoothManager|RNCallKeepModule|bravo.callaudio"`
> Expect BOTH `startSco:` (InCallManager) and
> `[RNCallKeepModule] setting audio route: Bluetooth` (Telecom). If only one appears,
> say which — that names the owner still losing. Also exercise a DROP: stop and restart
> the engine mid-call, and confirm audio returns to the car without touching the
> picker. That is the path B-391c fixes and the one no previous round tested.

## B-392 — ApprovalStatus shows the org OWNER's personal name, not the workspace name. LOW.

**Found during the 2026-08-07 enterprise scope-v2 verification sweep (code review, not device).**

`enterprise-join.service.ts` `myJoinRequest` selects `u.display_name AS org_name`
(line ~355), while `resolveReferralCode` for the SAME surface pair uses
`COALESCE(w.name, u.display_name)` (line ~179, joins `enterprise_workspaces`).
So an applicant sees the company name on the JOIN screen but the owner's
personal display name on the APPROVAL-STATUS screen. Inconsistent copy, and it
surfaces the owner's personal identity where the workspace name exists.

**Repro:** org owner sets a workspace name different from their display name;
applicant submits a join request; open Approval Status → header names the owner,
not the company.

**Fix queued (this session, Item E invitations batch):** add the
`LEFT JOIN public.org_workspaces w ON w.owner_user_id = r.org_user_id`

- `COALESCE(w.name, u.display_name)` to `myJoinRequest`, matching the resolver.
  Status: **FIXED 2026-08-08** in the Item E batch — myJoinRequest now uses
  the same COALESCE(w.name, u.display_name) + org_workspaces join as the
  resolver. Pinned by enterpriseJoin.spec.ts ("B-392: myJoinRequest names the
  WORKSPACE, not the founder" — source-region scan, fail-closed anchors).
  Device pass rides the next release build.

## B-393 — the Switch Dashboard row for your CURRENT product was a silent no-op. MEDIUM.

**Reported (founder, screenshots):** open the profile drawer inside Secure
Services, tap "Secure Services" (the row marked CURRENT) — you stay on the
"Book Close Protection" hero instead of landing on the Secure Plans chooser.

> Numbered B-393, not B-392: B-392 was taken by the ApprovalStatus naming bug
> in the parallel enterprise branch. The five commits landing this fix say
> "B-392" in their MESSAGES — written before that branch merged. The code,
> tests and this entry are the authority.

**Root cause.** The SWITCH DASHBOARD rows are a PRODUCT SWITCH, not a
navigate. `switchProduct` only writes `activeProduct`, and `MainNavigator`
keys the whole client tab tree on that value (`key={activeProduct}`). So
re-selecting the product you are already in wrote the value it already held:
no remount, so `SecureTab`'s `initialParams` (`{screen:'SecureServices',
initial:false}`, added by B-390) never re-applied. B-390 fixed where a real
SWITCH lands; nothing covered the non-switch.

Not Secure-only — "Messenger" from ProfileTab inside the messenger product,
and "Virtual Bodyguard" from ProfileTab inside vbg, were dead the same way.

**Fix.** `SwitchDashboardSection` navigates to the product root when
`p === activeProduct`. The store is deliberately NOT written: `setActiveProduct`
would clear B-352's `returnProduct`, silently turning "back at the Secure root
returns to VBG" into "back ejects to the product gate".

**The trap in the fix.** The landing is `navigate`, not `push`. StackRouter
pops back to an existing route rather than pushing a second one, so landing on
a product root ALREADY in the stack truncates everything above it — and
`SecureProApplyScreen` keeps all 15 application fields in local `useState`
with no store and no `beforeRemove`. New `mountedStackHasRoutesAbove`
(`navigation/navigationRef.ts`) confirms ONLY when something would actually be
popped, so the founder's path (BookingHome → drawer → Secure Services) is a
push and stays one tap. Deliberately NOT keyed on `isBookingDraftDirty`, which
is true whenever a pickup has ever been set — it would nag on that exact path
while still missing the Pro form it is not keyed on.

**Also this session (founder batch, 2026-08-08).**

- **Back hint on Secure Plans** — rendered CONDITIONALLY. Two cross-product
  entries land elsewhere (Profile → Secure Plans while the active product is
  `messenger` roots the lazy stack AT that screen because `ProfileScreen`'s
  `handleRow` omits `initial: false`; and inside `vbg` the stack is rooted at
  VBGHome). An unconditional line would state something false on a reachable
  path — and it is the accessibility label too.
- **ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 everywhere** (`utils/countryCodes.ts`). DISPLAY ONLY:
  alpha-2 stays the persisted news preference, the `/news/feed` parameter, the
  dispatch/pricing key and the flag-emoji source. Region badges retire
  UAE/KSA/RSA for ARE/SAU/ZAF and are now DERIVED from `code` (Issue 37 was a
  hand-typed badge disagreeing with its own contract). Country SEARCH had to
  learn alpha-3 or "DZA" — the only code on screen — matched nothing.
- **Operator Partner removed from the VBG onboarding path** only; the funnel
  is how a security company signs up and stays on every other path (D-5).
- **Albums in Files and Vault** — two INDEPENDENT spaces. Vault album state
  lives inside `vaultStore`'s persisted blob so `reset()` wipes album NAMES
  with the file list; a separate store would outlive a Forgot-PIN wipe and
  leave "Contracts"/"Licences" readable. Vault multi-select is NOT included:
  on that screen long-press already means "remove from vault", so bolting
  selection on risks deleting files and needs its own pass.
- **Step 5 TEAM COMPOSITION skew** — the two cells stretch to equal height but
  their content was top-aligned, and "VEHICLES + DRIVERS" wraps to two lines
  while "CPOs" does not, so the steppers sat on different baselines.

**Open, NOT fixed:** `ProfileScreen.tsx` `handleRow` omits `initial: false`,
so reaching Secure Plans from Profile while the active product is `messenger`
roots the lazy booking stack there and **iOS gets no back gesture at all**.
Pre-existing and already on `nestedNavigationInitialFlag`'s known-backlog list.
Fixing it changes back behaviour for every Profile-hosted row (back →
BookingHome instead of ProfileTab), which contradicts `PROFILE_HOSTED_ROUTES`
intent — needs a product decision, not a patch.

## B-394 … B-403 — Founder QA batch on v1.0.225 (Enterprise workspace), all FIXED (2026-08-08)

Founder device-tested vc259 and reported 14 issues against the Enterprise
workspace module; ten are bugs, logged here. All fixed in one batch,
two-reviewer loop (critic + edge-case, 4 rounds to dual AGREE — round 1
returned 19 findings incl. 2 HIGH, rounds 2-3 returned 8 more on the fixes
themselves; every one fixed). Server + client + 2 migrations
(`20260808050000_workspace_channel_names.sql`, `20260808060000_retire_referral_links.sql`).

> Round-2 lesson worth keeping: the round-1 HIGH fix ("tenant decides the
> demote target") was itself wrong ONE PERSONA OUT — agencies legitimately
> hold back-office `employee` rows, so "agency ⇒ cpo" corrupted exactly the
> persona the fix was protecting on the other tenant. The durable rule keys
> on the MEMBER's evidence (a managed-CPO `agents` row of this org ⇒ 'cpo',
> else 'employee'), not on the tenant. Round 2 also caught that the tenant
> table itself was spoofable — `createWorkspace` never refused a company
> agent; it does now (`provider_account_cannot_own_workspace`).

| #     | Sev  | Summary                                                                                                    |
| ----- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B-394 | MED  | Workspace surfaces used agency vocabulary ("CPO") for non-bodyguard staff                                  |
| B-395 | HIGH | Admin could not open their own seeded channels — solo group refused, every channel "Inactive"              |
| B-396 | MED  | Enterprise menu landed members on the channel directory instead of the Home dashboard                      |
| B-397 | LOW  | Dashboard "Admin" stat counted channels-the-caller-admins (5), read as "5 admins" next to 1 member         |
| B-398 | FEAT | Monthly roster could only plan one day at a time — no multi-date shift creation                            |
| B-399 | HIGH | Only the owner could manage roles; a co-manager couldn't even suspend an employee; no promote path existed |
| B-400 | HIGH | Post-join, members saw only channels — attendance/modules missing until a full app restart                 |
| B-401 | HIGH | Joining via invite code needed an app reload and landed on a dead status page instead of the workspace     |
| B-402 | HIGH | Workspace referral code was multi-use and never disappeared — two people could enter on one code           |
| B-403 | LOW  | Invite "Pick from contacts" opened the OS phonebook instead of the in-app registered-user picker           |

- **B-394** — no tenant-TYPE fact existed; `deptNoun` keyed on
  `isEnterprise && !isOrgAffiliated`, false for every workspace owner/member.
  Fix: `org_is_workspace` end-to-end (account-kind SQL → /auth/me → authStore →
  `isWorkspaceTenant`); `recheckMembership` was silently DROPPING the flag on
  every foreground resume (caught by the review scout). Round-2: the SQL is a
  CASE — an org member's flag follows THE ORG, a personal workspace only
  stands in when org-less.
- **B-395** — `createGroupChat` threw on zero other members, and seeded
  channels hold only the admin ("Inactive" == `group_conversation_id IS NULL`).
  Fix: `allowSolo` (key distribution untouched — fan-out runs zero times,
  later members ride the existing add-intent/rekey path) + an admin self-heal
  sweep provisions all stale channels once per directory mount + workspace
  seed names generalized (Team Roster/General/Operations/Announcements) with a
  rename migration for existing workspaces. Pinned by `soloGroupCreate.test.ts`
  (scan) — and `ensureChannelProvisioned` now dedups concurrent same-device
  callers via an in-flight map (round-1 finding: sweep + tap double-minted a
  group and orphaned a master key).
- **B-396** — `openDepartmentChannels(nav, {preferHome})`; the drawer passes
  `preferHome: isOrgAffiliated`. Round-2: the Home TAB is named explicitly —
  a bare navigate was a silent no-op from a warm shell. Non-member payload
  pin (never contains 'Departmental') still holds.
- **B-397** — chip counts people: 1 owner + active managers (listCpos);
  a member's 403 falls back to an honest "Managed" count.
- **B-398** — calendar multi-select → `ShiftEditor` `dates` param (shared
  time window, end ≤ start rolls to next day) → `CreateShiftDto.occurrences`
  (≤31, exclusive with repeat_weeks, deduped, sorted, one transaction,
  per-occurrence roster-month resolution; start/end carry the FIRST window so
  an old strip-mode server degrades to one real shift, and a strict server's
  unknown-field 400 maps to honest copy).
- **B-399** — `setMemberRole` widened to owner + UNSCOPED managers with hard
  lines: owner untouchable (explicit), scoped managers refused, **peer-manager
  demote OWNER-only** (round-1 critic: demote→suspend was a full peer-takedown
  chain), demote target decided by TENANT (round-1 HIGH: a workspace demote to
  'cpo' flipped an office worker into the §35A CPO shell; agency demote to
  'employee' unmade a deployable CPO), role UPDATE is a conditional claim
  (concurrent admins → `role_changed_concurrently`, no contradictory channel
  sweep). `setMemberStatus` rank check protects only manager peers now — a
  co-manager can finally suspend/remove employees. Demote CLEARS the stored
  'Manager' role_label (three-state `updateMemberRole`) so the roster renders
  the live tenant noun. EmployeesScreen: promote button (active employees),
  owner-only demote in a MANAGERS section. 13 new spec cases.
- **B-400/B-401** — NOTHING on the join path refreshed `/auth/me` (the shared
  flow's docstring promised the caller would; neither caller did), and the
  invite lane replaced to ApprovalStatus where an invitee has NO request row —
  a blank page read as "it didn't let me in". Fix: `acceptInviteFlow` owns the
  refresh (awaits `recheckMembership`, one retry if the store still shows no

  pickers already included employees — the invisibility WAS the staleness.

  DESIGN (no consumption concept). Founder decision: lane retired. Mint/list/
  revoke UI removed from ApprovalsScreen (direct invites — bound, single-use,

  (round-1: with the revoke UI gone, a NULL-expiry API-minted link would have

  untouched. `approvalsMintTeam.test.tsx` rewritten (retirement + the R9-3

- **B-403** — in-app picker modal over `useDiscoveredContacts` (device
  contacts matched to registered users — the group add-member source);
  permission prompt deferred to first open; denied/unavailable/empty states
  honest; manual entry unchanged.

**Verification:** full auth-service suite 2,421 green (128 suites, incl. ~25
new cases across org-cpo/attendance/workspace/account-kind specs); mobile tsc
43 ≤ 47 baseline, server tsc 0; deptchat+entry+messenger-screens 48 suites /

  (`ReferralCodesController`+`Service`, list open to any admin, mint/deactivate
  `SUPERVISOR/ADMIN` like subscription pricing; exactly-one of owner_user_id /
  partner_name; audited as `referral.*` under subject_type `system`); ops-console
  `/referral-codes` page (mint form + status/bookings table + deactivate) wired

  `20260809110000` adds the `lite_bookings.referral_code_id` partial index the
  list view's booking-count join needs. ATTRIBUTION-ONLY boundary untouched —
  the existing `referralCode.test.ts` dispatch/escrow never-reads pins still

  resolveReferralCode stays pure). Codes are minted via the console; deliberately
  NO seed migration (inventing partner names would be fake production data —
  founder mints e.g. `TRAVELCO-01` in seconds from the new screen).

  **3-agent review round (adversarial critic / edge-case hunter / deployment),
  fixes applied same session:**
  - Critic P2: bare `@IsISO8601()` is regex-only → calendar-invalid
    `2026-02-30` parsed to NaN, skipped the past-expiry guard, 500'd at the
    timestamptz bind. Fixed: `{strict:true}` + NaN-safe `!(t > Date.now())`
    guard + spec case.
  - Critic+edge P2: Reactivate on an expired code flipped the flag while the
    booking lookup (`expires_at > NOW()`) kept rejecting — unrevivable code
    behind a "clients can submit it again" console promise. Fixed: reactivation
    clears a lapsed expiry (SQL CASE), console confirm says so, spec pins the
    CASE.

    trap (module pin matched the import line even with the controller
    unregistered; role-gate pin matched ONCE anywhere so dropping it from
    @Post stayed green). Fixed: anchored to `controllers:[…]` and to each
    handler adjacency; BOTH mutation-proved RED (controller removed from
    array; @RequireRoles removed from @Post).
  - Edge P3s fixed: list "No codes yet" flashed during SWR load (Loading row
    added); client could type `-ABC` (leading dash) which the server DTO
    rejects with a raw-token alert (client now strips leading dashes);
    zero-width-only partner_name minted a blank attribution (Cf chars stripped
    before the exactly-one check); dead `owner_or_partner_required` error
    mapping (service now throws the bare token like sibling ops endpoints);
    expiry label says "end of day, UTC"; Bookings column tooltip states
    any-status semantics; DTO `@MinLength(2)` matches the console form.
  - Accepted/flagged, NOT fixed: repeat PATCH from stale UI writes a duplicate
    (harmless) audit row; soft-erased owner keeps codes live ("Deleted User"
    attribution); any live user qualifies as owner (schema comment says
    company account — follow-up role check); DB CHECK is OR while API is XOR
    (direct-SQL drift possible); auth-service specs only run via
    `npm --prefix apps/auth-service test` (pre-existing, CI dead); the mobile
    placeholder `e.g. TRAVELCO-01` still tempts typing an unminted code —
    staging smoke should mint that exact code (deployment plan step 3).
