## Session 2026-08-09 — approved auto/'later' booking looks un-approved on the client (founder repro) — FIXED same session + scheduled-booking UX build

**Repro (founder, on-device):** booked Secure Transfer for Wed 12 Aug 14:30Z
(→ `dispatch_mode='auto'`, `booking_mode='later'`), approved it on the ops
console, but the app kept showing "AWAITING BRAVO CONTROL SYSTEM APPROVAL" /
pill "Pending" and never asked for payment. Believing the approval hadn't
landed, the founder cancelled the request from that screen.

| #     | Sev | Summary                                                                                                                                                               | Status                   |
| ----- | --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| B-405 | MED | Approved auto+'later' booking rendered identically to an un-approved one on OpsRoomReview — founder cancelled a live booking because the screen never said "Approved" | **FIXED** (same session) |

- **B-405 root cause** — booking `79779a68-2ac9-4fd1-b02d-b2911bb42534`. DB timeline
  (lite_booking_audit + ops_audit, 2026-08-09 UTC): 04:41:43 DRAFT→PENDING_OPS ·
  06:03:49 `booking.approve` (ADMIN) → OPS_APPROVED · 06:11:03 → CANCELLED
  (`client_cancel`, refunded 0). The approve worked; the concurrent server work
  (auth container restart ~06:00Z) lost nothing ('later' needs no Redis publish —
  the scheduled-dispatch sweeper starts the search ~15 min before pickup).
  "Not asking to pay" is BY DESIGN for auto (escrow at CPO accept); the defect was
  that OpsRoomReview's poll had NO presentation for OPS_APPROVED+auto, so an
  approved future booking was pixel-identical to an un-approved one.

- **Founder build request (same session):** (1) a future booking must not trap the
  client — go-now bookable alongside; (2) submit of a 'later' booking returns to
  home with the upcoming booking visible; (3) reminder push 60 min before pickup.

**Shipped (mobile + auth-service + migration):**

- **Server slot semantics** (`booking.service.ts` create guard): a parked future
  reservation — 'later' + PENDING_OPS (any mode) or 'later' + OPS_APPROVED (AUTO
  only) — no longer occupies the one-active-booking slot. A LEGACY approved
  'later' row still holds it (payment due now; 3-agent review caught that parking
  it let the booking die unpaid at pickup+60 via drift-janitor
  `stale_uncrewed_expiry` behind a green APPROVED chip). Companion cap: max 3
  parked reservations (`too_many_scheduled_bookings`). Pins:
  `booking.b405.spec.ts` (guard SQL at the decision site incl. the auto-only
  OPS_APPROVED arm; DISPATCHING still blocks; 4th reservation rejected; cap
  never runs for go-now).
- **T-60 reminder** — `dispatch/booking-reminder.service.ts` (60s sweep, Redis NX
  lock, claim-first via new `lite_bookings.reminder_sent_at`; claim re-checks
  status+mode so a cancel between SELECT and claim never reminds; sweep NEVER
  throws — an escaping rejection from `void setInterval` would crash-loop the
  whole service pre-migration; lead env `BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_MINUTES`
  NaN/0-proofed). Migration `20260809140000_booking_reminder_sent.sql` applied to
  Supabase by direct SQL (ledger untouched, B-404 practice) BEFORE deploy. Push
  kind `booking-reminder` wired: bridge (opacity-spec'd, P0-N8 intact) →
  WAKE meta + BOOKING activity set + KIND_META + CLIENT_STAGE_SCREEN →
  OpsRoomReview; ActivityCenter bell rows for reminder/approved now route to
  OpsRoomReview, not LiveTracking. Pins: `booking-reminder.service.spec.ts`
  (7 cases incl. never-throws ×2, claim predicates, window shape),
  `booking-push-bridge.opacity.spec.ts` row.
- **Client flow** — all three submit sites (CustomizeAddOns, AddOns, ExecReview)
  send a 'later' booking home (popToTop + "Booking scheduled" alert);
  BookingHome grew an UPCOMING BOOKINGS section (soonest-first, deduped from
  RECENT, year shown when ≠ current); `isUpcomingScheduled` +
  `findResumableBooking` exclusion kills the auto-yank; hero/one-mission lock
  ignores parked reservations. OpsRoomReview: new 'scheduled' state
  (OPS_APPROVED+auto+'later' → "APPROVED — DETAIL SCHEDULED", charged-at-accept
  copy, CANCEL kept, CTA → home), 'later' never back-locks, poll keeps running
  in scheduled state at 30s (no 5-min give-up) and now routes NO_PROVIDER /
  COMPLETED / AGENCY_NO_SHOW terminals; screen state resets on bookingId
  re-target. Pins: `opsRoomAutoApprovedState.test.ts` (positive; the interim
  DOCUMENTS version existed working-tree-only — the positive pins fail against
  the pre-fix source by construction), `bookingResume.test.ts` B-405 block,
  `opsReviewCancel.test.ts` widened anchor.
- **B-339-class sweep (3-agent review):** the `activeBooking` store singleton is
  no longer single-owner once go-now + reservations coexist — OpsRoomReview and
  LiveTracking polls now id-guard every read (routing, lockBack, pay math,
  summary fields, GPS-push gate) and skip ticks whose load failed; LiveTracking
  never routes/arms GPS off another booking's status.

**3-agent review round (adversarial critic / edge-case hunter / regression), all
P0-P2 findings fixed same session** — crash-safe sweeper; claim status re-check;
legacy-approved-later reclassified ACTIVE (client+server mirrored); singleton
id-guards; scheduled-state poll cadence + terminal routing; state reset on
re-target; reservation cap; booking-first summary fields; bell-route fix;
alert copy de-over-promised. **Accepted/flagged, NOT fixed:** reminder push is
best-effort like every bridge wake (Redis outage → claim burned, inbox row is
the durable trace; repo-wide convention); reminder fires for still-PENDING_OPS
reservations with generic copy; a never-approved past-due reservation keeps its
upcoming card until drift-janitor/ops act; sweeper lock DEL is token-less (same
as sibling sweeps — row claim is the real gate); UTC-Z display on the upcoming
card (repo convention, non-UTC+0 clients see UTC not local).

**Verification:** booking 607/607 ×(re-run after fixes); auth-service full suite
green + new specs; mobile tsc 43 ≤ 47; ops-console tsc 0; lint 0 errors;

staging same session (auth-service rebuild). Device round-trip (book later →

## Session 2026-08-09 (cont.) — CPO live tracker: unreadable navigation (founder on-device)

**Repro (founder, two screenshots):** on `AgentLiveTrackerScreen` (the map-first screen a
CPO drives from) — (1) three system event cards printed on top of each other into
illegible mush over the route; (2) the turn-by-turn card too small to read at speed
("make it bigger so driver can navigate"); (3) with the keyboard open the screen is
"chaos": the composer + 6-step stepper + status card ride up as one block and swallow the
map, and the in-map FOLLOW pill climbs into the DARK/LIGHT/SAT/3D column.

| #     | Sev  | Summary                                                                                                                                                                                         | Status    |
| ----- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| B-406 | HIGH | System cards share a waypoint anchor and rendered pixel-perfectly on top of each other; maneuver card unreadable at driving speed                                                               | **FIXED** |
| B-407 | MED  | Keyboard-open state: whole bottom dock lifts as one block and buries the map; FOLLOW pill collides with the style column                                                                        | **FIXED** |
| B-408 | MED  | Message-dock control cluster: all five buttons below the 44/48 touch-target floor, none labelled, SOS reuses the `ptt` push-to-talk style + `C.ok` success token, and SOS UNMOUNTS while typing | **FIXED** |

- **B-406** — root cause: `pushSystem` anchors each card to a WAYPOINT lng/lat, and
  `relayoutBubbles` gave every one the same projected left/top with the same
  `translate(-50%, calc(-100% - 32px))`. Waypoint events routinely share a coordinate, so
  identical anchor = exact overlap; nothing capped the count either. Fix: screen-space
  de-collision (`rectAt`/`overlaps` + a `claimed` list; marker bubbles claim first, system
  cards walk upward in whole-card steps, bounded), `MAX_SYS_VISIBLE = 2` with promotion on
  TTL, and a top guard so a card is hidden rather than drawn over the maneuver banner.
  Card: distance 16→34pt (mono, now the dominant element), instruction 14→20pt + 2 lines,
  plate 44→64, minHeight 64→104; the hardcoded `navOffset = 76` became measured.
  **Palette untouched — hierarchy/scale only, so G8 holds.**

- **B-407** — the dock (`kbWrap`) holds composer + stepper + mini-status and is lifted as
  one block by `bottomPad()`. Neither the stepper nor the status card is actionable while
  typing, so both are now hidden on focus, along with the style toggle + slide handle
  (map controls). `--recenter-bottom` is additionally capped at 45% of window height —
  it is fed from a dock height that INCLUDES the keyboard inset, which is what launched
  the FOLLOW pill into the style column.

**3-agent adversarial review (critic / edge-cases / designer + verify pass, 12 agents):**
38 findings, 6 confirmed. **The panel caught a Critical defect in the B-406 fix itself**,
independently found by two reviewers: the system pass MEASURED before it un-hid, and a
node left `display:none` by the previous pass measures 0×0 → the walk stepped 8px instead
of a card, a zero-area rect overlapped nothing, the guard passed, and the card was redrawn
on its RAW anchor — the pile-up back, strobing once per frame (`relayoutBubbles` is bound
to move/zoom/rotate/pitch). Reproduced verbatim against the shipped code with a harness
modelling the CSSOM rule, then fixed (un-hide before measuring, mirroring the marker
branch) + degenerate-box guard. Also fixed from the panel:

- `SYS_TOP_GUARD = 156` was calibrated to the OLD 64pt banner; with the new card
  (~115-140 measured) plus `insets.top` (24 Android / 59 iPhone) cards were admitted
  into the covered band and sat invisible BEHIND the banner while still burning a slot.
  Now measured and pushed in via `window.setSysTopGuard`, mirroring `--recenter-bottom`.
- The measured `navOffset` was unbounded: at 320×568 / 360×640 with fontScale 1.3 the
  style column overlapped the stepper by 62-74dp and the slide handle the ETA row by
  108-120dp (gate G6). Clamping is NOT the fix (it computes below the old constant and
  drags the column under the zIndex-14 banner) — both controls are now anchored off the
  measured dock and are dropped entirely when the band cannot hold them.
- The new `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` + distance-bearing label made TalkBack
  re-read the card on every 4s poll (distance rounds to 10m; ~55m covered per poll at

  `VBGMapScreen` mounts `VbgKeyPointsMap` with `StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject`, i.e.
  FULL-BLEED behind its own header, while the controls were pinned inside the WebView at
  a hardcoded `top:10px` / `top:42px`. The WebView cannot see an RN overlay, so on a
  device with a 24-59dp status bar plus a ~44dp header the segment landed behind the
  status icons and the chip behind the title. Fix mirrors the tracker map's
  `--recenter-bottom` contract exactly: the controls read `var(--chrome-top, 10px)` (the
  literal is the pre-measure fallback, still correct for embedded card hosts that pass
  nothing), `VbgKeyPointsMap` gained an optional `topInset` prop injected as a CSS var
  (never rebuilt into the html — that would change `source` and remount the live map) and
  re-pushed on `ready` so a WebView remount restores it, and `VBGMapScreen` measures its
  header via `onLayout` rather than assuming a constant (insets.top varies 0-59 by device
  and the header grows with fontScale). Additive: the other four hosts
  (VBGHome/Nearby/GeoRisk embeds, ZoneMap) pass no `topInset` and are unchanged.

## Session 2026-08-09 (cont.) — B-408 message-dock control cluster (FIXED)

Surfaced by the B-406 3-agent review and deferred out of that diff on the verifier's
advice (pre-existing, dock-wide, and the reviewer's own fix collapsed the composer at
320dp). Fixed here as its own scoped pass.

- **SOS was inside the `draft.trim().length > 0 ? send : (emoji + SOS)` ternary**, so the
  panic control unmounted the instant the CPO typed a character — on the screen they use
  while driving a principal. The ternary now swaps **emoji ↔ send only**; SOS is a sibling
  and always mounted. That is also what avoids the collapse the reviewer predicted: their
  version put emoji + SOS + send in the row together (field ~75dp at 320dp), whereas
  swapping one slot keeps **exactly four buttons in both states**, the same as today's
  worst case. Verified by parsing the real styles across the device matrix — composer
  320/360/390/411/430dp = 89/129/159/180/199dp typing (floor 80), vs 145/185/215/236/255
  before; the only meaningful cost is the 320dp typing state, which still scrolls to the
  caret.
- **SOS read as SUCCESS.** The style was literally named `ptt` — an inherited WhatsApp
  push-to-talk button — filled/bordered with rgba of `C.ok` (#00C853, the success token)
  under a red glyph. Renamed `sos` and repainted with the danger token (#FF3B3B). This was
  both a semantic bug and a G8 deviation.
- **Touch targets + labels.** All five controls (voice, video, open-chat, send, SOS) were
  32-38dp and none had an `accessibilityLabel`. Send and SOS now meet the 44pt visual
  floor (they fit: the pill is 48dp inside its border, so no dock-height change and no
  cascade into `dockHeight` → `--recenter-bottom` / `bottomPad` / stepper). Every control
  clears **48dp tall** via `hitSlop`, per DESIGN_REVIEW_LOOP §3.4 which sanctions hitSlop
  where the visual is smaller. **Horizontal slop is capped at HALF the adjacent gap** —
  larger values make neighbouring hit areas overlap, and RN awards the shared region to
  the later sibling, which would turn a tap near the seam of "call" into "video". All five
  gained labels, roles, and SOS an `accessibilityHint` + `accessibilityState`.

**Residual (NOT fixed, deliberate):** the three secondary controls reach 48dp tall but
only 36-38dp WIDE — the single-row pill at 320dp cannot hold five 48×48 targets with
8dp separation and a usable composer. Closing that needs a two-row or overflow dock,
which is a redesign, not a patch. Audit H5 (SOS disabled+visible on a terminal mission)
and the crew-gated `monitor`-mode hide are both preserved and pinned.

**Verification:** `src/screens/agent/__tests__/dockControls.test.ts` — 14 cases, **ALL
mutation-proved RED** against the pre-fix source; booking 635/635 (53 suites); tsc 43 ≤ 47;
lint clean. Device pass NOT exercised.

## Session 2026-08-09 (cont.) — Bravo Feed rename + one category vocabulary

Founder 2026-08-09, three linked requests plus a follow-up:

1. Rename **"Bravo Intel" → "Bravo Feed"** in all areas.
2. Its filter chips must be **exactly the News Filter categories**.
3. **Signals** greyed out (inactive) for now.
4. Selecting News Filter options must **display the filtered options across both
   Bravo Feed and My Feed**, not only My Feed.

- **One vocabulary.** `NEWS_CATEGORIES` in `newsPrefs.ts` is now the single source and
  exports a `NewsCategoryId` union; `WireFilter = 'ALL' | NewsCategoryId`. The old chip set
  (ALL/CRITICAL/SECURITY/POLITICAL/FINANCE/MILITARY) mixed a **severity** — critical — in
  with topics and used names the preferences screen never offered, so a user literally
  could not filter the feed by anything they had subscribed to. Chips now render from
  `NEWS_CATEGORIES` with `categoryLabel()`, so a category added to one surface cannot be
  forgotten on the other (pinned by a type-level + runtime test over the whole table).
- **Aggregator retuned for the 10 categories.** `guardianQueryFor` splits into
  section-backed (world/business/technology) and keyword-backed (security/defence/finance/
  energy/aviation/realestate) queries; `CATEGORY_PATTERNS` replaces the old per-chip regex
  switch; `auxSourcesFor` re-mapped. `sevGate` (which existed only for the removed CRITICAL
  chip) became `categoryGate`, applying to keyword-backed chips — those have no server
  section, so an ungated worldwide sweep would fill the map with rows the chip never asked
  for. `categoriesFor` collapses to identity (a chip IS a server category id now).
- **Prefs scope the Bravo Feed (req 4).** The saved selection (a) chooses which chips
  appear — the strip shows what the user subscribed to, falling back to all when nothing is
  saved — and (b) gates the ALL pool via `matchesAnyCategory`. Two deliberate safety valves:
  an empty selection means _no preference_ (not "match nothing"), and if the keyword gate
  matches zero rows the unfiltered pool is shown rather than a blank feed — a heuristic must
  never present "no news" as fact. A saved selection that drops the active chip falls back
  to ALL instead of stranding the user on an empty list.
- **Signals parked.** It still renders a hardcoded demo set (`SIGNALS_CRITICAL` etc.), so
  the tab is disabled, dimmed, and announced "coming soon" rather than shipping placeholder
  intelligence as though it were live. The demo data and render block are left in place for
  when the feature ships.
- **Rename** applied to NewsHub (`title`/`browseLabel`), IntelFeedScreen header + stream
  label + subtitle, AgentDashboard (label AND the `case` that matched it — renaming the
  label alone would have silently dead-ended the menu row), ManagerPermissions. Route and
  component names (`IntelFeed`, `IntelFeedScreen`, `useIntelFeed`) are deliberately
  unchanged — they are not user-facing and renaming them would churn navigation types.
- **Two existing tests retargeted, not weakened:** `bravoIntelSource.test.ts` asserted the
  old chip→category translation and a CRITICAL world-gate; both guarantees survive in the
  new vocabulary (identity mapping; a keyword-backed chip still gates the sweep) and gained
  a companion case proving a section-backed chip does NOT gate. `newsHubLayout.test.ts`
  (written earlier today) referenced `title="Bravo Intel"` and follows the rename.

Pinned by `src/modules/news/__tests__/bravoFeedCategories.test.ts` (13 cases incl. every

"no user-facing Bravo Intel remains"). app 1468/1472 (4 skipped), tsc 43 ≤ 47, lint 0
errors. Device pass NOT exercised.

## Session 2026-08-10 — B-416: Ops Room key authority extended to delegated managers (single claimed authority)

**Context (founder "go for 2", 2026-08-10):** the B-414 campaign documented an
ARCH-GATED limitation on purpose — the mission Ops Room's E2EE group key could
only ever be minted/distributed by the agency OWNER's device. An offline owner
stranded every CPO/manager/client keyless ("Syncing this group's encryption
key…", group calls dead after the 25s key wait). Founder picked option 2:
extend key authority to agency managers, with the gatekeeper→fix→critic-loop
(+ edge-case agent) process.

| #     | Sev  | Summary                                                                                                         |
| ----- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B-416 | HIGH | Ops Room key authority was owner-only (SPOF): offline owner = keyless room forever; managers couldn't bootstrap |

- **B-416 — root cause & why naive widening is forbidden.** The drain
  (`dispatchRoomIntents.ts`) both BOOTSTRAPS the room's group (minting the
  master key via `runtime.ensureAssignedGroup`) and applies add/remove rekeys.
  Simply admitting managers to the old identity gate would let TWO admin
  devices race `ensureAssignedGroup` on one room and mint DIVERGING keys —
  `inboundGroupCreateGate` drops cross-owner creates (B-35 class), so a double
  mint is a permanent, mutually-invisible room split. The single-mint invariant
  therefore MOVED from the identity gate to a **server-side atomic claim**:
  `dispatch_room_crypto_claims` (migration `20260810100000`), PK on
  `conversation_id`, `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — first admin device to
  drain a room claims it; every other device reads the winner back and stands
  down on that room. Legacy rooms are pre-seeded with the pre-B-416 de-facto
  authority — the AGENCY ORG account, via COALESCE(intents' org_user_id →
  booking assigned_provider_user_id, both linkage shapes; no-org-linkage rooms
  left unseeded on purpose, see review round 2) — so a manager can never
  claim-and-fork a room whose key already exists.
- **Server:** `POST /dispatch/room-intents/rooms/:conversationId/claim`
  (OrgManagerGuard — owner or delegated manager, org-scoped through the intent
  rows, ambiguous 404 for cross-org; claimant = CALLER user id, not the org).
  `assignCrew` now seats + intents the PROVIDER too (a manager-claimed room
  must not lock the owner out; on owner-claimed rooms the owner's own
  add-intent hits the new cannot-add-self benign-ack — no churn).
- **Client:** ONE exported predicate `isOpsRoomKeyAuthority(u)` =
  `(account_kind==='agency' && !org) || !!managed_org` — NOT `is_org_manager`
  (TRUE for the owner too, the B-210 trap), NOT `account_kind` for the manager
  arm (a promoted-CPO manager reads 'cpo'), NOT `org` alone (managed CPOs have
  one). Drain gate + MessengerHome focus trigger + AgentDashboard trigger all
  use it; the dashboard drain is HOISTED OUT of the `getMe` try (a pure
  manager has no agents row → getMe throws → old in-try `agent.type ===
'company'` check made the trigger unreachable for exactly the accounts now
  admitted). `drainOnce` claims every distinct room BEFORE the runtime is even
  fetched; only claim-won rooms are bootstrapped/drained; lost/failed claims →
  skip WITHOUT ack (fail closed, intents stay pending for the claimant).
  Triage: `cannot add self` → benign-ack (else the owner's own intent churns
  `failed` forever); `only admins can` → skip-not-ack (defense-in-depth).
- **Decisions on record:** no TTL / force-reclaim lane in V1 (a reclaim lane
  re-opens the fork surface the PK closes); dead-claimant escape hatch is a
  manual `DELETE FROM dispatch_room_crypto_claims WHERE conversation_id = …`
  after which the next admin device claims (existing key recovered via the
  G-06 key-request window — repair, not re-mint; NOTE the window is
  best-effort/2.5s, so run the hatch only when a keyed member is online);
  `claimed_by` is permanent — no UPDATE/DELETE path exists in code, pinned by
  spec, and the FK carries NO delete action (a manual user hard-delete fails
  loudly instead of silently freeing an arbitrated room for a re-mint fork).
- **Review round 1 (critic APPROVE-with-conditions + edge-case REVISE)
  revisions applied:**
  (1) **Seed source rewritten** (edge finding 7, adjudicated REACHABLE: the
  legacy job-feed lane sets `conversations.created_by` = an HQ OPS ADMIN
  (`job-feed.service.ts` createMissionOpsRoom call omits creator_user_id),
  and `assignCrew`'s resume path matches ANY non-ABORTED mission on the
  org's booking — so such a room CAN later get agency intents, and a
  created_by-seeded claim would strand it un-drainable for everyone, a
  strict regression vs pre-B-416). Seed now COALESCEs the pre-B-416
  de-facto authority: intents' `org_user_id` → booking
  `assigned_provider_user_id` (both room↔booking linkages) → `created_by`
  last resort. Auto-path rooms are unchanged (created_by IS the provider,
  critic-verified `conversations.service.ts:63` + `org-mission.service.ts:549-556`).
  (2) **`claimed_by` FK CASCADE dropped** (critic F-3).
  (3) **Sweep hardened** (critic F-5): ops-console root added + a second
  sweep pinning raw `makeAssignedGroup(` to productionRuntime + the core
  definition site.
  (4) Owner-seat comment corrected (critic F-6 — the metadata seat always
  existed; the KEY intent was what was missing).
- **Review round 2 (both agents APPROVE):** edge agent verified the seed
  rewrite (deterministic — one org per room; idempotent; withdrew its own
  round-1 CASCADE remark in favor of fail-loud) and AGREED with the
  no-auto-delete-on-demotion reasoning; critic verified all five conditions
  landed in the files. Final nits folded in: the seed's `created_by` last
  resort DROPPED entirely (a no-org-linkage room is provably keyless — the
  pre-B-416 drain only minted where intents existed — so leaving it
  unseeded lets the first legitimate org claimant mint fresh, self-healing,
  instead of pinning a dead ops-admin seed only the manual hatch could
  clear; this also absorbs the "provider assigned after migration" residue
  the edge agent noted); the two stale "historical creator" comments
  (sqa.md root-cause bullet + the drain's claim-pass comment) corrected.
- **⚠️ DEPLOY SEQUENCING IS A SHIPPING CONDITION (critic F-1):** migration +
  auth-service deploy FIRST (new APK against the old server fail-closes every
  claim → drain silently no-ops → new rooms strand keyless). Then install
  the APK on an org's OWNER and ALL MANAGER devices TOGETHER: an old-build
  owner device claim-blind-mints while a new-build manager wins the claim
  and mints too → the exact B-35 fork, and the old owner then ACKS the
  intents on its fork so the claimant never retries. Never hand a manager
  the new build while their org's owner runs an old one.
- **Demoted-claimant procedure (critic F-2 / edge finding 2 — accepted
  residual, NOT auto-fixed on purpose):** demoting a manager does NOT free
  their claims (by design — auto-deleting claims re-opens the fork surface,
  and the G-06 repair the escape hatch relies on is conditional). After
  demoting a manager, ops MUST check
  `SELECT conversation_id FROM dispatch_room_crypto_claims WHERE claimed_by = '<manager-user-id>'`
  — for each live room either tear the mission down normally (settlement
  deletes the room + claim) or run the manual hatch WITH a keyed member
  online. Until then that room's pending intents stay stranded and the
  demoted manager remains its crypto owner (B-337-adjacent exposure,
  mission-lifetime-bounded).
- **Follow-ups logged, NOT in this diff:**
  **B-417 (FIXED same day, founder "cant we fix it… go" — full entry at the
  END of this file):** an agency OWNER who
  joins another org's workspace (allowed since the 2026-08-09 Phase B
  owner-join) gets `org` non-null from the four-arm fallback
  (`account-kind.ts` arm 4) → fails `(account_kind==='agency' && !org)` →
  their device stops draining their own agency's rooms ENTIRELY. Identical
  arm existed in the old owner-only gate (Phase B broke it, not B-416), but
  B-416 canonizes the predicate and seeds legacy claims to that owner, so
  for this persona the SPOF rescue silently fails (managers still rescue
  NEW rooms via claims; legacy seeded rooms stay owner-locked). Twin
  (edge 3b): a delegated manager who OWNS an active Enterprise workspace
  passes the predicate but OrgManagerGuard resolves Path 1b (their own
  workspace) first → drain runs, lists nothing, silently useless —
  fail-safe but no rescue. Fix direction: a server-computed `owns_agency`
  fact on /auth/me (mirrors how `managed_org` escaped proxy-discriminator
  rot); requires the recheckMembership full-field lesson (B-394 class).
  Minor follow-ups (pre-existing, adjacent): G-06 pre-mint key-request only
  targets the drain-bootstrap `members` list (= the client) — include known
  crew; `enqueueRoomIntent` dedup treats `done` as terminal so a
  removed-then-re-added member's second add-intent is suppressed (seated
  but keyless) — dedup should be pending-only or latest-action;
  `ConversationsService.remove` is the ONE room-teardown copy without the
  intents sweep (duplicate-copy class — orphaned intents churn the claim
  throttle); the 30/min claim throttle starves rooms behind ≥30 permanently
  stuck ones (bounded by the above fixes; consider a lost-claim memo).
- **Tests (all red-first where flippable, mutations verified applied before
  believing red):** `dispatchRoomIntents.test.ts` 21 cases — the old
  "manager never drains" pin FLIPPED to manager-drains (mutation A proved),
  pure-manager shape, managed-CPO-never, claim-lost stand-down (mutation C),
  claim-throw fail-closed (mutation D), claim-once-per-room-before-bootstrap
  order, cannot-add-self benign-ack (mutation B), only-admins skip, B-210
  owner regression kept. `missionOpsRoomStaticScan.test.ts` re-pinned: formula
  arms + is_org_manager still FORBIDDEN, home trigger uses the SHARED
  predicate, claim-before-mint order, `claimed_by === myUserId` comparison
  present, and a repo sweep proving `dispatchRoomIntents.ts` is the ONLY
  production `.ensureAssignedGroup(` call site. New booking-project scan
  `dashboardDrainAuthority.test.ts` (gate + placement + fire-and-forget).
  `org-mission.service.spec.ts` 4 flips (+owner seat/intent, incl. the resume
  path); `dispatch-room-intents.service.spec.ts` +4 claim cases (first-wins,
  loser-reads-back + no UPDATE/DELETE ever, cross-org 404 before INSERT,
  FK-cascade 404). `missionCommsRoom.test.ts` seat-list anchor re-pinned
  (client AND owner). `assignCrewKeyDelivery.test.ts` untouched, still green.
- **Gates:** messenger-crypto ×2 (run 1: 7 movers, run 2: 4286/4286 — B-126

## 2026-08-10 — B-415: a Pro member's own dedicated officer dead-ends as BUSY ⚠️ P1 product-flow · FIXED

> **Renumber note:** this bug shipped in commit `feat(pro): B-411 covered requests route
straight to the dedicated CPO` before the parallel session's push claimed B-411..B-414
> (messenger notif titles / workspace / Ops-Room calls). Lost the number race → renumbered
> to **B-415**; the commit message keeps the old number, this entry is authoritative.
> **Next free number: B-433** (B-416 = Ops Room claimed key authority, B-417 =
> Phase B owner-join predicate follow-up — both in the entry above; B-419..B-427
> claimed by the parallel call-audio branch; B-428..B-432 = the group-call
> entry batch dated 2026-08-12 evening).

**Founder repro:** Sirajul (Pro tier, dedicated officer Vinod assigned by ops) requests
protection ("secure booking") → the request lands in the ops REQUESTS queue → ops opens
ASSIGN OFFICERS → Vinod shows **BUSY** and is unselectable — while Vinod's own app shows
"No active mission".

**Root cause (two truths that both hold):**

- The BUSY pill comes from `listPool.busy_in_window` / `conflictsFor`
  (`pro-management.service.ts`), which count **any** overlapping `pro_cpo_assignments`
  row with `status='ASSIGNED'` — **including the officer's dedication window to this very
  member**. The DB gist exclusion (`pro_cpo_assignments_no_overlap`) enforces the same
  rule race-proof, so even force-assigning 409s (23P01 → `cpo_unavailable_overlap`
  naming the member himself).
- "No active mission" on the officer's app is CORRECT: a dedication is not a mission —
  nothing exists in `missions`/`mission_crew`; the ON DUTY tab reads org missions and the
  Pro mission view is the PMC-code screen. The two surfaces were reading different tables.

**Fix (founder decision: "it should directly go to that dedicated CPO"):**

1. `requestMission` (pro-applications.service.ts) — dedicated-officer fast path: if
   ASSIGNED window(s) on THIS application cover every requested date (`daterange @>`),
   the request is INSERTED as `SCHEDULED` with the derived team, a `system`
   `mission.scheduled` event, broadcast + `pro-mission-update` push. No ops step. The
   CPO's `resolveMissionCode` view derives protection dates from SCHEDULED rows by date
   overlap, so the officer sees the new dates with his existing PMC code.
2. `scheduleRequestWithCpos` / `createAssignment` (pro-management.service.ts) — a
   covering same-application assignment is REUSED (never inserted — the gist exclusion
   forbids it; never CANCELLED by the all-or-nothing rollback). `createAssignment` is
   idempotent over a covered window.
3. `listPool(from,to,application_id?)` (+ controller + console) — annotates
   `dedicated_in_window` (same-app covering) and keeps that officer `available`; the
   pool picker sorts him first and pills him **DEDICATED** instead of BUSY.
4. Client Assigned Team screen went LIVE (founder follow-up): new
   `GET /pro-applications/:id/team` (assertPlanAccess; identity+window projection —
   **mission_code never reaches the member**) + `ProAssignedTeamScreen` now fetches via
   `secureProApi.team`, WS `useProAppRealtime` + 10s poll, ON DUTY / SCHEDULED states,
   window dates. Fake `+ ASSIGN` toggle and hardcoded empty CPO list removed.
   `SecureProCalendarScreen` success alert branches for the auto-scheduled case.

**Pinned by (mutation-proven red first):**
`pro-applications.service.spec.ts` (fast-path SCHEDULED insert + covering-range params +
system event + push; REQUESTED preserved when uncovered; listTeam gate + mission_code
exclusion) and `pro-management.dedicated.spec.ts` (6: pool annotation/params/availability;
reuse-no-INSERT; rollback never cancels the dedication row; foreign dedication still 409s).

**Gates:** auth-service full suite green (exit 0); pro-\* suites 35/35 + 6/6; ops-console
tsc clean; mobile tsc 43 ≤ 47 baseline; eslint 0 errors on touched files. **Device pass
PENDING** (mobile changes need an APK rebuild; server+console changes need a Contabo
deploy — GH Actions dead, manual tar-overlay).

**Files:** `apps/auth-service/src/pro-applications/{pro-applications.service.ts,.controller.ts}`,
`apps/auth-service/src/pro-management/{pro-management.service.ts,pro-management-ops.controller.ts}`,
`apps/ops-console/src/{lib/api.ts,app/pro-applications/[id]/page.tsx}`,
`src/services/api.ts`, `src/screens/pro/ProAssignedTeamScreen.tsx`,
`src/screens/securepro/SecureProCalendarScreen.tsx`. No DB migration needed.

**Founder ("what should i do with that cant we fix it… made a plane than
excute it", same critic + edge-case process):** fix the B-417 follow-up logged
in the B-416 entry, and make the demoted-manager claims trap discoverable.
Plan doc: `docs/handoffs/B417_OWNER_AUTHORITY_PLAN_2026-08-10.md` — critic
reviewed the PLAN before any code (GO + 3 binding amendments, all folded in).

| ----- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B-417 | HIGH | Phase B owner-join makes `org` non-null for an agency owner → the `!org` owner inference fails → their device silently stops draining/claiming their own agency's Ops Rooms |

  `account_kind==='agency' && !org`. Phase B (2026-08-09) let an owner join
  another org's workspace; the four-arm precedence (`account-kind.ts` arm 4
  fallback) then resolves `org` = the joined workspace → the inference reads

  class as B-210 (`is_org_manager`) and the reason `managed_org` exists.

  `agent_type==='company' && agent_status==='ACTIVE'` (mirrors guard Path 1
  exactly, so fact and admission cannot disagree; deliberately STRICTER than
  the status-blind account_kind); fail-closed branch carries `false`; getMe
  spreads it (the ONE server assembly lane). Client: `authApi.me()` type,
  `User` type, `toUser` (param+body), all FOUR `authApi.me()` destructures,

  whose dropped fields silently revert on the next profile edit; the exact

  `(account_kind==='agency' && !org) || !!owns_agency || !!managed_org` —

- **Fix B — demotion stranded-claims discoverability (report-only, never

  → audit `member.crypto_claims_stranded` {trigger, rooms} + response field

## B-435 / B-436 — a notification tap read the WRONG organisation's data (vs2 edge A1/A2)

**Source:** `docs/qa/BRAVO_CHANNELS_VS2_CRITICAL_REVIEW_2026-08-13.md` Part 2, findings
A1 + A2. Fixed 2026-08-13. Both are one bug with three doors.

- **B-435 (Major) — incident push tap dead-ends for a multi-org manager.** Item 4 made a
  person able to belong to several organisations, and every org-scoped read is stamped
  with the ACTIVE workspace (`X-Org-Context`). Nothing on a tap ever set it. A manager of
  two orgs got "Acme: incident reported", tapped, and the fetch carried BOREALIS —
  `detail()` filters `WHERE id = $1 AND org_user_id = $2`, missed, and
  `IncidentDetailScreen` swallowed the 404 into `setReport(null)`. From a killed app it
  failed on EVERY tap for a non-default org: the context is session-only, so null at boot.
- **B-436 (Major) — the same mechanism on the enterprise join/approval wakes.** A two-org
  admin tapping org-B's "join request waiting" read org-A's (usually empty) Approvals inbox.

**Root cause (one sentence):** the wake blobs named the org for the BANNER (`orgName`) but
never for the TAP, and no push/bell path had ever written a workspace context.

**Fix — one contract, three doors.**

- Server: additive `orgId` on the incident + ADMIN-side enterprise blobs
  (`booking-push-bridge.service.ts`), threaded into the durable inbox row as a new nullable
  `org_user_id` (migration `20260813120000_notifications_org_context.sql`) and echoed on
  `GET /me/notifications`. `attendance.service.setDayStatus` is the ONE `record()` caller
  outside the bridge and threads it directly.
- Client: `src/store/adoptOrgContext.ts` — the ONLY writer. Refuses any org not already in
  `user.workspaces` (so a forged blob cannot even change what the UI asks for), lowercases
  before matching, and supersedes an older in-flight adoption.
- Doors: both `routeServerWakeTap` lanes (`fcmBootstrap.ts`) + the durable bell row
  (`ActivityCenterScreen.tsx`). The bell row was NOT in the review's finding — it is the
  lane that carries every delivery which missed the 5-minute blob, i.e. exactly the cold
  taps that fail on every non-default org.
- Deliberately UNSCOPED: `incident-status` → MyIncidents and the applicant-side enterprise
  kinds → ApprovalStatus. Both are cross-org self-reads (verified: neither endpoint reads
  the org header); scoping them would HIDE the other org's invites and reports.

**Also fixed in the same pass** (each found by the review agents, each mutation-proven):

- The wake-time bell row dropped `incidentId` entirely, so before the next server sync an
  incident row opened the QUEUE instead of the report — item 16's own contract, half-built.
- Enterprise banner ids were org-agnostic (`stableId = kind`), so with `orgId` on the
  payload org B's wake REPLACED org A's banner and its data: a two-org admin could only
  ever reach whichever org fired last. Now `${kind}:${orgId}`.

**Regression tests.** `adoptOrgContext.test.ts` (20: adoption, refusal, case normalisation,
supersede, ordering) + `activityCenterWiring.test.ts` (23 total, 14 new: the chain
server→blob→row→response→store→3 doors, per-door adopt-BEFORE-navigate ordering,
one-writer, settle > held frame). **Mutation-proven:** adopt-after-navigate → RED; `incident` dropped from the
scoping arm → RED; a hand-rolled `setActiveWorkspace` → RED; one `superseded` guard
removed → RED.

**⚠️ TWO TEST BUGS CAUGHT BY THE REVIEW AGENTS — both were shipping GREEN AND VACUOUS:**

1. `expect([label, source]).not.toContain(needle)` is ARRAY MEMBERSHIP, not substring. The
   tuple-wrap (added for a readable failure message) made the "ONE context writer" guard —
   the guard on the membership check that makes client-side adoption safe at all — incapable
   of ever going red. Verified empirically against this repo's own `expect`. **Use
   `it.each` for the label and assert on the raw string.**
2. A case-sensitivity test used an ALL-DIGIT uuid, so `.toUpperCase()` was the identity
   function. It "passed" while the code validated case-INSENSITIVELY (`/i`) and then
   compared case-SENSITIVELY against Postgres-lowercased ids — a mixed-case id passed the
   gate and then silently reported `skipped`, indistinguishable from "not a member".
   **Fixture values must contain the characters the assertion is about.**

**Accepted consequences (founder-visible, not bugs):**

- Adoption is session-sticky with no revert, and `X-Org-Context` decides the DESTINATION of
  two writes (clock-in, incident submit). Accepted because every door navigates INTO that
  workspace's own surface — the same contract as a hub tile. Do NOT extend adoption to any
  door that leaves the user outside that org's surface. Enumerated in the module header.
- A membership created while the app was KILLED is not in the persisted auth snapshot, so
  the FIRST wake from a brand-new org degrades to the sticky context until `/auth/me` lands.
  Self-healing; `[orgctx] wake org not a membership` names it in a device log.

**NOT fixed — A9 is NOT covered, contrary to the review's "resolves this seam for free".**
Verified: the dept-message wake carries only `{kind, conversationId, senderUserId}` and
messenger-service holds no org membership data; `resolveDeptConversation` returns
`{channelId}` with no org. Closing it needs a persisted `conversationId → orgId` map fed
from `armDeptConversationRegistry` (which already fetches `listChannels()` UNSCOPED, and
those rows carry `org_id`) — a separate change to the persisted messenger store.

**Gates:** crypto ×2 both fully green 4325/4325 (⚠️ 5-then-3 MOVING failures in
`freeSpacePrecheck` were the known B-126/B-153 flake — `npx jest --clearCache` → green,
confirming the stale-transform-cache mechanism); app 1877 ✓; auth-service 2703 ✓ (targeted
332 ✓); tsc 42 ≤ 47; auth-service tsc clean; lint 0 errors.

**DEPLOY ORDER — MIGRATION FIRST, SERVICE SECOND.** `NotificationsService.record()` and
`list()` both swallow their errors by contract, so a service that ships ahead of the
migration fails EVERY durable notification insert with 42703 at `warn` level only and
`list()` returns `[]` — emptying every user's bell, for every event class, silently. CI
`deploy-staging.yml` does not fire (CONTABO_SSH_KEY missing), so this is a manual ordering.

**DEVICE PASS OWED:** two-org manager, incident push + join-request push, warm and from a
killed app; confirm `[orgctx] wake adopted org=…` in the post-install log.

## B-437 — the workspace/agency form followed the USER, not the ORG (vs2 edge A3)

**Source:** `docs/qa/BRAVO_CHANNELS_VS2_CRITICAL_REVIEW_2026-08-13.md` finding A3. Fixed 2026-08-13.

`isWorkspaceTenant` is a USER-level predicate — true for anyone with ANY workspace
affiliation — and it was never narrowed to the org being administered. So the dual persona
(an agency company/manager who ALSO joined an Enterprise workspace) opened their **agency's**
Manage Channels and got the workspace-shaped UI. The damaging half: `ChannelEditorScreen`
DROPS the DEPARTMENT and TYPE fields on that shape, so new agency channels were created with
`department = NULL` — the live branch-scope key for attendance (13 handlers), incidents and
invite minting, and a null department also makes the channel mintable by every manager under
item 7's relaxation.

**Fix.** `listOrgChannels` already resolved the per-org answer for its OWN mint refusal and
simply never echoed it. It now returns `{workspace_tenant, channels}` — a RESPONSE field, not
a row field, because a clean P3 workspace has zero rows and a per-row flag could never speak
for it. `ManageChannelsScreen` uses `serverTenant ?? userTenant` and hands the fact to the
editor through ONE `openEditor` helper; the editor prefers its own freshly-fetched value,
then the param, then the user flag.

**Safety property worth knowing:** the fix can only ever narrow true to false. A server
`true` implies an `org_workspaces` row, and every route to such an org also lights a
user-level flag — so `serverTenant true / userTenant false` is not producible by real data.

**Also fixed in the same pass** (review findings, each mutation-proven):

- `openEditor` passed the RESOLVED boolean, which is always defined and therefore killed the
  editor's own `??` fallback — a tap before the list landed froze the wrong tenant in for the
  form's whole life. It now passes `serverTenant`, undefined included.
- The "New channel" footer renders OUTSIDE the loading fork, so it was the one editor door
  reachable before the server had answered. Gated on `!loading`.
- `serverTenant` was sticky across a SUCCESSFUL response that omitted the field; during a
  rolling auth deploy a refetch landing on an old instance paired the NEW org's rows with the
  PREVIOUS org's answer. Adopted on every success, retained only on `catch`.
- **A SAVE-TIME ORG-DRIFT REFUSAL.** The editor's tenant is a navigate-time snapshot but the
  write's org is a request-time header, and B-435's push adoption can now move the context
  under an open form — the editor lives on the outer messenger stack, which the departmental
  org-switch remount does not reach, and a push tap moves to another TAB rather than
  unmounting it. Save then POSTed the agency form's `department` into whichever workspace the
  context had moved to. It now compares the org it opened under against the live one and
  refuses. Precedent: `ModuleVisibilitySheet`.
- `root_channel_not_supported_for_agency` was rendering as a raw code; `data.channels` was
  read unguarded here while the other two readers use `?? []`.

**Regression tests.** `channelEditorSimplified` (19: dual-persona form shape both directions,
department actually SENT, org-drift refusal, compat) + `manageChannelsOrgScoped` (29: shape
follows the server, zero-channel workspace, failed-refetch stickiness, and a **one-door
scan**) + `channelTreeFields` (5 server pins incl. the controller pass-through).
**Mutation-proven:** `params?.workspaceTenant ?? userTenant` to `userTenant` = 3 RED;
`serverTenant ?? userTenant` to `userTenant` = 4 RED; controller re-wrapping = 1 RED.

**⚠️ A THIRD VACUOUS TEST, caught by review — same class as B-435's two.**
`fireEvent(scrollView, 'refresh')` does NOT fire pull-to-refresh: the handler lives on the
`refreshControl`, which is a CHILD on iOS (the preset's platform), and RNTL's event lookup
only walks UP. **This file already documented that** and the new case ignored it. Proven by a
coverage probe — the catch body was never entered, so the assertion was satisfied by the
first successful load alone. Use
`getByTestId('manage-scroll').props.refreshControl.props.onRefresh()`.

**Remaining holes (NOT fixed, deliberately):**

- `DepartmentChannelsScreen.tsx:270` still keys `orgFirst` and the blue Manage-Channels CTA
  off the user-level flag. Presentation only, no write gated on it — but its feed
  (`listChannels`) is called UNSCOPED across orgs in places, so closing it needs a per-ROW
  flag, not a per-response one.
- `deptNoun.ts` to `entitlements.ts` is a SECOND independent copy of the predicate (its own
  comment records that these two drifted once). The dual persona now gets the correct agency
  form with a hint that still says "Members" where agency wording is "CPOs".
- `ChannelEditor` has no `getId`, so two quick taps swap params without remounting and Save
  can write row A's fields onto row B. The repo fixed this exact class on `DepartmentChat`.
  Left alone here because it changes navigation semantics and wants a device pass.
- The department CLEAR sentinel (empty string) is unreachable from the client, so a channel
  that acquired a department cannot be un-set from the app.

**Damaged data:** candidates only, no backfill warranted (a null department on an agency
channel is a legal state). Detection query — channels with no department, nested, live, whose
org has no `org_workspaces` row:

```sql
SELECT c.id, c.org_id, c.name, c.created_by, c.created_at
  FROM public.department_channels c
 WHERE c.department IS NULL
   AND c.parent_id IS NOT NULL
   AND c.is_broadcast = FALSE
   AND c.archived_at IS NULL
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.org_workspaces w WHERE w.owner_user_id = c.org_id);
```

**Gates:** app 1904 ✓, auth-service 2708 ✓, crypto 4325 ✓, tsc 42 ≤ 47, lint 0 errors.
**DEPLOY:** server first — the client fix is INERT until auth-service ships the field, and
this repo ships APKs ahead of auth-service.
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** dual-persona account (agency manager + one workspace membership) →
agency Manage Channels shows the flat list and the editor keeps DEPARTMENT.

## B-438 — "freeze at Verifying ID" is the BiometricGate, not the call stack (vs2 review §4.5)

Founder-reported as a CALL symptom. The literal string is this gate's own
"Verifying identity…" (`BiometricGate.tsx`), and a cold boot from an incoming call with
Biometric Lock on must clear this gate while the 45s ring TTL burns — so a hang here eats
the call silently. Fixed 2026-08-13. No prior entry; **this file had no test at all.**

**Mechanism.** `LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync` had NO bound. If the native prompt
never resolved, status stayed `prompting` forever — and the retry button renders only on
`failed`, so there was no affordance of any kind. Worse, the re-entrancy guard made the
foreground relock a silent no-op while that call was wedged: it set `checking`,
`authenticate()` returned immediately, and the gate parked on a spinner nothing could move.
The file logged NOTHING on any path, which is why this never appeared in a device log.

**Fix.** An 8s prompt watchdog to a new `stalled` status that renders the retry button that
already existed, with honest copy; a `nextRun`/`ownerRun` ownership protocol so a superseded
run cannot write status or release the guard, while a LATE SUCCESS takes ownership back (and
the superseding run's own ownership check then aborts it, so it cannot re-lock someone who
just authenticated); `cancelAuthenticate()` before every prompt on Android; and
release-visible `[biogate]` warns on open / stall / close / late-success / throw.

**IT NEVER BYPASSES THE GATE.** `stalled` is excluded from `unlocked`; a test asserts
children stay unmounted. Weakening a biometric gate needs architecture approval — a
timeout-to-retry weakens nothing.

**Round-2 fixes (each a review finding against the first draft):**

- **The first draft re-created its own bug class:** `await cancelAuthenticate()` sat BEFORE
  the watchdog was armed. That call runs on the Android MAIN queue, and a blocked main thread
  is exactly what produces a wedged prompt — it could hang on `checking` with no button and
  no live timer. The id/ownership claim and the watchdog are now armed before ANY await.
- **20s was the worst possible value.** Every call tap lane waits exactly 20 000ms for
  `navigationRef.isReady()` then abandons the route, and the nav ref cannot become ready
  while this gate is up because `RootNavigator` is its CHILD — so a 20s watchdog handed the
  user their retry at the instant the call route gave up. **8s.**
- A ~250ms settle after the cancel: `cancelAuthenticate` does not resolve the outstanding
  promise (a background executor does, into the module's single `promise` field), so
  re-prompting immediately races it into resolving the NEW promise with `user_cancel`.
- **A BOOT WATCHDOG (6s)** for the wedge the prompt watchdog structurally cannot see: the
  opt-in flag read and `runAfterInteractions` both happen BEFORE `authenticate()`, and a hang
  in the flag read renders a spinner with no label AND no button. Fails closed — it offers a
  retry that re-reads the flag rather than forcing the gate on, because forcing it on
  immediately fires the auto-prompt effect and swallows the very button being shown.

**⚠️ TWO MORE VACUOUS ASSERTIONS, caught by review.** `getByText('UNLOCKED CONTENT')` cannot
detect a re-lock: once unlocked the gate keeps children mounted forever and re-locks with an
absolutely-positioned SIBLING overlay, and RNTL ignores stacking. Assert the ABSENCE OF THE
LOCK instead. Also `clearTimeout(watchdog)` was unpinned — deleting it left every test green
while the app would re-lock itself 8s after EVERY successful unlock.

**Test-harness note for the next person:** fake-timer advances must be in SEPARATE `act`
boundaries. React batches the flag-read continuation and only commits it when `act` finishes,
so the 250ms timer does not exist until the block ends — advancing inside the same block runs
every advance before the timer they are meant to fire. Verified with a probe.

**Regression tests.** `biometricGateWedge.test.tsx` (11) — escapable-not-bypassed, supersede,
late success/failure ownership, watchdog disarm, boot deadline, release-visible logs.
**Mutation-proven:** watchdog removed = 5 RED; `clearTimeout` removed = 2 RED; late-failure
guard removed = 3 RED.

**FIXED IN THE SAME PASS (founder decision, 2026-08-13): the Android LOCKOUT fail-open.**
`isEnrolledAsync()` is `canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_WEAK) == SUCCESS`, so five failed attempts
(a lockout) made it return false — and the gate read that as "no biometrics on this device",
took the `unsupported` arm, set `everUnlocked` and **opened the app with no authentication at
all**. Fail 5x, force-stop, relaunch, and you were in. Same for `HW_UNAVAILABLE`,
`SECURITY_UPDATE_REQUIRED`, and for an enrolment removed while the app ran. iOS already
counted `biometryLockout` as enrolled; Android did not. Both copies (`BiometricGate` and
`VbgScanPrompt` — where it turned "just failed five times" into an automatic PASS on a
security check-in) now use `getEnrolledLevelAsync()` and fall through only on `NONE`. The
hardware check is gone on purpose: `disableDeviceFallback:false` means a PIN-only device
still gets a working prompt, so dropping it TIGHTENS the gate without locking anyone out.
Pinned by two tests; mutation-proven (widening the predicate to require BIOMETRIC_STRONG
turns the suite red).

**⚠️ STILL NOT FIXED — need the founder + a device pass:**

1. **An AsyncStorage read ERROR disables the lock entirely** — `.catch(() => null)` conflates
   "read failed" with "not set", so one transient storage failure means no gate at all.
2. **A relock lands on top of a live auto-accepted call**: mic open, overlay covering every
   control — no hang-up, no mute, no caller identity. Plausibly the founder's literal
   "freeze at verifying ID during a call".
3. **The overlay does not cover RN `Modal`s** (separate native window) — any sheet open at
   relock time stays on top and interactive.

**Gates:** app 1906 ✓, crypto 4325 ✓, tsc 42 ≤ 47, lint 0 errors.
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** the founder's repro (cold boot from a call notification with Biometric
Lock on); confirm `[biogate] prompt open` and, if it stalls, `[biogate] STALLED` in logcat —
the whole point is that this lane is now visible at all. **iOS is unverified:**
`cancelAuthenticate` is Android-only and the suite pins `Platform.OS='android'`, so the iOS
supersede rests entirely on the ownership race.

## B-439 — cross-surface doors that switched silently (vs2 edges A5 + A6)

**Source:** `docs/qa/BRAVO_CHANNELS_VS2_CRITICAL_REVIEW_2026-08-13.md` findings A5/A6. Founder
decision 2026-08-13: make BOTH consistent, through the one shared helper. Fixed same day.

Item 18 gave cross-product switches a confirm. Three doors never got it:

- **A5 — the VBG Home "Secure Services" tile.** `switchProduct('secure', …)` bare: no
  `confirmSwitchDashboard` AND no `minimiseLiveCall`. The second half is the damaging one —
  `switchProduct` is a plain store write and the client shell is keyed on it, so the remount
  is a raw React unmount that never dispatches `beforeRemove`. A MINIMISED call survives via
  `FloatingCallOverlay` (mounted outside the shell); a full-screen one was **destroyed with
  no End button**. Every other cross-product path already called `minimiseLiveCall` — this
  tile was the one that did not.
- **A6 — the provider drawer.** The SAME physical row (Workspaces / Channels) is rendered
  twice: the client arm draws it inside `SwitchDashboardSection`'s `extraRow`, which wires
  the confirm by hand, and the provider arm draws it through the `rows` map, which did not.
  One persona was asked, the other teleported. "Return to Dashboard" — provider-only, and
  the biggest jump of the three — had no confirm at all.

**Fix (round 2, after review).** A NEW module `src/navigation/productSwitch.ts` owns the whole
pre-flight — `minimiseLiveCall` (moved out of `SwitchDashboardSection`, where being private is
exactly why the tile could not reuse it), the unanswered-group-ring peek, and
`confirmProductSwitch`, which asks, states the ring cost, minimises, then runs the caller's own
switch. All three doors call it. `MenuRow` gained `confirm?: boolean` for the drawer rows. NO
second confirm implementation anywhere.

**The first draft only fixed two of three halves** — it wired the confirm and the minimise but
dropped the ring warning, so the same user one tap away on the same screen would still have lost
an unanswered Ops Room ring, under generic copy. An unanswered group ring is in neither registry,
so `minimiseLiveCall()` no-ops and there is nothing to restore.

**Two review findings on the tests, both real:**

- The A5 fix was **pinned by nothing.** No test mounts `VBGHomeScreen`, so reverting the tile to
  the bare `switchProduct(...)` it had at `83d73825` left every gate in the repo green. Now a
  repo-wide source scan (`productSwitchPreflight.test.ts`): every `switchProduct` caller reaches
  the pre-flight, `minimiseLiveCall` has exactly ONE definition, and the tile is named
  explicitly. Comments are stripped first — the new prose names both tokens several times.
- "ONE dialog per press" was a **verbatim copy** of the case three above it, and could not fail
  for the reason its comment gave: the describe forces `account_kind: 'agency'`, so the client
  `extraRow` path it claimed to guard never renders. Worse, the client-arm case used
  `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, which passes just as happily with two calls — nothing in the suite
  would have failed if the client started prompting twice. Repointed at the client arm, by COUNT.

Also: the harness never invoked `onYes`, so nothing asserted the switch still happens after the
dialog. There is now a case that runs the callback and one that does not.

**A jest trap worth remembering:** importing `@utils/alert` statically into the new module made
jest evaluate that suite's mock factory at MODULE LOAD — before its `const mockAlert = jest.fn()`
ran — so the factory captured `undefined` and every `Alert.alert` died with "is not a function".
The code this was extracted from required it lazily for exactly that reason. Kept lazy.

**Deliberately NOT changed:** plan §10.7 left this open and leaned the other way, arguing the
drawer's Channels/Workspaces row "resolves inside the product" so a leave prompt there would be
false. Founder decision 2026-08-13 overrides it: make both drawers consistent. Worth knowing
that of the five doors now confirming, only two are real product switches — "Return to
Dashboard" is a plain in-shell navigate with no remount and no call at risk.

**Still asymmetric:** both documented workspace EXITS confirm nothing (`DepartmentalHomeScreen`
header chevron, `DepartmentalNavigator` messenger-tab exit). The user is asked going in and
asked nothing coming out.

**Also found, not fixed:** `ProductGateScreen` calls `setActiveProduct` bare. Unreachable today
(`requestGate` has had no production caller since item 18) but it becomes a live A5 the day one
returns, and nothing pins that.

**Regression tests.** `drawerItem18` (+5) and `productSwitchPreflight` (5).
**Mutation-proven:** reverting the drawer map's onPress to `row.go` = 2 RED; reverting the VBG
tile to a bare `switchProduct` = 1 RED.

**Gates:** app 1916 ✓, tsc 42 ≤ 47.
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** VBG Home → Secure Services during a live full-screen call — confirm the
call minimises to the floating overlay with a working End button instead of vanishing.

## B-440 — Delete had no door on the manage flow, and refused the workspace owner (vs2 edge A4)

**Source:** review finding A4. **Founder decision 2026-08-13: owner-OR-creator, WORKSPACE TENANT
ONLY** (the agency arm keeps `created_by`; it predates this and has its own consumers).

**Two faults, one ask.** `ChannelEditor` navigated `ChannelMembers` with NO delete flag, and the
button renders only behind one — so even the workspace owner never saw Delete on the admin path.
Separately the server restricted delete to `created_by`, so the owner could not delete a
delegated-manager-created channel and got a raw `only_creator_can_delete` alert.

**Fix.** `DepartmentService.canDeleteChannel(row, userId, workspaceTenant)` — static and pure,
the same shape as `mintRefusalFor`. `deleteChannel` enforces it; `listOrgChannels` echoes a
per-row `deletable`. The route param `ChannelMembers.isOwner` became `canDelete`: the old name
was a client GUESS about identity, and the manage path never passed it at all.

**⚠️ `userId === ch.org_id` really is "I am the workspace owner"** — verified, not assumed.
`org_workspaces.owner_user_id` is the PRIMARY KEY, so ownership IS the identity: one per user,
not transferable, no divergence representable. `deleteChannel` never reads the guard's org
context (it takes `claims.sub`), so the multi-org `X-Org-Context` header cannot move the answer.

**Review round 2 — five real defects in the first draft:**

- **`deletable` was a SECOND COPY of the rule, keyed on the CALLER's org while the enforcer keyed
  the ROW's** — and two comments claimed they were single-sourced. They already disagreed on a
  fixture this spec file contains: a foreign-`org_id` row rendered a Delete the server 403s.
  Unreachable only because the query filters `org_id` — which is verbatim the "equivalent today
  is how two readers start to drift" argument the mint predicate 400 lines up already makes.
  Now one static predicate, fed the ROW.
- **The flag mirrored only 1 of 3 refusals, so the new door rendered buttons that always 409.**
  A node with children (the self-FK RESTRICTs, and it counts ARCHIVED children the tree hides —
  so the admin taps Delete on an apparent leaf and is told it "still has channels inside it"
  that are nowhere on screen), and an AGENCY `#broadcast` (trigger-refused, and the mapped copy
  advised archiving, which that tenant ALSO refuses — dead-end advice on a dead-end button).
  Both folded in via a `has_children` EXISTS and a tenant-aware broadcast term.
- **The delete route had NO `OrgManagerGuard`** and never called `assertManagesChannel`, unlike
  create/configure/archive. A DEMOTED or REMOVED manager kept delete over everything they ever
  created. Guard added — A4 makes that path reachable from a real door, so the gap closes with it.
- **The confirm copy was FALSE.** "Permanently delete X? This removes it for everyone." —
  `deleteChannel` deletes the directory row and writes an audit entry, nothing else. See the
  teardown gap below. Copy now says what actually happens and that it cannot be undone.
- **Delete landed the user on a dead `ChannelEditor`** still showing the destroyed channel's Save
  and Archive, both of which fail with `channel_not_found`, a code that form does not map. Now
  pops past it when that is the door we came through.

Also: `created_by` and `has_children` are deciding inputs and are destructured OFF the wire (this
file already carries a disclosure-boundary test for that class); the `only_creator_can_delete`
copy no longer ASSERTS the rule, because during a rolling auth deploy the list can come from a
new instance while the DELETE lands on an old one — telling the owner "only the creator can
delete it" would be a confident lie about a rule that no longer exists.

**⚠️ I TOLD THE FOUNDER THE CHAT DOOR COULD OVER-OFFER DELETE. THAT WAS WRONG.**
`isOwner` on the `DepartmentChat` route is `created_by === userId`, i.e. CREATOR — exactly the
server's first arm — so that door can never over-offer. It systematically UNDER-offers: the
workspace owner opening a delegated-manager-created channel gets no Delete in the thread, walks
to Manage Channels, and finds it there. Same person, same channel, two answers, and the thread is
where they look first. It also under-offers on every push-tap entry, which omits the param
entirely. The fix is for `ChannelSummary` to carry the server verdict — NOT a second client
derivation. NOT DONE.

**Regression tests.** `channelTreeFields` (37: authority matrix both tenants, structural
refusals, row-vs-caller org keying, wire hygiene, one-query cost, enforcement parity) +
`channelEditorSimplified` (+3 door params) + `manageChannelsOrgScoped` (+4 END-TO-END SCAN).
**Mutation-proven:** dropping the tenant gate = 1 RED (after fixing mock-queue coupling that had
made attribution worthless); dropping `canDelete` from the editor door = 2 RED; dropping
`deletable` from `pick()` = 1 RED.

**Why the scan exists:** `ChannelMembersScreen` is rendered by NO test in the repo, and the chat
header navigates through `(navigation as any)` — so the rename was not typechecked at that call
site. A missed hop would have shipped green. That is exactly how A4 arrived.

**⚠️ NOT FIXED — the teardown gap (B-337/B-339 class), and A4 is what makes it reachable:**
`deleteChannel` removes the row and audits it. NO push, NO WS event, NO rekey intent, NO group
teardown. The Signal group named by `group_conversation_id` stays live on the relay and in every
member's SQLCipher store, KEY INCLUDED; `deptGroupByChannel` / `deptConversationIds` are additive
and never pruned. Members can keep posting (the send path swallows the role 404 and falls back to
the cached role), those posts fan out and raise push, and a push tap resolves through the
surviving pointer into a dead channel where every server call 404s. The cascade also silently
eats a PENDING remove+rekey intent, so a removed member keeps the group master key for a group
that is still alive. Before A4 the manage door did not exist and the server refused the owner, so
this was rarely reached. **It needs its own change.**

Also open: no org-drift refusal on this (irreversible) verb, unlike the A3 guard one screen back;
`isWorkspaceTenant` is not lapse-aware, so the API's "workspace owner" and `OrgManagerGuard`'s
now disagree for a lapsed owner (not UI-reachable — `manage/channels` 403s first).

**One-off prod probe** (app-layer exclusivity has no DB constraint; a legacy dual account would
get owner-delete over its agency): `SELECT w.owner_user_id FROM org_workspaces w JOIN agents a ON
a.user_id = w.owner_user_id AND a.type = 'company'` — expect zero rows.

**Gates:** app 1923 ✓, auth-service 2726 ✓, tsc 42 ≤ 47, auth tsc clean.
**DEPLOY:** server BEFORE client (see the rolling-deploy copy note).
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** workspace owner deletes a manager-created channel from Manage Channels →
Members; confirm the parent/broadcast rows offer no button rather than a 409.

## B-441 — a removed-then-RE-ADDED CPO is seated in the Ops Room but keyless

**Source:** `docs/qa/BRAVO_CHANNELS_VS2_CRITICAL_REVIEW_2026-08-13.md` Part 3 gap 2 (logged as a
B-416 follow-up, previously unfixed). Fixed 2026-08-13.

**Mechanism.** `enqueueRoomIntent`'s idempotency guard suppressed any same-(booking, member,
action) intent already in `('pending','done')`. That treats `done` as terminal FOR THE MEMBER,
which it is not:

1. CPO assigned → `add` → drained → `(add, done)`.
2. CPO removed → `remove` → drained → `(remove, done)`; the agency device rekeys the room and
   the CPO no longer holds the group key.
3. CPO assigned AGAIN → the stale `(add, done)` from step 1 matches → the INSERT is skipped →
   **no add-intent is ever produced.**

The member is nonetheless SEATED — `conversations` membership is written by the mission service,
not by this queue — so they are rung, they accept, and they fail the 25s in-call key resync.
Presents as "the CPO can't join the Ops Room call" with a completely green server and no error
anywhere.

**Fix.** A same-action intent now suppresses only when it is NEWER than the last OPPOSING one
(`s.created_at > COALESCE(MAX(o.created_at) WHERE o.action <> $5, '-infinity')`). Same-action
spam inside one membership episode is deduped exactly as before — which is what the guard exists
for, since an already-member `addGroupMember` throws and never acks — but a genuine
remove→re-add always enqueues.

**⚠️ VERIFICATION LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY.** This is a pure SQL-semantics fix and
`dispatch-room-intents.service.spec.ts` mocks `db.q` — **no SQL executes in the suite**. The
three new tests pin the SHAPE of the predicate (the opposing-action subquery, the `created_at >`
comparison, the `-infinity` fallback, the (booking, member) scope, and that a `failed` intent
never blocks a retry). They catch a revert or a deletion; they CANNOT catch a subtly wrong
expression. This repo has already lost five live defects to exactly this blind spot — nothing in
2,700 auth-service tests runs Postgres. Mutation-proven (reverting the predicate turns 2 RED).

**THE REAL VERIFICATION IS A LIVE SQL PROBE — owed before this is called fixed:**

```sql
-- On a booking whose crew was removed and re-assigned, expect THREE rows:
-- (add,done) → (remove,done) → (add,pending|done). Two rows means the re-add
-- was still deduped away and the CPO is seated-but-keyless.
SELECT action, state, created_at
  FROM public.dispatch_room_intents
 WHERE booking_id = '<booking>' AND member_user_id = '<cpo>'
 ORDER BY created_at;
```

**NOT FIXED — the second half of the same review gap:** the pre-mint key-request targets only
the CLIENT, not the crew. Left for its own change; it is a different lane (the request side, not
the intent queue) and wants the Ops Room device matrix that is already owed.

**Gates:** auth-service 2721 ✓ (full suite), tsc clean.
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** rides the Ops Room 3-device matrix that B-414/B-416/B-428..433 already owe
— remove a CPO from a live mission, re-assign the same CPO, then start a group call and confirm
they can JOIN, not merely ring.
