## B-442 / B-443 / B-444 — the last three vs2 edge findings (A7, A8, A9)

**Source:** review findings A7, A8, A9. Fixed 2026-08-13.

### B-442 (A7) — two organisations with the same name are indistinguishable

Hub tiles, the invite picker's stage 1 and Manage Channels' stage 1 all rendered an
organisation as its `name` and nothing else. Names carry NO uniqueness constraint — that fact
is load-bearing elsewhere (the Rev-7 security argument hinged on it) — so a person in two
organisations called "Acme" picks by coin flip. On the hub that choice decides which company's
data the whole Departmental surface then reads AND writes.

**⚠️ THE REVIEW'S PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and following it would have looked finished.** It said
to compute this "in the shared grouping helper so all three surfaces get it at once". They do
not share one: the hub reads `user.workspaces` from the auth store, the other two go through
`topLevelOf`. A helper in `organisationTree` would have covered two of three. So
`orgDisambiguation.ts` holds the DECISION (which names collide, and the id handle) and each
surface renders it in its own idiom — the hub already has a role line, Manage Channels already
has a channel count, the invite picker has neither.

Rendered ONLY on a collision: appending an id to every row is noise on the overwhelmingly
common single-org case, and noise is how people stop reading a line that matters.

**Found by the render test I wrote for it:** the ACCESSIBILITY LABEL was ambiguous too
(`findByLabelText` threw "Found multiple elements"). Fixing only the visible subtitle would have
left a screen-reader user hearing "Open organisation Acme" twice — the same bug, on the one
affordance that cannot see the subtitle. Both labels now carry the handle.

**Tests.** `orgDisambiguation.test.ts` (13: collision detection incl. case/whitespace/blank
folding, id-tail stability, the render string) + RENDER coverage at two of the three surfaces
(`manageChannelsOrgScoped`, `inviteTeamPicker`) — because the rule can be perfect and wired
nowhere, which no pure-rule test can see.

### B-443 (A8) — the Manager role radio never pre-greyed for a branch-scoped minter

The team rows greyed correctly via `mintable_by_me`, but ROLE offered "Manager" to a
branch-scoped manager and refused only at submit (`scoped_manager_cannot_grant_admin`). Honest,
but after the admin had filled in the whole form.

It needed its OWN signal: `mintable_by_me` is per-ROW and this refusal is per-MINTER — the
plan's G10 record states outright that it deliberately cannot express this. `listOrgChannels`
now echoes `can_grant_manager`, mirroring `enterprise-join.service`'s rule
(`managerDepartment != null && role === 'manager'`) at the one endpoint that already knows the
caller's branch scope. Absent (old server) → offered, i.e. today's behaviour; the submit-time
refusal is still the real boundary.

**⚠️ A MUTATION THAT DID NOT BITE, AND WHY.** Removing the `disabled` prop left the suite green:
RNTL's `fireEvent.press` already skips a node whose `accessibilityState.disabled` is true, so
the press assertion alone was pinning the a11y state — while on a device it is the PROP that
blocks the touch. The test now asserts both explicitly.

### B-444 (A9) — a dept-channel push leaves the directory belt-filtered to the wrong org

A dept-message tap opens the thread by `channelId` (that half works), and Back lands in a
directory `scopeChannelsToActiveWorkspace`-filtered to the STICKY org — one that does not
contain the thread just read, so the channel the user is standing in appears not to exist.

**The review claimed A1/A2's tap-time targeting would "resolve this seam for free". It does
not, and I verified why:** the dept-message wake carries `{kind, conversationId, senderUserId}`
and nothing else, because messenger-service holds no org membership data at all.

So the org has to come from the client's own knowledge. `armDeptConversationRegistry` already
fetches `listChannels()` **UNSCOPED** (it must, or workspace B's company files become vaultable)
— which makes it the only place the client ever learns which workspace a dept conversation
belongs to. A new persisted `deptOrgByConversation` map carries it; `resolveDeptConversation`
returns it; `navigateToThread` adopts it before routing.

Read from the ADDITIVE map, not derived from the pointer: `deptGroupByChannel` is overwritten on
a B-206 remap, so the org would vanish exactly when the pointer did.

**The ORDER is not optional.** Adopting a different org remounts `DepartmentalNavigator` (the
B-95 held frame), which would tear down a thread already navigated to — so the adoption settles
first. It no-ops instantly when the org is unknown or already active, which is every
single-workspace user.

**⚠️ THREE SOURCE SCANS BROKE ON THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, not its behaviour.** Hoisting the routing
body into a sibling function made two scans read the wrapper instead of the door; putting the
adoption block above it pushed the `channelId:` assignment out of a third's bounded window. The
body now stays inside `navigateToThread` and stays first, with a comment saying why. Worth
knowing: a scan anchored on a function NAME is a constraint on how you may refactor it.

**Gates:** app 1947 ✓, crypto 4329 ✓ (⚠️ two MOVING single-suite failures across runs —
`backupFlags` then `groupCallVideoEncodings`, each green in isolation and on the next full run;
the known B-126/B-153 stale-transform-cache flake), auth-service 2729 ✓ (⚠️ two flakes there too,
incl. a 177s `password.service` timeout under parallel load — both green in isolation and on
re-run), tsc 42 ≤ 47, lint 0 errors.

**DEPLOY:** server before client for A8 (`can_grant_manager`); A7 and A9 are client-only.
**DEVICE PASS OWED:** two same-named workspaces on the hub; a branch-scoped manager opening
Invite; and a cross-workspace channel push — tap it, press Back, confirm the directory contains
the thread you just read.

### B-442/443/444 — review round 2 (both agents), 2026-08-13

**⚠️ A9 DID NOT WORK AS FIRST WRITTEN. Both reviewers found it independently.**

`deptOrgByConversation` was written to `partialize` and snapshotted into `vaultByOwner`, and
**restored in neither `onRehydrateStorage` nor `setOwner`**. So the live map was `{}` at every
boot — and worse, the next store mutation flushed that empty map back over the persisted one,
destroying it before the boot-time registry arm could refill it.

The cold-boot fallback added to `mutedLookup` could not rescue it either: `resolveDeptRouteForTap`
asks the LIVE store first and returns the moment it is non-null, which it always is because
`deptConversationIds` IS restored. **On the killed-app tap — the case A9 was written for — the
fix was a no-op on disk data that held the right answer.** Both restore sites added.

The `setOwner` half is the same bug documented in a comment 14 lines above it, for the map right
beside it. The new field reproduced it directly under its own warning.

**⚠️ AND A9 VIOLATED A RULE I WROTE MYSELF, in `adoptOrgContext`'s own header:** _"do NOT extend
adoption to any door that does not put the user inside that org's surface."_ Only the AGENCY
shell routes `DepartmentChat` through `Departmental → Channels`; the client and CPO shells reach
`MessengerNavigator`'s copy, where Back lands on `MessengerHome` — which
`scopeChannelsToActiveWorkspace` explicitly excludes from scoping. So on those shells there was
no symptom to fix, and adopting repointed a sticky global that decides where **clock-in, incident
submit and invite mint land** — none of which has a drift guard — with nothing on screen naming
the new org. The client shell is where a plain workspace employee lives, i.e. the exact A9
persona. Adoption is now gated by `deptThreadEntersWorkspaceSurface()`, which lives beside the
routing table it mirrors so the shell rule cannot drift into a second copy.

**Also fixed this round:**

- A8 greyed the Manager row but did not DESELECT it. The row is live until the list lands, so a
  fast admin selects Manager, the row then greys, `role` stays `'manager'`, and Create still
  sends it — the late 403 A8 exists to remove, now under a control the UI says is unavailable.
- The two other `rememberDeptConversation` feeders passed no org, leaving one fire-and-forget
  boot-time network call as the only populator — which is what made the restore bug bite.
- `shortOrgRef`'s docstring promised a "stable handle … compared against a URL or support
  ticket". It is not: the hub feeds it a WORKSPACE org id while the other two feed a level-0
  `department_channels` row id, so one company reads differently on different surfaces, and the
  collision DOMAINS differ too (one workspace can hold several root channels). Docstring
  corrected to say what it is — a within-one-list disambiguator, not a name for a company.

**KNOWN-OPEN, logged not fixed** (each verified real, none blocking):

1. **The hub's other tile sources** — the agency fallback row and the legacy own/member cards are
   outside the collision scan, so an agency and a workspace sharing a name are not detected
   (they still differ by subtitle).
2. **The deferred navigate races B-324's re-route guard**, in both directions, and bypasses
   `stillOnTapTarget`: nothing re-checks where the user is before the deferred `go()` fires.
   Narrow (needs `convGuess` + a locally-resolvable conversation + a dept verdict with an org)
   and now agency-shell-only after the gate above, but real.
3. **A message tap remounts a warm `DepartmentalNavigator`**, discarding a half-filled Report
   Incident form or an open editor. Previously only a deliberate hub-tile tap could do that.
4. **`openConversation.ts` — the in-app row-tap door — ignores `orgId`.** Same
   wrong-directory-behind-the-thread symptom, reachable from the list instead of a push.
5. **Three A9 lines still have no red-on-revert coverage** (`mutedLookup`'s persisted reader,
   `partialize`, the vault snapshot), and **no test renders `WorkspaceHubScreen` at all** — so
   reverting the hub's disambiguator leaves the suite green on the surface A7's own docstring
   calls the most consequential. The A9 tests hand-build their maps in the very file whose header
   exists to forbid that; a real store→persist→rehydrate round-trip is what they need.
6. `setDeptChannelGroup` records a B-206 remap in `deptConversationIds` but not in the org map
   (degrades to null = prior behaviour).

**Gates after round 2:** app 1947 ✓, crypto 4329 ✓, tsc 42 ≤ 47, lint 0 errors.

### B-445 — `room-token.service.spec.ts` HMAC-tamper test flaked ~6.25% (tampered an IGNORED base64url bit) · FIXED 2026-08-14 (test-only)

Found during the audit-#4 review cycle (critic agent, verified by coordinator): the
"tampered signature fails verify" spec flipped the LAST char of the base64url
signature between 'A'↔'B'. A 256-bit HMAC renders as 43 base64url chars = 258 bit
slots, so the last char carries 4 significant + 2 ignored bits — and 'A'(000000) vs
'B'(000001) differ only in an ignored bit. Whenever a random signature ended in 'A'
(P = 1/16), the "tampered" token decoded to IDENTICAL bytes, `verify` correctly
returned ok, and the test failed. Measured 1253/20000 = 6.26%. This was one of the
named suites in the "moving failure" full-suite flakes (alongside the stale-transform
-cache mechanism). Fix: flip a MIDDLE character (always 6 significant bits). File:
`apps/messenger-service/src/sfu/room-token.service.spec.ts`. Production code
untouched — the verifier itself was always correct.

### B-446 --- a SECOND device's stale identity-refresh can rotation-wipe the fresh mirror (found by B-6 review, 2026-08-15) . OPEN (server-side, pre-existing)

**Found by:** the B-6 critic review (F9), reading `identityBackup.ts:454` against the
rotation comparison in `backup.service.putIdentity`.

**Shape:** the server's rotation test is BYTE-DIFFERENCE on `wrapped_master_key` with
no notion of key generation or freshness. Device A rotates (new password) --- server
wipes + installs key K2. Device B still holds `liveWrappedMasterKeyB64 = K1` in module
state and later fires `refreshIdentityBackup()` (the OPK-refill re-upload lane, which
re-sends the wrapped key verbatim). The server sees K1 != K2 --- classifies it a
ROTATION --- wipes device A's fresh mirror + snapshot + merkle commit and reverts the
identity row to K1. B-6's atomicity makes that wipe reliably COMPLETE where partial
failure previously left debris (narrower, but still wrong).

**Bounds:** requires the same account live on two devices (Phase-1 is
single-device-by-design, signalDeviceId=1) AND a rotation on one while the other holds
the old key in memory. Low likelihood today; will become live the moment multi-device
ships.

**Fix shape (not implemented):** a monotonic key-generation counter (or
`updated_at`-based precondition) on `identity_backups` that `refreshIdentityBackup`
must present --- a stale refresh then 409s instead of rotating. Belongs with the
multi-device work.

### B-447 --- OLD sent messages show a single tick after upgrading to v1.0.236 . KNOWN one-time cosmetic (v20 migration residual), reported 2026-08-15

**Report:** founder, on 1.0.236 (vc 274): older outgoing messages in a 1:1 (screenshot:
the Piyal chat, msgs from the previous evening) show a single tick where they showed
double before the upgrade. The peer had REPLIED to those messages, so real-world
delivery is not in question --- this is display state.

**Mechanism (matches the audit #14 stamped residual verbatim):** v1.0.236 runs the
one-time v20 dedup before installing the unique envelope index. Messages from the
B-124 era could exist as DUPLICATE rows (the same envelope filed under both the
`direct:` slot and the server-uuid conversation). Delivery receipts only ever updated
ONE of those copies to `delivered`; the other stayed `sent`. The cross-conversation
sweep keeps MAX(rowid) --- the newest FILING --- which for some pairs is the copy that
never received its receipt. The kept row's scalar `status` is what the bubble tick
renders, so those messages regressed to a single tick. The reviewers flagged exactly
this shape at review time: "MAX(rowid) is a filing-order heuristic for the live slot
--- a dead alias filed LAST still wins" (audit #14 stamp, residuals).

**Scope:** ONE-TIME and cosmetic. Only pre-1.0.236 messages that had duplicate rows;
new messages tick normally (the unique index prevents the duplicate class that caused
this). Delivery/read pipelines untouched (envelopeLegParity + messageTicks suites
green in the release gates).

**Not healable from data:** the deleted copy's `delivered` state came from transient
WS receipt frames; the relay deletes acked envelopes, so there is nothing to re-fetch.
Faking `delivered` for old rows (e.g. inferring from later peer activity) would
launder display state we cannot prove --- rejected.

**Action:** none planned beyond this record + telling affected users the old ticks are
display-only. If founder wants, a release-notes line for qa: "some pre-update messages
may show a single tick; delivery was unaffected."

### B-448 --- Workspace Hub had NO standing "join with a code" entry ⚠️ P2 UX dead-end · FIXED 2026-08-15

**Report:** founder, 2026-08-15: the workspace list page shows the workspaces you own or
joined, but offers no way to ENTER an invite/referral code to join one.

**Mechanism:** `JoinWorkspaceScreen` (the full code-entry flow: resolve, invite
auto-join vs approval request, B-413 refusal copy) exists and is registered in BOTH
navigators --- but `WorkspaceHubScreen` only surfaced it from the `code:null` fork of an
email-invite row (`invites.map`). No invite row on the server ⇒ no door. The only other
paths were EnterpriseSetup's "join instead" link (reachable only via the empty-state
"Create a workspace" CTA) and the DepartmentChannels directory CTA --- nothing on the
hub itself, which is exactly where a person holding an out-of-band referral code lands.

**Fix (same session):** a standing "JOIN A WORKSPACE" card on the hub (after
tiles/invites/empty state), `navigate('JoinWorkspace')`. Safe as a bare navigate: the
hub is registered ONLY in MessengerNavigator, which also hosts `JoinWorkspace` (the
multi-shell bare-navigate ban does not apply --- same stack, same shape as the existing
invite-fork navigate). Rendered unconditionally: eligibility stays server-decided and
JoinWorkspaceScreen already carries the honest B-413 owner / active-elsewhere refusals,
so no dangling per-row CTA is created.

**Pinned:** `joinApprovalFlow.test.ts` F-WSHUB "B-448 --- the hub carries a STANDING
door to code entry" --- mutation-proven RED by deleting the card (only that test failed),
restored GREEN 30/30. Gates: the 7 join/workspace suites 163 green; tsc 45 ≤ baseline 47.

### B-449 --- echo returned in v1.0.236: the call-audio fix was never merged to main · FIXED 2026-08-15 (merged, ships in v1.0.237)

**Report:** founder, 2026-08-15: echo is back on calls after updating to v1.0.236.

**Mechanism:** not a code regression --- a release-branch gap. Commit `a7768d1a`
"fix(calls): audio --- echo, Bluetooth routing, single mic, volume floor" (the AEC3
replaces-vendor-DSP incall-manager patch, `BravoCallVolumeModule.kt`,
`callVolumeFloor.ts`, single-mic capture) existed ONLY on `fix/calling-b419-b427`.
v1.0.233 was built FROM that branch and had it; v1.0.236 was built from `main`,
which never received it --- so 236 shipped the OLD audio path, unfixed. Proven against
the binary: `BravoCallVolumeModule` appears zero times across all 8 dex files of the
236 APK while control strings (MainApplication, InCallManager, bravosecure) hit
normally.

**Fix:** merged into main as `71f02784` --- via the branch's own last main-merge
(`33954706`), which already carried the conflict resolutions against the
B-428..B-433 / B-391c call fixes; verified the merge adds exactly `a7768d1a`'s
surface, preserves the audit-campaign symbols in CallScreen/GroupCallScreen, and
that the only removals are the expo-av second-recording visualizer (that removal IS
the single-mic fix). `react-native-incall-manager@4.2.1` patch re-applied clean.
Gates: messenger-crypto 441 suites / 4497 tests green twice; app messenger screen
tests green; tsc ≤ 47 baseline.

**Lesson:** a branch-built release (233) can silently carry fixes main never got;
the next main-built release re-exposes the bug and reads as a fresh regression.
Before any release build, diff the previous shipped build's branch against the
build branch for functional commits.

## 2026-08-15 — App-wide back-button audit (founder request: "check every page")

**Method:** 4 parallel static auditors over EVERY non-test screen (~220 files:
messenger, deptchat, activity, news, ops, liveops, agent, cpo, auth, booking,
executive, securepro, pro, settings, wallet, vbg, dashboard + page-like modals) plus
the navigators, `tapGuard.ts`, `departmentalEntry.ts`, and the notification-tap
routing in `fcmBootstrap.ts`. Items marked ✓ were independently re-verified against
source by the coordinating session; the rest are auditor-cited (file:line) and still
need a second pair of eyes before fix work. **No fixes shipped — findings only.**
Items use audit numbers BB-n; claim B-numbers at fix time (contract: RED test first).

**The dominant mechanism (accounts for BB-1..BB-4):** a screen navigated into a lazy
nested stack WITHOUT `initial: false` (or deliberately cold-seeded, B-319) becomes the
stack's ONLY route; every bare `navigation.goBack()` there is a silent no-op —
`goBackOnce` (`tapGuard.ts:85`) has NO `canGoBack()` fallback, so it amplifies rather
than heals this. `nestedNavigationInitialFlag.test.ts:131-147` already allowlists
several of these sites as known-unfixed.

### BROKEN (visible control does nothing / user stuck)

- **BB-1 ✓ IncomingGroupCallScreen — Decline leaves the user ON the ring screen and
  hardware back is swallowed, on the PRIMARY path.** `decline()` ends in bare
  `goBack()` (`IncomingGroupCallScreen.tsx:291`); hardware back = `decline(); return
true` unconditionally (`:299-308`). A cold ring is BY DESIGN the stack's only route
  (B-319 comments, `MainNavigator.tsx:800-801`/`:978-979`; flagless navigations at
  `MainNavigator.tsx:931/:980`, `fcmBootstrap.ts:866/:1914`). The decline frame IS
  emitted, so the caller stops ringing — but this user's screen never leaves. The two
  sibling call screens got the B-319 `canGoBack()` fallback (`CallScreen.tsx:473-481`,
  `GroupCallScreen.tsx:1595-1602`); this one did not.
  Ring timeout/host-cancel/roomMissing branches (`:121,:149,:204,:214,:223,:256`) are
  bare-goBack dead on the same path. P1.
- **BB-2 ✓ CallScreen / GroupCallScreen — Minimise and hardware back dead on a
  cold-answered call.** `CallScreen.tsx:2040` `minimise = () => navigation.goBack()`
  (bare, 1500 lines below the file's own B-319 guard); hardware-back terminal branches
  `:518/:523` bare-goBack-then-`return true`. GroupCallScreen: minimize chip
  `:1443-1446`, hardware `:1514-1515`, and the full/kicked/failed/unavailable blocker's
  Close `:1784` (those states are NOT in `isTerminalPopState`, so the `:1582-1606`
  fallback never fires). P1.
- **BB-3 ✓ Notification-tap booking/pro targets mounted flagless → no way out on a
  cold start.** `fcmBootstrap.ts:1491-1493/:1513-1514` dispatches
  `{name:'SecureTab', params:{screen,…}}` with NO `initial:false` for every

  exit is `popToTop()` (`MissionCompleteScreen.tsx:79`), no back affordance,

- **BB-4 ✓ Agent/CPO onboarding chain.** AgentTypeSelect: bare-goBack chevron

### RISK

### COSMETIC / dead code

## 2026-08-15 — founder bug batch 2 + vault end-to-end audit — **B-450..B-459 CLAIMED**

Process (founder-specified): audit by the coordinating session, code by Opus 5
agents, then an Opus 5 critic↔fixer loop to consensus + an edge-case agent.
Five audit agents ran (reply, albums, vault gate, calls, vault end-to-end); every
root cause below was line-verified by the coordinator before any fixer started.

### The founder's five reports → root causes

- **B-450 — cannot reply to picture/voice/video — founder broadened mid-fix to
  ANY message kind incl. documents and links (1:1 AND group).** No predicate
  blocks it: media bubbles mount an inner TouchableOpacity (open/play) that wins
  RN's responder negotiation, so the row wrapper's `onLongPress` (the door to the
  action sheet) never fires on media; text rows have no inner touchable. The whole
  downstream reply pipeline already handles media ('📷 Photo' etc. in
  `previewForReply`, test-pinned). Adjacent found bug: `sendPickedMedia` never
  consumes an armed quote — replying WITH an attachment silently drops the quote
  onto the NEXT text message. FIXED (Opus F1 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-451 — "album move makes a copy".** Structurally impossible — the model is a
  single-valued `assignments: Record<itemId, albumId>`; move overwrites. Real
  causes: an UNGUARDED PRUNE (`FilesScreen.tsx:258-260`) deletes every assignment
  not in the CURRENT row list (fires with rows=[] on cold start before SQLCipher
  hydration; the 200/convo hydration cap prunes older files; the workspace-shell
  instance is company-scoped and prunes every PERSONAL assignment) + no row ever
  shows its album (`albumOf` has zero callers; the subtitle is the CONVERSATION
  name), so even successful moves are unverifiable. FIXED (Opus F2 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-452 — multi-select move applies to 1 of N.** Same prune (the workspace-scope
  wipe reverts all but the company-scoped items) + the handler maps
  `selectedRows` (scope-filtered view) instead of the `selected` id set and
  discards `AlbumError` returns silently. FIXED (Opus F2 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-453 — phone vault must be PIN/biometric protected.** FilesScreen renders
  with ZERO vault check in all three shells (only the cloud shelf is gated;
  viewer/share/delete export plaintext ungated). Fix = replicate VaultScreen's
  `guardLock` (focus + AppState) into FilesScreen, entitlement-free (PIN must not
  paywall), with the Departmental Vault-tab lock↔files ping-pong made shell-aware.
  PIN is 6-digit (stricter than the asked 4 — kept). FIXED (Opus F2 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-454 — no way to swap who is enlarged on 1:1 video.** No swap state exists;
  streams hard-wired (remote=full, self=PiP). Fix: `swapped` state; streamURL /
  mirror / remount-key / fallback-placeholders follow the STREAM, zOrder follows
  the CONTAINER; PiP tap becomes the swap (chrome toggle stays on the full-screen
  pressable). **FIXED (Opus F3, uncommitted)** — `swapped` + one renderer per
  STREAM (`renderRemoteTile` / `renderLocalTile`, `slot: 'full' | 'pip'`); the
  remount key carries the slot; `mirror` goes through `shouldMirrorTile`; the
  remote side still resolves through `resolveRemoteTile` in BOTH slots. One
  predicate `canSwap` (video UI + not tearing down + not ended + a live remote
  stream) gates the gesture AND resets the flag — the ringing peer-avatar overlay
  is not part of either slot and would otherwise paint over the swapped-in local
  video. Pinned by `callSelfViewSwap.test.ts` (16, 6 mutants RED).
- **B-455 — self PiP video pokes square corners past the rounded frame.** Two
  stacked causes: `pipFill` uses deliberate −2 insets (video plane 112×152 in a
  108×148 frame) AND on Android the RTCView is a SurfaceView (zOrder=1 media
  overlay) that parent `overflow:hidden` radius clipping cannot touch.
  `FloatingCallOverlay` has the same class. **FIXED (layout half) / DOCUMENTED
  (Android half) (Opus F3, uncommitted)** — the frame keeps border+radius+shadow
  and a new inner container (`pipClip`, zero insets = the border's content box,
  radius 18−2, `overflow:'hidden'`) owns the video plane, which absolute-fills it;
  the −2 bleed is gone, so nothing reaches past the frame on either platform.
  Same treatment at BOTH `FloatingCallOverlay` videoCard sites (`videoCardClip`,
  radius 16−1.5). RESIDUAL, Android only: the vendored
  `@livekit/react-native-webrtc@125.0.12` has no clip/TextureView option at all —
  `RTCVideoViewManager` exposes only mirror/objectFit/streamURL/zOrder/
  onDimensionsChange and `WebRTCView.java:145,160` hard-codes
  `new SurfaceViewRenderer(...)`, with `setZOrder` (`:521-533`) only toggling
  `setZOrderMediaOverlay`/`setZOrderOnTop` — so the surface stays an unrounded
  rectangle INSIDE the frame and its corners still fill the sliver between the
  rounded inner edge and the square content box. Closing that needs a native
  TextureView renderer. Pinned by `callTileCornerClip.test.ts` (12, 3 mutants RED).

### Vault end-to-end audit ("is the vault working?") — **NO.** New bugs:

- **B-456 — the vault PIN never works (P0, dual mechanism).** (a) `hashPin` reads
  `result.encoded` but react-native-argon2 returns `encodedHash` → `pinHash` is
  undefined: never persisted (cold start = "Set New PIN" again), and in-session
  every entry reads "Incorrect PIN" with lockouts unreachable. Masked by a Jest
  mock that returns the same WRONG shape — the whole vaultStore suite is green
  against a fiction. (b) Salt encoding doesn't round-trip (hex-as-UTF8 in, PHC
  base64 back out, re-fed as UTF-8) → verify can never match even with (a) fixed.
  No migration needed: no user can have a validly stored PIN. FIXED (Opus F4 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-457 — vault temp-cache collision shows the WRONG file** (confidentiality-
  adjacent): `writeTempBytes` idHint sanitise+`slice(0,40)` truncates the per-file
  UUID away ('vault-'+userUUID exhausts the budget) → all same-mime vault files
  share one temp path and `if (!exists)` serves the first file's bytes for every
  later one. FIXED (Opus F4 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-458 — VaultScreen renders only the first 3 images** (`images.slice(0, 3)`;
  the `viewAll` style exists but is never used). FIXED (Opus F4 + consensus round; critic SIGN-OFF).
- **B-459 — biometric opt-in is dead code**: `setBiometricEnabled` has zero
  callers → auto-prompt never fires; meanwhile VaultLock's keypad fingerprint
  button ignores the flag (defeats audit fix #36). FIXED (Opus F4 + consensus
  round; critic SIGN-OFF). Consensus round went further on the critic's ruling:
  the fingerprint key is now HIDDEN unless `biometricEnabled && bioAvailable`
  (hard opt-in — with `disableDeviceFallback:false` the key was strictly weaker
  than the vault PIN it replaced: the DEVICE lock code opened the vault), and

## 2026-08-16 — CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC Phase 1: the identity spine (B-464..B-467)

**Task:** implement Phase 1 of `docs/planning/CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC.md` — WI-1.1..WI-1.6.
Outcome table, deviations, and the `[CALLSM]` log lane are in that spec's new §13. This
entry is the bug log.

The five structural defects in §2 of that spec are not five bugs, they are one: **there
was no call identity.** `callId` alone cannot tell a minimize→restore remount from a new
call, and the registries accepted writes that named no call at all. Everything below
falls out of that.

---

### B-464 — a stale hook could mutate or TEAR DOWN a newer call (1:1 registry accepted unkeyed writes) ⚠️ P0 race · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** "The call I was on just died", "the second call ended the first one",
"the app minimised a call I never minimised". Never reproduced on demand because it needs
two calls inside one app session and a specific interleaving.

**Root cause.** `patchActiveCall(patch)`, `setMinimized(min)` and `endActiveCall(reason, source)`
took no call id. Twenty-three call sites mutated "whatever is active". Any continuation
frozen on an older call — a late ring expiry, a queued hangup ack, an ICE-failed on a
closing PC, a stats tick, a screen's `beforeRemove` firing after the user started a new
call — applied to the entry that happened to hold the slot.

**Proof it was live, not theoretical.** `useCall.test.tsx` contained a passing test named
"End does not end — hangup() during the boot window still forces the registry teardown"
which seeded the registry with callId `endboot-N`, rendered the hook with callId
`other-N`, and asserted the FOREIGN call was torn down. The suite had been encoding the
defect as the contract. Reworked into two tests: the fallback tears down the entry when it
IS this call (registry entry with a null controller — the real B-319 boot window), and it
must REFUSE when the entry is a different call.

Worth stating plainly: in its own stated target scenario that fallback was always a no-op
(the boot window has no registry entry at all). The only case in which it ever did
anything was the case where it was wrong.

**Fix.** `gen: number` on `ActiveCallState`, minted per `setActiveCall` from a module
counter, with the key RETURNED so the booting hook can keep it. Every mutator now takes a
`CallRef` — `{callId, gen}` where the caller can know the generation, a bare `callId`
where it genuinely cannot (a server frame, the FGS notification action, a screen holding
only a route param). A mismatch is dropped and reported on `[CALLSM]`, never applied.
Adoption INHERITS the generation: a restored screen is the same session continuing.

`reason`/`source` were made REQUIRED at the same time. With `ref` leading the argument
list, an un-migrated `endActiveCall('ended')` type-checks as "end the call whose id is the
literal string 'ended'" — a no-op that reads as wired. That change is what surfaced the
last four un-migrated writers.

**Files:** `runtime/callRegistry.ts`, `runtime/callDiag.ts` (new), `webrtc/useCall.ts`,
`webrtc/callDispatcher.ts`, `runtime/callForegroundService.ts`, `push/fcmBootstrap.ts`,
`screens/messenger/{CallScreen,FloatingCallOverlay,GroupCallScreen}.tsx`,
`navigation/productSwitch.ts`, `store/authStore.ts`.
**Pinned by:** `callRegistryIdentity.test.ts` (30 tests) + `iosSwipeBackParity`,
`callTileCornerClip`, `missedCallNotifAge`, `CallScreen.deadOffer` pin updates.

---

### B-465 — `endActiveCall` was RE-ENTRANT: the whole teardown ran twice; and the dominant end path never recorded `recentlyEnded` ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause (a).** `endActiveCall` called `active.controller?.hangup(reason)` while the
slot was still populated. `hangup()` drives `useCall.onState('ended')` SYNCHRONOUSLY, and
that handler calls `endActiveCall` again — so `unregister`, `stopSharedAudioSession`,
the CallKit `reportEnded`, `clearIncomingCallPayload`, `dismissCallNotif`,
`stopCallForegroundService` and the listener `notify()` each ran twice per end.

**Root cause (b).** Only `setActiveCall` recorded into `recentlyEnded`. `endActiveCall`
nulls the slot without going through it, so the DOMINANT end path recorded nothing — and
CALL-N15 (ghost-redial guard) and FIX-14 (stale-ring sweep) both read that map. A call
that ended normally left no death signal for either.

**Fix.** Null the slot BEFORE `hangup()` — that is the actual mechanism; the re-entry then
fails the key check and returns. An `endInProgress` latch is kept as the belt for a
re-entry that arrives via a `notify()` listener rather than via hangup. `markRecentlyEnded`
now runs inside `endActiveCall`. `useCall`'s terminal branch only runs its own CallKit /
cache / notifee teardown when the registry did NOT handle the end, so those are exactly
once system-wide too.

**Found while fixing, latent:** everything after `notify()` in the teardown is keyed by
the OLD callId and therefore harmless — except `stopCallForegroundService('direct')`,
which is keyed by OWNER. A listener that starts a new call during `notify()` would have
had its foreground service stopped by the previous call's teardown. Now skipped when the
slot is no longer empty.

**Pinned by:** `callRegistryIdentity.test.ts` — a re-entrant controller proves each side
effect fires once, listeners see exactly ONE null transition, `wasRecentlyEnded` flips,
and a `notify()`-listener re-entry is refused.

---

### B-466 — media-state handlers ACCUMULATED across minimize/restore (N restores → N handlers) ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** `CallSignalling.onMediaState` is additive, which is right for genuinely
independent subscribers. But `useCall`'s adopt branch bound a fresh advisory handler on
every restore and never removed the previous mount's. After N restores a single peer
camera/mic toggle ran N handlers — each writing into a dead React tree, each firing its
own registry patch, so N `notify()` storms per advisory — and the composed unregister
chain grew with it.

**Fix.** `onMediaStateOwned(owner, handler)`: registering again under the same owner drops
the previous handler, and the returned disposer is identity-guarded so an older mount's
late teardown cannot remove the handler that replaced it. Boot and adopt both register
under `useCall:<callId>`.

**Pinned by:** `callRegistryIdentity.test.ts` WI-1.4 block — N registrations leave exactly
one live handler; a stale disposer is a no-op; different owners still coexist; the
un-owned `onMediaState` stays additive.

---

### B-467 — `endActiveGroupCall` nulled the registry BEFORE awaiting `leave()`, so every busy guard saw "no call" while the transports were still closing ⚠️ P1 race · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** The `transport_id_in_use` family: end a group call, immediately start
another (or tap "return to call"), and the new `sfu.join` races transports the previous
call has not finished closing.

**Root cause.** `active = null; notify(); await leave();`. For the whole duration of the
leave, `launchCall`'s busy gate, `useGroupCall`'s boot `existing` check, the rejoin hub and
the resume guard all read an empty registry and admitted a competing boot.

**Fix.** Mark the entry `ending: true`, notify, await `leave()` under the existing 3 s
bound, THEN null and notify. `groupLeaveInFlight()` exposes the in-flight promise and
`useGroupCall`'s boot awaits it before `sfu.join`, alongside the existing
`staleLeavePromise`. The slot is only cleared if it is still OURS — a boot that legitimately
took it is left alone, along with its audio session and foreground service.

**The regression this nearly caused, and the rule that prevents the next one.** Keeping the
entry alive for 3 s changes what EVERY reader of `getActiveGroupCall()` sees.
`callAudioSession.otherStackHasLiveCall('direct')` is `getActiveGroupCall() !== null`, and
it is called from INSIDE the group teardown — so an `ending` entry would newly refuse the
1:1 audio stop for the whole window and pin the device in `MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`, i.e. a
CALL-N5 regression with no test of its own. The rule, stated once:

- **launch/join side** (would create a competing session): `ending` is **BUSY**;
- **everything else** (resume, rejoin, ring presentation, UI): `ending` is **NOT LIVE**.

Applied to `launchCall` (and excluded from its `rejoiningOwnGroup` escape hatch),
`useGroupCall`'s adopt gate, `callResumeGuard.hasLiveCall`,
`groupCallRejoinHub.groupCallIsLive`, `callAudioSession.otherStackHasLiveCall`,
`MainNavigator`'s ring dedup and 1:1 waiting banner, `fcmBootstrap`'s W4.2 system-ring
gate, and `FloatingCallOverlay`'s group bar. A source scan pins all nine.

**Shipped alongside (WI-1.5):** the group registry is now keyed by `roomId` too — exactly
one of its thirty writers checked before. The `room_not_found` re-create needed its own
`renameActiveGroupCallRoom(from, to)`: at that point `rid` has already moved to the new
room while the registry still holds the old one, so the obvious
`patchActiveGroupCall(rid, {roomId: rid})` is a SILENT no-op that strands the entry on the
reaped room — and a stranded id makes `leaveInternal` skip teardown while `launchCall`'s
busy guard then blocks calls in other conversations with "Call in progress".

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRegistryIdentity.test.ts` (29 tests), incl. a competing boot that
awaits the in-flight leave and a wedged-leave bound.

- `npx jest --selectProjects app --testPathPattern "screens/messenger"` — 42 suites / 571 green.
- `npm run typecheck` — 44 errors, under the 47 baseline (down-only ratchet holds).
- **Mutation-proven:** 15 mutations across the two registries, the signalling client, the
  audio arbitration, the resume guard and the room rename — every one turned its pin RED,
  and each mutation was verified as APPLIED on disk first (the files are CRLF, so an
  LF-anchored substitution silently matches nothing and reports a false GREEN).
- **Flake note:** four consecutive full crypto runs produced four DIFFERENT non-call
  failure sets (`callAudioSessionArbitration`, then `batteryOptimization`+`backupFlags`,
  then `attachmentUriPipeline`+`freeSpacePrecheck`), each passing in isolation, with a
  fully green run in between after `npx jest --clearCache`. That is B-126/B-153/B-304, not
  this change.
- **Device pass: NOT YET RUN.** The spec's §7 matrix (rapid call/cancel, answer-from-
  notification, minimize/restore ×20, the end-race grid, second-call, network) needs a
  release APK on the Pixels. Nothing here is device-verified.

### What the review loop changed (3 rounds, 2 independent reviewers)

Phase 1 was NOT correct when the suites first went green. Two P0s survived a green
507-suite run, and one of them was **caused** by this work. Both were found by review, and
one was proved by executing the code rather than by reading it. Recorded here because the
mechanism matters more than the fix.

**P0 — WI-1.6 silently killed the group audio-session and FGS stops on the DOMINANT path.**
`endActiveGroupCall` decided "is the slot still literally ours" after awaiting `leave()`.
But `leave()` IS `useGroupCall.leaveInternal`, whose Fix-#14 tail nulls the registry itself
and has no `await` before it — so on every end `active` was already `null`, which the code
read as "somebody superseded me" and returned early. Measured against the real shape:
`stopSharedAudioSession('group')` **0 calls**, `stopCallForegroundService('group')` **0
calls**, where HEAD ran both unconditionally. That is the CALL-N5 mirror (device pinned in
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`, "no call audio" on the next call) plus B-256 (a permanently
stranded "Bravo Secure call · Hang up" notification) re-opened together, on exactly the
path with no screen mounted to clean up after it: End on the minimized bubble.

The test was green throughout **because its `leave` mock did not null the slot.** That is
the "verify mocks against shipped native source" class from the 2026-08-15 batch, in a new
costume. The suite now has `productionShapedLeave(roomId)` — a leave that nulls the slot
exactly like `leaveInternal` — and the ownership test is `successor.gen !== entry.gen`,
i.e. "did a genuinely NEWER entry claim the slot", never "is it still literally mine".

**P0 — `endActiveCall`'s boolean return was backwards on the local-hangup path.** The slot
is dropped before `controller.hangup()`, so the synchronous `useCall.onState` re-entry
always found it empty, always read "the registry does not own this call", and always ran
its fallback CallKit/cache/notif teardown — while the registry was running the same work
up-stack. Probe output: `reportEnded` twice, `['call-re','remoteEnded']` **then**
`['call-re','declined']`. `callKitBridge.reportEnded` has no dedupe and CallKit is
first-write-wins, so **a user-initiated End was reported to CallKit/Telecom as
REMOTE_ENDED** — wrong iOS Recents glyph, wrong Android call-log row. WI-1.2's "exactly one
CallKit report / cache tombstone" was not met by the first implementation.

Fixed by replacing the boolean with `EndCallOutcome = 'ended' | 'ending' | 'refused'` and
moving the re-entrancy check ABOVE the slot lookup, so "my own teardown is in flight" is
distinguishable from "somebody else's call". The first pin for this was NOT discriminating
— it only covered a REMOTE hangup, where both branches behave identically. The pin that
matters drives a LOCAL end and asserts `reportEnded` exactly once with `'declined'`.

**Other defects the review loop closed:** the group teardown was unkeyed in the same commit
that keyed its 1:1 twin (an End tap on a stale bubble tore down the call that had taken the
slot); a `refused` group end returned `void`, turning "await the teardown, then navigate"
into "navigate now" with the call fully live; ownership comparing `roomId` as well as `gen`
would have read a `renameActiveGroupCallRoom` as a successor and wedged `ending: true`
forever with no recovery short of a restart; the 3 s leave bound leaked its timer on the
winning path (the B-304 flake shape, now that the code logs on those continuations);
`groupKeyRef` was not inherited on adopt, so the generation guard silently degraded to the
id-only test for exactly the instance most likely to overlap a same-room successor; the
adopt-mirror's null-slot branch could report a live state for a call the registry had
forgotten, stranding the screen with an End button that was a keyed no-op.

**One proposed fix was withdrawn after review.** `launchCall` briefly deferred a blocked
launch behind the in-flight leave and retried. That fixes a 3 s "Call in progress" lie by
introducing a worse class: the retry navigates seconds later with no way to cancel, and
neither the CALL-17 latch (1:1 only — the group branch returns before it) nor the group
branch dedups deferred launches, so N taps inside the window would each fire
`ringRecipients` and a navigate. It now just tells the truth ("Ending the previous call —
try again in a moment") and lets the user tap again.

**One reported defect was NOT taken, with reasons.** The adopt-mirror's foreign-slot branch
was flagged for skipping `markRecentlyEnded`. Tracing showed nothing can move the slot from
A to B without `setActiveCall` (which marks the entry it displaces) or `endActiveCall`
(which marks the one it ends), and `patchActiveCall` cannot change identity — so the mark
had always already run. `noteCallEnded` was added anyway so the branch does not depend on
an invariant living in another function, and its comment says "belt" rather than claiming
to close a gap.

### B-468 — every 1:1 the user ends from CallScreen was logged as REMOTE-ended (wrong Recents / call-log glyph) ⚠️ P2 cosmetic-but-wrong · FIXED 2026-08-16

Found by the edge-case reviewer in the Phase-1 final pass. Pre-existing (the old code had
the same ordering with `source` defaulting to `'remote'`), but Phase 1's machinery is what
makes the fix a two-line reorder, so it shipped here.

**Root cause — ordering.** `CallScreen.endCall` ran `liveCall.hangup()` FIRST:

1. the controller goes terminal, and `useCall`'s terminal handler ends the registry entry
   with a hard-coded `source: 'remote'` — it genuinely cannot know who ended the call;
2. the slot is still live at that moment, so THAT call wins the whole teardown and reports
   `reportEnded(callId, 'remoteEnded')`;
3. the screen's own `endActiveCall(callId, 'ended', 'local')` then finds an empty slot,
   returns `'refused'`, and its `'local'` never reaches the bridge.

`reportEndCallWithUUID` is first-write-wins and `callKitBridge` maps `'declined'` →
`DECLINED_ELSEWHERE`, so **the dominant End path — the button on the call screen — landed
in iOS Recents and the Android call log with the remote-ended glyph.**

**Fix.** End through the registry FIRST, keeping the controller hangup as the belt for the
boot window where there is neither a registry entry nor a controller. The registry hangs
the controller up itself, and the terminal re-entry now gets `'ending'` (B-465's outcome
union) and skips its own fallback — so `'local'` is the reason that wins.

**Why it was invisible.** The new WI-1.2 pin drives `registry.endActiveCall(..., 'local')`
directly, which is what the floating-overlay End and the FGS action do — it is correct, but
it covers the registry-first path and reads like coverage of the End button. The new pin
anchors on the STATEMENTS rather than the symbols, because the explaining comment names both
and an `indexOf` on a bare token orders the comment instead of the code (the CLAUDE.md
"prose containing the anchor" trap, hit live while writing this pin).

**Pinned by:** `CallScreen.deadOffer.test.ts` — "the End button ends through the REGISTRY
first, so the reason is `local`". Mutation-proven RED by restoring the old order.

## 2026-08-16 — CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC Phase 3: group rejoin identity + serialization (B-469..B-481)

**Task:** implement Phase 3 of `docs/planning/CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC.md` — WI-3.1..WI-3.7.
The outcome table and the deviations from the spec text are in that spec's new §14. This
entry is the bug log.

Phase 1 gave the group-call _registry_ an identity. Phase 3 gives the group-call _rejoin_
one. `rejoinRoom` closes every consumer and both transports and then rebuilds them across
four `await` points, and nothing owned that window: a second rejoin could start inside it,
and three separate background readers (the 4 s producer reconcile, the resume reconcile,
the early-producer buffer) kept consuming into it. Everything below falls out of that.

**One thing to know before reading:** the four `groupCallHook*.test.ts` suites — 87 tests
that drive the real hook — passed against every defect here. They exercise the happy path
of each mechanism in isolation; none of them overlaps two.

---

### B-469 — two rejoins could run at once, and their writes interleaved destructively ⚠️ P1 race · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** "After the wifi blipped, everyone froze", "the call said Call failed but
I could still hear them", duplicate tiles, and mediasoup throwing "consumer already exists"
after a reconnect. Not reproducible on demand — it needs a second socket event inside the
first rejoin's rebuild.

**Root cause.** `rejoinRoom` had no identity. The rejoin hub serialised _starts_ (one claim
at a time) but the claim expired at 30 s, which a real 4-peer rejoin routinely exceeds — so
a second `onReconnect` took over a rejoin that was still working, and both ran. Their
writes then interleave: the loser's `consumedProducerIdsRef.clear()` erases the winner's
record so every producer is consumed twice; its `producersRef.push` appends producers bound
to a transport it is about to close; its `sendTxRef.current = reSendTx` re-points the live
refs at a dead socket; and its terminal `setState` lands after the winner's, in either
order — `failed` over a joined call, or `joined` over a failed one.

**Fix.** A per-attempt generation (`webrtc/groupCallAttemptGen.ts`). Every write after an
await is conditional on still being the newest attempt for the room.

Two design points that are load-bearing:

- **The counter is module-level and ROOM-KEYED, not a `useRef`.** `rejoinRoom` is stashed
  in `liveSfuHandlesByRoom` and ADOPTED by the hook instance that mounts after a
  minimize→restore, so the adopted closure reads the ORIGINAL instance's refs. A restored
  instance bumping its own ref would compare against a counter nobody incremented. The
  rejoin hub had already reached this conclusion for its in-flight guard.
- **The generation is taken inside `onJoined`, not when the reconnect handler fires.**
  Taking it on entry meant a rejoin that never got as far as joining — the server refuses,
  the state is no longer joinable, the socket dies again — still superseded the boot. See
  B-476.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallAttemptGen.test.ts` (the rejection matrix + the in-flight mark) and
`groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` (the real hook: a rejoin superseded mid-rebuild abandons it;
an unsuperseded one still completes).

---

### B-470 — the rebuild window was unserialized: three readers consumed onto half-built transports ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** While `rejoinRoom` had closed the transports and not yet rebuilt them, the
4 s producer reconcile, `consumeMissingAfterRestore` and the early-producer buffer all
carried on. They consume onto a half-built `reRecvTx` and re-insert tiles the rejoin has
just cleared. `consumeMissingAfterRestore` is the worst of the three: it issues
`recv.consume` DIRECTLY rather than through the `consumeProducer` funnel, so it bypasses
every dedup guard.

**Fix.** A room-keyed in-flight mark held for the whole rebuild; all three readers stand
down while it is held. Three things had to be got right:

- The mark **expires** (`GROUP_REBUILD_MARK_CEILING_MS`, 30 s) rather than latching —
  `sfu.join` rides an ack whose reject timer is a `setTimeout`, frozen while the screen is
  locked, so a rejoin can genuinely never settle. A boolean latch would disable the tile
  backstop for the rest of the call.
- Its release is **generation-checked**. A superseded attempt's `finally` runs while the
  winner is still mid-rebuild, and an unconditional delete would re-open the readers onto
  exactly the transports the mark protects. (Phase 1's `endActiveGroupCall` shipped the
  unguarded version of this same shape.)
- The rejoin **re-consumes its own producers through the same funnel**, so the guard
  compares generations rather than a boolean. A boolean "stand down while a rejoin runs"
  makes the rejoin stand down from its own work and rebuild a room with no remote tiles in
  it — every peer black and silent, permanently, with the backstop also standing down.
  Caught by mutation testing, not by review.

A `sfu.new-producer` arriving during the window is **parked** into the early-producer
buffer and drained after the mark is released, not dropped: no fresh frame is ever re-sent
for an already-announced producer.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` (the resume reconcile stands down, and does
NOT once the mark clears; the rejoin re-consumes its own room) + `groupCallAttemptGen.test.ts`.

---

### B-471 — a stale hook instance's teardown retired the LIVE call's rejoin handler ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** A group call that silently loses WS-reopen recovery for its entire life.
Nothing looks wrong until a socket bounces, at which point the call zombies: the bubble
still advertises a live call while the user is frozen and silent for every other
participant.

**Root cause.** The rejoin hub deliberately outlives the screen (B-101 LC-4), so "clear on
teardown" was ambiguous about WHOSE teardown. `clearGroupCallRejoinHandler()` was
unconditional, and a stale instance's `leaveInternal` is fired un-awaited by `launchCall`'s
`void staleLeave()` and by `endActiveGroupCall` — both of which run while the NEXT call is
already booting.

**Fix.** Ownership tokens: `setGroupCallRejoinHandler(token, ws, fn)` records the installer,
`releaseGroupCallRejoinHandler(token)` clears only for the owner and logs a refusal
otherwise. A refused release is safe rather than a leak — the subscription re-checks
`groupCallIsLive()` on every fire, so an orphaned handler is inert and the next install
replaces it. The unconditional clear survives for logout, where there is no owner to ask.

Two related repairs in the same file:

- the stuck-claim takeover went 30 s → 90 s (`GROUP_REJOIN_CEILING_MS`), because 30 s is
  routinely exceeded by a real 4-peer rejoin and the takeover was abandoning healthy work;
- `endGroupCallRejoin` is now **claim-guarded**. It was unconditional while its sibling
  `endAttemptRunning` had already been hardened for the identical reason: after a takeover
  the abandoned rejoin still settles and still runs its `.finally`, handing the slot away
  while the winner was mid-rebuild.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinHub.test.ts` — a stale instance cannot retire the live call's
handler; a superseded claim cannot release the winner's slot.

---

### B-472 — minimize→restore lost the consume-dedup sets, so the resume reconcile re-consumed live producers ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** The restore/adopt path rehydrated `consumersByPid` from the module stash
(populated) but `inFlightConsumes` and `consumedProducerIds` were plain `useRef`s on the
fresh instance, so they started EMPTY. `consumeMissingAfterRestore` then had no record that
a producer was already consumed and re-issued `recv.consume` for it — mediasoup throws
"consumer already exists". That is the exact B-17 class the reconcile exists to repair.

**Fix.** Both sets moved into `LiveSfuHandles` (as REQUIRED fields, so a missed stash site
is a compile error) and are adopted on restore, plus a backfill that derives "consumed" from
the adopted `consumersByPid`. The two are redundant BY DESIGN and cover different gaps: only
the stash carries `inFlightConsumes` (a consume still in flight across the minimize has no
consumer to derive from), and only the backfill catches a consumer registered before its
producer reached the consumed set (`attemptConsume` writes `consumersByPid` first).

The backfill **skips closed consumers** — map membership is not proof of a live consumer,
and marking a dead one's producer as consumed would make it permanently unrecoverable.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts`. Note the pin covers the PAIR, not each half:
removing either mechanism alone leaves the other covering. The test says so in place.

---

### B-473 — a second group ring re-using the mounted ring screen wrote a missed call into the WRONG conversation ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** "A missed group call appeared in a chat nobody called me in", a ring
screen that vanishes while you are looking at it, and an Accept button that silently does
nothing.

**Root cause.** A navigator can hand `IncomingGroupCallScreen` a NEW ring by swapping
`route.params` — no remount. The screen half-knew this (it reset `settledRef` on `roomId`)
and that made things worse rather than better:

- the 45 s ring-timeout was a `[]`-deps one-shot, so its only `clearTimeout` lived in an
  unmount cleanup. Ring #1's timer survived into ring #2 and then fired holding ring #1's
  `conversationId` and `dismissRing`: a missed-call bubble into the wrong conversation,
  `settledRef` latched so ring #2's Accept was swallowed, and ring #2 popped off-screen.
  The `settledRef` reset is what let the stale timer past its own guard.
- ring #2 got no 45 s fallback of its own, so a lost `sfu.ring.cancel` rang forever.
- `cancelledRef` only ever latched TRUE and was never reset, so a cancel for ring #1
  permanently poisoned ring #2: Accept took the BS-RING-RACE branch and recorded a missed
  call instead of joining a perfectly live room.

**Fix.** `cancelledRef` resets alongside `settledRef`; the `autoAccept` and `roomMissing`
effects gained `roomId` deps (two notification-answered rings in a row keep `autoAccept`
true across the swap, so the second never auto-joined); and the 45 s fallback moved into
its own `roomId`-keyed effect.

**What did NOT change, and why it matters.** The first attempt re-keyed the WHOLE ring
effect, which also re-ran the tone lifecycle — and that loses a race: React runs the cleanup
before the re-run, `stopRingtone()` synchronously puts the tone slot into `'stopping'`, and
the new run's `bindInAppRingOwnership` calls `startRingtone()` synchronously inside bind,
which refuses because the slot is not `'idle'`. **Ring #2 vibrated in silence.** Only the
timer had to be per-ring, so the tone lifecycle was left exactly as it was. Found by the
edge-case reviewer; see B-480 for the gap that leaves.

**Pinned by:** `groupRingScreenReuse.test.ts` (source scan — the screen imports `expo-av`
tones and `useGroupCall`, so it cannot mount in the node project).

---

### B-474 — a group ring nobody presented still burned its 60 s dedup marker ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom class.** An incoming group call that simply never rings, with no missed-call
record, most often right after a backup restore or on a CPO/agency shell.

**Root cause.** B-306 moved the dedup mark behind "at least one handler exists", reasoning
that "with at least one handler the ring is always either surfaced or parked". That claim
is **false**. Downstream of the mark, `MainNavigator.onIncoming` still returns without
presenting in at least five branches — restore mode active, navigation not ready, the route
already shows this room, a silently-dropped shell navigate, a thrown registry read — and
`IncomingGroupCallScreen` registers an `onIncoming` that is a literal no-op yet still
satisfies `handlers.length > 0`. Every one of those burned the room's one chance, so the
server's reconnect replay AND the FCM rescue copy were both suppressed for the full TTL.

**Fix.** The marker now burns on the handler's VERDICT. `onIncoming` returns `boolean |
void`; `ringAlreadySeen` split into a read (`ringRecentlySeen`) and a write
(`markRingSeen`); the write runs after the handler chain and only if someone returned
`true`. `MainNavigator` returns `true` at the park site and returns its navigate result at
the navigate site; every suppressing branch stays silent. Only a literal `true` counts, so a
handler returning some other truthy value cannot burn the marker by accident.

**Scope, stated honestly in the code:** `navigateToMessengerScreen` returns false for a
missing/not-ready navigator and for a throwing `navigate()`, and true otherwise. It CANNOT
see RN6 silently dropping an unresolvable NESTED navigate — the Ops-Room shell bug — because
that does not throw. This closes the cold-boot and hard-failure lanes, not that one.

**Pinned by:** `ringDedupPresented.test.ts` — a declining handler does not burn the slot; a
declining handler alongside a presenting one still marks; a throwing handler has not
presented; plus a MainNavigator source scan for the verdict sites.

---

### B-475 — three group-call timers fired against "whatever call is live now" ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** Phase 1 keyed the registries, but three timers still read the live slot with
no room comparison, and each outlives its own room in a real flow (hang up, immediately join
another; a rejoin re-pointing the transport refs):

- the `+5 s dumpSelectedPair` re-snapshot files its ICE diagnostics against the wrong room —
  in the one lane whose job is telling those cases apart;
- `rebuildVideoConsumer`, driven by a 500 ms stats poll, TEARS DOWN a live consumer and
  re-consumes it, so firing against a successor call blanks a tile the user is watching;
- the header's duration tick read `getActiveGroupCall()?.joinedAtMs` with no comparison at
  all, so a successor call's clock was painted into the previous screen's header.

**Fix.** All three compare against the room they were armed for; `CallDurationTimer` takes a
`roomId` prop and holds its last value rather than painting another call's clock.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRoomScopedTimers.test.ts`.

---

### B-476 — [INTRODUCED AND FIXED IN THE SAME SESSION, never shipped] the boot's own attempt generation aborted the boot, and permanently disabled the reconnect budget ⚠️ P0 · CAUGHT IN REVIEW 2026-08-16

Logged because the fix is an ABSENCE — a guard that is deliberately not there — and the next
reader needs to know why, or they will helpfully add it back.

WI-3.1 as specified says to bump the attempt generation "at boot". Doing that produced two
defects, both found independently by the critical and edge-case reviewers:

**(a) The boot aborted itself after a `room_not_found` re-create.** The generation was minted
against the room known at step 1, and the B-08 re-create path (the "whoever tapped Call
second" race) re-points `rid` at a freshly minted room without re-minting it. The guard then
compared a generation from the reaped room against a room with no counter at all, read
`superseded`, and returned — skipping `setState('joined')`, the BS-LEAK handle stash and
`setActiveGroupCall`. The second caller's group call joined the SFU, produced both tracks and
consumed every peer, behind a screen stuck on "Connecting…" forever, with the whole mediasoup
pipeline leaked and no call-history bubble.

**(b) The reconnect budget could never fail a call again.** `onBudgetExpiry` was guarded by
the boot's generation, and that generation never moves — so after the FIRST rejoin of a
call's life the guard was permanently true. B-108's documented contract that this handler is
"the only terminal authority" was silently retired: a call whose ICE died later sat in
`reconnecting` forever, holding the audio session, the foreground service and `launchCall`'s
busy guard, with no way out but a force-quit.

**Fix.** The boot holds no generation at all — it protected nothing, because no `await`
separates `rejoinRoomRef.current = rejoinRoom` from the terminal `setState`, so no rejoin can
interleave there. And `onBudgetExpiry` now asks a different question: not "has a newer
attempt superseded the boot?" but "is a rebuild running RIGHT NOW?", which hands terminal
authority back the moment the rebuild finishes. It re-arms rather than returning, so the
foreground probe cannot be left re-arming a dead deadline forever.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` — "the boot's terminal setState is NOT
generation-guarded" and "the reconnect-budget expiry defers to a rebuild IN PROGRESS, and
only that". Both are mutation-proven by re-introducing the guard.

---

---

### Phase 3 review round 2 — four more defects, all in code Phase 3 made load-bearing · FIXED 2026-08-16

None of these is a Phase 3 regression; three are pre-existing and one is a gap in the round-1
fix. They are recorded here rather than as separate B-numbers because each is a guard on the
same rebuild window as B-469/B-470 and none is independently observable.

**R1 — the re-produced producers were pushed into the LIVE refs before the next stale check.**
`groupCallAttemptGen.ts`'s own header claimed this write was guarded and it was not:
`reSendTx.produce()` is a full `sfu.produce` round-trip and `attachSenderCryptor` is another
await, with the next checkpoint one await too late. A superseded attempt therefore appended a
producer bound to a transport the WINNER had already closed into the winner's live array —
where `toggleVideo`, the GC-01 self-pause re-assert (which would then emit
`sfu.producer.pause` for a producerId the server no longer has), the minimize resume path and
`leaveInternal` all read it. Fixed by collecting into local arrays and publishing under
`stale('rejoin.produced')`; a superseded attempt now closes what it built.

**R2 — `withTrackBlanked` could permanently disable the microphone.** It captured
`wasEnabled` per call, so when two overlapping rejoins blanked the SAME track the inner one
saw `enabled === false` (the outer had already blanked it), recorded "was off", and its
`finally` declined to restore. The mic or camera then stayed disabled for the rest of the
call while the UI showed it live. Now depth-counted: the ORIGINAL state is recorded once by
the outermost entrant and restored once at the outermost exit. GC-06's guarantee is unchanged.

**S5(b) — a stale consume stole the winner's in-flight marker.** `consumeProducer`'s `finally`
re-read `inFlightConsumes.current`, so a consume that started before a rebuild deleted its
producerId out of the set the rebuild had since created — switching the Fix-#12 in-flight
dedup off for that producer and letting a second concurrent `recv.consume` through. Fixed by
capturing the Set at entry, and by having `rejoinRoom` REPLACE both dedup sets rather than
clearing them in place, so an orphaned consume lands harmlessly in the old one.

**S3 — the resume reconcile guarded only on entry.** `consumeMissingAfterRestore` checked the
rebuild mark before its `sfu.producers` request, which is a full WS round-trip; a rejoin
taking the room inside that window found the reconcile adding to the dedup sets it had just
rebuilt, making the rejoin silently skip a peer. Now re-checked after the await.

**NEW-1 — the round-1 fix inverted the generation ordering.** Moving `beginAttempt` into
`onJoined` (so that an attempt which never joins cannot supersede anything — the property
that made the budget fix possible) ordered generations by ACK ARRIVAL rather than attempt
start. That is safe only while attempts are serialised, and the 90 s stuck-claim takeover
exists precisely to break that, on the explicit premise that the first attempt's ack can
arrive LATE. So after a takeover the ABANDONED attempt's late ack minted the HIGHER
generation and tore down the transports its replacement had just built — the exact
interleaving the generation exists to prevent, on the one path where two attempts are
guaranteed to overlap. Fixed by refusing in `onJoined` when the hub claim is no longer ours
(`currentGroupCallRejoinClaim()`), which keeps both properties.

**Pinned by:** the `review round 2 — wiring (source scan)` block in
`groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` and two new executable cases in `groupCallRejoinHub.test.ts`.
All ten round-2 mutations RED, no survivors.

## Phase 3 reviewer findings logged NOT FIXED (B-477..B-481)

All five were raised by the review agents, confirmed against the code, and deliberately left
alone — each needs a change outside Phase 3's scope. None is a regression from this work.

### B-477 — the adopted `rejoinRoom` writes the BOOT instance's refs ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

After a minimize→restore, `rejoinRoomRef.current = stash.rejoinRoom` hands the restored
instance a closure over the ORIGINAL instance's refs. A rejoin on that path therefore writes
`sendTxRef` / `recvTxRef` / `participantTagRef` on the unmounted instance, and nothing
re-syncs the restored one. The restored hook keeps pointing at the transports the rejoin
closed: `consumeMissingAfterRestore` issues `recv.consume` against a dead transport every
4 s, the audio-level poller binds a closed transport, `leaveInternal` closes the OLD pair so
the new transports leak, and the frozen tiles' consumerIds block the reconcile from rebuilding
them. Pre-existing (the L14 adopt), but WI-3.2 makes it more load-bearing: that reconcile is
now the only recovery for producers parked during a rebuild on that path. Fixing it means
re-syncing the restored instance from the stash after a rejoin, or moving the mediasoup
handles out of per-hook refs entirely.

### B-478 — the parked-ring consume ladder discards its own navigate result ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

`MainNavigator`'s registry-null fallback calls `consumePendingGroupRing()` — which
destructively clears the park AND cancels its expiry timer — and then discards the boolean
from `navigateToMessengerScreen`. On a shell whose nested navigate is dropped, the ring is
left not parked, not presented, and (post-B-474) dedup-marked by the park site's own
`return true`. It is lost with no missed-call record. Fixing it means reworking the ladder to
re-park or re-arm on failure. The park site's comment now records this gap in place.

### B-479 — the server's ring replay is one-shot and can be burned during restore mode ⚠️ P1 · FULLY FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

`messenger.gateway.ts` deletes the pending-ring artifacts as soon as it replays them, and the
backup-restore flow connects a socket while restore mode is still active. So a ring suppressed
by restore mode can have its ONE server-side replay consumed and discarded before the restore
finishes. B-474 keeps the client's dedup marker eligible, but it cannot resurrect an artifact
the server already deleted. Needs a server-side change (do not clear until acked).

### B-480 — NA-06 ring ownership stays bound to ring #1's roomId across a param swap ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

`bindInAppRingOwnership` lives in the `[]`-deps tone effect, so a second ring re-using the
mounted screen evaluates native-ring ownership for the wrong room. Deliberately not fixed:
re-keying that effect is what caused the silent-ring regression in B-473. It needs the tone
slot to grow a restart-safe transition first.

### B-481 — the parked-ring TTL (45 s) is shorter than the ring dedup TTL (60 s) ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

A ring parked behind a 1:1 expires at 45 s and writes its missed-call bubble while the user is
still on the call; between 45 s and 60 s the room is still dedup-marked, so on a pre-B-336
relay (no `ringId`) a host's Re-ring in that window is swallowed. Post-B-336 a new fan-out
mints a fresh `ringId` and rings normally, which is why this is P2. Either the park TTL should
meet the dedup TTL, or `expireUnconsumed` should call `clearRoomDedup`.

### B-482 — `consumedProducerIds` can be marked for a consumer built on a transport the rejoin already closed ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

Raised in review round 3 by both reviewers, who converged on the same diagnosis from opposite
directions. `attemptConsume` re-reads `recvTxRef.current` on every attempt, so a consume that
started before a rebuild usually succeeds against the NEW transport and its
`consumedProducerIds.add` belongs in the winner's set — which is why capturing that set (the
treatment `inFlightConsumes` correctly got in round 2) would be wrong and would re-introduce
the double-consume WI-3.4 exists to prevent. The narrow bad case is the other one: `recv.consume`
resolved against the OLD transport, the rebuild then closed it, and the `add` still lands — so
the peer is marked consumed with a dead consumer and is skipped forever by both
`consumeProducer` and the resume reconcile. The window is not sub-millisecond: an
`attachReceiverCryptor` and a `sfu.consumer.resume` round-trip sit between the resolve and the
add.

The discriminator is LIVENESS, not set identity. The clean fix is to have `attemptConsume`
return the consumer id rather than a bare boolean and gate the success write on
`consumersByPid.current.has(id)` — the rebuild clears that map, so a consumer built on the
closed transport is absent and the write is skipped. Deferred because it changes a return type
on the hot consume path with no device verification available this session.

### B-483 — `onTxState` stays subscribed to a superseded rejoin's transports ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-17 (see the CLOSED section at the end)

`rejoinRoom` registers `connectionstatechange` on the transports it builds with no ownership
check, so a LOSER's transport emitting `'failed'` while the winner is `'joined'` knocks the
winner into `'reconnecting'`, calls `startBudget()` and fires a spurious `restartTransport` on
the winner's transport. Weaker than the rest of the class — mediasoup's `close()` normally
emits `@close` rather than a final `connectionstatechange`, and after the round-2 R1 fix the
loser has no other levers left — but nothing in the code relies on that. The handler reads the
live refs for its ACTIONS, which is correct; it is the DECISION that is driven by the event
source.

### Note on B-477 severity

Both reviewers argued B-477 (the adopted `rejoinRoom` writing the boot instance's refs) should
be treated as P1 rather than backlog: after minimize→restore→WS-bounce the symptom is frozen
tiles plus a leaked transport pair, unrecoverable inside the call, and Phase 3's guards stop it
being made worse without fixing it. It is also coupled to B-482 and to the Set-replacement
exception recorded on `LiveSfuHandles` — the three want fixing together.

The seven findings the Phase 3 review confirmed and deferred are now fixed. Every entry above

### B-477 — the adopted `rejoinRoom` wrote the BOOT instance's refs ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

**Fix.** The stash now has a change signal. `rejoinRoom` republishes
`liveSfuHandlesByRoom` (it already did) and then calls `notifyLiveSfuHandles(rid)`; every
mounted hook for that room re-adopts. The hydration itself moved out of the restore branch
into a shared `adoptLiveHandles` callback so both callers run the same code — a second copy is
how the two paths would drift apart again.

Re-adoption is pure ref assignment and idempotent, so the instance that OWNS the rejoin
re-adopting its own values is a no-op, and the boot-only path (one instance, which already
owns its refs) is unaffected.

This also closes the Set-replacement exception recorded on `LiveSfuHandles`: the rejoin
replaces the two dedup Sets rather than clearing them in place (so an orphaned consume's
`finally` cannot delete the winner's entry), and the republish is what makes that invisible to
a restored instance. The two are a pair — the comment says so in place.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` — a restored instance re-adopts after the adopted
rejoin rebuilds (executable, through the real hook), a rejoin with no restored instance still
works, plus scans that the notify comes AFTER the republish and that both callers share the
one adopter.

**Fix.** Both consume sites now keep the resolver's verdict and give the ring BACK on refusal.
`consumePendingGroupRing()` is destructive — it clears the park and cancels its 45 s expiry —
so a refused navigate previously left the ring not parked, not presented, and already
dedup-marked by the park site's own `return true`: no ring, no replay, no missed-call record.
The registry-null fallback re-parks and re-enters its retry ladder; `CallScreen`'s primary
consume re-parks too (its old comment, "user can still be re-rung", stopped being true the day
the dedup marker began burning on a parked ring).

**Pinned by:** `ringDedupPresented.test.ts` — the DOCUMENTS pin was inverted into a
fix assertion for both sites, which is exactly what that kind of pin is for.

### B-479 — a ring suppressed by restore mode lost its one server replay ✅ CLIENT HALF FIXED 2026-08-17 (server half below)

**Fix, client-side only.** Two halves:

- `restoreMode.ts` gained `subscribeRestoreMode` — it was a bare boolean that every consumer
  POLLED at decision time, so anything the flag caused to be dropped had nothing to re-trigger
  it. Still a leaf module (a Set of callbacks, no imports).
- MainNavigator's restore branch now PARKS the ring and reports `true` instead of dropping it,
  and a new subscription re-presents it when the flag clears.

The server half is unchanged and remains the real constraint: the gateway clears the
pending-ring artifacts as soon as it replays them, and the restore flow connects a socket
while the flag is still armed. Parking is what makes that survivable — the ring gets an owner
and a 45 s expiry that writes the missed-call bubble, rather than relying on a replay that may
already have been consumed and discarded.

A restore lasting longer than the park TTL (the common case — real restores take minutes) is
covered by B-481: the expiry re-arms the room so a later copy can still ring.

**Pinned by:** `ringParkRecovery.test.ts` (the subscription contract, incl. no-op sets and a
throwing listener) + `ringDedupPresented.test.ts` (the branch parks and returns true).

### B-480 — NA-06 ring ownership stayed bound to ring #1's roomId ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

**Fix.** The blocker was never the screen — it was that `bravoTones`' slot could not survive a
stop and a start in the same tick. React runs an effect's cleanup BEFORE its re-run, and
`stopSlot` sets `'stopping'` synchronously before its first await, so the re-run's
`bindInAppRingOwnership` → `startRingtone()` hit the "not idle" guard and was dropped. That is
why WI-3.5 reverted the re-key: ring #2 vibrated in silence.

The slot now QUEUES a start that arrives mid-teardown and drains it once it reaches `'idle'`;
a stop cancels any queued restart, so sign-out (`stopAllTones`) cannot be undone by a start
queued moments earlier. With that in place the group ring screen's tone effect is re-keyed on
`[roomId, autoAccept, roomMissing]`, which closes both recorded gaps: the ownership binding
follows the room, and the `autoAccept || roomMissing` early return is re-evaluated per ring
instead of once per screen instance.

**Note:** `CallScreen`'s 1:1 ring effect is keyed `[isRinging, callId]` and therefore already
carried this race for a call-waiting second offer. The slot fix repairs that site too.

**Pinned by:** `bravoTonesAudioMode.test.ts` (against the REAL module — `inAppRingOwnership.test.ts`
substitutes a naked `jest.fn()` for the tones and is structurally incapable of seeing this) +
`groupRingScreenReuse.test.ts`, whose old pin LOCKED the one-shot and was deliberately inverted.

### B-481 — the parked-ring TTL (45 s) was shorter than the ring dedup TTL (60 s) ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

**Fix.** `expireUnconsumed` now clears the room's dedup markers via a new
`clearGroupRingDedup(roomId)` export. A park that dies unconsumed was presented to nobody, so
the room must become ring-eligible again rather than staying suppressed for the remaining
~15 s. A park that is CONSUMED deliberately does not re-arm — the user is being shown the ring,
and a replay landing straight after would give them two ring screens.

The lazy `require` keeps the runtime dependency one-directional (the dispatcher requires
`pendingGroupRing`, not the other way round).

**Pinned by:** `ringParkRecovery.test.ts` — expiry re-arms, consume does not, and only the
room that expired.

### B-482 — a producer could be marked consumed against a closed transport ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

**Fix.** `attemptConsume` returns the CONSUMER ID instead of a bare boolean, and
`consumeProducer` writes `consumedProducerIds` only when that consumer is still in
`consumersByPid`. A rebuild landing mid-consume closes the transport the consumer was built on
and clears the map, so the old unconditional write left the producer marked consumed with no
live consumer behind it — skipped forever by both dedup guards.

Capturing the set (the treatment `inFlightConsumes` correctly got) would have been wrong here:
`attemptConsume` re-reads `recvTxRef.current` on every attempt, so a stale consume that retries
after the rebuild succeeds against the NEW transport and its write belongs in the winner's set.
The discriminator is liveness, not set identity.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` wiring scan.
