### B-483 — a superseded rejoin's transports still drove the live call ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

**Fix.** `onTxState` takes the transport that emitted the event and drops the event when it is
not the live one. The handler already read the live refs for its ACTIONS; it was the DECISION
that was driven by whichever transport fired, so a dying loser reporting `'failed'` knocked a
healthy call into `'reconnecting'`, started the reconnect budget and fired a spurious
`restartIce` on the WINNER's transport. The parameter is REQUIRED, so a missed registration is
a compile error rather than a silently unguarded one; all four sites name their transport.

**Pinned by:** `groupCallRejoinRace.test.ts` wiring scan (including that all four registrations
are present and named).

### B-484 — a stop landing inside the tone load window BRICKED the slot permanently ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-17

Found while fixing B-480; unrelated to Phase 3 and long-shipping.

**Root cause.** `stopSlot`'s `'starting'` branch marks the slot `'stopping'` and returns
early, deliberately delegating teardown to the in-flight `startSlot` ("start handler will
unload the sound when it resolves"). But that handler's race guard unloaded the sound and
returned **without ever restoring `'idle'`**. The slot then sat in `'stopping'` forever: every
later start refused at its guard, every later stop refused at its own. The slots are
module-scoped singletons shared by CallScreen and IncomingGroupCallScreen, so the effect is
**no ringtone and no ringback for the rest of the process** — the user simply stops hearing
incoming calls until they force-quit.

**Trigger.** A cleanup landing inside the `setAudioModeAsync` + `Sound.createAsync` window —
two awaits of real device latency. Any ring dismissed quickly (answered from a notification,
cancelled by the caller, a re-keyed effect) can hit it.

**Fix.** The race guard restores `'idle'` and drains any queued restart. That drain is
load-bearing on its own: `stopSlot`'s `'starting'` branch returns before any await, so its own
tail drain never runs on that path — the guard is the only place a start queued in the load
window can be released.

**THREE exits, not two — the third was found by self-diffing, not by a test.** `startSlot`
returns the slot to `'idle'` from the post-load race guard, from `stopSlot`'s tail, and from
its own `catch`. The catch was missed on the first pass: a stop can land while a start is
awaiting (marking `'stopping'` and delegating teardown to it), a restart can queue behind
that, and THEN the original start can fail — leaving a queued start nothing would ever run,
and a silent ring. Every path back to a terminal state must release what the transitional
state collected. This is the generalisation of the bug, and it is the thing to check next time.

**Pinned by:** `bravoTonesAudioMode.test.ts` — a stop inside the load window leaves the slot
usable, a start queued during that window is still run, and a start queued behind a FAILING
start is still run. All mutation-proven RED.

### Round 4 — six defects found IN THE FIXES, all closed 2026-08-17

The review loop was run again against the B-477..B-484 fixes themselves. It found six
problems, one of them a P1 that re-opened a device-proven bug. Recorded here because the
pattern is now three-for-three across this campaign: **the fix is where the next defect
lives.**

**P1 — the B-479 restore-exit consume had no busy guard.** The restore branch is the FIRST
test in `onIncoming`, so a ring arriving during a restore parks under it and the 1:1 ladder
is never armed. Presenting on restore-exit without a busy test pushed the ring screen on top
of a live `CallScreen`, whose ended auto-dismiss is a delayed `goBack` that pops whatever is
on top — the ring popped ~50 ms later, already consumed, its expiry cancelled and its room
dedup-marked. That is B-306 exactly, re-opened on a new path. Both sibling consume sites
already carried the guard; the new one now does too.

**The re-park reset the ring's age.** `parkGroupRing` stamps `Date.now()`, and B-478/B-479
introduced three re-park sites. The TTL exists to bound how STALE a ring the user can be
walked into ("consuming it would walk the user into a room where nobody is ringing them"), so
resetting it defeats the one thing it measures. Added `reparkGroupRing`, which preserves the
original age and routes an already-dead ring through the expiry path instead of reviving it.

**`parkGroupRing`'s latest-wins overwrite skipped B-481's contract.** A displaced ring dies
unconsumed but left its room dedup-suppressed for the rest of the 60 s window. Now released.
The missed-call bubble is deliberately still NOT written — `pendingGroupRingExpiryBubble.test.ts`
pins supersede-is-not-expiry and that decision stands; only the dedup release was missing.
(The reviewer proposed routing the overwrite through `expireUnconsumed`, which would have
flipped that pinned behaviour silently. Split instead.)

**B-478 was incomplete in two places.** `CallScreen` tested `navigationRef.isReady()` INSIDE
the timeout, after the destructive consume had already run — so a not-ready bail lost the
ring. And both outer `catch` rationales ("the park TTL still bounds it") had become false the
moment the consume cancelled the park. Readiness now precedes the consume, and both catches
put the ring back.

**B-477 fixed the refs and not the TILES.** The restored instance ended up holding the
winner's transports and the pre-rejoin tiles, whose streams come from consumers the rebuild
closed. Nothing repaired them: the resume reconcile keys `haveTile` on producerId (unchanged
across a rejoin) and has no prune branch. Video eventually healed via the stall watchdog;
**audio never did.** The re-adopt now also refreshes tiles — from the REGISTRY, which the
rejoin patched as it re-consumed. Filtering the instance's own tiles against `consumersByPid`
(the reviewer's suggestion) would have left it with none at all, because the rejoin's
`setRemoteTiles` calls land on the instance that owns the closure.

**B-482 left a dead tile behind.** `attemptConsume` registers the tile before returning, so
correctly declining to mark the producer consumed still left a permanently blank cell beside
the live one the rebuild creates — the B-17 "extra blank tile" symptom, which neither
reconcile removes. The tile is now dropped with its consumer.

**Also closed:** `startSlot`'s `catch` — the third exit that returns the tone slot to `'idle'`
— did not drain the queue, so a start queued behind a FAILING start was silently lost. Found
by self-diffing rather than by review, and it is the same B-484 shape one branch over.

**Where the reviewers disagreed:** one argued a start queued inside a stop's await window
survives `stopAllTones` and bleeds onto the login screen; the other traced the same path and
found it safe, because `stopSlot` nulls `pendingStart` unconditionally BEFORE its state
branch. The second reading is correct — that statement ordering is load-bearing, and is now
pinned. The residual order (stop → sign-out → start queues) needs a ring effect to run after
sign-out has cleared the handlers and unmounted the screens; left unfixed and recorded here.

### B-479 SERVER HALF — the ring replay is no longer destructive ✅ FIXED 2026-08-17

The client half (park + restore-exit re-present) stopped the user losing a ring to restore
mode. This closes the underlying cause: **the server deleted a queued ring the instant it
replayed it**, so the replay had exactly ONE chance to land regardless of what the client
could do with it.

**Root cause.** `drainPendingGroupRings` emitted `sfu.ring.incoming` and pushed the roomId
onto `settled` in the same pass; the loop then deleted the payload, the missed-call marker
and the index entry. Any client that could not present the ring at that instant was left with
nothing to recover from — no ring, no replay, and (because the marker went too) no missed-call
record. The sharpest trigger is a socket coming up mid backup-restore, which the restore flow
does twice while its own suppression flag is still armed, but it is not restore-specific: a
handler gap during boot or a sign-in transition burns it just as thoroughly.

**Fix — emit, then wait for confirmation.**

- The live-ring lane no longer settles on emit. The artifacts stay queued.
- The replayed frame carries `replayed: true`. Live fan-out frames deliberately do NOT.
- New `sfu.ring.ack {roomId, roomToken?}`: the recipient confirms it has taken responsibility,
  and THAT clears the artifacts — exactly what the old post-emit delete did, only conditional
  on the client having actually taken the ring.
- An unacked ring is re-emitted on the next reconnect, bounded by the existing 45 s live-window
  check, after which it degrades to a missed-call record. It cannot queue forever.

**Why only replays are acked.** The queued artifacts include the missed-call marker, whose TTL
is days. Acking a LIVE ring would delete that marker the moment a ring was shown, costing the
user their missed-call record for a call they simply never answered. `replayed: true` is what
keeps the change scoped to the lane that was broken.

**What counts as "responsibility" on the client.** Wider than "showed a ring screen", and it
reuses the verdict WI-3.6 already computes:

- the dispatcher PRESENTED it (a handler returned true) → ack;
- the dispatcher DEDUP-SUPPRESSED it because this client already has it → ack. Suppression is
  ownership, not a decline. Without this the server would re-emit on every reconnect until the
  window closed and then land a spurious missed call for a ring the user actually saw;
- every handler declined, or there were none → NO ack, and the server tries again.

The ack sender is registered with the dispatcher by the runtime (which owns the transport)
rather than returned from `dispatchGroupRingFrame`, so the FCM rescue lane acks for free too —
a ring the push lane surfaced is just as owned as one the socket delivered. It resolves the
transport lazily from the registry: the replay arrives on a freshly-reconnected socket, and a
captured handle would ack over a dead one exactly when it matters.

**Authority.** The ack's entire blast radius is the CALLER'S OWN queued ring — every Redis key
it touches is namespaced by the authenticated `sub`, and a caller can already discard their own
queued ring by declining it. So the session is the authority. The room token is verified when
supplied but not required: the FCM lane's payload may not carry one, and rejecting there would
leave the ring queued forever rather than protect anything. Rate-limited
(`sfu.ring.ack`, 2/s burst 20) because an unmetered verb is a free Redis-write loop, and a
refused ack fails SAFE — the ring stays queued and is replayed again.

**Pinned by:**

- `messenger.gateway.calls.spec.ts` — the replay is marked, is NOT cleared on emit, is replayed
  again on the next connect, and the missed-marker lane still settles immediately; plus six
  cases on the ack handler itself (auth, rate limit, blank roomId, token verified when supplied,
  token not required, own-namespace clear).
- `messenger.gateway.missed-call-ttl.spec.ts` — the SYNC-5 pin that asserted the marker was
  deleted by the replay is inverted; it now asserts the marker SURVIVES.
- `ws-payload.guard.ts` gained the `sfu.ring.ack` spec — the AUDIT #16 completeness pin caught
  the missing entry, which is precisely what it exists for.
- `ringDedupPresented.test.ts` — the client half: acks a presented replay, acks a
  dedup-suppressed replay, does NOT ack a declined one, does NOT ack a LIVE frame, does not ack
  with no handlers, survives a throwing sender, and drops the sender on sign-out.

**11 mutations RED, 0 survivors.**

**DEPLOY NOTE.** This is a `messenger-service` change and the staging auto-deploy does not fire
(B-314 — GitHub org billing). It needs the manual tar-sync to Contabo before the client half is
meaningful on staging. The client is backward-compatible in the meantime: an old server never
sets `replayed`, so the client never acks, and the old destructive drain keeps working exactly
as before. The server is forward-compatible too: an old client never acks, so a replayed ring
simply re-emits until the 45 s window closes and then becomes a missed-call record.

## 2026-08-16 — CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC Phase 2: the 1:1 state machine (B-485..B-489)

**Task:** WI-2.1..WI-2.5. Written up on 2026-08-17 — Phase 2 shipped alongside Phases 1 and 3
and was the only part of the campaign with no bug log, which is exactly the gap this entry
closes. Outcome table and deviations are in `docs/planning/CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC.md` §16.

Phase 1 gave a call an IDENTITY. Phase 2 gave it a LEGAL SHAPE: `CallController.setState` now
refuses a transition that is not in the table, terminal states absorb everything, and every one
of the twelve call sites names itself so a refused move says who tried it. The deadlines the
machine runs on moved into one `webrtc/callDeadlines.ts` so two guards can no longer disagree
about the same number.

**The most important thing here is B-485**: writing the table down immediately exposed a
transition that was firing on the DOMINANT outgoing path, in production, on every call.

### B-485 — a healthy connected 1:1 call killed itself ~20 s in ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Symptom.** An outgoing 1:1 call connects, audio is flowing, and roughly twenty seconds later
it drops itself with "Call failed".

**Root cause.** `connected → connecting` was reachable. Nothing in the code declared it illegal
because nothing declared ANY transition legal — the machine was a set of independent
`setState` calls. Re-entering `'connecting'` re-armed the connecting watchdog
(`CONNECTING_WATCHDOG_MS`, 20 s), and that watchdog then fired against a call that had been up
and healthy the whole time and ended it.

The spec's own draft table listed the transition as valid, so this was NOT a case of restoring
a documented rule — the rule had to be derived from what the code actually did and then
corrected. `connected` now goes only to `reconnecting | ended | failed`.

**Fix.** `LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` in `callController.ts`, checked in `setState`, with terminal
absorption as a separate branch above it and a self-transition short-circuit so a repeated
`setState(same)` is not reported as illegal. A refused transition leaves the state UNCHANGED
and emits `[CALLSM] illegal <from>→<to> src=<site>` — the state must not move on a rejection,
or the watchdog block below it still runs.

**Pinned by:** `callStateMachine.test.ts` (RED-first: 9 of its 10 assertions failed before the
table existed).

---

### B-486 — an offer-replay re-assert could send `busy` to the very call being answered ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** WI-2.5(b) added a re-assert: when the relay replays a `call.offer` for a call
the user has already explicitly accepted, the client re-drives the accept rather than ignoring
the frame. But the re-assert entered `MainNavigator`'s incoming handler through the front door,
and B-107's restore-mode branch answers `busy` — so a re-assert arriving during a backup
restore busied the call the user was in the middle of answering.

Pre-Phase-2 this was unreachable: the replay died at `sig.ingest` and never reached the
handler. `clearAllCallDispatchState` runs only on sign-out, so a restore starting mid-ring
leaves the registered signalling intact and made the path newly live.

**Fix.** `if (!opts?.reassert && isRestoreModeActive())` — a re-assert is never busied. It only
fires for a call whose signalling is already registered and whose accept the user has latched.

---

### B-487 — the re-assert latch was spent BEFORE the handler navigated ⚠️ P1 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** The one-shot `reassertedCallIds` latch was added before invoking the handler, so
any early return inside the handler burned the callId permanently — and the reconnect replay,
the very recovery the re-assert exists to consume, was swallowed. The call then rang out.

**Fix.** The handler reports whether it actually navigated, and the latch is spent only on a
literal `true`. This is B-460's lesson applied at a second site: `navigateToMessengerScreen`
already returned a verdict and the call site was discarding it.

---

### B-488 — the audio-route re-apply could latch the speakerphone after the call ended ⚠️ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** CallScreen's 350 ms route re-apply is deliberately exempt from the unmount
timer sweep (it has to survive a minimize), which means it owns its own liveness check — and it
had none. A call ending inside that window re-drove `InCallManager`, setting the speakerphone
force flag with no session left to clear it: the CALL-N5 latched-speaker shape leaking into the
NEXT call.

**Fix.** The callId is captured at ARM time and re-checked against the registry when the timer
fires. Reading `callIdRef.current` at fire time would have been tautological — the trap the
sibling accept-retry had already been fixed for.

---

### B-489 — the floating overlay refused End and Restore SILENTLY ⚠️ P2 diagnosability · FIXED 2026-08-16

**Root cause.** Phase 1 made the overlay refuse to act when the bar it is rendering no longer
matches the live call (otherwise a bar still showing call A would end call B). Correct — but
the refusal returned before reaching the registry, so it bypassed the `[CALLSM]` lane entirely.
"I pressed End and nothing happened" left no trace at all.

**Fix.** Three `logCallSm('overlay.{restore,end,group-end}.refused', …)` calls at the refusal
sites, on the release-visible channel, because "End landed nowhere" is precisely the line an
engineer greps a field logcat for.

---

### DECISION (not a bug) — the 1.5 s accept retry has been dead since B-274

Recorded so nobody "fixes" it by accident. `CallScreen`'s retry-once-then-end recovery (B-62)
is UNREACHABLE: since B-274, `accept()` calls `hangup('failed')` before re-throwing, so the
controller is terminal by the time the retry arms and its `'ringing'` gate always bails.

Both reviewers agreed this is a DECISION, not a defect: restoring the retry means changing
`accept()`'s two-honest-outcomes contract, which B-274 chose on device evidence. It is left
dead deliberately, with an in-code note at the site. **Either restore the retry (and revisit
B-274's contract) or delete it and its WI-2.4 hardening — do not read the ownership work around
it as coverage of a live lane.**

## 2026-08-17 — CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC Phase 4: notification & background delivery (B-490..B-503)

**Task:** WI-4.1..WI-4.10. The central invariant: **WS + FCM + Telecom + Notifee + cold
start → ONE logical incoming call.** Phase 4's defects were all violations of that in one
direction or the other — either two surfaces for one call, or ZERO surfaces for a real one,
or a user action (Answer, decline, thread-open) that one lane recorded and another ignored.

Every fix below was RED-first (the failing test existed before the code changed) and
mutation-proven (24 mutations across three review rounds, each verified applied on disk, each RED, each restored).
New suites: `answerIntentSurvival`, `acceptTombstoneGate`, `incomingPayloadLifetime`,
`fcmHeadlessCallSeed`, `notifeeBgSingleOwner`, `groupRingCleanup`, `missedCallLifecycle`,
`fcmForeground1to1Rescue`.

---

### B-490 — a body tap on the ring notification disabled the Answer button ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.4)

**Symptom.** Tap the incoming-call notification to see who is calling → land on the ring
screen → press Answer → nothing. The call rings out.

**Root cause.** `markAccepted` (the navigate dedupe that stops the notifee Answer tap and
the Telecom Answer event from BOTH mounting CallScreen and sending two `call.answer`
frames) sat in the SHARED path of the rich notifee handler — any interaction burned it.
A body tap therefore consumed the answer dedupe, and the real Answer that followed hit
`navigate skipped (already accepted)` and returned: no navigation, no autoAccept.

**Fix.** The answer dedupe belongs to a REAL Answer. Body taps get their own
`bodyTapNavIds` dedupe (they still must not re-navigate on every press — the FSI body
press and the cold-launch `getInitialNotification` replay can describe the same tap),
and only the Answer branch touches `acceptedCallIds` + `explicitAcceptIds`. The
`autoAccept` param became `isAnswerAction || explicitAcceptIds.has(callId)` — a body
press landing AFTER the Answer event (FSI ordering) re-asserts instead of un-answering
via RN6's param replace.

---

### B-491 — a slow cold launch erased the user's Answer ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.3)

**Root cause.** Both 20 s nav-readiness waits (notifee lane and the inlined Telecom
twin) called `clearAcceptedCallId` on abandon — which deletes `explicitAcceptIds` too.
That latch is the only record that the USER PRESSED ANSWER, and MainNavigator's offer
navigation reads it to re-assert `autoAccept` after RN6 replaces params (B-102 A1). A
navigator that took >20 s to mount silently downgraded the Answer to a plain ring: the
offer replay landing seconds later re-showed the ring screen on a call the user had
already accepted.

**Fix.** New `releaseAcceptDedupe` clears ONLY the two navigate dedupes (which is all
the abandon ever needed — its own comment said so). The intent latch survives; every
TERMINAL lane (decline, cancel, call end) still clears everything via
`clearAcceptedCallId`.

---

### B-492 — Telecom's End event declined the call the user had just answered ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.8)

**Root cause.** `onEnd`'s decline branch treated "payload present + registry empty" as
"still ringing, unanswered" — but the registry is empty for the WHOLE null-controller
window of an accept in flight (notification Answer → cold nav → controller build). A
Telecom End in that window — typically the system tearing its own ring surface down as
it loses the race against the in-app answer — sent `call.hangup{declined}` to the
caller of the call being answered.

**Fix.** The decline branch consults `wasCallExplicitlyAccepted(callId)` first. While
the Answer intent holds, an End is never converted into a decline: dismiss the card and
return, leaving the payload and latches for the mid-flight accept. A genuinely
un-answered ring still declines exactly as before.

---

### B-493 — the incoming payload's TTL starved a late answer ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.8)

**Root cause.** Three misaligned lifetimes: payload TTL 60 s (private literal in
`incomingCallCache`), ring window 45 s, cold-nav wait 20 s (FOUR inline `20000`
literals). A ring answered near its 45 s deadline on a cold launch hydrates its route
(SDP / deviceId / conversationId) from the cache at t≈65 s — after the payload
evaporated. The route landed empty and the answer stalled (the B-102 A1 starvation,
manufactured by a TTL). The cache header's own claim — "an in-app-answered call keeps
its cached payload for the whole call", which `onEnd`'s branch order RELIES on — was
false for any call longer than 60 s.

**Fix.** TTLs promoted to `callDeadlines.ts` with ordering asserted:
`NAV_READY_WAIT_MS` 20 s (one constant, four sites), `INCOMING_PAYLOAD_TTL_MS` 90 s
(> ring + nav wait), `INCOMING_TOMBSTONE_TTL_MS` 120 s (> payload; kept tight for the group re-ring window — B-502). And `gc()` now
EXEMPTS the live call's entry (lazy registry probe) — the payload is aligned with the
call's lifetime, not a wall clock. The drift scanner gained both push-layer files.

---

### B-494 — the killed-app ring was a picture of a call, not a call ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.1)

**Root cause.** The headless voip-wake lane ran verify → notifee card and nothing else,
while the warm lane ran verify → gates → cache seed → tombstone check → Telecom →
card. So a killed-app ring had: no cached payload (an immediate Telecom/system Answer
found nothing to hydrate — the accept stalled), no tombstone check (a callId the user
had already declined re-rang on the caller's retry), and no Telecom report (no system
call UI, no CXCall for the Answer to land on). The headless call-cancel likewise only
dismissed the card: no tombstone (a queued Accept could resurrect the dead call) and no
`reportEnded` (the system UI kept showing a call that was over).

**Fix.** The headless lane now mirrors the warm lane's exact order — restore gate, busy
gate, cache seed with merge semantics, tombstone refusal skipping ALL presentation,
Telecom report with group kinds collapsed — and the headless cancel does the full
teardown (dismiss + `reportEnded('remoteEnded')` + tombstone + empty-callId guard).
The runtime is NOT booted: every collaborator is a leaf module. The accept latch is
deliberately not touched there — it lives in fcmBootstrap and is empty by construction
in any VM where this handler is still the registered one (loading fcmBootstrap
displaces it at module scope).

---

### B-495 — two notifee background handlers raced on an undocumented last-write-wins ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (WI-4.2)

**Root cause.** `index.js` registered the slim handler at bundle entry;
`fcmBootstrap.installNotifeeHandlers` registered the rich one post-login. notifee keeps
ONE background-handler slot, so this worked only because the rich registration
displaced the slim one — an implicit contract spread across two files that any future
registrar or boot re-ordering would silently break, deciding by accident which
behaviours exist for killed-app taps. (Evaluation order was verified before changing
anything, per the work item: slim owns the whole pre-login/headless window, rich owns
everything after.)

**Fix.** `callNotification` owns THE registration (`ensureNotifeeBgRegistration`,
exactly once). The rich handler installs itself as a DELEGATE
(`setNotifeeBgHandlerDelegate`); the registered closure routes to it when present and
serves the slim behaviour until then. iOS — which never runs the Android-gated slim
install — gets its registration through the delegate installer, preserving its old
timing exactly.

---

### B-496 — accept() answered a call the caller had already cancelled ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (WI-4.7)

**Root cause.** Every cancel lane tombstones the callId, and the dead-offer watchdog
polls that tombstone — at 1 Hz. `accept()` itself never looked. In the sub-tick window
between a cancel landing and the watchdog's next probe, an Answer went all the way
through: `markCallAccepted` burned the dedupe, `reportAnswered` answered the CXCall,
and `controller.accept()` sent `call.answer` at a peer that had hung up.

**Fix.** `accept()` consults `isIncomingCallDead(callId)` after the B-319
null-controller bail and BEFORE the CallKit bridge calls — refuse before anything burns
state, returning `false` (which CallScreen's belt-and-braces `.then` treats as
latch-release; the watchdog then makes the verdict terminal within a tick).

---

### B-497 — group answer/end/decline left every ring artifact behind ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.5)

**Root cause.** The 1:1 lifecycle cleans the notification card, the native ringtone,
the payload and (on end) the tombstone + accept latch. The group lifecycle cleaned
NONE of them: `IncomingGroupCallScreen.accept` navigated away and left the
`bravo-call-<roomId>` card + looping native ringtone running to their 45 s timeout;
its decline sent `sfu.ring.decline` and left card, payload and latch; and
`endActiveGroupCall` tore down transports and audio but left the payload
un-tombstoned and the latch set.

**Fix.** Accept dismisses the card + ringtone before `navigation.replace` (payload
deliberately kept — an answered call keeps it, and a tombstone would mark the call
being JOINED as dead). Decline dismisses + tombstones (matching the notifee decline
lane). `endActiveGroupCall` cleans all three at the single owner point — after the
three refusal branches, before the teardown gate is constructed — so a REFUSED
stale-room end touches nothing and the WI-1.6 ordered teardown is untouched
(behaviourally pinned: the `ending` flag is still published before `leave()` runs).

**Trade-off, stated:** tombstoning the roomId at end/decline blocks the FCM lane's
cache seed for the SAME roomId for 150 s. A genuine re-invite (Add member, B-334/
B-336) still rings via the WS lane — which never consults the tombstone — so the
degraded case is only a killed-app member re-invited to the same still-live room
inside 150 s of their own leave. The decline half of this window pre-existed (the
notifee decline lane has always tombstoned roomIds); the end half is new and is the
price of killing the stale-queued-wake resurrection class.

---

### B-498 — a group ring replay un-answered the call ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (WI-4.6)

**Root cause.** Group Answer taps latch `explicitAcceptIds` under the roomId (the
gateway reuses it as the callId), but none of the three IncomingGroupCallScreen
navigate sites in MainNavigator read it — unlike the 1:1 offer path, which B-102 A1
taught to re-assert. A WS ring frame landing after the notification Answer replaced
the params WITHOUT `autoAccept`, and the ring screen sat there un-joined after the
user had answered.

**Fix.** All three sites (primary ring handler, busy-1:1 consume ladder, restore-exit
re-present) spread `...(groupRingExplicitlyAccepted(roomId) ? {autoAccept: true} : {})`
— the exact 1:1 mirror, lazily required. **Load-bearing dependency on B-497:** the
latch is now CLEARED at group end/decline, so a stale latch can never auto-join a
FUTURE re-ring of the same room (the B-110 ghost answer, groupified). The two fixes
ship together or not at all.

---

### B-499 — the missed-call banner was born five ways and died one way ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (WI-4.9)

**Root cause.** Five producers post `bravo-missed-<callId>`; the only consumer was its
own tap. Opening the caller's thread, calling them back, or them calling again all left
"Missed call from X" sitting in the shade — stale the moment the user acted by any
other door, and immortal otherwise.

**Fix.** New `dismissMissedCallNotifs({fromUserId?, conversationId?})` — matches only
`bravo-missed-*` ids by the data block (the banner id is keyed by callId, which none of
these lanes know), never touches a ring card, and no-criteria is a no-op. Wired at:
ChatScreen's dismiss-on-read (thread opened), launchCall's 1:1 dial site (called back),
and `showIncomingCallNotif` (the caller rings again — the funnel every ring lane passes
through). `showMissedCallNotif` now carries `conversationId` where the producer knows
it. And `sweepStaleCallNotifications` ages out missed banners older than
`MISSED_NOTIF_MAX_AGE_MS` (24 h) on boot/foreground — a banner with an unreadable
posted-date is left alone (fail open; the notifee-stringified-date audit lesson).

---

### B-500 — a foreground 1:1 call could ring nobody ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-4.10)

**Root cause.** AC-3 gave GROUP wakes a foreground rescue after the 2026-07-27 device
run disproved "the live WS lane always presents the ring". The 1:1 branch of
`onMessage` kept exactly that assumption ("the WS call.offer frame drives that UI").
With the socket mid-reconnect or the offer frame lost, a caller rang a user who was
LOOKING AT THE APP and saw nothing.

**Fix.** The 1:1 mirror of the group rescue, gates first and in the background lane's
order: HMAC verify (ring admission stays signed — the unverified group re-dispatch gap
is pre-existing and NOT copied) → restore gate → registry gates (same-id skip; busy on
a different call suppresses — the in-call banner owns busy per W4.2) → CallScreen route
skip (the WS lane demonstrably presented) → cache seed with merge → tombstone refusal →
Telecom report + notifee card. Dedup is preserved: both surfaces key by callId, and the
SDP-carrying WS offer merges over the seed whenever it arrives.

---

### B-501 — an unbounded Answer latch + reused group roomIds = a zero-touch auto-join ⚠️ P0 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED (round 1)

**Found by the critical reviewer before anything shipped.** WI-4.6 turned
`explicitAcceptIds` into a NAVIGATION INPUT keyed by roomId — and group roomIds are
REUSED across re-rings while the room has participants. The latch was a bare `Set`
with no TTL, WI-4.3 deliberately stopped clearing it on nav-abandon, and NO group
ring-screen exit (decline, host cancel, roomMissing, 45 s timeout, the
no-FrameCryptor bail) cleared it either. One failed group Answer therefore left the
latch set for the life of the process, and the NEXT legitimate ring of that room
auto-joined the user — a live mic with zero interaction.

**Fix, three layers (rounds 1+2):** the latch is a timestamped `Map` scrubbed at 5
minutes on read; `IncomingGroupCallScreen.dismissRing` — the funnel every
non-accept exit passes — clears it (`notifyCallEnded(roomId)`); and the GROUP
navigate re-assert reads it through `wasCallExplicitlyAcceptedWithin(roomId,
RING_TIMEOUT_MS)` — bounded to ONE ring window, because the re-assert only has to
outlive the seconds between a landed navigation and its chasing WS frame (round 2
traced the nav-abandon survivor auto-joining the room's next ring at t+60 s under
the 5-minute bound alone). The successful accept path deliberately does NOT pass
the funnel: an answered ring keeps its latch for the offer-replay re-assert.
Pinned by `answerIntentSurvival` (TTL) + `groupRingCleanup` (funnel scan + the
window scan); all mutation-proven.

### B-502 — the group END tombstone made a re-invited member silently unreachable ⚠️ P1 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED (round 1)

**Found independently by BOTH reviewers** — the exact B-337 class ("enumerate the
consumers of state you delete"): WI-4.5's first draft tombstoned the roomId at
`endActiveGroupCall`. The FCM lanes refuse to present a tombstoned id, and the FCM
lane is the ONLY producer of a group ring card — so a member who left a live group
call and was re-Added within the tombstone TTL got no card, no ringtone, no
Telecom, and no missed-call record on a backgrounded/killed device.

**Fix, two rounds:** END uses a new `dropIncomingCallPayload` (delete, no
tombstone) — ending MY call is not a verdict about the room's future rings.
Decline and cancel still tombstone (they ARE verdicts about that ring) — and round
2 found the SAME class one door over: the decline/cancel tombstone silenced the
killed lane's re-ring of the reused roomId for the whole tombstone TTL, a window
WI-4.1's cache seed had newly imposed on the killed lane ("host rings → member
slow → host cancels → host rings again" went silent). The tombstone therefore
became **per-RING, not per-room**: it records the consumed fan-out's B-336
`ringId`, and a seed carrying a DIFFERENT ringId — a genuine new fan-out —
supersedes it entirely (the tombstone is deleted so the new card survives the
stale-card gate). Same-ringId and no-ringId seeds stay refused: 1:1 and
pre-B-336-relay semantics are exactly the old fail-closed ones.
`INCOMING_TOMBSTONE_TTL_MS` also came back from 150 s to 120 s. **Round 3 (F1)
widened the supersede to identity-less tombstones:** the WS/foreground group
lanes never seed the cache, so THEIR decline/cancel tombstoned with no captured
ringId and the killed-lane re-ring stayed refused ("decline while looking at the
phone, put it down, host re-rings → silence"). A seed CARRYING a ringId on a
group id whose tombstone has none can only mean foreground consumption, so it
supersedes — while 1:1 (whose seeds never carry a ringId) keeps the byte-identical
fail-closed refusal, and a same-fan-out duplicate after a foreground decline
re-rings once, bounded by the 45 s card timeout + notifee id dedup. The supersede is
STRUCTURALLY group-only (F1-R4): ringId rides unsigned and every 1:1 tombstone lacks
one, so without a kind gate a smuggled ringId on a 1:1 wake would delete the tombstone
and disarm the WI-4.7 accept gate, the dead-offer watchdog and the offer-replay guard —
the guard now enforces what the server merely happened to do. Pinned by
`groupRingCleanup` (supersede / foreground-consumed supersede / same-ring refusal
/ no-ring refusal / 1:1 unchanged); mutation-proven both directions.

### B-503 — a stale card event re-joined a dead call ⚠️ P2 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED (round 1)

**Found by the edge-case reviewer (scenario 11).** A queued notifee press event
delivered after its call died (declined, cancelled) sailed through the rich
handler: the Answer branch re-latched and navigated with `autoAccept`, and the
GROUP lane — unlike 1:1 — has no dead-offer watchdog and no accept()-tombstone
gate, so the stale event dropped the user straight back into `sfu.join`.

**Fix:** the rich handler drops any card-driven event whose callId is dead
(`isIncomingCallDead || wasRecentlyEnded`) right after the entry dismiss. The gate
is sound because no lane draws a card for a tombstoned id — a card-driven event
for a dead call is stale BY CONSTRUCTION. It is deliberately NOT a registry
liveness check: an on-screen accept of a WS-delivered re-ring is legitimate while
the same roomId carries an older decline's tombstone, and that flow never passes
through the notifee handler. **Round 2 closed the residual:** after a group END (which no
longer tombstones — B-502) the gate's first two signals were both blind, so
`dropIncomingCallPayload` — whose only caller is the group teardown — now marks
the room in a `consumedGroupRooms` map (third OR-signal in the gate), and ANY
successful seed self-heals the marker so a genuine re-invite's card is never
blocked: stale Answer after END → dropped; FCM re-invite → seed clears marker →
answers; WS re-invite → no card, gate not in that path; cold VM → marker absent →
the `getInitialNotification` replay passes. Mutation-proven (the third signal
removed → RED — a survivor caught and killed in the same round).

### ADJUDICATION (round 2, not a bug) — the Telecom End no-op on an answered-but-not-yet-live call stays

The critic asked for the WI-4.8 guard branch to also tear down locally
(reportEnded + tombstone) so a REAL user End mid-accept is honored instantly. Both
options were weighed and the no-op won: a real End and the spurious
system-ring-teardown End are indistinguishable at this event, and acting on it
tombstones the call — which the WI-4.7 accept gate then refuses, killing the accept
the user just made. That is the B-109 regression resurrected through a new door.
The no-op's whole cost is one ignored press: the in-app surface mounts within the
same window and its End works. **Round 2 tightened it on the critic's
counter-proposal:** the branch is AGE-BOUNDED to the plausible accept-in-flight
window (`NAV_READY_WAIT_MS + TURN_FETCH_CEILING_MS`, 26 s) via the latch's
timestamps — past it a system End cannot still be racing the answer, so a real End
declines exactly as it did at HEAD. Pinned ("a late Telecom End declines again");
mutation-proven. Recorded in the branch comment.

### B-504 — the group FOREGROUND ring lane presented without HMAC verification ⚠️ P2 security · FIXED 2026-08-17

**The last Security-S3 asymmetry, carried out of the Phase 4 review as known-open and
closed on founder instruction.** Every other ring-admission lane verified the voip-wake
HMAC before presenting — background (Round 5/S3), headless (WI-4.1), the foreground 1:1
rescue (WI-4.10) — but the foreground GROUP re-dispatch (AC-3, B-306 rider) fed
`dispatchGroupRingFrame` straight from the unverified push payload: a forged or
replayed FCM data message could present a full-screen group ring UI to a foregrounded
app.

**Fix.** One verification gate at the top of the `onMessage` voip-wake branch, covering
BOTH kinds — verify (real `selfUserId`, so the nonce LRU namespaces properly) → drop on
any failing verdict → only then the group re-dispatch or the 1:1 rescue. The rescue's
own inner verify was removed as now-redundant (one gate, one order, no drift). A
THROWING verifier fails CLOSED, matching every sibling lane's exception path.

**Pinned by:** `fcmForegroundWakeLane` — a failing verdict never reaches the dispatcher;
the verifier receives the signed fields + the real selfUserId; a throwing verifier
dispatches nothing. **Mutations:** verdict check disabled → RED; catch made fail-open →
RED (25th/26th of the campaign, both restored).

## 2026-08-18 — Driver-grade navigation (B-505..B-513)

Founder feedback (`docs/planning/Bravo_Secure_App_Developer_Feedback_August_2026.pdf`,
19 annotated device screenshots): _"The current map is not good enough for real driver
navigation."_ Seven requirements, with an explicit constraint that the **existing Mapbox
GL JS WebView is kept** — no new map technology.

Investigation found that three of the seven were already implemented (turn-by-turn
maneuver banner, counting-down ETA, off-route re-routing) but were being fed data far too
stale and coarse to be usable, and that the camera never rotated at all. The root cause of
"not suitable for driver navigation" is **B-505**, not the map rendering.

Spec: `docs/planning/DEV_FEEDBACK_AUG2026_NAV_SPEC.md`.
Gate: `driverNavCamera`, `navVoice`, `ownPositionBus`, `mapHtmlSyntax` (plus the existing
`navBannerLegibility`, `mapboxDirections`).

### B-505 — the driver navigated from their own position via a SERVER ROUND TRIP ⚠️ P0 · FIXED

`AgentLiveTrackerScreen` rendered the driver's own marker from
`mission.current_lat/current_lng` — the position the device had pushed to the server and
then read back. The push (`MissionLeadConsoleScreen`, `useLeadTelemetry`) is throttled to
~10 s and the tracker polls the mission every 4 s, so **the driver's own dot could be
~14 s behind the vehicle** — nearly 400 m at 100 km/h. Turn-by-turn distances, off-route
detection and any follow camera are meaningless at that latency: the map describes where
the vehicle _was_.

**Fix.** New `src/services/ownPositionBus.ts` — a ref-counted 1 Hz `watchPosition` whose
fixes drive rendering and navigation directly. The telemetry push to ops is untouched (a
separate concern). `'monitor'` mode (a remote observer, not in the vehicle) keeps reading
the server's copy, and a 15 s TTL hands the marker back to the server value if the device
GPS goes quiet. Gated on screen FOCUS, not mount — the tracker stays mounted underneath
Chat and the call screen.

### B-506 — a second `watchPosition` silently inherits the FIRST watcher's cadence ⚠️ P0 · FIXED

`react-native-geolocation-service` keeps one native stream and a module-level
`updatesEnabled` flag: `startObserving(options)` runs **only for the first watcher**, and
every later `watchPosition` call silently discards its own options
(`js/Geolocation.native.js:36-54`). `AgentDashboardScreen` starts a watcher at
`interval 30_000 / fastestInterval 15_000 / distanceFilter 20` **while a mission is
active** — exactly the window the driver is navigating in — so the new 1 Hz bus would have
been ignored and the driver would have navigated on 15-30 s fixes. That is worse than the
latency B-505 removed, and it is completely invisible: every test still passes.

**Fix.** The bus re-issues its options through `NativeModules.RNFusedLocation
.startObserving` directly (the native module re-runs `requestLocationUpdates` on every
call, so the stream re-tunes), and hands the stream back to an ambient 5 s profile on stop
— issued BEFORE its own `clearWatch`, so a provider is still alive to receive the
downgrade and the GPS can never be left running for nobody. `AgentDashboardScreen`'s
location POST, the one mission-time consumer with no throttle of its own, gained a 10 s
throttle.

### B-507 — the follow camera never rotated: the map was permanently north-up ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

`setCpo`'s follow branch called `map.easeTo({center, zoom})` — no `bearing`, no `pitch`.
`heading_deg` rotated only the marker's CSS cone. Requirement 1 ("track the vehicle and
rotate the map according to its direction") was simply absent.

**Fix.** Course over ground derived from consecutive fixes (gated on at least 6 m of real
movement, so a parked vehicle cannot spin the map on GPS noise), shortest-arc smoothing,
pitch 55, and a screen offset that seats the vehicle in the lower third. New
`window.setNavCamera({mode})` exposes Track Up / North Up; Track Up is the default for a
driver, North Up for a remote observer. The heading cone is counter-rotated against the
map bearing (it is a screen-space DOM element with no `rotationAlignment`, so it would
otherwise double-count the rotation) and is repainted on `rotate`, not only on a new fix.

### B-508 — there was no voice guidance, and the API was never asked for it ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

Nothing spoke. `fetchDirections` requested `banner_instructions` but not
`voice_instructions`, so even Mapbox's own phrasing and announcement distances were
unavailable.

**Fix.** `voice_instructions=true&voice_units=metric&language=en` (the `language=en` also
addresses the founder's separate complaint that UAE place names came back in Arabic
script). New pure `src/utils/navVoice.ts` decides WHAT to say and WHEN — unit-testable and
provider-free — with a synthesized 800/300/80 m ladder when the API returns no cues.
Speech goes through `expo-speech` (new dependency, `~14.0.8`), resolved by a lazy
`require` so a build where it is not linked degrades to silent navigation instead of
throwing during module init and taking down the navigator. Muted while a call is active,
and driver-toggleable from the maneuver banner.

### B-509 — `window.setRoute` re-fired on every fix, rebuilding the pickup/drop-off markers ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

The route-push effect listed `currentLat`/`currentLng` in its dependencies but used them
only as a fallback anchor for the re-route bubble. `window.setRoute` **removes and
rebuilds** the pickup and drop-off DOM markers, so once own-GPS raised the fix rate those
markers were torn down and recreated roughly once per second. The same pattern re-ran the
group-message bubble loop at 1 Hz.

**Fix.** Both effects read the position from a ref (`posRef`) and dropped it from their
dependency arrays. Two further 1 Hz guards were added: the split polyline (the WHOLE route
geometry, tens of KB per send) is re-injected only when the split actually moves, and the
maneuver banner re-renders only when its visible content changes.

### B-510 — the split-polyline throttle was blind to a reroute ⚠️ P2 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED

The throttle added for B-509 keyed on `targetKey` — the leg destination — which is
byte-identical before and after a reroute to the same target. Its `idx` term compared an
index into the OLD geometry against one taken from the NEW geometry, and `movedM` stays
under the threshold while the vehicle is stopped. A driver who deviated and then stopped
at a red light could receive a new route whose line was **never drawn**: the WebView kept
rendering the abandoned route while the banner and the spoken cue described the new one.

**Fix.** Key on route identity (`routeVoiceId`, which already existed for the voice
history), so the index comparison is guaranteed to be within one geometry.

### B-511 — the map-init error reporter was in its own temporal dead zone ⚠️ P3 · PRE-EXISTING, FIXED

`const post` was declared roughly 36 lines AFTER the `catch` around
`new mapboxgl.Map(...)` that calls it, in the same top-level script scope. A WebGL
context-creation failure — the one case that catch exists for — therefore raised
`Cannot access 'post' before initialization` instead of reporting, RN received nothing,
and the tracker sat out the full 15 s watchdog rather than failing fast. **Fix:** the
declaration moved above the map init.

### B-512 — the review screen claimed "waiting for approval" on an APPROVED booking ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

Dismissing the auto-pay sheet on an `OPS_APPROVED` booking dropped the client back onto a
locked footer bar reading `WAITING FOR BRAVO CONTROL SYSTEM`. The booking was approved;
what was actually outstanding was the wallet debit. Found while acting on the founder's
screen-01 note that the same waiting status was told in four places at once (nav pill,
hero panel, a decorative tri-state row, and that bar).

**Fix.** The duplicate tri-state row and the locked bar are gone; the `approved` state now
offers `APPROVED · PAY NOW`, which resumes the debit countdown. Cancel moved out of the
status hero into the fixed bottom controls slot, with the founder's own expectation stated
as copy ("Last chance to cancel..."), and B-405's scheduled reservation keeps its honest
"free to cancel until a protection officer accepts" wording.

### B-513 — a suppressed voice cue was recorded as spoken, swallowing the turn ⚠️ P2 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED

The cue key was added to the spoken set before `speakNav` ran, but `speakNav` declines
when voice is muted or a call is in progress. The cue was then permanently suppressed:
un-muting mid-approach gave silence through the turn. **Fix:** `speakNav` returns whether
it actually spoke, and only a delivered cue is recorded.

**NOT device-verified at time of writing** — a Pixel 6a release build was in flight. The
checks that most need a real drive: track-up smoothness and bearing stability at speed,
voice timing against real Mapbox cues, the reroute redraw (B-510), and battery over a full
mission with the retuned shared GPS stream (B-506).

## 2026-08-18 (2) — The Client Picked Up checkpoint (B-514..B-517)

Second pass on the founder's deck, completing the driver-navigation lane. The deck's
release blocker had two halves; the navigation half shipped in B-505..B-513, this is
the checkpoint half (deck pages 3 and 21).

### B-514 — telemetry took the mission LIVE by itself, so no checkpoint could exist ⚠️ P0 · FIXED

`MissionLeadService.pushTelemetry` — the lead's GPS heartbeat, which fires every few
seconds — ran:

```sql
UPDATE missions SET status = 'LIVE', live_at = COALESCE(live_at, NOW())
 WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'PICKUP'
```

So a mission flipped to "protection active" within seconds of reaching the pickup point,
from a location ping, before anyone was in the vehicle. **A "Client Picked Up" button on
top of this would have been decorative.** Worse, `live_at` is money- and SLA-load-bearing:
it drives the proof gate, the pre-LIVE full-refund boundary and the executive hourly
check-in schedule. It was recording "a GPS ping arrived", not "the principal is aboard".

**Fix.** The lead's confirmation is now the real transition. This path survives only as an
anti-strand fallback behind a 15-minute grace window (`pickup_at < NOW() - interval`), and
its booking-audit row is written under `reason: 'telemetry_go_live_fallback'` so a fallback
can never be mistaken for a confirmation. Removing it outright was rejected: Finish requires
LIVE/SOS, so a lead who never taps would leave an unfinishable mission and unsettled escrow.

**Pinned by:** `mission-lead.telemetry-mirror` — the go-live UPDATE carries the `pickup_at`
grace predicate and passes a window of at least 10 minutes. **Mutation:** guard removed → 2 RED.

### B-515 — the confirm branch advanced the wrong action ⚠️ P1 · REVIEW-CAUGHT, FIXED

`AssignedMissionDetailScreen.onAdvance` read `if (av.confirm)` and then called
`runAction('finish')` — hard-coded, because Finish was historically the only confirmed
action. The moment Client Picked Up also required confirmation, **confirming a pickup would
have completed the mission and released payment to the agency.** Caught by self-diff while
adding the confirmation, before it could ship.

**Fix.** The confirm branch advances `av.action`, and the dialog copy moved into the shared
`missionActionConfirm()` so both screens attest to the same sentence.
**Pinned by:** `missionCheckpoint` — no screen may contain `runAction('finish')`.

### B-516 — the driver had no mission control on the navigation screen ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

`AgentLiveTrackerScreen` rendered zero FSM controls and did not even read `is_lead`. To
advance a mission the driver had to leave the map for the CPO Mission tab; the agent build
had no route to go-live at all. The slide-in lead console can only mark waypoints.

**Fix.** One contextual pill on the tracker — Arrived at pickup → Client Picked Up →
Client Dropped Off — driven by the existing `missionActionView` selector and a new shared
`useMissionAdvance` hook (a pure extraction of the CPO screen's transition body, so the two
screens cannot drift on the deploy-checks translation, the session-loss branch or the
never-optimistic re-read). Shown within 150 m of the pickup; beyond that it stays visible
but demoted, and the confirmation names the distance — the deck's "operational override".
Every assigned crew member sees the same stage; a non-lead gets a read-only
"LEAD CONFIRMS · …" row rather than a button the server would reject with `lead_only`.
Anchored off the measured dock (never appended to it, which would grow `dockHeight` and
silently unmount the style column on a short screen).

### B-517 — a SECOND, less-gated path into PICKUP ⚠️ P2 · OPEN, NOT FIXED

`MissionLeadService.markWaypoint('PICKUP')` — the lead console's "Principal Onboard" row —
runs its own `UPDATE missions SET status='PICKUP' WHERE status='DISPATCHED'` with **neither**
the `agent_deployment_checks` gate **nor** the geofence warning that
`AgentService.flipMissionStatus` applies. With the checkpoint made prominent this is a
bypass: a lead who cannot pass deploy checks can tap the console instead.

**Not fixed here on purpose.** On the agent build (which has the lead console but no CPO
Mission tab) that row is currently the only path into PICKUP, so removing its side effect
must land _after_ the tracker checkpoint is confirmed working on device, or agent-build
leads are stranded. Sequence it next, and relabel the row so exactly one control in the app
means "the principal is with me".

**NOT device-verified** — the APK is built and the bundle verified to carry the new labels,
but the Pixel disconnected before install. Needs a real mission: confirm the pill appears at
the right stage, that confirming it flips navigation to the drop-off within a second or two,
that a non-lead sees the read-only row, and that the out-of-radius override reads correctly.

## 2026-08-18 (3) — Checkpoint record + deck pages 13 / 16 / 20 (B-518..B-521)

Third pass on the founder's deck. Closes the one amber row left on the page-3
checkpoint contract, and completes deck pages 13, 16 and 20.

### B-518 — the checkpoint recorded WHO and WHEN but never WHERE ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

Deck page 3 requires the checkpoint to record "mission ID, user/driver ID, GPS position,
timestamp". `pickup_at` / `live_at` gave the when and `mission_crew` gave the who, but the
device fix posted with the transition was consumed ONLY by the fire-and-forget geofence
warning (`warnIfFarFromMissionPoint`) and then discarded. After the fact there was no way
to answer "where was the driver when they confirmed the client was aboard".

**Fix.** `flipMissionStatus` writes an `ops_audit` row —
`mission.arrived_at_pickup` / `mission.client_picked_up`, subject the mission, actor the
lead, metadata carrying lat/lng plus an explicit `has_fix` so a denied permission is
recorded honestly rather than implying an unknown position. **No migration:**
`ops_audit.metadata` is already jsonb. Written only when the conditional UPDATE actually
matched, so a replayed idempotent 200 cannot fabricate a second record, and best-effort by
design — these actions are deliberately NOT in `OpsAuditService.CRITICAL_ACTIONS`, because
a transient audit failure must never roll back a real mission transition.

**Pinned by:** `agent.checkpoint-record` (5). **Mutation:** INSERT removed → 3 RED.

### B-519 — the booking discarded the place name the user chose, and stored Arabic ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

**The root cause of "descriptions is not what I chose" and "description - English (UAE)",
and it was never on the tracking screen at all.** In `LocationPickerScreen.pickResult` the
user taps an English Search-Box result and the screen stores that label — then the very
next line recentres the map. The recentre fires `moveend`, whose `reverseGeocode` in
`bravoLocationPickerMapHtml.ts` did **not** pass `language=en`, so `place_name` came back in
the local script; the moveend handler overwrote `pin.address` with it, and `confirm()`
shipped THAT to the booking.

So the Arabic address was manufactured at BOOKING time. Every later surface — the route
timeline, the map pins, the booking summary — was faithfully replaying a value that was
already wrong when it was saved.

**Fix.** Two halves: the picker geocode now requests `language=en`, and the moveend handler
recognises its own recentre (coordinate match within ~1 m) and keeps the chosen name. A
genuine user pan still adopts the geocoded name, so a dragged pin cannot keep a stale label.

**Pinned by:** `clientRouteClarity` (both halves, plus the pan case).

### B-520 — six stage labels could not fit, at any font size ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (deck page 20)

`StepperBar` rendered each label under its dot inside a FIXED `cell: {width: 52}`.
`scaleTextStyles` rewrites only fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing, so the cell stayed 52 dp
at every screen width and every fontScale while the glyphs grew. Six non-shrinking cells are
an incompressible **312 dp — wider than a 320 dp screen before any padding** — and the only
elastic child (`conn: {flex: 1}`) collapsed to zero and the row overflowed its host. At
fontScale ≥ 1.15 the labels also character-wrapped inside 52 dp: "Prote ction act…",
"Team disp atched", "Complete d".

**Fix.** Six readable labels do not fit across a phone at any font size, so the words moved
to a full-width caption that cannot truncate ("Step 5 of 6 · Protection active"), the cell
shrank to 30 dp (row minimum 312 → ~180 dp), and every dot carries its own accessibility
label. The six `STEP_LABELS` strings are deliberately **unchanged** — `agentAcceptance`
pins them and their order (Issue 41: the client must not read "dispatched" before an officer
accepts). Renders on ten surfaces across client, agency and CPO.

**Caveat for the founder:** the page-23 checklist line "all six mission-stage labels are
readable" is met in the sense that nothing is clipped and every stage is announced, but only
the CURRENT stage is spelled out on screen. Abbreviating all six to fit the rail needs a
wording decision (longest word ≤ 7 characters).

Also on page 20: the DARK/LIGHT/SAT/3D column was a permanently expanded 154 dp block in the
map gutter. It now collapses to a single layers button while navigating and expands on tap;
`STYLE_TOGGLE_H` keeps its name but is derived, so the band gate reserves the height actually
rendered. **Pinned by:** `stepperBarLabels` (9), `driverNavCamera` (+4).

### B-521 — the client's progress pill read 0% for the whole approach ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 16)

Two defects on the client map. The pins drew `origin.label` / `dest.label` — the FULL stored
address — into a `.tag` that is `white-space: nowrap` with no width cap, so one pin painted a
black bar across the route. And the progress pill was `window.setProgress(isLive &&
hasRealFix ? pct : 0)`, a bare percentage to "B" that showed **0% for the entire pickup leg**
and was not tied to the mission stage at all.

**Fix.** Pins take a short place name (new pure `src/utils/placeLabel.ts`, unit-tested against
the founder's real UAE string) and `.tag` is width-capped in CSS as a backstop. `setProgress`
now takes a label, and the screen sends the remaining distance with its leg —
"4.2 km to pickup" / "4.2 km to drop-off" — or says "Awaiting live GPS" instead of showing a
false 0%. Reuses `remainingRouteM` / `formatDistance`, the same helpers the driver screen
uses, rather than a second progress formula.

**Pinned by:** `placeLabel` (15), `clientRouteClarity` (10).

**NOT device-verified** — the APK is built and the bundle verified to carry every new string,
but the Pixel disconnected from USB before install could run.

## 2026-08-18 (4) — Remaining deck pages: client map, verify code, cancel rule, call naming (B-522..B-527)

Fourth pass. Closes deck pages 6, 11, 18, plus page 5's cancel rule and page 19's call
naming/terminology.

### B-522 — expanding the map hid the verification code ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (deck page 6)

His note: "when I got in cpo, code gone". The verify card is pinned as a sibling of the
header, and the fullscreen map is a `<Modal>` whose content is ONLY the map plus a collapse
button — so tapping the expand control covered the card completely and the code the client
is meant to read aloud vanished. He was expanding the map to look for his officer, which is
why "code gone" and "cannot see cpo" sit on the same annotation.

**Fix.** The fullscreen view mirrors the code. Deliberately mirrored, not re-mounted: a
second `VerifyGuardCard` would fetch again and rotate on its own clock, so the two copies
could disagree mid-handshake. The one mounted card reports its code upward via `onCode`.

### B-523 — the verify card read the UNGUARDED booking singleton ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

A second, independent way to lose the same code. `bookingStore.loadActiveBooking` overwrites
ONE global slot and four other screens call it (BookingConfirmation, CreditPaywall,
OpsRoomReview, and the tracker's own poll). This screen already applies the B-405 id-guard
for its poll and its GPS arm (`abOwn`), but `missionStatus` and `bookingStatus` were read
straight off the raw singleton — so another booking loading anywhere could drive this
screen's status, unmount the card and destroy the code. It self-healed only on the next poll
tick, and only while the screen was active.

**Fix.** Both derived statuses now go through the same `abOwn` id-guard as everything else.

### B-524 — Recenter framed the route but not the client ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 11)

"cannot see agent" on the fold view. `lastBounds` extends pickup, drop-off and the vehicle;
the client's own dot is deliberately excluded so the automatic framing does not chase a
client who wanders. But Recenter reused those same bounds, so an explicit "show me
everything" could not show the client.

**Fix.** Automatic framing stays route-only; an explicit Recenter builds fresh bounds
including the client's own position. The deck's ask was "recenter should frame all active
mission markers, not only one endpoint".

### B-525 — the client could not tell which dot was which ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 18)

"cpo / moving / me" pointing at two dots. They were already colour-distinct (violet client,
blue officer, amber pickup, green drop-off) but nothing said so: only the vehicle and the
two endpoints carried tags, and there was no key.

**Fix.** The client's own dot is labelled YOU, and a small persistent legend names all four
markers so the client and the Bravo Control System read the same map the same way.

### B-526 — cancel was still offered after a crew was dispatched ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (deck page 5)

He struck out CANCEL BOOKING with "no cancel option". The gate was `!dispatchedLive`, and
`dispatchedLive` is only booking LIVE or mission LIVE / SOS — **mission DISPATCHED and PICKUP
were not covered**, so the client could cancel while a crew was already assigned and driving
to the pickup. Server-side that cancel is accepted and in one transaction aborts the mission,
stands the crew down and deletes the mission room. Money: with `DISPATCH_CANCEL_FEE_PCT`
defaulting to 0, a post-assignment cancel refunds in FULL today.

**Fix (client).** Cancel hides as soon as a crew is committed
(`mission_status` ∈ DISPATCHED/PICKUP/LIVE/SOS). Gating on mission_status is what keeps
B-405 intact: a mission_status only exists once crew has ACCEPTED, so the five
pre-commitment states (DRAFT / DISPATCHING / PENDING_OPS / OPS_APPROVED / PAYMENT_PENDING)
stay unconditionally cancellable and a parked 'later' reservation is untouched.

**STILL OPEN — needs a founder decision.** The server still accepts a post-assignment cancel
and still refunds in full. Whether that should carry a cancel fee, and at what percentage, is
a business rule, not something to set silently. `DISPATCH_CANCEL_FEE_PCT` already exists and
already splits correctly when non-zero.

### B-527 — the mission call announced itself as a system identifier ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 19)

The incoming-call screen showed "MISSION MSN-956AF85E0956 · OPS ROOM". That string is the
mission group's NAME, set once at room creation by
`SystemMessengerService.createMissionOpsRoom`. Two problems: shouted-caps "OPS ROOM" breaks
the locked client-facing terminology (it is the Bravo Control System), and it reads as a
system identifier rather than a call from the client's own detail.

**Fix.** `Mission <short-code> · Bravo Control System`. Applies to newly created rooms;
existing rooms keep their stored title.

**Note on "agent call all":** a mission group-call control DOES already exist — two icon-only
16 px buttons in the driver tracker's message dock, wired to `launchCall(..., isGroup: true)`.
They carry no visible text, which is why the founder reported the feature as missing. Making
that action legible is a UI change on the mission surfaces, not new call machinery.

**NOT device-verified** — build in flight when this was written.

## 2026-08-18 (5) — The last deck pages (B-528..B-532)

Fifth and final pass on the founder's deck: team photos, the destination in the Route tab,
the dispatch-state contradiction, and making "call all" legible.

### B-528 — the client could not see who was arriving ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 12)

His annotation: "onboard photo of worker, guard, cpo, employee". The client is asked to
match a face against a rotating code at handover, but the TEAM card rendered only initials
in a circle — a name and two letters are not an identification.

The photo existed the whole time: `users.avatar_url` and a public `avatars` bucket have been
in the schema since the initial migration, and the crew query already JOINs `public.users`.
It was simply never selected.

**Fix.** `avatar_url` added to the mission-crew projection, the `AssignedCpo` /
`AssignedCpoDto` shapes and the client TEAM row, which renders the photo and keeps initials
as the fallback. The legacy `cpo_pool` path returns null explicitly — many of its rows are
not real users, so null is the honest answer there. **No migration.**

### B-529 — the Route tab never said where the detail was going ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 9)

His annotation was a literal question mark beside the rows: "destination?". The tab listed
events but named no destination anywhere.

**Fix.** A destination row above the timeline showing the short place name, tapping to reveal
the full stored address (the deck asks for "short English place labels, with the full address
available on tap").

### B-530 — the confirmation screen told three different stories at once ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (deck page 5)

"The dispatch state and next action must be unambiguous." Three independent signals disagreed:

1. the nav pill was the **literal string 'Paid'** and never reflected state — a booking that
   had since gone CANCELLED still showed a green Paid chip until a redirect fired;
2. the stepper was driven by `journeyStep()`;
3. the TRACK button used a THIRD predicate (`dispatchedLive`, i.e. LIVE/SOS only).

Concretely: at mission DISPATCHED the stepper read "Team dispatched" while the button read
AWAITING DISPATCH and was disabled.

**Fix.** One derived state feeds the pill and the action together
(`Cancelled / Completed / SOS / Protection active / Team dispatched / Paid`), and the primary
action unlocks as soon as a crew is committed rather than only at LIVE.

### B-531 — a legacy LIVE booking rendered "Searching for your detail" ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

`journeyStep()` had branches for every mission state and for booking COMPLETED / CANCELLED /
NO_PROVIDER / CONFIRMED / DISPATCHING — but **not for booking LIVE**. The legacy ops
"Dispatch" path flips a booking CONFIRMED→LIVE directly and never creates a mission row, so
such a booking fell through to the pre-dispatch default: the client saw step 1 of 6,
"Searching for your detail", while the TRACK button beside it was enabled. The screen
contradicted itself.

**Fix.** A `booking === 'LIVE'` branch returning step 5 (Protection active). Shared by
client, agency and CPO, since they all render the same stepper.

### B-532 — "agent call all" already existed and looked like nothing ⚠️ P3 · FIXED (deck page 19)

The founder asked for an "Agent Call All / Mission Group Call action". It was already there
and already correct: two buttons in the driver tracker's message dock calling

assigned crew. They were **icon-only 16 px glyphs** crammed beside the composer, so it read
as a generic phone button and the feature was reported missing.

**Fix.** The voice control is labelled ALL and its accessibility label is now
"Call all — ops and crew". No call machinery was touched, so the messenger gate does not
apply. The word is the feature.

## 2026-08-19 — Closing the audit's 27 outstanding dev actions (B-533..B-540)

An adversarial audit of the whole deck against HEAD found 22/49 dev actions done, 21 partial
and 6 not started — against an earlier claim that every page was addressed. That claim was
wrong; this section closes the gap. The 27 items were six root causes, not 27 misses.

### B-533 — the client map framed itself once and never looked again ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

The single biggest gap, and the "not centered" half of deck pages 6, 8, 9 and 14. Automatic
framing fitted pickup/drop-off/vehicle once per origin|dest key and never re-framed, so the
officer could drive out of the viewport and stay there for the rest of the mission. The only
escape hatch — the Recenter pill — was `display:none` until the client happened to drag the
map, so a client who never touched it had no control at all, and every expand/collapse
remount reset that state to hidden.

**Fix.** One `missionBounds()` covering pickup, drop-off, vehicle, the client's own dot AND
the drawn route line (which can bulge outside the straight three-point box), used by both the
Recenter tap and a new `window.refit()`. The pill is always on screen. The camera re-frames
itself when the vehicle leaves the viewport — but only while the camera is still ours, so a
client who has panned keeps what they chose.

### B-534 — the progress pill was dead on the leg the founder photographed ⚠️ P1 · FIXED

Deck pages 11/16/17. The distance label was gated on `isLive && hasRealFix`, and
`lite_bookings.status` only flips to LIVE in the SAME transaction that sets the mission LIVE —
so for the entire approach-to-pickup leg it read "Awaiting live GPS" and the `'to pickup'`
branch was unreachable on the normal auto-dispatch path. SOS additionally fell to the else
branch and said "to pickup" during a live drive.

**Fix.** Both the leg word and the gate now key off the MISSION stage
(`onDropoffLeg = LIVE || SOS || booking LIVE`), and distance shows as soon as there is any
real fix to measure from.

### B-535 — the client map had no orientation, no compact mode, no top guard ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

Deck pages 7/10/17. The client map had **zero** bearing code (the track-up work shipped on the
DRIVER map and had been credited to the client page). The ~328×252 collapsed box rendered the
same four-corner chrome as fullscreen. And the legend added in the previous pass collided with
the fullscreen verify bar added in the same pass.

**Fix.** `setNavCamera({mode})` with course-over-ground derived from consecutive vehicle fixes
(gated on real movement so a parked vehicle cannot spin the map), North Up by default for a
watching client and Track Up once protection is ACTIVE, plus a tappable N/TRK control.
`setCompact()` drops the secondary chrome in the collapsed box. `setTopGuard(px)` lets RN
report the space its own overlays occupy — the same contract the driver map already uses — so
the legend and style segment sit below the verify bar rather than underneath it. Style
segments and the expand control are now ≥44 dp.

### B-536 — four markers, one shape ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 18)

Pick-up and drop-off were byte-identical 16 px circles; only colour separated any of them,
which fails for colour-blind users and at a glance. Now four shapes: teardrop pin (pick-up),
square flag (drop-off), rotating arrow (officer, counter-rotated against map bearing so it
does not double-count in track-up), plain dot (client).

### B-537 — a phantom officer parked on the pickup pin ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (deck page 11)

Before the first real fix the vehicle marker is drawn on the PICKUP coordinates, labelled with

The server rename runs only at room creation, and the client caches the first name it synced —

**Caller-completeness sweep (MESSAGE_LOOP §5) — this is what the first pass got wrong.** The

and the legacy title reached four of them:

| Site                                         | Renders                                  |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `launchCall.ts`                              | the outgoing call title                  |
| `IncomingGroupCallScreen.tsx`                | the ring screen (the founder screenshot) |
| `GroupCallScreen.tsx`                        | in-call header + FGS notification        |
| `ChatScreen.tsx`                             | the chat header                          |
| `MessengerHomeScreen.tsx` (`rowDisplayName`) | the conversation-list row                |
| `ChatInfoScreen.tsx`                         | the chat-info title                      |

`GroupCallScreen` transforms once at the param boundary so the header, the foreground-service
notification and the missed-call bubble cannot disagree. It falls back to the RAW value rather
than `undefined`, which keeps the type identical to the route param — the first version used
`|| undefined`, widened `string` to `string | undefined` and pushed typecheck to exactly
baseline (47). Now 46.

Scope note: display strings only. No crypto, no envelope, no protocol, no store writes —
the cached conversation name is left exactly as synced and only the rendered text changes.

### B-545 — the verify code could outlive its booking ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (self-diff find)

Found by the founder's standing self-diff rule, not by a test. `VerifyGuardCard` holds the code
in component state and refetches on `bookingId` change, but the component is NOT remounted when
that prop changes — so between the id changing and the new fetch landing (or indefinitely, if
that fetch fails) the card kept rendering the PREVIOUS booking's code. The fullscreen mirror
added for the map inherited the same staleness.

This is the identity handshake: the client reads the code aloud to confirm the officer at the
door is theirs. A stale number means either accepting the wrong person or rejecting the right
one. Now keyed on `bookingId` so the card remounts (clearing code, lead and phase together),
and the parent clears the mirror on the same signal.
