## 2026-08-17 — CALL_RACE_HARDENING_SPEC Phase 5: transport (B-546..B-553)

**Task:** WI-5.1..WI-5.7. The transport rule: ONE source of truth
(`packages/messenger-core`; `src/modules/messenger/transport/*` stays a tombstone —
`deadForkLock` untouched), and every hardening layered WITHOUT disturbing the
preserve-list: `connectGeneration`, teardown-before-reopen (RELAY-C1), the owner
epoch, the call-frame exemption, and every existing wall-clock guard.

New suites: `pushDeclineDurability`, `callFrameInboundOrder`,
`dispatcherDisposeHygiene`, `iceOutboundBuffer`, `transportSwapFollows`,
`transportCloseHygiene`. RED-first where the defect was reachable; 19 mutations RED across three
reviewer rounds (one more resolved by DELETING redundant code), each verified
applied on disk and restored — plus the edge agent's own independent 3-mutant
table on the dispatch-epoch fence.

---

### B-546 — a second `token_revoked` during the refresh stranded the transport for good ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.1)

**Root cause.** The inline `error{unauthorized|token_revoked}` handler asked
`handleAuthReject()` to own the reject; `false` meant BOTH "no refresh hook" and
"a refresh is already in flight", and the caller's fallback for `false` was
TERMINAL (`closedByUser = true` + `'unauthorized'` + disconnect). The second
reject is the NORMAL shape of this failure — the server emits the error, closes
the socket, socket.io retries with the same stale token and is rejected again
before the refresh resolves — so the resolving refresh then bailed at `doOpen`'s
`closedByUser` check: permanent strand, mid-call death at the grace timer. The
sibling `connect_error` path had the benign fallback all along.

**Fix.** `handleAuthReject` OWNS the in-flight case: benign `'reconnecting'`,
drop the rejected socket, return `true` — neither caller runs its fallback, and
`false` now means exactly one thing (no refresh hook; that give-up pin is
unchanged). **The RN `DOCUMENTS` pin was flipped** per its own WHEN-FIXED note:
refresh called once, the reopen LANDS (`ioMock` twice), state back to
`'connecting'` — the DOCUMENTS→fixed pattern working as designed.

---

### B-547 — `close()` left a corpse that revived with the old session's listeners ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.2)

**Root cause.** `close()` cleared sockets and timers but not `frameListeners`,
`reconnectListeners`, or `hasConnectedOnce`. A stale holder calling
`forceReconnect()` revived the corpse with every old listener attached — and
because `hasConnectedOnce` was still true, the revival's very FIRST `connect`
fired the reconnect listeners immediately: a group rejoin issued against a
brand-new session, and the previous session's per-screen frame listeners
double-dispatching alongside the new client's.

**Fix.** `close()` clears all three. A close ends the subscriptions with the
session: whoever legitimately revives the client re-subscribes, and the first
connect of the new life is a first connect, not a reconnect.

---

### B-548 — push-lane declines were lost whenever the send THREW ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.4)

**Root cause.** The live transport's `send()` THROWS on a disconnected socket
(never queues), and `getLiveTransport()` happily returns a non-null client whose
socket is down. All four fcmBootstrap call-control sites guarded on `tx`
TRUTHINESS with `enqueuePendingAction` in the `else` — a thrown send unwound past
the enqueue into a log-and-swallow catch. The decline was lost, the caller kept
ringing to the 45 s timeout — and at two sites the throw ALSO skipped the local
teardown (cache tombstone + latch clear) that sat after the send in the same try.

**Fix.** One never-throwing `sendCallControlDurable(frame, durable, tag)` —
try the live send; on ANY failure (null transport OR thrown send) enqueue the
durable action, which the pendingActions drain flushes over HTTP on the next
connect. Local teardown after the call can no longer be skipped. This is the
same contract the slim killed-app handler always had; the rich lanes caught up.

---

### B-549 — inbound call frames could overtake their own offer's verification ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.5)

**Root cause.** `dispatchCallFrame` is synchronous by contract, but the offer's
Audit-S7 verification is async and was fire-and-forget — a
`call.answer`/`call.ice`/`call.hangup` that followed the offer ON THE WIRE was
fully processed before the offer finished verifying. Worst shape: the hangup's
no-controller teardown ran (tombstone + `reportEnded`) and then the verified
offer presented a ring for a call the caller had already abandoned.

**Fix.** A per-callId promise chain (`inboundChains` — the mirror of the
outbound `callIdQueues`): the verify is the chain head; answer / ice / hangup /
media-state / reoffer / reanswer / missed for the SAME callId append behind it
and run in wire order. A callId with no chain takes the old synchronous path
untouched — no cross-call serialization, no added latency while healthy, and
`dispatchCallFrame` still returns synchronously.

---

### B-550 — trickle ICE produced during a WS blip was silently lost ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.6)

**Root cause.** Non-restart trickle used fire-and-forget `safeSend`; the
transport throws before socket.io could ever buffer, so every candidate during a
1–3 s reconnect window vanished with one console.warn. There is no server-side
replay lane (deliberate — ICE restart is the mid-call recovery), so a blip
during setup stranded the handshake.

**Fix.** The immediate path stays FIRST (zero added latency while healthy);
only a failed send buffers per-callId — drop-OLDEST at 64, the same bound and
policy as the two sibling ICE queues in `CallController` — with one drainer
chained on the per-callId queue flushing via `waitOpenThenSend` under
`ICE_WAIT_OPEN_MS` (5 s, promoted to `callDeadlines` with ordering pins: under
the setup budget and the connecting watchdog). Past the budget the remainder is
dropped (stale candidates would chase a dead handshake); `cancelPending` clears
the buffer so End is never delayed behind candidates.

---

### B-551 — stale transport captures outlived every runtime rebuild ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.3)

**Root cause.** After `disposeLiveRuntime()` → new transport: `CallSignalling`
held its constructor capture (every send threw-and-swallowed against the corpse
while a healthy replacement sat in the registry), the rejoin hub stayed bound to
the dead client's reconnect listeners until the next fresh mount, and the
`useGroupCall` rejoin closures captured `ws` by value — a minimized group call
silently died across any rebuild.

**Fix, three layers.** `CallSignalling.liveTransport()` resolves
`getLiveTransport()` per send with the constructor param as fallback (tests and
pre-boot keep the old behaviour exactly); the hub watches
`transportRegistry.onTransport` and re-binds itself to each new non-null
transport — ownership tokens untouched, the same handler simply follows the
socket; and both rejoin closures resolve `getLiveTransport() ?? ws` at fire
time and refresh `transportRef.current`, so the rejoin rides the live socket.

---

### B-552 — dispatcher state survived every disposal path except signOut ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (WI-5.7)

**Root cause.** `clearAllCallDispatchState` ran only on signOut. The restore
rebuild, the backup-setup rebuild and the account switch all pass
`disposeLiveRuntime` — where nothing dropped the dispatcher's queued frames or
registered signalling. The owner epoch fences NEW frames; frames already QUEUED
pre-registration drained into whatever signalling later registered the same
callId, across the account boundary, inside the 30 s TTL.

**Fix.** `clearCallDispatchTransients()` (active + pending + inbound chains +
the re-assert latch) wired into `disposeLiveRuntime` — and it deliberately
PRESERVES `onIncoming` and `verifyOfferAuth`: both are MainNavigator-owned
(installed on `[user?.id]`, NOT re-installed on a mid-session rebuild). Clearing
the handler would leave incoming 1:1 calls dead after every restore; clearing
the verifier would drop offers to the legacy UNVERIFIED fallback in the
dispose→rebuild gap — a security downgrade. signOut still clears everything.

---

### B-553 — `forceReconnect` had no floor while disconnected ⚠️ P2 · FIXED (WI-5.7/G8)

**Root cause.** The Fix #18 throttle only damped a HEALTHY socket; from
`reconnecting`/`disconnected` every public call ran a full handshake — a flurry
of AppState transitions or a stale holder hammering a corpse re-handshook at
call cadence.

**Fix.** The public surface is wall-clock floored on the not-connected side too
(same 2 s window; a floored call coalesces onto an in-flight open, so awaiting
it still means "an attempt ran"). The internal recovery paths — the B-14 ladder,
`notifyNetworkChange`, the SEC-1 reauth reopen — route through the unfloored
private `reopenNow()`, which retains the healthy-socket throttle they always
relied on; flooring them would have stalled the ladder, whose retry is only
re-armed by connection events. Two refactor defects were caught by the existing
suites en route (the connected-throttle had to move INTO `reopenNow`, and the
floor stamp had to start at `-Infinity` for mocked clocks).

---

### The reviewer loop (round 1 → fixes)

CRITIC: 4×P1, 6×P2, 5 notes. EDGE: 1 HIGH (reproduced with a live probe), 2 MED,
1 LOW across 12 scenarios + 4 self-chosen. The two reviewers CONVERGED on three
findings independently — the strongest signal in the round:

- **The chain defeats the clear** (edge HIGH B == critic P1-3): clearing the
  `inboundChains` MAP does not cancel already-scheduled chain WORK — a frame
  chained behind a slow verify ran after the session clear and re-populated
  `pending` for the next session, and an in-flight verify presented the
  PREVIOUS session's offer through the preserved handler. Fixed with a
  `dispatchEpoch` captured at append, checked pre-work AND re-checked after the
  verify await (the pre-work check alone missed the in-flight case — the edge
  agent's own repro shape became the pin).
- **`active.clear()` deafened a minimized call** (edge C == critic P2-10): a
  minimized call's signalling is exactly the class the transients clear was
  told to preserve (its owner deliberately skips the unregister and nothing
  re-installs it). The clear now preserves the LIVE registry call's entry +
  queued frames; signOut still clears all (the registry is emptied first
  there). This also restored the B-486 restore-mid-ring premise.
- **The rebind never fired on a fresh client's first connect** (edge E ==
  critic P1-4): `onReconnect` deliberately skips a client's first connect
  (B-05), and a rebuild constructs a NEW client — so the hub re-bound
  correctly and then sat silent through the exact moment the SFU had torn the
  participant down. `TransportClient.onceConnected()` (immediate when up,
  one-shot on the next connect edge, cleared by close) + the hub arming it on
  every registry rebind.

Also from the round: the WI-5.1 in-flight guard was a bare boolean — the exact
pattern the same file's own REAUTH_STUCK_MS comment forbids — and became a
permanent invisible strand that even forceReconnect could not clear (its reopen
landed back in the same branch); now wall-clocked (UNAUTH_REFRESH_STUCK_MS).
The headless notifee decline sites FLOATED the durable enqueue — notifee kills
the headless task when the handler settles, so the write could die with the
process; now awaited, and the pin was made discriminating by giving the storage
mock macrotask-deferred writes (the floated variant is RED). One drain deadline
instead of per-candidate; a verify deadline (OFFER_VERIFY_DEADLINE_MS,
fail-closed); the G8 floor resets on connect; a dead-offer 'failed' never
degrades into a durable decline (NA-02 honored); wire-time TTL stamps.

**One finding was resolved by DELETING code:** the suggested post-cancel ICE
gate turned out redundant under mutation — the drain's `cancelledCalls` bail
already covers the pre-drain window, and in the post-drain window the marker is
gone so NO gate at that site can read anything. The decorative check and its
decorative test were removed; the residual (a post-teardown straggler, bounded
by the controller clearing its candidate handlers) is documented instead of
papered over.

**Adjudicated, not fixed** (challenge recorded): the lazy `liveTransport()` can
in principle substitute a DIFFERENT user's socket for a 40s-budget frame from a
call in setup at signOut. Epoch-gating the substitute would break WI-5.3's
entire purpose (the substitution exists FOR the post-rebuild epoch change);
the real guards are signOut ending active calls + navigation reset cancelling
setup before dispose. Documented as residual.

### Rounds 2–3 (the convergence)

Round 2: CRITIC **AGREED** (with 3 residuals, all landed: the racy site-B pin →
bounded poll; two lint warnings + an indentation regression; a stale comment
contradicting the code beneath it). EDGE returned five more findings with its
own mutation table — including the round's sharpest catch, made one layer out
from its own round-1 finding:

- **R-1** — the fresh client's up-edge one-shot was SPENT when the rejoin's
  claim was still held (a pre-dispose rejoin's ack survives ≤15 s on the dead
  socket): no recovery until a genuine reconnect. Fixed event-driven — the
  refused fire flags `retryOnClaimRelease`, and `endGroupCallRejoin` fires the
  handler once when the stale claim frees. No timer (banned for backgrounded
  recovery), no second edge needed.
- **F-1** — the offer chain head kept a DISPATCH-time sig lookup while all
  five sibling frame classes had moved to PROCESS time: a user answering from
  the notification mid-verify got the FULL present (reportIncomingCall on a
  uuid with a live connection — the orphaning the reassert flag exists to
  prevent), and the phase's own pin had codified that ordering as correct.
  The head now re-reads the registration after the epoch re-check and takes
  the ingest + re-assert lane; the pin was reshaped, both mutation-proven.
- **F-2/F-3/F-4** — the 'declined'-only durable rule applied at the second
  (latent) site; `onceConnected` pinned against the REAL client (the
  inert-double shape that let round-1's DEFECT-E through, closed at the test
  layer too); an over-promising comment de-overclaimed.

EDGE also settled the 9c question with numbers: the feared 90 s claim-block is
unreachable (a dead socket's ack rejects synchronously; a post-emit death
settles at the 15 s ack timeout; all dispose triggers are foreground so timers
run) — 15 s worst case, which is exactly the window R-1 closes.

**Harness warning worth keeping (edge agent, verbatim class):** the repo's
babel `module-resolver` rewrites `@/...` BEFORE jest's `moduleNameMapper` runs,
so a mutant "installed" via an alias mapping never executes — every mutant runs
pristine code and reports GREEN. A false-GREEN generator for any alias-based
mutation harness; resolve mutants by direct require/copy instead.

**Gates at Phase 5 sign-off:** tsc 46 (baseline 47) · lint 0 errors on every
touched file · full `messenger-crypto` ×2 — final run **6426/6426**, earlier
runs red only on the four NAMED flake suites (every one green in isolation) ·
app `screens/messenger` 574 · both reviewers ran the gates independently and
reported the same shape. Both reviewers AGREED at round 3.

**NOT device-verified** — same standing position as Phases 1–4. The §7 rows
this phase most needs: token-revoked double-reject during a live call, a
1–3 s WS blip during call setup (trickle survival), restore rebuild with a

`sfu.service.join-cap.spec` (+6), the WI-6.5 describe in `push.service.spec`
(+5), client `callSyncProbe.test` (15) and `groupRingCancelIdentity.test` (17),
plus 4 silentWire pins in `callRegistryIdentity.test`. 14 mutations RED
(A/D/E/F/G/H/I/J/K round 1; L/M/N/O round 2; P round 3), each byte-verified
applied and restored. Convergence: CRITIC round 1 = 5 findings, EDGE round 1 =
2 defects + recordings; round 2 = dual AGREED (CRITIC with one advisory,
landed same round); round 3 = the advisory's confirm pass caught B-565 in the
landed hardening, re-keyed, CRITIC CONFIRMED + EDGE re-simulated; the AUDIT
#16 payload-spec completeness gate caught the missing `call.sync`
WS_PAYLOAD_SPECS entry during the full-suite run.

### B-554 — FIXED. No 1:1 answer arbitration: a second `call.answer` was forwarded into a live call

`handleCallAnswer` had no idea a session was already answered: a second device's
answer (or a same-device duplicate) was RELAYED, handing the caller two
competing SDP answers — state-machine corruption on a live call. Artifacts were
cleared only on the ANSWERING socket's lane, so another device's reconnect
could drain a live replay of an answered call, and nothing collapsed the other
devices' rings. Fix (WI-6.1): `CallSession.answeredBy {userId, deviceId}`
recorded on the FIRST answer (check+track run synchronously before the first
await, so one-process concurrency cannot double-pass); a later answer for an
`active` session returns the idempotent success shape and is NOT forwarded;
the first answer clears BOTH the answering lane and the session-pinned callee
lane, and fans ONE answered-elsewhere cancel push (`missed=false`). The
durable-answer drain stamps `answeredBy` from the flushed frame (`??=`
first-writer-wins). Pinned: `messenger.gateway.answer-arbitration.spec`.

### B-555 — FIXED. WS group decline cleared nothing; HTTP group decline never collapsed other devices

`handleSfuRingDecline` verified authority and emitted to the host — and left
the decliner's queued ring artifacts alive (ghost re-ring on reconnect,
phantom "missed group call" for an explicitly declined call) and their other
devices ringing out the 45 s wake TTL. Fix (WI-6.2): after the byte-identical
C2 gate, the WS lane now runs the same two actions as the HTTP lane —
`clearPendingGroupRingArtifacts` + `sendCallCancel(missed=false)` — and the
HTTP group branch gained the cancel push it was itself missing (its 1:1 branch
always had one). Group artifacts are per-USER, so one clear serves every
device. Pinned: ring-lifecycle spec (incl. authority-refusal = zero side
effects, hostless-room decline still clears).

### B-556 — FIXED. The artifact CLEAR paths could tear (missed-call records for answered calls)

`clearPendingCallArtifacts` / `clearPendingGroupRingArtifacts` were three
sequential awaits; a failure mid-sequence left marker+index alive with no
payload — which the reconnect drain classifies as a MISSED call for a call
that was answered/declined. Fix (WI-6.3): one Redis MULTI each (writer parity
with Phase-0 item 5 / D-3), per-command error inspection surfaced as a
`[CALL]`/`[SFU]` partial-failure warn, keep-marker keeps marker AND index
(P1-15 preserved). A rejected exec stays silent by design — that failure mode
leaves all three artifacts intact and degrades to replay-not-missed. Pinned:
ring-lifecycle + calls-spec keepMarker/settle assertions (existing fakes gained
multi() forwarding so they observe real state).

### B-557 — FIXED. SFU join cap and host election raced across the awaited transport creation

Cap check and `participantTags.add` were separated by two awaited
`createWebRtcTransport` calls: two concurrent joins both passed at size cap-1
(over-cap room), and two simultaneous FIRST joiners could both claim host (or a
failed claimer leave a hostless room — no call-key mint, no ring-cancel
authority). Fix (WI-6.4): `room.pendingJoins` reservation map — cap and host
election count established+reserved, the reserve happens in the same
synchronous stretch as the checks, rollback on transport failure frees the slot
and hands a claimed host to `firstUserOf` (first established, else earliest
reservation, else nobody → clean re-election). SFU-05 stale-supersede ordering
untouched. `endRoomIfEmptyByHost` and the zombie sweep treat reservations as
occupancy. Pinned: join-cap spec's concurrent describe (gated transports,
genuinely interleaved).

### B-558 — FIXED. The VoIP wake budget could brick a sender→recipient pair permanently

`commitVoipWakeBudget` was `INCR` then conditional `EXPIRE`: a crash or Redis
error between them minted a TTL-LESS, ever-growing counter that permanently
denied that pair's wakes at the cap (the D-5 rate-limiter class); the per-call
dedup key had the same shape plus an unbounded key leak. Fix (WI-6.5): the
pair/recipient counters are TIME-BUCKETED (`:floor(now/60s)` suffix) — a
counter whose EXPIRE never lands simply stops being read one window later —
with a 2×-window hygiene EXPIRE riding one MULTI with the INCRs; the per-call
key's INCR+EXPIRE is one MULTI. Fixed windows allow ≤2× cap across one
boundary straddle (documented; same class as the budget's pre-existing
bounded-concurrency caveat). The per-call TTL now slides per attempt —
strictly stricter. Pinned: push spec WI-6.5 describe (frozen-clock EXPIRE-never-
fires world, window rotation admits).

### B-559 — FIXED. No 1:1 reconcile primitive: zombie call UI waited out its own timers

The SFU has `sfu.producers`; 1:1 had nothing — a client that missed a hangup
(Doze, deploy, dropped frame) sat in a dead call UI. Fix (WI-6.6): read-only
WS `call.sync {callId}` → `{ok, state: ringing|active|ended|unknown}` over the
socket.io ack (event-less, SFU-01); a NON-participant gets exactly the
nonexistent answer (`unknown`) — no existence oracle; rate bucket
`call.sync {1/s, burst 5}`; the AUDIT #16 gate caught the missing
`WS_PAYLOAD_SPECS` entry (added: `{callId: 'string'}`). Client:
`runCallSyncProbe` (new `runtime/callSyncProbe.ts`) — fires with a live 1:1
call from the transport `connected` branch and the resume `probe` branch,
hard-ends through the KEYED `endActiveCall({callId, gen}, 'ended', 'remote',
{silentWire: true})` (wire-silent — B-565) ONLY on an explicit
`ended`/`unknown` verdict, keeps the call on every transport error, and
re-checks `{callId, gen}` post-await (the Phase-5 lesson). A relay restart therefore ends the local call in ≤1 probe — the
documented relay-session contract. Pinned: ring-lifecycle (server) +
`callSyncProbe.test` (client unit + productionRuntime wiring scans).

### B-560 — FIXED. Group ring cancel was roomId-wide: a second ring for the same room could not be cancelled independently

Cancel/missed push reused `roomId` as the id even though `ringId` existed
(B-336), so a stale cancel for ring #1 destroyed ring #2's queued artifacts,
missed-marker and UI. Fix (WI-6.7): the `sfu.ring` ack returns the fan-out's
`ringId`; `sfu.ring.cancel` carries it (validated ≤64 chars); the
`sfu.ring.cancelled` frame, the cancel push payload and the RING-SCOPED
artifact clear all thread it (the missed marker now stores its fan-out's
ringId too, so a late cancel can't destroy a newer ring's missed record).
Every client consumer matches on ring identity with a room-wide fallback when
either side lacks an id: the ring screen (route param + per-ring handler
rebind), the parked-ring clear, the dispatcher dedup re-arm (scoped so a
presented ring #2 stays replay-suppressed), and both push lanes
(fcmBootstrap + fcmHeadless compare the cached ring's id). Read→MULTI TOCTOU
on the scoped clear is documented-bounded (a Lua compare-and-del would close
it; WATCH unusable on the shared client). Pinned: ring-lifecycle +
`groupRingCancelIdentity.test`.

### B-561 — FIXED (review round 2, critic F1/F2 + edge F1). The answered-elsewhere collapse was ignored by exactly the devices it targeted

Round 1 shipped the WI-6.1 cancel push and a client guard protecting the
winner — but the guard shielded ANY non-terminal registry state including
bare `'ringing'`, and the loser's own accept latch shielded IT. Consequences:
the loser stranded at "Answering…" until a watchdog whose hangup is AUTHORIZED
(the loser is a participant) could tombstone and kill the LIVE call; a
foreground-ringing sibling rang the full 45 s next to the answered call and
logged a false missed call, with the same expiry-hangup kill tail. Fix, three
layers: (1) the duplicate-answer drop emits a DIRECTED
`call.hangup {reason:'ended', from: caller}` on the answering socket itself
(never the shared deviceRoom — that would hit the winner); (2) the client
guard excludes bare `'ringing'` (the accept window stays covered by the
bounded 20 s latch); (3) `handleCallCancel` actively ends a registry-mounted
bare ring via the keyed teardown, scoped to `missed !== '1'` so caller-gave-up
cancels leave the WS-hangup/expiry lanes as owners of the missed record.
Plus the rounds-2/3 hardening: `CallController.endSilently` — an end that
acts on a verdict the far side ALREADY ISSUED sends no wire hangup (under the
shared deviceId a live sibling transport would relay an authorized kill into
the winner's session), keyed on an EXPLICIT `endActiveCall(..., {silentWire:
true})` opt-in — see B-565 for why it is NOT keyed on `source`. Pinned:
answer-arbitration spec (directed emit, winner silent),
`groupRingCancelIdentity.test` (guard scans, keyed collapse, endSilently
wire-silence, opt-in population scan), `callRegistryIdentity.test`
(silentWire routing + the glyph-class inverse contract, ×4).

### B-562 — FIXED (round 2, critic F3). WI-6.2/6.7 turned two unmetered WS frames into push amplifiers

`sfu.ring.decline`/`sfu.ring.cancel` had no rate bucket while now firing
FCM/APNs cancel pushes per frame/recipient; a 30-min ring token replayed in a
loop was a free push cannon. Fix: both events bucketed `{1/s, burst 5}` +
`rateGate` before the untouched C2 gate, event-less refusals. Pinned:
ring-lifecycle (`rate-limited decline does nothing`).

### B-563 — FIXED (round 2, critic F4). The ring screen's per-ring effects were keyed per-room

A same-room re-ring swaps route params with an UNCHANGED roomId, so ring #2
inherited ring #1's remaining 45 s clock (dismissal + missed bubble while the
user looks at a live ring) and its latched settle (Accept swallowed — the
WI-3.5 class one key short). Fix: the settled/cancelled latch reset and the
45 s fallback timer are keyed `[roomId, ringId]` (the cancel-listener rebind
already was). The B-473 pin in `groupRingScreenReuse.test` was updated to the
widened key — contract evolution, comment updated in place. Pinned there +
`groupRingCancelIdentity.test`.

### B-564 — FIXED (round 2, edge F2 + critic F5). The host's cancel-all named ONE fan-out and stranded the others

`lastRingIdRef` was latest-wins and both cancel callers are cancel-ALLs
(host End, boot-failure teardown): with two fan-outs of disjoint recipients
(mid-ring Add), the cancel named ring #2, so ring #1's recipients — whose
artifacts, screens and caches hold r1 — correctly IGNORED it and kept ringing
a withdrawn call (a WI-6.7 regression vs the room-wide era). Fix:
`mintedRingIdsRef` records every acked fan-out; the cancel names a ring ONLY
when exactly one was minted; zero (ack in flight — critic F5's staleness) or
many → the unscoped room-wide cancel every consumer already falls back to.
Pinned: `groupRingCancelIdentity.test` scans; MUT-N (size>=1) RED.

### B-565 — FIXED (review round 3, caught pre-ship). The round-2 hardening keyed wire-silence on a glyph-coupled field

Round 2's `endSilently` routing keyed on `source === 'remote'` — but `source`
does NOT mean "the far side already knows" in this codebase: it picks the
CallKit endedReason GLYPH, and three semantically-LOCAL live-call ends carry
`'remote'` purely for the `'remoteEnded'` glyph while RELYING on the wire
hangup — the Telecom/headset End on a live call, the system-UI End on an
accepted call, and logout with a live 1:1. Keying on source silently removed
the peer's only "Call ended" signal at all three: the peer's media died
against a closed PC, burned the B-108 reconnect ladder's 30 s budget, and
surfaced "Call failed" — while a concurrent `call.sync` CONFIRMED the zombie
(the session was never tombstoned, since tombstoning happens on a RECEIVED
hangup). The round-2 pins could not see it — spy doubles asserted the routing,
nothing asserted the three glyph sites still put `call.hangup` on the wire
(the inert-mock class, again). Fix: `endActiveCall` gained an EXPLICIT
`{silentWire: true}` opt-in — `source` stays glyph-only; the opt-in exists at
exactly the two remote-verdict sites (the ring collapse, the probe), pinned by
an inverse contract test (remote WITHOUT the opt-in → wire hangup) AND a
population scan (opt-in count per file, zero in authStore/callDispatcher).
Never shipped — the entire lifetime of the bug was inside review round 3.

### Known-open / residuals (recorded, not fixed here)

- **Probe-vs-rehydration race** (edge scenario 11): a `call.sync` racing the
  post-restart offer/answer rehydrators can return `unknown` for a call the
  server was about to rescue — outcome equals the pre-FIX-07 restart contract,
  Redis-local RTT usually wins; no code change.
- **1:1 WS decline** (`call.hangup{declined}`) still lacks the other-device
  cancel push its HTTP twin has — pre-existing, backlog.
- **SFU**: `leaveInternal`'s last-one-out room delete is the one deletion site
  not counting `pendingJoins`; reservations carry no TTL (a never-settling
  transport pins the room — pathological-only); a same-user CONCURRENT double
  join can reserve two slots (SFU-05's supersede sees established tags only).
- **Host handoff divergence**: a joiner that completed before a failed
  host-claimer's rollback holds `isHost:false` client-side while the server
  hands it authority — pinned honest in the join-cap spec.
- **answeredBy in the zombie-socket window**: a forward that "succeeded" into
  a dead-but-unreaped caller socket still records the winner; the old
  accidental recovery (another device re-answering with a fresh forward) is
  gone — trade-off accepted with the directed-hangup verdict in place.
- **Cancel-all reaches only `opts.recipientUserIds`** — an added-but-never-
  joined invitee gets no cancel (ring-out ≤45 s) — pre-existing shape.
- **Same-device double answer-emit** would receive the directed hangup and end
  the winner's own call — reachable only via an app-level double emit, which
  the accept latch already guards (B-109); recorded as a residual, do not
  "fix" by removing the directed hangup.
- **WI-6.8 deliberately NOT built**: multi-pod call state. The single-replica
  constraint is boot-ENFORCED by `replica-guard.service.ts` (a competing
  replica refuses to boot; `REPLICA_GUARD=off` logs the warning form);
  options documented in `docs/architecture/CALL_STATE_SCALING.md` (new).

## 2026-08-18 — CALL_RACE Phase 7 (WI-7.1/7.2) + known-open closure + FULL SYSTEM REVIEW (B-566..B-568)

**Task:** WI-7.1 (client [CALLSM] transition lane), WI-7.2 (server SFU/call
lifecycle logs), fix the Phase-6 known-open ledger, then a three-agent full
system review across Phases 1–7 (architecture critic, race/edge timelines,
security/regression constraints) to CLEAN.

### B-566 — FIXED. The Phase-6 known-open ledger, closed (7 items)

- **KO-1 — call.sync is rescue-aware.** A session miss no longer means
  `unknown`: the handler consults the ASKER'S OWN durable lanes
  (`pendingOfferKey`/`pendingAnswerKey`, namespaced by the authenticated sub —
  no oracle widening). A queued FIX-07 answer → `active`; a still-live queued
  offer → `ringing`; expired/blip → `unknown` (the pre-fix answer). Closes the
  probe-vs-rehydration race: the probe can no longer hard-end a call
  milliseconds before its own restart rescue lands.
- **KO-2 — 1:1 WS decline collapses the decliner's other devices.** The
  callee-decline branch of `handleCallHangup` now fans the same missed=false
  cancel push as `declineCallViaHttp`'s 1:1 branch (the P1-14 pin that
  codified the gap was updated to the new contract).
- **KO-3 — `leaveRoom`'s last-one-out delete counts reservations.** The one
  deletion site that ignored `pendingJoins` no longer closes the router under
  a mid-admission joiner.
- **KO-4 — reservations carry a TTL** (`RESERVATION_TTL_MS` 30 s, timestamped
  records). A never-settling transport creation is pruned at the next join's
  cap check and by the zombie sweep — it can neither hold `room_full` nor pin
  the room unsweepable. Wall-clock, not a boolean latch (the REAUTH law).
- **KO-5 — same-user reservation supersede + self-abort.** A same-user retry
  deletes the old reservation (SFU-05 for reservations); the superseded join's
  post-transport re-check closes its transports and throws
  `join_superseded` — one user can never hold two slots.
- **KO-6 — host handoff is announced.** The rollback handoff broadcasts
  `sfu.host-changed {roomId, hostUserId}`; both useGroupCall frame handlers
  (primary + restore twin) promote — promote-ONLY, keyed on own userId — so a
  joiner that completed before the failed claimer's rollback learns it holds
  authority (call-key mint + ring-cancel work). The completing-after case was
  already correct via its own ack (spec-pinned).
- **KO-7 — cancel-all covers every rung user.** `rungUsersRef` records the
  targets of all three ring emits (boot/invite/re-ring); both cancel-all
  sites union it with the boot list, so a mid-ring invitee who never joined
  now receives the cancel instead of ringing out against a withdrawn call.

Deliberately NOT fixed, with reasons (unchanged from the Phase-6 ledger):
the zombie-socket `answeredBy` trade-off (needs socket-liveness the relay
doesn't track; the directed loser hangup is the compensating verdict), the
scoped-clear MGET→MULTI TOCTOU (one-RTT window; a Lua closer is blocked by
ioredis-mock's unfaithful eval — house rule), and WI-6.8 multi-pod state
(excluded by mandate; boot-guarded).

Round 1 verdicts: SECURITY/REGRESSION **CLEAN** (all 15 hard constraints,

### B-567 — FIXED (review round 1, race F1 — P1). KO-6's client half was DEAD CODE: the frame was unroutable

`sfu.host-changed` was missing from `SFU_FRAME_EVENTS` (sfuDispatcher.ts) —
the runtime frame loop dropped it before `dispatchSfuFrame`, so both
useGroupCall handlers could never fire and the real host never learned it
held ring-cancel/call-key authority — exactly the outcome KO-6 was built to
prevent. THE THIRD instance of this class in that very allowlist (SFU-08's
`sfu.unmuted`; the producer-paused pair), and my pin was vacuous for it (it
scanned handler EXISTENCE in useGroupCall, never the routing set — the
inert-pin class). Fix: allowlist entry + the pin now requires
`SFU_FRAME_EVENTS.has('sfu.host-changed')` on the real module. Mutation
MUT-Q (entry removed) → RED on that pin specifically.

### B-568 — FIXED (review round 1, race F2 — P2). An ANSWERED group ring left a days-long phantom missed-call landmine

No group answer-time clear existed (the 1:1 lane has had one since
N-02/WI-6.1): the ring's 45 s payload expired but the ~7-day missed marker
survived, so ANY later reconnect by any of the user's devices — including a
WS bounce during the live call — drained `sfu.ring.missed` and wrote a
phantom "Missed group call" bubble for a call the user answered. B-432
had named the marker gap but only closed the re-ring door. Fix:
`handleSfuJoin` clears the joiner's own artifacts after a successful
join (sub-namespaced keys) and fans the answered-elsewhere
`sendCallCancel(missed=false)` to the joiner's other devices — skipped
for the HOST's own boot-join (never rung; no pointless multicast per call
start). A failed join clears nothing. Pinned (calls.spec B-568 describe);
mutation MUT-R2 (clear removed) → RED.

### Round-2 architecture items (all landed)

- **WI-7.1 group gap (P3-3, corrected round 3):** the first cut put the
  record in `patchActiveGroupCall` — which the critic's interrupted round-3
  grep proved VACUOUS (no production writer patches `state`; milestones
  re-register via `group.set`, ends via `group.end`, and the live
  intermediates — `reconnecting`↔`joined` above all — exist only in the
  hook's React state). The real funnel: `useGroupCall`'s setter is wrapped
  once (`setStateRaw` reachable ONLY through the wrapper — pinned; updater
  forms resolved against a synchronously-maintained `lastStateRef`, exact
  because the wrapper is the only writer; transition logged before the
  write). The registry patch record is KEPT with an honest comment as a
  future-writer guard. First wrapper cut broke the 6 updater-form call
  sites (typecheck 46→58, caught by the baseline gate); widened and back
  to 46 ≤ 47.
- **Payload specs (P3-4):** `sfu.ring.cancel` + `sfu.ring.ack` gained
  `ringId: 'string?'`.
- **Ring-scoped ACK (P3-5):** `ClientSfuRingAck.ringId` threaded
  end-to-end (replay payload → ackReplayedRing → runtime sender →
  `{onlyRingId}` clear) — a late ack for replay #1 can no longer destroy
  a ring #2 that overwrote the queue. The DECLINE clear stays deliberately
  room-wide: a decline is the user's verdict on the ROOM's call (documented,
  not coded).
- **Probe outbound exemption (P3-6):** `runCallSyncProbe` keeps an
  outbound unanswered ring ('calling') on an `unknown` verdict — the

**Task:** the founder re-sent `Bravo_UI_Screenshot_Review_and_Corrections.pdf` with three
new asks on top of the 15-Aug deck (which shipped as `1485f759`). Audit what was and was
not implemented, then implement the gaps. Plan + decisions:
`docs/planning/UI_CORRECTIONS_2026-08-19_FOLLOWUP.md` (markers **G1..G6** in the code).

**Audit result — two of the four asks were DEPLOY gaps, not code gaps:**

| Ask                                | State found                | Cause                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Admins organisation-specific       | no mechanism at all        | `listOrgChannels` is `WHERE c.org_id = $1`, i.e. the whole TENANT; inside a workspace an "organisation" is a root CHANNEL and nothing scoped a manager to one             |
| Kill the global Announcements list | half — member surface only | Rev 4 §2.4 kept the ADMIN block deliberately as "the only door" for legacy `#broadcast`; §8 step 7 gated its removal on the purge migration, which is **still unapplied** |
| Lateral channels at every level    | coded, hidden              | `serverKnowsLaterals` (D-6) correctly hides the button until the server emits `is_lateral`; migration `20260816000000` is **unapplied**                                   |
| Whole-card dropdown                | the opposite shipped       | founder decision **F3** (15 Aug) was "chevron expands, row name opens"; this message reverses it                                                                          |

> ⚠️ **`20260816000000_dept_channel_lateral.sql` and `20260817000000_purge_legacy_workspace_broadcasts.sql`
> are still not applied.** Until the first lands, `+ Add lateral channel` stays hidden BY DESIGN —
> in production `forbidNonWhitelisted` is false, so an old server silently strips `lateral: true`
> and creates a permanently-wrong, un-re-parentable structural child. Rollout order and the two
> blocking gates are in the 15-Aug plan §8. No client change can honestly reveal that button first.

### B-569 — FIXED. The global ANNOUNCEMENTS list could announce to the wrong organisation

Founder, on the Manage Channels screenshot: _"This should not be there. Announcements should
be within the organization itself. To avoid announcing to wrong organization/association."_

`placeRow` classifies a broadcast FIRST, so it never enters the tree: it lands in
`directoryBuckets.announcements` and draws as an unparented row — a global list whose rows
carry no organisation at all. Fixed by `nestParentedBroadcasts` (`organisationTree.ts`),
which re-places a broadcast that HAS a parent as an ordinary lateral under it, at both
workspace-tenant tree call sites. `placeRow` itself is untouched: Rev 4 §2.4 rejected
changing it for AGENCIES, whose per-level broadcast is parented to an arbitrary node while
every member is seeded into it, and that reasoning still holds.
Pinned: `channelTreeModel` (6 cases), `manageChannelsOrgScoped` (4).

### B-570 — FIXED. Admins could see and administer every organisation in the workspace

Founder: _"When adding Admins, it should be organization specific only. Admins should not be
able to see other organizations."_ No mechanism existed. `listOrgChannels` now derives
`manager_scope_root_ids` from `department_channel_members` — DERIVED, not stored: this
service `SELECT`s its columns literally, so a client shipping ahead of an unapplied
migration takes `42703 undefined_column`, which is a 500 across the whole Department
Channels module (Rev 4 §8 documents exactly that). `null` = unscoped (owner, agency, no
seeded membership) and empty NEVER becomes `[]`. Client honours it on stage 1, the header
pill, the ARCHIVED list and the invite picker.
Pinned: `managerOrgScope.spec` (11), `manageChannelsOrgScoped` (9), `inviteTeamPicker` (4).

### B-571 — FIXED. A manager invite defaulted to a whole-workspace grant

The invite form starts with no team, and a teamless invite seeds the joiner across every
organisation (`resolveSeedScopeInTx` → `{kind:'orgWide'}`). For a MANAGER that is the exact
thing B-570 exists to stop, and it was the default. Refused on the form AND in
`createMemberInvite` (`manager_invite_requires_team`) — the server rule is the real
boundary, because the client pre-flight reads `workspace_tenant` from a list that can fail
to load, and an older APK bypasses it entirely.

### B-572 — FIXED. The dropdown was only on the chevron (founder decision F3 reversed)

_"the drop down must not only be on the little arrow, it must be when you click on the whole
card/button."_ The whole card now toggles a level that has children. **No door was lost**:
admin mode's pencil already navigates where `onOpen` does, and the member tree gained an
explicit open button — F3's own reasoning (every level row is a real channel, and dept
conversations are hidden from every messenger list) is why that button exists rather than
Rev 4 §2.6's two withdrawn designs.

### B-573 — FIXED (review round 1, P0). Nesting a broadcast under a BUCKET row deleted it

The first B-569 fix. `buildChannelTree` walks only organisation roots; the leftover buckets
are emitted as flat depth-0 rows and their subtrees are never walked, while
`directoryBuckets` drops descendants of a bucketed row. A broadcast escaped that hole ONLY
via the `!r.is_broadcast &&` short-circuit in front of `nestsUnderAnotherBucketRow` —
clearing the flag handed it straight in. A `#broadcast` under a case-5 masked root (a member
of a restricted, unseeded root — the module's docs call it "the common shape") vanished from
the directory outright: no walk, no bucket, zero doors. Fixed by `parentIsWalked`. Found
independently by both reviewers AND by my own probe.

### B-574 — FIXED (review round 1, P1). A whole-workspace manager lost Create-new-organisation

`scopeApplied` was `orgs.every(o => scoped.has(...))`, which is trivially true when the scope
covers every root — the shape produced by the still-supported whole-workspace employee invite
followed by the plan's own G6 mitigation (promote to manager). It cost them two doors,
including the residual announcements door Rev 4 §8 says must never disappear. A scope that
excludes nothing is not a scope.

### B-575 — FIXED (review round 1, P1). G5 was not applied to the ADDING-ADMINS screen

The plan asserted the invite picker "is fed by the same endpoint, so a scoped admin can only
pick inside their own organisation". False: the endpoint narrows only the new FIELD, never
`channels`, and the screen never read the field. So the founder's sentence — literally about
_adding Admins_ — was satisfied on Manage Channels and not on the screen it names.

### B-576 — FIXED (review round 1, P2). A live broadcast under an ARCHIVED parent had zero doors

The scope first blanked the residual announcements section for ANY scoped admin. Two very
different rows land there: a genuinely parentless legacy row (the owner's problem), and one
whose parent is merely archived — which IS inside a real organisation, possibly the scoped
admin's own. The latter is in neither tree stage (its parent is not among the live rows), not
in ARCHIVED (it is not archived), and was now not in the section either. Same defect class as
B-573, one screen over.

### Also fixed en route — a pre-existing RED on the branch

`switchDashboardProductRoot.test.tsx` reported "0 calls" against `minimiseLiveCall`. Not a
product bug: CALL_RACE WI-1.1/1.5 made the registries identity-keyed, so `minimiseLiveCall`
now reads `getActiveCall()` first — a double without that getter throws a TypeError that the
function's own try/catch SWALLOWS, and the minimise silently no-ops in the test only. Exactly
CLAUDE.md's recorded trap ("a mock that does not mutate the registry cannot see either").
The doubles now model the keyed shape; mutation-proved RED.

### Known limitation, recorded rather than hidden

`manager_scope_root_ids` is derived from MEMBERSHIP filtered to `role = 'admin'`. A manager is
always seeded `'admin'`, so this can never drop their own organisation — but `memberRoleFor`
also returns `'admin'` to a plain member of an `open` channel, so a manager who merely
participates in another organisation's open channel still widens their own scope. Closing that
needs a real "manages organisation X" fact, which does not exist; a new `org_members` column was
deliberately refused (see the field docblock and the plan's rejected list). Fail-OPEN is the safe
side: the scope is a visibility affordance, and every mutation is still gated by
`OrgManagerGuard` + `assertManagesChannel`.

### Review round 2 — seven more, all in the round-1 FIXES (B-577..B-583)

Two independent reviewers again, re-pointed at the fixes rather than the original code.
Every one of these is a defect the round-1 repair introduced or left half-closed. Recorded
with numbers because the contract is "a bug is not fixed until a test would catch it coming
back", and each now has a mutation-proved pin.

**B-577 — an ARCHIVED organisation made the scope report itself inert.** `scopeApplied` was
decided against `topLevelOf(treeRows)`, which is LIVE rows only. Archive one whole
organisation bottom-up — the ordinary way one is retired — and the live root set shrinks to
exactly what the scope covers, so "does this scope exclude anything?" answered no: the
ARCHIVED list and the create-organisation card both un-scoped, and the scoped admin got the
retired organisation's name and its whole archived subtree back with a working editor door on
each row. Now measured against `allRootIds`, which counts archived roots too.

**B-578 — the invite form could MINT a team it displayed no selection for.** `loadTeams`
validates the `params.channelId` pre-select against the unnarrowed list; G5 narrowed
`pickable`. A pre-select in another organisation therefore survived and matched no row on
screen: nothing rendered selected, no breadcrumb, no explanation, the escape-hatch radio read
blank — and Create still sent `team_channel_id` for a team in the organisation the screen had
just been narrowed to hide. It also slipped past the G6 guard, whose condition is `!teamId`.
Reachable with no typing: a channel → Members → "Invite someone new" passes `{channelId}`.
Same finding from both reviewers. Fixed with an effect that drops a `teamId` `pickable` does
not contain, reusing the existing `droppedPreselect` copy. **The picker's scope walk was also
walking LIVE rows while Manage Channels walked the archived-inclusive set** — two surfaces
answering "which organisation is this row in" two ways — now one shape, one bound, and O(n)
rather than the quadratic per-row `ancestorPathOf`.

**B-579 — the G6 client predicate was a strict SUBSET of the server probe.** `mintDisabled`
asks _may this minter name this row_; the server asks _does a nameable row exist_. A mintable
row is always live/non-broadcast/non-announcement and never the reverse, so the only possible
disagreement was **server refuses what the form invited**: a workspace whose only root is
`restricted` (reachable on anything predating `restricted_root_not_allowed`) enabled the
org-wide row and then took a 400. The client predicate is now the server's, restated verbatim
over the same set, with a test pinning both directions.

**B-580 — the blocked banner instructed the action the greyed hatch forbade.** Every branch
ended "…so you can only invite with no specific team", two inches under the disabled control.
The second half of each sentence is now G6-conditional.

**B-581 — `unplacedBroadcasts` and `parentIsWalked` disagreed, leaving a zero-door gap.** The
residual section re-stated the nesting rule and claimed the two sets were "disjoint by
construction". `parentIsWalked` (the B-573 fix) then added a SECOND reason not to nest, and a
row refused by it belonged to neither set: no stage-1 door, no stage-2 door, no section, not
archived. Latent today — the archive guards make the shape unreachable — but the invariant the
comment leaned on was gone. The section now DERIVES its list from what the tree actually
nested, so any future refusal lands there automatically.

**B-582 — G4 turned a member's flat one-tap list into a collapsed accordion.** Nesting a
parented `#broadcast` gives a previously CHILDLESS root a child, so it stops collapsing into
the `chats` bucket and becomes a real L1 — which the collapse seed then shut by default. Two
one-tap rows became one closed card, and the root's own thread moved from the card (which now
toggles, per G1) to the small open button. The seed now closes a level only when it hides a
sub-LEVEL, which is what "users should only open the branches they need" actually means and
what the founder's own mockups draw.

**B-583 — three consistency/a11y defects in the new controls.** The greyed escape hatch
announced itself _selected_ to VoiceOver while the eye saw it unselected and Create refused it
(and the radio group then had no selected member at all). The chevron's `accessible={false}` +
`importantForAccessibility` pair is **Android-only**, so on iOS a labelled control had been
replaced by an unlabelled PUA glyph — `accessibilityElementsHidden` added. And the scoped
header pill omitted the unplaced rows rendered directly beneath it, reproducing one section
out the "two numbers describing the same thing" the pill had just been fixed for.

### And the finding that mattered most had no user impact at all

**G1 — the founder's actual ask — was pinned by NOTHING.** Nine green interaction tests all
used `getByLabelText`, which cannot reach the card: it is `accessible={false}` (required, or
iOS groups the row and swallows the pencil/open/chevron for VoiceOver), so every query
silently resolved the INNER name touchable, which calls the same handler. A reviewer replaced
the entire outer `TouchableOpacity` with a plain `View` and all five suites stayed green.
**Generalise it: hiding an element from accessibility also hides it from every label-based
test — give it a `testID` in the same edit.** Now `channel-tree-card-{id}`, pressed by testID
on both the unit and the screen surface.

Three further pins were found decorative during mutation and rewritten rather than kept:
the member-surface G4 call site (its fixture's only broadcast was PARENTLESS, so the helper
was a no-op there), the blocked-banner copy (its fixture produced `mixed`, not the
`managersOnly` branch it claimed to pin), and the nesting assertion itself (finding the row
proves nothing — un-nested it is still on screen, just at the root; the proof is that a
nested row is HIDDEN while its level is closed).

### B-584 — the crew navigation map cold-loaded the CDN on every mission ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

`MapPrewarm` (B-90 T-07) warms the WebView HTTP cache with mapbox-gl.js, the CSS and
the style JSON — but it was mounted **only** on `BookingHomeScreen`, the CLIENT
booking lane. `AgentLiveTrackerScreen` lives in `AgentNavigator`, a separate stack, so
an agent/CPO never passes through that screen: the crew navigation map fetched ~1 MB
from `api.mapbox.com` on every single mission. Now mounted on `AgentDashboard` (the
agent's first screen). The one-attempt-per-session latch is module-level, so a second
lane cannot double-run it, and the picker HTML warms exactly the shared assets the
tracker needs.

### B-585 — map boot cost was unmeasurable ⚠️ P3 · INSTRUMENTED (not a fix)

"Map loading takes too long" had no numbers behind it, and this repo has a documented
history of plausible-but-wrong performance fixes (CLAUDE.md: eight measured dead ends,
one of which made things 2x worse). Both tracker maps now report phase timings on
`ready`, tagged `[MAPPERF]` so console.warn carries them into a release build's logcat:

    [MAPPERF] crewnav ready=1840ms gl=612ms cached=false style=310ms tiles=14 net=1180kB

`cached` is the load-bearing field — Resource Timing reports `transferSize === 0` on a
cache hit, so it answers "did the prewarm actually work?" directly rather than by
inference.

**DO NOT** self-host mapbox-gl.js to remove the fetch until these numbers say it is the
dominant cost. `mapWebViewSource.ts` documents that the `https://api.mapbox.com` baseUrl
is load-bearing: it is what stops WKWebView refusing Mapbox's blob workers and rendering
a BLACK MAP on iOS (founder-reported 2026-08-11).

Trap hit while adding this, for the third time in this repo: a backtick inside a comment
**inside a JS template literal** terminates the string. `mapHtmlSyntax` (@babel/parser)
caught it.

### B-586 — the incoming mission call name rendered left-ragged ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

`callerName` carried no `textAlign`, so once a room name wrapped to two lines it rendered
left-aligned inside a centre-aligned column. Every neighbouring line only LOOKED centred
because each happened to fit on one line — which is why this surfaced exactly when mission
rooms got their longer "Mission <code> · Bravo Control System" name (B-544). Now centred
with an explicit line height, and `callerSub`/`youAre` centred too so they cannot drift if
they ever wrap.

Foldable: width capped via `useContentWidth(420)`, which is driven by
`useWindowDimensions` — so unfolding RE-MEASURES. A one-shot `Dimensions.get()` would keep
the folded width on the inner screen. Capped at 3 lines so a long name can never push the
accept/decline row off a short screen.

**Not a bug — already fixed:** the founder also reported clipped stepper labels
("Searching for your de..."). That screenshot is the PRE-B-520 build: `HEAD~1` had
`numberOfLines={2}` with full labels in a 52dp cell. Current code has one StepperBar render
site, always passing one-word `shortSteps` at `numberOfLines={1}` plus an unclippable
full-width caption. Shipped in v1.0.239 (278).

## 2026-08-20 — PDF acceptance-checklist sweep (B-587..B-589)

**Task:** the founder asked whether the whole PDF was actually built. A fresh
audit of all 17 §13 checklist items against CURRENT SOURCE (not plan docs, not
commit messages) found 13 built, 3 partial, 1 not built. The founder then asked
for the gaps closed. Three were; two are blocked and say so below.

### B-587 — FIXED. Emergency calls never reached the Calls Log (PDF item 08)

_"Emergency Calls have not been added to Calls Log."_ There was no
implementation anywhere — no bridge between the emergency surfaces and
`CallsLogScreen`, which projects WebRTC call bubbles only.

**Why it is not just a UI row.** An emergency call is a `tel:` HAND-OFF. Both
platforms refuse to report back, so there is no duration, no answered/missed,
no callee identity beyond the number passed in. The only honest moment to
record anything is the instant of hand-off, and the only honest content is
"this number, at this time". New `src/store/emergencyCallLog.ts` (local,
persisted, capped at 100, 15s dedupe for the double-tap while the dialler
foregrounds), wired at all three real dial sites.

**Built as a DISCRIMINATED UNION, not an `isEmergency` flag**, and that is
load-bearing: every `CallLog` field is WebRTC-derived and the row tap calls
`launchCall({conversationId})` — for an emergency row that resolves no peer and
silently does nothing. The union makes it unrepresentable; the tap MUST be
written separately, and it re-dials.

⚠️ **SOS IS DELIBERATELY NOT LOGGED.** It raises an alert and places no call.
"Emergency call placed" in the call history of a security app when no call
happened is a false record in the one log people consult after an incident. SOS
history is server-side and belongs to `ProtectionHistoryScreen`. A source scan
asserts SOS/Panic screens never call the recorder.

**A scan caught a real bug in the fix within minutes of being written.** The
Calls Log's own re-dial was going unrecorded. My first reading was "correct,
avoid double-counting" — wrong: calling the police again an hour later IS a
second emergency call, and the immediate double-tap it was meant to avoid is
already handled by the store's dedupe. Fixed by making the rule uniform rather
than adding an exception, which also let the scan drop its exception list.

### B-588 — FIXED. The item-12 clipping fix was never ported to ChatScreen

_"The buttons at the top right of the screen is cut off."_ Fixed on
`MessengerHomeScreen` on 2026-08-15 and NOT on `ChatScreen`, which has the
identical shape: a root applying only `insets.top`, a header with a flat
`paddingHorizontal`, and the voice/video buttons last in the row. `ChatScreen`
referenced `insets.left/right` ZERO times.

**Why five days of green suites missed it:** portrait phones have no horizontal
safe-area inset, so `16 + 0` and `16` render identically. It bites only in
landscape or on a side-cutout device — which is also why no render test can see
it, and why the pin is a source scan. `messengerHeaderFit` now covers both
screens.

### B-589 — FIXED. The tier vocabulary was hardcoded in FOUR drifted copies

PDF §13 line 9: _"Admins can choose the names of levels and lateral channels."_
Channel names were already free text. The TIER vocabulary was not — and it was
not one hardcoded list but four, which had already drifted:

| Copy                              | Shape                                            | Keyed on        |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------- |
| `ManageChannelsScreen.LEVEL_NOUN` | `['Enterprise','Main','Sub','Sub-sub']`          | stored `level`  |
| `ChannelEditorScreen`             | the same array, INLINE, for the "becomes …" hint | `level + 1`     |
| `DepartmentChannelsScreen.LEVELS` | `'LEVEL 1 — ENTERPRISE'` …, upper-cased          | 0-based `level` |
| `ChannelTree`'s `Ln` pill         | `L1..L4`                                         | the WALKED tier |

They disagreed ON SCREEN: a row could read "Main" beside an "L2" pill. One
product decision, four copies, visibly wrong — this repo's most-shipped defect
shape.

Now `src/screens/deptchat/levelNames.ts` is the only definition, with a source
scan banning a fifth. Names are stored per-org in `level_names text[]` on the
existing `org_workspace_settings` (migration applied to production 2026-08-20).

⚠️ **PRESENTATION ONLY, and that table's header states the rule that must not
change: "Nothing in this table is read by an authorisation check."** A tier NAME
decides nothing — depth is still governed by `department_channels.level` and its
CHECK, so a rename cannot move a channel, change who sees it, or add a fifth
level. Indexed by DISPLAY tier rather than the stored column, because `level` is
0-based AND its root value differs by tenant (0 for a `root:true` organisation,
1 for every legacy workspace), so naming had to follow what the user SEES.

Empty = built-ins, which is every org today, so it is invisible until used. A
short/sparse array fills the rest from the built-ins (rename L2 alone); an
interior blank is PRESERVED because position is which tier was renamed; an
all-blank array clears back to the defaults, which is what makes clear-to-reset
work without a separate action.

**Four existing scans pinned the literal words** and were re-pointed at the new
contract rather than deleted — they now pin the header FORM and the shared
resolver. A fifth (`Row`'s exact prop destructure) was over-tight and failed on
an unrelated prop; loosened to the coupling it actually protects.

### STILL BLOCKED — and the reasons are not caution

**The `#broadcast` purge is REFUSED BY ITS OWN SECURITY GUARD.** Full dry run
2026-08-20: guard 2 (live invites) 0, guard 3 (children) 0 — but **guard 1 finds
2 PENDING REKEY INTENTS**, on `#broadcast` in orgs `2c13f774…` and `2b8dc53a…`,
both open since 2026-08-05. `channel_membership_intents.channel_id` is ON DELETE
CASCADE, so deleting those channels destroys an un-broadcast rekey instruction —
the thing that stops a removed member keeping the group master key, with up to
30 days of relay dwell still decryptable. Remedy is the migration's own: an admin
device drains them (`listMembershipIntents` → ack), then re-run. **Do not strip
the guard.** Gate 4 is also still unmet (0 replacement announcement channels, 15
of 16 workspaces would be stranded).

**PDF item 11a (back navigation) is NOT fixed, deliberately.** `backBehavior`
stays `firstRoute`. Flipping it to `history` was already reasoned out as harmful
— an unhandled GO_BACK bubbles to the parent navigator and can eject the user
out of the workspace entirely from any of ~26 deptchat screens, turning "leave"
into up to 5 presses. Today's behaviour is correct for every path that exists,
because Home is the only door to Attendance/Incident. It needs the founder's
device repro first; that was the 15-Aug plan's conclusion and it still holds.

### Deploy state

Migrations `20260816000000` (is_lateral) and `org_workspace_level_names` applied
to production. auth-service redeployed TWICE — the second time because the first
deploy predated B-589, so the box was serving code with no `level_names` (0

### B-590 — FIXED (code; DB migration pending approval). Legacy workspace roots cost their trees a visible tier

**Root cause, from LIVE data, not the plan docs.** `department_channels` for
the founder's tree: Okes `level 1, parent_id NULL` (created 2026-07-23, before
the hierarchy existed), Hjt 2, Gjh 3. The Phase-1 migration defaulted every
pre-hierarchy row to level 1, and the CHECK caps levels at 3 — so a tree rooted
in a legacy channel tops out after TWO nestings, one tier short of the PDF's
"exactly four organisational levels". vs2 item 8 RECORDED this as a permanent
asymmetry (§10.6: "their trees top out one tier shallower … that asymmetry is
permanent"); the founder has now overruled it by reporting it as a bug.

**Worse: the button at the cap was a DEAD BUTTON.** `ChannelTree` rendered
"+ Add sub-level" whenever the wiring passed a handler (one function for the
whole tree), and the handler's `manageLevelOf(c) >= 3` guard could only no-op.
A button that renders and silently does nothing IS the founder's "I can't go
further".

**The fix, three layers:**

1. **Migration `20260820120000_promote_legacy_workspace_roots.sql`** — the
   trigger gains ONE narrow allowance (a parentless, non-broadcast, non-lateral
   row may move level 1 → 0; everything else stays frozen — both sides must be
   parentless, so no mid-tree level can ever be lowered through it), then a
   data fix promotes every legacy level-1 workspace root that has children and
   touches descendants generation-by-generation until stored level agrees with
   the trigger's own derivation. WORKSPACE-ONLY (agency #broadcast arithmetic
   keys on the stored level). Collision-safe: a live parented #broadcast
   shifting onto an occupied level (`dept_channels_one_broadcast_per_level`)
   rolls back THAT org only, with a NOTICE — measured on production: 2 of 5
   candidate orgs collide (`608290a3…`, `d83a3403…`); the founder's org
   `88d34848…` shifts clean. Re-runnable after the broadcast purge.
2. **Service** — `createChannel` promotes a legacy level-1 root the moment it
   takes its FIRST structural child (go-forward door: every flat pre-hierarchy
   channel is still a parentless level-1 row). Only while the parent has no
   structural children; best-effort under the unique index (collision keeps
   the level-1 root and the create proceeds with the old capacity).
3. **Client** — `admin.canAddSubLevel` per-node gate on `ChannelTree`: at the
   stored-level cap the row is HIDDEN, never dead. Wired in
   `ManageChannelsScreen` off the same `manageLevelOf(c) >= 3` the handler
   uses.

Pinned by: `department.hierarchyMigration.spec` (new describe — the allowance
is EXACTLY parentless 1→0, tenant gate, collision rollback, `liveSql()` now
resolves to the new file so every existing trigger pin runs against it),
`department.service.spec` (promotes on first structural child / not with an
existing child / not for agency / collision keeps the create), and
`channelTreeInteraction` (canAddSubLevel hides the row).

**Migration APPLIED to production 2026-08-20 with the founder's explicit
approval** (the auto-mode classifier had blocked the first attempt), then
re-applied once more with the review hardenings below. Verified live: the
founder's Okes tree reads 0/1/1/1/2 (the 4th tier is open), only the two
known collision orgs remain level-1-rooted, and zero rows anywhere disagree
with the trigger's derivation.

PDF §03: "branch lines identify parentage" — CONTINUOUS coloured lines from a
