## 2026-08-20 — Founder device batch #2 (B-593..B-595)

Three reports off build 1.0.241. Each root cause was a layer below the symptom,
and two of the three were things the code KNEW and threw away.

### B-593 — FIXED. A `#broadcast` channel in the Messenger chat list

_"in messenger list i can see broadcast that was created in the departmental
chat. it should not be there. no channel there should not be in the messenger
list."_

**The filter was never the problem — the DATA behind it was.** Three surfaces
filter dept channels (`MessengerHomeScreen`, `GroupsScreen`, the forward
picker), all reading `deptConversationIds` / `deptGroupByChannel`. Every id in
those maps came from ONE place: a `listChannels` HTTP response. So whether a
channel stayed out of the list was decided by a race between a local write and a
network round trip — and there was **no local writer at all**.

Meanwhile the code that MINTS the conversation holds the channel id in its hand
and drops it: `provisionOnce` calls `createGroupChat` and never records the
link. The specific trigger the founder hit: `#broadcast` is created
server-side on EVERY channel create, with the org account seeded as `admin`
(so on a personal workspace the founder is a member of their own), and the
admin self-heal sweep in `DepartmentChannelsScreen` provisions every
unprovisioned channel it administers **without navigating to it** — so
`setDeptChannelGroup`, the only writer that ran at mint time, was skipped
entirely. Provision from a sibling tab, switch to Messenger, see `#broadcast`.

Worse, a _permanent_ variant: `registerGroup` is first-writer-wins, and a
losing device keeps its own local group row forever. The Home prune only
touches dashed-UUID ids and dept groups are 32-hex, so nothing ever collects
it.

**Fixed by recording what the minting path already knows** — the minted id
(BEFORE `registerGroup`, so an interrupted provision cannot strand an
unnameable row), the canonical id after a race (the registry is additive, so
recording BOTH is what makes the orphan permanently hideable), the sweep's
`already` branch, and `onGroupLearned` (which previously wrote React state
only, so the id lived for one screen's lifetime). Two more holes closed:
`armDeptConversationRegistry()` sat BELOW MainNavigator's degraded-session
early return, so a claims-only boot never armed at all — moved to the top of
the effect, where it needs neither the ownerKey nor the runtime; and
`GroupsScreen`'s belt was a MOUNT effect, so a channel provisioned while it was
already mounted leaked until the app remounted — now `useFocusEffect`, and it
feeds the persisted registry like Home does.

⚠️ **Deliberately NOT changed: Files and Links.** The audit proposed filtering
dept content there too. Both encode the OPPOSITE decision on purpose — Phase 4
pins that outside the workspace shell the personal Files browser keeps its full
scope with vault actions suppressed, and Links guards the TAP rather than
visibility. My filter broke 6 pinned tests, which is the contract working.
Reverted; the founder's rule is about the chat list.

### B-594 — FIXED. Deleted chats reappear for a fraction of a second

_"whatever chat list we delete, it appears for a fraction of a second when the
backup thing happens — like those mission chats."_

**The delete was COSMETIC.** `removeConversation` deleted the Zustand row and
nothing else: no tombstone, no `notifyBackupRemoved`, no server call — unlike
`removeMessage` beside it, which ships a `status='deleted'` mirror tombstone.
So `conversation_backups` and `messages_backup` kept the conversation in full
(neither has a per-conversation delete endpoint at all), and the restore's
conversation apply re-inserted it. That apply's guard — _"never over a row the
live store already holds"_ — exists to avoid stomping FRESHER state, so a
deliberately-deleted row is precisely the case it waves through.
`upsertConversation` unshifts, so it came back at the TOP of the list.

The FLICKER is the Home screen's server prune removing it again once
`listMine` lands, one network round-trip later. Appear → prune → appear, for
as long as the restore streams. Mission rooms are the clearest repro because
`completeBooking` hard-deletes the membership server-side, so they are the one
class where both the appear side and the disappear side are guaranteed to fire.

**Fixed with a persisted, owner-keyed conversation-tombstone set**
(`conversationTombstones.ts`), modelled on the message-level `restoreTombstones`
it sits beside. Recorded at the single choke point inside `removeConversation`
so no future deleter can forget it; consulted by all four minters (the restore
apply, both group upserts, and `appendMessage`'s shadow-create).

**SUPPRESSION-ONLY, and that is load-bearing** (BACKUP_LOOP §2): the gate is at
the UPSERT, never at the mirror walk. Every mirrored row is still hashed into
the Merkle leaf set (I3) and still recorded in the flush ledger (I7) — filtering
the walk would manufacture `rows_count` drift and re-open the `root_mismatch`
class that shipped five times. Reads FAIL OPEN (I8) and only ids are stored,
never names (I9).

**A tombstone that never lifts would be worse than the bug** — a re-added
mission room, or a peer who messages you after you cleared the thread, would be
permanently invisible. But the sealed-archive replay runs the FULL live receive
path deliberately (audit §12.4), so the receive path cannot tell "a peer just
wrote" from "the restore is handing back what I deleted". The replay now
brackets itself with a counter, so a live arrival lifts the tombstone and a
replayed one is suppressed.

⚠️ **Divergence from the review's I5 advice, on purpose:** the set is NOT
cleared on a backup wipe. A server wipe changes what the BACKUP holds, not what
the USER deleted; clearing would make "wipe the backup, set it up again"
resurrect every deleted chat. The cross-account hazard I5 is really about is
already closed by owner-keying.

**Known and NOT fixed here (recorded, not silently dropped):** the mirror still
GROWS forever, because a conversation delete still ships no `mirrorRemoval`
tombstones and purges no SQLCipher rows. That is "delete means delete" and a
separate, larger change with real I4 drift risk (a `rows_count` shrink is a
hard verifier fail, so removals must travel as tombstone ROWS, never as absences).
The founder's flicker is fixed; the storage growth is not.

### B-595 — FIXED. The call notification outlives the group call

_"whenever group call happened, we end the call, the call thing is still in
notification. be careful, we are touching the notification again."_

Heeded — this area has a long regression history, so the exhaustive artifact
audit came first. It found **two independent causes**, and only one of them is
the foreground service:

1. **The End button never reached the teardown.** `hangup` called
   `call.leave()`, not `endActiveGroupCall` — so the single funnel that owns
   the ring card, the incoming payload, the push notify, the audio session and
   the foreground service ran on NONE of it. The 1:1 stack's End button does
   reach its registry; the group stack's never did.
2. **RNCallKeep's Telecom notification is never ended for group calls.** Both
   group ring lanes call `reportIncomingCall({callId: roomId})` (backgrounded
   `fcmBootstrap`, killed `fcmHeadless`), and the connection service posts its
   OWN ongoing "Bravo Secure call in progress" card that only `reportEnded`
   removes. `reportEnded` had **zero group call sites** — the 1:1 registry ends
   its connection, the group registry never did. So any participant whose ring
   arrived over FCM kept a call notification forever, and no amount of
   foreground-service fixing would have touched it.

And a third, which is why the first fix draft was incomplete: **the release
cleanup was often never REGISTERED.** `if (!markGroupAudioSessionStarted(room))
{return;}` returns before the effect's cleanup closure, so after any
minimize→restore or `joined→reconnecting→joined` round trip (an ordinary ICE
hiccup) the release path simply did not exist. The stranded flag then made the
NEXT call in that room skip its own audio session and foreground service —
the silent no-audio call the registry's own comments warn about. The gate now
guards only the START; the cleanup is always armed.

The release decision moved into a pure `shouldReleaseSharedCallResources`,
because `GroupCallScreen` cannot be imported by a node test — which is exactly
how this survived. It also closes a latent inverse: the old form fell through
and RELEASED when a live entry named a DIFFERENT room, tearing the session and
notification off a newer call. The rule is "is ANY group call live", not "is
the registry pointing at me".

**Preserved deliberately:** the group end still DROPS the incoming payload and
never tombstones it (B-502 — the gateway reuses a roomId across re-rings, and a
tombstone makes a member who left a live call unreachable on the killed-app
lane); the FGS and audio stops stay owner-arbitrated (B-243/B-256); missed-call
banners live in their own id space and survive an end.

### The review rounds caught EIGHT defects in MY OWN fixes

`loadConversationTombstones` was called **only from its test**. Every gate in
that module fails open by design, so an unwired load looks exactly like
"nothing was ever deleted" — the whole B-594 suppression was inert while all 13
behavioural tests passed, because they armed the cache themselves. Now loaded
at runtime boot beside the message tombstones and the blocked-peer cache
(owner-keyed, same as P1-10), and pinned by a source scan that goes RED when
the call is removed. Mutation-verified.

**Round 1 (critic + edge, both Opus) then found seven more**, every one of
them in the remedies rather than the original bugs:

1. **A HOT MIC.** `endActiveGroupCall` returns `'ended'` having cleaned
   NOTHING when the slot is null, and the entry is not published until AFTER
   `getLocalMedia()`. My `hangup` only fell back to `leave()` on `'refused'`,
   so pressing End during the camera-acquire window skipped the leave, left
   `isLeavingRef` unset, and the ~30 boot abort checkpoints never tripped —
   the call went on to join the SFU with a live mic and no screen. The old
   unconditional `await call.leave()` is what used to cancel that boot. Now
   unconditional again, and the in-flight latch is released so a failed pop
   cannot kill the button for the rest of the mount.
2. **An unkeyed End.** `endActiveGroupCall(call.roomId ?? undefined)` degrades
   to "end whatever is live" — the exact form WI-1.5 says is not a
   convenience. Now keyed-only.
3. **A re-added member permanently invisible.** Both group minters used a
   bare `isConversationTombstoned` where they needed `suppressResurrection`,
   and they `return` before `appendMessage` — so nothing downstream could
   ever lift. Re-adding someone to a mission room left them staring at
   nothing until somebody happened to send a message. This is precisely the
   case the tombstone module's own docblock calls worse than the bug.
4. **The remote-end lane was untouched.** `sfu.room.ended` (the HOST hangs
   up) and `sfu.kicked` call `leaveInternal` directly and never reach the
   teardown — so I had fixed the notification for the one person who pressed
   End and nobody else. The artifact cleanup is now a shared
   `clearGroupCallArtifacts(roomId)` called from the teardown, from
   `leaveInternal`'s tail, and from `dismissRing`.
5. **`reportEnded` was in the decline CALLBACK, not the funnel.** Four of the
   five non-accept ring exits (45 s timeout, WS host-cancel, `roomMissing`,
   the FrameCryptor bail) still stranded the Telecom card. Moved into
   `dismissRing`, which the code's own comment already names as the single
   funnel.
6. **An uncatchable iOS throw.** A roomId is 16 random bytes hex, NOT a
   formatted UUID, so on iOS `initWithUUIDString:` yields nil and it reaches
   CXProvider inside a native call no JS try/catch can contain. Android-gated
   (the lanes that raise the connection are Android-only anyway).
7. **A live message could be dropped during a restore.** The replay bracket is
   a global time window and the transport stays live, so a genuine WS
   envelope landing inside one of the replay's awaits read as replayed. The
   store now records WHEN each conversation was deleted, and anything composed
   after that lifts regardless of the bracket — the precise answer the window
   cannot give. Legacy bare-id records load as "deleted at time 0", which
   fails open.

Also from round 1: the Home prune writes durable tombstones on every focus, so
one truncated `listMine` could permanently suppress a live conversation —
server truth now LIFTS a tombstone in the same pass; and my move of the dept
registry arming above the degraded-session early return was REVERTED, because
`setOwner` snapshots the registry into the outgoing owner's slice and an arm
that resolves first writes user B's ids into user A's. The degraded-boot leak
is the lesser evil and is now stated as such in the code.

⚠️ **And the revert itself broke two suites** — I deleted the arming call
instead of moving it back, which `vaultProvenanceForwarding` caught. A third
pin (`groupCallRegistryIdentity`'s `ending` scan) went red because it anchored
on the exact line I had refactored away; the RULE still holds inside the pure
predicate, so the pin was re-pointed at both ends rather than weakened.

**Round 2 then found two more — both in the round-1 remedies**, which is
exactly the class a second round exists for: each one's comment asserted a
property the code did not have.

1. **The new remote-lane cleanup ran AFTER the successor check instead of
   being GATED BY it** — and said it was gated. `rid` is the STALE
   instance's room, and a same-room successor is a documented shape (the
   reconnect-while-minimized path fires the old instance's leave for the same
   roomId when its transports are dead). Ungated, that stale leave would end
   the LIVE call's Telecom connection — taking its "call in progress" card
   and silently disabling `reportAudioRoute` for the rest of the call — clear
   the accept latch, and mark the room's ring consumed, all mid-call to a
   healthy call. Now gated on `gen`, matching the slot null above it.
2. **Releasing `hangupInFlightRef` reversed the guard's own purpose**, stated
   60 lines above it: the second resolution fires `goBack()` from a stale
   navigation prop against an already-popped screen and POPS THE PARENT,
   ejecting the user out of the messenger stack. My reset was speculative
   ("a failed pop shouldn't kill the button") and made the hazard MORE
   likely, because the handler now completes within a tick — an ordinary
   double-tap would land right after it. Reverted to a one-shot latch.

### Known limitations, stated rather than implied fixed

- **B-594 only covers conversations the server no longer lists.** Home's
  `listMine` loop re-upserts every server-listed conversation on every focus,
  so deleting a plain 1:1 was already non-durable and still is. The fix
  covers mission rooms — the reported case — and the tombstone is inert for
  the rest.
- **Tombstones are per-install.** They live in AsyncStorage and are never
  mirrored, so a fresh-install / device-migration restore resurrects deleted
  conversations exactly as before.
- **The compose-time comparison crosses clocks.** `deletedAt` is local
  `Date.now()`; `composedAtMs` is the sender's seal timestamp. A skewed peer
  can make an archived message read as newer than the delete, which lifts the
  tombstone and returns the flicker. Fail-open, no data loss — it degrades to
  the pre-fix behaviour. Tightening it means comparing against the relay
  accept time instead.
- **A genuine group re-add landing INSIDE a restore is dropped** (the create
  carries no per-arrival timestamp, so the bracket wins). Self-heals on the
  next message in that group or the next `listMine`.
- **The stranded audio-session flag still silences the FIRST call after a
  strand.** The cleanup is now always armed so it stops compounding, but the
  start side is unchanged. Separate defect, not fixed here.
- **The backup mirror still grows forever** on a conversation delete — no
  `mirrorRemoval` tombstones, no SQLCipher purge. "Delete means delete" is a
  larger change with real I4 drift risk and is not attempted here.

crypto ×2 (run 1: 3 failures that MOVED to zero on run 2 — the documented

## 2026-08-20 — Call join latency audit (B-596..B-602) — AUDIT ONLY, nothing fixed

_"When we get a call and we accept to join the call or room — 1:1 or group, any kind of
call — it takes time to come into the room and then we can communicate. Why is it so
slow?"_

Full report + the eight step prompts (builder / edge-case agent / critic consensus loop,
Opus 5 for mechanical steps, Fable 5 where the reasoning is the work):
**`docs/audits/CALL_JOIN_LATENCY_AUDIT_2026-08-20.md`**. Five read-only lane tracers +
my own reads + the staging relay log (`docker logs -t bravo-staging-msgr`, UTC) — **no
device measurement today; Step 0 of the plan is the instrumentation that makes one
possible.** Diagnosis in one line: not one bug but a strictly serial chain where the
expensive steps that could run while the phone rings (TURN, PeerConnection build, camera,
`Device.load`, the E2EE key wait) run only after Accept — plus the real defects below.
Staging note: `bravo-staging-msgr` (Up 3 days) predates the uncommitted Phase 6/7 tree —
no `[SFU] join` WI-7.2 lines exist there yet.

### B-596 — FIXED (Step 1, 18a76a98; deployed to staging). The relay bins the caller's first ICE candidates — B-273's server half 🔴 P1 · was LIVE on staging

`handleCallOffer` awaits `privacy.isBlockedEither(...)` (Supabase HTTPS, 60 s cache, **no
timeout**; the M-07 gate added 2026-07-06 `dd8c184a`) BEFORE `trackCallStart`
(`messenger.gateway.ts:1486` → `:1501`). `handleCallIce` → `authorizeCallFrame` → no
session → `{ignore:true}` → silent drop, no log (`:1750-1752`, `:3158-3168`). The client's
B-273 fix (2026-07-26 `93a793c2`) flushes its whole candidate buffer the instant the offer
frame is emitted — so the host/srflx candidates arrive in the SAME TCP read and socket.io
dispatches them while the offer handler is parked. **Staging proof:** cid `30538aee`
2026-08-19 05:21:56 — five `[CALL] ICE` lines at .5814-.5815, the `[CALL] OFFER` line at
.58157, one later candidate survived; cid `e35bd9d0` — three ICE before OFFER. The 80 µs
gap means even a cache HIT loses the burst (microtask vs the synchronous frame loop). The
server log looked identical before and after the B-273 fix because the OFFER line prints
after the await — which is why nobody saw it. Effect: the call connects on later relay
candidates (slower, via TURN), and whether a given call loses its burst is a race between
gathering speed and `buildOfferAuth`+emit time — "sometimes slow". Same class on the group
ring (B-597). **Pin landed this session (DOCUMENTS, passes on current code):**
`apps/messenger-service/src/gateway/messenger.gateway.offer-ordering.spec.ts` — the fix must
flip `['call.offer']` → `['call.offer','call.ice']`. Fix shape = audit Step 1 (register the
session before the first await; hold and flush candidates after the offer forward; keep the
M-07 no-oracle semantics; bound the block-check). Files: `messenger.gateway.ts`,
`users/user-privacy.service.ts`.

### B-597 — FIXED (Step 1, 18a76a98). Group ring fan-out waits on the block-check for ALL targets before the first WS ring ⚠️ P2

`handleSfuRing` awaits `Promise.all(isBlockedEither ×N)` (`messenger.gateway.ts:2445`) before
the first `sfu.ring.incoming` emit; cold = one Supabase HTTPS per target, no deadline
(`user-privacy.service.ts:125-131`). Fix shape: emit cached-clean targets first / bound the
check (audit Step 1 C).

### B-598 — FIXED (Step 3a, 54f1d948). Group TURN fetch has NO ceiling and is awaited before any transport exists 🔴 P1

`useGroupCall.ts:1628` starts `fetchTurnCredentials()` (`:5662-5690`, bare `fetch` via
`fetchWithRefresh`, `api.ts:308-318`); `:2501` `await turnPromise` before `createSendTransport`.

Boot order in `useGroupCall.ts`: `await getLocalMedia` (`:1913`) → `await sfu.join` (`:1997`;
server creates two transports SEQUENTIALLY, `sfu.service.ts:481-482`) → (host) `await

`GroupCallScreen.tsx:288-292, 329`: `InCallManager.start` only when `state==='joined' &&

## 2026-08-20 — Audit Step 1 SHIPPED: the relay's ICE-before-session drop (B-596) + the bounded call-lane block-check (B-597) · consensus loop: 2 rounds (Critic + Edge), dual AGREE

### B-596 — **FIXED** (server). The relay bins the caller's first ICE candidates — B-273's server half

**Fix (`apps/messenger-service/src/gateway/messenger.gateway.ts`):** `handleCallOffer` now
calls `trackCallStart` SYNCHRONOUSLY before its first await and marks the session
`offerPending`; `handleCallIce` HOLDS candidates for such a session (cap 64, drop-oldest —
the client's own `MAX_PENDING_ICE`) and flushes them BEHIND the offer frame once it has been
forwarded (fire-and-forget `forwardToDevice` with `skipOnlineProbe`, the second and last
legitimate site of that flag), or discards them if the offer never reached the callee
(`peer_offline` → the replay lane never carried early candidates either). **An offer-pending
session is NOT LIVE for anything else** (the reviewers' round-1 catch — my first cut guarded
only ICE): answer / media-state / reoffer / reanswer ignore it; a hangup or disconnect inside
the window ENDS it silently (no forward, no `sendCallCancel` "Missed call" push, no artifact
clear — the callee may be a blocked pair and has never heard of the call); after the forward
the session is re-read — a hangup that landed DURING the forward await suppresses the Redis
replay + VoIP wake and, because the offer frame already left, forwards the late `call.hangup`
so the callee does not ring for 45 s; a throwing gate/forward releases the hold
(`clearOfferHold`). A BLOCKED pair is `untrackCallSilently`-ed: no session, no tombstone, so
a retried callId reads as never-seen (no `duplicate_call_id` oracle) — M-07's no-forward /
no-queue / no-wake / no-error contract is byte-for-byte preserved and a WI-7.2
`session …→forgotten src=blocked` line completes the lane.

**Pins (RED-first; inverting the hold turns 6 tests RED):**
`messenger.gateway.offer-ordering.spec.ts` (26: held+flushed in order with ZERO `ICE
ignored` warns, session exists before the first await, post-offer immediate forward,
concurrent in-window duplicate offer, blocked → no trace/no oracle/third-party ignore, every
sibling handler in-window incl. the REAL `handleCallHangup`, hangup during the forward await,
throwing forward releases the hold, peer_offline discard, cap 64, deadline fail-open /
stale-cached-blocked stays blocked / blocked-within-deadline drops, `no_session` marker,
population scan over all 6 `authorizeCallFrame` consumers + the disconnect sweep, static
order pin `trackCallStart` < first `await`); `calls.spec.ts` P1-11 harness carries the real
session map and asserts "no session remains" (not "trackCallStart not called"); the
`skipOnlineProbe` pin allows exactly 2 comment-stripped sites, each on a `call.ice` builder;
`missed-call-ttl.spec.ts` + `ring-lifecycle.spec.ts` harnesses carry the real map / bounded
gate. Client-side acceptance signal after the staging deploy: `[CALL] ICE ignored …
reason=no_session` → 0 for healthy calls, `[CALL] ICE flushed cid= n=` as its counterpart.

### B-597 — **FIXED** (server) with a founder-visible trade-off. Call-lane block-check is DEADLINE-bounded

`privacyGateBounded(a, b, lane)` wraps `isBlockedEither` for the two CALL lanes only (1:1
offer, group ring fan-out per target; messaging / typing / receipt lanes keep the raw await).
`PRIVACY_CALL_GATE_DEADLINE_MS` default **500** (the audit's cold Supabase estimate is
50–300 ms; `0` / non-numeric = unbounded = today). On deadline: **(1)** if this process has
EVER seen a verdict for the pair — even an expired cache entry (`peekBlockedEither`) — that
verdict is used, so a pair once known as blocked STAYS blocked under a Supabase stall; **(2)**
only a never-seen pair fails OPEN, the same outcome the privacy service already returns on a
probe error, bounded to one frame per pair per 60 s because the in-flight lookup keeps
running and warms the cache. Timer is cleared / `unref`'d; the warn names the verdict source.

> **Plain words for the founder (the reviewers asked that this be said, not buried):** before
> this change a slow-but-successful block lookup meant the call simply never went out
> ("fail-closed by hanging"). Now, if the database is slower than 500 ms for a pair this
> relay has never checked, that one ring goes through (WS + push) and the verdict is enforced
> from the next frame on. A person who blocked you can therefore be rung at most once per
> minute and only while the DB is that slow and only if the pair was never seen before. Set
> `PRIVACY_CALL_GATE_DEADLINE_MS=0` on the box to restore the old behaviour. The
> `[CALL] privacy gate deadline lane=… verdict=…` count on staging is the signal — if it
> fires often, the default is wrong, not the design.

### B-603 — pre-existing, NOT FIXED (recorded by the Step 1 reviewers). Two call-lane block oracles

`call.sync` returns `ringing` for an unblocked offer and `unknown` for a blocked one; a retried
callId returns `duplicate_call_id` for an unblocked ringing call and silence for a blocked one.
Both predate Step 1 (the early session does not change them — a blocked pair's session is
untracked with no tombstone exactly as before). Fix shape: answer `call.sync` for the caller's
OWN calls only from a caller-scoped view, and make the duplicate check symmetric; belongs to a
privacy pass, not this latency campaign.

## 2026-08-20 — Audit Step 2 (1:1 client TURN cache + prewarm) — B-601/B-598 client half · 1 review round + 1 fix round, AGREE

**Scope decision (senior call, reviewer-agreed):** shipped **2.1** (the measured 46–76 % win)
and **2.3a**; **DEFERRED 2.2** (pre-build the PC at ring) and **2.4** (a second accept entry
point). 2.2's own spec mandates keeping the build-at-accept path as a fallback, so deferring
the pre-built optimization is safe by construction; its ~10–50 ms / ~1-frame payoff is not
worth the teardown-enumeration + double-fire risk in the B-274/B-319/B-339-scarred accept
code, especially now that 2.1 removed the 150–450 ms TURN chunk. The 2.3 media-parallelization
attempt was reverted after the CALL-N1 adopt test caught a double-camera-open — its correct
residue (single-flight `ensureLocalMedia`) was kept.

### B-601 (client half) — **FIXED**. TURN credentials are cached + pre-warmed for the session

New `src/modules/messenger/webrtc/turnCredentials.ts` is the single source of TURN creds for
the 1:1 (and, after Step 3a, group) paths: `getIceServers({ceilingMs})` returns cached creds
while > 30 min from `expiresAt`, else races a SINGLE-FLIGHT fetch (moved verbatim from
CallScreen — same `X-Signal-Device-Id`, `fetchWithRefresh`, STUN unshift) against the ceiling
and returns STUN-only (never cached) on a miss while the fetch keeps running to warm the cache
for the next call. `prewarmIceServers()` is fired while the phone rings — MainNavigator 1:1
offer handler, group ring handler, AppState-active — and after BOTH voip-wake HMAC verifies in
fcmBootstrap (fg + bg), so a notification answer finds TURN warm. `invalidateIceServers()`
(on signOut) drops the cache AND epoch-fences any in-flight fetch, so a signOut→signIn never
serves the previous user's creds (reviewer P1 — the inflight is stamped with its epoch; a
stale-epoch inflight is discarded and its `.finally` cannot clobber a newer fetch).
CallScreen's raw fetch is gone (it consumes `getIceServers`); `useGroupCall` keeps its own
`fetchTurnCredentials` until Step 3a retires it (interim: a group answer costs one extra warm
— acceptable, same shape).

### B-601 (2.3a) — **FIXED**. getLocalMedia skips the no-op permission round-trip

`getLocalMedia` only calls `PermissionsAndroid.requestMultiple` when `check()` proved a
permission is actually missing — the second-and-later calls no longer await a no-op prompt
round-trip on the accept path. Fails SAFE: if `check()` throws, `pending` seeds to ALL perms
so a first-ever call still prompts (reviewer P1 — never fail open into the B-340 racing-prompt
error). B-340 warns unchanged.

### Latent bug fixed en route — double camera open

`ensureLocalMedia` (useCall) memoised only the RESULT, so two concurrent callers both passed
`if (acquiredMedia)` while the first `getUserMedia` was in flight and opened the camera TWICE
(caught by CALL-N1). Now SINGLE-FLIGHT (memoise the in-flight promise). Strict correctness fix.

**Pins:** `turnCredentials.test.ts` (10 — cache hit / single-flight / ceiling-STUN-not-cached /
failed-fetch-retry / expiry refetch / prewarm / invalidate fence / the cross-user P1;
mutation-proved: removing the epoch fence → RED), `turnPrewarmWiring.test.ts` (5 — CallScreen
holds no raw fetch, prewarm at ≥3 MainNavigator sites + both fcm verifies, signOut invalidate,
single-flight, the brace-balanced permission-guard pin; mutation-proved: reverting the
fail-safe seed → RED). Two shifted source-scan windows widened (escalationRingHandoff
3400→3800, addCallAuditPins AC-3 2600→3200) — ordering assertions unchanged.

**Owed:** device before/after — only the NOTIFICATION lane's `turn:ok` moves materially
(it now precedes the tap); the warm in-app answer already fetched during the ring, so its
delta is small. 2.2/2.4 remain a documented follow-up.

**Deferred → still OPEN under B-601:** 2.2 (pre-built PC at ring), 2.4 (accept from the press
handler). Next free B-604 unchanged (Step 2 claimed no new B-number — it completes B-601's

### 3a.2 — presence broadcast is fire-and-forget (a B-599 slice)

`broadcastGroupCallPresence` (step 10 — a per-recipient pairwise Signal fan-out, HTTP on a cache
miss) was AWAITED before `setState('joined')`; now a `void (async …)()` so "in the room" no
longer waits on work nothing downstream consumes. Pinned by `groupCallHookBoot` "reaches JOINED
even while presence is in flight" (mutation-proof: awaiting a hanging presenceGate hangs the
boot) AND a step-10-anchored source scan (mutation-proof: step-10-only void→await → RED).

## 2026-08-20 — Audit Step 3b.1 (group client: parallel consume) — B-599 slice · 1 review round, dual AGREE

Shipped ONLY 3b.1 (parallel consume of the boot's existing producers); DEFERRED 3b.2 (overlap
the E2EE key wait — touches the S6 fail-closed contract) and 3b.3 (Device pre-warm cache —
additive). File: `useGroupCall.ts` step-9 burst; pins in `groupBootStep3aWiring.test.ts`.

### B-599 (3b.1) — group boot consumes existing producers in PARALLEL

The step-9 boot burst was `for (const ep of existingProducers) { await consumeProducer(ep) }` —
2N sequential WS acks (consume + resume per producer) for N peers, so peer #3's audio waited
behind peer #1's video. Now: sort audio-before-video, then
`await Promise.all(ordered.map(ep => consumeProducer(ep, …, /* batch */ true)))`. mediasoup-client's
awaitQueue serializes the recv.consume SDP munging internally (no corruption) while the WS acks
overlap, and the recv transport's `@connect` (sfu.transport.connect) is a shared connect promise
awaited once. SAFE under the existing dedup: `consumeProducer` skips an in-flight/consumed
producerId (`inFlightConsumes` + `consumedProducerIdsRef`) — the same guards that already cover
the join-iteration vs sfu.new-producer race and the B-482 superseded-transport case; a rejoin
landing mid-burst parks each consume via the attemptGen check exactly as before. `Promise.all`
does not sink siblings on a failure: `consumeProducer` swallows into its retry loop and resolves
(never rejects). Pins: `groupBootStep3aWiring` (Promise.all + audio-first sort + dedup guards
intact; mutation-proved RED on a serial-loop revert). All 35 group suites (520 tests) green,
including groupCallConsumeOrder / attemptGen / rejoinRace / reconcile / recovery.

DEFERRED (stay OPEN under B-599): 3b.2 key-wait overlap, 3b.3 Device pre-warm. Next free B-604.

Reviewer (combined edge+critic, dual AGREE) confirmed the KEY risk from mediasoup source, not the
comment: `ReactNative106.receive()`→`setupTransport()` fires `@connect` inside `if
(!_transportReady)` and sets the flag, so `sfu.transport.connect` runs EXACTLY ONCE across the
burst; the shared `_awaitQueue` drains `recv.consume` SDP tasks strictly serially (no SDP
corruption) while only the WS acks overlap. Non-blocking P2s left OPEN (not defects): (a) no
behavioral concurrency hook test for "a failing consume doesn't sink the others" — safe today by
the no-throw contract of `consumeProducer`, so it is a missing regression pin, folded into the
same B-604 follow-up as the 3a.3 screen test; (b) `Promise.allSettled` would make failure-
isolation structural rather than dependent on the callee never being changed to throw.

## 2026-08-20 — Audit Step 4.1 (group server: parallel transport creates) — B-604 · 1 review round, dual AGREE (edge Opus 5 + critic Fable 5)

Shipped ONLY 4.1 (the join's two WebRtcTransports created concurrently); DEFERRED 4.2 (audio
consumers unpaused), 4.3 (`sfu.consume.batch` endpoint) and 4.4 (join ack carries pre-created
consumers) as a coordinated CLIENT+SERVER follow-up — none is safe/useful to ship server-only.
File: `apps/messenger-service/src/sfu/sfu.service.ts` (`joinRoom`); pins in new
`sfu.service.parallel-transport.spec.ts`.

### B-604 (4.1) — the SFU join creates send+recv transports in PARALLEL

`joinRoom` built the two `WebRtcTransport`s with `sendTx = await create; recvTx = await create` —
two serial mediasoup worker round-trips on the join critical path, the single largest server-side
serial cost of a group join. Now `Promise.allSettled([create, create])`, assign each fulfilled
value, then `throw` the first rejection into the UNCHANGED rollback catch (closes both, rolls back
the WI-6.4 `pendingJoins` reservation, hands off / clears a claimed host per KO-6/B-566). ~2 worker
RTT → ~1.

**allSettled, NOT Promise.all — a real leak, not a style choice.** With `Promise.all`, a one-sided
rejection rejects the combinator WHILE THE OTHER CREATE IS STILL IN FLIGHT; that transport then
resolves to a live `WebRtcTransport` that is never assigned to `sendTx`/`recvTx` and never closed —
its ICE ports + FDs leak on the router until the whole room closes. That is the exact leak the
original ordered sequential close was written to prevent; allSettled captures BOTH outcomes so the
catch can close whichever succeeded. Every WI-6.4/KO-3..6 invariant is untouched (the cap check,
reservation, host election/handoff, the KO-5 post-transport re-check, the observability tx.on loop
all run exactly as before — only the two awaits fused into one settle).

Pins (`sfu.service.parallel-transport.spec.ts`, mutation-proved):

- parallelism — with a hanging factory, BOTH creates are dispatched before either resolves
  (MUTATION serial `await;await` → RED, only one call after the first tick).
- leak-free close, both directions — one create rejects, the sibling that resolved has `close()`
  called + the reservation rolled back (MUTATION naive `Promise.all` → RED, the resolved sibling
  leaks). The serial mutation ALSO reds the recv-succeeds case (serial never creates recv when send
  fails), which is the parallel-specific "close the winner" property.

Gates: `sfu.service.join-cap` 14 (all WI-6.4/KO concurrency cases) + new pins 3 green; full
messenger-service **53 suites / 694 tests green**; service `tsc --noEmit` clean; mobile typecheck
unaffected (server-only). **Staging deploy DONE 2026-08-21** (tar overlay, `bravo-staging-msgr` healthy, /healthz 200, compiled dist carries `allSettled`) — the `[SFU]`
join + tx.ice/tx.dtls duration lines from Step 0 are the evidence.

### DEFERRED under B-604 (coordinated client+server follow-up, stay OPEN)

- **4.2 audio consumers UNPAUSED** — the round-trip saving only lands when the CLIENT stops sending
  `sfu.consumer.resume` for audio (a client step). Server-only it changes when the first audio RTP
  arrives relative to the client's FrameCryptor/E2EE decryptor attach — a security-adjacent media-
  path ordering that needs the Critic's explicit blessing, not a solo ship. mediasoup fact recorded
  for the follow-up: `Consumer.resume()` ALWAYS issues a worker request (Consumer.js:165) — old-
  client resume-on-unpaused is idempotent/safe but NOT a free no-op, so the audit's "no-op" phrasing
  is imprecise.
- **4.3 `sfu.consume.batch` endpoint** — a new WS event needs a `WS_PAYLOAD_SPECS` entry + rate-limit
  - guard test AND a feature-detect handshake (`capabilities:{consumeBatch:true}` in the join ack)
    so old/new clients negotiate. Useless until a client calls it — Step 3b.1 shipped client parallel
    consume over the EXISTING per-producer `sfu.consume`, which already overlaps the WS acks. A server
    endpoint no client invokes is dead code; ship it WITH its client consumer.
- **4.4 join ack carries pre-created consumers** — audit-flagged "only if the Critic agrees"; couples
  join to consume. Deferred by default.

Next free B-605.

## 2026-08-20 — Audit Step 5 (notification / killed lanes, device-independent half) — B-602 + B-601 wake-lane · 2 review rounds (critic OBJECT R1: vacuous epoch pin + missing sqa record, both test/doc-side → fixed → R2), dual AGREE (edge + critic, Fable 5)

Step 5 is HIGH-risk and its core (5.2/5.4/5.6/5.7 boot reorderings) is **prerequisite-gated on Step
0's killed-lane device numbers**, which were NOT captured (5555 logged out) and device-verify is
deferred (founder). Shipped the two device-INDEPENDENT items justified by already-measured numbers /
a defined bug; DEFERRED the number-gated reorderings (shipping a boot reorder blind is the B-125
trap). Files: `callFrameRouter.ts`, `groupCallRingDispatcher.ts`, `productionRuntime.ts` (buffer
gate), `fcmHeadless.ts`; pins in `callFrameRouter.test.ts`, new `groupRingDepsReadyBypass.test.ts`,
`turnPrewarmWiring.test.ts`.

### B-602 (5.8) — group RING frames now bypass the depsReady buffer like 1:1 call frames

On a cold boot, `productionRuntime`'s `onFrame` buffers every frame behind `depsReady` (the
SQLCipher hydrate) EXCEPT 1:1 call frames (`isCallFrame`). Group ring frames (`sfu.ring.*`) were
NOT exempt, so the B-479 restore-mode park/ack lane waited out the whole hydrate (seconds on a long
thread) while 1:1 calls rang through. Fix: the buffer gate now also exempts `isGroupRingFrame`.
SAFE because `dispatchGroupRingFrame` only navigates / dedups / acks — it touches NONE of the
SQLCipher deps the buffer guards (verified by reading it: no sqlMessages/txnDb/seenEnvelopes/
appendMessage). `sfu.ring.missed` is deliberately NOT a ring frame here (it writes a missed-call
bubble via appendMessage → needs the store → stays buffered). **Behavior change worth naming
(edge review N2):** pre-B-602 a live WS ring landing in a handler gap (pre-sign-in / headless boot)
was BUFFERED and could land on the post-hydrate drain; now the WS copy is dispatched immediately,
so if no handler is registered yet it is not re-buffered — recovery leans on the B-479 reconnect
replay + the FCM rescue copy of the same ringId (exactly the WI-3.6/B-479 contract). In the UI lane
the ring handler registers in the SAME MainNavigator mount flush as `configureMessengerRuntime`
(declared as an earlier effect, so configure runs first), before the socket handshake can
complete — so the realistic gap is headless/pre-auth where FCM was always authoritative. The Phase-5 epoch gate
(`if (!isOurEpoch()) return`) still runs BEFORE the buffer gate, so an out-of-epoch ring is dropped,
never fast-pathed. Single source of truth: `GROUP_RING_FRAME_EVENTS` moved to the pure
`callFrameRouter` module (eager-importable, unit-testable — the same home as `isCallFrame`, which is
why the predicate lives there and not in the lazy-required dispatcher) and is re-exported from
`groupCallRingDispatcher` for its existing consumer, so the buffer-bypass eligibility and the
dispatch routing can NEVER drift. Pins: `callFrameRouter.test.ts` (isGroupRingFrame membership +
`sfu.ring.missed`/room-scoped/1:1 excluded + an identity drift-guard that the dispatcher's set IS
the callFrameRouter one) and `groupRingDepsReadyBypass.test.ts` (source scan: the gate exempts BOTH
predicates; the epoch gate precedes it — anchored to `onFrame:` per edge review N1 so it is NOT
vacuous, mutation-proved RED on deleting the onFrame epoch gate). The two bypass pins are
mutation-proved (gate→isCallFrame-only RED; re-inlined set RED).

### B-601 (5.1) — the KILLED-app headless voip-wake lane now warms TURN

The prewarm was wired at the ring / group-ring / foreground / both fcmBootstrap voip-wake lanes
(Step 2) but NOT in the headless slim handler (`fcmHeadless.ts`) — the truly-killed lane. Now, the
moment a voip-wake passes HMAC verify (and before the incoming-call cache seed that presents the
ring), it fires `prewarmIceServers()` fire-and-forget, so the Answer tap's `getIceServers` is a hit
instead of a fresh fetch on the answer critical path (measured 164-442 ms of the caller's
launch→offer, TURN off the path). Same-process only (a reaped VM loses the cache; the UI boot path
re-fetches as the fallback) and best-effort (a failed fetch caches nothing — turnCredentials
contract). Pin: `turnPrewarmWiring.test.ts` (warm AFTER the `voip-wake DROPPED` verify, BEFORE
`setIncomingCallPayload`; mutation-proved RED on removal).

### DEFERRED (device-number-gated / UI — stay OPEN)

- **5.2 call-lane-first boot** (move call-irrelevant awaited loads after the socket open) — a
  productionRuntime boot reorder; each move must be justified by the Step 0 lane number that shows
  it on the critical path. No number → the B-125 trap. Respects `stashDrainGateParity`'s drain gate.
- **5.6 pre-boot on voip-wake** (run the bounded headless drain so the socket + offer replay are
  cached before the tap) — the big one; needs the measured "tap→ws→SDP" split to justify, and the
  B-331/B-354/B-352 hazards. Deferred.
- **5.7 route the initial notification earlier** (out from behind the configure effect +
  runAfterInteractions) — boot-order reorder, number-gated; keep B-479/B-481 park + explicitAcceptIds.
- **5.4 lean-runtime decision** — a "decide with numbers" spec task, not a code change.
- **5.3 killed-lane progress text** — UI only; needs DESIGN_REVIEW_LOOP + a screen test; low priority.

Gates: messenger-crypto 6654 green (run 1; run 2 also 6654 green); app messenger screens 611; typecheck

## 2026-08-21 — B-605: deleted chats resurrect on a FRESH-INSTALL restore (completes B-594) · 2 reviewers, dual AGREE

Founder: "when the backup happened it restored all the chat — like mission chats we deleted came
back for a couple of minutes then went away." B-594 made the conversation-tombstone CODE correct
(4 minters + the restore apply at `restoreMessages.ts:886` consult `isConversationTombstoned`), but
the tombstone DATA lived ONLY in per-install AsyncStorage (`messenger.deletedConversations.v1:`),
never in the backup. A fresh-install / device-migration restore (uninstall→reinstall→restore, the
normal trigger) boots with an EMPTY set → every guard fails open → every deleted conversation is
re-minted. The "couple of minutes then gone" is `MessengerHomeScreen` `listMine` pruning the
server-UNLISTED rooms (completed missions / removed depts); server-LISTED rooms stay resurrected.
This was the documented B-594 known limitation (sqa.md ~22050).

### The fix (Option B — a `deleted` flag rides the conversation_backups round-trip)

Mirrors the proven message `status='deleted'` H-3 pattern, since Android wipes all app storage on
reinstall (no client-only fix exists). Migration
`supabase/migrations/20260821000000_conversation_backups_deleted.sql` =
`ALTER TABLE conversation_backups ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`.

- **Server** (`backup.service.ts`): `putConversations` groups rows by COLUMN SIGNATURE so `deleted`
  (and `group_state`) are omit-if-absent — a bare/legacy mirror never clobbers a stored `true`; only
  an explicit `true`/`false` writes (the same BUG-M/B-178 mechanism). `getConversations` selects +
  returns it, fail-open (`Boolean(r.deleted ?? false)`). Round-8 legacy-column fallback preserved.
- **Client**: `backupClient` shapes carry `deleted?`; `messengerStore.removeConversation` (the single
  B-594 choke point) captures the row before the commit and mirrors `{deleted:true}` AFTER it
  (`notifyBackupConversationDeleted`); a LIVE mirror sends `deleted:false` (re-add clears the flag);
  `restoreMessages` arms ids-where-deleted into the tombstone set via
  `armDeletedConversationsFromRestore` BEFORE the apply at :886 (covers BOTH the streaming and the
  Merkle-background restore lanes). The existing `isConversationTombstoned` guard then suppresses.

### The LIFT is preserved (a delete must not be permanent)

Three independent lifts, all intact: a live `mirrorConversation(deleted:false)` on re-add clears the
server flag; `MessengerHomeScreen` `listMine:247` `clearConversationTombstone` for any server-listed
room; `suppressResurrection`'s compose-time-after-delete rule (the arm uses deletion-time 0, so any
genuine arrival lifts). A per-device delete is intentionally not durable while another device holds
the room live (the module's documented "server truth lifts" model).

### BACKUP_LOOP I1-I9 (both reviewers CONFIRMED)

Message Merkle/ledger byte-identical (conversations are a SEPARATE table/lane — the message flush,
`setMerkleCommitPending`, `recordFlushedVersions`, `scheduleMerkleHook` have ZERO hunks; verified by
the full backup/merkle suite 26 suites/175 green). Suppression at the UPSERT only, never the mirror
walk (I3/I7). Fail-open I8. Ids/boolean only, no name/plaintext/`signature` (I9). Owner-keyed I5.
`verifyMerkleCommit` untouched.

### Pins (RED-first, mutation-proved)

- `restoreStreamingWalk.test.ts` — a `deleted:true` row is NOT re-created on a fresh-install restore
  (RED when the restore-arm is disabled; the resurrected row reappears — mutation-proved on the
  shared executing path of both restore lanes).
- `conversationDeleteMirror.test.ts` (NEW) — the WRITE half: `removeConversation` ships
  `mirrorConversation(owner, conv, undefined, {deleted:true})` after the commit (RED when the
  delete-mirror call is removed) — the critic's pre-merge ask, so neither half can regress green.
- `backup.conversations.spec` (+6) — true/false written, absent omitted, signature split, get
  selects + defaults false. `mirrorConversationLane` — a live row carries `deleted:false`.

### DEPLOY ORDER (critic Finding 4 — HARD): migration → messenger-service → APK

An OLD server 400s the new `deleted` field (`forbidNonWhitelisted`), and the client maps 400 →
non-retryable → the WHOLE conversation lane (incl the `group_state`/master-key mirror) drops for the
skew window. So: apply the migration, deploy messenger-service (staging AND prod before a prod APK),
THEN ship the client build.

### Residuals (non-blocking, sqa-noted)

- Kill between delete and mirror flush → the flag never reaches the server; a fresh-install restore
  resurrects that ONE room. Same-install still protected by the local tombstone. Narrow, strictly
  better than pre-fix.
- blockPeer-rollback flag-flap: a failed block rolls back via `upsertConversation(snapshot)` but
  `mirrorBootstrap.prevConvVersions` still holds the pre-delete hash, so an identical-hash re-add
  fires no `deleted:false` and nothing clears the local tombstone; heals at the next boot sweep /
  listMine. Cheap follow-up (mirror false + clearConversationTombstone in the rollback branch).
- `deleted=true` rows are never purged (count against the H-11 cap) + delete-mirror can upsert
  local-only ids — the module already defers mirror-purge.
- Deleted-conv-WITH-messages restore is handled by code (`hydrateMessages` never mints a parent
  row) but not yet pinned by a test — follow-up assertion.

Review: edge (Opus) + critic (Fable), dual AGREE; both re-ran the gates. Next free B-607
(B-606 = the keyboard K4 fix).

## 2026-08-21 — B-606: system emoji keyboard hides the composer (K4) · 2 review rounds, dual AGREE (edge Opus + critic Fable)

Founder (screenshot, a channel chat): opening the emoji keyboard leaves the text box invisible —
blank area above a light system emoji keyboard. Affects 1:1, group, AND departmental chat.

### Root cause (documented residual K4, sqa.md ~9133)

Under mandatory edge-to-edge, `windowSoftInputMode=adjustResize` is inert, so the composer's
position above the keyboard comes ENTIRELY from `useKeyboardLayout`'s `overlap` (bottomPad). That
overlap is driven by RN `Keyboard.addListener('keyboardDidShow')`, which on Android fires ONLY on a
visibility TRANSITION. Tapping the system keyboard's own emoji key resizes the IME in place
(letter→emoji pad, taller) with NO hide/show — so no event fires, `overlap` stays frozen at the
shorter letter height, and the taller emoji pad draws OVER the composer. Not the app's dark inline
emoji panel (that has no search bar) — the screenshot is the light SYSTEM keyboard. All three
surfaces share `useKeyboardLayout`, so all three reproduce.

### The fix — `react-native-keyboard-controller` as a WindowInsets source (founder-approved dep)

Added `react-native-keyboard-controller@1.22.4` + `<KeyboardProvider navigationBarTranslucent
statusBarTranslucent>` at App.tsx root. Inside `useKeyboardOverlap`, a `useKeyboardHandler.onEnd`
worklet → `runOnJS` → feeds the height into the overlap. The controller reads the IME height off
`WindowInsetsAnimation`, so `onEnd` fires on EVERY settle — first open, hide, AND an in-place resize.

- **Env-independent** (critic Finding 1 fix): under translucent bars the controller reports the FULL
  covered band = the overlap directly. New pure `keyboardControllerOverlap(fullHeight, windowHeight,
prev)` clamps it to the window with NO `barBand` — deliberately NOT routed through
  `computeKeyboardOverlap` (which would re-inject the JS `safeBottom` sampled at event time and, if
  pre-settle, leave a permanent gap — the B-252 trap inverted). The raw full height is stored in
  `kcFullRef`; the env-settle effect re-CLAMPS from it, never re-barBands.
- **Close/implausible** (Finding 2): 0 → overlap 0 (nulls kcFullRef → RN fallback); an implausible
  cold-start reading (B-277 5dp) → RETAINS `prev` (never a truthy-zero, never drops the composer);
  kcFullRef is set only for a plausible height.
- **Android-only** (Finding 5): the callback early-returns on iOS — iOS already re-fires
  `keyboardWillShow` on a type-swap and carries the `screenY` the undocked-iPad branch needs.
- The RN listener + reseed + learned-height + `computeKeyboardOverlap` are UNCHANGED (the source when
  kcFullRef is null; iOS + Android fallback). For a normal open both sources compute the same overlap
  (`(imeInsets−navBar)+safeBottom == imeInsets == the controller's full band`), and the 4dp noise
  floor absorbs the echo — verified from BOTH libraries' native sources (no thrash, single-fire per
  transition).

### Departmental in-app emoji ALSO fixed (critic Finding 3 / "for all incl departmental")

DepartmentChatScreen still used the pre-B-281 MODAL `<EmojiPicker>` that covered the composer (the
exact bug B-281 removed from ChatScreen). Ported to the inline `<EmojiKeyboard>` in the padded
composer column, `Keyboard.dismiss()` on open, search bar dropped — which also moots the
KeyboardProvider→Modal `ADJUST_NOTHING` concern for that surface.

### Pins (mutation-proved)

- `useKeyboardLayout.test.tsx` — `keyboardControllerOverlap`: full band is the overlap; taller emoji
  > letter; close → 0; implausible → retain prev (RED without the plausibility guard).
- `keyboardContract.test.ts` — (a) the rule module subscribes to keyboard-controller's
  `useKeyboardHandler` (RED if removed); (b) the onEnd→runOnJS→applyOverlap(keyboardControllerOverlap)
  seam FEEDS the overlap (RED on the gutted `useKeyboardHandler({}, [])`); (c) no 2nd consumer under src/.
- `emojiSheetLifecycle.test.ts` — dept now inline (no modal), Keyboard.dismiss on open.
  Gates: keyboard 95, app screens+keyboard+emoji 706, typecheck 46≤47.

### DEVICE watch-list (owed — Firebase build; keyboard-controller is a NATIVE module, needs a rebuild)

1. controller `onEnd` fires on the MIUI system keyboard's letter→emoji in-place swap (Redmi + stock
   Gboard). 2. translucent-height parity: no 24/48dp jump at open-settle on gesture AND 3-button nav.
2. B-277 first-open after cold start reports truth, not garbage. 4. no stuck gap (Finding 1 window).
3. Modal+TextInput sweep (KeyboardProvider forces `ADJUST_NOTHING` on modals — should be fine given
   edge-to-edge + useKeyboardLayout, kc reroutes; verify). 6. iPhone smoke.

Review: 2 rounds — edge (Opus) AGREE R1; critic (Fable) OBJECT R1 (7 findings) → all fixed → dual AGREE R2 (+ behavioral seam pin, parity pin, stale-comment nit closed).

## 2026-08-21 — B-607 / B-608: the Files album "copy", and Profile's missing Workspaces row

Founder, two screenshots, same session. Both are CONSISTENCY defects, not data defects — the
stores were correct in both cases and the suites were green throughout.

### B-607 — "moving files into a folder only creates a duplicate, it doesn't move them" · FIXED

Reported once before as B-451 (2026-08-15) and fixed then; the founder saw it again because the
_visible outcome_ never changed. Nothing is copied and nothing ever was: `assignments` is
single-valued (`itemId -> albumId`), so one file cannot hold two albums, and
`filesAlbumMoveIntegrity` (B-451/B-452, 18 tests) was green the whole time.

**Root cause — the view, not the move.** `FilesScreen`'s default is `albumFilter === undefined` =
**All**, and All lists every file whatever its album (`FilesScreen.tsx`, the `visible` memo). So:

1. select files → the AlbumBar is HIDDEN in selection mode, removing the only "which album am I in"
   signal;
2. pick a destination → the assignment is written correctly;
3. selection ends → back on **All**, where the rows sit exactly where they were, now carrying the
   destination's name.

Indistinguishable from "it copied them in and left the originals". The count never changes.

The real defect is a FOLDER affordance (folder-with-arrow icon, "move into a folder") driving LABEL
semantics. In a folder model, moving something out of the current view removes it from that view;
"All" is not a folder, so nothing leaves.

**Fix:** the move now FOLLOWS into the destination — `setAlbumFilter(albumId)` at both move sites
(the destination picker, and create-album-from-selection, which had the same dead end). Pinned by
`B-607 — a completed move lands the list IN the destination album`, mutation-proven RED with the
one line removed. The `AlbumBar` mock now renders its `active` prop so the assertion can see which
album the list is showing (the bar mounts outside selection mode — the state a completed move
returns to). Gate: app messenger screens 612/45 suites; filesAlbumMoveIntegrity 19/19.

### B-608 — SWITCH DASHBOARD shows four rows in the drawer and three on Profile · FIXED

Founder, side-by-side screenshots: `ProfileDrawerModal` lists Messenger / Secure Services / Virtual
Bodyguard / **Workspaces**; `settings/ProfileScreen`'s copy of the same section lists only the three
products. One menu, two answers, depending on how it was opened.

**Root cause.** The row was only ever built inside the drawer and handed to
`SwitchDashboardSection` as `extraRow` MARKUP, so a second host could not render it without copying
the derivation. `ProfileDrawerModal` already carried a warning that the row is drawn twice and the
copies must be kept in step — a third hand-written copy would have made drift a certainty.

**Fix:** `useWorkspaceSwitchRow` owns the derivation once (affiliated → Workspace Hub, labelled
"Workspaces"; otherwise "Channels", dimmed without the entitlement, tap still runs the resolver so a
printed induction code is never a dead row). Hosts differ only in how they LEAVE, so that is the
hook's single parameter: the drawer is a modal and must animate out first (220 ms), Profile is a
full screen and navigates immediately. `SwitchDashboardSection` gains `extraRowData`, drawing the
row with the product rows' own styling so the two hosts cannot drift visually; the drawer keeps
passing markup because `drawerItem18` pins it, and data wins over markup so no host can render the
row twice.

## 2026-08-22 — B-623: news/Bravo Intel could not be shared into a workspace channel · 1 review round (critic DISAGREE → fixed → green), builder + adversarial critic

**Client ask.** "The Bravo Intel / news items are shareable to the chat list, but they should be
shareable to departmental chat as well — any workspace, any thread." Asked whether it was built.

**It was NOT built, and the exclusion was deliberate — which is why this needed design, not a
one-liner.** `ShareNewsSheet` reused `ForwardList` (ChatScreen's forward picker), which excludes
department channels outright. That exclusion is the F7 fix: a channel is stored as an ordinary
`type:'group'` row, `sendText` fans a sealed envelope to EVERY member, and the generic picker has no
channel id, no roster and no role, so it cannot evaluate whether the caller may post. Simply listing
channels there would have reopened the hole.

**Fix — a SECOND door that carries the check the first one cannot.** `ForwardList` is untouched
(its F7 pin stays green); channels get their own picker built on the channel DTOs, which DO carry
`my_role`:

- **`shareChannelTargets.ts` (pure):** `shareWorkspaceGroups()` → workspace groups (level 1) each
  holding its channels depth-first (level 2), reusing `nestParentedBroadcasts`/`directoryBuckets`/
  `subtreeOf` from `organisationTree.ts` (a second copy of the grouping rule is banned, and the rule
  is subtle — a masked `parent_id` makes "no parent" ambiguous). Every row is marked `postable` +
  `blockedReason` ('read_only' | 'not_active') BEFORE the UI sees it; a sweep bucket guarantees no
  channel is unreachable.
- **The predicate is `my_role === 'admin'`, and only that.** Verified end-to-end rather than assumed:
  the server seeds membership with `memberRoleFor(postMode) = postMode === 'open' ? 'admin' : 'viewer'`
  (`department.service.ts:791`), `listChannels` and `listMembers` both serve the same
  `department_channel_members.role` column, and every writer routes through `memberRoleFor` except
  two fenced by `assertBroadcastPostingAllowed`. Re-deriving from `post_mode` would be a drifting
  second copy.
- **The gate is at the WRITE, not the list.** `sendToChannel` re-fetches `listMembers` and obeys it
  via the pure `allowShareToChannel()`; a 4xx is an ANSWER (refuse — `listMembers` 403s for a
  non-member), only a transport failure falls back to the cached role, which is what
  `DepartmentChatScreen.send()` does. A disabled row is an affordance, never the boundary (A4).
- It also refreshes `participants` from that same roster call before sending — `sendText` fans out to
  the LOCAL row, so a member who joined since this device last opened the channel would otherwise be
  silently missed while the user saw "Shared".

**The critic round earned its keep (verdict DISAGREE, 2 × P1 + 5 × P2, all fixed):**

- **P1 the pins were decorative.** Three named mutations stayed GREEN: the drill-in handler made a
  no-op (the client's entire ask, pinned by nothing — the `accessible={false}` lesson repeating), the
  open/close reset deleted, and — worst — `allowed = canPostToChannel(data) || t.postable`, which
  leaves every ordering assertion passing while making the server re-check a **no-op**. Fixed by
  extracting the two levels into `ShareChannelPicker.tsx` (imports only React Native → RENDER-tested,
  13 cases) and the decision into pure `allowShareToChannel` (behaviour-tested). Both mutations
  re-run afterwards and are now RED.
- **P1 Android nested ScrollView.** The root view wrapped `ForwardList` (which brings its own
  `ScrollView`, no `nestedScrollEnabled`) in another `ScrollView` — on Android nested scrolling is OFF
  by default, so chats past ~6 rows would have been UNREACHABLE: a regression of the already-shipped
  share-to-chat path. The workspace list is now a plain header block above it; the level-2 list sets
  `nestedScrollEnabled`.
- **P2s fixed:** broadcast/announcement channels were all landing in "Other channels" instead of under
  their workspace (`placeRow` classifies them separately so `subtreeOf` never emits one) — now run
  through `nestParentedBroadcasts` exactly as the member directory does, with fixtures; 403-vs-offline
  split; roster refresh; double-tap interlock moved to a ref; the file-wide `not.toMatch(/post_mode/)`
  scoped to the callback (an inverted version of the absence-scan trap); dead filter removed.
- **Verified clean by the critic (do not re-litigate):** the `{isGroup:true}` write shape; a device
  with no group master key fails CLOSED inside `runWithGroupAdminLock` and the runtime fires its own
  `requestGroupKeyResync`; `enforcePosters` cannot filter the shared story out (the sender was just
  proven an admin); grouping totality/cycles; `'__loose__'` cannot collide with a uuid.

Gates: app 2703, crypto ×2, typecheck 45 (baseline 47), eslint 0 errors, 3 mutations proved RED.
**DEVICE-OWED:** the drill-in on a real workspace, a share landing in a channel, and the Android
chats-list scroll.
