## 2026-08-22 — Client device batch (B-624..B-631) · builder + 2 read-only investigations, 1 stalled-agent recovery

**Task.** Six screenshots from the founder in one pass, plus "the app is a little bit slow, can you find
out and fix something". Logged together because they shipped as one change set.

**B-624 — FIXED. Different organisations' channels rendered in ONE flat list.**
"Service Providers" / "ABC Security" (Jacques' org) sat as siblings of "BAG" (the user's own workspace).
ROOT CAUSE was not the tree: the org scope (`activeWorkspaceOrgParam` / `scopeChannelsToActiveWorkspace`)
is fail-open and NO-OPS whenever no workspace context is set — and `activeWorkspace` is SESSION-ONLY,
written in just four places (hub tile, invite accept, notification adopt, ejection reconciler). So every
cold boot and every entry that is not the Workspace Hub asks the server with no `orgId`, and the server
returns every channel the caller is a member of, across tenants. The tree stage then never read `org_id`
at all, so `placeRow` called three roots from two tenants "organisations". Fix: `orgSectionsOf` in
`organisationTree.ts` — the ONLY thing in that module that reads `org_id`, because a second copy of the
grouping rule is banned by `organisationTreeSingleSource` — then one tree per section, with an org header
rendered only when there is more than one. Fail-open by construction: rows with no `org_id` share one
section rather than disappearing, and a single-tenant user gets exactly one section and no new chrome.

**B-625 — FIXED. No way to find a channel.** A search field under the stat row, where the founder drew it.
FILTERING A TREE IS NOT FILTERING A LIST: a match drags its ANCESTORS in (else the hit hangs off nothing
and `buildChannelTree` never walks to it) _and_ its SUBTREE (else `directoryBuckets`' `collapseChildless`
re-classifies a matched organisation as a plain chat row — the same row redrawn without its level pill,
purely because you typed its name). Matched branches force-expand: a hit inside a collapsed parent is the
same as no hit. A blank query returns the INPUT ARRAY IDENTITY, so the unsearched screen keeps every
`useMemo` identity it had.

**B-626 — FIXED. The emergency quick-dial card was too heavy.** Founder: make it like the "Links" menu.
The inline card is gone; the Calls header now has an **Emergency** door beside **Links** that opens the
full Emergency Services page VBG already has (every country + search). Registered in the messenger AND
agency stacks — an unregistered route is the N2 dead tap — and the page suppresses the VBG product footer
outside its own stack, where those tabs would be three dead taps.

**B-627 — FIXED. The Channels tab jumped inside one workspace.** Founder: "it should go to the workspace
interface where all the workspaces are listed." It now lands on `WorkspaceHub` — which is ALSO what sets
the org context B-624 defends against, so the two fixes compose. Resolved, not assumed: a shell without
the hub falls back to the previous exit-hop rather than dying. `WorkspaceHub` registered in the agency
shell too.

**B-628 — FIXED. The share picker was one undifferentiated pile, with no avatars.** Founder asked for
three sections: workspace, individual, group. `ForwardList` now emits INDIVIDUALS and GROUPS (order within
each unchanged), 1:1 rows show the peer's photo with the initials disc as the FALLBACK, and the picker's
channel list draws the same branch/elbow rails as the channel tree (`treeGuides`, derived from the depth
sequence, pure and tested). The sheet's own "CHATS" header was dropped — it would have been a fourth,
redundant heading.

**B-629 — FIXED. The MESSENGER wordmark collapsed to "M…".** The header row is avatar + mark + title +
tier chip + three action pills, and only the title could shrink, so it was the one that ellipsised — worst
with the back chevron present. Now: shrink-to-fit before ellipsis (floored, so it degrades to smaller
rather than unreadable — the ObsidianTabBar remedy), tighter type (18→16px, less tracking), and the
decorative message glyph yields whenever the chevron shows, which is exactly the crowded case. The item-12
pin was RE-POINTED, not relaxed, plus two new pins.

**B-630 — FIXED. The "Modules on Home" sheet was see-through.** It used `OB.card` = `rgba(22,27,37,0.72)`
— correct for a card sitting ON the page, wrong for a sheet FLOATING over one, so the Home cards read
straight through the copy. Now opaque + elevated, matching every sibling sheet in the module (already
`#0C1017` / `#10141C`); this one was the outlier.

**B-631 — PARTIALLY FIXED (measured, not guessed). "The app is a little slow."**
CLAUDE.md records eight MEASURED dead ends, so none of them was re-proposed. The investigation went
straight at the one lead that file names but never chased — the per-send backup work — and found it:

- `mirrorBootstrap` diffs conversations with **NO reference guard at all**, so `convVersion`
  (JSON.stringify + FNV) ran for EVERY conversation on EVERY store commit — including commits that touch
  no conversation: typing indicators, presence ticks, draft writes. Cost grows with chat count, forever.
- The message loop re-hashed every row of a changed list (~200 `JSON.stringify`, body included) to find
  the one that moved — and a group send mints one commit per recipient leg, so tens of times per post.
- `useRegisteredNames` (mounted in `MainNavigator`, i.e. always) selected the whole `conversations` map,
  which `appendMessage` replaces per message — so the ROOT NAVIGATOR re-rendered several times per
  message, app-wide.

Fixes: object-identity guards on both diff loops — the trick the array loop one line above already uses;
immer replaces changed paths, so `m === last` proves nothing changed and `messageVersion` is pure over
`m` — plus a steady-state-only narrowing of the hook. **A first cut of that last one broke the documented
"a failed fetch retries on the next conversations change" contract** (muting a chat does not change WHICH
peers are unresolved), so the broad subscription is KEPT while anything is pending and narrows only once
every name is resolved. Both halves pinned.

**NOT DONE, deliberately:** the Merkle commit re-downloads and re-hashes the WHOLE backup every ~5s while
sending (`MERKLE_DEBOUNCE_MS`), and `computeRootFromLeaves` is still one unyielded synchronous block. That
is the best candidate for the multi-second freeze, but it is BACKUP_LOOP territory (the pipeline that
shipped `root_mismatch` five times) and the debounce was lowered deliberately by B-45r3. `[LAGDIAG]`
probes already exist — ONE release-build log while reproducing "send fast, then press back" settles the
ranking. Do not touch it blind.

**Process note — a stalled agent nearly cost a file.** The org/search builder died mid-task; recovering its
work I ran a slice-by-index script whose start anchor matched an EARLIER docblock than intended (the agent
had written the same client quote I had given it), cutting ~340 lines out of `organisationTree.ts`. Caught
immediately by a `grep -c` that returned 0. Restored from the committed blob and re-applied every addition
with the Edit tool. **Never slice a source file by `indexOf` on prose that appears more than once** — and
`git checkout --` is blocked in this environment, so the recovery path is `git show HEAD:path` + copy.

Gates: app 2766, booking 815, crypto ×2 (B-126 moving flake only — `productionRuntimeGroupSend` red once,
fully green on the re-run), typecheck 45 (baseline 47), eslint 0 errors. **DEVICE-OWED:** every one of
these, plus the `[LAGDIAG]` capture above.

### B-607 r2 — REOPENED by the client, and the first fix was not enough · FIXED

Client, after 1.0.245: still reports it. The screenshots settle what is and is not happening —
the album bar reads `All 2 · Test 1 2 · Unfiled 0`. **`Unfiled 0` is the proof there is no
duplication**: both files are filed once, into Test 1. The data was never wrong.

What makes it read as a copy is the VIEW. `All` lists every file whatever its folder, so after a
move the rows sit exactly where they were, and the same count appears on two chips at once
(`All 2` beside `Test 1 2`) which scans as four files. The r1 fix (follow the move into the
destination) made the result visible but did not make it a MOVE — tap back to All and the
originals are still there, which is precisely the complaint.

**Root cause, stated properly: a folder affordance over a label model.** The screen is called
Files, the action is a folder-with-arrow icon, the sheet says "Move 2 items to…". All of that
promises exclusivity. A label model cannot deliver it while the default view contains everything.

**Fix (r2):** once at least one folder exists, the browser opens on **Unfiled** instead of All, so
filing something genuinely removes it from the view you were standing in. `All` stays one tap away
as the flat library. Derived rather than initial state, because albums arrive from a persisted
store and an initialiser would read an empty list on first render and stick on All. With no folders
yet Unfiled IS the whole library, so nothing changes for a user who has never made one — pinned by
its own test. Empty state is context-aware: "Everything is filed" pointing at the folders, never
the send-an-attachment copy, which would read as data loss.

Pinned by `B-607 r2 — after a move the file is GONE from the view it was in` (mutation-proven RED)
plus the no-folders default test. Gate: filesAlbumMoveIntegrity 21/21, app messenger screens
614 passed / 45 suites, typecheck 46 vs baseline 47.

## 2026-08-22 — B-632..B-634: "the app feels laggy on all phones" — the named lead, measured and closed

Founder: _"the app feels laggy for all phone, pull latest and see."_ then _"fixed all"_. Nothing to pull —
`origin` appeared to 404 all session; it was an AUTH fault (git was acting as `piyaldeb`,
and the repo is org-owned, visible only to `omnidevxstudio-bit`). Origin was in fact 19 commits

No device was attached this session, so these are static + microbenchmark findings, not
on-device numbers. CLAUDE.md's lag section names eight MEASURED DEAD ENDS and one untested
lead: **the per-send backup work**. That lead is real, and B-632 is it.

### B-632 — `markDirty` was O(whole history) and ran once per marked message · FIXED

`markDirty` is called from ten store mutation sites (status flip, receipt, reaction, retract
token, envelope id, media patch, edit, delete-for-everyone). It did two linear scans:

1. the dedup was a `Set` of `owner:id:version` composites, so dropping ONE row's entry meant
   walking the WHOLE set with `startsWith` — and that set is seeded at boot from the entire
   `mirror_flushed` ledger, i.e. **one entry per message in the user's history**;
2. the re-enqueue then scanned **every hydrated conversation's message array** to locate the id.

`recordReadReceipts` fires it once per row it marks, so opening a chat paid both scans per
unread message. Measured (V8 — a floor; Hermes is several times slower):

| history | hydrated | one chat-open (200 rows) | per markDirty |
| ------- | -------- | ------------------------ | ------------- |
| 1,000   | 1,000    | 15 ms                    | 0.15 ms       |
| 5,000   | 5,000    | **214 ms**               | 1.07 ms       |
| 15,000  | 8,000    | **667 ms**               | 3.33 ms       |
| 40,000  | 12,000   | **1,738 ms**             | 8.69 ms       |

That is the reported symptom exactly — press feedback is an Animated opacity change that runs
without JS, `onPress` is a JS callback, so "renders but registers late" means the JS thread was
busy when the touch landed. It also explains the compounding the founder described, and why it
looks device-independent: the cost tracks HISTORY, not hardware.

**Fix.** The dedup becomes a `Map` keyed `owner:id` holding the last version — deliberately the
same shape as the ledger's own `PRIMARY KEY (owner_user_id, message_id)`. Every per-message op
is now one keyed lookup: `markDirty`, `mirrorRemoval` and `clearDedupForItems` all drop the
scan. `clearMirrorDedupForOwner` keeps its walk (repair path, once, deliberately). `markDirty`
also takes the `conversationId` every store site already has as its own first argument, so the
store lookup probes one list and falls back to the full scan only when the caller had no id — a
mis-hint can never silently lose the re-enqueue.

**One deliberate semantic change**, in the I1/I8-safe direction: the Set had "seen" every
version it ever held, so a revert (A to B back to A) was skipped and the server stuck
permanently on B. The map holds only the LAST version, so a revert re-ships and the server
converges on local truth. Extra upload, never a skipped one.

Invariants re-checked against BACKUP_LOOP section 2: I1 (idle boots still silent — an unchanged
row's version still matches the seeded ledger version), I4 (per-owner clear still owner-scoped),
I5, I7 (`seedMirrorDedup` unchanged in effect; on a version race it now re-enqueues rather than
skips — the safe direction), I8. I3 untouched: nothing here goes near `verifyMerkleCommit`.

Pinned by `mirrorDedupKeying.test.ts` (12 tests). **Six mutation-proved RED** by stashing the
fix and re-running — the four source scans, the revert case, and the timing case (1.6 s down to
single-digit ms against a 300 ms bound). Caller-completeness: `markDirty` has exactly ONE
production caller (`notifyBackupDirty`), updated.

**Gate:** messenger-crypto 6672 tests x2 runs (run 1: 3 suites red, run 2: 1 DIFFERENT suite
red, zero overlap — the documented B-126 moving flake, none in mirror/store); app messenger
screens 614 passed / 45 suites; typecheck 46 vs baseline 47.

### B-633 — `persist` serialized the whole vault on EVERY `set()` · FIXED

zustand 5.0.12 wires `api.setState` to call `savedSetState(...)` and then `setItem()`, and
`createJSONStorage.setItem` does `JSON.stringify` **before** reaching our adapter. So
`makeDebouncedAsyncStorage`'s 500 ms debounce deferred only the AsyncStorage bridge call — the
`partialize` deep rebuild plus the serialize ran synchronously on the mutator's stack, per
mutation. Audit fix #13's own comment says it set out to stop "a JSON.stringify of the entire
vault per keystroke"; it had been only half-applied for eight months.

Measured per `set()` (V8 floor): 0.17 ms at 20 conversations, 0.56 ms at 60, 1.70 ms at 120
(+2 vaulted owners), 4.82 ms at 250 (+3) — payloads 27 KB to 678 KB. Unlike B-632 this scales
with CONVERSATION count and is paid by **every account whether or not backup is on**, which
makes it the better match for "all phones".

**Fix.** `makeDebouncedAsyncStorage` (a `StateStorage`) becomes `makeDebouncedJsonStorage` (a
`PersistStorage`), so it receives the partialized OBJECT and does the `JSON.stringify` inside
its own debounced flush — once per quiet window instead of once per mutation. Splitting the
cost showed stringify was **80-89%** of it, so this removes the great majority. Holding the
object across the window is safe: immer never mutates a committed snapshot in place, a later
`set()` REPLACES references, and the next `setItem` supersedes the pending value anyway. A
serializer throw is caught so it can never take the mutation down with it.

The security strips deliberately **stayed in `partialize`** — MSG-10 (no plaintext body at
rest) and P0-S3 (no `masterKeyB64` at rest) still run before anything reaches the adapter, so
that boundary did not move and `storeSinksAndPersist`'s pins are untouched. The residual
`partialize` rebuild (0.09-0.67 ms) was left alone on purpose: memoising it would put a
stale-cache hazard on the MSG-10/P0-S3 path to buy ~0.5 ms.

**One trap, caught by the gate and worth remembering.** Writing the adapter's `getItem` as
`async (name) => {...}` adds microtask ticks before persist resolves hydration, which delays
`onRehydrateStorage` and flipped `DepartmentChannelsScreen`'s initial collapse seed:
`departmentDirectoryRender` G4 went red **only under a full app-project run** and passed in
isolation. Confirmed it was mine by re-running the same sweep on stashed sources (HEAD green,
change red) rather than writing it off as the known flake. `getItem` now mirrors
`createJSONStorage` tick-for-tick — parse synchronously when the read is synchronous, else
`promise.then(parse)`. B-633 is a WRITE-path change; read timing must not move. Pinned.

### B-634 — the dirty nudge fired INSIDE the immer recipe · FIXED

All ten `notifyBackupDirty` calls sat inside their `set(s => ...)` recipes, so `markDirty`'s
`getState()` returned the PRE-commit snapshot. The store already documents this exact trap on
`notifyBackupRemoved` ("MUST be called AFTER the immer commit — calling it inside the recipe
made markDirty read the pre-commit state"); the lesson was never applied to the dirty nudge.

Not data loss — the post-commit mirror subscriber re-mirrored the row with the real new
version. It was **write amplification**: two encrypts and two server rows per mutation, the
first re-uploading unchanged plaintext under a fresh AES-GCM IV. That is precisely the
server-byte churn BACKUP_LOOP I1 exists to prevent, and it doubled flush volume on the hot path.

**Fix, two halves.** (1) Each of the ten actions now collects the ids it touched into a local
`dirty` array inside the recipe and calls `flushBackupDirty(dirty, conversationId)` after
`set()` returns. Collecting ids rather than notifying unconditionally after the commit
preserves every action's own guards — a recipe that bails early still nudges nothing, which
matters: `recordDeliveredReceipt` only tracks rows the user SENT. (2) `markDirty` no longer
force-invalidates blindly — if the queue already holds that EXACT committed row object (the
subscriber ran synchronously inside the same `set()`), it returns without touching the dedup.

**Why that guard is a queue scan and not a version compare** — the thing that nearly broke
this: `versionHash` uses the mirror's local `serializeMessage`, which does **not** include
`receipts` / `envelope_ids`, while the actual wire (`serializeMessageForBackup`) **does**. So a
receipt-only change has an unchanged version hash, and `markDirty`'s forced invalidation is the
only thing that gets delivered/read ticks to the server. Deduping on version instead would have
silently reintroduced the B-116 class (restored chats losing their ticks). Making the hash cover
receipts was rejected: it changes every stored ledger version, so the next boot re-uploads the
entire history with fresh IVs — the I1 drift factory, unacceptable to ship blind. The queue scan
is bounded by MAX_QUEUE_SIZE (500 reference compares), i.e. noise next to what B-632 removed.

Also fixed while moving the delete below the guard: the lazy-`require` catch now invalidates the
dedup too. Without it a store-not-ready failure would have SKIPPED an upload it could not prove
happened, which I8 forbids — degrade to re-upload, never to skipping.

Pinned by `storePerSetCost.test.ts`, mutation-proved: "mirrors the COMMITTED row" and "the store
supplies a PersistStorage" both go RED on stashed sources, while the receipt-only pass-through
and the MSG-10/P0-S3 strip guards stay green on both sides (they are guards, not discriminators).
`mirrorDedupKeying` additionally pins that `notifyBackupDirty` appears EXACTLY twice in the whole
store — its declaration and the helper's loop — so a call re-added at a mutation site fails.

**Gate (all three fixes):** messenger-crypto 6677 tests x2 runs (run 1 `attachmentUriPipeline`,
run 2 `freeSpacePrecheck` — different suites, zero overlap, and both were already flaking in the
pre-change baseline: the documented B-126 moving flake); app messenger screens 614 passed / 45
suites, identical to HEAD; typecheck 46 vs baseline 47; eslint 0 errors.

### Still open, and honest about it

All three are fixed and gated, but **none of it is device-confirmed**. The `[LAGDIAG]` probes
have been in the tree since 2026-07-27 and have still never been read off a device — a release
APK on a phone with real history would turn `[backup.markDirty]`, `[backup.flush]` and
`[backup.merkle]` into a direct read of how much of the founder's stall these three accounted
for. That is the next step, and it is the only thing that closes this honestly.

Sizing what is left, so nobody re-derives it: at ~1k messages the old `markDirty` cost was
15 ms and B-633 was ~0.2-0.6 ms per `set()`, which together still do NOT explain a 350-500 ms
per-send stall. **On a small account these three cannot be the whole story.** They matter most
on the accounts that hurt most (B-632 grows with history, B-633 with conversation count), so the
right read is "the structural per-mutation costs are gone", not "the lag is solved". What has
never been instrumented at all is the rest of the per-send path — the SQLCipher write, and the
`[backup.merkle]` commit cadence.

Residuals accepted deliberately: the `partialize` rebuild (0.09-0.67 ms per `set()`, left
un-memoised because a cache on the MSG-10/P0-S3 path is a bad trade for ~0.5 ms), and
`markDirty`'s bounded 500-entry queue scan (the only correct guard while `versionHash` is blind
to `receipts`/`envelope_ids` — see B-634).

Next free B-635.

## 2026-08-22 — B-635: a deletion made just before sign-out is discarded, PERMANENTLY · 4 plan rounds + 2 code rounds, dual AGREE

**Found during PLAN REVIEW, not by a tester.** While designing the deferred-Merkle-commit change
(`docs/planning/BACKUP_BOUNDARY_BATCHING_PLAN.md`), the critic traced the sign-out teardown to show why
that plan's original shape was unsafe — and the trace exposed a live bug in the CURRENT build. Worth
noting for provenance: the rest of that teardown path deserves the same look.

**The bug.** `signOut` called `disposeMirror()` (`authStore.ts:743` pre-fix) with **no preceding
drain**, and `disposeMirror` does `queue.length = 0` (`messageMirror.ts:270`) + `convQueue.clear()`
(`:271`). So anything still inside the 1.5 s flush debounce was thrown away.

**Why that is data loss and not latency.** A deletion is not a row that can be re-derived:
`mirrorRemoval` (`:481-523`) queues a **SYNTHETIC** tombstone, because the SQL row is already gone
(`messengerStore.ts:570-572`); `backupNow`'s `loadAll()` therefore has nothing to walk, and
`markDirty`'s BUG-3 note explicitly forbids manufacturing one. **And re-login does not heal it:**
`mirror_flushed` still holds that row's LIVE version, so the next catch-up sweep's `seedMirrorDedup`
(`mirrorBootstrap.ts:150`) skips it **by design** (I1). The server keeps the live row forever and
**every future restore resurrects the message.**

**BOTH queues, not just messages.** `notifyBackupConversationDeleted` (`messengerStore.ts:585-593`)
→ `mirrorConversation(..., {deleted:true})` → `convQueue`, cleared at `:271`. So this equally broke
**B-605** ("deleted chats survive a fresh-install restore") and **B-594** — both shipped 2026-08-21,
both silently reverted by a sign-out inside 1.5 s. Anyone re-testing those two must read this entry.

**THE ROOT CAUSE IS POSITIONAL, and the first fix was wrong.** The drain must run **before**
`authApi.signOut(deviceId)` (`authStore.ts:726`). After it the JTI is revoked, so `putMessages` 401s,
`flush()` classifies `unauthorized` as **RETRYABLE** (`messageMirror.ts:691`), the batch is requeued
— and `disposeMirror` then discards it. **A drain placed after would ship nothing, fix nothing, and
pass every mocked test**, because a mocked `backupClient` never 401s. `authStore.ts:672-680` already
documents this exact hazard for push tokens; the review caught that my plan had put it at `~741`.

**The fix.** Immediately before `authApi.signOut`: gate on `isMirrorEnabled()` (a locked-backup
sign-out costs 0 ms), then `await Promise.race([drainMirrorOutbox() → fireMerkleHookNowIfPending(),
2 s timeout])`, in try/catch with a `finally` clearing the timer. **Order inside is load-bearing:**
drain FIRST — `fireMerkleHookNowIfPending` only fires when the debounce slot is armed, and it is the
drain's own flushes that arm it, so firing first skips the commit and then uploads, leaving rows on
the server with the pending flag set and no covering commit (the I2 window).

**Invariants (BACKUP_LOOP §2).** I1 untouched — no sweep/dedup/ledger-seed code in the diff.
**I2 STRENGTHENED** — an owed commit that was previously abandoned now ships; the flag-before-upload
order (`:650`) is byte-untouched; an abandoned drain stays safe because `mirrorSessionGen++` (`:264`)
staleness-guards the in-flight flush at `:657`/`:679` while the flag survives for the boot heal.
I3 untouched (no verifier code). **I4 untouched** — this reuses `repairBackupCommit`'s own
`drainMirrorOutbox` and never signs directly; the commit goes through the GATED hook, so nothing can
sign a torn set. I5/I6/I7/I8 untouched. I9 satisfied — the new `console.warn` carries
`queued=<n> drained|timeout ms=<n>` only, and `logAudit` is green.

**Tests — and two of them were decorative until the code review.** Six behavioural cases + a
comment-stripped source scan, all RED first (they fail against pre-fix code; that failure IS the
bug). The code review then proved **two realistic mutations survived green**, and both are now
pinned + mutation-proved:

1. **Swapping drain/fire** inside the IIFE — re-opens the I2 window; nothing asserted the order. Now
   one four-step assertion: `['drain','fire','revoke','dispose']`.
2. **`await` → `void` on the drain** — the obvious "snappier sign-out" edit, which reinstates B-635
   outright; every behavioural test still passed because the order mock records synchronously and the
   race resolves. Now pinned by scan; the mutation also crashes the run via the detached rejection.
   ⚠️ **Do not delete the ordering source scan as redundant.** `authStore.ts:673` contains the literal
   token `authApi.signOut()` **inside a comment**, so an unstripped scan matches PROSE before the real
   call site and passes vacuously with the drain on the wrong side. Comments are stripped for that
   reason.

**Residual:** a drain exceeding the 2 s budget is ABANDONED (`Promise.race` does not cancel) —
covered by the pending flag + boot heal (I2). `{wipeAtRest:true}` is the path where a lost tombstone
would be **unrecoverable** (the wipe destroys the local history B-81 repair needs), so the drain
running there is pinned explicitly.

**DEVICE VERIFICATION OWED — the exact script (BACKUP_LOOP §5.3):** delete a message **and** a chat →
sign out within 1.5 s → reinstall → restore → **both must stay deleted**. Also expect
`[bravo.backup.signout] queued=… drained ms=…` in logcat. NOT YET RUN — no ADB device in this lane.
§5.1 idle-boot silence is not on any path this diff touches; §5.2 kill-window heal is not exercisable
here but the risk direction is favourable (this only ever NARROWS the window).

Gates: backup/merkle 16 suites/97 (incl. `logAudit`), app 2775, crypto ×2 earlier (A fully green
6671/6671; B three MOVING flakes — `productionRuntimeGroupSend`, `blockedPeersAndTombstones`,
`backupFlags` — all 35/35 in isolation, B-126 signature, none touching this diff), typecheck 45
(baseline 47), lint 0 errors.

**Not built, deliberately:** the deferred-commit tuning (W1 15 s ceiling + W2 blur boundary) that this
work started as. It is the only part that WIDENS the window behind five shipped `root_mismatch`
incidents, and its premise — that the Merkle commit is the multi-second freeze — is still UNMEASURED
(B-310 already made the hashing yield, so the remaining cost is the walk + `res.json()`). Gated on one
`[LAGDIAG] [backup.merkle]` release-build capture; **if the commit is not the block, close the plan
rather than build it smaller.** Plan Rev 4 carries the full build order and a do-not-re-propose list
(deferring the UPLOAD; "commit-only deferral reverts B-45r3" — stale by three fixes; deleting
`scheduleMerkleHook`; a queue-cap trigger; gating on `mirrorOutboxSize`).

**The device marker, and how to read it.** `[bravo.backup.signout] queued=N drained|timeout ms=X`.
It appears under BACKUP_LOOP §5.1's EXISTING capture (`grep -E "bravo.backup|backup.merkle"`) — no doc
change needed. Repro conditions must be exact: **backup unlocked**, delete a message AND a chat, sign
out **within 1.5 s**. ⚠️ **Absence of the line is AMBIGUOUS** — nothing owed, backup locked, or the
drain threw (the `catch` jumps past the marker). A tester must not read "no line" as "not fixed".

**What is pinned, and what is not.** The suite now catches NINE specific mutations, including the two
that stayed green until the code review: drain-before-fire, and `await`→`void` on the drain. The 2 s
budget itself is deliberately UNPINNED — any value ≳1 s behaves identically, and pinning a timing
constant would only make the suite brittle.

**`logAudit` was widened in this commit, because its green run here was VACUOUS.** That scanner covers
`src/modules/messenger`, the two services, `messenger-core` and `ops-console` — **not `src/store`** —
so it never looked at the new warn. `STORE_ROOT` added (verified clean across all of `src/store` first,
so it is a pure ratchet, the CORE_ROOT precedent). Same shape as the B-133 ops-console gap: the leak
survived because the scanner's roots did not cover the file.

**SCOPE BOUNDARY — only step 1 shipped.** `MERKLE_DEBOUNCE_MS` is still **5 s**; W2 (the blur
boundary) is **not built**. Both stay gated on the `[LAGDIAG] [backup.merkle]` measurement, and if that
shows the commit is not the multi-second block the recorded expected outcome is to **close the plan**,
not to build it smaller.

## 2026-08-23 — B-636: the Channels search matched channel NAMES only · client request

**Client, on the Channels screen search box (screenshot, box circled in red):** _"this search option
should allow you to also search for conversions or words in conversations that's inside the chats."_

**What it did.** B-625 shipped the box a day earlier as a NAME filter: `filterTreeRows` →
`channelMatchesQuery` → `row.name.toLowerCase().includes(q)`. Nothing read a message body, so a word
somebody actually typed in a channel was unfindable from the one control that looks like it should
find it.

**What it does now.** Two answers, in the order of how strong each hit is:

1. **Channels whose NAME matches** — unchanged, still instant, still a tree with its ancestors.
2. **Messages whose BODY matches** — a new "Messages" block underneath, newest-first, one row per
   hit: the channel it was posted in, the matched term highlighted inside a line of its own context,
   and the date. Tapping a row opens that channel.

**SCOPE IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, and it is belt-and-braces.** `SqlMessageStore.searchContent` takes an
explicit conversation-id ALLOW-LIST and an empty list returns nothing — it is never read as "no
filter", which is how a scoped query silently becomes a global one. The screen passes the
conversation ids of the channels it is already rendering, which are organisation-scoped upstream
(B-624). Then `channelMessageHits` DROPS any row whose conversation is not in the caller's channel
map, so even a leaked row cannot reach the screen: the organisation separation does not depend on
the layer below it being correct. Consequences that fall out for free — a 1:1 chat can never surface
on the Channels tab, and a channel the caller was removed from is gone from `listChannels`, so its
still-resident local rows are unreachable.

**Sectioned per organisation, like the tree above it** (B-624: _"different organization channels must
never mix… It must ALWAYS be separate here"_). A flat hit list under a per-org tree would have put
the same pile straight back on the screen under a different name.

**Three things the query must never return, all asserted rather than assumed:**

- **A delete-for-everyone body.** `messageMutationApply` already blanks it, so the SQL guard is depth
  — but a search that can resurrect deleted text is precisely the class this repo shipped in
  B-594/B-605, so `deleted_for_all` is in the WHERE clause and mutation-proved.
  ⚠️ The guard is `IS NULL OR = 0`, never a bare `= 0`: every pre-tombstone row holds NULL, and the
  bare form hides essentially the whole history. Both forms are pinned (removing the clause reds one
  test; narrowing it to `= 0` reds twenty-four).
- **An expired disappearing message** — mirrors `loadOlder`/`loadLinkMessages`.
- **A wildcard the user typed.** `%` and `_` are ESCAPED (`ESCAPE '\'`, backslash escaped first or it
  re-escapes its own output). Unescaped, a typed `%` matches every message on the device: a wrong
  answer AND an unbounded scan. `loadLinkMessages` needed none of this because its pattern is a
  literal; this one is user input.

**A REAL BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT MID-BUILD.** Conversation ids are chunked at 400 (SQLite's 999-parameter
cap), and the merge across chunks was gated on `out.length > limit` — so whenever the total happened
to FIT, two hits from different chunks came back in chunk order instead of newest-first. That is the
common case, not the rare one. Now any multi-chunk read merges. Found by the real-engine test, not by
reading the code.

**A SECOND ONE, in the same diff.** `setHits([])` allocates a fresh array, which can never satisfy
`useState`'s `Object.is` bail-out — so clearing re-rendered this (heavy) screen on every effect run,
including the mount pass where nothing is being searched. A module-level `NO_HITS` makes it a real
no-op. Symptom that exposed it: an UNRELATED pre-existing test went red only under a full-file run
(987 ms against a 1000 ms `findBy` timeout) and was green in isolation — the B-632 lesson, again: a
suite that flips green→red under load is not automatically the known flake.

**And the box was INERT on the agency/legacy-FLAT surface.** That branch renders from `channels`
directly, so `filterTreeRows` never reached it and B-625's search box did nothing there at all.
Filtered by the ids `filterTreeRows` already kept rather than by a second `channelMatchesQuery` call
— the same rule evaluated twice is the duplicate-copy class, and this copy would have drifted the
moment the tree's ancestor/subtree behaviour changed.

**Design decisions worth not re-litigating.**

- **Two-character floor on the BODY scan** (`MESSAGE_SEARCH_MIN_CHARS`). The name filter still runs
  from one character — it is a scan over a few dozen rows in memory. A single letter matches most
  messages on the device, so the body scan would spend the whole budget returning noise. The empty
  state says so rather than implying an empty result.
- **200 ms debounce, separate from the name filter.** Names stay instant on every keystroke (B-625's
  behaviour, unchanged); bodies settle once. One SQLCipher read per keystroke is the JS-thread class
  in the lag register.
- **Cap 30, no pagination.** A search box answers "where did I see that"; an answer 30 rows long has
  already failed to answer it.
- **The empty state is honest about WHICH search ran** — "Searching messages…" while the debounce is
  in flight, "no channels or messages" only once it has actually returned. Declaring "no messages
  match" during the 200 ms wait is a lie the user sees on every single query.
- **Sorted by recency, not relevance.** No per-channel cap either, so one very chatty channel can
  fill the list. Deliberate: recency is the rule people can predict, and the fix for a flooded list
  is a narrower query.

**Tests — 44 new, and FIVE realistic mutations proved red.**

| Suite                                      | Project          | Pins                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `channelMessageSearch.test.ts` (25)        | app              | the query floor, the snippet offsets, the map-as-scope drop, per-org sectioning |
| `sqlMessageStoreEngine.test.ts` (+17)      | messenger-crypto | the SQL itself, against a REAL SQLite engine (`node:sqlite`)                    |
| `departmentDirectoryRender.test.tsx` (+11) | app              | the screen ASKS for the right scope, and the answer renders and opens           |

Mutations verified applied (`perl -0pi -e` silently no-opped AGAIN — grep every mutation before
believing a green run):

| Mutation                                            | Result                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `escapeLikeTerm` returns its input                  | 3 red                 |
| the `deleted_for_all` clause removed                | 1 red                 |
| that clause narrowed to a bare `= 0`                | 24 red                |
| `channelMessageHits` falls back instead of dropping | 3 red (both projects) |
| the screen passes a truncated `conversationIds`     | 1 red                 |

**Security.** Nothing leaves the device — the relay holds ciphertext, so a server-side index cannot
exist and this is a local scan, exactly like `loadLinkMessages`. No query text and no body is ever
logged (`logAudit` green). The runtime wrapper checks `isOurEpoch()` BEFORE and AFTER its await: a
search is the one read whose result is rendered as somebody's message text, so a handle belonging to
the previous user is not a degraded answer, it is the wrong person's plaintext.

Gates: messenger-crypto 6706/6706 ×2 (546 suites, both runs identical — no flake), app 2819/2823
(4 pre-existing skips), typecheck 45 vs baseline 47, lint 0 errors.

**NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED.** No ADB device in this lane. What a tester must exercise: type a word that
exists only INSIDE a channel message and confirm the Messages block appears and opens the right
channel; confirm a deleted message's text is NOT findable; confirm a message in another
organisation's channel never appears; confirm typing stays smooth on an account with real history
(the body scan runs off the JS thread, but the scan cost itself is unmeasured on a large store).

## 2026-08-23 — B-642: a dead group-call boot kept the camera — "the 'Call failed' loop"

**Found while investigating B-640** (the client's "call fails in the mission group" report), not by a
tester. Source-provable, no device needed — which is why it was built first while B-640's own root
cause still waits on evidence.

**The defect.** `useGroupCall`'s boot IIFE ends in a catch that performs four teardown steps. Four
sites never reach it — they set a terminal state and **`return`** instead of throwing:

| Site                                                     | Line    |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| pre-join FrameCryptor refusal (S6/B-111)                 | `:2071` |
| `room_full`                                              | `:2122` |
| post-join FrameCryptor refusal (S6)                      | `:2209` |
| **group-key lane catch — the dominant Ops Room failure** | `:2490` |

Two of the four steps therefore never ran for them:

1. **The B-343 media release.** Tracks are acquired at step 2 (`:1998`), long before the key lane. A
   boot that dies after that leaves the camera held, and B-343's own comment says what follows:
   _"wedges EVERY subsequent call's getUserMedia behind it (**the 'Call failed' loop**)"_.
2. **The BS-MINIMIZE-RING registry clear**, whose comment names _"key-wait failure"_ explicitly — i.e.
   precisely the site that could not reach it. Minimize during the 25 s key wait and the floating
   bubble hangs on "connecting…" forever.

**Why it matters for B-640.** The Ops Room failure is the group-key lane: a keyless member re-throws
after the 25 s wait. So the client's "the call fails" is exactly the path that also strands the
camera — turning one failure into a run of them.

**The fix.** One `releaseDeadBoot()` helper inside the boot effect, called at all four sites.

**⛔ THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FIX HAD A WORSE BUG THAN THE ONE IT FIXED, and both reviewers found it
independently.** It matched the registry entry on `reg.conversationId === opts.conversationId`. That
is **not an identity** — several rooms and several generations share one conversation, and
`launchCall` **explicitly permits** a second call in the same group (`rejoiningOwnGroup`,
`launchCall.ts:302-305`). So a boot stuck in the 25 s wait would have called `endActiveGroupCall` on
**the call the user started afterwards**. `leaveInternal` already learned this at `:5675` — same
generation test, same reason, and its comment names the same symptom. The fix now keys on
`groupKeyRef.current` (`{roomId, gen}` — the key `setActiveGroupCall` RETURNS), per CLAUDE.md's
WI-1.5 rule.

**Three more review-caught defects in the same fix:**

- **It could stop a LIVE call's microphone.** The resume path ADOPTS the previous instance's track
  **objects** (`:1287-1288`) and inherits its generation, so a stale twin timing out would stop the
  mic and camera of the call the user is looking at. Now skipped when a registry entry that is _not_
  ours holds the very objects being stopped.
- **It ran after a real teardown, where it can only be a no-op or a wrong-call teardown.**
  `cancelled` is set only in the cleanup's real branch, which runs `leaveInternal` — that already
  stops both refs and nulls the slot under its own gen check. Now `if (cancelled) {return;}` first.
  ⚠️ The MINIMIZE path returns from the cleanup **before** setting `cancelled` (`:4100`), so the case
  this helper exists for is unaffected — that asymmetry is what makes the guard safe.
- **`room_full` was missed** — same class, same blocker card, media held, no leave.

**A comment that taught the opposite of the truth, now corrected.** The first version claimed the
room reap was excluded because `participantTagRef` is set before the sites. True for the post-join
ones; **false for the pre-join site**, where `neverJoined` really is true and `createdRoomIdRef` was
set at `:1796` — so that IS a site where the reap would do real work, and it sends no `sfu.leave` at
all. A FrameCryptor-less build can leave a host-owned zero-participant room behind. **NOT fixed**:
the reap's safety rests on `endRoomIfEmptyByHost` refusing unless the caller IS the recorded host and
the room is empty (`messenger.gateway.ts:2465-2472`), a server invariant this change has not audited.
Recorded as a known gap rather than guessed at. **Also not covered:** the two mid-call exits
(reconnect-budget exhaustion `:2749`, transport-failed-before-joined `:2977`) — they are not
boot-IIFE returns, and the suite is named so it does not imply otherwise.

**Tests — `groupCallDeadBootRelease.test.ts`, 12 source-scan cases.** ⚠️ **The first version of this
test was decorative and the review proved it**: three realistic mutations stayed GREEN, including
deleting the identity guard — the single most dangerous edit available. Two causes, both worth
remembering:

1. **`src.slice(at, at + 900)` overran the ~500-char helper by ~400 chars**, so
   `toContain('getActiveGroupCall()')` was satisfiable by a call **outside** the helper, and the
   `not.toContain` assertions covered unrelated code (false-RED in the other direction). It now
   slices to the helper's own closing brace.
2. **It asserted tokens, never the decision** — the CLAUDE.md class: _"asserting a token exists
   somewhere in a file rather than at the decision site"_.

Both mutations were re-run after the hardening and now go RED. **Known limitation, stated:** a source
scan cannot see `if (false) { …stop() }` — deleting the line is caught, disabling it is not.

Gates: messenger-crypto 6714/6714 (run 1 had 6 moving failures, run 2 fully green — B-126 signature;
the group-call suites specifically were 571/571 **twice**), app `screens/messenger` 670, typecheck 45
vs baseline 47, `logAudit` green (the outer catch now newly receives group-key-lane errors).

**NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED.** No ADB device in this lane. What a tester should exercise: fail a group call
at the key step, then immediately start another call — the camera must be available. And: minimize
during the 25 s wait, let it fail, and confirm the floating bubble dismisses instead of hanging on
"connecting…".

Next free B-643.

## 2026-08-23 — B-638: the EMERGENCY CALLS card restored; LINKS button removed

**Client, with two screenshots:** wants the emergency entry point to look like the CARD (image 3), not
the header word (image 4), _"and remove the link option."_ Follow-up when asked whether that meant
off the Calls header or deleting the feature: _"just remove the button link that it."_

**⚠️ THIS REVERSES B-626, WHICH SHIPPED THE DAY BEFORE.** B-613 added the card at 14:47 on
2026-08-22; B-626 removed it at 19:32 the same day, turning it into a header word "like Links". The
client has now reversed that. Recorded so nobody re-derives the flip as a regression. The B-626
rationale comment was rewritten, not left to contradict the code.

**What the screenshots actually settle.** Image 3's header reads `CALLS` **only** — there is no
emergency word in it. So the card REPLACES that door rather than sitting beside it, and the header
now carries nothing. Also worth recording: the card in the screenshot is **not** the card that was
deleted (`git log -S "Reach emergency services"` on this file returns nothing — that phrase only ever
existed as prose in `VBGEmergencyScreen`). The shipped card was chip-based. Built the card the
screenshot shows AND kept the chips: the chips dial in ONE tap, and a chevron-only card costs two,
which is the wrong trade on this surface.

**LinksScreen now has NO entry point** — `CallsLogScreen.tsx:292` was its only one. Route left
registered in both navigators and the screen untouched, so restoring a door is a one-line change; the
screen's own docblock says so. This is a **G2 "no door lost" deviation taken on the client's explicit
instruction**, not an oversight. ⚠️ **knip does NOT flag it** (the navigators still import it), so
there is no automated signal that a screen went dark — do not read a green `deadcode` run as evidence.

### The safety defect the review caught, and the fix that was ALSO wrong

`getDeviceCountryIso()` reads the phone's **LOCALE** (`I18nManager.localeIdentifier` / `AppleLocale`,
falling back to `Intl`). It is offline and has **nothing to do with where the user is**. The recovered
card rendered `{entry.name} · tap a number to call`, so **a user in Bangladesh on an `en_US` phone
would be shown "United States" and offered 911** — a confidently wrong number on an emergency card.

My first fix was to **drop the country name**. The edge review showed that is WORSE: strip the label
and the same user sees "tap a number to call" over a 911 chip with nothing saying whose 911 it is —
the wrong guess becomes hidden instead of visible and correctable. Final shape: **name the country,
attribute it, and offer the way out** — `United Kingdom · from your phone's language` + `All countries`
→ the searchable directory.

⚠️ **The affordance says "All countries", NOT "Change".** `VBGEmergencyScreen` has a search over every
country but **no picker and no persistence** — it cannot change what this card shows. "Change" would
have promised something the app does not do. **Still owed (B-643):** that screen labels the same
locale guess **"Your Location"**, so the card tells the truth and its own destination re-asserts the
claim one tap later.

### Five more defects the reviews caught in my own fix

| #   | Defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Fix                                                                                            |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **112 emphasised over 911/000/111.** My first rule always made 112 `strong`, reasoning that the country is a guess. **That inverts when the guess is RIGHT** — on a correctly detected US phone it de-emphasised the number that is official, guaranteed and location-routed. | Emphasise the country's OWN number when known, 112 when not. 112 is always PRESENT either way. |
| 2   | **A plain dedupe deleted a whole service in 47 countries.** Ireland is `all:112, police/ambulance/fire:999`, so someone needing an ambulance was shown a button labelled **Police**; Japan lost "Fire" behind "Ambulance".                                                    | Labels MERGE onto the shared number (`Police / Ambulance / Fire`).                             |
| 3   | **~30 dp touch targets, no `hitSlop`**, 8 dp apart, on chips that dial DIFFERENT services. The two header buttons this replaced both HAD hitSlop — the change traded padded targets for undersized ones exactly where a panicked mis-tap costs most.                          | `hitSlop` on every chip and the head row.                                                      |
| 4   | **The provenance caveat was the part that truncated.** `numberOfLines={1}` left ~200 dp for ~235 dp of text, so it ellipsised **"from your phone's language"** and kept the country — the exact inverse of the point. RTL runs no layout, so the test could not see it.       | `numberOfLines={2}`.                                                                           |
| 5   | **A container `accessibilityLabel` on the card `View`.** On Android a contentDescription on a ViewGroup can make TalkBack focus the container and shadow its children — putting every dial chip out of a screen reader's reach. Same family as B-569.                         | Removed; each child carries its own name.                                                      |

### Two pre-existing bugs found by the review and fixed here

- **`ja-u-ca-japanese` resolved to CANADA.** `regionFromLocale` accepted any 2-letter segment at index
  ≥ 1, so a BCP-47 extension's KEY (`-u-ca-` = calendar) was harvested as a region — offering a
  Japanese user 911. Now stops at the extension singleton. Proven by executing the real function.
- **The Netherlands "Police" chip was `0900-8844`** — the Dutch **non-emergency**, premium-rate,
  queued line, rendered as a one-tap chip labelled Police on an emergency card. NL uses 112 for all
  services; the entry is removed.

### Tests — 32, and the first version was decorative

⚠️ **The locale mock was not load-bearing.** Nothing asserted the country NAME, so every assertion
passed whether the mock applied or not (GB→999 vs US→911 — neither checked). Now pinned.

⚠️ **A source comment claimed `emergencyDialSites.test.ts` enforced "record before dial". IT DOES
NOT** — that suite only checks both tokens appear in the same file, so swapping the two statements was
caught by **nothing in the repo**. A real ordering pin now exists, driven with a **rejecting**
`openURL` (the case the order exists for).

Also added: the null-country render (the branch **44 real regions** land in, previously untested), the
`tel:` hand-off itself (the old test asserted only the log, so a chip that recorded and never dialled
would have passed), a **property test over all 192 shipped countries** (exactly one strong chip, 112
always present, no duplicate numbers, every number dial-safe), and a **source scan pinning the card
OUTSIDE the ScrollView** — RTL renders the whole tree regardless of scroll position, so the §F-26
placement decision had no gate at all.

`agentShellFooterRoutes.test.ts` now pins **`EmergencyServices`** in the agency shell — the card is its
only door, and an embedded body navigating to a route one shell does not register is the B-257/B-258
class. `Links` stays pinned as registered-but-deliberately-door-less.

Gates: app `screens/messenger` + `screens/vbg` + `navigation` = **1049 passed**, typecheck 45 vs
baseline 47, lint clean.

**NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED.** Owed: the card renders in BOTH the pushed Calls screen and the embedded Calls
tab; a chip dials; the subtitle does not truncate at 320 dp / fontScale 1.3; TalkBack reaches every
chip.

## 2026-08-24 — B-643..B-645 + two founder UI calls (client batch, live-testing session)

Reported live while testing on device. Four separate things; the date-picker one is the
"app is still hanging" report narrowed down — it is **not** the JS-thread freeze class
(B-631/B-632..B-634), it is a native dialog fighting a re-render.

### B-643 — the Lite "choose date" dialog reset itself under the user's finger · FIXED

**Founder:** _"the app is still hanging … like when we want to choose date on lite app hanging."_

Live screen is `CustomizeAddOnsScreen` (the Secure Transfer dashboard — Schedule was folded
in from the legacy `BookingDateTimeScreen`). It drove the Android picker DECLARATIVELY, as a
mounted component under a `Platform.OS === 'android' && dateOpen` guard with an inline
`onChange` arrow.

Three library facts make that a trap, all source-verified in `node_modules`:

1. **`datetimepicker.android.js` re-invokes `open()` from an effect keyed on the `onChange`
   IDENTITY** — deps `[onChange, valueTimestamp, mode]`. The handler is an inline arrow, so it
   is a NEW identity on every render. Every re-render while the dialog is up calls `open()`
   again.
2. **`DatePickerModule.java` answers a second `open()` with
   `oldFragment.update(arguments); return;`** — it snaps the calendar back to `value` and
   **never settles the new promise**. So the day the user just tapped reverts, and that
   invocation's `onChange` never fires.
3. **This screen re-renders on its own.** The debounced server estimate does
   `setServerTotal(null)` → 400 ms → HTTP → `setServerTotal(total)` — two state writes per
   cycle, deps including `draft.start_time`, which the sibling `updateDraft({start_time})`
   effect writes. Tap the date field, the estimate lands, the calendar jumps back.

**The permanent-death case** (why "hanging", not just "janky"): a fragment left in the
FragmentManager by an activity restore has NO listeners — they are set only at `open()` time
and never persisted — so `findFragmentByTag` keeps returning it, every future `open()` takes
the `update(); return;` branch, `onChange` never fires, `dateOpen` sticks `true`, and the
date field is dead for good. `getCurrentActivity() == null` rejects into `onError`, which
this screen does not pass, so that path is silently swallowed too.

**Second, independent bug in the same handler.** The library's DISMISS path calls back with
`originalValue` — a **DEFINED** date (`eventCreators.createDismissEvtParams`). The handler
only checked the date argument, so **Cancel was treated as a pick**: it committed a date and
then chained on into the time sheet 50 ms later. Pressing Cancel opened another picker.

**Fix.** New `src/screens/booking/androidPicker.ts` — Android opens the dialog
**imperatively** from the press gesture (`DateTimePickerAndroid.open`), so there is exactly
one `open()` per real gesture and no re-render can reach it; and the helper filters on
`ev.type === 'set'`, so dismiss can never commit. iOS is untouched (its in-`Modal` spinner is
a real view, not a dialog fragment — and `datetimepicker.ios.js` emits `type: 'set'`, so the
new guard is safe there; verified before shipping it).

Applied to the three LIVE Lite doors: `CustomizeAddOnsScreen` (date), `ExecReviewScreen`
(date), `ExecTransportScreen` (time — it already checked the event type, but was still
mounted declaratively).

⚠️ **`BookingDateTimeScreen` and `ExecScheduleScreen` still carry the old pattern and were
deliberately NOT fixed: nothing navigates to them** (no `navigate('BookingDateTime')` or
`navigate('ExecDuration')` call site anywhere). They are registered-but-dead legacy wizard
steps. `androidPickerContract.test.ts` uses them as its **anti-vacuity check** — the scan
asserts they DO still match the bug pattern, so if someone "cleans" them the suite tells you
the detector went blind rather than silently passing. Fix or delete them, but do not edit
that assertion to go green.

### B-644 — ARRIVED AT PICKUP read as the live action 12 km from the pickup · FIXED

**Founder, with a screenshot mid-mission:** _"This was shown when I was on way to client."_
Stepper on 3 of 6, LEFT 12 km, ETA 16:40 — and a full-width primary-blue **ARRIVED AT
PICKUP** button.

It is not a dead button and it was not a wiring bug — worth recording, because that was the
first question asked: the tap runs `onAdvance` → `runAction('start')` →
`agentApi.missionPickup(missionId, fix)` → the server records checkpoint
`mission.arrived_at_pickup` (`agent.service.ts:1656`) and advances the FSM, after which the
screen **re-reads truth** rather than moving optimistically. A best-effort GPS fix rides
along so ops get a geofence WARNING (LM-C3), which never blocks.

The real defect is that the 150 m gate was **invisible until after the tap**. `farFromPickup`
existed and only swapped `#1E88FF` for `#2B5C9E` — one solid fill for a slightly darker
solid fill, which on a dark satellite map is just a primary button — and the distance lived
only in the confirm Alert.

**Fix.** The far state is now OUTLINED (translucent fill, no primary lift), takes a
`map-marker-distance` glyph instead of the check, and **carries the range on the button**
(a `12 km` pill), with the a11y label saying "Not there yet — 12 km from the pickup point".
The tap-through override is **kept on purpose**: hiding or hard-disabling it strands an
officer whose pickup pin is wrong or whose GPS has drifted, which is the worse failure.

### B-645 — two mapbox-gl versions meant two cold downloads · FIXED

**Founder:** _"another map takes so much time for loading."_

Every WebView map fetches `mapbox-gl.js` (~1 MB) + CSS from `api.mapbox.com` on open, and
that is the dominant share of time-to-ready. `MapPrewarm` (B-90 T-07) exists precisely to put
those bytes in the WebView's shared HTTP cache, and it mounts from `BookingHomeScreen` (which
sits beneath `ProDashboard` for PRO clients) and `AgentDashboardScreen` (the crew lane).

`ProLiveMissionScreen` and `CpoProtectionSessionScreen` pinned **v3.5.1** while all five other
map surfaces used **v3.9.0**. A different URL is a different cache entry, so the prewarm could
never warm those two — they re-downloaded the entire library on **every** open. Both use only
`accessToken` / `new Map` / `new Marker().setLngLat().addTo()` / `LngLatBounds().extend()`,
identical across those versions, so the fork bought nothing. Bumped both to v3.9.0 (14/14
references now one version) — this is a de-fork, not a version upgrade: v3.9.0 is already what
the app ships everywhere else.

Pinned by `mapLibraryVersionSingleSource.test.ts` over all seven map-HTML files, with a
non-vacuity check (each file must actually reference the library) — a second version silently
splits the cache again, and nothing else would catch it.

**Industry check (founder asked).** Uber's own Uber Lite writeup rejects WebView for the core
experience in as many words — _"fragmentation across different Android versions, inability to
integrate critical features, poor performance"_ — and Uber's Maps Display team owns a native
rendering engine and tile pipeline. So the native-SDK direction commit 1669b9c4 started for
the mission map is the right one; **the ordering matters though: `BravoMap` is still marked
NOT YET RUN ON A DEVICE.** Migrating six more screens onto an unverified renderer is the wrong
order. Sequence agreed: (0) de-fork the version — done; (1) widen `MapPrewarm` past the two
dashboards; (2) flip `EXPO_PUBLIC_NATIVE_MAP` and device-verify the mission map; (3) only then
migrate screen-by-screen, `LocationPicker` and `LiveTracking` first.

### Two founder UI calls in the same session

**AWAITING DISPATCH had no border and an unreadable label** (`BookingConfirmationScreen`).
_"Can you give this button a line around. Does not look neat."_ It sat next to the OUTLINED
INVOICE button as a solid green fill, so the pair read as two different components; and the
disabled treatment was a blanket `opacity: 0.5` over `UI.bg` text on `UI.signal` green, which
made the label the least readable thing on the screen. Now: a border in both states (same
construction as INVOICE), and the waiting state is a proper outlined "pending" chip —
translucent green fill, green border, green text, no glow — plus `adjustsFontSizeToFit` so
"AWAITING DISPATCH" cannot clip at 320 dp.

**Request Protection removed from Pro entirely** (`ProDashboardScreen`), founder's call after
first asking for a swap. Safe removal: it was a SECOND route to `ProLiveMission` and the Live
Map module still opens that screen, so no destination was lost — a Pro session is scheduled
through Booking Requests and approved in the ops console, so an always-live "start a session
now" door promised something the plan does not do. **Additional Services** loses its SOON lock
and now targets `ServiceType` (Select Service). Founder chose to leave it in place in the grid
rather than promote it to the vacated banner slot. Four orphaned `protect*` styles deleted.

### Gates

typecheck **45** (baseline 47) · eslint **0 errors** across all changed files (1 pre-existing
`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning in `ProLiveMissionScreen`, untouched by the 2-char URL
bump) · booking project **70 suites / 840 tests** · app project over
`(booking|pro|cpo|executive|agent|navigation|vbg)` **54 suites / 592 tests** ·
`secureServicesGapClosure` 26/26 (the B-615 pins survive — the iOS block still carries
`<DateTimePicker mode="date">` and the `minimumDate` floor).

New pins, all three **mutation-proved RED first**: `androidPickerContract` (10),
`mapLibraryVersionSingleSource` (3), and 2 added to `missionCheckpoint` (16 total).

**NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED — all five items.** Owed on a phone: pick a Book-Later date and confirm
the calendar no longer jumps back while the estimate is in flight, and that Cancel closes
without opening the time sheet; the Exec date + transfer-time doors; ARRIVED AT PICKUP showing
its range out of radius and still tapping through; the Pro/CPO maps opening warm on a second
visit; AWAITING DISPATCH at 320 dp / fontScale 1.3.

## 2026-08-24 — B-646: the time wheel "freezes"; B-647: three identical Fabric mount crashes

Live device session on the founder's Pixel 6a, reported as _"the app is still hanging"_ →
narrowed to _"freeze the wheel"_ → resolved by deleting the wheel.

### B-646 — the hand-rolled time wheel, three bugs, replaced with the native picker · FIXED

`WheelTimePicker` reimplemented snapping, momentum and a centre-rail highlight in JS. Each
of those cost a bug, and they masked each other:

1. **The scroll effect re-fired on every render.** `Column`'s effect drives an IMPERATIVE
   `ref.scrollTo()` and depended on `[selected, values]` — but the parent rebuilt `values`
   with `Array.from()` inline in its render body, so the identity changed every render. The
   effect re-issued `scrollTo({animated: true})` on all three columns, an animated scrollTo
   emits its own scroll events and fires `onMomentumScrollEnd`, which called `onChange`,
   which re-rendered, which scrolled again. **Same shape as B-643** (the Android date
   dialog): an unmemoised identity in an effect dep array driving an imperative call.
2. **The guard released at finger-lift, not at momentum end.** `onScrollEndDrag` fires the
   instant the finger leaves; the wheel keeps gliding until `onMomentumScrollEnd`. In that
   window a re-render found the guard down with `appliedIdx` still on the OLD row and
   scrolled the wheel back mid-glide.
3. **THE one that made it un-scrollable: the centre rail had `zIndex: 1`.** On Android a
   z-indexed sibling is lifted above its siblings for **hit-testing**, not just painting, and
   `pointerEvents="none"` did not save it. The rail sits exactly over the selected row —
   precisely where a thumb lands.

**Measured on the device, not reasoned:** four drags starting inside the rail band
(y 1756-1866 on a Pixel 6a) moved the column zero rows; an identical drag starting below the
band scrolled it 3 → 8. Read out of `uiautomator dump`, which also confirmed all three
columns were genuinely `scrollable="true"` with correct bounds — the layout was never wrong.

⚠️ **A trap that cost part of this session: `adb shell input swipe` is NOT a reliable proxy
for a finger here.** Short synthetic swipes moved nothing and I reported the wheel
"reproduced as frozen" — wrong. With `disableIntervalMomentum` + `snapToInterval` a coarse
synthetic gesture can land back on its starting row. Only a long, slow swipe (>500 px,

> 1000 ms) behaves like a real drag. Verify a wheel/scroll repro with a slow drag AND read
> `uiautomator dump` before calling it frozen.

**Fix — founder's call: stop fighting it, use the platform picker.** `TimeDropdownField` now
opens the **native Android clock dialog** (`is24Hour: false`, so B-615's 12-hour rule is now
the OS's own AM/PM face) and the native iOS spinner in a sheet. The wheel's three bug classes
are deleted rather than patched.

- **The public API is deliberately UNCHANGED** — `hour`/`minute` in and out stay 0-23,
  `onChange` still hands back a 24-hour hour — so Secure Transfer, Exec review and the
  transfer pickup time needed no logic edits. That was the point of the request.
- **`snapToStep` is exported and pure**: Android's clock has no minute interval, so the FIELD
  enforces it. It rounds TOTAL minutes, so 11:58 at step 5 is 12:00 (never 11:60) and 23:59
  wraps to 00:00 (never hour 24). Both pinned.
- **The ref is gone** (founder: _"remove the ref"_): `TimeDropdownFieldHandle`, `forwardRef`,
  `useImperativeHandle` and both `laterTimeRef`s, and with them the
  `setTimeout(() => ref.open(), 50)` that auto-popped the time picker after a date pick. That
  auto-chain is what made Cancel feel like a loop.
- `androidPicker.ts` moved `src/screens/booking/` → `src/components/booking/` so a component
  may legitimately import it.

`WheelTimePicker.tsx` still exists but is now referenced ONLY by `BookingDateTimeScreen`,
which nothing navigates to. Both are dead; delete them together or not at all.

### B-647 — three identical Fabric view-mounting crashes · ONE CAUSE FIXED, NOT PROVEN

Found in `dumpsys dropbox`, not by a tester — and **not visible in any test or log we watch**:

```
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
java.lang.IllegalStateException: addViewAt: failed to insert view [1404] into parent [1406] at index 0
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: The specified child already has a parent.
           You must call removeView() on the child's parent first.
    at com.facebook.react.fabric.mounting.SurfaceMountingManager.addViewAt
```

- **2026-08-23 23:13:13** · **2026-08-23 23:35:23** · **2026-08-24 12:22:21**, all v294
  (1.0.252), all byte-identical. Process-runtime 58 s / 22 min / 3.2 min — action-triggered,
  not time-triggered.
- Signature: the child tag is always exactly **parent − 2**, at index 0 — a fresh parent and a
  fresh child where the child somehow already has one. That is a duplicated/conflicting mount
  instruction, not a slow thread.
- `newArchEnabled=true` (Fabric) and `.env:47 EXPO_PUBLIC_NATIVE_MAP=1`, so the native Mapbox
  map IS live in this build; the first crash is 7 minutes after `1669b9c4` landed. Correlation
  only — `@rnmapbox/maps` 10.3.5 does ship full Fabric codegen, so it is not trivially
  incompatible.

**Fixed one real instance of the class:** `BravoAlertHost` — mounted once in `App.tsx`, so it
is the one Modal that can churn on ANY screen — was conditionally mounting its whole `<Modal>`
(`if (!request) {return null;}`). On Fabric an Android Modal owns its own SURFACE, so every
alert started and stopped one. It now mounts once and is driven by `visible`, with the content
gated inside.

**RULED OUT — `BravoAlertHost` is NOT the cause.** A FOURTH crash landed at **2026-08-24
13:47:46**, with the identical signature (`view 1410 into parent 1412 at index 0`). The alert-host
fix was installed at **13:22:42**, i.e. 25 minutes EARLIER. The Modal-surface churn it removed is
still a genuine latent bug and the fix is kept, but it does not explain this crash. Do not
re-propose it.

**Still unidentified.** Four records now, all byte-identical, process-runtimes **58 s / 22 min /
3.2 min / 41 s** — two of the four died within a minute of launch, but **5 scripted cold launches
on the fixed build produced nothing**, so plain boot is not the trigger; it needs a specific
interaction.

Next step is the cheap A/B, still unrun: build with `EXPO_PUBLIC_NATIVE_MAP=0`. Either the
crashes stop (the native Mapbox map's children are being reparented) or that whole line is
eliminated in one build. Ruled out so far: `BravoAlertHost` (above); `@rnmapbox/maps` 10.3.5
being trivially Fabric-incompatible (it ships full `codegenConfig`); `@react-navigation/stack`'s
`Animated.add`-based card interpolators (that package is in `package.json` but **imported
nowhere in `src`**).

⚠️ **`dumpsys dropbox` is the only place these surface.** They are absent from a cleared logcat,
invisible to every Jest project, and a user reports them as "the app is frozen" — the last frame
holds, then the process dies. Check `adb shell dumpsys dropbox | grep data_app_crash` FIRST on any
"it hangs" report.

### The instrument was on the wrong thread — why two sessions of lag work missed this

The `[LAGDIAG]` JS-thread watchdog reports **zero stalls** on the fixed build while the
founder still reported freezing. It cannot see UI-thread work, and Fabric mounts views on the
UI thread. CLAUDE.md's own earlier `gfxinfo` data already said every jank bucket that fired
was **"Slow UI thread"** — the UI thread MOUNTING views. The eight "measured dead ends" were
all measured with a JS-thread instrument against a UI-thread problem. **A hard crash also
reads to a user exactly like a freeze.** Before chasing "lag" again, check `dumpsys dropbox`
for `data_app_crash` first — it is one command and it would have found this immediately.

### First device read of the `[LAGDIAG]` backup probes (since 2026-07-27)

```
[backup.bulkWalk] tookMs=211  messages=1515 conversations=42 source=sql
[backup.drain]    tookMs=1193 rows=42 iterations=1
JS thread blocked ~181ms / ~124ms / ~178ms
```

`iterations=1` and **no `[backup.flush]` line at all** (that probe fires at ≥100 ms) means the
message lane was empty and the whole 1193 ms was `flushConversations` — 42 rows, matching
`bulkWalk`'s conversation count exactly. Only 181 ms of it was a contiguous JS block, so the
rest is awaits (encrypt + one `putConversations` POST), i.e. wall time, not a freeze.

**The finding worth acting on: the conversation lane has NO ledger dedup.** `mirrorConversation`
dedups only within the pending queue ("latest snapshot wins") and `backupNow()` enqueues every
conversation unconditionally, so **every boot re-uploads all of them** — the message lane's I1
protection has no conversation equivalent. Clearance already done: `commitMerkleRoot`
page-walks `/backup/messages` only, so conversations are **not** in the Merkle leaf set and
deduping them cannot cause root drift.

**NOT IMPLEMENTED, deliberately.** It needs the BACKUP_LOOP §2 pass, and one design constraint
is already known: `mirror_flushed` is keyed `(owner_user_id, message_id)`, so conversation
entries must be namespaced AND `loadFlushedVersions` must exclude them — otherwise a
conversation id colliding with a message id would make the sweep skip a real message, which is
the I7 silent-data-loss class. Do not bolt this on at the end of a session.

### Gates

typecheck **45** (baseline 47) · eslint **0 errors** · booking **70 suites / 841 tests** ·
app over `(booking|pro|cpo|executive|agent|navigation)` **50 suites / 563 tests**.

`timeDropdownField.test.tsx` rewritten: 14 tests over `snapToStep` edge cases (hour carry,
midnight wrap, no-op step) and both platform paths, including that Android mounts **no** picker
component and no sheet. `secureServicesGapClosure` GAP-1 updated to pin the native picker
instead of the wheel — the 12-hour rule and the money path are untouched.

**NOT DEVICE-VERIFIED.** Owed: the native clock opens from every time field, 5-minute snapping
holds, cancel commits nothing, and no `data_app_crash` appears in `dumpsys dropbox` after a
session of heavy alert + picker use.

## 2026-08-24 — B-648: client cold start "15-20 s before I can work" — the idle-boot backup pipeline re-uploads every conversation, every boot

Client report (via founder): app takes 15-20 s from open before it is usable, "for 2 days"
(≈ the 1.0.250/1.0.251 window). Measured on the founder's Pixel (1.0.252, 1,515 msgs /
42 convos): cold start → interactive dashboard in **~4-5 s** — the client's 15-20 s does
NOT reproduce on a small account. But the boot logs surfaced a real, scaling defect.

### B-648 — every idle boot walks the whole history AND re-encrypts + re-uploads every conversation row · FIXED same day (conv rows joined the mirror_flushed ledger)

Two consecutive idle cold starts, identical numbers both times:

```
[LAGDIAG] [backup.bulkWalk] tookMs=219 messages=1515 conversations=42 source=sql
[LAGDIAG] [backup.drain]    tookMs=1114 rows=42 iterations=1        (run 1)
[LAGDIAG] [backup.bulkWalk] tookMs=220 messages=1515 conversations=42 source=sql
[LAGDIAG] [backup.drain]    tookMs=1060 rows=42 iterations=1        (run 2)
```

`rows=42` = the 42 **conversation** rows. An idle boot should upload NOTHING (BACKUP_LOOP
I1) — instead every boot ships every conversation again. Mechanism, all on the JS thread:

1. The boot catch-up sweep calls `backupNow()` (`mirrorBootstrap.ts`), which walks the
   ENTIRE SQLCipher history via `loadAll()` (message side dedups against the
   `mirror_flushed` ledger, so messages are correctly silent) **and** calls
   `mirrorConversation()` for every conversation.
2. `mirrorConversation()` (`messageMirror.ts`) has **no version/ledger dedup at all** —
   `convQueue.set()` unconditionally; `flushConversations()` then AES-GCM-encrypts each row
   (incl. a `group_state` encrypt per group) and POSTs all of them. There is no
   conversation analogue of the message ledger, so every boot looks like first contact.

Both costs are linear in account size. At 1,515 msgs / 42 convos this is ~1.4 s — annoying,
not the symptom. At a heavy client account (tens of thousands of msgs, 100+ convos, mid
device where Hermes is several times slower than the V8 floor, slower uplink) the same
pipeline is plausibly the whole 15-20 s. **This is the hypothesis for the client lag, NOT a
confirmation** — the per-boot conv re-upload predates 1.0.250 (the sweep is Round 8-era), so
"started 2 days ago" is not yet explained by a specific commit; most likely the client
UPDATED ~2 days ago and/or their account crossed a size threshold. Also ruled out this
session: BiometricGate wedge (no `[biogate]` warns), first-frame cost (COLD launch 962 ms),
staging TLS/connect (curl ttfb ≤1.2 s on auth + relay).

**FIX (same session, founder asked):** conversation versions now live in the SAME
`mirror_flushed` table under a `conv:` id namespace — no schema change, and
`clearFlushedForOwner` purges them for free on every wipe path (I5). `mirrorConversation`
dedups at enqueue against a ledger-seeded `convSeen` map (`seedMirrorDedup` routes `conv:`
entries there); a successful `flushConversations` records the shipped versions
(gen-guarded, BUG-6 class), a permanent drop clears the dedup (H-7 parity), and the B-81
repair's `clearMirrorDedupForOwner` clears conv entries so its full re-upload still covers
conversations. The hash is FNV-1a over `serializeConvForMirror` — ONE builder shared by the
wire row and the hash, so a field added to the wire cannot dodge the hash (the B-116 class);
group_state is hashed as PLAINTEXT (the wire's fresh-IV ciphertext would defeat dedup).
Deliberately NO merkle-pending flag from a conv flush — conv rows are not Merkle leaves, so
an idle boot that only heals a conv row stays commit-free. The message `versionHash` was
refactored to share `fnv1a` byte-identically — changing its output would invalidate every
stored ledger version and re-open the I1 drift factory.

Pinned by `convMirrorLedger.test.ts` (7 tests: I1 skip/ship, `conv:` namespace + no pending
flag, same-session dedup, tombstone-once + B-594 lift, I8 fail-open, H-7 drop-clears-dedup,
group-epoch re-ship). RED first (6/7 failed pre-fix), mutation-proved (disabling the dedup
check kills 4). Gates: backup/merkle sweep 44 suites green; full messenger-crypto 100%
green (6725/6725 — earlier moving failures reproduced on STASHED sources, the B-126 flake);
app-project messenger screens 685 green ×2; tsc 46 ≤ baseline 47. Known post-fix cost: the
first boot after a RESTORE re-uploads all conv rows once (restore seeds message versions
only) — fail-open, converges, acceptable.

**NOT yet device-verified** — the fix needs the next QA build; the acceptance probe is two
idle cold starts showing NO `[backup.drain] rows=<conv count>` line (or rows=0) where
1.0.252 showed rows=42 twice. The client-side 15-20 s conviction still needs their LAGDIAG
capture (see above).

**Next data needed (client device, no new build required — 1.0.251 already has the probes):**
`adb logcat -d | grep LAGDIAG` right after a cold start. The `bulkWalk messages=/tookMs=`
and `drain rows=/tookMs=` numbers either convict this pipeline or acquit it in one capture.
Also capture their exact version (`dumpsys package com.bravosecure.app | grep versionName`)
— see the same-day Firebase note below.

**Same-day distribution note (not a bug):** the 601 MB v1.0.252 upload vs the tester's
519 MB download — 519 MB is exactly the v1.0.251 fingerprint (1.0.252 = +~80 MB native
Mapbox SDK, commit 1669b9c4). The tester installed the previous release from a stale App
Tester card/cached binary while the console logged a "latest" download event. Remedy:
