## 2026-08-24 — B-649: second VBG→Secure round-trip pins the app to an endless spinner

Founder live repro on the Pixel (v1.0.252), captured under a streaming logcat: from the
sidebar, VBG → Secure works ONCE; VBG → Secure a second time lands on a full-screen
spinner that never resolves (photographed still spinning 6+ minutes later; JS thread
completely idle after mount — no error, no dropped-action warning, nothing).

### B-649 — SecureLanding's decide-once latch + a swallowed navigation.reset = permanent spinner · FIXED

The stuck screen is `SecureLandingScreen` (the PDF-1 #1 tier resolver). It latched
`decided.current = true` and dispatched ONE `navigation.reset` — and if that reset went
nowhere, nothing ever fired again. The eater: the product switch remounts the client shell
keyed on `activeProduct`, and B-95's own comment documents that the OLD tree's deferred
nested-state cleanup (`useNavigationBuilder` unmount → `setTimeout(0)` → state=undefined)
is only held off by a 30 ms hold-frame. The repro log shows 300-400 ms JS stalls in
exactly that window (presence replay burst + product remount), so the cleanup can land
AFTER the resolver's reset, wiping the freshly-reset stack back to the seeded
[BookingHome, SecureLanding] while the resolver instance — and its spent latch — survives.
First switch after boot rides a calm thread and wins the race; later switches lose it.
Evidence consistent: back-press on the stuck screen jumped to VBG home via B-352's
`returnProduct`, proving the resolver was at the stack root with its reset gone.

**Fix — the resolver self-heals instead of latching.** The TARGET is still decided exactly
once (a late store change can never re-aim it — pinned), but the DISPATCH now repeats every
500 ms while the screen is still mounted: a successful reset unmounts the resolver, so a
retry can only ever fire when the previous dispatch provably went nowhere, and it always
re-dispatches the identical routes. Robust to ANY reset-eater — the cleanup race above, a
future one, or a hasLoaded that arrives late.

Pinned by `secureLandingResolver.test.tsx` (11 tests): the new "swallowed reset retries",
"retry lives in the effect + cleared by its cleanup", and the sharpened "TARGET decided
once — every dispatch, including retries, carries the ORIGINAL routes". Mutation-proved
(no-op'ing the retry kills 2). Adjacent sweeps green: switch/product/landing suites (71),
tsc 46 ≤ baseline 47. Device verify rides the v1.0.253 build (this session).

⚠️ **Bug-number collision to reconcile:** a parallel session's uncommitted
`secureProStore.ts` change (stale-while-revalidate so a loaded Secure re-entry does not
FLASH a spinner) labels itself B-648 in comments — but B-648 is this session's backup
conv-ledger bug (above). That change is a different, lesser symptom of the same complaint;
when it lands it should renumber to its own id.

## 2026-08-24 (evening) — B-650/B-651/B-652 + the founder's on-device batch (v1.0.254)

Founder inspecting v1.0.253 live; requests and finds landed as one gated batch.

### B-650 — SQLCipher mlock WARN spam: ~200+ log lines/second during any DB activity · FIXED

`cipher_memory_security=ON` (audit P0-S4) makes every internal SQLCipher allocation attempt
`mlock()`; Android's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (~64 KB) is exhausted immediately, so each attempt fails
ENOMEM and logs `sqlcipher_mlock: mlock() returned -1 errno=12` at WARN. Measured across
today's captures: 80-87% of the ENTIRE logcat buffer (7.7k lines in one 35 s boot, 129k in a
40-min stream) — a per-allocation syscall+log tax on the hot paths (boot loadAll walk,
restore hydration, send bursts) and it rolled real stall evidence out of the buffer (stalls
#1-#7 of a 5045 ms-worst sequence were unrecoverable). Fix: `PRAGMA cipher_log_level=ERROR`
on BOTH handles, right after memory_security — **verbosity only; the mlock attempts and the
memset-on-eviction hygiene are untouched** (P0-S4 posture unchanged; real cipher errors
still log). Bundled SQLCipher 4 supports the pragma; a pre-4.5 cipher no-ops via try/catch.
Pinned in `cryptoDbOpenMigrations.test.ts` (both handles, exact slot). NOTE: the 5 s worst
stall remains UNEXPLAINED — needs a fresh capture now the spam is gone.

## B-655 — messenger lag: the `display:'none'` perf spine made it worse (FIXED)

`a47c692d` stopped unmounting MessengerHome's Chats/Calls tab bodies and toggled
`display:'none'`. **`display` is a Yoga property — React does not know about it**: the hidden
subtree still renders, reconciles, and holds every store subscription. What got pinned mounted was
`CallsLogBody` — a non-virtualised `ScrollView` over the whole call history, un-memoised, with a
bare whole-`conversations` subscription. Tap-shaped costs: one tab tap re-rendered BOTH panes (the
conditional used to skip the inactive one), and Yoga SKIPS layout for a hidden subtree, so flipping
back dirtied the whole thing at once — a full layout+draw on the UI thread at tap time.

FIX: conditional mounts restored + the calls log virtualised (`FlatList` + memo row). **A pair —
either alone re-opens a lag.** Also: memoised `contentContainerStyle`, keyed the new full-history
search effect on a joined id string (it re-fired a SQLCipher LIKE scan per inbound message), and the
FAB `bottom` double-count fixed itself with the wrapper.
Register: `docs/audits/MESSENGER_LAG_AUDIT_2026-08-24.md`. Pin: `callsLogVirtualized.test.ts`
(mutation-proved). `messengerPersistentTabs` assertion REVERSED — it pinned the regression.

**Corrections the critic pass forced on the first draft** (recorded so they are not re-derived):
`selectCallMessages`'s scan is ~0.3 ms, NOT the 350-500 ms stall — `s.messages` is capped at
`MAX_HYDRATE_PER_CONVO = 200`; the earlier figure was the SQLCipher history, a different dataset.
`appendMessage` bumps the conversation row in the SAME immer recipe, so there is no second render.
The "0-height layout collapses the list window" theory is REFUTED by
`YogaLayoutableShadowNode.cpp:729-732` — layout never recurses into a `display:none` subtree.

## B-656 — Bravo Feed (Intel) screen lag (FIXED, UNMEASURED)

NOT a regression: the scanlines date to April, the radar animation to late April, the Mapbox GL
globe to July. `docs/audits/MAPBOX_AUDIT.md:81/174/176` **already documented both causes in July**
and was never closed. Founder noticed it now because B-655 removed the louder noise.

Two critics reached OPPOSITE conclusions; an adjudication round settled it. The ruling that
matters: **`dumpsys gfxinfo` is structurally blind here** — Android WebView composites in a separate
renderer process and hands the host one draw functor, so CLAUDE.md's "GPU is never the bottleneck"
prior came from an instrument that could not have seen this cost. It does not bind the diagnosis; it
DOES bind the remedies (do not pay design cost on an unmeasured hypothesis).

FIXED, JS side: 1 Hz clock extracted (`<UtcClock/>`) — it re-rendered an 805-line tree to move one
glyph; scanline overlay hoisted to a module constant (NOT deleted — it is the intended CRT tint);
wire list virtualised (~60 rows x ~10 views mounted synchronously on the tab tap = the "stuck for
seconds" freeze); ticker rows memoised (they are `Animated.View` children, and RN's AnimatedProps
memo retains arrays BY REFERENCE, so a fresh array each render tore down and re-attached the live
marquee's native animation); one-pass stat row; stable `EMPTY_EXTRAS` (a fresh `[]` invalidated the
whole memo chain every load); `geotag` matchers precompiled (98 `new RegExp` per un-geotagged item,
NOT the 486 first claimed).

FIXED, WebView side — shipped on founder instruction ("fix both the js and webview side") after
being told plainly they were unmeasured: `mix-blend-mode: screen` removed from the full-viewport
crosshair; `backdrop-filter` removed from every marker badge + HUD + 3 zoom buttons; the radar
animation made opt-in (CRITICAL/HIGH only) so a resting map has NO frame source; `renderThreats`
reconciles instead of rebuilding via `innerHTML` twice per feed load; `map.on('error')` posts only
pre-`load` (it was one bridge hop per tile 404). Marker payload capped at 30 at the RENDER boundary
— never on `clusters`, which also feeds the LOCATED stat and `regionHits`.

**STILL UNMEASURED.** `adb shell top -o %CPU` on the `:sandboxed_process*` renderer, idle on BRAVO
MAP. If it did not help, RESTORE the visuals — each is a one-line revert.

## B-657 — clipped headers app-wide + the Secure-tab double-nav flicker (FIXED)

**Root cause, app-wide:** `scaleTextStyles` ran `letterSpacing` through `scaleFont`, which ends in
`Math.round`. Tracking is normally sub-1dp, so it broke both ways AND became device-dependent:
0.4 to 0 (deleted), 1.5 to 1 at 360dp but **2 at 393dp**. On the founder's phone that added 7.5dp to
"SECURE SERVICES" on a row already ~39dp overfull, giving "SECURE SE...". 177 files use
`scaleTextStyles`. Tracking is a typographic constant, not a responsive size — removed from
`TEXT_KEYS`. Narrowing only, so a layout can lose an overflow but never gain one.

Also: Secure home header trimmed to fit; `AgentHomeScreen` + `OpsDashboardScreen` were CLIPPING (a
long name pushed the LIVE pill and bell off-screen — both missing the `flex:1` + `minWidth:0` pair,
without which the flex is INERT because a flex child defaults to `min-width:auto`); `ObHeader`
`minWidth:0` (~27 screens, one line); `NewChatScreen` tracking 3 to 1.5 (a 33-char group name spent
99dp on tracking alone); 23 screens' `headerSub` now shrinks instead of wrapping.

**Flicker:** a STATE-TIMING window, not a slow screen. `getFocusedRouteNameFromRoute` reports the
LAST COMMITTED state, so when `SecureLanding` resets to `[SecureShell]` the shell draws its own
footer while the root navigator still shows the outer bar. Fixed by adding `SecureLanding` to
`SECURE_FULLSCREEN_ROUTES` and by making the pre-commit fallback resolve to the SEEDED route instead
of `''`. NOT fixed: the wait itself — `secureProStore` is not persisted, so the first Secure entry
per session still blocks on `/pro-applications/me`.
Pin: `headerFitContract.test.ts` (mutation-proved).

> **`src/utils/textDefaults.ts` is INERT and its test is decorative.** It sets
> `Text.defaultProps.maxFontSizeMultiplier`, but RN 0.81's `Text` is a FUNCTION component and React
> 19 resolves `defaultProps` for CLASS components only. The app-wide 1.3x font cap has never
> applied; every header is exposed to system fontScale 2.0. Its test asserts the ASSIGNMENT, so it
> passes forever. Needs a wrapped `Text`. **OPEN.**

## B-658 — mission comms dock: the CPO could not reach the client (FIXED)

Founder: "the agent needs to be able to msg client and vice versa. Also must not just say 'or'."

**The premise inverted.** On the agency dispatch lane the client IS already a member
(`org-mission.service.ts:594-599` seats client + provider + managers + crew, each with a key
intent). So "Message ops or crew..." was a **safety inversion** — it told a CPO the principal was
absent while they read every word. But BOTH lanes are live and mutually exclusive:
`dispatch_mode='auto'` gives the agency lane (client seated); `dispatch_mode=NULL` gives the
ops-console lane, which excludes the client by explicit comment (`ops.service.ts:1215-1221`) and has
a real DISPATCH button. Both write `missions.comms_channel_id`.

## B-659 — mission chat/call showed raw id fragments instead of names (FIXED)

`AgentLiveTrackerScreen:783` read only `groupMemberNames` — populated by department-chat surfaces,
**empty for a mission Ops Room** — then fell through to `U-3F5E`. `GroupCallScreen`'s
`recipientNameFor` searched only for a 1:1 thread then `uid.slice(0,6)`. In a mission room the
others are an agency, a client and a CPO the device has no 1:1 with, so both showed hex. On a
protection detail the CPO could not tell the principal from the crew.

FIXED: both now use the full chain (group alias, then directory profile, then a neutral word) with a
debounced directory backfill. The call screen uses `resolveMemberName` — **the same helper its own
video tiles already used 700 lines below**. The tracker fetches off the room's PARTICIPANTS, so a
member is named the moment they speak. `driverNavCamera` deps pin re-pointed (it asserted an exact
array; the invariant is "no 1 Hz dep").

## B-640 — Ops Room "Call failed" (ROOT CAUSE FOUND, fix NOT shipped)

Re-reported by the founder. Not a regression of B-414 (nav verified fixed) and not a role gate
(`apps/messenger-service` has NO role or membership check on any call path). The card is
`GroupCallScreen` on `state==='failed'`; a 1:1 failure is an `Alert`, so mis-routing is ruled out.

**The mechanism, and why every server probe looked clean.** `productionRuntime.ts` ~:6186:

    const keyed = await reshareGroupKeyState(stateAfterRekey, [newMember.userId]);
    if (keyed === 0) { console.warn(...); }   // warns, then CONTINUES

`addGroupMember` RESOLVES when the new member's inline key delivery reached ZERO.
`dispatchRoomIntents` then acks the intent on that SUCCESS path — member seated, intent `done`,
**no key**. A call from that device dies at the 25 s key gate. That is exactly 4 members / 4 intents
`done` / 1 claim, which is what the 2026-08-23 probe found and could not explain. It does not
self-heal reliably: `reshareGroupKeyState` drops a target absent from the SERVER roster copy and the
serve gate needs owner-or-member, so the agency device can be the only possible server of that key —
and for an agency org account it may never be online (the B-416 SPOF).

SHIPPED: **ids-only observability at both sites**, correlatable on `memberUserId`. No gate, no key
flow, no ack semantics touched.

**Three proposed fixes were REJECTED, do not re-propose without new evidence:**
(a) never-ack on the benign arm — the CLIENT's add-intent throws ALREADY_MEMBER by construction, so
it would leave every client intent permanently pending and re-fire a sealed reshare on every drain
(the churn the arm exists to stop); (b) leave the intent pending on `delivered===0` — provably
INERT, `ensureAssignedGroup` early-returns on local `masterKeyB64` which the zero-delivery path
keeps; (c) narrow the `hasKey()` re-throw in `useGroupCall` — **actively harmful**: `hasKey()` can be
true via the PREVIOUS call's key through the callKeyRegistry, so the host would encrypt with a key
none of this call's recipients hold — a connected call with undecryptable media and no error.

**THE fix, owed:** do not ack an add-intent when inline key delivery returned 0; retry it. Touches
key distribution, so architecture stop-condition + a device run, in its own commit.
**Device-free discriminator for the remaining unknown:** `POST {MSG_BASE_URL}/sfu/rooms` with any
valid JWT. A `503 sfu_announced_ip_unconfigured` means the SFU plane is disabled in prod and this is
an ops task; a non-empty `hostRoomToken` means that theory is dead.

Also corrected: `launchCall.ts`'s B-247 comment claimed a mission Ops Room "is not a server
conversation row at all". FALSE — `system-messenger.service.ts:270` (`ensureRoomMembers`) inserts
real `conversation_members` rows, which is why `listMine` sees it.

## B-660 — Secure Services header clipped on a Pixel 7 and not on a Pixel 6a (FIXED)

**Founder, 2026-08-24:** _"fix this text cutting make it responsive for all Design that it
should not cutting and first do web search then fix — my pixel 6a doesn't cut but pixel 7 did."_

**The research came first and it invalidated my own previous fix.** B-657 had reached for
`adjustsFontSizeToFit` + `minimumFontScale`. That combination does not work in this app:

- `minimumFontScale` is **ignored under the New Architecture on both platforms**
  (facebook/react-native#50248, still open). This app is `newArchEnabled=true`, so the text
  shrinks with **no floor** — "MESSENGER" can collapse to unreadable rather than clip.
- `adjustsFontSizeToFit` has its own Android/Fabric history of simply not resizing
  (#43104, fixed by #44075) and of collapsing straight to the minimum on Samsung (#32258).

So the whole approach was replaced with **deterministic breakpoints read off the live
window** (`useWindowDimensions` / `useContentWidth`), which are reactive on fold and rotate and
have no platform caveat.

**Why the two Pixels disagreed.** They are not the same width in dp. A header row with a fixed
pill budget leaves the title whatever remains, so the same constant font size fits one and
overflows the other. That is a layout-budget bug, not a device bug — nothing about the phone
needed detecting.

Fixed in `BookingHomeScreen.tsx` (title steps 15/13.5/12/11 by width; `compactRegion` below
390dp drops the region label to the flag alone; `numberOfLines` on the widest tier label).
Pinned by `src/utils/__tests__/headerFitContract.test.ts`.

Also in this batch: **`src/utils/scaling.ts` no longer scales `letterSpacing`.** `scaleFont`
ends in `Math.round`, so tracking of 0.4 became **0** (deleted outright) and 1.5 became 1 at
360dp but 2 at 393dp — the same string measured differently on two phones for a reason that had
nothing to do with the design. `TEXT_KEYS` is now `fontSize` + `lineHeight` only.

## B-661 — one build, two different apps: the Pro client had no footer (FIXED)

**Founder, 2026-08-24:** _"i dont know why i install the same version and my friend install the
same version but the footer is not updating, rest is updating and fixing each version."_
Then, once the cause was explained: _"it should be for lite and pro version both. but the
channel menu should not be accessible to lite version person."_

### The cause was never the version — it was the ACCOUNT TIER

`secureRootRoute()` returned a **different root route per tier**: an ACTIVE Pro plan landed on
`ProDashboard` (a bare pushed screen), everyone else on `SecureShell` (the 4-tab shell). The
footer lives in the shell. So a Pro client was on a screen that structurally **cannot** have
one, and every release that improved the footer improved it only for Lite users. Two people on
identical APKs, different navigation — indistinguishable from "your build didn't update".

Same class as the duplicate-copy bug: **one product, two structural paths, and only one of them
gets the fixes.**

### The fix — one shell for everyone, the tier decides the CONTENT

- `secureRoot.ts` now returns `'SecureShell'` for every input, and its return type was narrowed
  to that single literal **on purpose**: TypeScript then flags every stale `=== 'ProDashboard'`
  branch as unreachable. It immediately found one in `SecureLandingScreen.tsx` (TS2367) that a
  green suite had not.
- The tier moved **into** the shell: `SecureTabNavigator` renders `SecureHomeTab`, which picks
  `ProDashboardScreen` or `BookingHomeScreen` at render time. Deliberately ONE `Tab.Screen`
  chosen inside, never two conditional ones — declaration order IS the bar order, so a
  conditional `Tab.Screen` reorders the footer as the plan loads.
- `ProDashboardScreen` is a tab root now, so its back chevron is conditional on
  `navigation.canGoBack()` — a dead chevron on a root is worse than none.

### The second half — Channels is not offered to a LITE account

The rule lives in **one** place, `src/screens/messenger/channelsAccess.ts`, with two entry
points (`canSeeChannels(user)` for a host holding the raw user, `canSeeChannelsFor(entitlements)`
for one that already derived them — the second **delegates**, it does not re-derive).

**A hook inside `MessengerTabBar` was tried FIRST and backed out.** Putting the store read in
the shared bar looked like the DRY answer, but it gave a presentational footer a transitive
dependency on `expo-local-authentication` and `@react-native-firebase/crashlytics` and killed
four unrelated suites. A footer that cannot render without Crashlytics is the wrong shape; the
bar takes a `showChannels` prop instead, defaulting **TRUE** so a future host added without the
prop keeps the door rather than silently losing it.

**FilesScreen was left behind on the first pass** — and because the default is TRUE, a LITE user
still saw Channels there while it was gone from MessengerHome. Same account, same session, two
answers. Both hosts are now wired and a pin asserts BOTH.

> ⚠️ **This is a UX gate, not an access boundary.** Hiding a tab hides a door, not the room.
> Workspace access is enforced server-side by org membership; if a tier must be genuinely
> denied, that belongs in the service.

### Third half — the chat header (same founder message, later image)

_"the messenger text is so small for one device and another device it's correctly sized… the
text are overlapping… the icon can be smaller to do that but all over same size."_

- The chat header row is a **fixed budget**: back pill + avatar + two call pills + gutters are
  all constant, so the peer name gets the remainder — ~124dp on a 360dp phone for a 16pt display
  face. Name size and gutter now step off the live window.
- **Three pill sizes in one row** (`backBtn` 36/r12, `iconBtn` 40/r20, glyphs 18/16/17). Now one
  size (34) and one radius (11), matching MessengerHome. The two 40s were eating 88dp before the
  name got any — shrinking them is what buys the room, exactly as the founder proposed.
- **The overlap**: `memberStackRow` ("N operators / E2E", the GROUP header subtitle) had no
  `flexShrink`/`minWidth`, so it ran past the header actions instead of truncating. Its 1:1
  counterpart (`PeerPresencePill`) has had that since it was written — one behaviour, two copies,
  only one hardened.

### Pins (all mutation-proved)

| Suite                                 | Pins                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `secureTabNavigator.test.ts`          | BOTH tiers get the shell; ONE `Tab.Screen` for Home, chosen at render                                                                                      |
| `secureLandingResolver.test.tsx`      | re-pointed: `PRO_ROUTE_STACK` is the stack that must never be produced again                                                                               |
| `switchDashboardProductRoot.test.tsx` | re-pointed: the truncation guard asks about `SecureShell` for every tier                                                                                   |
| `messengerFooterAndBack.test.ts`      | the rule is stated ONCE; both entry points delegate; BOTH hosts pass it; the bar takes a prop and never imports the store; omitting the prop KEEPS the tab |
| `messengerHeaderFit.test.ts`          | name size steps off the window; NOT `adjustsFontSizeToFit`; every header pill one size/radius; the group subtitle row can shrink                           |

Three test-authoring traps hit while writing these, worth re-reading:

1. **A quoted shell heredoc still collapsed a double backslash to a single one** in this
   environment, so a regex written through a JS string layer silently became a different regex
   (a CRLF pattern turned into a literal newline inside the pattern). Write test blocks as
   **literal text** and splice them, or build escapes from `String.fromCharCode(92)`.
2. **`node -e` resolves `/tmp` to `C:\tmp`** while Git Bash does not. Use the scratchpad path.
3. **`String.prototype.split().join()` replaces EVERY occurrence.** `useContentWidth(720)`
   appears twice in `ChatScreen.tsx`, so the header block was inserted into the composer too —
   caught by eslint `no-unused-vars`, NOT by any test.

A fourth, in the pins themselves: the "state the rule ONCE" scan originally anchored on the
variable **name** (`ent.`), so an inline copy that renamed it to `e.` passed it. It is anchored
on the name-agnostic shape now.

**Device verification OWED** for all of B-660/B-661 (founder rule: not fixed until the change is
seen on a device).

## B-662 — chat-list preview shows "(encrypted)" instead of the latest chat (FIXED, residuals open)

**Founder, 2026-08-26:** _"sometime form the chat screen it shows encrypted instead of latest chat"_

### Root cause (primary, fixed)

`previewOf` (MessengerHomeScreen) and the Groups list both ended in `last.content || '(encrypted)'`
with NO branch for two message kinds whose body is legitimately empty:

1. **`type: 'call'` history rows** — every ended/missed call appends `content: ''`
   (`CallScreen.tsx`, `callDispatcher.ts`, `useGroupCall.ts` x2). A chat whose newest event is a
   call read "(encrypted)" until the next text arrived. This is unfixed **MSG-13 residue** — the
   2026-07 fix added audio/video branches and never call/tombstone.
2. **Delete-for-everyone tombstones** — `deleted_for_all = true; content = ''`
   (`messengerStore.ts` + `messageMutationApply.ts`); the open thread says "This message was
   deleted" while the list said "(encrypted)".

**Fix:** ONE shared rule `src/screens/messenger/conversationPreview.ts` (`lastMessagePreview`) —
tombstone first, then file/image/audio/video/call/system labels, `(encrypted)` only as the
text-with-empty-body last resort. Wired into `MessengerHomeScreen.previewOf` and
`GroupsScreen`. Pinned by `src/screens/messenger/__tests__/conversationPreview.test.ts`.

### Residuals (OPEN — same symptom, rarer mechanisms, NOT fixed here)

- **Cold-start window:** persisted previews are body-stripped (MSG-10, `content: ''`), the list
  paints at AsyncStorage-hydration while the SQLCipher body re-seed (B-78) lands later — every
  row shows the fallback at once for a moment; permanent for the session if `loadRecent` throws
  (that failure is swallowed at `productionRuntime.ts` SQL-hydrate catch).
- **Stale stripped pointer:** `removeMessage` never clears `convo.last_message`, and the B-78
  re-seed is forward-only — after a disappearing-message burn or "delete for me" of the NEWEST
  message, the stripped pointer is newer than anything in SQL and `(encrypted)` sticks until a
  new message arrives. (In-session mirror image: the sweeper-burned message's plaintext stays on
  the list row until restart — a retention leak worth its own fix.)

Store-side fixes for the residuals touch `messengerStore.ts` (MESSAGE_LOOP trigger) — deferred to
a dedicated pass.

### 2026-08-26 — new lag repro detail (B-279/B-285 investigation, still OPEN)

**Founder:** _"there is a laggy like when we click one button 20 time says then rapid back,
forward sometimes its lagged"_ — i.e. rapid REPEATED taps on one button, then fast back/forward
navigation, intermittently lags.

This matches the measured model exactly (CLAUDE.md lag dossier): press feedback is native, the
handler is JS — 20 rapid presses queue 20 handler executions plus their navigation commits, and
the back-press then waits behind that queue. It is NEW EVIDENCE for the same unnamed JS-thread
cost, not a new bug class. Do NOT re-propose the eight measured dead ends. Next step remains the
one already owed: read the `[LAGDIAG]` probes + `jsThreadWatchdog` off a release APK on a device
with real history while performing THIS repro (button×20 → back/forward), and check whether the
pressed button's handler is idempotent-guarded (tapGuard exists for nav; per-button double-fire
guards may not).

### 2026-08-28 — founder: emergency directory shows the WRONG country · B-684 FIXED

Founder report: _"I live in Germany and my phone shows Germany's emergency numbers, my
friend in Bangladesh shows Bangladesh — but my client in Dubai is shown UK numbers. It
has to show the country they are physically in, regardless of VPN or whatever."_

| Bug   | Status | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B-684 | FIXED  | **Emergency directory pinned the country from the phone's LOCALE, not its location.** `VBGEmergencyScreen`'s chain was param-ISO → param-name → cached geocode → `getDeviceCountryIso()` (reads `I18nManager.localeIdentifier` / `AppleLocale` / `Intl` — a LANGUAGE setting). Only the VBG-Home door ever supplied a param or populated the cache (it reverse-geocodes a GPS fix); every other door opens param-less — the messenger Calls emergency card (`CallsLogScreen.tsx:619`) and the agency shell — so they all landed on the locale. A Dubai client on an "English (United Kingdom)" phone → `en_GB` → **United Kingdom**, offered UK 999 (UAE ambulance is 998). Germany-on-a-German-phone and Bangladesh-on-a-Bengali-phone were correct only by COINCIDENCE, which is why it survived: the happy path and the broken path are indistinguishable until someone travels. The hazard was already written down at `CallsLogScreen.tsx:206` (B-638) — it was scoped to the removed chips, never to the directory itself. **VPN was a red herring**: no source in this feature is or was IP-derived. |

**Fix — one ladder, in one place** (`src/screens/vbg/resolveEmergencyCountry.ts`):
`param > gps > network > fresh-cache(<12h) > sim > stale-cache > locale`. Each rung is
tried in turn and a rung naming a country the bundled directory lacks FALLS THROUGH
(a 'XX' must not pin nothing and hide the real answer).

- **New rung `network`** — `TelephonyManager.networkCountryIso` via a new native module
  (`BravoNetworkCountryModule.kt`, registered in `MainApplication`). The MCC of the tower
  the handset is CAMPED ON: current, correct while roaming, **permission-free** — which
  is the point, because it is the lane that works when location is denied, i.e. exactly
  when the locale guess used to do the damage. Ranked ABOVE the cache because the cache
  is by definition from the past; that ordering is what makes London→Dubai flip on
  landing with no GPS. `simCountryIso` is the SIM's HOME country (a German SIM roaming in
  Dubai still reads DE) so it sits below every current signal. iOS returns null on
  purpose — `CTCarrier.isoCountryCode` is deprecated and yields "--" on iOS 16+.
- **New rung `gps`** — the directory now geocodes ITSELF (`vbgApi.geocode`, the existing
  cached ~1km endpoint) instead of waiting for VBG Home to have been visited, and
  persists the result so the next open starts from a real location.
- **It never prompts.** `getSilentFix()` reads a fix only when permission is ALREADY
  granted (`PermissionsAndroid.check`, never `.request`). A permission modal must never
  stand between a user in trouble and the number they came to dial; the permission-free
  network rung covers the denied case.
- **It never blocks.** Offline signals pin a country on mount; the GPS→geocode lane is a
  pure upgrade. The directory still works with zero signal — which is why the numbers
  ship in-app at all.
- **Provenance is rendered.** `precise` splits current physical facts (param/gps/network/
  fresh-cache) from inference (sim/stale-cache/locale); inferred sources render amber
  under "Best Guess" with "confirm before dialling", never as confident green. B-638's
  finding stands: a guess shown as fact is worse than no country, because it hides the
  guess behind a dialable number.
- Dial events now log the RESOLVED ISO, not the (usually absent) route param.

**A second defect found in my own fix during self-diff** (founder standing rule):
`setLastKnownCountry` merged field-by-field (`next.iso ?? cache?.iso`). A geocode
resolving a place NAME but no country short_code then pairs the STALE iso with the FRESH
name and stamps it newly-observed — cache `{iso:'GB', name:'United Arab Emirates'}`, and
the resolver reads the ISO first, so the London→Dubai traveller is pinned back to the UK
**by the very cache meant to fix them**. The write is now ATOMIC (one observation replaces
both fields). Both callers derive iso+name from the SAME response, so there was never a
caller that legitimately knew only half.

**Pins** (all RED-first, mutation-proved): `emergencyCountryResolution` (24 — the Dubai
case, ladder order, stale/legacy/NaN/future timestamps, fall-through, plus CRLF-safe
comment-stripped source scans of the screen incl. a no-IP-geolocation assertion),
`networkCountry` (13 — rejects `''`/`--`/`ARE`/`424`/whitespace/null/non-string, never
rejects), `lastKnownCountry` (7 — the merge poisoning above, no-coordinates, legacy
no-timestamp read). Mutation evidence: hoisting `locale` to rung 1 reproduces the exact
report (`Expected "AE", Received "GB"`, 10 red); restoring the field-merge reddens the
cache pin.

**Gates**: full app project 227 suites / 3148 tests green; typecheck 47 = baseline;
eslint clean; `:app:compileDebugKotlin` exit 0.

> **DO NOT "fix" a future country-detection report by adding an IP lookup.** Every rung
> is a device-local physical signal (GNSS, tower MCC, SIM, locale), which is precisely why
> a VPN cannot move any of them. An IP-geolocation rung is the ONLY mechanism a VPN could
> poison and would re-open this class.

**Adversarial review — FIVE more defects, four of them mine, found AFTER the first
green run.** A second reviewer read the diff plus the `react-native-geolocation-service`
Android/iOS sources. Every one of these was invisible to a 3148-test green suite:

1. **The "silent" fix was NOT silent.** `showLocationDialog` DEFAULTS TO TRUE
   (`LocationOptions.java`: `!map.hasKey(k) || map.getBoolean(k)`). Omitting it sends a
   device with permission GRANTED but the Location master toggle OFF down
   `FusedLocationProvider`'s RESOLUTION_REQUIRED branch → `startResolutionForResult` →
   the Google Play "turn on device location" **system modal over the emergency
   directory**. The permission check could not prevent it: it fires on the granted path.
   Now `showLocationDialog: false` (+ `forceRequestLocation: true`, so a
   location-on-but-settings-unsatisfied device still yields a silent fix), pinned.
2. **The GPS lane threw away a country it had resolved.** `/vbg/geocode` genuinely
   answers `country: null` with a usable context (VBG Home has always handled that
   shape); the screen kept only the ISO. A no-SIM tablet in Dubai on an en_GB phone got
   a LIVE correct answer in the response and still fell through to **United Kingdom**.
   Added a `gpsName` rung, symmetric with `param`.
3. **First paint pinned the LOCALE with live dialable chips.** The memo resolved on
   render 0, before the offline reads landed — an Indian-locale phone in the US offered
   **Police 100** for that window, on a screen opened under stress, in an app with
   measured multi-second JS stalls. Now gated on `signals.ready`.
4. **A fresh cache was rendered as "Your Location" for 12 h.** `'cache'` was in
   `PRECISE`, and the freshness window was sized ABOVE a long-haul flight — backwards:
   the London→Dubai cache must expire BEFORE landing, not after. Now 1 h, and the cache
   is never unhedged: it describes where the user WAS.
5. **The emergency screen could log you out.** `vbgApi.geocode` rides `authHttp`, whose
   interceptor clears the vault + fires `authLost` on a dead refresh token. The
   directory previously made ZERO network calls by design. Now gated on a present access
   token, so a session-less open is fully offline.

**And the safety pin was VACUOUS.** The `not.toMatch(/PermissionsAndroid\.request/)` scan
ran against `VBGEmergencyScreen.tsx`, which contains **zero** occurrences of that token —
it could never fail, and the prompting code lives in `silentLocationFix.ts`. The
no-prompt guarantee, the property that matters most here, had no pin at all. Replaced by
a real `silentLocationFix` suite that spies on `PermissionsAndroid.request`. Two other
scans were weak (a one-shape locale ban that `const fallback = …` walks past; an
IP-vendor-name ban that `fetch('https://api.country.is')` walks past) and are now
assertions about the decision site and the screen's complete outbound-call set.

**Known limitations, stated rather than hidden:**

- **iOS has no permission-free lane.** `CTCarrier.isoCountryCode` is deprecated and
  returns "--" on iOS 16+, so there is no radio country to read. An iOS user who denies
  location falls to the locale — hedged amber, but still a guess. Android is fully
  covered.
- **Dual-SIM reads the DEFAULT subscription only.** Enumerating subscriptions needs
  `READ_PHONE_STATE`, and a sensitive runtime permission is not worth this. A UK eSIM
  default with no service alongside a registered local SIM can fall to the SIM rung —
  hedged amber, and the GPS rung normally covers it.
- **The native module is DEVICE-UNVERIFIED.** `:app:compileDebugKotlin` passes, but no
  device/emulator was attached this session, so no real `networkCountryIso` has been
  read. Founder rule: not "fixed" until seen in a post-install device log.

Final gates: app project 228 suites / 3162 tests green; vbg 110/110; typecheck 47 =
baseline; eslint clean. Mutation evidence for each new pin recorded above.

**Second adversarial round — TWO more, one of them the worst of the batch.**

6. **`emergencyForName` returned the first ALPHABETICAL substring match.** The
   directory is alphabetical and the fallback was `find(e => n.includes(e.name))`, so
   **`'Hong Kong SAR China'` → CHINA** — 110/120/119 handed to someone in Hong Kong,
   where the number is **999** and none of the three mainland numbers work. Probing the
   real directory found a second live wrong hit:
   **`'Democratic Republic of the Congo'` → CG** (Republic of the Congo, police 117)
   instead of CD's 112 — and no substring rule can ever reach that one, because the long
   form does not contain the string "DR Congo". This got WORSE with the `gpsName` rung
   from round 1, which feeds geocoder names straight in and renders the result under the
   confident green "Your Location". Fix: exact → alias table → **longest** substring
   match, with an ambiguous tie returning null (falling through beats a confident wrong
   country). `endsWith` is explicitly NOT the fix — `'hong kong sar china'.endsWith('china')`
   is true and picks China straight back.
7. **The round-1 first-paint gate keyed on param PRESENCE, not param RESOLUTION.** VBG
   Home passes `countryName` on every open, and the geocoder really returns
   `Deutschland` / `Türkiye` / `Nederland` / `Suomi` / `Republic of Korea` (all verified
   misses against the directory). Such a param skipped the gate, missed its own rung, and
   landed on the locale — the first-paint hole reopened through the ONE door that always
   passes params. Now: resolve the param first, return it if it resolved, otherwise gate
   on `signals.ready`.

**Both of my first pins for these were VACUOUS, and the mutation run is the only reason
that is known.** The Hong Kong test passed under a reverted comparator because the new
alias table short-circuited it; the unresolvable-param test passed because the alias I
added in the _same change_ made `'Deutschland'` resolvable. Fixed by pinning the
substring path with pairs the alias table does not cover (`'Lagos, Nigeria'` → NG not NE,
`'Kinshasa, DR Congo'` → CD not CG) and by making the param test **self-verifying** — it
asserts its own fixture is unresolvable first, so a future alias fails it loudly instead
of quietly hollowing it out. Lesson, again: **a green test proves nothing until the
mutation has been seen red.**

Also closed: the outbound-call scan missed `authHttp.get(...)` (ends in neither `Api` nor
`fetch`); spies in `silentLocationFix.test.ts` leaked between cases (`restoreMocks` is not
set project-wide).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: passing `language=en` to the server geocode would kill the endonym
class at source, but `/vbg/threats` feeds that same `context` into the OSINT place-term
search, so anglicising it could quietly degrade local-news matching. Not worth coupling to
an emergency fix.

Final: app project 230 suites / 3191 tests green; vbg 132/132; typecheck 47 = baseline;
eslint clean; `:app:compileDebugKotlin` BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

**The exhaustive sweep — the old rule had NINE wrong-country outcomes, not one.** After
fixing Hong Kong by hand, a systematic probe (`"Someplace, {name}"` for every one of the
192 entries, asserting none resolves to a DIFFERENT country) was added. Reverting the
comparator lists what was actually latent in the shipped matcher:

```
DR Congo → Congo        Dominican Republic → Dominica    Guinea-Bissau → Guinea
Nigeria  → Niger        Papua New Guinea   → Guinea      Hong Kong     → China
Somalia  → Mali         Romania            → Oman        Macau         → China
```

`Romania → Oman` and `Somalia → Mali` are the ones no amount of case-by-case review would
have produced — "r-OMAN-ia", "so-MALI-a". This is the pin to keep: it is O(n) over the
directory, it fails with the offending pairs NAMED, and it will catch the next entry
someone adds whose name contains an existing one.

**Third round — CLEAN, plus three test-strength items closed.** The reviewer ran a
differential of the old matcher against the new one across 192 entries × 4 shapes (768
cases): **0 regressions, 0 old-non-null-now-null, 14 improvements.** The tie-guard never
fires on a real country name. Nine shapes were swept; the only one that still produces
wrong answers is `"{name} SAR China"`, which is synthetic for 190 of 192 entries and
correct for the two real ones (Hong Kong, Macao) via the alias table — that result is the
justification for the alias stage, not a bug: longest-match alone puts `China` (5) above
every 4-letter country.

Three items closed rather than deferred:

- **The sweep accepted `null`, so an always-null substring path PASSED it.** Mutation-
  proved by the reviewer. Now asserts `toBe(e.iso)` — free today (all 192 resolve
  correctly) and a deliberate forcing function: a future entry colliding ambiguously
  reds the suite until someone adds an alias. Re-mutated after: 3 red.
- **`NAME_ALIASES` was hand-copied into its own guard test** — the duplicate-copy class,
  guarding only the aliases someone remembered to copy. Now exported and iterated.
- **`'TÜRKİYE'` missed its alias.** The Turkish dotted capital İ (U+0130) lowercases to
  `i` + U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE, and NFC cannot recompose it (no precomposed
  "i with dot above" exists). NFD input missed every accented alias too. One line:
  `.toLowerCase().normalize('NFC').replace(/\u0307/g,'')`. Miss-only, never wrong — but
  free to fix. (The regex uses the `\u0307` ESCAPE, not a literal combining char, which is
  invisible in source and unreviewable.)
- Nit closed: `'Kowloon, Hong Kong'` passed under BOTH comparators ("Kong" is not an
  entry) and was decorative beside two real pins. Replaced with four more genuine
  collisions — Romania/Oman, Somalia/Mali, Dominican Republic/Dominica, Papua New
  Guinea/Guinea.

REJECTED, with the reviewer agreeing: `language=en` on the server geocode. Beyond the
OSINT blast radius, it **would not fix the class that bit us** — `'Hong Kong SAR China'`
and `'Democratic Republic of the Congo'` ARE the English forms Mapbox returns under
`language=en`. And `cachedName`/`paramName` can carry strings written by older builds, so
no server change can retroactively clean them. If ever wanted, the right shape is a
`language` param on `/vbg/geocode` ONLY, leaving `/vbg/threats` localized.

Verdict: SHIP. Final gates — app 230 suites / **3195 tests** green; typecheck 47 =
baseline; eslint clean; `:app:compileDebugKotlin` BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

STILL OWED (cannot be done without hardware): the native `TelephonyManager` read has
never executed on a device. A passing Kotlin compile is not a device returning a real MCC.

## 2026-08-28 — Dead-phone smoothness audit: B-685..B-688 (audit only, NO fixes shipped)

Founder asked for an audit + roadmap: make the messenger smooth on the weakest Android
("even a dead mobile"). Two-agent adversarial pass (primary + context-sharing partner,
rebuttal rounds). Full findings, budgets, debate record, and the 5-workstream roadmap:
**`docs/planning/DEAD_PHONE_SMOOTHNESS_PLAN.md`**. No device attached; APK numbers are
measured from the shipped artifact, ms figures are V8 floors / prior device runs.

### B-685 — release APK is 604 MB; ~70 % is ABIs no user has · P1 · OPEN

Measured from `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`: lib/ = 521 MB
across FOUR ABIs (arm64 150, x86_64 132, x86 132, armeabi-v7a 108 — x86 exists for
BlueStacks QA only); classes.dex 28 MB with R8/minify default-OFF
(`android/app/build.gradle:82`) and shrinkResources off. Dead deps shipping native
code with ZERO src imports: `react-native-mmkv`, `react-native-worklets-core`;
`expo-av` ships alongside its replacements expo-audio/expo-video. On a 16–32 GB
low-end phone 604 MB is frequently uninstallable, and the resulting storage pressure
degrades eMMC write latency under every SQLCipher write. Fix = W1 (per-ABI artifacts,
R8, dep purge); QA keeps a universal build — do NOT delete x86 from
`reactNativeArchitectures`.

### B-686 — a second, non-functional call engine ships in every build (Agora) · P1 · OPEN (founder decision)

`react-native-agora` is ~60 MB PER ABI (core + lip-sync + clear-vision +
spatial-audio + 2× AI-noise-suppression + ffmpeg) next to the real engine
(`libjingle_peerconnection` 11 MB). The feature it serves cannot work end-to-end:
token endpoint "NOT YET IMPLEMENTED on the server" (`agoraStart.ts:7-9`), fallback
"was never wired to a real Agora SDK boot" (`useCall.ts:243`). JS side is lazily
required — the dependency only inflates the artifact. Removal is decision box D1 in
the plan (recommended: remove package, keep the JS seam).

### B-687 — steady-state Merkle commit re-downloads + re-hashes the ENTIRE history after every chat burst · P1 · OPEN

The after-flush hook (`mirrorBootstrap.ts` → `commitMerkleRootNow`) calls
`commitMerkleRoot` with no leaves/rows → full-walk branch: page-cursor download of
the user's whole encrypted backup (`merkleCommit.ts`) + base64-decode + pure-JS
sha256 per row (`backupMerkle.ts`), debounced **5 s after each flush burst**
(`messageMirror.ts:62`) — the 2026-07-02 audit's "every 30 s" is stale; under active
chatting it is MORE frequent. Code's own comment records 9.5 s of hashing at 1,372
rows co-timed with 4.7 s LAGDIAG stalls; B-310 made it yield but the O(history)
CPU/radio/battery cost remains per burst. The M-12 `leaves` fast path already exists
and is never fed. Fix = W2 (`docs/planning/BACKUP_BOUNDARY_BATCHING_PLAN.md`),
write-side ONLY — `verifyMerkleCommit` + the verifier's synchronous
`computeMerkleRoot` are ARCH-GATED and untouched (BACKUP_LOOP I3).

### B-688 — every crypto digest and wire text codec runs in interpreted JS · P2 · OPEN (arch review to prepare)

`index.js` → `src/modules/messenger/crypto/polyfills.ts` deletes Hermes's native
TextEncoder/TextDecoder app-wide (pure-JS `text-encoding`, for jose/op-sqlite
utf-16le) and routes ALL `subtle.digest` through pure-JS `@noble/hashes`
(quick-crypto@0.7 native EVP digest broken: "Invalid Hash Algorithm!"). Verified NOT
on the per-DB-read path (rows cross JSI as strings; `JSON.parse` is native) — hot
consumers are send/receive (`outerEcies.ts`, `groupCrypto.ts`), Merkle leaves, and
mirror rows, so it is a send/receive/restore multiplier. Fresh-install restore of a
large account pays pure-JS sha256 over the whole history in the user's first minutes
on a new phone — the path B-687's fix cannot touch. Fix = W5, implementation-only
(same algorithms), GATED on W3 device measurement + architecture review.

STILL OWED (hardware): the `[LAGDIAG]` probes (in tree since 2026-07-27) have never
been read off a device; SQLCipher write path + `[backup.merkle]` cadence + curve-op
timing uninstrumented; `dumpsys meminfo` never captured; no 2 GB Android Go reference
device exists (plan decision D3).

## 2026-08-28 (same session, later) — B-687 SHADOW MODE SHIPPED (W2 of the dead-phone plan)

W2 of `docs/planning/DEAD_PHONE_SMOOTHNESS_PLAN.md`: the fix for the O(entire-history)
Merkle re-download+re-hash per chat burst, built SHADOW-FIRST. Commit behavior is
**byte-unchanged** (test-pinned: the shipped commit is identical with and without a
cache); a persistent leaf cache (`merkleLeafCache.ts`, `merkle_leaves` schema v22) is
captured at flush time from the EXACT uploaded bytes and compared against every walk,
logging `[backup.merkle.shadow] match=…`. Full mechanism + probe guidance:
BACKUP_LOOP.md §1b + §5.1-4. NOT committed (tree also carries unrelated VBG work).

**The finding that justified shadow-first (partner audit, from server source):** the
client's `toISOString()` timestamp does NOT round-trip — `messages_backup.msg_created_at`
is TIMESTAMPTZ and PostgREST returns the Postgres `to_json` form (`+00:00`, trailing
fractional zeros stripped). A naive upload-time cache would mismatch on EVERY row — the
five-times-shipped root_mismatch class, caught at design review. `pgTimestamptzText`
reproduces the server form; every walk rebuilds the cache on divergence (self-healing,
including against a future Postgres/PostgREST format change). Ciphertext round-trips
(canonical b64 → bytea → canonical b64). Deletions are server UPSERTS (tombstone rows
remain) — the founder's "deleted chats must never come back after restore" requirement
rides through unchanged, pinned by the existing conversationTombstones/B-648 suites.

**Design review record:** 2 partner rounds pre-build (Q1 ts-round-trip BREAKS, Q2
delete=upsert, Q3 single-writer-today, 4 P1 hardenings — all built: epoch-gated compare
AND rebuild with a re-read before the write; purge inside `clearFlushedForOwner`; dirty
raised BEFORE `putMessages`, only clearable by its raiser or a walk rebuild; additive
v22). Adversarial code review post-build: **AGREE, 0 P0 / 0 P1** across 6 lanes (flush
loop shape incl. retry lifecycle → complete-but-dirty never wrong-but-clean; I1-I9
re-checked, I3 verifier byte-untouched by diff inspection; v21 build opening a v22 DB
ignores the extra table — no refuse/wipe; all 5 scan anchors code-only ×1; no import
cycles; all 4 clearFlushedForOwner callers want the purge). Bonus: the B-311/463 heal
commits flow through the shadow block, so restore heals seed the cache for free.

Gates: BACKUP_LOOP §4.1 27 suites/196 green; full crypto run1 **550/550 (6769)**, run2
one MOVING flake (`callAudioSessionArbitration` — same suite flaked pre-change; B-126);
server backup spec 4/50 green; typecheck 47 = baseline; eslint clean. New suite
`merkleLeafCacheShadow.test.ts` (21) — transform-removal and epoch-gate-removal
mutations both proven RED then reverted; `merkleYieldingRoot` anchors RE-POINTED (never
deleted) to the leaves decomposition, verifier ban widened.

**OWED:** (1) device soak on the founder's phone reading `[backup.merkle.shadow]` —

## 2026-08-28 (device night session) — B-690: unbounded backup body read wedges the Merkle commit chain SILENTLY · FIXED + first W1/W2 device evidence

Founder's Redmi Note 11 (043dd12e3dad, Android 13, arm64, 7.6 GB) attached — the same
device as every B-279-era measurement. arm64 W1 APK (110 MB) installed clean over ADB
(MIUI needs the on-phone accept). First-ever R8 boot: ZERO fatals, zero missing
class/resource errors; the `[crypto/polyfills] XEd25519 self-test could not run` warn is
the documented benign path (calculateSignature not exposed), not R8 damage. Fresh login +
restore of 1,319 rows succeeded INCLUDING a live self-heal: `root_mismatch rows=1319
committed=1293` (old device left 26 rows uploaded-but-unsigned) → B-45r3 additive-prefix

- B-50 seq adopt (`local=1 server=1054 → 1055`) → clean restore. A few very old rows
  skipped as undecryptable (known ratchet-recovery class, cumulative≥4, pre-existing).

### B-690 — found live, root-caused to the socket, FIXED

After the founder's first fast-send burst, the debounced Merkle commit NEVER logged —
no `[backup.merkle]`, no `merkle hook failed`, no retry warns, 2+ min, app foreground
(timer probe: backgrounding fired nothing → the hook HAD run). Server side nailed it:
Caddy logged the commit's walk page `GET /backup/messages?limit=1000` aborted at
**1.002 s** with `write: connection reset by peer` — the phone's network hiccuped
mid-body (BT/Wi-Fi churn co-timed in logcat). Client side: the H-14 AbortController is
cleared in doFetch's `finally` when HEADERS land (`backupClient.ts:71-72`), so
**`res.json()` ran unbounded** — RN leaves it pending FOREVER on a broken stream. No
throw ⇒ `withNetRetry` (which only retries thrown 'network' errors) never fired ⇒ the
hung promise sat inside `commitChain` (the BUG-1 single-flight), **silently blocking
every subsequent commit**. It self-cleared only when the dead socket errored at the
OS level ~5.9 min later (23:33:00 hang → 23:38:58 first commit), after which
**14 queued commits drained back-to-back**.

**Fix:** `withBodyTimeout` — the body read races a 30 s bound (10 s on the small
409/text error paths) and throws `BackupError('network','fetch_failed:body_timeout')`,
exactly the kind netRetry retries. Race ABANDONS the hung json (the request is dead;
the documented house trade). Pinned in `backupClientErrorMap.test.ts` (B-690 block, 3
tests; the source scan mutation-proved RED by unwrapping). Gates: crypto 6772 ×2 (run 2
= the B-126 moving flake, `productionRuntimeGroupSend`, green in run 1), messenger
screens 731, typecheck 47 = baseline, eslint clean.

### The B-687 cost, finally measured end-to-end on a real account

The drained backlog put numbers on the steady-state disease: **fourteen commits,
8.8–33.8 s EACH (median ~13 s), rows=1342–1356, ~4.5 minutes of near-continuous
re-download + re-hash** to certify a handful of new texts — plus that data burn ×14 on
mobile. Several commits differed by ZERO new rows (receipt-only churn). This is the
live justification for the W2 flip; the shadow soak decides it.

### Per-send / smoothness numbers vs July (same physical device)

- Fast-send burst: stalls **155–776 ms**, `[send.total]` 982–1962 ms, **no compounding
  into 3+ s** (July: 350–500 ms/send compounding to 3.4 s).
- Restore (one-time): worst stall 8.7 s during 1,319-row import; post-restore normal
  use: worst 569 ms.
- Merkle heal commit (M-12 leaves path): 2.0 s vs July's 9.5 s full-walk at ~same rows.
- Cold start → first frame: 3.7 s cold / ~2.1 s warm (first-ever baseline).
- PSS foreground ≈ 318 MB (first-ever baseline).

→ first `[backup.merkle.shadow]` line + commit-under-fix confirmation; the scroll-jank
A/B vs the B-279 table.

## 2026-08-29 — B-691: chat-open animation stutter — mount side effects moved OUT of the 220 ms slide (F2/F3/F4 of the chat-open lag plan)

Founder: opening a chat animates "laggy instead of fluid, not like WhatsApp." Root
cause decomposition (two-agent): `docs/qa/CHAT_OPEN_ANIMATION_LAG_2026-08-29.md` —
extends the still-open B-279 residue. The slide is native (native-stack, 220 ms) and
the GPU is measured-idle; the stutter is (1) the JS thread busy at tap time delaying
the slide's START (W2/W5 territory, now shipped) and (2) EVERY ChatScreen mount
effect landing INSIDE the animation window: the relay pull's decrypt burst, the group
roster sync, the notif dismiss, `setActive`'s unread-zeroing re-render of the
still-unfrozen list behind the slide, and the markRead commit on a 200 ms timer
detonating at the tail of the 220 ms animation.

**Fix (B-691):**

- New `useOpenTransitionGate` (`src/hooks/useOpenTransitionGate.ts`) — false until
  the OPEN `transitionEnd` (closing=false), with a 400 ms fallback so a gated effect
  is DELAYED, never lost. SIDE EFFECTS ONLY — content is never gated (the list
  deferral is the measured-2×-worse dead end; a scan pins that no JSX keys on it).
- ChatScreen: the five mount effects above now key on the gate. `setActive` split
  (F3): the id pins at mount via `setActiveConversation(id, {skipUnreadClear:true})`
  — inbound routing / notification suppression / unread-increment guard all keep
  their timing — and the full clearing form (incl. the L20 sibling sweep) runs at
  transitionEnd. Store opts param is additive; DepartmentChatScreen + all other
  callers keep the one-arg form unchanged (§5 sweep: no change).
- F4 bracket: `openConversation` stamps the tap (`chatOpenPerf.ts`, 10 s TTL);
  ChatScreen's gate emits ONE `[LAGDIAG] [chat.open] conv=<id8> mountToEnd=Nms
tapToEnd=Nms via=transition|fallback` warn (survives release). `perf-journey.ps1`
  gains opt-in `-ChatOpen` (4× tap top row → BACK; needs the chat list on screen)
  and reports tap→transitionEnd against the <300 ms plan-§3 budget — the harness
  never exercised the founder's actual complaint before.

**Deliberate behaviour change:** a sub-transition peek (back out <220 ms) no longer
zeroes the badge — consistent with markRead, which never fired in that window either.

Pinned: `useOpenTransitionGate.test.tsx` (7, behavioural), `chatOpenTransitionGate
.test.ts` (13, comment-stripped CRLF-safe source scan, anchors inside the executing
effect closure), 2 new cases in `conversationKeyspaceWrites` (skipUnreadClear leaves
every badge; deferred full call still runs L20). Mutation-proved ×3: store guard
stripped → 2 red; pull guard removed → exactly its scan red; hook closing-check
inverted → exactly its case red.

Gates: crypto 6804 ×2 green; app project 3211 green (232 suites); MESSAGE_LOOP §7
invariant suites 331; NAV loop pins 174; tsc 47 = baseline; eslint 0 errors on
changed files. Device A/B (OLD/NEW interleaved, `-ChatOpen`) OWED — no measurement
claim until the bracket is read off the Redmi.

**Critic pass (one-agent adversarial, AGREE):** two P1 test-hardening holes found
and closed same-session — (1) the guard-presence scans could not see a DELETED
`transitionDone` dependency (markRead would then never fire on a quiet chat, the
B-356 class): a deps-array count pin (exactly 5) closes it; (2) `{fallbackMs: 0}`
at the call site would silently reopen the bug: ChatScreen is scanned for the
absence of `fallbackMs` and the default is range-pinned 300–1000 ms. Two context
notes for future sessions: `backgroundMessageNotifier` (~:200) ALREADY dismisses
this conversation's banner keyed on the id change at mount — the deferred
ChatScreen dismiss is belt-and-braces, do NOT "deduplicate" by re-keying the
notifier off unread; and the tap mark deliberately covers ONLY `openConversation`
list rows (notification opens / in-place Chat→Chat report `mountToEnd` only) —
stamping inside ChatScreen would double-stamp real taps. Critic also verified
native-stack emits `transitionEnd` per route key with `closing:true` on
push-over/pop (the gate ignores both) and that `onAppear` fires on non-animated
appears, so the notification cold route opens the gate promptly.

Founder: "the notification is not live — a message takes time to appear; the
animation feels laggy; send/receive should update immediately like WhatsApp,

ranked fix plan (S-0..S-7), dead-end list, invariants. No code changed.

Findings (NL-1..NL-8, file:line in the doc):

- **NL-1 (P0)** killed-app lane draws NOTHING until a full runtime boot + drain
  completes or the 8 s budget expires (`fcmHeadless.ts:37,276-298` →
  `headlessDrain.ts:179-197`): AsyncStorage + keychain + up-to-3 s hydration wait +
  SQLCipher open + libsignal install + AWAITED `publishOwnBundle` + WS + pull,
  serially, before the first banner. The Signal model inverted (placeholder-first is
  the fix). This is the known-open lean-headless item (NOTIF_TAP audit §4 P1-5,
  spec 5.4) now named as the dominant "not live" cause.
- **NL-2 (P1)** `ALERT_BURST_MS=10_000` keyed PER CONVERSATION
  (`callNotification.ts:133,349`): every banner within 10 s of the last alert for
  that conversation posts silent — no heads-up/sound. In a live exchange ~1 message
  per 10 s alerts; reads exactly as "notifications not updating". Side-effect of the
  N-29 double-sound fix — the dedupe should be per-MESSAGE, not per-conv-10s.
- **NL-3 (P1)** FEATURE GAP: with the app OPEN there is no in-app message banner and
  no receive sound/haptic at all (foreground msg-wake branch only pulls,
  `fcmBootstrap.ts:630-649`; notifier bails foregrounded,
  `backgroundMessageNotifier.ts:245`; `bravoTones.ts` has call tones only; haptics
  on send only). The WhatsApp comparison is mostly THIS.
- **NL-4 (P2)** server chat-wake debounce holds msg #2+ of a burst up to 2 s
  (`push.service.ts:164,704-720,883-888`) — B-352 A1 already cut it 6→2; it remains
  the burst latency floor, and `collapseKey` coalesces Doze bursts to one wake.
- **NL-5 (P2)** banner display gates on that message's SQLCipher COMMIT at the tail
  of the GLOBAL serialized receive chain (`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts:324` →
  `receiveTransaction.ts:50,267-281`) — CORRECT per M16, but burst-N latency scales
  linearly; do not un-gate, make the chain cheaper.
- **NL-6 (P2)** per-message JS-thread jank: full map+filter+SORT of the conversation
  list on every commit with an uncached `Date.parse`×2 comparator
  (`MessengerHomeScreen.tsx:516-524`, `conversationListOrder.ts:14-24`, ≈1300
  parses/message @100 convs), plus the notifier's synchronous whole-store diff doing
  its work BEFORE the foreground bail (`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts:195-338`).
- **NL-7 (P3)** a message older than 2 s skips the bubble entrance animation
  entirely (`ChatScreen.tsx:3117-3119`) — pipeline-delayed messages POP IN; this is
  the perceived "animation lag" in-chat.
- **NL-8 (P3)** an awaited notifee `syncMsgSummary()` round-trip sits in front of
  every banner's first paint (`callNotification.ts:330-334`).

pass is still owed. Device rules: never BlueStacks for push (tokens reaped ~90 s);

## 2026-08-29 — B-693: end-to-end message DELIVERY latency (1:1 / group / dept channels) — root-cause decomposition (INVESTIGATION ONLY, no fixes)

Founder: "on WhatsApp the other device gets the message immediately; in our app it
takes a little time — 1:1, groups, AND departmental/workspace channels; should be
smooth even on a dead phone." Companion to B-692 (which owns the notification
half). Two-agent decomposition (full sender/server/recipient trace, then a
5-point verification round) + independent adversarial critic (verdict AGREE; 7
findings, 2 P0s, all folded in):
**`docs/qa/MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LATENCY_2026-08-29.md`** — verified wire topology,
DL-1..DL-9 ranked causes, the before/after ledger (previous→now measured pairs,
owed baselines, post-fix targets), fix plan F-0..F-7, dead ends, invariants.

Key verified facts (file:line in the doc; re-grep before trusting):

- 1:1 send = one WS frame (`envelope.send`, HTTP fallback behind a 5-20s ack
  watchdog); group/dept send = **N pairwise ratchet encrypts + N HTTP POSTs, no
  WS lane**; dept/workspace channels ARE groups on the wire
  (`DepartmentChatScreen.tsx:1002`). Optimistic append before any crypto/network
  in both lanes (M3 holds).
- Server hot path is Redis-only and live delivery is an **immediate WS emit
  carrying the full envelope** — no wake-then-pull. The recipient's bubble
  renders BEFORE COMMIT (append inside the txn, notifications post-COMMIT/M16).
- **DL-1 (P0, UNMEASURED):** recipient's global `txnChain` serializes
  decrypt+COMMIT one envelope at a time; the receive frame holds chain A then
  awaits per-conversation chain B (`applyDirectText.ts:93`/`applyGroupText.ts:140`),
  which a fast-send burst's 50ms coalesced flush occupies — best current
  explanation of "send fast then stuck". **NO receive-side latency probe exists**
  — `[RECVLAT]` proposed (doc F-0).
- **DL-2 (P0):** idle-but-alive recipient — socket half-death detection (server
  30s ping / client 40s silence / 0.5-30s jittered reconnect ladder) IS the
  latency; the server's emit lands on a dead fd and the message rides the B-692
  FCM lane. Sender urgency fast-path exists (`hasPendingOutbound`); the idle
  recipient has none.
- DL-3 group sender CPU×N (cap 250); DL-4 outbox detour (rescue is edge-driven
  and unthrottled on WS/NetInfo/foreground — residue is the 60s quiet-socket
  timer); DL-5 half-dead-fd sender 5-20s blind window (a KNOWN-dead socket falls
  back to HTTP instantly, `client.ts:397-400`); DL-6 group ✓✓ waits ≤60s receipt
  poll (sites: WS-connected + 60s timer ONLY — not chat-open, not resume); DL-7
  fixed 1:1 costs (awaited outbox enqueue pre-network = dead-phone plan F8);
  DL-8 missing-group-key stash (minutes); DL-9 delayed bubbles skip the entrance
  animation (rides B-692 S-6).
- Critic P0s (both fixed in-doc): (1) an earlier draft claimed the statusFlush
  batches ride the global chain — FALSE: the live coalescer is `upsertCoalesced`
  → per-conversation `chainOp`, raw autocommit (the B-130 fix shape);
  `upsertBatch:685` has zero live callers (restore importer only). (2) F-5's
  server-side delivered-push for HTTP submits is **sealed-sender ARCH-GATED**
  (`envelope.controller.ts:100-103`, `envelope.service.ts:279-283` OM-03 both
  document the no-submitter-link rule) — only the client-side poll-trigger half
  is safe to build.

Measure FIRST (doc F-0): build `[RECVLAT]` + `[send.total]` group sub-stages,
lower the `send1v1` stage threshold 120→40ms, then the two-device A/B protocol
(release APK, real phones, interleaved runs). Existing sender baseline:
`[send.total]` 982-1962ms (2026-08-28 device night). Targets (doc §3d): 1:1
alive→alive <500ms p50 to the recipient's screen; group ≤30 members <800ms to
first member; group ✓✓ <5s vs today's ≤60s.

### B-694 — productionRuntimeGroupSend harness assumed fan-out COMPLETION order · P2 (test-only) · FIXED

The session's rotating `productionRuntimeGroupSend` failures ("outer sealed
authentication failed", tests moving between runs) were NOT the B-126
transform-cache flake: five sites read `relaySends[0]` as "Bob's envelope",
but the mock relay pushes in POST-arrival order — under parallel-suite load
the members' crypto interleaves and slot 0 can be Carol's leg, which Bob then
fails to unseal. The exact `groupBroadcast` B-126 class (allSettled resolution
order ≠ member order) reborn in a harness. All 5 sites now use the suite's own
`.find(r => r.recipient.userId === BOB)!` pattern (3 sites already did it
right). 3 isolated + 2 full-suite green runs since; this closes one real
mechanism behind the "moving flake" noise on this suite.

### B-695 — CallScreen shows "CONTACT" for a peer the app knows by name ⚠️ P2 · OPEN

**Root cause.** `CallScreen.tsx:214` — `const peerName = convo?.name ?? 'Contact'`, where
`convo` is a RAW dictionary lookup (`selectConversation`, `messengerStore.ts:2305`).
CallScreen never got the B-411 name ladder that every other surface has
(`resolveNotifTitle`: conversation name → directory name → phone; `ChatScreen.tsx:392-408`).
The avatar is resolved SEPARATELY by userId (`UserAvatar userId={remoteUserId}`,
`CallScreen.tsx:3484`), which is exactly why the founder sees the right photo over the
wrong name. The all-caps "CONTACT" is `styles.voiceName`'s `textTransform:'uppercase'`.
`launchCall` navigates with the caller's conversationId VERBATIM (`launchCall.ts:467`),
and `resolvePeerForCall` succeeds for a rowless `direct:<peer>` id
(`launchCall.ts:79-90`), so the call dials fine with no row behind it.

**Most probable trigger lane (critic-found — the B-18 merge deletes the row under a
pinned route):** message a NEW person (chat opened by contact/by number mints and
navigates under the synthetic `direct:<peer>` id, `NewChatScreen.tsx:363-381`) → the
peer replies / listMine syncs, and the B-18 merge in `upsertConversation` DELETES the
synthetic row in favour of the server-UUID row (`messengerStore.ts:769-818`, the
`delete s.conversations[synthId]` at :816) → ChatScreen stays pinned to its route-param
id (documented in-source, `ChatScreen.tsx:342-352`) and still looks healthy via the
slot read-merge + its own header ladder → tap the call button (`ChatScreen.tsx:2117`)
→ launchCall carries the now-dead synthetic id → CallScreen finds no row → "CONTACT".
No deletion, no notification, no cold boot needed. `ChatInfoScreen.tsx:893/896` passes
the same stale route id.

**Knock-ons found on the way:** `FloatingCallOverlay.tsx:208` and the FGS notification
(`CallScreen.tsx:1456/1664` via `patchActiveCall` at :278) inherit "Contact"; outgoing
call records never shadow-create a row (the `sender_id !== 'self'` gate,
`messengerStore.ts:955`), so rowless slots accumulate hex-named, avatar-less calls-log
rows whose tap reproduces the bug (`CallsLogScreen.tsx:376/439`).

**Lanes ruled OUT by the critic (do not re-derive):** deleted-conversation call-back —
dead, the log rows are derived from messages which die WITH the row
(`messengerStore.ts:1536-1541`); the WS incoming lane — mints a `Bravo · <hex>`
placeholder so it renders "BRAVO · XXXXXXXX", never "CONTACT"
(`MainNavigator.tsx:1057-1069`); the FCM `direct:` fallback lanes
(`fcmBootstrap.ts:1189/1932`) are real but INCOMING (`isIncoming:true` renders
"Answering…", not the screenshot's "Calling…") — note they mint NO placeholder row,
an asymmetry vs the WS lane worth a fix of its own.

**Fix shape (when picked up):** canonicalize the id in `launchCall` (via
`resolveDirectConversationIdFromState`) AND give CallScreen the B-411 ladder
(directory name → phone) instead of the bare `?? 'Contact'`. Client-only.

### B-696 — vault PIN and the ONLY copy of the vault file keys destroyed on uninstall AND plain sign-out ⚠️ P1 data-loss · OPEN · ARCH-GATED

**What the founder saw** (PIN setup demanded after reinstall) **is the small half.**
The PIN hash AND the entire vault index — including each file's AES-256 key/IV, which
exist NOWHERE else — live only in the zustand persist blob `bravo-vault-v1` on
AsyncStorage (`vaultStore.ts:49-50`, partialize :591-607). `allowBackup="false"`
(`AndroidManifest.xml:121`) means uninstall destroys it. **Sign-out destroys it too,
unconditionally**: `authStore.ts:1001-1005` calls `useVaultStore.reset()` OUTSIDE the
`wipeAtRest` gate — while the SQLCipher chat history deliberately SURVIVES a plain
sign-out (comment :948-953). So sign-out/sign-in on the SAME account keeps your chats
but permanently orphans your vault. The server-side ciphertext still exists but is
undecryptable forever, and `vaultClient.ts` has NO list endpoint (:47-85) — the client
cannot even enumerate the orphans, and nothing GCs them.

**Why the wipe exists:** the store is account-UNSCOPED (fixed persist key), and
Issue-30/20 made sign-out wipe it because the next account inherited the previous
user's PIN + file index. Pinned by `vaultPinFirstAccess.test.ts:38-53`. The founder's
ask directly conflicts with that pin — this is a product/architecture decision, not a
patch.

**Also found:** the Forgot-PIN flow is fail-closed vaporware — `VaultForgotScreen.tsx:20-24`
and `VaultOTPVerifyScreen.tsx:21-24` both state "no /auth/vault-reset/\* route exists
today" and open a support mailto that can help nobody; `reset()`'s docstring ("Used by
the Forgot PIN flow") is stale — its only production caller is signOut. Today a
forgotten PIN is unrecoverable except by wiping the files.

**Feasibility note for the design doc:** the PIN is a pure UX gate over PIN-independent
per-file keys (`vaultStore.ts:29-34`), so per-person PIN durability (server-side
verifier) needs NO key escrow. Durable FILES additionally need owner-scoped vault
state + the vault index inside the E2E backup mirror (zero backup coverage today).
Both touch the File-Vault-MFA / key-handling CLAUDE.md stop-conditions — founder +
architecture sign-off before any code.

### B-697 — every vault move fails "the server declined the vault MFA challenge" ⚠️ P1 · OPEN — server-env verification owed

**Dialog provenance (exact-text unique):** `vaultOps.ts:106-108`, shown ONLY when
`mintActionToken` yields no proof for a reason OTHER than tier (`vaultOps.ts:92-119`).
The founder got past FileViewer's pre-flight `hasCloudVault` gate (:164-167) and the
B-591 tier routing (:193-196) — so this was NOT a tier refusal surfacing wrongly
(B-591 stands; its pins verified intact, incl. the no-message-field raw-body fallback,
`transportKeysHttpClient.test.ts:222-240`).

**Root-cause hypothesis (favoured):** the client has NO real Play Integrity attestation
— it always sends `attestationToken:'attestation-unavailable'` (`keysClient.ts:116`) —
so vault moves work ONLY while the server's `BIOMETRIC_DEV_BYPASS` is effective.
`devFlag` requires `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` AND the literal `'true'`
(`configuration.ts:6-7`); P0-A9 (`main.ts:35-48`, in tree since 2026-05-24) refuses to
BOOT a production-mode service with the var set. The bypass was verified ON and working
2026-08-20 (B-591). On 2026-08-28 FOUR commits touched auth-service boot files
(`36911d2e`, `6dfa7b2e`, `09553ee2`, `ed7d256b` — the secure-services remediation) and
plausibly triggered a redeploy; `infra/env/auth.env.example` defaults to exactly the
killing combination (`NODE_ENV=production` :19, `BIOMETRIC_DEV_BYPASS=false` :64). The
box has documented env-drift history (JWT secret, TURN secret). With the gate live and
no `GOOGLE_PLAY_INTEGRITY_KEY`, EVERY vault move on EVERY client fails with exactly
this dialog — and iOS attestation is unconditionally pending
(`biometric.service.ts:105-106`), so the blast radius is platform-wide. Tier is
excluded for the founder's own account (Pro until 2027-02-20, renewed under B-591).
Transient alternatives (401-after-failed-refresh, fetch timeout, non-JSON proxy body →
all map to the same dialog, single-shot with no retry) are possible but disfavoured —
the repro was deterministic right after a fresh PIN setup.

**OWED — the one measurement that settles it (SSH + curl were classifier-blocked this
session):** EITHER on the box: `docker exec <auth> env | grep -E 'NODE_ENV|BIOMETRIC'`

- `docker logs <auth> | grep auth.biometric.assert` around 2026-08-29 09:18 (every
  assert logs to stdout with a `detail` field, `audit.service.ts:66-68`); OR black-box:
  authenticated `POST https://auth.94-136-184-52.sslip.io/auth/biometric/assert` with
  `{purpose:'vault-access', platform:'android', attestationToken:'attestation-unavailable'}`
  — `actionToken` ⇒ server fine, hunt transients; 403 `attestation_failed` (detail will
  literally say `GOOGLE_PLAY_INTEGRITY_KEY not configured`) ⇒ bypass off, restore it;
  403 `tier_insufficient` ⇒ bypass on, account not entitled; connection refused ⇒ P0-A9
  crash-loop (NODE_ENV=production with the var still `'true'` — which ALSO produces this
  dialog via the network-error→null lane).

**Two cheap client hardenings for the eventual fix commit:** surface the server's 403
`detail` in the dialog (the client discards diagnostic gold, `keysClient.ts:138-141`),
and retry `mintVaultProof` once — today every transient blip presents as a
security-sounding dialog.
