## 2026-08-29 (later) — B-696 BUILT + server-deployed; B-697 root cause REVISED with box evidence; B-699 logged

### B-696 — vault durability: BUILT, all four phases, founder-approved ("do it all steps")

Design doc `docs/planning/VAULT_DURABILITY_DESIGN_2026-08-29.md` (write-first per the
founder's instruction), then built:

- **Phase A (owner stash):** sign-out now STASHES the vault slice per owner
  (`stashAndClearOwner`, `vaultStore.ts`) instead of destroying the only copy of the
  per-file AES keys; sign-in adopts it back (`adoptVaultOwner`, wired in MainNavigator's
  ownerKey effect). Remove-account keeps total destruction (`purgeOwner`, wipeAtRest-gated).
  Issue-30/20 isolation preserved by the clear; `vaultPinFirstAccess` re-pointed (never
  deleted), new functional pins in `vaultOwnerStash.test.ts`. Both mutation-proven RED.
- **Phase B (server PIN verifier):** new auth-service module `vault-pin/` — argon2id
  verifier in `public.vault_pins` (migration applied), GET/POST/verify + Redis lockout
  (TOTP P0-V2 pattern, uniform errors); client re-adopt lane in VaultNewPinScreen (fresh
  install + server-has-PIN → "enter your existing PIN" once, local gate re-mints);
  `reconcileServerPin` on every unlock self-heals the legacy base. S2 rule held: a bare
  JWT can NEVER overwrite an existing verifier (mutation-proven; TS also enforces it).
- **Phase C (Forgot PIN, the real one):** audit-S2 closure exactly as its register asked —
  `/auth/vault-pin/reset/{request,verify,complete}`: ACCOUNT PASSWORD gates the OTP send,
  server-checked OTP, single-use 5-min purpose-bound action token (`vault-pin-reset`, NOT
  in VAULT_MFA_PURPOSES), jti burned BEFORE the verifier write. Both stub screens rebuilt
  live (one code box, account-bound, masked phone). **FILES ARE KEPT through a reset.**
- **Phase D (files survive reinstall):** E2E vault index blob — files+albums sealed
  AES-256-GCM under HKDF(backup master key, 'bravo-vault-index-v1') with per-user AAD,
  stored opaque in `public.vault_index_blobs` (migration applied) via new JWT-only
  `/vault-index` endpoints (messenger-service, deliberately OUTSIDE MfaGuard — single-use
  proofs can't fund a background sync; `backup_session_snapshots` precedent) and OUTSIDE
  the Merkle mirror entirely (BACKUP_LOOP untouched: no `backup/**` file changed except
  one additive pull call in BackupRestoreScreen after `saveMirrorMasterKey`). Client sync
  `vaultIndexSync.ts`: 5s debounced push, stale_seq adopt-ONCE (I6), pull-merge on empty
  index, removal non-resurrection (session-scoped), counts-only logging.

**Critic round (one adversarial agent over the full diff): F1 FIX-FIRST — fixed.** The
design's §4.2 sync-debt self-heal wasn't armed (the repo's "documented mitigation never
implemented" class). Now: persisted `pinSyncPending`/`pinServerDiverged` per owner,
`reconcileServerPin` retries the debt on unlock (verify only WHILE a debt is recorded —
a per-unlock probe would burn the server lockout budget), divergence prompts EXACTLY once
and points at Forgot-PIN (the S2-sanctioned overwrite door). Pinned by
`vaultPinServerSync.test.ts`, mutation-proven RED on both the retry and the one-shot edge.
Also fixed: F3 (probe can't yank a mid-entry user), F8 (doc drift). Accepted/documented:
F2 (biometric-only users mint on first PIN unlock), F4 (seq SELECT-then-UPSERT race, the

## 2026-08-29 — B-698: v1.0.268 first-QA pair — click sound per message + "Member 7f8f75 added Member bc9bc9" banner on every app open · FIXED (notifier) + OPEN (re-mint driver)

Founder, minutes after installing 1.0.268: (1) "sound per message send it raise
click sound i dont want that"; (2) screenshot of the NEW in-app banner showing
"Member: Member 7f8f75 added Member bc9bc9" — a group membership line, bannered
"when i open the app", for an add nobody performed.

Root cause (both symptoms, one lane): the B-692 foreground alert layer treats
EVERY fresh non-self row as an arrival. A `type:'system'` membership event row
carries the ACTOR's raw userId as `sender_id`, so it (a) passes the
`sender_id === 'self'` filter — the user's OWN group actions ding — and
(b) banners with `resolveMemberName`'s "Member <6hex>" fragment fallback when
the directory hasn't hydrated. The every-open recurrence: the deterministic-id
event row is RE-MINTED by a boot lane that runs BEFORE message hydration
(`appendMemberAddedEvent`'s idempotence check reads the in-memory list, empty
pre-hydration), lands as a single-row conversation — which slips the
notifier's bulk-hydration guard (`list.length > 1`) — with a fresh
`created_at`, and alerts again.

FIXED (shipped v1.0.269):

- `backgroundMessageNotifier`: system rows are watermarked but NEVER alert
  (banner/tone/notifee) on any lane. Pinned RED-first-equivalent +
  mutation-proved (filter removed → exactly the B-698 case red); the
  follow-the-real-message control keeps W29's "every committed MESSAGE
  notifies" honest.
- `messageTone`: in-app sounds DEFAULT OFF (founder veto — "I don't want
  that"). Converted the const kill switch to a gated fn + test hook; the
  guard suite exercises the audible layer via the hook and pins the shipped
  default silent end-to-end. Re-enabling requires a real settings toggle.

OPEN (residual, needs device logcat): WHICH boot lane re-processes the admin
add each open (stash replay vs relay redelivery vs group-state reset) — the
row still re-appears IN-THREAD with a fresh timestamp until that driver is
found. Capture: `adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS` on open, look for the group id

### B-697 — CLOSED: a missing barrel export killed EVERY vault MFA mint inside the phone — "the server declined" never involved the server ⚠️ was P1 · FIXED

**The founder reproduced live on v1.0.269 with the phone on adb**, which bought the
investigation real evidence per attempt:

1. Server truth: one minute BEFORE a failing move, the same phone successfully round-
   tripped `auth.vault_pin.set` (12:16:25Z, audit log) — online, authed, same base URL.
   30 s AFTER the fingerprint, the runtime fetched peer key bundles fine. A 10-minute
   `tcpdump` on the auth container captured rich app traffic (logins, /auth/me, 200+ key
   fetches) and **ZERO `/auth/biometric/assert` arrivals** — ever, from any build.
2. The B-697 hardening built this session (surface the mint-failure `detail` in the
   dialog instead of the uniform scare line + retry once) made an EXISTING test fail
   with the answer in its output: `TypeError: (0, _src.fetchWithTimeout) is not a
function`.
3. That test — `transportKeysClientFetchBinding.test.ts` — was a **DOCUMENTS entry a
   prior session wrote without a B-number or an sqa entry**: `keysClient.ts:2` imports
   `fetchWithTimeout` from the `@bravo/messenger-core` barrel, and the barrel exported
   only `TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS` beside it — never the function. The binding resolved to
   `undefined`; every method of the mobile KeysHttpClient threw before a byte reached
   the network; `mintActionToken`'s catch swallowed it to null; vaultOps rendered null
   as "the server declined the vault MFA challenge". The `TS2305` for the import sat
   INSIDE the 47-error tsc baseline the whole time. Every earlier hypothesis (bypass
   off, env drift, tier, transient network) was wrong; the dialog wore a security
   costume over a one-line import bug, on every build, for every user, always.

**Fix:** export `fetchWithTimeout` (+`isTimeoutError`) from the messenger-core barrel;
DOCUMENTS pins flipped to their prescribed inversions (binding is a function, all four
request paths reach fetch, the mint resolves a real token). The B-591 mapping pins and
the new detail pins re-pointed (`transportKeysHttpClient`: every non-tier/attestation
failure now resolves `{denied:'other', detail}` — the collapse-to-null WAS the mask).
tsc baseline INTENTIONALLY lowered 47 → 46 so the fixed TS2305 can never re-bury
itself. Full crypto 560/560 suites 6901/6901 tests green.

**Three lessons, all standing-rule material:** (a) a DOCUMENTS test without an sqa
entry is a bug report nobody reads — it sat findable for the whole hunt; (b) an error
allowed by the tsc baseline is an error nobody sees — audit the 46 that remain;
(c) "absence at the service layer" ≠ "absence at the box": the assert lines were
missing from app logs because Nest logs nothing for requests that never arrive, and
tcpdump was needed to prove never-arrive vs bounced-at-guard.

### B-703 MR-1 — FIXED (same session). Killed-lane wake honesty.

`'drained'` now means INGESTED, not "the function returned". New Tier-A
`runtime/relayPullReport.ts` (report shape + the one classification rule); `drainRelay`
accounts per-envelope **by id** (a short page is re-pulled with the cursor unmoved and
acks on a 200 ms timer, so counters inflated up to 10x and a re-acked envelope could
mask a stuck one) and returns it; `pullEnvelopes` still never throws but REPORTS, and
refuses a stale report via a sequence stamp (a resolved `coalescedDrain` does not prove
a drain ran — the epoch gate bails synchronously). `headlessDrainAndNotify` classifies;
`fcmHeadless` falls through to the fallback banner unless the drain finished or a banner
already posted. New `isEnvelopeInFlight` so a skip is only re-checked once the pass that
held it released it (`markSeen` commits at the END of that pass's txn).

**THREE adversarial critic rounds; two of my own refinements were REJECTED by them and
both are recorded in the doc's §9 so they are not re-proposed:** (1) requiring
`acked === 0` for 'incomplete' — defeated because the leave-on-relay path itself sends a
rehandshake nudge, which acks silently; (2) a notifier "judged" counter (post OR
muted/own withhold) — defeated because a fresh headless VM has an EMPTY `messages` map
(they live in SQLCipher, not the vault), so the runtime's own hydration replays history
through the notifier and a thread whose only row the user sent silenced the FIRST wake of
every VM. Only a POSTED banner may suppress; a wake that draws no banner while something
is stuck falls back generically — the fallback still suppresses an EXPLICITLY named muted
conversation (P2-BR-5's gate is intact), and the ambiguous case it cannot mute is
P2-BR-5's own documented trade. Under sealed sender the wake never carries a
conversationId, so ambiguous is the only live case.

**A fourth (closing) round** caught two more, both fixed: the load-bearing
`const ackedBefore = pageProgressed;` was unpinned — `= 0` reads as a harmless hoist,
turns the verdict into `pageProgressed > 0` so any earlier ack on the page masks every

was unpinned, so trusting a wedged hold forever re-armed the B-126 class inside the
notification lane. Both now mutation-proven RED.

### B-704 — FIXED: every ImageryBackdrop photo rendered as a 1:1-dp top-left CROP

**Found by** a founder art drop (new AI-Itinerary card art) rendering BLANK. The asset was
not the bug. `ImageryBackdrop`'s `<Image>` carried `style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill,
{opacity}]}` — and under the New Architecture, position + insets WITHOUT dimensions does not
size an Image: it falls back to its INTRINSIC size, anchored top-left. `resizeMode="cover"`
therefore never receives a box to cover, and the card paints a **1 asset px = 1 dp** corner
crop of the art.

**Evidence** (Pixel 6a, density 2.625, instrumented assets served through Metro):

| probe                         | expected under `cover`        | observed                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 720x540, 6 vertical hue bands | all six bands across the card | RED spanning card 0-70%, ORANGE to the edge — yellow/green/blue/magenta never on screen (asset x 0→~24%) |
| 60x45, same bands             | scaled UP to fill the card    | drew at exactly 158x118 device px = 60x45 dp in the card's TOP-LEFT corner, rest of card empty           |

458 device px showing 173 asset px = 2.65x = the device density — i.e. 1 asset px = 1 dp.
The sibling `LinearGradient` — the SAME `StyleSheet.absoluteFill`, but a View — spanned the
card correctly (its scrim ramp measured 48→201 across the full width), which is what isolated
the fault to `Image` rather than to the wrapper or the card.

**Why it hid for so long:** every shipped asset is full-frame art LARGER than the card, so the
2.65x top-left zoom still looked like a (dark, soft) photograph. It only became visible when an
asset was authored with a deliberately EMPTY region in the top-left — the obsidian copy field.
Every imagery surface was affected: hero, card, tile and art.

**Fix:** explicit `width: '100%', height: '100%'` on the Image style. Pinned by 4 new cases in
`imageryBackdrop.test.tsx` (`... — the photo is given the card box explicitly (B-703)`, run over
ALL FOUR variants incl. `art`), **mutation-proven RED** by reverting the fix: 4 failed / 8 passed.
Device-verified on the Pro dashboard.

**Same session — the asset side.** The AI-Itinerary art is authored PORTRAIT (660x697) while the
card is ~1.4 landscape with `cover`, so a raw drop loses its top and bottom. Founder requirement
is the image renders WHOLE, and `contain` is not available (tried 2026-08-26, reverted — letterboxed
bands read as broken). New `scripts/compose-card-art.py` pre-composes the drop onto the 1200x900
card canvas the ImageryBackdrop contract already specifies — art right, obsidian copy field left,
97% canvas height so the card's ~5% `cover` crop cannot bite the artwork. Its MANIFEST entry
deliberately lives OUTSIDE `SMART_DIR`, because `smart_crop` would re-crop the composition back
(and is a no-op on the raw portrait anyway: the bright-region bbox covers the whole frame and a
portrait source can never reach the 1.30 aspect).

**Gates:** imagery suites 17 green; the two suites that failed the first full sweep
(`proLiveMissionRequestedCard`, `fileViewerCompanySuppression`) pass with the fix — 26 green
together — and `fileViewerCompanySuppression` ran 7.4 s here vs **182 s** in the sweep, i.e. a
load/async artifact, not this change. tsc 46 = baseline.

## Session 2026-08-30 (evening) — founder screenshots: photo caption + album dialog under the keyboard

Two founder reports, both pure UI, both fixed in this session. Neither touched crypto, the wire,
the envelope or the runtime.

### B-707 — a photo could not carry a message ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

**Report.** _"I still cannot add message to image before sending, just like WhatsApp we can attach
image and can attach msg also."_ Screenshot: a photo delivered with no text under it.

**Root cause — the plumbing was already there; only the input was missing.**
`sendMedia(convId, media, {caption})` has accepted a caption since the media-parity work:
`productionRuntime.ts` puts it in the optimistic bubble's `content` (~:4974) and ships it as the
message body via `sendText(convId, mediaOpts?.caption ?? '', {attachment})` (~:5055), and the bubble
already renders "Optional caption under any attachment" (`ChatScreen.tsx` ~:3581). Two UI facts were
what the founder was hitting:

1. `MediaPreviewTray` had **no caption field** — its own header said so
   (_"Captions are intentionally out of scope (media messages carry no caption field in the envelope
   yet)"_), a comment that had gone stale against the runtime it describes.
2. **A single pick never reached the tray.** Both chat screens carried
   `if (assets.length === 1) { enqueueMediaAssets(assets); return; }`, and `captureImage` pushed a
   camera shot straight down the queue. So the one case the founder hits daily had no surface to
   type on — the tray only ever appeared for a 2+ multi-select.

**Fix.**

- `MediaPreviewTray` gains a multiline caption `TextInput` between the thumbnail strip and the
  actions row, and `onSend` now carries the typed text. Deliberately **not** autofocused (most sends
  are wordless and the IME would bury the thumbnails the tray exists to show); reset on close,
  because the host keeps the component MOUNTED across openings and the next pick would otherwise
  inherit the previous photo's text — which `sendMedia` would publish as a message body.
- `pickImage` and `captureImage` route **every** pick through the tray, on `ChatScreen` and
  `DepartmentChatScreen` alike.
- `withBatchCaption(assets, caption)` (`pickedAssets.ts`) stamps the caption onto the **first** item
  of the batch — WhatsApp semantics, and the same rule B-450 already applies to a reply quote. It
  rides on the **asset**, never a screen-level ref, so it cannot leak into a later batch. A blank or
  whitespace-only caption is dropped, which also keeps an uncaptioned burst collapsing into an album
  tile (`imageAlbums.ts` breaks an album run on a caption, deliberately).

**Gates.** `pickedAssets` + new `mediaCaptionWiring` + `mediaPreviewTrayInset` + `voiceNoteLifecycle`
green; messenger-crypto **570 suites / 7108 tests** green (run twice — one intermediate red named
MD-08 / P3-B-2, moved, then vanished: the B-126 moving flake); app project **238 suites / 3261**
green ×2; `screens/messenger` 55 suites green; tsc **46 = baseline**; eslint 0 errors;
`expo export --platform android` produces a 14.5 MB Hermes bundle (the compile gate — no device was
attached this session, see below).

**Two pins this touched, both re-pointed rather than relaxed.** `mediaPreviewTrayInset` forbids a
literal `paddingBottom:` anywhere in the tray (B-284), so the caption field pads with
`paddingVertical`. `voiceNoteLifecycle` anchored the queue call on `next.ephemeralSource)` including
the closing paren; the caption argument now follows it, so the anchor became
`next.ephemeralSource[,)]` — the B-149 invariant (the flag IS forwarded through the queue) still
fails if the flag is dropped.

**Mutation-proved.** Every new assertion was checked against the pre-fix sources at HEAD, not just
against a hand mutation: the single-pick fast path, the camera's immediate `enqueueMediaAssets`, the
bare `onPress={onSend}` and the absent `TextInput` are all present/absent there exactly as the pins
require them not to be. Three live mutations (restore the fast path, bare `onSend`, drop the album
dialog's lift) each turned the matching pin red and were reverted.

### B-708 — the "New album" dialog sits behind the keyboard ⚠️ P2 · FIXED

**Report.** _"Pls shift box higher. It covered by keyboard. Its on vault, image upload, album
creating."_ Screenshot: Files ▸ New album, Cancel/Save behind the IME suggestion bar.

**Root cause.** `NameAlbumModal` (`albumUi.tsx`) `autoFocus`es its name field, so the IME is up for
the dialog's whole life — and the box was centred in the FULL window, which puts the button row
squarely behind the keyboard. It reacted to the IME not at all: no hook, no inset, nothing.

**Fix.** `useKeyboardLayout().overlap` on the sheet —
`style={[s.sheet, overlap > 0 && {marginBottom: overlap}]}`. On a **centred** backdrop the margin is
part of the child's outer box, so `justifyContent: 'center'` shifts the box up by exactly half the
overlap, which is the definition of centred in the space the keyboard leaves. Applied to the SHEET
and not the backdrop: the backdrop's `padding: 24` would be overridden by an inline `paddingBottom`
and the box would then touch the keyboard. One component, three consumers fixed — `FilesScreen`,
`VaultScreen` and the shared `FileViewer` all render this modal, and the founder reported it from
the Files tab.

**Gates.** `albumWiring` (+3 new assertions) and `keyboardContract` green; no dp constant, no banned
idiom (KAV / `keyboardVerticalOffset` / `Keyboard.addListener` / `kbHeight`).

### Owed on both — the device pass

No ADB device or emulator was reachable this session (`adb devices` empty; BlueStacks 5555 / 5565 /
5575 all refused the connection), so **neither fix has been seen on a phone**. Both are UI-only and
the production bundle compiles, but per the standing founder rule they are not "fixed" until they
appear in a post-install device log or screenshot. What to exercise:

## B-709 — Family spending-quota system: the §19 negative-remaining bug, and the whole credit-request lifecycle ⚠️ P1 · FIXED (not deployed)

Full-spec implementation against the existing family/wallet architecture. **Audited first**
— most of the spec was already built and is preserved, not rewritten:

| Spec           | Existing implementation (unchanged)                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| §1-§3 concepts | `family_members.holder_id` = Root, `member_id` = member, `spend_limit_credits` = quota, `spent_credits` = used, `wallet_balances.bravo_credits` = root credit           |
| §4/§5/§7       | Single txn, `family_members FOR UPDATE` **then** `wallet_balances FOR UPDATE` — the MON-4 lock order, in `BookingService.payWithCredits` and the dispatch escrow accept |
| §6             | `IdempotencyInterceptor`                                                                                                                                                |
| §10            | both limits already gated at the charge                                                                                                                                 |
| §24/§25/§51    | quotas may exceed the root balance; the balance is re-checked under lock at spend time                                                                                  |
| §26/§27        | refund reversal pinned to the CHARGE-TIME row via `wallet_transactions.metadata->>'family_row_id'`, `GREATEST(0,…)` underflow guard, escrow refund idempotent           |
| §31            | **INTEGER credits throughout** — no float anywhere, verified against the live schema                                                                                    |

### The live bug (§19)

`setSpendLimit` was a bare `UPDATE … SET spend_limit_credits = $3`. **No floor.** A holder
could set Alice's quota to 4,000 with 4,500 already spent and produce `Remaining = -৳500` —
the exact state §2 forbids. Now: a transaction, the member row `FOR UPDATE` (so the check is
against a value a concurrent charge cannot move underneath it), refusal with
`QUOTA_BELOW_SPENT` **plus the minimum** so §44's dialog can name it, and an audit row.

### What did not exist at all

- **§11-§17 credit requests.** New `family_credit_requests` table + full lifecycle: request,
  partial approval (§14), reject, cancel by either side, lazy expiry (§50). §12's duplicate
  gate is a **partial UNIQUE INDEX**, not a check-then-insert — two simultaneous taps both
  pass a preceding SELECT; only one can win an index.
- **§13/§18/§37 audit trail.** New `family_quota_audit`: previous/new limit, delta, the used
  amount at decision time, actor, request id. Written in the SAME transaction as the quota
  change. Quota used to be overwritten with no history at all.
- **§33/§34 threshold warnings.** New `family_members.quota_notified_pct` — a crossing marker
  claimed with a CONDITIONAL update, so ten transactions inside one band produce one warning
  and two racing charges cannot both announce it.
- **§21 root suspension.** `resolvePayer` now reads `users.suspended_at`; the dispatch path
  reads it **in the same locked statement** as the cap (`FOR UPDATE OF fm` — locking only the
  membership row, never the joined `users` row, which would be a new lock in a new order).
- **§8/§9 error split.** `SPENDING_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` vs `ROOT_CREDIT_UNAVAILABLE` vs
  `ROOT_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`, each with its own copy. §9 is explicit that a member whose quota
  is fine must never be told their quota is exhausted.
- **UI.** New member-side `FamilyQuotaCard` (§41 figures, §42 states, one non-duplicating
  action) and a §43 pending-request panel with approve/reject on `SecureProMembersScreen`.

### Deliberately NOT built (spec's own guidance)

- **§35/§36 quota reset** — the product is NO_RESET today. The spec says to document and
  preserve the current model rather than invent complexity. No reset period exists to honour.
- **§29 pending-transaction reservation** — already satisfied by the escrow model
  (`holdToEscrow` at accept), so nothing was invented on top of it.
- **§22 member suspension** — the product's `held_until` hold deliberately falls back to the
  member's OWN wallet rather than blocking outright. That is an existing, documented product
  decision that differs from the spec; preserved rather than rewritten, and flagged.

### Approval does NOT reserve root credit (§51) — documented on purpose

Raising a quota raises a **permission**, not a reservation. A holder with ৳1,000 may approve
two ৳800 requests; the balance is enforced again, under a lock, at spend time. That is what
makes `Root balance = -৳600` unreachable however fast the holder taps approve.

### Three pins re-pointed, never deleted

`MON-4` and `B-384` both anchored on the dispatch cap-read's exact column text, which the §21
JOIN aliased (`fm.spend_limit_credits`) and whose lock clause became `FOR UPDATE OF fm`. Both
re-pointed, and a NEW assertion added that the lock is `OF fm` — a bare `FOR UPDATE` across
the join would take a `users` lock this path has never held. `B-380` anchored on the phrase
"family spend limit"; §8 mandates different wording, so the pin now asserts the real
invariant (no raw code reaches the user, and the copy still routes them to the plan holder).

### Gates

auth-service **164 suites / 3037 tests green**; app project **3278 green** (three consecutive
clean runs — one intermittent failure never named the same test twice); booking project
**883 green**; mobile tsc **46 = baseline**; auth-service tsc clean; eslint 0 errors (one
pre-existing warning in `activitySync.ts:141`, untouched). New: 53 quota-math tests, 50
service tests, 20 client-error tests, 17 member-card render tests.

### A producer↔consumer pin caught a real gap in this work

`serverWakeKindParity` failed on the four new push kinds: a server kind with no client meta is
a wake the app cannot render, backfill or route. All four were then wired through
`serverWakeNotifications` (banner + BOOKING class), `activitySync` KIND_META (bell) and
`fcmBootstrap` (tap routing — holder kinds → members screen, member kinds → profile).

### DEPLOYED 2026-08-30 (staging)

**Migration APPLIED** to Supabase project `qkkfkicgoncxslbwhyhz` — confirmed to be the right
database by reading the box's own `docker-compose.staging.yml` `DATABASE_URL`, which points at
that project's pooler. The box's local `postgres` container is NOT what auth-service uses;
checking that first is what stopped this landing in the wrong database.

Post-migration verification (read-only): both tables exist; `quota_notified_pct` is `smallint`
and all **32** existing `family_members` rows defaulted to `0`; the partial index reads exactly
`UNIQUE (family_row_id) WHERE status = 'pending'`; RLS is ENABLED **and** FORCED on both tables;
**zero** `anon`/`authenticated` grants.

**The §12 race gate was proven against real Postgres**, not a mock — the one piece of SQL no
unit test could reach (`ON CONFLICT (family_row_id) WHERE status = 'pending' DO NOTHING` needs
the index predicate repeated for inference). In a rolled-back transaction, two inserts for the
same membership produced **one** row, and the survivor was the FIRST request (2,000), not the
second (5,000). Rollback verified clean: 0 rows in both new tables afterwards.

**auth-service BUILT + DEPLOYED.** `rsync` is absent in Git Bash on Windows, so this used the
manual tar flow the deploy script's own `need_cmd` failure names. The Docker build runs
`nest build`, so the build gated the deploy.

Verified inside the RUNNING container, not from the exit code:
`QUOTA_BELOW_SPENT`, `family_credit_requests`, `family_quota_audit`, `quota_notified_pct`,
`holder_suspended_at`, `SPENDING_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `root_account_suspended`,
`CREDIT_REQUEST_PENDING` — all present in `dist/`. All **7** new routes mapped at boot. From
outside, all six probed endpoints answer **401** (exist + JWT-guarded) against a **404** control
on a non-existent path — the control matters, or a blanket guard would look identical.
Container healthy, **0** errors in the logs since restart.

**Watchdog pristine snapshot REFRESHED** — and this was load-bearing, not hygiene. The B-376
self-heal watchdog runs every 5 min from cron and restores `pristine-main.tgz` on a stale

## B-710 — Message notifications stuck on the first message ⚠️ P0 · FIXED

**Founder report (2026-08-30):** _"The first incoming message appears in the notification. When a
second/third message arrives, the notification may remain stuck on the first message. New message
notifications sometimes arrive late. Multiple messages may arrive together. Background/killed-app
behaviour is inconsistent."_

Full audit: [`docs/qa/MSG_NOTIF_LIVE_UPDATE_AUDIT_2026-08-30.md`](docs/qa/MSG_NOTIF_LIVE_UPDATE_AUDIT_2026-08-30.md)
(method: 5 parallel lane auditors + 2 adversarial critics; the display layer was reproduced with a
scratch Jest probe before any fix was written).

**Six client defects, not one.** The MessagingStyle card that WhatsApp-style grouping depends on was
already correct; everything deciding _which draw wins_, _which rows reach it_, _whether it is ever
erased_, and _whether the notifier is even listening_ was not.

| #   | Defect                                                                       | Mechanism                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1  | A killed-app wake **erased** the card it was meant to back up                | `fcmHeadless.ts` resolves a DM's conversation id LOCALLY (`resolveDirectConversation`), so a content-free wake landed on the store notifier's own notifee id and `displayNotification` replaced the card with "New secure message". Under sealed sender a GROUP message resolves to the sender's DM, so it also overwrote the wrong thread. A comment in `callNotification.ts` asserted this was impossible — its premise (the SERVER sends no conversationId) was right, its conclusion was not, because the CLIENT resolves one. The warm lane had already refused the guess; the two lanes had drifted. |
| F2  | One headless wake **silenced the foreground cue lane for the whole process** | `startBackgroundMessageNotifier` returned early on `running` and left `headlessMode` set. The FCM headless task shares the app's JS VM, so with the app on screen `foregroundUi` (`!headlessMode && ...`) and `isBackgrounded()` (`s !== 'active'`) both read false and EVERY message hit the `!foregroundUi && !isBackgrounded()` bail. Three lanes found this independently.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| F3  | The card was draw-ordered, never deduped                                     | `thread.push` with no sort and no `messageId` check. Out-of-order draws rendered `[one, three, two]` and regressed `Notification.when` — Android's shade sort key — to the OLDER message. A duplicate draw rendered the same text twice and the 7-cap then evicted a real message.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| F4  | Only the newest row of a commit reached the card                             | `fresh.reduce(newest)` bannered one row per commit while `rememberSeen` watermarked the rest, so an offline catch-up lost the messages in between permanently. The self-send filter also ran AFTER the newest row was chosen, so one outbound row in the same commit burned the inbound ones.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| F5  | Nothing observed `EventType.DISMISSED`                                       | A swiped-away banner kept its accumulator: the next message re-rendered up to seven already-dismissed previews onto the lock screen, and the group summary counted banners that were gone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| F6  | The 10 s alert-collapse window was GLOBAL                                    | Any alerted wake silenced every conversation for ten seconds. The pair it exists to collapse always shares a `senderUserId` — which the store notifier had and was not forwarding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Plus a **headless hydration hold**: the runtime's history replay could re-banner a one-row
conversation on every wake (the `list.length > 1` anti-spray guard cannot catch that shape), and
that draw then told the wake's own fallback "a banner exists" for the message that actually arrived.

**Server (contributing):** S1 `sendEachForMulticast` RESOLVES on per-token failure, so a quota block
left the 2 s debounce armed and coalesced the whole burst behind a wake that reached nobody; S2 the
per-response error codes were discarded, which is why the report was not falsifiable from logs; S3
`sentAtMs` had been dropped from `scheduleTrailingChatWake`'s signature, so the trailing wake
stamped its own fire time — the only orderable field in the payload, invented and ~2 s wrong.

**Deliberately NOT built:** multi-device read-clear — **DESCOPED BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-31**
(_"no we don't need for now, this app can run only one device"_). **The product is single-device;
its absence is not a defect and must not be re-raised or half-built.** Details and the known
second-login token-eviction consequence are in the audit §4. Also not built: skipping the wake for
a socket-live recipient (would cut FCM quota burn but a lost socket emit would then produce NO
notification — rejected on "never lose a message"); an FCM push-identity dedupe (battery, not
correctness); iOS dismissal.

**Verification.** `messenger-crypto` 571 suites / 7136 tests green, run twice; app-project messenger
screens 54 / 743 green; `messenger-service` 54 / 712 green; tsc 46 = baseline; eslint clean. Every
new pin RED first — the display pins failed 12/20 before the fix, and the notifier and server pins
were mutation-proven afterwards with the mutation verified as applied before the result was
believed. Two pins were RE-POINTED, not deleted, including the one whose own comment said _"if the
ids collide, the downgrade becomes real, and THIS TEST MUST BECOME the assertion that the named card
survives."_

**Deployed 2026-08-31:** `messenger-service` shipped to staging via the manual tar flow (rsync is
absent on Windows/Git Bash and the script fails loudly rather than deploying stale code). Verified
the way the runbook demands — not by exit code: `releaseDebounce` and `logCodes` went 0 → 3 inside
the RUNNING container's `dist/`, `/healthz` returns 200, startup logs clean with FCM initialised,
and the watchdog pristine snapshot was refreshed and confirmed to carry the new source (otherwise
the self-heal watchdog restores the OLD tree).

**Owed: a device pass** — the 12-case matrix is §6 of the audit. Case 6 first: kill the app, take a
message, open the app, then receive one while looking at the screen (the F2 regression).

## B-711 — "Mark as read" from the notification leaves the unread count behind ⚠️ P2 · OPEN

Found while auditing B-710 (Lane D, finding F-2). Not fixed: it is a store change on a different
surface from the notification pipeline, and bundling it into B-710 would widen a
already-large diff into `messengerStore.ts`.

**Mechanism.** The action handler (`fcmBootstrap.ts`, `e.t === 'read'`) calls
`productionRuntime.markRead(convId)`. That flips each message's `status` to `'read'` via
`updateMessageStatusBulk` and emits `transport.sendReadReceipt` — so the SENDER does get the blue
tick — but neither function touches `unread_count`. The only thing that zeroes it is
`setActiveConversation`, and nothing on this lane calls it.

**What the user sees.** Press _Mark as read_ on the banner: the banner goes, the sender sees
✓✓ — and the chat-list row keeps its unread pill, the Messenger tab keeps its count, and the
NEXT banner drawn re-asserts a launcher badge that still counts the conversation they just read.

**Fix shape.** A dedicated store action (zero `unread_count` for the conversation and its
`direct:<peer>` sibling slot — `directConversationSlots` already answers that), called from the
pending-action drain next to `markRead`. Do NOT put it inside `markRead` itself:
`productionRuntime.ts` is a MESSAGE_LOOP trigger file and that would owe the §5 caller sweep.

## B-712 — a one-row conversation re-banners its old message on every killed-VM boot ⚠️ P2 · OPEN

Found during B-710. The anti-spray guard in `backgroundMessageNotifier.onStoreChange` is
`if (firstSight && !(cid in prev.messages) && list.length > 1) {continue;}` — it needs MORE THAN
ONE row, so a conversation holding exactly one message (a quiet channel, a first-contact DM)
walks straight through when the runtime boot replays SQLCipher history through the subscriber.
A fresh VM's once-ever alert record is empty, so it **dings** as well. Worse, that draw bumps the
cue generation, so the wake's own fallback concludes "a banner exists" for the message that
actually arrived.

**A fix was written and reverted — do not re-derive it.** A `hydrationHold` (suppress draws
between a headless start and the runtime being ready) creates a strictly worse bug:
`getMessengerRuntime` fires `void transport.connect()` **un-awaited** and the gateway flushes
pending envelopes the moment the socket authenticates, so the wake's own message can be committed
_inside_ the hold — watermarked by `rememberSeen`, suppressed, then invisible to `pullEnvelopes`,
which reports `'drained'` and makes `fcmHeadless` skip its fallback too. **Zero notification for a
real message.** The hold can also stick ON: its one release runs after an awaited runtime build
whose rejection is cached for the process lifetime.

**Correct fix shape.** A hydration SIGNAL, not a time window: have the store's bulk loader
(`hydrateMessages`) mark the commit it produces, and have the notifier skip exactly that commit.
That distinguishes "replayed from disk" from "arrived over the wire", which no timing heuristic
can.

Pinned as `DOCUMENTS B-712 — a one-row boot replay still re-banners its old message` in
`src/modules/messenger/__tests__/backgroundMessageNotifier.test.ts`; when the real fix lands, that
assertion becomes `expect(display).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. The companion case
`a message arriving during the runtime boot is never swallowed` pins the regression the revert
exists to prevent — do not delete it.

---

## B-713 — Product-gate card photos rendered near-black ⚠️ P3 · FIXED (renderer); asset follow-up owed

**Report.** Founder, 2026-08-31, with a screenshot of the "Choose your dashboard" gate:
_"Can you make these images maximum brightness, because there's no writing over it."_

**Root cause.** `ProductGateScreen` drew its card photo band with `ImageryBackdrop
variant="hero"`. That variant exists for a full-bleed hero where the headline, sub-line and
CTA sit ON the photo, so its scrim ramps to 78% obsidian by 42% of the height and 95% by 72%,
on top of `imageOpacity: 0.9`. But this screen's `cardBand` (height 104) contains ONLY the
backdrop — the icon, title and description live in the sibling `cardBody` below it. **No copy
crosses the image at all**, so the entire scrim was protecting text that is not there.

Measured across the 104 dp band, visible image fraction = `imageOpacity × (1 − scrimAlpha)`:

| dp into band | before (`hero`) | after (`band`) |
| ------------ | --------------- | -------------- |
| 0            | 0.702           | 1.000          |
| 44           | 0.196           | 1.000          |
| 75           | 0.045           | 0.755          |
| mean         | **0.238**       | **0.825**      |

i.e. **3.46× brighter overall**, and completely unscrimmed across the top 62%.

**Fix.** A NEW `band` variant — NOT a change to `hero`, which has **23 consumers** and almost
all of them do put copy over the photo; editing it would have silently dropped contrast on 22
other screens, which is exactly the failure the existing pin's comment warns about. `band` is
`imageOpacity: 1` with the gradient clear to 62% and ramping only inside the bottom third.
That tail is a BLEND, not a scrim: the band has no border of its own, so without it the photo
ends on a hard horizontal cut against the card body.

`band` is the only variant with no alpha floor (`minTextAlpha: 0`, `textStops: []`), so its
safety rests entirely on "no copy over it". That is pinned two ways rather than trusted: the
recipe is asserted genuinely unscrimmed + full opacity, and a **source scan fixes the allowed
call sites** — a second consumer has to come to the test and state that its photo is text-free
instead of quietly inheriting the exemption. Both mutation-proved (revert the call site → red;
put a 0.3 alpha on the top stop → red).

Checked for the duplicate-copy class: `ProductGateScreen` is the ONLY screen where the
backdrop is the sole child of a dedicated band view. Every other usage is an absolute-fill
behind content, where the scrim is doing its real job — `HomeSelectionScreen` verified by
hand and correctly left on `hero`.

**Gates.** `imageryBackdrop` 16 green (was 13); app project 239 suites / 3282 green; tsc
**46 = baseline**; eslint clean.

### Asset follow-up (the renderer is now at its ceiling)

Measured luminance of the exact centre-crop region each card actually renders (`cover`
centre-crops), so this is what the fix can and cannot buy:

| card              | source       | visible band mean L | before → after (of 255) |
| ----------------- | ------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Messenger         | 1080×810     | 24.7                | 5.9 → **20.4**          |
| Secure Services   | 853×**1661** | 15.2                | 3.6 → **12.6**          |
| Virtual Bodyguard | 1080×608     | 38.8                | 9.2 → **32.0**          |

Secure Services stays the dimmest and it is **not** the renderer: `heroBookProtection.jpg` is a
PORTRAIT asset (aspect 0.51) squeezed into a ~3.3:1 band, so only **16%** of the file is
visible and that centre strip is genuinely dark (mean 15/255). Per this component's own note —
"the real fix is the ASSET CONTRACT, not the renderer" — that card wants a landscape crop or a
brighter drop. Full brightness is now applied; there is nothing further to win in code.

**Device pass owed** — no ADB device was reachable, so this is measured, not seen on a phone.

## B-715 — "single tick, then 4 s, then the notification AND the double tick together" ⚠️ P2 · server hold FIXED; device split OWED

**Founder report.** A sends a 1:1 message; A sees ✓ immediately; ~4 s later B (who is not in
the app) gets the notification and A's tick flips to ✓✓ at that same moment.

### What the ticks actually mean (verified — the ticks are honest, do not "fix" them)

`messageTicks.ts:44-54` is a pure status→glyph table with no timers. The optimistic bubble is
written `status:'sending'` → `'pending'` → a **progress-clock, not a check** (`tickIcon.ts:28`).
`'sent'` (the ✓) is set ONLY on the relay's `envelope.accepted` frame (`productionRuntime.ts:7796`)
or after the HTTP fallback's POST returns (`:4719`). So **the founder's 4 s window starts at the
relay accept**, and every pre-network sender cost sits outside it. "A immediately sees ✓" is itself
evidence the submit round-trip was fast.

✓✓ is `envelope.delivered`, emitted only inside `ack()` after the recipient hard-deletes the
envelope (`envelope.service.ts:447-483`). Correction to a first draft of this entry: it is gated on
a recipient-**originated** event, not strictly the ack — a read receipt drives `'sent'` → `'read'`
directly with no `'delivered'` precondition (`productionRuntime.ts:7604-7664`), and `ackQueue.ts:110`
DROPS a failed batch, so a message can be read with its ack never landing. Not this bug's path
(B never opened the app), but the invariant is weaker than it looks.

### Root cause of the reported case: the recipient's process is FROZEN, so FCM is the only lane

Nothing disconnects the messenger socket on background — the AppState handler only sends
`presence:'away'` and HTTP-drains the outbox (`productionRuntime.ts:2179-2199`). That is NOT the
same as the socket being usable: RN freezes the JS timer queue for a backgrounded process
(`:2184-2189`, `client.ts:817-823`), so the server's immediate `envelope.deliver` emit lands on a
**buffered dead fd** — already documented as **DL-2** in
`docs/qa/MESSAGE_DELIVERY_LATENCY_2026-08-29.md`. The high-priority FCM data wake is therefore not
redundancy; it is the only thing that thaws the process.

That upgrades the founder's "they happen together" from coincidence to **causation**: the same wake
that draws the banner is what un-freezes the code that acks. The killed lane makes it exact — the
drain persists first and banners fully-resolved (`fcmHeadless.ts:276-278`), and `headlessDrain.ts`
awaits `flushAcksBounded` at the very END of that drain. Banner and ✓✓ are both terminal events of
one chain, which is why they land in the same instant instead of 200 ms apart.

**The server is NOT the bottleneck for this case (measured).** Staging, 2026-08-31, container
`bravo/messenger-service:staging` created 03:15Z with `CHAT_DEBOUNCE_SEC=2` verified in the running
`dist/`. `[envelope.send] accepted` → `push.chat.delivered` for isolated messages:
138.1 145.1 145.3 147.1 155.6 160.0 176.4 180.6 182.8 187.9 192.9 200.3 316.5 343.9 ms
(n=14, median **178.5 ms**, max 343.9 ms).

Two labelling corrections a critic caught, both load-bearing for anyone re-reading this:

1. That interval is **not** "accept → push trigger". The wake is voided at `messenger.gateway.ts:1409`
   and the `accepted` log prints at `:1430`, so the wake was already in flight when the anchor
   printed. The number bounds the wake's OWN work: debounce SET + token-registry read + the FCM
   HTTPS round-trip. The post-`put` Redis work that precedes it (aux writes + the awaited
   `tryFanOut` → `getOrMintAckToken`, four sequential round-trips in total) is still unmeasured.
2. `push.chat.delivered` means **the FCM API call returned**. It says nothing about the device.

### The separable server defect that WAS found and fixed (this is B-715 proper)

Messages 2..N of a burst are coalesced behind a 2 s window, and the trailing wake that covers them
fired `CHAT_DEBOUNCE_SEC * 1000` from the moment it was SCHEDULED — overshooting the window end by
however far into the window the message landed. Measured hold, accept → the trailing wake that
covered it: 828.8 1319.2 1814.4 2086.6 2154.7 2303.4 **2847.5** ms (n=7; 7 of 51 wake attempts over
7 days = 13.7%). Worst case: accepted 06:49:54.395, pushed 06:49:56.482, against a window that
ended at 06:49:54.461 — **1.94 s of the 2.09 s hold was overshoot.**

Fixed by firing at the `PTTL` remainder plus a 100 ms guard, with `pttl >= 0` (not `> 0`: Redis
clamps a sub-millisecond remainder to 0, and `> 0` dropped exactly that case onto the 2 s fallback —
a latency cliff at the precise boundary the change exists to remove).

**The second defect, un-masked by the first fix.** Firing at the window end leaves the
`push-chat-trailing` marker (EX 2 from scheduling) still live, so the next window's first in-window
message finds `claimed !== 'OK'` and schedules NOTHING — the tail of a sustained burst gets no wake
at all. The arithmetic: window opens at W0, timer fires at W0+2100, a message claiming the marker at
C kills it at C+2000, so the marker outlives the timer whenever **C > W0+100** — i.e. every
in-window message after the first 100 ms, the common case, not an edge. Previously masked because
the flat 2 s delay expired the marker at the same instant it fired. The timer now DELs the marker
before re-entering, and logs a failed DEL instead of swallowing it ("it TTLs out anyway" is exactly
the assumption the arithmetic above disproves).

**A defect in my own first fix, caught by the adversarial critic — recorded so it is not
re-proposed.** An intermediate cut dropped the guard and had the timer DELETE the debounce key
instead, to avoid the guard's ~100 ms cost for a message arriving at the very start of a window.
That `DEL` is **not owner-scoped**: a timer delayed past its own window's expiry deletes whichever
window is live _then_, which may be a newer message's. It does not lose a wake — it INFLATES,
collapsing the coalescer for that pair so a burst tail reverts toward one FCM per message, undoing
N-32/P2-14. The owner-safe form would be a Lua compare-and-delete on a token the timer wrote; the
guard buys the same safety for 100 ms and no new script. The guard is now pinned by two tests
(a guard-less revision was green against the first cut of them).

Also handled: `pttl === -1` (a key with no TTL) is unreachable — `sendChatWake` is the only writer
and always uses `EX` — but the old "keep the conservative full-window delay" answer was the worst
available for it, since the key never expires and the re-entry would self-debounce, re-claim the
marker it just released, and reschedule every 2 s forever, delivering nothing. The key is now healed
with `PEXPIRE` instead.

**Scope honesty:** this fix cannot explain the founder's report. An isolated message takes the
leading edge and never schedules a trailing wake. It is a real, measured, separate defect found
while instrumenting the reported one.

### The one experiment that settles the rest — OWED

`heldMs=` was added to `push.chat.delivered` for exactly this (the first server-side latency number
this pipeline has had; previously it had to be reconstructed by hand-diffing two log lines, which is
how a 2.8 s hold sat unnoticed). Pair it with the client `[NOTIFLAT]` probes, which have shipped
since 2026-08-01 and **have still never been read off a phone**:

```bash
# device B, release APK, swipe-killed (never Force-stop, never BlueStacks)
adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS | grep -E "NOTIFLAT|recv\.total"
# server
docker logs -f bravo-staging-msgr | grep -E "push.chat|envelope.send"
```

If `push.chat.delivered heldMs=180` prints at T and the device's
`[NOTIFLAT] msg-wake pending placeholder at +30ms` prints at T+3.8 s, the 3.8 s is **pure FCM
transit under Doze** and nothing downstream matters. If the gap is small and `outcome=` is late,
**DL-1** (the serialized decrypt+commit chain on the single global `txnChain`,
`receiveTransaction.ts:50`) is live — still the only open P0 in the delivery-latency doc, and still
⚠ UNMEASURED. Until that runs, the device half of this entry is a hypothesis, not a finding.

**DEPLOY TRAP — read before the staging capture.** `package.json` `start` is `node dist/main`, and
messenger deploys go out through the manual tar-to-Contabo flow, not a CI build. The local
`apps/messenger-service/dist/` is untracked, ignored, and older than this fix — `grep -c
"pttl\|TRAILING_WAKE_GUARD_MS" dist/push/push.service.js` → **0**. Tarring or restarting without
`npm run build` first ships the PRE-FIX bundle, and the capture taken to validate B-715 then
reproduces the same 2087 ms hold — which reads as "the fix doesn't work" rather than "the fix isn't
deployed". `heldMs=` exists nowhere in the old bundle, so its presence in the live log is the cheap
one-line proof the new binary is running.

### Related, found during this investigation, NOT fixed

- **Killed-lane perceived latency is the drain, by design.** The first thing a killed-app wake shows
  is `bravo-messages-pending`, `AndroidImportance.LOW`, no sound, no heads-up
  (`callNotification.ts:846-857`) — deliberately silent (a sealed-sender wake may be a receipt or
  reaction, P2-BR-3). The audible banner waits for the drain, raced against
  `HEADLESS_DRAIN_BUDGET_MS = 8000` (`fcmHeadless.ts:37`). Founder-approved 2026-07-29 (Signal's
  drain-then-notify model). Not changed — the lever, if the founder wants the banner sooner, is to
  alert on the placeholder, which re-opens the reaction/receipt ding class.
- **`index.js` evaluates the whole app graph before the headless handler is installed.** `index.js:18`
  `import App from './App'` and `:13-14` `registerWebRTCGlobals()` are hoisted above the
  `setBackgroundMessageHandler` at `:47`, so a cold headless wake that only needs notifee + Keychain
  pays the full module-graph eval first. Structural; unmeasured.
- **Messenger message priority — INVESTIGATED, NO CHANGE WARRANTED (founder decision 1,
  2026-08-31).** The question was whether the msg-wake's own priority contributes to the delay. It
  does not: a chat wake is already at the maximum on both platforms, so there is no priority
  headroom left to buy.
  - Android: `push.service.ts` chat-wake block — `android: {priority: 'high', collapseKey,
ttl: CHAT_WAKE_FCM_TTL_MS}`. `'high'` is what permits Doze bypass AND is the precondition for
    the headless task starting at all (`ReactNativeFirebaseMessagingReceiver.java:61-64` logs
    "Background messages only work if the message priority is set to 'high'").
  - iOS: `apns: {headers: {'apns-priority': '10', ...}}` — 10 is the maximum; the payload also
    carries a visible `alert` alongside `content-available` (OR-3), because `content-available`
    alone is a silent push iOS does not deliver to a force-quit app.
  - TTL is 28 days (FCM max, P2-BR-4), so the wake is not discarded on a long-offline device.
    **Conclusion: our backend is not delaying the messenger wake through priority.** Do not change it.
- **Separately, and deliberately NOT changed** (founder: do not globally change unrelated classes):
  the SERVER-EVENT lane `sendDataOnlyToUser` ships `priority: highPriority ? 'high' : 'normal'`
  (`push.service.ts:446-450`) against a closed allow-list (`:296-300`), so `payout-settled`,
  `*-hour-checkin` and `enterprise.*` are data-only at NORMAL priority — which cannot wake JS on a
  killed device and which FCM discards past its 10-minute TTL. A deliberate App-Standby quota trade
  (`:293-295`). Recorded as a known limitation of those classes; it does not touch messaging.
- **`default_notification_channel_id` is the empty string** in the merged release manifest. Latent
  only: every chat wake is data-only with no `notification` block (`push.service.ts:788-798`), so it
  never bites today. Config hygiene.
- ~~**`addPendingDelivered` is keyed by userId, not device**~~ — **RETRACTED 2026-08-31, founder
  correction.** The premise was wrong: this product does not support concurrent sessions for one
  account. `auth.service.ts:109-148` performs a **single-device takeover** on login — it evicts the
  user's other same-platform devices by revoking their access jti, and the gateway's revoked-socket
  sweep drops their sockets (the `platform !== 'web'` guard at `:116` is B-71, so ops/web is
  deliberately outside the mobile takeover). One account, one active device: there is no second
  device to race for the receipt, so keying by userId is not a defect, it is the correct key for
  this data model. **Do not introduce multi-device receipt or data-model changes.** Receipt
  correctness is to be tested only within the single-active-device architecture.

## B-712 — a one-row conversation re-banners its old message on every killed-VM boot ✅ P2 · FIXED 2026-08-31

**Founder decision 4 (2026-08-31): fix it, idempotently, without weakening the
notification/privacy model.**

**Root cause.** A killed-VM boot replays the whole SQLCipher history through the notifier's store
subscriber. The anti-spray guard was `firstSight && !(cid in prev.messages) && list.length > 1`
(`backgroundMessageNotifier.ts`), whose `length > 1` term is a PROXY for "this is bulk disk
replay". A conversation holding exactly one message fails that proxy, walks through to the draw,
and re-banners — **with sound**, because a fresh VM's once-ever alert ledger (`alertedMessageIds`)
is empty. That draw then bumped `messagePostedGeneration`, which told the wake's own fallback
witness "a banner exists" for the message that had actually just arrived.

**Fix — the store signal the B-710 revert note asked for, not a time window.**
`hydrateMessages` bumps a new `hydrationGeneration` counter **inside its own immer producer**;
`onStoreChange` computes `isHydrationCommit = state.hydrationGeneration !== prev.hydrationGeneration`
once per commit and skips the draw for such a commit — after `rememberSeen`, so the rows are still
watermarked and can never be drawn later either.

Three properties that make this different from the reverted B-710 "hydration hold", which was a
TIME WINDOW and swallowed a real message that committed inside it:

1. **It marks a COMMIT, not an interval.** zustand `set` is synchronous, so a live `appendMessage`
   is always a different commit with an unchanged counter. It is structurally impossible for the
   mark to cover a live arrival — the exact failure that got the hold reverted.
2. **It cannot stick on.** A counter that differs only on the hydration commit is self-clearing;
   a boolean would still read true after the subscriber returned.
3. **It is not persisted** (the `partialize` whitelist omits it) — a generation restored from disk
   would make the first live commit of a session look like a hydration.

`list.length > 1` was **kept** alongside it rather than replaced: it also covers bulk
materialisation this counter cannot see, and several suites pin its behaviour. Two narrow
conditions beat one widened one.

**Why the one-commit constraint mattered.** `bootstrapDrainYield.test.ts` pins
`hydrateMessages` at **exactly one** store commit, so the bump had to ride the existing producer —
a second `set` to flip a flag would have failed that pin. `orphanConversationRepair.test.ts` is a
source-TEXT scan requiring the literal `hydrateMessages: (map, bypassCap)` signature, so the params
were left untouched.

**Test trap worth recording.** The old `DOCUMENTS B-712` pin faked the boot replay with a raw
`useMessengerStore.setState(...)`, which does **not** go through `hydrateMessages` and therefore
does not bump the counter. A correct fix would have left it green at the OLD assertion and read as
"the fix does nothing". The test now drives the replay through `hydrateMessages` and asserts three
things: no banner, `messagePostedGeneration` unmoved, **and** that a live `appendMessage` in the
very next commit still draws — the anti-revert half.

**Gates.** `backgroundMessageNotifier` 52/52; the pins that guard this surface (`logAudit`,
`recvLatProbe`, `bootstrapDrainYield`, `orphanConversationRepair`, `statusWriteMissWarn`,
`sendProbes`) 104/104; app-project messenger screens 743 green; tsc **46 = baseline**. Both halves
mutation-proved independently — neutering the notifier check and removing the store bump each turn
the B-712 case red on its own. **Device pass owed.**

---

## B-715 instrumentation — the T0…T13 timeline is now assemblable ⚙️ 2026-08-31

**Founder ask: stop changing things that _could_ explain the delay; instrument it and name the
interval.** This is that instrumentation. Nothing below changes behaviour.

### The join key, which is what was actually missing

A timeline spanning three processes needs one id. `envelopeId` (truncated to 8) was already on the
server's `accepted`/`deliver` lines and on the recipient's WS receive path — but **the sender never
logged any id at all**, and the push lines carried none, so the chain was broken in two places.
Both are closed:

| Was                                                                                    | Now                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| sender's `[LAGDIAG] [send.*]` lines carry no id — A's half of the timeline is orphaned | `[LAGDIAG] [send.accepted] clientMsgId=<8> env=<8>` in `handleAccepted` — the ONLY place on the client where both ids coexist, and it is also the ✓ instant |
| `push.chat.*` lines name only the recipient                                            | all four carry `env=<8>` (`delivered`, `debounced`, `no-tokens`, `voip-fallback`)                                                                           |
| HTTP submit lane logs no `accepted` at all                                             | `[envelope.send] accepted … lane=http` mirrors the WS line; both now carry `lane=` and `postPutMs=`                                                         |

`envelopeId` is **log-only and never reaches the FCM payload** — putting a per-message identifier in
front of Google for no client benefit would be a metadata regression, not an instrumentation win.
`push-chat-wake.spec` pins the `data` block at exactly its four keys, so a leak fails there; the two
wake-gating specs now assert the opts shape EXACTLY (not `objectContaining`) so anything new added
at that boundary has to be declared.

### Stage coverage

| Stage         | Probe                                             | Note                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T2b (✓ shown) | `[LAGDIAG] [send.accepted]`                       | new — the join                                                                                                                              |
| T3            | `[envelope.send] accepted … lane= postPutMs=`     | HTTP lane new; `lane`/`postPutMs` new                                                                                                       |
| **T4**        | `[envelope.deliver] emit … localSocket=`          | **no offline/background decision exists to instrument** — see below                                                                         |
| T3→T5         | `[submit] slow post-persist tail … postPutMs=`    | new, warns ≥50 ms                                                                                                                           |
| T5→T6         | `push.chat.delivered … heldMs= fcmMs=`            | `fcmMs` new — splits provider cost from our hold                                                                                            |
| T7            | `[NOTIFLAT] T7 wake in kind= transitMs=`          | **was `console.log` → invisible in release.** `transitMs` differences the wake's `sentAtMs` against arrival = FCM transit, directly         |
| T7b           | `[NOTIFLAT] T7 warm wake in …`                    | same; the old line dumped the whole payload, so it was NOT promoted verbatim                                                                |
| T8→T10        | `[NOTIFLAT] headless drain <verdict>: drainMs= …` | **un-gated** — it only printed when the verdict was NOT 'drained', hiding the baseline a capture compares against                           |
| T9b/T11b      | `[LAGDIAG] [recv.drain] env=<8> handled= page=`   | new — the push-woken pull lane had NO per-message evidence. Gated to pages ≤10 so a 1000-envelope bootstrap page still cannot drown the log |
| T12/T13 (✓✓)  | `[LAGDIAG] [send.delivered] env=<8> flipped=`     | new. `flipped` distinguishes "receipt arrived but moved nothing" from "no receipt arrived"                                                  |

**Release-visibility is the point.** `babel.config.js` strips `console.log` and keeps `warn`, so
every client probe here is `console.warn`. Two of the most important stages were `console.log` and
therefore did not exist on the only build worth measuring.

### T4 — the answer is that there is no such step

The founder's timeline asks for "relay decides recipient is offline/background". **The relay never
makes that decision.** `tryFanOut` emits to the recipient's room and returns a this-node-only hint;
the wake is then fired **unconditionally** on `urgent !== false && wakeEligible`, with recipient
presence never consulted. So there is no branch to instrument and no decision cost — which is also
why §10/§11 of the brief are already satisfied: nothing waits for a WS attempt to fail.

### How to read the capture

```bash
# recipient, release APK, swipe-killed (never Force-stop, never an emulator)
adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS | grep -E "NOTIFLAT|LAGDIAG"
# sender
adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS | grep -E "send\.accepted|send\.delivered|send\.1v1"
# relay
docker logs -f bravo-staging-msgr | grep -E "envelope.send|push.chat|submit\]"
```

Join on `env=<8>`. The decisive number is `T7 transitMs`: it is measured against the relay's own
accept time, so it is **FCM transit under Doze, standalone, with no clock-sync between the two
phones required** — the single reading that says whether the remaining seconds are the provider's
or ours. If it is large, the backend is exonerated and the work is OS/provider-side. If it is small
and `drainMs` is large, the recipient's boot/pull chain is the target and DL-1 (the serialized
decrypt+commit chain, still the only open P0 in the delivery-latency doc) is live.

**Not deployed, not device-verified.** Build before tarring — see the B-715 deploy trap above.

Next free B-716.
